title: Validity, Conceptual Robustness and Confounding
tldr: Where and how the validity, conceptual robustness and confounding of empirical ML research break, mapped across the field's research questions.
about: VCRC reads any empirical ML result as a measurement-and-inference chain and asks where its VALIDITY, conceptual robustness and confounders break. The ROOT axis RQ carries the field's research questions about validity (construct definition, construct/discriminant validity, operationalization fidelity, measurement reliability, sampling, contamination/gaming, evaluation awareness, annotation/ground truth, causal warrant, external/criterion validity, temporal validity, Goodhart, harness confounds, positive/negative validity evidence, reproducibility, fair comparison). The other axes are read per paper: LOCUS is the pipeline link the issue sits on; THREAT is the kind of validity threat or confound; VALIDITY is the classic validity type (construct / internal / external / statistical-conclusion / temporal); DOMAIN is the research subject / evaluation class; INSTRUMENT is the measurement instrument the finding rests on. A cell is one full coordinate point; the papers sitting there answer it, and authored empty points are research gaps. Papers are weighted by recency + citations so the current research front and the canon read heaviest.

axes.name: Research question
axes.desc: The field's research questions about the validity, conceptual robustness and confounding of empirical ML research - the mandatory ROOT axis, assembled first from the seed brief and the papers' future-work. Each paper carries the validity question its finding answers, read from its own content.

valueDescs.RQ1: Is the target construct defined and theory-grounded (nomological network, AI-native constructs) before a measure is built?
valueDescs.RQ2: Does the measure capture the intended construct and not a confounder or surface proxy (construct + discriminant validity)?
valueDescs.RQ3: Is the operationalization (items/tasks/prompts) a faithful, sufficiently-complex realization that does not leak format or shortcut cues?
valueDescs.RQ4: How reliable is the scorer/measurement instrument (LLM-judge variance and bias, item-response theory, statistical power, uncertainty)?
valueDescs.RQ5: Is the evaluation set representative and realistic, not convenience sampling, and does it cover the population?
valueDescs.RQ6: Can the evaluation be gamed, and can train/test contamination be detected (including under reinforcement-learning or evasive hiding)?
valueDescs.RQ7: Does the system behave differently because it knows it is being evaluated (evaluation awareness, sandbagging, reactivity)?
valueDescs.RQ8: Are per-item scores annotated and aggregated without annotator/label/ground-truth dependencies (annotation science, rater effects)?
valueDescs.RQ9: Is the causal inference about the system warranted, free of confounds, spurious correlations and shortcut features (internal validity)?
valueDescs.RQ10: Do results generalize to real-world / out-of-distribution outcomes (external / criterion / ecological validity, transportability)?
valueDescs.RQ11: How does validity drift over time and with scale (temporal validity, benchmark saturation, scaling-law validity)?
valueDescs.RQ12: How does optimization pressure corrupt the metric (Goodhart, reward hacking), and what principled limits exist?
valueDescs.RQ13: In agentic/protocol-heavy evaluations, how does the harness/scaffold/training setup confound what is being measured?
valueDescs.RQ14: How do we provide positive (confirmatory) and negative (red-team / falsification) evidence that an evaluation is valid?
valueDescs.RQ15: Is the empirical result reproducible and statistically sound (replication, significance testing, multiple comparisons, nondeterminism)?
valueDescs.RQ16: Are baselines and comparisons fair (tuning and compute parity, no leakage between conditions, sound ranking/aggregation)?

axes.name: Validity type
axes.desc: The classic validity type (Cook & Campbell taxonomy) the finding bears on - read per paper from its own content.

valueDescs.construct: Whether the measure captures the intended theoretical construct.
valueDescs.internal: Whether the inferred causal relationship is free of confounds within the study.
valueDescs.external: Whether the result generalizes to other populations, settings and times.
valueDescs.statistical-conclusion: Whether the statistical inference (significance, power, uncertainty) is sound.
valueDescs.temporal: Whether validity holds over time and across scale (drift, saturation).

axes.name: Measurement instrument
axes.desc: The measurement instrument a paper's finding rests on - read per paper from its own content.

valueDescs.LLM-judge: An LLM acts as the scorer/judge of the output.
valueDescs.statistical / metric: A statistical estimator or metric produces the score (IRT, conformal, error bars, correlation, power analysis, psychometrics).
valueDescs.human: Human annotation or rating is the scoring instrument.
valueDescs.rule-based / verifier: A deterministic rule, exact-match, unit test, programmatic verifier or contamination detector produces the score.
valueDescs.classifier / probe: A trained classifier or activation probe produces the score.
valueDescs.none / theoretical: No measurement instrument - a theoretical, position, taxonomy or survey work.

axes.name: Pipeline locus
axes.desc: Which link of the empirical-ML measurement-and-inference pipeline the validity issue sits on - read per paper from its own content.

valueDescs.Construct definition: Defining the abstract target construct and mapping the real-world target onto it.
valueDescs.Operationalization: Turning the construct into concrete items, tasks or prompts.
valueDescs.Data sampling: Choosing which items/data make up the evaluation or training set.
valueDescs.Measurement / scoring: Scoring an output into a number (judge, metric, classifier, verifier).
valueDescs.Score aggregation: Combining per-item scores into a reported metric or ranking.
valueDescs.Statistical inference: Drawing statistical conclusions (significance, uncertainty, power) from the scores.
valueDescs.Generalization / deployment: From the measured score to the real-world / out-of-distribution deployment claim.
valueDescs.Experimental protocol / harness: The surrounding experimental setup, agent scaffold, tooling or training protocol that runs the study.

axes.name: Validity threat
axes.desc: The kind of validity threat or confound the paper concerns - read per paper from its own content.

valueDescs.Construct misrepresentation: The measure under- or mis-represents the intended construct (a surface proxy).
valueDescs.Confounding: A confounder or spurious/shortcut feature breaks the causal link between score and construct.
valueDescs.Contamination / leakage: Train/test overlap, memorization or look-ahead leakage inflates the score.
valueDescs.Gaming / Goodhart: Optimization pressure or adversarial manipulation corrupts the metric.
valueDescs.Unreliability / variance: Noise, instability or scorer bias make the measurement unreliable.
valueDescs.Sampling bias: The evaluation set is unrepresentative or convenience-sampled.
valueDescs.Reactivity / evaluation awareness: The system behaves differently because it detects the evaluation.
valueDescs.Reproducibility failure: Results fail to replicate across runs, setups or implementations.

axes.name: Research subject
axes.desc: The research subject or evaluation class a paper's finding concerns - read per paper from its own content.

valueDescs.capability: Capability or general benchmark-performance measurement (knowledge, psychometrics, leaderboards).
valueDescs.safety: Safety-oriented evaluation (jailbreaks, harmfulness, guardrails, misuse, alignment).
valueDescs.honesty: Honesty / truthfulness evaluation (hallucination, factuality, faithfulness, lying).
valueDescs.generation-quality: Open-ended response-quality / preference evaluation (NLG, summarization, translation, judges of quality).
valueDescs.general-methodology: General empirical-ML methodology not tied to one task (statistics, causal inference, reproducibility, measurement theory).

statuses.name: Aspect Gap
statuses.desc: How many of a tensor point's depth sub-questions stay unanswered: an authored gap (no papers at all), then 3/2/1 open, down to fully answered. Read off the authored aspect checklist; the worst (most-open) cell wins in aggregates.

statuses.name: Importance (recency + citations)
statuses.desc: A paper's recency + citation importance weight: freshest papers (and the mega-cited canon) read heaviest, older un-cited work lightest. Drives node size and the green->red emphasis ramp.

articles.tldr: Data contamination hinders fair LLM evaluation by introducing test data into newer models' training sets. Existing studies solve this challenge by updating benchmarks with newly collected data.
articles.contribution: AntiLeakBench guarantees contamination-freeness by constructing questions only from real-world knowledge introduced after each model's training cutoff, tying benchmark validity to the temporal ordering of knowledge vs. training data.

articles.title: When Benchmarks Age: Temporal Misalignment through Factuality Eval
articles.tldr: The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) and the real world has outpaced the static nature of widely used evaluation benchmarks, raising concerns about their reliability for evaluating LLM factuality.
articles.contribution: While substantial works continue to rely on the popular but old benchmarks, their temporal misalignment with real-world facts and modern LLMs, and their effects on LLM factuality evaluation remain underexplored. Therefore, in this work, we present a systematic investigation of this issue by examining five popular factuality benchmarks and eight LLMs released across different years.

articles.title: On Robustness and Reliability of Benchmark-Based Evaluation

articles.contribution: In this paper, we introduce a new task, Prompt Sensitivity Prediction, and a dataset PromptSET designed to investigate the effects of slight prompt variations on LLM performance. Using TriviaQA and HotpotQA datasets as the foundation of our work, we generate prompt variations and evaluate their effectiveness across multiple LLMs.

articles.title: Reality Check: A New Evaluation Ecosystem Is Necessary
articles.tldr: An ecosystem is needed to evaluate the real effects of AI (I->R).
articles.contribution: AI capability evaluations can capture detail about first-order effects, such as whether immediate system outputs are accurate, or contain toxic, biased or stereotypical content, but AI's second-order effects, i.e. any long-term outcomes and consequences that may result from AI use in the real world, have become a significant area of interest as the technology becomes embedded in our daily lives.

articles.title: The Hawthorne Effect in Reasoning Models: Evaluating and Steering Test Awareness
articles.tldr: Microsoft: reasoning models change behavior when they detect a test; steering test awareness.
articles.contribution: We present the first quantitative study of how such "test awareness" impacts model behavior, particularly its performance on safety-related tasks. We introduce a white-box probing framework that (i) linearly identifies awareness-related activations and (ii) steers models toward or away from test awareness while monitoring downstream performance.

articles.title: Self-Recognition in Language Models
articles.tldr: A rapidly growing number of applications rely on a small set of closed-source language models (LMs).
articles.contribution: This dependency might introduce novel security risks if LMs develop self-recognition capabilities. Inspired by human identity verification methods, we propose a novel approach for assessing self-recognition in LMs using model-generated "security questions".

articles.title: Reasons to Doubt the Impact of AI Risk Evaluations
articles.tldr: Berkeley: a direct critique of evals' impact on real risk (I->R).
articles.contribution: This paper questions the core value proposition of evaluations: that they significantly improve our understanding of AI risks and, consequently, our ability to mitigate those risks. Evaluations may fail to improve understanding in six ways, such as risks manifesting beyond the AI system or insignificant returns from evaluations compared to real-world observations.

articles.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
articles.tldr: Evaluating large language model (LLM) based chat assistants is challenging due to their broad capabilities and the inadequacy of existing benchmarks in measuring human preferences.
articles.contribution: To address this, we explore using strong LLMs as judges to evaluate these models on more open-ended questions. We examine the usage and limitations of LLM-as-a-judge, including position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases, as well as limited reasoning ability, and propose solutions to mitigate some of them.

articles.title: BadJudge: Backdoor Vulnerabilities of LLM-as-a-Judge
articles.tldr: This paper proposes a novel backdoor threat attacking the LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation regime, where the adversary controls both the candidate and evaluator model.
articles.contribution: The backdoored evaluator victimizes benign users by unfairly assigning inflated scores to adversary. A trivial single token backdoor poisoning 1% of the evaluator training data triples the adversary's score with respect to their legitimate score.

articles.title: Sycophancy to Subterfuge: Investigating Reward-Tampering
articles.tldr: In reinforcement learning, specification gaming occurs when AI systems learn undesired behaviors that are highly rewarded due to misspecified training goals.
articles.contribution: Specification gaming can range from simple behaviors like sycophancy to sophisticated and pernicious behaviors like reward-tampering, where a model directly modifies its own reward mechanism. However, these more pernicious behaviors may be too complex to be discovered via exploration.

articles.title: Play Favorites: Statistical Method to Measure Self-Bias
articles.tldr: Large language models (LLMs) can serve as judges that offer rapid and reliable assessments of other LLM outputs.
articles.contribution: However, models may systematically assign overly favorable ratings to their own outputs, a phenomenon known as self-bias, which can distort evaluations of true model performance. Previous studies often conflate genuine differences in model quality with bias or incorrectly assume that evaluations from LLMs and humans follow the same rating distributions.

articles.contribution: As benchmarks play an increasingly central role, they also grow more susceptible to distortion. Chatbot Arena has emerged as the go-to leaderboard for ranking the most capable AI systems.

articles.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform
articles.authors: Teun van der Weij et al.
articles.tldr: Trustworthy capability evaluations are crucial for ensuring the safety of AI systems, and are becoming a key component of AI regulation.
articles.contribution: However, the developers of an AI system, or the AI system itself, may have incentives for evaluations to understate the AI's actual capability. These conflicting interests lead to the problem of sandbagging, which we define as strategic underperformance on an evaluation.

articles.title: Universal Adversarial Attacks on Zero-shot LLM Assessment
articles.tldr: Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful zero-shot assessors used in real-world situations such as assessing written exams and benchmarking systems.
articles.contribution: Despite these critical applications, no existing work has analyzed the vulnerability of judge-LLMs to adversarial manipulation. This work presents the first study on the adversarial robustness of assessment LLMs, where we demonstrate that short universal adversarial phrases can be concatenated to deceive judge LLMs to predict inflated scores.

articles.title: Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals With Fewer Than a Few Hundred Datapoints
articles.tldr: Rigorous statistical evaluations of large language models (LLMs), including valid error bars and significance testing, are essential for meaningful and reliable performance assessment.
articles.contribution: Currently, when such statistical measures are reported, they typically rely on the Central Limit Theorem (CLT). In this position paper, we argue that while CLT-based methods for uncertainty quantification are appropriate when benchmarks consist of thousands of examples, they fail to provide adequate uncertainty estimates for LLM evaluations that rely on smaller, highly specialized benchmarks.

articles.title: Criterion Validity of LLM-as-Judge for Business Outcomes
articles.tldr: Multi-dimensional rubric-based dialogue evaluation is widely used to assess conversational AI, yet its criterion validity -- whether quality scores are associated with the downstream outcomes they are meant to serve -- remains largely untested.
articles.contribution: We address this gap through a two-phase study on a major Chinese matchmaking platform, testing a 7-dimension evaluation rubric (implemented via LLM-as-Judge) against verified business conversion. Our findings concern rubric design and weighting, not LLM scoring accuracy: any judge using the same rubric would face the same structural issue.

articles.title: From Lists to Emojis: How Format Bias Affects Alignment
articles.tldr: In this paper, we study format biases in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
articles.contribution: We observe that many widely-used preference models, including human evaluators, GPT-4, and top-ranking models on the RewardBench benchmark, exhibit strong biases towards specific format patterns, such as lists, links, bold text, and emojis. Furthermore, large language models (LLMs) can exploit these biases to achieve higher rankings on popular benchmarks like AlpacaEval and LMSYS Chatbot Arena.

articles.title: Quantifying Test Set Contamination on Generative Evaluations
articles.tldr: As frontier AI systems are pretrained on web-scale data, test set contamination has become a critical concern for accurately assessing their capabilities.
articles.contribution: While research has thoroughly investigated the impact of test set contamination on discriminative evaluations like multiple-choice question-answering, comparatively little research has studied the impact of test set contamination on generative evaluations. In this work, we quantitatively assess the effect of test set contamination on generative evaluations through the language model lifecycle.

articles.title: Lost in Benchmarks? Rethinking with IRT (PSN-IRT)
articles.tldr: The evaluation of large language models (LLMs) via benchmarks is widespread, yet inconsistencies between different leaderboards and poor separability among top models raise concerns about their ability to accurately reflect authentic model capabilities.

We first propose Pseudo-Siamese Network for Item Response Theory (PSN-IRT), an enhanced Item Response Theory framework that incorporates a rich set of item parameters within an IRT-grounded architecture.

articles.contribution: Demonstrates that swapping candidate order flips an LLM judge's verdict, isolating position as a confound that drives the score independent of response quality, and quantifies its prevalence across judges.

articles.title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
articles.authors: Peiyi Wang, Lei Li, Liang Chen, Zefan Cai et al.
articles.tldr: Shows LLM judges suffer strong positional bias in pairwise evaluation and proposes calibration (multiple-evidence and balanced position) to mitigate the resulting unfair verdicts.
articles.contribution: Proposes balanced-position calibration and multiple-evidence aggregation that reduce the variance and bias of the aggregated judge score, restoring more reliable pairwise rankings.

articles.title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
articles.authors: Arjun Panickssery, Samuel R. Bowman, Shi Feng
articles.tldr: Shows LLM judges can recognize their own outputs and that this self-recognition causally drives self-preference, a confound that inflates a model's score when it evaluates itself.
articles.contribution: Establishes a causal link between an LLM judge's ability to recognize its own generations and its self-preference, isolating self-recognition as a confound that biases self-evaluation scores upward.

articles.title: Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
articles.authors: Chujie Zheng, Hao Zhou, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Minlie Huang
articles.tldr: Shows multiple-choice benchmark scores are corrupted by models' selection bias toward specific option IDs (e.g., 'A'), a token-position artifact, and proposes debiasing that stabilizes the measured accuracy.
articles.contribution: Shows the multiple-choice format leaks a shortcut: models are biased toward particular option symbols regardless of content, so the operationalization measures option-position preference rather than knowledge.

articles.title: Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
articles.authors: Chujie Zheng, Hao Zhou, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Minlie Huang
articles.tldr: Shows multiple-choice benchmark scores are corrupted by models' selection bias toward specific option IDs (e.g., 'A'), a token-position artifact, and proposes debiasing that stabilizes the measured accuracy.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that permuting option order changes measured accuracy substantially and proposes a debiasing method (PriDe) that removes the prior, making the MCQ measurement more reliable.

articles.title: Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research (A Report from the NeurIPS 2019 Reproducibility Program)
articles.authors: Joelle Pineau, Philippe Vincent-Lamarre, Koustuv Sinha, Vincent Larivière et al.
articles.tldr: Reports the NeurIPS reproducibility program (code submission policy, ML reproducibility checklist, reproducibility challenge) and its measured effect on reporting practices in ML research.
articles.contribution: Introduces the ML reproducibility checklist and code-submission policy and measures their uptake, giving a concrete intervention to reduce under-reporting that causes irreproducible ML results.

articles.title: Humans or LLMs as the Judge? A Study on Judgement Bias
articles.authors: Guiming Hardy Chen, Shunian Chen, Ziche Liu, Feng Jiang, Benyou Wang
articles.tldr: Compares biases of human and LLM judges under a reference-free protocol, finding both exhibit systematic biases (e.g., authority, bandwagon, distraction) that threaten the validity of preference-based evaluation.
articles.contribution: Quantifies authority, bandwagon and distraction biases in LLM judges via injected cues, isolating confounds that shift verdicts away from response quality.

articles.title: Humans or LLMs as the Judge? A Study on Judgement Bias
articles.authors: Guiming Hardy Chen, Shunian Chen, Ziche Liu, Feng Jiang, Benyou Wang
articles.tldr: Compares biases of human and LLM judges under a reference-free protocol, finding both exhibit systematic biases (e.g., authority, bandwagon, distraction) that threaten the validity of preference-based evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows human judges share several of the same biases and disagree substantially, arguing human preference is not a clean gold standard for the target construct.

articles.title: Pretrained Transformers Improve Out-of-Distribution Robustness
articles.authors: Dan Hendrycks, Xiaoyuan Liu, Eric Wallace, Adam Dziedzic et al.
articles.tldr: Measures OOD generalization of NLP models across seven distribution-shift pairs and shows pretrained transformers are substantially more robust, formalizing how in-distribution accuracy overstates real-world performance.
articles.contribution: Constructs paired in-distribution/out-of-distribution NLP test sets and shows a large IID-vs-OOD accuracy gap, quantifying how held-out-set accuracy fails to predict out-of-distribution performance.

articles.title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
articles.authors: Miao Xiong, Zhiyuan Hu, Xinyang Lu, Yifei Li et al.
articles.tldr: Benchmarks methods for eliciting calibrated confidence from black-box LLMs and shows verbalized confidences are systematically overconfident and poorly calibrated, threatening any inference that reads model confidence as reliability.
articles.contribution: Systematically evaluates confidence-elicitation strategies and shows verbalized LLM confidences are miscalibrated and overconfident, so reported confidence is an unreliable measurement of correctness.

articles.title: JudgeLM: Fine-tuned Large Language Models are Scalable Judges
articles.authors: Lianghui Zhu, Xinggang Wang, Xinlong Wang
articles.tldr: Fine-tunes dedicated LLM judges at scale and identifies position, knowledge and format biases in the judging task, proposing swap augmentation and reference support to mitigate them.
articles.contribution: Names position, knowledge and format biases in the judging task and mitigates them with swap augmentation and reference/answer support, reducing confounds in the fine-tuned judge's verdicts.

articles.title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models
articles.authors: Katherine Tian, Eric Mitchell, Allan Zhou, Archit Sharma et al.
articles.tldr: Shows that verbalized confidence prompts yield better-calibrated confidence than conditional model probabilities for RLHF-tuned LLMs, giving a practical measurement of answer reliability.
articles.contribution: Finds verbalized-confidence elicitation is better calibrated than conditional token probabilities for RLHF models, giving a more reliable statistical instrument for reading model confidence.

articles.title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
articles.authors: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma et al.
articles.tldr: Introduces IFEval, a set of verifiable instructions whose satisfaction can be checked programmatically, removing subjective judge variance from instruction-following evaluation.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes instruction following as programmatically verifiable instructions (e.g., word counts, formats), replacing subjective judgement with a deterministic verifier so the measure matches the construct without judge bias.

articles.title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
articles.authors: Naman Jain, King Han, Alex Gu, Wen-Ding Li et al.
articles.tldr: Builds a continuously-updated code benchmark from problems released after model cutoffs to avoid contamination, and evaluates code beyond generation (self-repair, execution, prediction).
articles.contribution: Samples coding problems by release date after each model's training cutoff, using time-segmentation to build a contamination-free test set and showing prior code benchmarks were inflated by leakage.

articles.title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
articles.authors: Naman Jain, King Han, Alex Gu, Wen-Ding Li et al.
articles.tldr: Builds a continuously-updated code benchmark from problems released after model cutoffs to avoid contamination, and evaluates code beyond generation (self-repair, execution, prediction).
articles.contribution: Uses live, continuously-refreshed problems to track how measured code ability drifts as contamination accrues over time, making temporal validity of code benchmarks measurable.

articles.title: HaluEval: A Large-Scale Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.authors: Junyi Li, Xiaoxue Cheng, Wayne Xin Zhao, Jian-Yun Nie, Ji-Rong Wen
articles.tldr: Builds a large benchmark of hallucinated vs faithful samples and shows that LLMs struggle to identify hallucinations in text, quantifying a gap between fluent generation and factual reliability.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes 'hallucination' as a labeled construct via sampled-then-filtered hallucinated/faithful pairs, giving an explicit target that separates factuality from fluency in generation evaluation.

articles.title: HaluEval: A Large-Scale Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.authors: Junyi Li, Xiaoxue Cheng, Wayne Xin Zhao, Jian-Yun Nie, Ji-Rong Wen
articles.tldr: Builds a large benchmark of hallucinated vs faithful samples and shows that LLMs struggle to identify hallucinations in text, quantifying a gap between fluent generation and factual reliability.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM judges detect hallucinations unreliably (near-chance on hard cases), so using an LLM to score factuality is an unreliable measurement instrument for the honesty construct.

articles.title: News Summarization and Evaluation in the Era of GPT-3
articles.authors: Tanya Goyal, Junyi Jessy Li, Greg Durrett
articles.tldr: Shows reference-based summarization metrics and low-quality reference summaries systematically mis-rank GPT-3 zero-shot summaries, and that careful human evaluation reverses conclusions drawn from automatic metrics.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that noisy reference summaries and reference-based metrics penalize genuinely good GPT-3 summaries, so the ground-truth references misrepresent summary quality.

articles.title: News Summarization and Evaluation in the Era of GPT-3
articles.authors: Tanya Goyal, Junyi Jessy Li, Greg Durrett
articles.tldr: Shows reference-based summarization metrics and low-quality reference summaries systematically mis-rank GPT-3 zero-shot summaries, and that careful human evaluation reverses conclusions drawn from automatic metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows that only carefully-designed human evaluation (trained annotators, clear rubric) yields reliable rankings, whereas crowd ratings and automatic metrics disagree, changing which system wins.

articles.title: Large Language Models Are State-of-the-Art Evaluators of Translation Quality
articles.tldr: Introduces GEMBA, using GPT models to score machine-translation quality, and shows LLM scores correlate with human MQM judgements at the system level better than prior automatic metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows an LLM prompted to score translation quality (GEMBA) is a usable measurement instrument whose scores track the intended MT-quality construct better than surface-overlap metrics.

articles.title: Large Language Models Are State-of-the-Art Evaluators of Translation Quality
articles.tldr: Introduces GEMBA, using GPT models to score machine-translation quality, and shows LLM scores correlate with human MQM judgements at the system level better than prior automatic metrics.
articles.contribution: Provides validity evidence by correlating LLM scores with human MQM at the system level across languages, while noting the correlation weakens at the segment level, bounding where the instrument is trustworthy.

articles.title: Towards Understanding and Mitigating Social Biases in Language Models
articles.authors: Paul Pu Liang, Chiyu Wu, Louis-Philippe Morency, Ruslan Salakhutdinov
articles.tldr: Formalizes representational and allocational social biases in LM generation and proposes A-INLP, a projection-based mitigation, along with measurements that separate bias from task performance.
articles.contribution: Distinguishes representational from allocational bias and builds measurements for each, arguing single fairness scores conflate distinct bias constructs.

articles.title: Towards Understanding and Mitigating Social Biases in Language Models
articles.authors: Paul Pu Liang, Chiyu Wu, Louis-Philippe Morency, Ruslan Salakhutdinov
articles.tldr: Formalizes representational and allocational social biases in LM generation and proposes A-INLP, a projection-based mitigation, along with measurements that separate bias from task performance.
articles.contribution: Shows bias measurements are confounded with fluency/task quality and proposes mitigation that trades off bias against performance, warranting caution in inferring fairness from a bias score alone.

articles.title: A Critical Look at the Evaluation of GNNs Under Heterophily: Are We Really Making Progress?
articles.authors: Oleg Platonov, Denis Kuznedelev, Michael Diskin, Artem Babenko, Liudmila Prokhorenkova
articles.tldr: Shows the standard heterophilous graph benchmarks are flawed (duplicates, leakage, unreliable splits) and that under corrected evaluation the claimed advantage of specialized GNN architectures largely disappears.
articles.contribution: Exposes duplicate nodes, train/test leakage and unreliable splits in the standard heterophily datasets, so conclusions drawn on them do not generalize.

articles.title: A Critical Look at the Evaluation of GNNs Under Heterophily: Are We Really Making Progress?
articles.authors: Oleg Platonov, Denis Kuznedelev, Michael Diskin, Artem Babenko, Liudmila Prokhorenkova
articles.tldr: Shows the standard heterophilous graph benchmarks are flawed (duplicates, leakage, unreliable splits) and that under corrected evaluation the claimed advantage of specialized GNN architectures largely disappears.

articles.title: Prometheus: Inducing Fine-grained Evaluation Capability in Language Models
articles.authors: Seungone Kim, Jamin Shin, Yejin Cho, Joel Jang et al.
articles.tldr: Trains an open-source evaluator LM that scores responses against user-supplied fine-grained rubrics and shows it correlates with GPT-4 and human judgements, making rubric-conditioned evaluation reproducible.
articles.contribution: Conditions the judge on explicit fine-grained score rubrics, operationalizing 'quality' into named criteria so the measurement targets specified sub-constructs rather than an opaque global preference.

articles.title: Prometheus: Inducing Fine-grained Evaluation Capability in Language Models
articles.authors: Seungone Kim, Jamin Shin, Yejin Cho, Joel Jang et al.
articles.tldr: Trains an open-source evaluator LM that scores responses against user-supplied fine-grained rubrics and shows it correlates with GPT-4 and human judgements, making rubric-conditioned evaluation reproducible.
articles.contribution: Shows an open-weights evaluator can match proprietary-judge and human agreement, reducing reliance on a single closed judge and the reproducibility risk that entails.

articles.title: Replacing Judges with Juries: Evaluating LLM Generations with a Panel of Diverse Models
articles.authors: Pat Verga, Sebastian Hofstatter, Sophia Althammer, Yixuan Su et al.
articles.tldr: Shows that a Panel of LLM evaluators (PoLL) composed of several smaller models reduces intra-model self-preference bias and correlates better with human judgement than a single large judge, at lower cost.
articles.contribution: Aggregates verdicts from a diverse panel of judge models and shows this cancels each model's self-preference confound better than a single large judge.

articles.title: Replacing Judges with Juries: Evaluating LLM Generations with a Panel of Diverse Models
articles.authors: Pat Verga, Sebastian Hofstatter, Sophia Althammer, Yixuan Su et al.
articles.tldr: Shows that a Panel of LLM evaluators (PoLL) composed of several smaller models reduces intra-model self-preference bias and correlates better with human judgement than a single large judge, at lower cost.

articles.title: Autorubric: Unifying Rubric-based LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Open-source framework unifying rubric-based LLM-judge evaluation with ensemble judging, bias mitigation, calibration, and psychometric reliability metrics.
articles.contribution: Provides ensemble multi-judge grading with inter-judge agreement tracking, few-shot calibration, and psychometric reliability metrics to reduce single-judge variance in rubric scoring.

articles.title: Autorubric: Unifying Rubric-based LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Open-source framework unifying rubric-based LLM-judge evaluation with ensemble judging, bias mitigation, calibration, and psychometric reliability metrics.
articles.contribution: Decomposes rubrics into atomic per-criterion binary/ordinal/nominal judgments with mandatory per-verdict explanations to prevent criterion conflation and surface-proxy scoring.

articles.title: BenchBench: Benchmarking Automated Benchmark Generation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation pipeline that benchmarks LLMs as benchmark designers, measuring validity, discrimination, ranking stability, and self/family bias of generated suites.

articles.title: BenchBench: Benchmarking Automated Benchmark Generation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation pipeline that benchmarks LLMs as benchmark designers, measuring validity, discrimination, ranking stability, and self/family bias of generated suites.
articles.contribution: Quantifies item invalidity via a non-core rate using objective exact/numeric/symbolic verifiers, showing invalidity is negatively associated with discrimination (r about -0.62).

articles.title: BenchBench: Benchmarking Automated Benchmark Generation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation pipeline that benchmarks LLMs as benchmark designers, measuring validity, discrimination, ranking stability, and self/family bias of generated suites.
articles.contribution: Audits self/family bias in the designer-answerer matrix, showing family effects are measurable but modest and not uniformly own-family favorable.

articles.title: TruthTensor: Evaluating LLMs through Human Imitation on Prediction Market under Drift and Holistic Reasoning
articles.tldr: Contamination-free live-prediction-market evaluation paradigm scoring LLMs on calibration, drift, and reproducibility rather than static accuracy.
articles.contribution: Eliminates train/test contamination by construction, evaluating only forward-looking market events whose outcomes are unknown at prediction time, reinforced by cryptographically hashed instruction locking.

articles.title: TruthTensor: Evaluating LLMs through Human Imitation on Prediction Market under Drift and Holistic Reasoning
articles.tldr: Contamination-free live-prediction-market evaluation paradigm scoring LLMs on calibration, drift, and reproducibility rather than static accuracy.
articles.contribution: Centers evaluation on narrative/temporal/confidence drift metrics, showing models with similar forecast accuracy diverge markedly in calibration and drift over time.

articles.title: TruthTensor: Evaluating LLMs through Human Imitation on Prediction Market under Drift and Holistic Reasoning
articles.tldr: Contamination-free live-prediction-market evaluation paradigm scoring LLMs on calibration, drift, and reproducibility rather than static accuracy.

articles.title: Assessment Design in the AI Era: A Method for Identifying Items Functioning Differentially for Humans and Chatbots
articles.tldr: Applies Differential Item Functioning plus negative-control and item-total-correlation analysis to find assessment items functioning differently for humans versus chatbots.
articles.contribution: Adapts logistic-regression DIF (humans as reference, chatbots as focal group) to flag items where equal ability yields systematically different correctness, characterizing where LLM and human capabilities diverge.

articles.title: Assessment Design in the AI Era: A Method for Identifying Items Functioning Differentially for Humans and Chatbots
articles.tldr: Applies Differential Item Functioning plus negative-control and item-total-correlation analysis to find assessment items functioning differently for humans versus chatbots.
articles.contribution: Adds a placebo/negative-control step and item-total-correlation filtering to control DIF false positives and establish statistical reliability of flagged items.

articles.title: Improving deep neural network generalization and robustness to background bias via layer-wise relevance propagation optimization
articles.tldr: Optimizes Layer-wise Relevance Propagation heatmaps (ISNet) to suppress background/spurious features so classifiers stop shortcut learning and generalize out-of-distribution.
articles.contribution: Shows background/spurious features (Clever-Hans effect) confound classifier decisions and inflate i.i.d. accuracy, and that penalizing LRP relevance outside the object suppresses this confound.

articles.title: Improving deep neural network generalization and robustness to background bias via layer-wise relevance propagation optimization
articles.tldr: Optimizes Layer-wise Relevance Propagation heatmaps (ISNet) to suppress background/spurious features so classifiers stop shortcut learning and generalize out-of-distribution.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that i.i.d. test sets sharing background bias overstate real performance, so external OOD databases are needed; ISNet's OOD generalization surpassed eight benchmark DNNs.

articles.title: Enhancing Trust in LLMs: Algorithms for Comparing and Interpreting LLMs
articles.tldr: Survey cataloging LLM evaluation metrics and techniques to enhance trustworthiness assessment, noting the construct limitations of surface metrics.
articles.contribution: Surveys measurement instruments and their construct limitations (perplexity captures fluency not semantics; BLEU/ROUGE are surface n-gram proxies), motivating stratified evaluation and human evaluation for nuance.

articles.title: The Vulnerability of Language Model Benchmarks: Do They Accurately Reflect True LLM Performance?
articles.tldr: Systematic review of how LLM benchmarks are hacked via contamination, task-specific gaming, and biased human/LLM judges, undermining leaderboard validity.
articles.contribution: Catalogs test-set contamination/leakage mechanisms (public dataset overlap, memorization) and detection strategies including contamination audits, the exposure metric, provenance tracking, and hidden test sets.

articles.title: The Vulnerability of Language Model Benchmarks: Do They Accurately Reflect True LLM Performance?
articles.tldr: Systematic review of how LLM benchmarks are hacked via contamination, task-specific gaming, and biased human/LLM judges, undermining leaderboard validity.
articles.contribution: Frames benchmark overfitting as Goodhart's law (B=P+eps, max(B) not equal max(P)) and documents task-specific optimization exploiting dataset artifacts rather than genuine understanding.

articles.title: The Vulnerability of Language Model Benchmarks: Do They Accurately Reflect True LLM Performance?
articles.tldr: Systematic review of how LLM benchmarks are hacked via contamination, task-specific gaming, and biased human/LLM judges, undermining leaderboard validity.

articles.title: The Vulnerability of Language Model Benchmarks: Do They Accurately Reflect True LLM Performance?

articles.title: Stop Evaluating AI with Human Tests, Develop Principled, AI-specific Tests instead

articles.title: Addressing Pitfalls in the Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation Methods for Natural Language Generation

articles.tldr: Proposes a disjoint train/validation/test splitting algorithm for hyperspectral image classification to eliminate data leakage that inflates accuracy.

articles.tldr: Psychometric latent-trait audit of frontier LLMs detects durable provider-level 'lab signatures' (sycophancy, moderation), using decoy masking to defeat evaluation awareness.
articles.contribution: Uses Thurstonian-IRT forced-choice latent-trait estimation plus MixedLM/ICC variance decomposition to separate the lab signal from item framing without ground-truth labels.

articles.title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
articles.tldr: CLExEval uses progressive information masking plus 5,600 expert annotations to expose an 'evaluation illusion' where fluent clinical reasoning masks wrong diagnoses and fools LLM judges.
articles.contribution: Defines Hallucination Approval Rate; standalone judges approve 47.9-100% of human-verified clinical failures even when given the gold diagnosis, with a +0.096 self-preference bias.

articles.title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
articles.tldr: CLExEval uses progressive information masking plus 5,600 expert annotations to expose an 'evaluation illusion' where fluent clinical reasoning masks wrong diagnoses and fools LLM judges.
articles.contribution: Shows Communication-vs-Diagnostic-Precision correlation is only rho=0.482, so surface fluency is an unreliable proxy for medical correctness (the evaluation illusion).

articles.title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
articles.tldr: CLExEval uses progressive information masking plus 5,600 expert annotations to expose an 'evaluation illusion' where fluent clinical reasoning masks wrong diagnoses and fools LLM judges.
articles.contribution: Progressive masking reveals verbosity bias (GPT-4o-mini accuracy 95% to 32.5%, ISS 62.5pp) and 68.6% reasoning-to-output mismatch, isolating shortcut cues from robust reasoning.

articles.title: Testing the Testers: Human-Driven Quality Assessment of Voice AI Testing Platforms
articles.tldr: First human-centered framework to meta-evaluate voice-AI testing platforms on both simulation realism and evaluation accuracy against human ground truth.
articles.contribution: 'Evaluates the evaluators': measures how accurately testing platforms match human consensus (top F1 0.92 vs 0.73) using 21,600 human judgments with bootstrap CIs and permutation tests.

articles.title: Testing the Testers: Human-Driven Quality Assessment of Voice AI Testing Platforms
articles.tldr: First human-centered framework to meta-evaluate voice-AI testing platforms on both simulation realism and evaluation accuracy against human ground truth.
articles.contribution: Separately scores simulation quality (whether generated test conversations are realistic and representative) via pairwise human comparisons yielding Elo/league rankings (61.0 vs 43-49).

articles.title: Does Capability Transfer to Subjective Behavior -- and Would Our Instruments Tell Us? A Self-Evolving, Trust-by-Construction Evaluation Paradigm
articles.tldr: Builds a self-evolving, trust-by-construction LLM-judge instrument for subjective emotional-support behavior, revealing that objective-benchmark capability does not transfer uniformly to subjective axes.
articles.contribution: Trust-by-construction: three certificates (reliability, cross-instrument replication, historical-footprint calibration) substitute for a saturated human gold standard (rho approx 0.45).

articles.title: Does Capability Transfer to Subjective Behavior -- and Would Our Instruments Tell Us? A Self-Evolving, Trust-by-Construction Evaluation Paradigm

articles.contribution: Shows within-judge replication noise is statistically independent of cross-judge noise, justifying ensembling different judge families over re-running one, and isolates a judge-competence floor.

articles.title: Does Capability Transfer to Subjective Behavior -- and Would Our Instruments Tell Us? A Self-Evolving, Trust-by-Construction Evaluation Paradigm
articles.tldr: Builds a self-evolving, trust-by-construction LLM-judge instrument for subjective emotional-support behavior, revealing that objective-benchmark capability does not transfer uniformly to subjective axes.
articles.contribution: A multiplicative anti-gaming fitness (discrimination x reliability x OOS x orthogonality) blocks dropping a discriminative dimension to inflate orthogonality; the aggregate hid a sharp advice_restraint regression.

articles.title: Efficient multi-prompt evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: PromptEval uses Item Response Theory to estimate an LLM's full performance distribution across 100+ prompt templates under a budget of about two single-prompt evaluations.
articles.contribution: Estimates performance quantiles across many prompt templates to build robust metrics (median, 95% quantile), directly addressing single-prompt leaderboard non-reproducibility.

articles.title: Efficient multi-prompt evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: PromptEval uses Item Response Theory to estimate an LLM's full performance distribution across 100+ prompt templates under a budget of about two single-prompt evaluations.
articles.contribution: Extends pIRT/Rasch models to borrow strength across prompts and examples, with proven consistency in estimating the performance distribution and its quantiles.

articles.title: ConStat: Performance-Based Contamination Detection in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Redefines data contamination as artificially inflated, non-generalizing benchmark performance and proposes ConStat, a statistical test that detects and quantifies it by comparing primary vs reference benchmarks relative to reference models.
articles.contribution: ConStat detects and quantifies contamination as non-generalizing inflated performance by contrasting a primary benchmark against rephrased/synthetic/parallel reference benchmarks relative to a pool of reference models, escaping the evasion problem of n-gram/membership detectors.

articles.title: SimpleQA Verified: A Reliable Factuality Benchmark to Measure Parametric Knowledge
articles.tldr: Rebuilds OpenAI's SimpleQA into a cleaner 1,000-prompt parametric-factuality benchmark by removing noisy/incorrect labels, topical bias and redundancy, and improves the LLM autorater for more robust grading.
articles.contribution: Multi-stage curation (unique source URLs, Gemini-embedding cos>0.77 and TF-IDF>0.4 de-duplication, topic/answer-type rebalancing, publisher-choice filtering) removes convenience-sampling artifacts so the factuality set is more representative and diverse.

articles.title: SimpleQA Verified: A Reliable Factuality Benchmark to Measure Parametric Knowledge
articles.tldr: Rebuilds OpenAI's SimpleQA into a cleaner 1,000-prompt parametric-factuality benchmark by removing noisy/incorrect labels, topical bias and redundancy, and improves the LLM autorater for more robust grading.
articles.contribution: Reconciles conflicting sources with search-augmented models and code-execution numeric checks to correct incorrect/ambiguous ground-truth labels, raising label fidelity of the measured factuality construct.

articles.title: SimpleQA Verified: A Reliable Factuality Benchmark to Measure Parametric Knowledge
articles.tldr: Rebuilds OpenAI's SimpleQA into a cleaner 1,000-prompt parametric-factuality benchmark by removing noisy/incorrect labels, topical bias and redundancy, and improves the LLM autorater for more robust grading.
articles.contribution: Improves the prompted autorater by encoding per-question numeric acceptable ranges and clarified hedging/commit rules, reducing grader disagreement on approximate-numeric and hedged answers.

articles.title: An Empirical Analysis of Uncertainty in Large Language Model Evaluations
articles.tldr: Empirically characterizes uncertainty/instability of LLM-as-a-Judge across 9 evaluators, shows prompting and uncertainty-aware fine-tuning reduce it, and builds ConfiLM to improve OOD evaluation.
articles.contribution: Quantifies LLM-evaluator instability via token-probability confidence across single-answer vs pairwise settings, showing single-answer grading is markedly less confident/stable and that evaluation confidence is highly sensitive to data-distribution shift.

articles.title: An Empirical Analysis of Uncertainty in Large Language Model Evaluations
articles.tldr: Empirically characterizes uncertainty/instability of LLM-as-a-Judge across 9 evaluators, shows prompting and uncertainty-aware fine-tuning reduce it, and builds ConfiLM to improve OOD evaluation.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates same-model-family self-preference bias inflating both scores and confidence, and shows CoT prompting can partially alleviate this self-preference and increase fine-grained discrimination.

articles.title: Towards Reliable Generative AI-Driven Scaffolding: Reducing Hallucinations and Enhancing Quality in Self-Regulated Learning Support
articles.tldr: Evaluates the reliability and quality of LLM-generated self-regulated-learning scaffolds using a multi-agent reliability approach and LLM-as-a-Judge, and is first to empirically test LLM-as-a-Judge biases on educational feedback.
articles.contribution: A multi-agent reliability-evaluation approach assessing whether LLM-generated scaffolds target the intended SRL processes achieves near-perfect alignment with human experts, outperforming single-agent LLM and ML baselines as a pre-screening scorer.

articles.title: Towards Reliable Generative AI-Driven Scaffolding: Reducing Hallucinations and Enhancing Quality in Self-Regulated Learning Support
articles.tldr: Evaluates the reliability and quality of LLM-generated self-regulated-learning scaffolds using a multi-agent reliability approach and LLM-as-a-Judge, and is first to empirically test LLM-as-a-Judge biases on educational feedback.
articles.contribution: Empirically identifies position bias, self-enhancement bias, sequential-API-call bias and verbosity bias in the LLM-as-a-Judge quality evaluation of educational feedback and discusses mitigations.

articles.title: VALOR-EVAL: Holistic Coverage and Faithfulness Evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces VALOR-Bench (object/attribute/relation hallucination with associative-bias image selection) and VALOR-Eval, a two-stage LLM metric generalizing CHAIR that scores both faithfulness and coverage of LVLM captions.
articles.contribution: VALOR-Eval adds open-vocabulary LLM semantic matching to CHAIR and jointly measures faithfulness and coverage, correcting CHAIR's precision-only bias that favored precise-but-uninformative captions.

articles.title: VALOR-EVAL: Holistic Coverage and Faithfulness Evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces VALOR-Bench (object/attribute/relation hallucination with associative-bias image selection) and VALOR-Eval, a two-stage LLM metric generalizing CHAIR that scores both faithfulness and coverage of LVLM captions.
articles.contribution: Selects challenging images by exploiting GQA co-occurrence/associative-bias statistics (frequency and conditional probability) so the benchmark deliberately exposes hallucinations that convenience-sampled images miss.

articles.title: Benchmarking LLMs for Unit Test Generation from Real-World Functions
articles.tldr: Builds ULT, a decontaminated function-level unit-test-generation benchmark of 3,909 high-complexity real-world Python functions, plus a leaked pair (PLT) to isolate memorization vs reasoning.
articles.contribution: A multi-stage curation decontaminates test-case data and pairs ULT with a deliberately leaked PLT twin, enabling controlled measurement of how much test-generation performance is memorization vs reasoning.

articles.title: Benchmarking LLMs for Unit Test Generation from Real-World Functions
articles.tldr: Builds ULT, a decontaminated function-level unit-test-generation benchmark of 3,909 high-complexity real-world Python functions, plus a leaked pair (PLT) to isolate memorization vs reasoning.
articles.contribution: Filters for high cyclomatic complexity so tasks are not structurally trivial toy programs, making the benchmark measure genuine, generalizable test-generation ability rather than surface pattern recall.

articles.title: DynaCode: A Dynamic Complexity-Aware Code Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Code Generation
articles.tldr: Presents DynaCode, a dynamic complexity-aware code benchmark generating up to 189M nested problems via cyclomatic-complexity units and 16 call-graph structures to mitigate memorization and control difficulty.
articles.contribution: Dynamically composes nested code problems from freshly sourced units so test cases are not memorizable, and empirically shows fine-tuning gains transfer far less to DynaCode than to the static MBPP+, evidencing reduced memorization.

articles.title: DynaCode: A Dynamic Complexity-Aware Code Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Code Generation
articles.tldr: Presents DynaCode, a dynamic complexity-aware code benchmark generating up to 189M nested problems via cyclomatic-complexity units and 16 call-graph structures to mitigate memorization and control difficulty.
articles.contribution: A two-dimensional complexity-aware metric combining cyclomatic complexity units with call-graph complexity levels operationalizes graded difficulty, differentiating models beyond isolated-function benchmarks.

articles.title: Skewed Score: A statistical framework to assess autograders
articles.tldr: Proposes a Bayesian generalised-linear-model framework that jointly evaluates LLMs and assesses autograder behaviour, quantifying grader biases and uncertainty within one model.
articles.contribution: Bayesian ordered-logistic/binomial GLMs model scores as functions of grader and item covariates, augmenting inter-rater agreement (e.g., Krippendorff's alpha) with posterior uncertainty and separating disagreement due to noise from systematic bias.

articles.title: Skewed Score: A statistical framework to assess autograders
articles.tldr: Proposes a Bayesian generalised-linear-model framework that jointly evaluates LLMs and assesses autograder behaviour, quantifying grader biases and uncertainty within one model.
articles.contribution: Explicitly quantifies autograder self-bias via grader-LLM interaction terms and length bias via token-length-difference slopes, and captures intransitive pairwise preferences that Bradley-Terry models cannot.

articles.title: Principles from Clinical Research for NLP Model Generalization
articles.tldr: Imports clinical-research validity principles into NLP, arguing internal validity (freedom from spurious correlations) must precede external validity and that 'out-of-distribution' is an insufficient explanation for generalization failure.
articles.contribution: Uses interpretable surrogate models (Naive Bayes and NB+decision-tree with hand-crafted distance/surface features) to demonstrate that a BioBERT relation-extractor relies on spurious surface patterns, breaking internal validity and causing generalization failure.

articles.title: Principles from Clinical Research for NLP Model Generalization
articles.tldr: Imports clinical-research validity principles into NLP, arguing internal validity (freedom from spurious correlations) must precede external validity and that 'out-of-distribution' is an insufficient explanation for generalization failure.
articles.contribution: Adapts clinical population-definition and RCT-style matching/contrast-set evaluation to NLP, proposing that generalization claims require defined population boundaries and that matched-pair scoring exposes shortcut reliance.

articles.title: Latency-Response Theory Model: Evaluating Large Language Models via Response Accuracy and Chain-of-Thought Length
articles.tldr: LaRT extends item response theory by jointly modeling response accuracy and chain-of-thought length via correlated latent ability and speed, improving the statistical validity of LLM ranking.
articles.contribution: Joint accuracy+CoT-length latent model whose asymptotic estimation precision of ability exceeds standalone IRT whenever ability and speed correlate.

articles.title: Latency-Response Theory Model: Evaluating Large Language Models via Response Accuracy and Chain-of-Thought Length
articles.tldr: LaRT extends item response theory by jointly modeling response accuracy and chain-of-thought length via correlated latent ability and speed, improving the statistical validity of LLM ranking.

articles.title: When Benchmarks Lie: Evaluating Malicious Prompt Classifiers Under True Distribution Shift
articles.tldr: Leave-One-Dataset-Out evaluation exposes that same-source train/test splits inflate prompt-attack classifier AUC by ~8.4pp, and 28% of top SAE features are dataset-provenance shortcuts rather than attack semantics.
articles.contribution: Introduces LODO protocol showing standard CV/held-out splits overestimate true OOD AUC by 8.4pp (0.996 vs 0.912) with per-dataset gaps of 1.2-25.4%.

articles.title: When Benchmarks Lie: Evaluating Malicious Prompt Classifiers Under True Distribution Shift
articles.tldr: Leave-One-Dataset-Out evaluation exposes that same-source train/test splits inflate prompt-attack classifier AUC by ~8.4pp, and 28% of top SAE features are dataset-provenance shortcuts rather than attack semantics.

articles.title: Measure what Matters: Psychometric Evaluation of AI with Situational Judgment Tests
articles.tldr: Scenario-based situational-judgment-test psychometrics with multidimensional IRT provides more reliable, construct-valid measurement of LLM behavioral traits than classical self-report inventories.
articles.contribution: Shows SJT-derived trait scores predict external behavioral benchmarks better than self-report HEXACO (e.g. Agreeableness-EmoBench 0.70 vs 0.51), capturing constructs self-report misses.

articles.title: Measure what Matters: Psychometric Evaluation of AI with Situational Judgment Tests
articles.tldr: Scenario-based situational-judgment-test psychometrics with multidimensional IRT provides more reliable, construct-valid measurement of LLM behavioral traits than classical self-report inventories.

articles.title: MM-OPERA: Benchmarking Open-ended Association Reasoning for Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: Open-ended multimodal association-reasoning benchmark whose LLM-as-judge scoring (dual-judge plus process-reward) is validated for reliability, human alignment, and resistance to verbosity/position bias.
articles.contribution: Validates a dual-judge (GPT-4o + DeepSeek-V3) process-reward scoring scheme, mitigating self-enhancement bias and confirming negligible position bias and minimal verbosity bias.

articles.title: MM-OPERA: Benchmarking Open-ended Association Reasoning for Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: Open-ended multimodal association-reasoning benchmark whose LLM-as-judge scoring (dual-judge plus process-reward) is validated for reliability, human alignment, and resistance to verbosity/position bias.

articles.title: Judging the Judges: A Systematic Evaluation of Bias Mitigation Strategies in LLM-as-a-Judge Pipelines
articles.tldr: Systematic comparison of nine debiasing strategies across five LLM judges finds style bias dominates (0.10-0.76) while position bias is now negligible, with statistically significant debiasing gains for several models.
articles.contribution: Mixed-effects logistic regression with Holm-Bonferroni finds style bias dominant (0.10-0.76), position negligible (<=0.04), and Claude S8 (+11.5pp) and Flash S8 (+7.5pp) significant debiasing.

articles.title: Judging the Judges: A Systematic Evaluation of Bias Mitigation Strategies in LLM-as-a-Judge Pipelines

articles.title: Quantifying Label-Induced Bias in Large Language Model Self- and Cross-Evaluations

articles.title: Heaven-Sent or Hell-Bent? Benchmarking the Intelligence and Defectiveness of LLM Hallucinations
articles.tldr: HIC-Bench reconceptualizes hallucination measurement by distinguishing intelligent from defective hallucinations using TTCT creativity metrics and a composite Intelligent-Fidelity Score, judged by averaged LLM judges with human verification.
articles.contribution: Defines Intelligent vs Defective Hallucination constructs and an Intelligent-Fidelity Score grounded in TTCT, arguing factual-consistency-only hallucination metrics misrepresent epistemically valuable content.

articles.title: MUSE: Benchmarking Manufacturable, Functional, and Assemblable Text-to-CAD Generation

articles.contribution: Argues geometric-similarity metrics (Chamfer Distance) measure visual resemblance not design validity, and defines functionality/manufacturability/assemblability constructs via structured design specifications.

articles.title: MUSE: Benchmarking Manufacturable, Functional, and Assemblable Text-to-CAD Generation

articles.title: Understanding LLM Evaluator Behavior: A Structured Multi-Evaluator Framework for Merchant Risk Assessment

articles.contribution: Consensus-deviation metric that excludes the focal judge (proven zero-sum, derivative=1) removes circularity and measures both positive and negative LLM-judge self-evaluation bias.

articles.title: PhyGround: Benchmarking Physical Reasoning in Generative World Models
articles.tldr: Criteria-grounded physics benchmark for video generation that decomposes physical adherence into 13 per-law sub-questions, uses a social-science-grounded human protocol for annotation reliability, and releases an open VLM judge with far lower bias than a closed frontier judge.
articles.contribution: Releases PhyJudge-9B, an open physics-specialized VLM judge whose aggregate relative bias is 3.3% versus 16.6% for closed Gemini-3.1-Pro, making automated scoring auditable and reproducible.

articles.title: PhyGround: Benchmarking Physical Reasoning in Generative World Models

articles.title: PhyGround: Benchmarking Physical Reasoning in Generative World Models
articles.tldr: Criteria-grounded physics benchmark for video generation that decomposes physical adherence into 13 per-law sub-questions, uses a social-science-grounded human protocol for annotation reliability, and releases an open VLM judge with far lower bias than a closed frontier judge.

articles.title: VISTA: Verification In Sequential Turn-based Assessment
articles.tldr: VISTA reframes dialogue hallucination detection as sequential claim-level verification, decomposing turns into atomic claims verified against sources and dialogue history, beating FActScore and LLM-as-Judge and improving human annotator agreement.
articles.contribution: Structured multi-stage claim-verification pipeline substantially improves hallucination-detection accuracy over monolithic FActScore and single-pass LLM-as-Judge baselines, especially for smaller open-weight models.

articles.title: VISTA: Verification In Sequential Turn-based Assessment

articles.title: Conformal P-Value in Multiple-Choice Question Answering Tasks with Provable Risk Control

articles.title: ArenaBencher: Automatic Benchmark Evolution via Multi-Model Competitive Evaluation

articles.contribution: Iteratively regenerates ability-preserving test cases so benchmarks stay contamination-resilient against pretraining-corpus leakage while remaining comparable over time.

articles.title: ArenaBencher: Automatic Benchmark Evolution via Multi-Model Competitive Evaluation

articles.title: Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs
articles.tldr: The Open Graph Benchmark supplies large realistic graph datasets with domain-specific splits, standardized evaluators, and reproducible protocols, arguing that prior small datasets and random splits give inflated, non-reproducible, poorly-generalizing results.

articles.title: HalluLens: LLM Hallucination Benchmark

articles.contribution: Proposes a taxonomy that separates hallucination (inconsistency with model training data / input context) from factuality (needing an external oracle), fixing conflated construct definitions across surveys.

articles.title: HalluLens: LLM Hallucination Benchmark

articles.title: TofuEval: Evaluating Hallucinations of LLMs on Topic-Focused Dialogue Summarization

articles.title: Evaluating Cognitive Maps and Planning in Large Language Models with CogEval
articles.tldr: CogEval is a cognitive-science-inspired protocol (multiple tasks, control conditions, iterations, statistics) that debunks emergent planning in LLMs using construct-grounded tasks absent from training sets.
articles.contribution: Imports established cognitive-science construct validity for planning by basing task prompts on human experiments with prior construct grounding rather than anecdotes.

articles.tldr: CogEval is a cognitive-science-inspired protocol (multiple tasks, control conditions, iterations, statistics) that debunks emergent planning in LLMs using construct-grounded tasks absent from training sets.
articles.contribution: Uses tasks deliberately absent from LLM training sets plus control conditions to rule out training-set contamination when testing claimed emergent planning abilities.

articles.title: Evaluating Cognitive Maps and Planning in Large Language Models with CogEval
articles.tldr: CogEval is a cognitive-science-inspired protocol (multiple tasks, control conditions, iterations, statistics) that debunks emergent planning in LLMs using construct-grounded tasks absent from training sets.
articles.contribution: Applies repeated iterations and a logistic-regression repeated-measures analysis with control conditions to give statistically robust capability claims rather than single-run anecdotes.

articles.title: Quantifying Contamination in Evaluating Code Generation Capabilities of Language Models
articles.tldr: Precisely quantifies overlap between code-generation benchmarks (MBPP, HumanEval) and open pretraining corpora, showing contamination inflates measured code capability.
articles.contribution: Substring-level Levenshtein + Dolos AST matching pipeline quantifies that up to 20.8% of MBPP and 18.9% of HumanEval gold solutions are already seen in the Pile/Stack.

articles.title: Quantifying Social Biases Using Templates is Unreliable
articles.tldr: Shows template-based social-bias measurements are brittle: semantically-preserving edits to the templates swing bias values and flip conclusions across four NLP tasks.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that manually paraphrasing bias-eval templates in a meaning-preserving way changes task-specific bias measures by 81% (NLI) up to 162% (MLM), making the simplistic template operationalization an unreliable proxy for the bias construct.

articles.title: CalibraEval: Calibrating Prediction Distribution to Mitigate Selection Bias in LLMs-as-Judges
articles.tldr: Introduces CalibraEval, a label-free calibration of an LLM judge's prediction distribution to mitigate selection (position/ID-token) bias in pairwise evaluation.
articles.contribution: Reformulates judge debiasing as an optimization aligning the observed prediction distribution to an unbiased one via a non-parametric order-preserving algorithm (NOA), removing position/token selection bias without labels.

articles.title: A comprehensive taxonomy of hallucinations in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: A comprehensive taxonomy and formal framework of LLM hallucinations, arguing hallucination is theoretically inevitable and clarifying the honesty constructs measured by evaluations.
articles.contribution: Provides a formal definition and theoretical framework for hallucination and disentangles the underlying constructs: intrinsic vs extrinsic and factuality (absolute correctness) vs faithfulness (adherence to input), grounding what hallucination evaluations should measure.

articles.title: Pairwise or Pointwise? Evaluating Feedback Protocols for Bias in LLM-Based Evaluation
articles.tldr: Shows the LLM-judge feedback protocol (absolute scoring vs pairwise preference) materially changes evaluation reliability, with pairwise far more vulnerable to spurious distractor features.
articles.contribution: Establishes that the choice of feedback protocol (absolute scores vs relative preferences) systematically changes judge reliability, with absolute scoring producing judgments that better reflect true response quality.

articles.title: Pairwise or Pointwise? Evaluating Feedback Protocols for Bias in LLM-Based Evaluation
articles.tldr: Shows the LLM-judge feedback protocol (absolute scoring vs pairwise preference) materially changes evaluation reliability, with pairwise far more vulnerable to spurious distractor features.
articles.contribution: Shows generator models can embed spurious distractor features favored by the judge to inflate lower-quality outputs, flipping pairwise preferences in ~35% of cases versus only 9% for absolute scoring.

articles.title: ModeLing: A Novel Dataset for Testing Linguistic Reasoning in Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces modeLing, a contamination-resistant benchmark of newly-written low-resource Rosetta-stone linguistics puzzles for evaluating multilingual few-shot reasoning without data leakage.
articles.contribution: Designs an evaluation using extremely low-resource languages and entirely newly-written puzzles to avoid leakage, and empirically verifies contamination is absent by showing 0% accuracy when models are given no example pairs.

articles.title: Adaptive Testing for LLM Evaluation: A Psychometric Alternative to Static Benchmarks
articles.tldr: Proposes ATLAS, an IRT-based computerized adaptive testing framework that estimates LLM ability with 90% fewer items while adding psychometric validity checks static benchmarks lack.
articles.contribution: Uses 3PL IRT with Fisher-information-guided adaptive item selection and precision-based stopping to estimate model ability with up to 90% fewer items (e.g. 41 items, 0.157 MAE on HellaSwag) while reporting M2/RMSEA model-fit diagnostics that prior IRT-reduction methods omit.

articles.title: Our Evaluation Metric Needs an Update to Encourage Generalization
articles.tldr: Proposes the WOOD Score, an evaluation metric that reweights samples by their out-of-distribution hardness to counter benchmark-score inflation from spurious biases and dataset hacking.
articles.contribution: Introduces WOOD Score, weighting each test sample in proportion to its OOD hardness (via train-test semantic textual similarity) so that leaderboard accuracy no longer rewards models that exploit spurious biases and fail to generalize.

articles.title: Beyond Consensus: Mitigating the Agreeableness Bias in LLM Judge Evaluations
articles.tldr: Quantifies an 'agreeableness bias' in LLM-as-judge (high TPR, very low TNR) and corrects it with a minority-veto ensemble and a regression that models each validator's reliability.
articles.contribution: Empirically quantifies validator agreeableness bias across 14 LLM judges on 366 buggy programs: True Positive Rate exceeds 96% but True Negative Rate stays below 25%, so invalid feedback is rarely rejected and precision is systematically overestimated.

articles.title: Beyond Consensus: Mitigating the Agreeableness Bias in LLM Judge Evaluations
articles.tldr: Quantifies an 'agreeableness bias' in LLM-as-judge (high TPR, very low TNR) and corrects it with a minority-veto ensemble and a regression that models each validator's reliability.

articles.title: The Stanford Acuity Test: A Precise Vision Test Using Bayesian Techniques and a Discovery in Human Visual Response

articles.contribution: Builds a Bayesian adaptive acuity exam that models a calibrated posterior over the ability parameter, incorporates a slip term and priors, and uses posterior-sampling item selection to cut measurement error 74% vs chart exams and up to 67% vs the prior best digital test.

articles.title: RubricBench: Aligning Model-Generated Rubrics with Human Standards

articles.title: EffiEval: Efficient and Generalizable Model Evaluation via Capability Coverage Maximization

articles.title: Debunk the Myth of SFT Generalization

articles.title: TTA-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Text-to-Audio Models

articles.tldr: TTA-Bench broadens text-to-audio evaluation beyond perceptual quality to reliability, robustness, fairness and toxicity, cross-checking objective metrics against 118K expert and non-expert human annotations.

articles.tldr: AURA shows audio-visual models reach high answer accuracy through flawed reasoning, and introduces AuraScore to separately measure factual grounding and logical inference of the reasoning trace.

articles.title: AURA: A Fine-Grained Benchmark and Decomposed Metric for Audio-Visual Reasoning
articles.tldr: AURA shows audio-visual models reach high answer accuracy through flawed reasoning, and introduces AuraScore to separately measure factual grounding and logical inference of the reasoning trace.

articles.title: Quantifying and Mitigating Socially Desirable Responding in LLMs: A Desirability-Matched Graded Forced-Choice Psychometric Study
articles.tldr: Quantifies and mitigates socially desirable responding (SDR) that biases questionnaire-based LLM auditing, using IRT effect sizes and a desirability-matched graded forced-choice inventory.

articles.title: Quantifying and Mitigating Socially Desirable Responding in LLMs: A Desirability-Matched Graded Forced-Choice Psychometric Study
articles.tldr: Quantifies and mitigates socially desirable responding (SDR) that biases questionnaire-based LLM auditing, using IRT effect sizes and a desirability-matched graded forced-choice inventory.

articles.title: LLM-as-a-judge validity in physics assessment depends more on the task than the model
articles.tldr: LLM-as-judge marking validity in physics is task-dependent, not model-dependent: strong rank-order agreement on structured questions and plots, near-zero on essays, and reference-anchoring biases absolute accuracy.
articles.contribution: For structured physics questions and code-based plots, LLM judges reach robust rank-order agreement with human markers (Spearman rho>0.6 and >0.84 respectively), and providing the official solution strengthens agreement.

articles.title: LLM-as-a-judge validity in physics assessment depends more on the task than the model

articles.contribution: For essays, anchored exemplars pull the AI mean to the human mean and compress variance, but script-level rank-order agreement stays near zero, showing distribution-matching can masquerade as valid discrimination.

articles.title: Evaluating Tool-Using Language Agents: Judge Reliability, Propagation Cascades, and Runtime Mitigation in AgentProp-Bench
articles.tldr: Validates that automated evaluation of tool-using LLM agents is unreliable: substring judging is chance-level (kappa=0.049) vs an ensemble kappa=0.432, and quantifies injection propagation and a runtime mitigation.
articles.contribution: Against a 100-label human-validated subset, substring-based judging agrees at chance (kappa=0.049) while a three-LLM ensemble reaches kappa=0.432 with a conservative bias, so agent-hallucination scores need human calibration.

articles.title: Evaluating Tool-Using Language Agents: Judge Reliability, Propagation Cascades, and Runtime Mitigation in AgentProp-Bench
articles.tldr: Validates that automated evaluation of tool-using LLM agents is unreliable: substring judging is chance-level (kappa=0.049) vs an ensemble kappa=0.432, and quantifies injection propagation and a runtime mitigation.
articles.contribution: Because the heuristic judge is chance-level, downstream propagation and mitigation comparisons only become interpretable once evaluation is validated, making judge reliability a prerequisite for any agent ranking or intervention claim.

articles.title: Fair splits flip the leaderboard: CHANRG reveals limited generalization in RNA secondary-structure prediction

articles.title: Fair splits flip the leaderboard: CHANRG reveals limited generalization in RNA secondary-structure prediction

articles.title: VIDA: A dataset for Visually Dependent Ambiguity in Multimodal Machine Translation

articles.title: Knowing When to Defer: Selective Prediction for Responsible Knowledge Tracing

articles.title: VeRA: Verified Reasoning Data Augmentation at Scale

articles.title: VeRA: Verified Reasoning Data Augmentation at Scale
