articles.title: VeRA: Verified Reasoning Data Augmentation at Scale
articles.tldr: Converts benchmark problems into executable specifications (template + generator + verifier) to auto-generate fresh verified variants, exposing memorization/contamination and restoring headroom.

articles.title: Beyond the Training Distribution: Mapping Generalization Boundaries in Neural Program Synthesis

articles.title: Enhancing Anomaly Detection Generalization through Knowledge Exposure: The Dual Effects of Augmentation

articles.title: Enhancing Anomaly Detection Generalization through Knowledge Exposure: The Dual Effects of Augmentation
articles.tldr: Shows anomaly-detection benchmarks carry inductive biases misaligned with real deployment and proposes semantic-shift-aware test protocols that expose large generalization drops plus a rotation-anomaly shortcut.

articles.title: Tape: A Cellular Automata Benchmark for Evaluating Rule-Shift Generalization in Reinforcement Learning

articles.title: Tape: A Cellular Automata Benchmark for Evaluating Rule-Shift Generalization in Reinforcement Learning
articles.tldr: A cellular-automata RL benchmark that isolates latent rule-shift to cleanly attribute OOD degradation, with oracle-calibrated, replicated, uncertainty-reported evaluation.

articles.title: When Accuracy Is Not Enough: Uncertainty Collapse between Noisy Label Learning and Out-of-Distribution Detection

articles.title: When Accuracy Is Not Enough: Uncertainty Collapse between Noisy Label Learning and Out-of-Distribution Detection

articles.title: SuperValid: Capability-Aligned OOD Validation for Generalizable Downstream Scaling

articles.title: SuperValid: Capability-Aligned OOD Validation for Generalizable Downstream Scaling
articles.tldr: Argues IID validation loss and benchmark-level metrics are unreliable proxies for downstream capability, and synthesizes OOD capability-aligned validation data as a better-correlated predictor.

articles.title: Auditing Generalization in AI-Generated Video Detection: A Six-Control Protocol and the VidAudit Toolkit

articles.title: Auditing Generalization in AI-Generated Video Detection: A Six-Control Protocol and the VidAudit Toolkit

articles.title: SPDEBench: An Extensive Benchmark for Learning Stochastic PDEs
articles.tldr: First unified SPDE-learning benchmark that treats data-generation parameters as controlled variables and adds Sobolev/distributional metrics beyond L2 to avoid biased evaluation.
articles.contribution: Argues data-generation choices (noise approximation, basis, renormalization, truncation degree) are normally treated as fixed implementation details yet significantly change datasets and model evaluation, and elevates them to explicitly controlled benchmark variables.

articles.title: SPDEBench: An Extensive Benchmark for Learning Stochastic PDEs
articles.tldr: First unified SPDE-learning benchmark that treats data-generation parameters as controlled variables and adds Sobolev/distributional metrics beyond L2 to avoid biased evaluation.
articles.contribution: Augments evaluation with 7 metrics including Sobolev W^{1,2} and distributional metrics (ACF, cross-correlation, signature-based) beyond standard L2 error, exposing that L2 alone yields biased or incomplete assessment for rough stochastic dynamics.

articles.title: Blending Human and LLM Expertise to Detect Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health Chatbot Responses
articles.tldr: LLM-as-judge fails at mental-health hallucination/omission detection; human-informed interpretable features are far more reliable
articles.contribution: Quantifies that leading LLM judges reach only ~52-54.6% accuracy with near-zero recall on mental-health data and vary 8x in F1 across datasets (coefficient of variation 1.23), demonstrating scorer brittleness.

articles.title: Blending Human and LLM Expertise to Detect Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health Chatbot Responses
articles.tldr: LLM-as-judge fails at mental-health hallucination/omission detection; human-informed interpretable features are far more reliable
articles.contribution: Shows LLM judges misinterpret professionally appropriate therapeutic hedging as 'uncertainty' (r=-0.565 with relevance, -0.542 with professionalism), so the judge fails to capture the clinical construct it is meant to measure.

articles.title: Blending Human and LLM Expertise to Detect Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health Chatbot Responses
articles.tldr: LLM-as-judge fails at mental-health hallucination/omission detection; human-informed interpretable features are far more reliable
articles.contribution: Builds ground truth through unanimous 3-annotator multi-stakeholder consensus and characterizes annotator reliability: human baseline F1=0.536 with wide variance across groups (clinicians 0.426, patients 0.623, general public 0.667).

articles.title: Distributional Process Reward Models: Calibrated Prediction of Future Rewards via Conditional Optimal Transport
articles.tldr: Calibrates poorly-calibrated Process Reward Models via conditional optimal transport for structurally-valid uncertainty
articles.contribution: Shows SOTA PRMs are overconfident and poorly calibrated, and that conditional-OT calibration improves ECE by +69.5% and Brier by +43.6% on MATH500 while yielding crossing-free quantiles at arbitrary confidence levels.

articles.title: Distributional Process Reward Models: Calibrated Prediction of Future Rewards via Conditional Optimal Transport
articles.tldr: Calibrates poorly-calibrated Process Reward Models via conditional optimal transport for structurally-valid uncertainty
articles.contribution: Evaluates calibration fully out-of-distribution on held-out AIME24-25 (ECE improved +51.6%), and shows the method degrades when the base PRM's ranking signal is unreliable or under distribution shift.

articles.title: Re$^2$Math: Benchmarking Theorem Retrieval in Research-Level Mathematics
articles.tldr: Benchmark for tool-grounded theorem retrieval from partial proofs with leakage control and citation-invariant scoring
articles.contribution: Each instance provides an optional leakage-controlled anchor hint, and the construction pipeline audits anchor sanitization (Appendix B) to prevent look-ahead leakage from the author-cited source.

articles.title: Re$^2$Math: Benchmarking Theorem Retrieval in Research-Level Mathematics
articles.tldr: Benchmark for tool-grounded theorem retrieval from partial proofs with leakage control and citation-invariant scoring
articles.contribution: Defines success as source-grounded but citation-invariant (any admissible theorem sufficient for the proof transition is accepted, not exact citation recovery) and decouples citation recall, source grounding, and proof-gap sufficiency.

articles.title: Re$^2$Math: Benchmarking Theorem Retrieval in Research-Level Mathematics
articles.tldr: Benchmark for tool-grounded theorem retrieval from partial proofs with leakage control and citation-invariant scoring
articles.contribution: Executes model-authored queries through a shared release-frozen retrieval artifact so hidden ranking, browsing, and context-packaging differences do not confound the mathematical source-tool policy being measured.

articles.title: Bias at the End of the Score
articles.tldr: Audit shows text-to-image reward models encode demographic biases, invalidating them as neutral image-quality metrics
articles.contribution: OLS regression shows RM scores are significantly predicted by race, gender, and their interaction and track U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics occupational distributions, so RMs measure demographic conformance rather than image quality.

articles.title: Bias at the End of the Score
articles.tldr: Audit shows text-to-image reward models encode demographic biases, invalidating them as neutral image-quality metrics
articles.contribution: Reward-guided ReNO optimization amplifies hypersexualization (PickScore raises NSFW rate 19% for female vs 7% for male subjects) and collapses demographic diversity (>80% of Black subjects reclassified as White under ImageReward/HPS).

articles.title: Bias at the End of the Score
articles.tldr: Audit shows text-to-image reward models encode demographic biases, invalidating them as neutral image-quality metrics
articles.contribution: Treats demographic attributes as confounders of the reward score; ranking analysis finds HPS and ImageReward consistently rank White subjects highest even under negative prompts, revealing a structural demographic prior.

articles.title: Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF
articles.tldr: Fact-RLHF counters reward hacking and introduces leakage-controlled MMHal-Bench to measure LMM hallucination
articles.contribution: Identifies that the vanilla RLHF reward model is hacked by the policy producing longer, more hallucinated responses, and proposes Factually Augmented RLHF that gives the reward model image captions / ground-truth options to prevent this.

articles.title: Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF
articles.tldr: Fact-RLHF counters reward hacking and introduces leakage-controlled MMHal-Bench to measure LMM hallucination
articles.contribution: Constructs MMHal-Bench from OpenImages validation/test images with brand-new questions explicitly to avoid data leakage or evaluation on data the LMMs saw during training.

articles.title: Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF
articles.tldr: Fact-RLHF counters reward hacking and introduces leakage-controlled MMHal-Bench to measure LMM hallucination
articles.contribution: Uses GPT-4 as the MMHal-Bench judge (agreeing with human judgment in 94% of cases) while cautioning that short or evasive responses can inadvertently attain high scores, an intrinsic honesty-helpfulness trade-off.

articles.title: Towards Out-Of-Distribution Generalization: A Survey
articles.tldr: Survey of out-of-distribution generalization: problem definition, methods, spurious correlations, and distribution-shift benchmarks
articles.contribution: Formally characterizes OOD generalization, where the test distribution differs from training and the i.i.d. assumption fails, causing considerable model-performance degradation upon deployment.

articles.title: Towards Out-Of-Distribution Generalization: A Survey
articles.tldr: Survey of out-of-distribution generalization: problem definition, methods, spurious correlations, and distribution-shift benchmarks
articles.contribution: Reviews spurious/shortcut correlations (Colored MNIST, Waterbirds bird-background correlation) and invariant-learning methods designed to break these confounds between features and labels.

articles.title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
articles.tldr: Survey and TRC-Bench benchmark assessing RAG trustworthiness across six dimensions
articles.contribution: Decomposes RAG trustworthiness into six theory-grounded dimensions (factuality, robustness, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy) as the construct foundation before building the TRC-Bench measure.

articles.title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
articles.tldr: Survey and TRC-Bench benchmark assessing RAG trustworthiness across six dimensions
articles.contribution: Catalogs RAG robustness against retrieval-stage, backdoor, interaction-level and structural attacks alongside fairness stress-testing, providing red-team / falsification evidence for trustworthiness claims.

articles.title: ROBBIE: Robust Bias Evaluation of Large Generative Language Models
articles.tldr: Compares 6 prompt-based bias/toxicity metrics across 12 demographic axes and 5 LLM families, exposing metric divergence and validating classifier scorers against humans.
articles.contribution: Defines 'bias' as the share of subgroups whose toxicity/negative-regard rate exceeds a demographic-parity threshold, and shows different datasets/metrics capture different bias constructs so no single metric suffices.

articles.title: ROBBIE: Robust Bias Evaluation of Large Generative Language Models
articles.tldr: Compares 6 prompt-based bias/toxicity metrics across 12 demographic axes and 5 LLM families, exposing metric divergence and validating classifier scorers against humans.
articles.contribution: Validates the Regard/toxicity classifier scorers against human annotations via Pearson correlation, finding negative-regard far better correlated than positive/neutral.

articles.title: ROBBIE: Robust Bias Evaluation of Large Generative Language Models
articles.tldr: Compares 6 prompt-based bias/toxicity metrics across 12 demographic axes and 5 LLM families, exposing metric divergence and validating classifier scorers against humans.
articles.contribution: Expands demographic coverage to 12 axes and identity intersections via new AdvPromptSet (~197k prompts) and HolisticBiasR (~214k prompts) to counter prior single-axis convenience sampling of bias evaluation.

articles.title: DyVal 2: Dynamic Evaluation of Large Language Models by Meta Probing Agents
articles.tldr: Psychometrics-inspired dynamic evaluation (Meta Probing Agents) regenerates benchmark items via probing+judge agents to expose data contamination and decompose ability.
articles.contribution: Dynamically transforms MMLU/GSM8K/BBH/ARC-C items into fresh variants; substantial accuracy drops on the regenerated sets imply prior contamination/benchmark overfitting.

articles.title: DyVal 2: Dynamic Evaluation of Large Language Models by Meta Probing Agents
articles.tldr: Psychometrics-inspired dynamic evaluation (Meta Probing Agents) regenerates benchmark items via probing+judge agents to expose data contamination and decompose ability.
articles.contribution: Decomposes a single benchmark score into three psychometric abilities (language understanding, problem solving, domain knowledge), revealing what an aggregate score conflates.

articles.title: Which of These Best Describes Multiple Choice Evaluation with LLMs? A) Forced B) Flawed C) Fixable D) All of the Above
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing multiple-choice QA evaluation is both format-flawed and dataset-flawed (leakage, unanswerability, shortcuts, saturation), with education-based fixes.
articles.contribution: Argues the MCQA 'pick the best answer' format cannot test generation/subjectivity and misaligns with real LLM use, so it under-represents the knowledge construct it claims to measure.

articles.title: Which of These Best Describes Multiple Choice Evaluation with LLMs? A) Forced B) Flawed C) Fixable D) All of the Above
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing multiple-choice QA evaluation is both format-flawed and dataset-flawed (leakage, unanswerability, shortcuts, saturation), with education-based fixes.
articles.contribution: Documents MCQA dataset leakage (models 'peek at answer keys'), unanswerable items, and saturation, proposing Item Response Theory to cull easy items and build harder ones.

articles.title: Which of These Best Describes Multiple Choice Evaluation with LLMs? A) Forced B) Flawed C) Fixable D) All of the Above
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing multiple-choice QA evaluation is both format-flawed and dataset-flawed (leakage, unanswerability, shortcuts, saturation), with education-based fixes.
articles.contribution: Shows LLMs beat random guessing from partial inputs (choices-only shortcuts), and proposes calibrated scoring to deter guessing and shortcut-proof MCQ design.

articles.title: Measuring and Reducing LLM Hallucination without Gold-Standard Answers via Expertise-Weighting
articles.tldr: FEWL measures LLM hallucination without gold-standard answers by expertise-weighting off-the-shelf reference LLMs, with theoretical guarantees.
articles.contribution: Quantifies each reference LLM's expertise with a 'laziness penalty' (penalizing superficial answers to related questions), yielding more accurate hallucination scores than naively averaging reference LLMs.

articles.title: Measuring and Reducing LLM Hallucination without Gold-Standard Answers via Expertise-Weighting
articles.tldr: FEWL measures LLM hallucination without gold-standard answers by expertise-weighting off-the-shelf reference LLMs, with theoretical guarantees.
articles.contribution: Removes dependence on costly, human-error-prone gold-standard answers by treating reference-LLM outputs as noisy-label proxies aggregated into a factualness score.

articles.title: LiveMCPBench: Can Agents Navigate an Ocean of MCP Tools?
articles.tldr: Large-scale MCP tool-use agent benchmark (70 servers/527 tools) with a human-validated LLM-as-Judge, diagnosing retrieval as the dominant failure mode.
articles.contribution: Validates the LLM-as-Judge outcome verifier against human trajectory annotations (81.05% human-model agreement) and runs a single-evaluator bias analysis to establish scorer reliability.

articles.title: LiveMCPBench: Can Agents Navigate an Ocean of MCP Tools?
articles.tldr: Large-scale MCP tool-use agent benchmark (70 servers/527 tools) with a human-validated LLM-as-Judge, diagnosing retrieval as the dominant failure mode.
articles.contribution: Shows retrieval errors cause nearly half of all failures, so the multi-server retrieval scaffold confounds what the benchmark attributes to agent tool-use capability.

articles.title: FENICE: Factuality Evaluation of summarization based on Natural language Inference and Claim Extraction
articles.tldr: FENICE is an interpretable, efficient NLI + claim-extraction factuality metric for summarization that sets SOTA on AGGREFACT while avoiding LLM-metric contamination.
articles.contribution: Proposes an NLI-alignment-over-atomic-claims factuality metric (DeBERTa-v3-large NLI + GPT-3.5/T5 claim extractor, coreference-aware, multi-granularity) that sets new SOTA balanced accuracy on AGGREFACT.

articles.title: FENICE: Factuality Evaluation of summarization based on Natural language Inference and Claim Extraction
articles.tldr: FENICE is an interpretable, efficient NLI + claim-extraction factuality metric for summarization that sets SOTA on AGGREFACT while avoiding LLM-metric contamination.
articles.contribution: Warns that closed LLM-based factuality metrics (ChatGPT-DA/CoT, G-Eval) may have seen benchmark test data and are non-reproducible/costly, motivating FENICE's restriction of the LLM to claim extraction only.

articles.title: CRUXEval-X: A Benchmark for Multilingual Code Reasoning, Understanding and Execution
articles.tldr: CRUXEval-X is a 19-language code-reasoning benchmark that attacks the Python-dominance sampling bias and contest-site contamination of existing code evals.
articles.contribution: Counters the >95% Python dominance of code benchmarks by covering 19 languages (>=600 subjects each, ~19K tests) so non-Python coding ability is no longer unmeasured.

articles.title: CRUXEval-X: A Benchmark for Multilingual Code Reasoning, Understanding and Execution
articles.tldr: CRUXEval-X is a 19-language code-reasoning benchmark that attacks the Python-dominance sampling bias and contest-site contamination of existing code evals.
articles.contribution: Builds content-consistent tests via an automated, execution-feedback-guided generate-and-repair pipeline to avoid the training-data contamination of Leetcode-sourced code benchmarks.

articles.title: Principles and Guidelines for the Use of LLM Judges
articles.tldr: Position/guidelines paper on how LLM relevance judges can falsely indicate success and self-reinforce in information-retrieval evaluation.
articles.contribution: Enumerates 13 ways LLM relevance judges negatively impact IR evaluation (bias reinforcement, inconsistent assessment methodology) and proposes quantifying tests and guardrails.

articles.title: Principles and Guidelines for the Use of LLM Judges
articles.tldr: Position/guidelines paper on how LLM relevance judges can falsely indicate success and self-reinforce in information-retrieval evaluation.
articles.contribution: Warns that an LLM judge sets itself as a performance ceiling and creates circular, self-reinforcing evaluation (Goodhart, loss of variety) when the same LLM drives both system development and assessment.

articles.title: HalluDial: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Automatic Dialogue-Level Hallucination Evaluation
articles.tldr: HalluDial is a large dialogue-level hallucination benchmark plus a meta-evaluation of LLM hallucination-evaluators and a trained judge, HalluJudge.
articles.contribution: Meta-evaluates LLMs as hallucination detectors and trains HalluJudge, which surpasses GPT-4/GPT-4o on dialogue-level detection F1/accuracy, showing specialized judges beat general LLM evaluators.

articles.title: HalluDial: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Automatic Dialogue-Level Hallucination Evaluation
articles.tldr: HalluDial is a large dialogue-level hallucination benchmark plus a meta-evaluation of LLM hallucination-evaluators and a trained judge, HalluJudge.
articles.contribution: Broadens the hallucination construct to dialogue level covering both factuality and faithfulness (with localization and rationale), which sentence/passage benchmarks under-represent.

articles.title: PeFoMed: Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning of Multimodal Large Language Models for Medical Imaging
articles.tldr: A medical MLLM fine-tuning paper whose evaluation analysis shows lexical-similarity metrics are unreliable relative to GPT-4 and human semantic judgments.
articles.contribution: Shows GPT-4 semantic-similarity judgments align closely with human raters and are more stable than lexical metrics for Med-VQA and medical report generation.

articles.title: PeFoMed: Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning of Multimodal Large Language Models for Medical Imaging
articles.tldr: A medical MLLM fine-tuning paper whose evaluation analysis shows lexical-similarity metrics are unreliable relative to GPT-4 and human semantic judgments.
articles.contribution: Argues lexical-similarity metrics like BLEU fail to capture semantic correctness of generated medical answers/reports, questioning their reliability as quality measures.

articles.title: RevisEval: Improving LLM-as-a-Judge via Response-Adapted References
articles.tldr: Generates response-adapted references by revising the response, then judges against them to make LLM-as-a-Judge more reliable and less biased.
articles.contribution: Shows a reference-free LLM judge has a reliability gap vs humans and that revising the response into a response-adapted reference (used as an anchor) closes it across NLG and preference tasks.

articles.title: RevisEval: Improving LLM-as-a-Judge via Response-Adapted References
articles.tldr: Generates response-adapted references by revising the response, then judges against them to make LLM-as-a-Judge more reliable and less biased.
articles.contribution: Uses the adaptive reference to suppress verbosity and positional bias confounds in pairwise judging, lowering position-swap flip rates on LLMBar/MT-Bench/AlpacaFarm.

articles.title: ZSC-Eval: An Evaluation Toolkit and Benchmark for Multi-agent Zero-shot Coordination
articles.tldr: First evaluation toolkit/benchmark for zero-shot coordination, arguing mean-return metrics and self-similar eval partners invalidate ZSC evaluation, and proposing deployment-representative partners plus a generalization-gap metric.
articles.contribution: Argues evaluation partners generated by the same training algorithm are unrepresentative of the deployment-time partner distribution, and generates behavior-preferring partners selected by Best-Response Diversity to approximate it.

articles.title: ZSC-Eval: An Evaluation Toolkit and Benchmark for Multi-agent Zero-shot Coordination
articles.tldr: First evaluation toolkit/benchmark for zero-shot coordination, arguing mean-return metrics and self-similar eval partners invalidate ZSC evaluation, and proposing deployment-representative partners plus a generalization-gap metric.
articles.contribution: Shows mean episode return conflates task performance with generalization and ignores unbalanced partner ability, and replaces it with Best-Response Proximity (BR-Prox) that measures the generalization gap.

articles.title: ZSC-Eval: An Evaluation Toolkit and Benchmark for Multi-agent Zero-shot Coordination
articles.tldr: First evaluation toolkit/benchmark for zero-shot coordination, arguing mean-return metrics and self-similar eval partners invalidate ZSC evaluation, and proposing deployment-representative partners plus a generalization-gap metric.
articles.contribution: Identifies that cross-play among trained ZSC agents yields unfair comparisons because of overlap between training and evaluation partners, and separates evaluation partners from training to fix it.

articles.title: Everything You Wanted to Know About LLM-based Vulnerability Detection But Were Afraid to Ask
articles.tldr: Argues LLM vulnerability-detection benchmarks are context-deprived, and shows that adding execution/data-flow context overturns 'unreliable/insensitive/plateaued' beliefs, using LLM-as-judge to validate rationales.
articles.contribution: Shows isolated-function/file benchmarks omit the execution and data-flow context that governs real vulnerabilities, so they mis-measure the detection construct and produce misleading conclusions; builds a 2,000-pair context-rich dataset.

articles.title: Everything You Wanted to Know About LLM-based Vulnerability Detection But Were Afraid to Ask
articles.tldr: Argues LLM vulnerability-detection benchmarks are context-deprived, and shows that adding execution/data-flow context overturns 'unreliable/insensitive/plateaued' beliefs, using LLM-as-judge to validate rationales.
articles.contribution: Documents the 'right answer, wrong reason' confound (correct label from an irrelevant rationale) and uses LLM-as-a-judge to verify the natural-language rationale actually identifies the root cause, not just the binary label.

articles.title: AI-Slop to AI-Polish? Aligning Language Models through Edit-Based Writing Rewards and Test-time Computation
articles.tldr: Introduces a writing-quality benchmark showing SOTA LLM judges score near random, and trains/validates edit-based reward models against expert writers.
articles.contribution: The WQ benchmark (4,729 judgments from five preference datasets) shows SOTA LLMs and reward models barely beat random on writing quality, i.e. current judges fail to capture the writing-quality construct.

articles.title: AI-Slop to AI-Polish? Aligning Language Models through Edit-Based Writing Rewards and Test-time Computation
articles.tldr: Introduces a writing-quality benchmark showing SOTA LLM judges score near random, and trains/validates edit-based reward models against expert writers.
articles.contribution: Motivates the work with reward-hacking risk from uncalibrated LLM feedback and self-preference bias of LLM evaluators, and validates a calibrated reward model against human experts to resist it.

articles.title: MCP-Atlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Tool-Use Competency with Real MCP Servers
articles.tldr: Large-scale tool-use benchmark against real MCP servers with claim-level scoring decoupled from style, distractor tools, a held-out private split, and a failure taxonomy.
articles.contribution: Introduces claim-level scoring against atomic factual claims grounded in tool outputs, disentangling task success from agent verbosity/style and crediting valid alternative tool-call trajectories.

articles.title: MCP-Atlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Tool-Use Competency with Real MCP Servers
articles.tldr: Large-scale tool-use benchmark against real MCP servers with claim-level scoring decoupled from style, distractor tools, a held-out private split, and a failure taxonomy.
articles.contribution: Reserves a 500-task private split for exposure monitoring and leaderboard integrity, guarding the benchmark against contamination as it is released.

articles.title: MCP-Atlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Tool-Use Competency with Real MCP Servers
articles.tldr: Large-scale tool-use benchmark against real MCP servers with claim-level scoring decoupled from style, distractor tools, a held-out private split, and a failure taxonomy.
articles.contribution: Evaluates against production MCP servers (not mocks) with a controlled tool set mixing required tools and semantically plausible distractors, and an 11-category taxonomy separating tool-call failures from cognitive failures.

articles.title: When Can We Trust LLMs in Mental Health? Large-Scale Benchmarks for Reliable LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Builds real-clinical mental-health dialogue benchmarks and an ICC-based framework to quantify when LLM judges can be trusted against human experts.
articles.contribution: Introduces the Affective-Cognitive Agreement Framework using intraclass correlation coefficients with confidence intervals to quantify LLM-judge agreement, consistency and bias per attribute, defining when judges are trustworthy.

articles.title: When Can We Trust LLMs in Mental Health? Large-Scale Benchmarks for Reliable LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Builds real-clinical mental-health dialogue benchmarks and an ICC-based framework to quantify when LLM judges can be trusted against human experts.
articles.contribution: Grounds seven therapeutic attributes (grouped into Cognitive Support and Affective Resonance scores) in clinical-expert human ratings over 70,000 judgments, exposing per-attribute rater-agreement differences.

articles.title: When Can We Trust LLMs in Mental Health? Large-Scale Benchmarks for Reliable LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Builds real-clinical mental-health dialogue benchmarks and an ICC-based framework to quantify when LLM judges can be trusted against human experts.
articles.contribution: Argues prior mental-health benchmarks rely on synthetic or social-media data and consolidates 10,000 conversations from three authentic clinical-scenario datasets to make the evaluation set representative.

articles.title: RL Grokking Recipe: How Does RL Unlock and Transfer New Algorithms in LLMs?
articles.tldr: A controlled synthetic-coding benchmark (DELTA) that removes topic/difficulty confounds and pretraining contamination to validly measure whether RL unlocks genuinely new algorithms and how they transfer OOD.
articles.contribution: Introduces the Manufactoria family with entirely novel program syntax unavailable in any pretraining corpus so that learnability gains cannot be explained by memorized patterns or tool shortcuts.

articles.title: RL Grokking Recipe: How Does RL Unlock and Transfer New Algorithms in LLMs?
articles.tldr: A controlled synthetic-coding benchmark (DELTA) that removes topic/difficulty confounds and pretraining contamination to validly measure whether RL unlocks genuinely new algorithms and how they transfer OOD.
articles.contribution: Argues uncontrolled open benchmarks mix topics and difficulty (blurring capability-sharpening vs genuine acquisition), and uses templated generators with tight train-test control to attribute gains to specific isolated skills.

articles.title: RL Grokking Recipe: How Does RL Unlock and Transfer New Algorithms in LLMs?
articles.tldr: A controlled synthetic-coding benchmark (DELTA) that removes topic/difficulty confounds and pretraining contamination to validly measure whether RL unlocks genuinely new algorithms and how they transfer OOD.
articles.contribution: Measures transfer along exploratory, compositional and transformative axes plus cross-family transfer to test whether learned strategies generalize OOD rather than being memorized.

articles.title: Evaluating Image Hallucination in Text-to-Image Generation with Question-Answering
articles.tldr: Defines image hallucination as factual infidelity and proposes I-HallA, a VQA-based metric validated against humans, arguing prompt-alignment metrics like TIFA cannot capture factuality.
articles.contribution: Argues prompt-alignment metrics (TIFA, CLIPScore) only check elements explicitly mentioned in the prompt and cannot verify external-knowledge facts, so they mis-measure factuality; defines image hallucination and operationalizes it via VQA over external-knowledge questions.

articles.title: Evaluating Image Hallucination in Text-to-Image Generation with Question-Answering
articles.tldr: Defines image hallucination as factual infidelity and proposes I-HallA, a VQA-based metric validated against humans, arguing prompt-alignment metrics like TIFA cannot capture factuality.
articles.contribution: Validates the I-HallA metric's reliability by demonstrating a strong Spearman correlation with human judgments, establishing criterion agreement for the automated scorer.

articles.title: From Intention to Execution: Probing the Generalization Boundaries of Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.tldr: A 50-task simulation probing suite (INT-ACT) that systematically measures VLA generalization, adding an intention metric to reveal an intention-action gap that aggregate success rates hide.
articles.contribution: Argues existing VLA benchmarks have too few tasks and don't target generalization, and builds 50 tasks systematically varying OOD object diversity, language complexity and vision-language distractors to measure it.

articles.title: From Intention to Execution: Probing the Generalization Boundaries of Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.tldr: A 50-task simulation probing suite (INT-ACT) that systematically measures VLA generalization, adding an intention metric to reveal an intention-action gap that aggregate success rates hide.
articles.contribution: Adds a separate intention metric so success rate no longer conflates high-level planning with motor execution, exposing that coherent intentions can coexist with failed execution.

articles.title: Learning to Reason for Factuality
articles.tldr: Shows automatic factuality metrics get reward-hacked when used as online-RL rewards and benchmarks that reasoning LLMs hallucinate more, then designs a gaming-resistant multi-part reward.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that using automatic factuality metrics (FActScore/VeriScore) directly as an online-RL reward is Goodharted: models shortcut to shorter/less-detailed answers or recite factual-but-irrelevant text to inflate the score.

articles.title: Learning to Reason for Factuality
articles.tldr: Shows automatic factuality metrics get reward-hacked when used as online-RL rewards and benchmarks that reasoning LLMs hallucinate more, then designs a gaming-resistant multi-part reward.
articles.contribution: Argues long-form factuality cannot be reliably assessed by rule-based heuristics or a single LLM judge, and constructs a three-component reward (precision + detail + answer-relevance via LLM-as-a-judge) plus a 30x-faster VeriScore to score it stably in real time.

articles.title: Building Trust in Mental Health Chatbots: Safety Metrics and LLM-Based Evaluation Tools
articles.tldr: Develops an expert-validated safety-evaluation framework for mental-health chatbots and benchmarks LLM-judge, agentic and embedding scorers against human experts.
articles.contribution: Shows base LLM judges systematically over-score chatbot safety (GPT-4 base MAE 3.14, mean 9.81 vs human 6.50) and that only the agentic scorer with real-time data is statistically indistinguishable from experts.

articles.title: Building Trust in Mental Health Chatbots: Safety Metrics and LLM-Based Evaluation Tools
articles.tldr: Develops an expert-validated safety-evaluation framework for mental-health chatbots and benchmarks LLM-judge, agentic and embedding scorers against human experts.
articles.contribution: Argues surface-similarity metrics fail to capture clinical safety and constructs an expert-validated 100-question benchmark plus five guideline dimensions and ideal responses as the safety construct/ground truth.

articles.title: DHP Benchmark: Are LLMs Good NLG Evaluators?
articles.tldr: DHP benchmark quantifies LLM NLG-evaluator discernment via hierarchical text perturbation plus statistical tests, avoiding the response-style bias of human-alignment metrics.
articles.contribution: Introduces perturbation-based discernment scores measuring whether an LLM judge reliably assigns lower quality to progressively degraded text, finding models under 8B parameters unreliable and GPT-4-Turbo most stable across four NLG tasks.

articles.title: DHP Benchmark: Are LLMs Good NLG Evaluators?
articles.tldr: DHP benchmark quantifies LLM NLG-evaluator discernment via hierarchical text perturbation plus statistical tests, avoiding the response-style bias of human-alignment metrics.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that correlation-with-human alignment scores are confounded by an evaluator's response-style bias, and proposes response-style-invariant Wilcoxon-based discernment scores as a cleaner measure of evaluation capability.

articles.title: Fairness Evaluation with Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: First application of Item Response Theory to fairness evaluation, jointly estimating a model's fair-prediction ability and each individual's difficulty/discrimination.
articles.contribution: Uses item-characteristic-curve flatness plus beta-IRT difficulty/discrimination to disentangle whether unfairness originates from an individual's intrinsic characteristics versus the predictive model, rather than conflating the two.

articles.title: Fairness Evaluation with Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: First application of Item Response Theory to fairness evaluation, jointly estimating a model's fair-prediction ability and each individual's difficulty/discrimination.
articles.contribution: Elicits a latent 'fair-prediction ability' per model and difficulty/discrimination per individual from a model-by-individual situation-test-score matrix, giving finer fairness estimates than aggregate pairwise-metric comparisons.

articles.title: NOVA: A Benchmark for Anomaly Localization and Clinical Reasoning in Brain MRI
articles.tldr: Evaluation-only brain-MRI benchmark of ~900 scans over 281 rare pathologies that stress-tests vision-language-model OOD generalization and exposes closed-set benchmark leakage.
articles.contribution: Argues that benchmarking on a few common outlier types 'silently collapses evaluation back to a closed-set problem', and curates 281 rare pathologies with heterogeneous protocols so the evaluation set actually covers the open-world clinical distribution.

articles.title: NOVA: A Benchmark for Anomaly Localization and Clinical Reasoning in Brain MRI
articles.tldr: Evaluation-only brain-MRI benchmark of ~900 scans over 281 rare pathologies that stress-tests vision-language-model OOD generalization and exposes closed-set benchmark leakage.
articles.contribution: Keeps NOVA strictly evaluation-only and never used for training, and flags that proprietary VLMs may already have seen public cases so reported scores are an upper bound on genuine zero-shot generalization.

articles.title: LLM4VV: Exploring LLM-as-a-Judge for Validation and Verification Testsuites
articles.tldr: Probes LLM-as-a-judge reliability for validating OpenACC/OpenMP compiler tests via negative probing, then boosts it with an agent-plus-pipeline harness.
articles.contribution: Measures the standalone deepseek-coder-33B judge's accuracy (56.63% OpenACC, 40.60% OpenMP) and a strong permissiveness bias, showing a bare LLM judge is an unreliable verifier of compiler-test validity.

articles.title: LLM4VV: Exploring LLM-as-a-Judge for Validation and Verification Testsuites
articles.tldr: Probes LLM-as-a-judge reliability for validating OpenACC/OpenMP compiler tests via negative probing, then boosts it with an agent-plus-pipeline harness.
articles.contribution: Shows that wrapping the judge in an agent-based approach with compiler feedback and a staged validation pipeline raises accuracy to 80.53% (OpenACC) / 92.57% (OpenMP) but flips the bias toward restrictiveness, i.e. the harness reshapes what is measured.

articles.title: A Survey of Multimodal Hallucination Evaluation and Detection
articles.tldr: Survey of multimodal-hallucination evaluation benchmarks and detection methods across I2T/T2I, organized by a faithfulness-versus-factuality taxonomy.
articles.contribution: Proposes a hallucination taxonomy splitting faithfulness (output vs input) from factuality (output vs world knowledge) across I2T and T2I, unifying the construct definitions used across disparate hallucination benchmarks.

articles.title: A Survey of Multimodal Hallucination Evaluation and Detection
articles.tldr: Survey of multimodal-hallucination evaluation benchmarks and detection methods across I2T/T2I, organized by a faithfulness-versus-factuality taxonomy.
articles.contribution: Reviews I2T/T2I hallucination benchmarks and detection methods by construction, objectives and metrics, and identifies limitations in scalable, explainable and domain-specific factuality evaluation as open validity gaps.

articles.title: ALBA: Adaptive Language-Based Assessments for Mental Health
articles.tldr: Adaptive language-based mental-health assessment (ALIRT / Actor-Critic) applies IRT and Classical Test Theory to score latent depression/anxiety traits from few language responses.
articles.contribution: Shows the ALIRT IRT-based method reaches Pearson r ~ 0.93 with the full-questionnaire latent score after only ~3 adaptively-ordered language questions versus 7+ normally needed, without compromising measurement validity.

articles.title: ALBA: Adaptive Language-Based Assessments for Mental Health
articles.tldr: Adaptive language-based mental-health assessment (ALIRT / Actor-Critic) applies IRT and Classical Test Theory to score latent depression/anxiety traits from few language responses.
articles.contribution: Grounds the assessment in two psychometric measurement theories (Classical Test Theory and Item Response Theory) to operationalize latent depression/anxiety severity from open-ended language rather than fixed summed scores.

articles.title: Zero-shot Benchmarking: A Framework for Flexible and Scalable Automatic Evaluation of Language Models
articles.tldr: Zero-shot Benchmarking builds fully-automatic benchmarks (LLM-generated test data plus LLM judge) and meta-evaluates them by ranking correlation against human gold rankings.
articles.contribution: Finds through ablations that judge model size is a crucial driver of benchmark quality, so LLM-judge scoring becomes reliable only above a size threshold, otherwise producing rankings that diverge from human preferences.

articles.title: Zero-shot Benchmarking: A Framework for Flexible and Scalable Automatic Evaluation of Language Models
articles.tldr: Zero-shot Benchmarking builds fully-automatic benchmarks (LLM-generated test data plus LLM judge) and meta-evaluates them by ranking correlation against human gold rankings.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory evidence that the fully-synthetic benchmarks are valid by showing their system rankings correlate strongly with human gold rankings and outperform widely-adopted standard benchmarks across five text tasks and one multimodal task.

articles.title: Zero-shot Benchmarking: A Framework for Flexible and Scalable Automatic Evaluation of Language Models
articles.tldr: Zero-shot Benchmarking builds fully-automatic benchmarks (LLM-generated test data plus LLM judge) and meta-evaluates them by ranking correlation against human gold rankings.
articles.contribution: Shows dataset variety, not size, drives benchmark validity, so diversifying the generation prompts produces a more representative evaluation set than simply scaling the number of instances.

articles.title: Generalizable deep learning for photoplethysmography-based blood pressure estimation—A benchmarking study
articles.tldr: Benchmarking study showing in-distribution accuracy overstates the out-of-distribution generalization of PPG-based blood-pressure deep models.
articles.contribution: Quantifies the gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution error to show single-dataset PPG blood-pressure benchmarks overstate real-world generalization.

articles.title: Truth or Mirage? Towards End-to-End Factuality Evaluation with LLM-Oasis
articles.tldr: Large-scale Wikipedia-derived resource plus a human-validated gold benchmark for end-to-end factuality evaluation of language models.
articles.contribution: Human-validates the automated claim-extraction/falsification/text-generation pipeline to establish label quality for the factuality gold-standard benchmark.

articles.title: Truth or Mirage? Towards End-to-End Factuality Evaluation with LLM-Oasis
articles.tldr: Large-scale Wikipedia-derived resource plus a human-validated gold benchmark for end-to-end factuality evaluation of language models.
articles.contribution: Paraphrases factual texts and discards original Wikipedia passages so pretraining or RAG memorization cannot leak answers into the factuality benchmark.

articles.title: GT23D-Bench: A Comprehensive General Text-to-3D Generation Benchmark
articles.tldr: Text-to-3D benchmark proposing geometry-aware metrics that correlate with human judgment better than 2D-proxy and GPT-based scores.
articles.contribution: Introduces 3D-aware metrics measuring geometric fidelity and alignment instead of 2D image-text similarity, fixing the surface-proxy misrepresentation of text-to-3D quality.

articles.title: GT23D-Bench: A Comprehensive General Text-to-3D Generation Benchmark
articles.tldr: Text-to-3D benchmark proposing geometry-aware metrics that correlate with human judgment better than 2D-proxy and GPT-based scores.
articles.contribution: Shows GPT-based scoring (GPTEval3D) inherits model biases and correlates poorly, even negatively, with human judgment, motivating non-LLM geometry metrics.

articles.title: What Matters in Memorizing and Recalling Facts? Multifaceted Benchmarks for Knowledge Probing in Language Models
articles.tldr: Multifaceted knowledge-probing benchmark measuring accuracy, consistency and reliability of LLM factual knowledge across many diverse prompts.
articles.contribution: Measures accuracy fluctuation, prediction consistency and overconfidence across diverse prompts, exposing single-prompt knowledge probing as an unreliable instrument.

articles.title: What Matters in Memorizing and Recalling Facts? Multifaceted Benchmarks for Knowledge Probing in Language Models
articles.tldr: Multifaceted knowledge-probing benchmark measuring accuracy, consistency and reliability of LLM factual knowledge across many diverse prompts.
articles.contribution: Shows masked-LM fill-in-the-blank probing operationalization underestimates decoder LLMs, and MyriadLAMA's diverse templates reduce prompt-format bias in the probe.

articles.title: Any Large Language Model Can Be a Reliable Judge: Debiasing with a Reasoning-based Bias Detector
articles.tldr: Quantifies systematic biases in LLM-as-judge evaluators and adds a reasoning-based bias detector that debiases their verdicts.
articles.contribution: Quantifies verbosity, position, bandwagon and sentiment bias across eight LLM judges and shows an external reasoning-based detector restores judge accuracy and consistency.

articles.title: Any Large Language Model Can Be a Reliable Judge: Debiasing with a Reasoning-based Bias Detector
articles.tldr: Quantifies systematic biases in LLM-as-judge evaluators and adds a reasoning-based bias detector that debiases their verdicts.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates judges latch onto surface cues (length, option order, majority opinion, tone) that break the link between the assigned score and true answer quality.

articles.title: GraphBench: Next-generation graph learning benchmarking
articles.tldr: Standardized multi-domain graph-learning benchmark with unified hyperparameter tuning and explicit out-of-distribution generalization tests.
articles.contribution: Replaces fragmented, inconsistent graph-benchmark protocols with standardized splits, domain-specific metrics and a unified hyperparameter-tuning framework for reproducible comparison.

articles.title: GraphBench: Next-generation graph learning benchmarking
articles.tldr: Standardized multi-domain graph-learning benchmark with unified hyperparameter tuning and explicit out-of-distribution generalization tests.
articles.contribution: Moves beyond convenience molecular/citation datasets to real-world domains (chip design, SAT, combinatorial optimization, weather) for a more representative evaluation set.

articles.title: GraphBench: Next-generation graph learning benchmarking
articles.tldr: Standardized multi-domain graph-learning benchmark with unified hyperparameter tuning and explicit out-of-distribution generalization tests.
articles.contribution: Adds explicit out-of-distribution splits by time and problem size to measure size and temporal generalization rather than in-distribution accuracy.

articles.title: Min-p, Max Exaggeration: A Critical Analysis of Min-p Sampling in Language Models
articles.tldr: Critical reanalysis showing that the reported superiority of min-p sampling fails to hold under correct statistics and fair hyperparameter tuning.
articles.contribution: Shows min-p received far more hyperparameter tuning than its baselines, and equalizing tuning volume makes it indistinguishable, exposing an unfair-comparison confound.

articles.title: Min-p, Max Exaggeration: A Critical Analysis of Min-p Sampling in Language Models
articles.tldr: Critical reanalysis showing that the reported superiority of min-p sampling fails to hold under correct statistics and fair hyperparameter tuning.
articles.contribution: Documents omitted data, improper pooled t-tests and missing multiple-comparison correction, and shows proper analysis collapses the claimed significance.

articles.title: Min-p, Max Exaggeration: A Critical Analysis of Min-p Sampling in Language Models
articles.tldr: Critical reanalysis showing that the reported superiority of min-p sampling fails to hold under correct statistics and fair hyperparameter tuning.
articles.contribution: Finds the LLM-as-judge AlpacaEval results used an indirect common-baseline design confounded by non-transitivity and selectively reported the favorable min-p score.

articles.title: When Models Lie, We Learn: Multilingual Span-Level Hallucination Detection with PsiloQA
articles.tldr: Scalable multilingual span-level hallucination-detection benchmark auto-annotated by GPT-4o and validated against human annotators.
articles.contribution: Validates GPT-4o automatic span annotation against human annotators to justify low-cost labels for hallucination-detection evaluation.

articles.title: When Models Lie, We Learn: Multilingual Span-Level Hallucination Detection with PsiloQA
articles.tldr: Scalable multilingual span-level hallucination-detection benchmark auto-annotated by GPT-4o and validated against human annotators.
articles.contribution: Extends span-level hallucination evaluation to 14 languages, countering the English-only convenience sampling of prior hallucination benchmarks.

articles.title: Measuring Bias or Measuring the Task: Understanding the Brittle Nature of LLM Gender Biases
articles.tldr: Gender-bias evaluation prompts trigger a distinct LLM 'testing mode', undermining the validity of bias measurement.
articles.contribution: Shows prompts that look like bias-evaluation setups shift pronoun distributions (~0.5 sensitivity), inducing 'testing mode' behavior with limited ecological validity outside benchmarks.

articles.title: Measuring Bias or Measuring the Task: Understanding the Brittle Nature of LLM Gender Biases
articles.tldr: Gender-bias evaluation prompts trigger a distinct LLM 'testing mode', undermining the validity of bias measurement.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates discrete-choice metrics amplify measured bias via categorical flipping while token-probability metrics are more stable, so metric choice materially changes the reported bias.

articles.title: Measuring Bias or Measuring the Task: Understanding the Brittle Nature of LLM Gender Biases
articles.tldr: Gender-bias evaluation prompts trigger a distinct LLM 'testing mode', undermining the validity of bias measurement.
articles.contribution: Shows gender-salience and instruction cues make bias benchmarks measure the task framing rather than persistent underlying bias, threatening construct validity.

articles.title: Evaluating how LLM annotations represent diverse views on contentious topics
articles.authors: Megan A. J. Brown et al.
articles.tldr: LLM annotation bias on subjective tasks is dataset-specific, and item difficulty predicts agreement far more than annotator demographics.
articles.contribution: Finds LLM annotators show no systematic demographic disagreement; biases are dataset-specific and shared across GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.3, and Gemini rather than model-specific.

articles.title: Evaluating how LLM annotations represent diverse views on contentious topics
articles.authors: Megan A. J. Brown et al.
articles.tldr: LLM annotation bias on subjective tasks is dataset-specific, and item difficulty predicts agreement far more than annotator demographics.
articles.contribution: Shows label entropy (item difficulty) is by far the strongest predictor of LLM-annotator agreement and must be explicitly modeled before attributing demographic bias.

articles.title: Do ImageNet-trained models learn shortcuts? The impact of frequency shortcuts on generalization
articles.tldr: ImageNet-trained CNNs and transformers learn frequency shortcuts that current OOD benchmarks fail to account for.
articles.contribution: Introduces HFSS to uncover frequency shortcuts at ImageNet scale, showing both CNNs and ViTs can classify shortcut classes from ~5% of the spectrum (texture-aligned frequencies).

articles.title: Do ImageNet-trained models learn shortcuts? The impact of frequency shortcuts on generalization
articles.tldr: ImageNet-trained CNNs and transformers learn frequency shortcuts that current OOD benchmarks fail to account for.
articles.contribution: Shows frequency shortcuts inflate accuracy on texture-preserving OOD sets (IN-C, IN-v2, FGSM) but harm rendition sets (IN-R/IN-S), so current OOD benchmarks misjudge true generalization.

articles.title: Rethinking Human Evaluation Protocol for Text-to-Video Models: Enhancing Reliability, Reproducibility, and Practicality
articles.tldr: T2VHE is a standardized human-evaluation protocol that improves the reliability, reproducibility, and cost of text-to-video assessment.
articles.contribution: Introduces well-defined metrics with explicit reference perspectives plus annotator training that raises non-expert inter-annotator agreement close to paid AMT-Master levels.

articles.title: Rethinking Human Evaluation Protocol for Text-to-Video Models: Enhancing Reliability, Reproducibility, and Practicality
articles.tldr: T2VHE is a standardized human-evaluation protocol that improves the reliability, reproducibility, and cost of text-to-video assessment.
articles.contribution: Replaces biased win-ratio ranking with the Rao-Kupper pairwise model plus a dynamic evaluation module, cutting annotation cost ~50% while stabilizing model rankings.

articles.title: ScratchEval : A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for LLMs in Block-Based Programming
articles.tldr: ScratchEval is an executable, reproducible benchmark for LLM Scratch repair with explicit construct-validity analysis.
articles.contribution: Enforces reproducible evaluation via deterministic VM execution, fixed RNG seeds, rerun-stabilized differential oracles, and paired McNemar significance tests on repair outcomes.

articles.title: ScratchEval : A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for LLMs in Block-Based Programming
articles.tldr: ScratchEval is an executable, reproducible benchmark for LLM Scratch repair with explicit construct-validity analysis.
articles.contribution: Argues functional pass/fail under a finite test suite is construct-incomplete, augmenting correctness with block-level edit distance and behavioral-trajectory drift to catch near-miss patches.

articles.title: ScratchEval : A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for LLMs in Block-Based Programming
articles.tldr: ScratchEval is an executable, reproducible benchmark for LLM Scratch repair with explicit construct-validity analysis.
articles.contribution: Calibrates its rubric-guided LLM judge of explanation quality against two human annotators, reporting 85% agreement and Cohen's kappa=0.74 (95% CI [0.50, 0.90]).

articles.title: OpenGenAlign: A Preference Dataset and Benchmark for Trustworthy Reward Modeling in Open-Ended, Long-Context Generation
articles.tldr: OpenGenAlign benchmarks reward models for open-ended long-context generation and shows RewardBench scores do not transfer.
articles.contribution: Builds a 33K preference set labeled by o3 with three-way majority voting over four quality metrics, validated at 81% human agreement across QA, Data-to-Text, and Summarization.

articles.title: OpenGenAlign: A Preference Dataset and Benchmark for Trustworthy Reward Modeling in Open-Ended, Long-Context Generation
articles.tldr: OpenGenAlign benchmarks reward models for open-ended long-context generation and shows RewardBench scores do not transfer.
articles.contribution: Shows top RewardBench reward models (~90%) drop below 80% on long-context OpenGenAlign, and high RewardBench scores fail to predict long-context evaluation performance.

articles.title: Who can we trust? LLM-as-a-jury for Comparative Assessment
articles.tldr: BT-sigma models per-judge reliability to aggregate inconsistent LLM comparative judgments without human labels.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses that LLM pairwise comparison probabilities violate transitivity and commutativity (positional bias), so probability calibration alone cannot recover reliable rankings.

articles.title: Who can we trust? LLM-as-a-jury for Comparative Assessment
articles.tldr: BT-sigma models per-judge reliability to aggregate inconsistent LLM comparative judgments without human labels.
articles.contribution: Introduces BT-sigma, a judge-aware Bradley-Terry extension whose learned discriminators downweight noisy judges, beating averaging and supervised temperature scaling without human labels.

articles.title: Fact or Fiction? Can LLMs be Reliable Annotators for Political Truths?
articles.tldr: Open-source LLMs can annotate political factuality reliably, judged by multiple LLM-as-judges against human gold labels.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks five open LLM annotators for binary political factuality against human-verified gold labels, with three-reviewer human oversight resolving majority-vote discrepancies.

articles.title: Fact or Fiction? Can LLMs be Reliable Annotators for Political Truths?
articles.tldr: Open-source LLMs can annotate political factuality reliably, judged by multiple LLM-as-judges against human gold labels.
articles.contribution: Uses two LLM judges (GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-70B) to avoid self-enhancement bias, showing judge agreement rates diverge and both fall short of ground-truth agreement.

articles.title: LoViF 2026 The First Challenge on Holistic Quality Assessment for 4D World Model (PhyScore)
articles.tldr: Challenge on holistic quality metrics for world-model videos, since perceptual metrics miss physics violations, with reliably human-annotated labels.
articles.contribution: Argues perceptual video-quality metrics under-represent the construct because they miss physical-plausibility violations; requires metrics that jointly predict physical realism, temporal consistency and condition alignment plus anomaly localization.

articles.title: LoViF 2026 The First Challenge on Holistic Quality Assessment for 4D World Model (PhyScore)
articles.tldr: Challenge on holistic quality metrics for world-model videos, since perceptual metrics miss physics violations, with reliably human-annotated labels.
articles.contribution: Secures label reliability of the quality scores and anomaly timestamps through trained human annotation plus an additional automated quality-control pass.

articles.title: SWE-QA-Pro: A Representative Benchmark and Scalable Training Recipe for Repository-Level Code Understanding
articles.tldr: Repository-level code-understanding benchmark that filters memorization-solvable questions and flags LLM-judge reward hacking in its training recipe.
articles.contribution: Difficulty calibration filters out questions answerable from memorized pretraining knowledge (via a no-tool direct-answer baseline) so the benchmark isolates questions requiring genuine codebase interaction rather than recall on popular repos.

articles.title: SWE-QA-Pro: A Representative Benchmark and Scalable Training Recipe for Repository-Level Code Understanding
articles.tldr: Repository-level code-understanding benchmark that filters memorization-solvable questions and flags LLM-judge reward hacking in its training recipe.
articles.contribution: Identifies that its RLAIF reward shares the LLM-as-Judge distribution with the evaluation metric, creating reward-hacking risk, and mitigates it with a judge distinct from the eval judge plus correctness up-weighting.

articles.title: The Creative Psychometric Item Generator: a Framework for Item Generation and Validation Using Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Psychometric framework using LLMs to auto-generate valid and reliable creativity test items, with a length-confound check on the originality metric.
articles.contribution: Builds a psychometrically grounded creative-problem-solving item generator (CPIG) whose generated items are shown to be as valid as human-written items, operationalizing the creativity construct via iteratively selected exemplars.

articles.title: The Creative Psychometric Item Generator: a Framework for Item Generation and Validation Using Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Psychometric framework using LLMs to auto-generate valid and reliable creativity test items, with a length-confound check on the originality metric.
articles.contribution: Tests that the rising originality scores are not a response-length artifact by correlating response length with the originality metric, defending the internal validity of the item-quality signal.

articles.title: Evaluating the Limits of Large Language Models in Multilingual Legal Reasoning
articles.tldr: Multilingual legal-reasoning evaluation of LLaMA/Gemini emphasizing run-to-run stability, prompt sensitivity, adversarial robustness and cross-lingual external validity.
articles.contribution: Quantifies measurement instability of LLM legal-reasoning scores via variance/entropy across repeated runs and prompt sensitivity, using an LLM-as-a-Judge for human-aligned scoring of open-ended answers.

articles.title: Evaluating the Limits of Large Language Models in Multilingual Legal Reasoning
articles.tldr: Multilingual legal-reasoning evaluation of LLaMA/Gemini emphasizing run-to-run stability, prompt sensitivity, adversarial robustness and cross-lingual external validity.
articles.contribution: Shows English-centric evaluation does not generalize across the 15 languages, with performance rising as a language becomes more syntactically similar to English, undermining external validity of English-only legal benchmarks.

articles.title: Leveraging Vision-Language Models to Select Trustworthy Super-Resolution Samples Generated by Diffusion Models
articles.tldr: Uses VLMs to select trustworthy diffusion super-resolution samples, showing PSNR/LPIPS fail information fidelity and proposing a human-validated Trustworthiness Score.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/DISTS fail to reflect information trustworthiness of super-resolved images and proposes the hybrid TWS (CLIP semantic + edge-SSIM + wavelet-artifact) validated to correlate with human preference.

articles.title: Leveraging Vision-Language Models to Select Trustworthy Super-Resolution Samples Generated by Diffusion Models
articles.tldr: Uses VLMs to select trustworthy diffusion super-resolution samples, showing PSNR/LPIPS fail information fidelity and proposing a human-validated Trustworthiness Score.
articles.contribution: Runs a prompt-robustness analysis with 20 semantically-equivalent prompts per axis to measure VLM selection consistency and its agreement with human preferences as a scorer-reliability check.

articles.title: WoundAmbit: Bridging State-of-the-Art Semantic Segmentation and Real-World Wound Care
articles.tldr: Fair, standardized benchmark of wound-segmentation models using cross-validation, out-of-distribution evaluation and physician-validated masks.
articles.contribution: Standardizes training, data augmentation and evaluation and uses cross-validation to minimize partitioning bias, so the model ranking reflects architecture rather than differing training setups.

articles.title: WoundAmbit: Bridging State-of-the-Art Semantic Segmentation and Real-World Wound Care
articles.tldr: Fair, standardized benchmark of wound-segmentation models using cross-validation, out-of-distribution evaluation and physician-validated masks.
articles.contribution: Assesses generalization to a held-out out-of-distribution wound dataset as an external-validity check, finding transformer-based TransNeXt generalizes best.

articles.title: ManipArena: Comprehensive Real-world Evaluation of Reasoning-Oriented Generalist Robot Manipulation
articles.tldr: Standardized real-world robot-manipulation evaluation that bridges sim-to-real, isolates visual confounders, separates train/test, and enforces fair reproducible protocol.
articles.contribution: Argues simulator-centric benchmarks fail to predict real-world performance and provides standardized real-robot evaluation (with synchronized real2sim) to close the reality-gap external-validity failure.

articles.title: ManipArena: Comprehensive Real-world Evaluation of Reasoning-Oriented Generalist Robot Manipulation
articles.tldr: Standardized real-world robot-manipulation evaluation that bridges sim-to-real, isolates visual confounders, separates train/test, and enforces fair reproducible protocol.
articles.contribution: A green-screen fixed-lighting enclosure isolates visual variables so cross-trial performance differences are attributable to designed object/spatial changes rather than lighting or background confounders.

articles.title: ManipArena: Comprehensive Real-world Evaluation of Reasoning-Oriented Generalist Robot Manipulation
articles.tldr: Standardized real-world robot-manipulation evaluation that bridges sim-to-real, isolates visual confounders, separates train/test, and enforces fair reproducible protocol.
articles.contribution: Server-side inference on identical hardware, a one-model-for-all-tasks rule and a relocatable booth enable fair and reproducible cross-platform comparison, eliminating hardware/latency advantages and fragmented-platform unfairness.

articles.title: ManipArena: Comprehensive Real-world Evaluation of Reasoning-Oriented Generalist Robot Manipulation
articles.tldr: Standardized real-world robot-manipulation evaluation that bridges sim-to-real, isolates visual confounders, separates train/test, and enforces fair reproducible protocol.
articles.contribution: Enforces strict train/test object separation plus a designed uniform-diversity training distribution so high OOD scores require genuine generalization rather than memorization of training instances.

articles.title: Trust Your Critic: Robust Reward Modeling and Reinforcement Learning for Faithful Image Editing and Generation
articles.tldr: Builds robust reward-model critics for image editing/generation, benchmarks them against human judgment, and analyzes reward hacking.
articles.contribution: Shows zero-shot MLLM critics assign hallucinated/noisy reward scores and trains FIRM reward models validated for alignment with human judgment on the human-annotated FIRM-Bench for editing and generation critics.

articles.title: Trust Your Critic: Robust Reward Modeling and Reinforcement Learning for Faithful Image Editing and Generation
articles.tldr: Builds robust reward-model critics for image editing/generation, benchmarks them against human judgment, and analyzes reward hacking.
articles.contribution: Analyzes reward-function hacking and formulates a Base-and-Bonus reward (Consistency-Modulated Execution for editing, Quality-Modulated Alignment for generation) to balance competing objectives against degenerate optimization.

articles.title: Rethinking Multilingual Vision-Language Translation: Dataset, Evaluation, and Adaptation
articles.tldr: Rethinks multilingual vision-language-translation evaluation, exposing unreliable references and context-dependent metric instability, proposing human-verified data and density-aware scoring.
articles.contribution: Shows existing 'human-annotated' VLT datasets carry OCR errors and semantically-flat or culturally-misaligned reference translations, and introduces the human-verified, OCR-corrected AibTrans dataset to restore ground-truth quality.

articles.title: Rethinking Multilingual Vision-Language Translation: Dataset, Evaluation, and Adaptation
articles.tldr: Rethinks multilingual vision-language-translation evaluation, exposing unreliable references and context-dependent metric instability, proposing human-verified data and density-aware scoring.
articles.contribution: Shows BLEU/BERTScore/COMET behave inconsistently with sentence length and text-region count so naive averaging misranks models, and proposes a Density-Aware (DA) Score for context-sensitive aggregation.

articles.title: Singing Timbre Popularity Assessment Based on Multimodal Large Foundation Model
articles.tldr: Reference-free multi-dimensional singing assessment that shows expert annotation disagreement invalidates accuracy metrics and proposes a perceptual-ranking benchmark instead.
articles.contribution: Quantifies severe inter-expert disagreement on singing quality (exact agreement <45% across four dimensions), arguing a single 'ground-truth' score is a statistical fiction that invalidates MAE/accuracy metrics.

articles.title: Singing Timbre Popularity Assessment Based on Multimodal Large Foundation Model
articles.tldr: Reference-free multi-dimensional singing assessment that shows expert annotation disagreement invalidates accuracy metrics and proposes a perceptual-ranking benchmark instead.
articles.contribution: Proposes H-TPR (Human-in-the-loop Tiered Perceptual Ranking) as a construct-valid evaluation that judges perceptual rank-consistency rather than matching a noisy scalar score.

articles.title: Singing Timbre Popularity Assessment Based on Multimodal Large Foundation Model
articles.tldr: Reference-free multi-dimensional singing assessment that shows expert annotation disagreement invalidates accuracy metrics and proposes a perceptual-ranking benchmark instead.
articles.contribution: Identifies a 'label-input mismatch' (30s clip input vs full-song label) that forces models to learn spurious correlations, and uses rule-based pre-screening to remove pitch/rhythm confounds from timbre judgement.

articles.title: Ice Cream Doesn't Cause Drowning: Benchmarking LLMs Against Statistical Pitfalls in Causal Inference
articles.tldr: CausalPitfalls benchmark rigorously measures the reliability of LLM statistical causal inference across six pitfall categories with rubric grading and a human-validated judge.
articles.contribution: Quantifies LLM susceptibility to confounding and spurious-association pitfalls (Simpson's paradox, selection bias, branding-driven conclusions), exposing large causal-inference reliability gaps even in frontier models.

articles.title: Ice Cream Doesn't Cause Drowning: Benchmarking LLMs Against Statistical Pitfalls in Causal Inference
articles.tldr: CausalPitfalls benchmark rigorously measures the reliability of LLM statistical causal inference across six pitfall categories with rubric grading and a human-validated judge.
articles.contribution: Validates its automated GPT-4o rubric grader against three human statisticians on 150 stratified responses (mean gap 0.11) to justify scalable, reproducible scoring of causal reasoning.

articles.title: Ice Cream Doesn't Cause Drowning: Benchmarking LLMs Against Statistical Pitfalls in Causal Inference
articles.tldr: CausalPitfalls benchmark rigorously measures the reliability of LLM statistical causal inference across six pitfall categories with rubric grading and a human-validated judge.
articles.contribution: Shows models are weakest on the external-validity/transportability and mediation categories and collapse on hint-free 'very hard' items, indicating causal conclusions do not generalize across contexts.

articles.title: Toward Robust LLM-Based Judges: Taxonomic Bias Evaluation and Debiasing Optimization
articles.tldr: JudgeBiasBench systematically quantifies 12 task-irrelevant biases in generative and discriminative LLM judges and proposes bias-aware debiasing training.
articles.contribution: Introduces the Bias Sensitivity Rate metric and a controlled bias-injection pipeline to quantify 12 bias types across both generative and discriminative judges, distinguishing judgment bias from judgment error.

articles.title: Toward Robust LLM-Based Judges: Taxonomic Bias Evaluation and Debiasing Optimization
articles.tldr: JudgeBiasBench systematically quantifies 12 task-irrelevant biases in generative and discriminative LLM judges and proposes bias-aware debiasing training.
articles.contribution: Argues biased judges used as reward models emit spurious, exploitable reward signals (reward hacking) and shows bias-aware RL/contrastive training reduces this while preserving general evaluation ability.

articles.title: Toward Robust LLM-Based Judges: Taxonomic Bias Evaluation and Debiasing Optimization
articles.tldr: JudgeBiasBench systematically quantifies 12 task-irrelevant biases in generative and discriminative LLM judges and proposes bias-aware debiasing training.
articles.contribution: Finds discriminative reward-model judges are more vulnerable to gender and race identity cues than generative judges, raising fairness/safety concerns for alignment pipelines that rely on them.

articles.title: JE-IRT: A Geometric Lens on LLM Abilities through Joint Embedding Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: JE-IRT is a geometric joint-embedding item-response framework showing a single scalar LLM ability score is invalid, with embedding norm encoding difficulty and direction encoding semantics.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that compressing LLM abilities into a single scalar score violates the global-ordering assumption of traditional IRT and misrepresents inherently multidimensional, specialized capability.

articles.title: JE-IRT: A Geometric Lens on LLM Abilities through Joint Embedding Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: JE-IRT is a geometric joint-embedding item-response framework showing a single scalar LLM ability score is invalid, with embedding norm encoding difficulty and direction encoding semantics.
articles.contribution: Shows directional alignment in the learned embedding space is a diagnostic for out-of-distribution generalization: benchmarks probing ability directions weakly covered by training data (e.g. MMLU) fail to transfer.

articles.title: Quantifying the Statistical Effect of Rubric Modifications on Human-Autorater Agreement
articles.tldr: A statistical study of how rubric modifications (examples, decomposition, aggregation, positional bias) shift human-autorater agreement in essay scoring and instruction following.
articles.contribution: Shows with bootstrapped Kendall's tau that adding representative examples plus context and reducing positional/confirmation bias significantly raises human-autorater agreement, while higher rubric complexity lowers it.

articles.title: Quantifying the Statistical Effect of Rubric Modifications on Human-Autorater Agreement
articles.tldr: A statistical study of how rubric modifications (examples, decomposition, aggregation, positional bias) shift human-autorater agreement in essay scoring and instruction following.
articles.contribution: Finds decomposing holistic into analytic rubrics does not consistently improve agreement because conservative aggregation (Pareto dominance / yes-no ratio) and higher human inter-rater disagreement drag agreement down.

articles.title: DREAM: Deep Research Evaluation with Agentic Metrics
articles.tldr: Argues deep-research evaluators suffer a 'Mirage of Synthesis' and capability mismatch, and makes evaluation itself agentic (DREAM) to detect factual/temporal/reasoning defects static judges miss.
articles.contribution: Names the 'Mirage of Synthesis': fluent, well-cited deep-research reports score high on existing benchmarks despite factual/reasoning defects, i.e. surface fluency and citation alignment act as construct-invalid proxies for research quality.

articles.title: DREAM: Deep Research Evaluation with Agentic Metrics
articles.tldr: Argues deep-research evaluators suffer a 'Mirage of Synthesis' and capability mismatch, and makes evaluation itself agentic (DREAM) to detect factual/temporal/reasoning defects static judges miss.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses an evaluator 'capability mismatch': static LLM-judges lack retrieval/tool-use and temporal context needed to verify the very claims they score, and proposes capability-parity agentic evaluators (KIC, RQ, Factuality) routed to the simplest evaluator that closes the gap.

articles.title: DREAM: Deep Research Evaluation with Agentic Metrics
articles.tldr: Argues deep-research evaluators suffer a 'Mirage of Synthesis' and capability mismatch, and makes evaluation itself agentic (DREAM) to detect factual/temporal/reasoning defects static judges miss.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory/falsification evidence an evaluation is valid via controlled sensitivity studies (temporal-cutoff report variants, injected reasoning flaws, and a factual-corruption sweep) showing DREAM metrics degrade with degradation while DRB-RACE/FACT stay flat.

articles.title: SHALE: A Scalable Benchmark for Fine-grained Hallucination Evaluation in LVLMs
articles.tldr: Builds SHALE, an automated synthetic LVLM hallucination benchmark that reduces data leakage and adds input perturbations to probe faithfulness/factuality reliability.
articles.contribution: Argues benchmarks reusing public datasets (e.g. MSCOCO) risk train/test leakage, builds an automated synthetic text-to-image generation pipeline, and quantifies leakage with Multimodal Gain/Leakage (MG/ML), reporting SHALE has the lowest ML and highest MG vs POPE/AMBER/SEED.

articles.title: SHALE: A Scalable Benchmark for Fine-grained Hallucination Evaluation in LVLMs
articles.tldr: Builds SHALE, an automated synthetic LVLM hallucination benchmark that reduces data leakage and adds input perturbations to probe faithfulness/factuality reliability.
articles.contribution: Hierarchical induction framework (image/instruction/combination perturbations) reveals language-prior shortcuts confound hallucination scores — misleading prefixes and scene-text injection collapse many LVLMs toward random guessing, showing scores depend on ungrounded priors rather than visual evidence.

articles.title: URAG: A Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces URAG, reformulating RAG QA into MCQA to apply conformal prediction, jointly measuring accuracy and calibrated uncertainty across 8 RAG methods and 5 domains.
articles.contribution: Applies conformal prediction (LAC and APS nonconformity scores) over MCQA-reformulated tasks to produce distribution-free prediction sets with a 1−α coverage guarantee, using average set size as a principled uncertainty metric that entropy-based scores cannot match.
