articles.title: URAG: A Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces URAG, reformulating RAG QA into MCQA to apply conformal prediction, jointly measuring accuracy and calibrated uncertainty across 8 RAG methods and 5 domains.
articles.contribution: Designs an NLI-filtered iterative distractor-generation pipeline enforcing that distractors are factually wrong, plausible, same-type and entailment-confusable, preventing models from exploiting superficial lexical/semantic cues that would trivialize the MCQA measurement.

articles.title: NOAH: Benchmarking Narrative Prior driven Hallucination and Omission in Video Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Identifies 'narrative prior' as a confound driving Video-LLM hallucination and omission, and builds NOAH with controlled composite videos to isolate and measure it.
articles.contribution: Isolates the 'narrative prior' confound by inserting event clips at 3 positions × 3 similarity levels into target videos (9,000 composites), so observed hallucinations/omissions can be attributed to storyline-coherence bias rather than visual input, holding original content fixed.

articles.title: NOAH: Benchmarking Narrative Prior driven Hallucination and Omission in Video Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Identifies 'narrative prior' as a confound driving Video-LLM hallucination and omission, and builds NOAH with controlled composite videos to isolate and measure it.
articles.contribution: Uses a GAVIE-inspired LLM-judge to parse captions into events and compute caption/event-level hallucination and omission rates, and validates scorer reliability by showing GPT-4o and Gemini judge scores agree at Pearson/Spearman >0.95.

articles.title: INFELM: In-depth Fairness Evaluation of Large Text-To-Image Models
articles.tldr: INFELM improves text-to-image fairness evaluation by fixing inaccurate pixel-based skintone classification and separating representation bias from content-alignment error.
articles.contribution: Shows prior fairness audits' pixel-detection skintone classifiers are inaccurate (uneven Monk-scale color spans, illumination, annotation subjectivity) and builds a fused facial-topology + dominant-pixel-distribution classifier that raises precision ≥16.04%, making the downstream fairness measurement reliable.

articles.title: INFELM: In-depth Fairness Evaluation of Large Text-To-Image Models
articles.tldr: INFELM improves text-to-image fairness evaluation by fixing inaccurate pixel-based skintone classification and separating representation bias from content-alignment error.
articles.contribution: Argues fairness measured only as demographic representation is an incomplete construct and adds content-alignment error (whether generated demographics match the prompt) as an indispensable second dimension, applying a four-fifth-rule threshold across 6 bias-sensitive domains.

articles.title: Prediction-Powered Inference Across Many Tasks for AI Evaluation&Social Science Research
articles.tldr: Introduces multi-task prediction-powered inference (GRePPI/ARePPI) that borrows cross-task structure to tighten confidence intervals under scarce labels while keeping per-task statistical validity.
articles.contribution: Proposes cross-task recalibrated PPI that learns a nonlinear proxy-to-ground-truth map from related tasks to cut confidence-interval width and variance in the sparse-label regime, proving (Corollary 3.2) improvement over the identity surrogate requires nonlinear structure since affine recalibration leaves oracle variance unchanged.

articles.title: Prediction-Powered Inference Across Many Tasks for AI Evaluation&Social Science Research
articles.tldr: Introduces multi-task prediction-powered inference (GRePPI/ARePPI) that borrows cross-task structure to tighten confidence intervals under scarce labels while keeping per-task statistical validity.
articles.contribution: Frames AI evaluation as inference with abundant biased LLM-judge proxies and a handful of expensive human ground-truth labels, using within-task rectification/power-tuning to debias the proxy so scarce annotations still yield valid task-level estimates.

articles.title: ATime-Consistent Benchmark for Repository-Level Software Engineering Evaluation
articles.tldr: A time-consistent, matched A/B benchmark protocol for repository-aware SWE agents that controls temporal contamination and prompt leakage to causally isolate repository-knowledge effects.
articles.contribution: Enforces temporal consistency by snapshotting a repo at T0, building knowledge only from pre-T0 artifacts, and drawing tasks from PRs merged in (T0,T1], explicitly excluding post-T0 diffs/reviews/tests from the admissible knowledge boundary to block look-ahead contamination.

articles.title: ATime-Consistent Benchmark for Repository-Level Software Engineering Evaluation
articles.tldr: A time-consistent, matched A/B benchmark protocol for repository-aware SWE agents that controls temporal contamination and prompt leakage to causally isolate repository-knowledge effects.
articles.contribution: Formalizes a matched A/B design holding model, prompt, snapshot, execution environment and metric fixed so the only variable is repository-derived code knowledge, enabling estimation of its marginal causal contribution rather than a confounded aggregate score.

articles.title: ATime-Consistent Benchmark for Repository-Level Software Engineering Evaluation
articles.tldr: A time-consistent, matched A/B benchmark protocol for repository-aware SWE agents that controls temporal contamination and prompt leakage to causally isolate repository-knowledge effects.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates prompt-generation granularity is a first-order benchmark variable: overly guided prompts leak the fix direction and inflate baseline scores, so prompt construction must be standardized and Contextual prompting is the most defensible operating point.

articles.title: OODBench: Out-of-Distribution Benchmark for Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: OODBench constructs a covariate-shift out-of-distribution benchmark for VLMs using generalized OOD detectors, exposing large external-validity gaps that standard in-distribution benchmarks hide.
articles.contribution: Argues existing VLM benchmarks only test in-distribution data and therefore overstate generalization, and builds an instance-level covariate-shift OOD benchmark showing 20-30% accuracy degradation to measure real-world external validity under distribution shift.

articles.title: OODBench: Out-of-Distribution Benchmark for Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: OODBench constructs a covariate-shift out-of-distribution benchmark for VLMs using generalized OOD detectors, exposing large external-validity gaps that standard in-distribution benchmarks hide.
articles.contribution: Proposes an automated OOD sampling pipeline that 'purifies' logits and cross-validates CLIP∩BLIP2 failure-detection to select representative covariate-shift instances (OOD-Hard vs OOD-Simple) with minimal human effort, avoiding rare-category convenience sampling.

articles.title: The Paradox of Robustness: Decoupling Rule-Based Logic from Affective Noise in High-Stakes Decision-Making
articles.tldr: Rigorously measures LLM sensitivity to emotional narrative framing in rule-bound decisions, using length-matched controls, construct-validity ablations and a full statistical framework to establish a near-zero effect.
articles.contribution: Introduces a controlled perturbation framework that isolates affective narrative from length and information confounds via length-matched neutral controls (within 10%) and an evidence-modification positive control (82.2% pass), so the measured null reflects genuine robustness not output rigidity.

articles.title: The Paradox of Robustness: Decoupling Rule-Based Logic from Affective Noise in High-Stakes Decision-Making
articles.tldr: Rigorously measures LLM sensitivity to emotional narrative framing in rule-bound decisions, using length-matched controls, construct-validity ablations and a full statistical framework to establish a near-zero effect.
articles.contribution: Runs seven ablations (instruction, construct-validity, schema, adversarial-override, base-model) to test whether measured robustness reflects genuine capability versus a methodological artifact of instruction-following, defining 'narrative vulnerability' distinctly from sycophancy and prompt sensitivity.

articles.title: The Paradox of Robustness: Decoupling Rule-Based Logic from Affective Noise in High-Stakes Decision-Making
articles.tldr: Rigorously measures LLM sensitivity to emotional narrative framing in rule-bound decisions, using length-matched controls, construct-validity ablations and a full statistical framework to establish a near-zero effect.
articles.contribution: Establishes the effect is practically zero (not merely undetected) using BCa bootstrap CIs (B=2000), Bayes factors, a calibrated ±3% Region of Practical Equivalence, and Minimum-Detectable-Effect power analysis, and releases a replicable 162-prompt benchmark.

articles.title: From Guidelines to Guarantees: A Graph-Based Evaluation Harness for Domain-Specific Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: A graph-based evaluation harness turns clinical guidelines into a knowledge graph and dynamically instantiates MCQA queries, giving coverage guarantees, contamination resistance and expert-inherited validity.
articles.contribution: Provides surface-form contamination resistance by dynamically generating MCQA at evaluation time via graph traversal with randomized ages, distractors and templates, and supports relationship-level/versioned probing by regenerating from updated guidelines that postdate training.

articles.title: From Guidelines to Guarantees: A Graph-Based Evaluation Harness for Domain-Specific Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: A graph-based evaluation harness turns clinical guidelines into a knowledge graph and dynamically instantiates MCQA queries, giving coverage guarantees, contamination resistance and expert-inherited validity.
articles.contribution: Template ablation shows question phrasing shifts accuracy independently of the tested clinical relationship (e.g. cond_followup_t1 14-57% vs cond_symp_t3 50-90%), so averaging over multiple templates is needed to avoid phrasing artifacts contaminating capability estimates.

articles.title: From Guidelines to Guarantees: A Graph-Based Evaluation Harness for Domain-Specific Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: A graph-based evaluation harness turns clinical guidelines into a knowledge graph and dynamically instantiates MCQA queries, giving coverage guarantees, contamination resistance and expert-inherited validity.
articles.contribution: Guarantees complete coverage of all encoded guideline relationships via graph traversal (200+ nodes, 300+ edges), overcoming the incomplete, convenience-curated coverage of static medical benchmarks, with validity inherited from the expert-authored graph.

articles.title: Mitigating Judgment Preference Bias in Large Language Models through Group-Based Polling
articles.tldr: Diagnoses LLM-as-a-judge self-preference bias with the HSPP metric and mitigates it via unsupervised multi-agent group-based polling (Genii) that curates DPO preference pairs.
articles.contribution: Quantifies judgment preference bias with Harmful Self-Preference Propensity (HSPP) — the rate a judge selects its own incorrect answer over another model's correct one — and mitigates it via unsupervised group-polling DPO, also validating robustness to position bias.

articles.title: QEDBENCH: Quantifying the Alignment Gap in Automated Evaluation of University-Level Mathematical Proofs
articles.tldr: QEDBench is a dual-rubric benchmark quantifying the alignment gap of LLM-as-a-Judge on university-level math proofs, exposing systematic judge positive bias and a discrete-domain reasoning gap.
articles.contribution: Quantifies systematic positive bias (score inflation) of frontier LLM judges on proof grading via a 7-judge x 5-solver dual-evaluation matrix against 1,000+ hours of human expert evaluation.

articles.title: QEDBENCH: Quantifying the Alignment Gap in Automated Evaluation of University-Level Mathematical Proofs
articles.tldr: QEDBench is a dual-rubric benchmark quantifying the alignment gap of LLM-as-a-Judge on university-level math proofs, exposing systematic judge positive bias and a discrete-domain reasoning gap.
articles.contribution: Uses a dual-rubric design (course-specific rubrics vs expert common-knowledge criteria) to separate what a proof-grading judge actually measures from pedagogical/knowledge-gap confounds in discrete domains.

articles.title: Learning an Efficient Multi-Turn Dialogue Evaluator from Multiple Judges
articles.tldr: MTDEval distills the collective preference knowledge of multiple LLM judges into one dialogue evaluator, modeling per-judge reliability to mitigate single-judge biases while removing multi-judge inference overhead.
articles.contribution: Targets the reliability/consistency failures of single LLM-as-a-judge dialogue evaluation caused by self-preference, position, and length biases, distilling multi-judge feedback into one evaluator.

articles.title: Learning an Efficient Multi-Turn Dialogue Evaluator from Multiple Judges
articles.tldr: MTDEval distills the collective preference knowledge of multiple LLM judges into one dialogue evaluator, modeling per-judge reliability to mitigate single-judge biases while removing multi-judge inference overhead.
articles.contribution: Aggregates preference knowledge from multiple LLM judges by modeling the reliability of each judge (rater-effects weighting) rather than a plain majority vote of judgments.

articles.title: Rubrics as an Attack Surface: Stealthy Preference Drift in LLM Judges
articles.tldr: Identifies Rubric-Induced Preference Drift (RIPD): benchmark-compliant rubric edits stealthily shift LLM-judge preferences on target domains, can be weaponized as attacks, and propagate through alignment pipelines into trained policies.
articles.contribution: Shows rubric-based preference attacks with benchmark-compliant edits steer judgments away from a trusted reference, reducing target-domain accuracy by up to 9.5% (helpfulness) and 27.9% (harmlessness).

articles.title: Rubrics as an Attack Surface: Stealthy Preference Drift in LLM Judges
articles.tldr: Identifies Rubric-Induced Preference Drift (RIPD): benchmark-compliant rubric edits stealthily shift LLM-judge preferences on target domains, can be weaponized as attacks, and propagate through alignment pipelines into trained policies.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that passing rubric benchmark validation does not guarantee target-domain preference validity: criterion-preserving edits induce directional drift undetectable by aggregate benchmark metrics or limited spot-checking.

articles.title: Rubrics as an Attack Surface: Stealthy Preference Drift in LLM Judges
articles.tldr: Identifies Rubric-Induced Preference Drift (RIPD): benchmark-compliant rubric edits stealthily shift LLM-judge preferences on target domains, can be weaponized as attacks, and propagate through alignment pipelines into trained policies.
articles.contribution: Traces how RIPD-biased judge labels used for downstream post-training propagate through the alignment pipeline and become internalized as persistent, systematic drift in trained policy behavior.

articles.title: Thinking in Groups: Permutation Tests Reveal Near-Out-of-Distribution
articles.tldr: HOoD reframes near-OoD detection for correlated biomedical data as group-wise permutation hypothesis testing, yielding interpretable p-values and outperforming point-wise and ensemble detectors on hard near-distribution inputs.
articles.contribution: Because models trained on biased/incomplete non-IID data face near-OoD inputs at deployment, HOoD tests whether a group of correlated replicates matches known subpopulations via permutation-based p-values to flag when predictions are untrustworthy.

articles.title: Thinking in Groups: Permutation Tests Reveal Near-Out-of-Distribution
articles.tldr: HOoD reframes near-OoD detection for correlated biomedical data as group-wise permutation hypothesis testing, yielding interpretable p-values and outperforming point-wise and ensemble detectors on hard near-distribution inputs.
articles.contribution: Shows point-wise and ensemble OoD scores are unreliable in the near-OoD regime, whereas aggregating group-level permutation p-values gives a statistically grounded, calibrated OoD signal.

articles.title: Exploring the Feasibility of LLMs for Automated Music Emotion Annotation
articles.tldr: Assesses GPT-4o as a music-emotion annotator versus three human experts on GiantMIDI-Piano, finding GPT less accurate/nuanced but with inter-rater variability within the range of natural human disagreement.
articles.contribution: Evaluates the reliability of GPT-4o as a scalable annotator against three human experts using standard accuracy, inter-expert-weighted accuracy, inter-annotator agreement, and label distributional similarity.

articles.title: Exploring the Feasibility of LLMs for Automated Music Emotion Annotation
articles.tldr: Assesses GPT-4o as a music-emotion annotator versus three human experts on GiantMIDI-Piano, finding GPT less accurate/nuanced but with inter-rater variability within the range of natural human disagreement.
articles.contribution: Finds GPT annotations less nuanced in categorizing specific emotional states within the four-quadrant valence-arousal framework, a construct-coverage limitation of the automated annotator.

articles.title: SCISSOR: Mitigating Semantic Bias through Cluster-Aware Siamese Networks for Robust Classification
articles.tldr: SCISSOR shows imbalances in the semantic distribution of sample embeddings (not just superficial features) induce spurious shortcut correlations, and a Siamese cluster-intervention remaps the space to improve OOD robustness without data augmentation.
articles.contribution: Attributes shortcut learning to imbalance in the semantic distribution of embeddings that induces spurious semantic correlations, with Lemma 3.1 upper-bounding classifier output change by representation-space distance.

articles.title: SCISSOR: Mitigating Semantic Bias through Cluster-Aware Siamese Networks for Robust Classification
articles.tldr: SCISSOR shows imbalances in the semantic distribution of sample embeddings (not just superficial features) induce spurious shortcut correlations, and a Siamese cluster-intervention remaps the space to improve OOD robustness without data augmentation.
articles.contribution: Suppressing latent clusters exploited as shortcuts improves OOD F1 by +7.7 (Chest-XRay), +5.3 (GYAFC), +7.3 (Yelp), and +1 (Not-MNIST) without any data augmentation or rewriting.

articles.title: DAJ: Data-Reweighted LLM Judge for Test-Time Scaling in Code Generation
articles.tldr: DAJ trains a reasoning-based LLM judge for Best-of-N code selection under distribution shift using bi-level data reweighting that learns importance weights to optimize generalization on a target-aligned meta set.
articles.contribution: Identifies three distribution shifts that make Best-of-N LLM judges unreliable: easy/hard problem imbalance, train-task vs evaluation-benchmark mismatch, and trajectory mismatch from training data generated by cheaper models.

articles.title: DAJ: Data-Reweighted LLM Judge for Test-Time Scaling in Code Generation
articles.tldr: DAJ trains a reasoning-based LLM judge for Best-of-N code selection under distribution shift using bi-level data reweighting that learns importance weights to optimize generalization on a target-aligned meta set.
articles.contribution: Uses a bi-level data-reweighted framework that learns domain-level or instance-level importance weights to optimize judge generalization on a held-out meta set aligned with target benchmarks.

articles.title: Benchmark for Uncertainty & Robustness in Self-Supervised Learning
articles.tldr: Builds a reliability benchmark evaluating self-supervised methods on both generalization (in/out accuracy) and uncertainty (expected calibration error) across covariate-shift datasets, with reproducible baseline code.
articles.contribution: Argues SSL reliability must be judged by uncertainty as well as accuracy, using expected calibration error (ECE) and NLL and requiring low ECE on both in-data and out-of-data distributions to call a model reliable.

articles.title: Benchmark for Uncertainty & Robustness in Self-Supervised Learning
articles.tldr: Builds a reliability benchmark evaluating self-supervised methods on both generalization (in/out accuracy) and uncertainty (expected calibration error) across covariate-shift datasets, with reproducible baseline code.
articles.contribution: Evaluates SSL variants (Jigsaw, Context, Rotation, Geometric Transformations, BERT/GPT) under covariate shift on MNIST-C, CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-10.1, and MNLI, releasing reproducible code to compare robustness.

articles.title: HackerSignal: A Large-Scale Multi-Source Dataset Linking Hacker Community Discourse to the CVE Vulnerability Lifecycle
articles.tldr: HackerSignal is a temporal-OoD cyber-threat-intelligence benchmark enforcing prospective CVE-disjoint splits and releasing leakage/source-shortcut diagnostics and manual-audit packets to guard against memorization-inflated scores.
articles.contribution: Enforces prospective CVE-disjoint train/test splits (C_train and C_test disjoint) and ships source-shortcut and leakage diagnostics plus manual-audit packets so benchmark scores are not inflated by memorization or cross-source leakage.

articles.title: HackerSignal: A Large-Scale Multi-Source Dataset Linking Hacker Community Discourse to the CVE Vulnerability Lifecycle
articles.tldr: HackerSignal is a temporal-OoD cyber-threat-intelligence benchmark enforcing prospective CVE-disjoint splits and releasing leakage/source-shortcut diagnostics and manual-audit packets to guard against memorization-inflated scores.
articles.contribution: Uses temporal splits across a 36-year (1990-2026) window to evaluate prospective generalization on CVE linkage retrieval, 8-class exploit-type classification, and temporal generalization tasks.

articles.title: Bidirectional regression for monocular 6DoF head pose estimation and reference system alignment
articles.tldr: Alongside the TRGv2 head-pose method, identifies inconsistent cross-dataset head-center definitions as an overlooked evaluation bias and proposes a reference-system alignment that corrects the translation offset for fair cross-dataset comparison.
articles.contribution: Identifies inconsistent head-center definitions across 6DoF datasets as a previously overlooked construct-definition confound that biases translation evaluation, the first work to systematically define this domain-misalignment problem.

articles.title: Bidirectional regression for monocular 6DoF head pose estimation and reference system alignment
articles.tldr: Alongside the TRGv2 head-pose method, identifies inconsistent cross-dataset head-center definitions as an overlooked evaluation bias and proposes a reference-system alignment that corrects the translation offset for fair cross-dataset comparison.
articles.contribution: Proposes a reference-system alignment that computes the head-center offset between mesh structures and applies it as a correction term during evaluation, enabling fair cross-dataset comparison and surfacing methods undervalued by annotation mismatch.

articles.title: GetNetUPAM: Ecologically Informed Nested Cross-Validation and Noise-Robust Attention for Marine Bioacoustic Monitoring
articles.tldr: Nested site-year cross-validation framework that exposes deployment failure modes and shortcut learning masked by single-split bioacoustic benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Shows random-subset cross-validation inflates UPAM detector performance because train/test folds share site- and year-specific noise traits; site-year-blocked nested CV enforces strict development/evaluation separation to estimate deployment-condition generalization.

articles.title: GetNetUPAM: Ecologically Informed Nested Cross-Validation and Noise-Robust Attention for Marine Bioacoustic Monitoring
articles.tldr: Nested site-year cross-validation framework that exposes deployment failure modes and shortcut learning masked by single-split bioacoustic benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates standard CNNs on 60s windows exploit global, non-biological cues (noise floors, hydrophone coloration) as shortcuts rather than call structure, and that CBAM spatial attention suppresses these confounds, evidenced by embedding and saliency analysis.

articles.title: GetNetUPAM: Ecologically Informed Nested Cross-Validation and Noise-Robust Attention for Marine Bioacoustic Monitoring
articles.tldr: Nested site-year cross-validation framework that exposes deployment failure modes and shortcut learning masked by single-split bioacoustic benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Uses the nested inner loop to report fold-level standard deviation as a stability profile instead of a single inflated hold-out score, surfacing variance that scalar leaderboard metrics obscure.

articles.title: Challenges in Deep Learning-Based Small Organ Segmentation: A Benchmarking Perspective for Medical Research with Limited Datasets
articles.tldr: Systematic study showing deep-learning segmentation benchmarks in low-data medical settings are unstable, with rankings driven by statistical noise and CV-protocol choice rather than algorithmic superiority.
articles.contribution: Uses 10,000-sample bootstrap 95% CIs, Friedman and Nemenyi post-hoc tests, and Cohen's d to show that fine-grained rankings among top models are statistically indistinguishable despite significant omnibus tests, i.e. differences are statistical noise.

articles.title: Challenges in Deep Learning-Based Small Organ Segmentation: A Benchmarking Perspective for Medical Research with Limited Datasets
articles.tldr: Systematic study showing deep-learning segmentation benchmarks in low-data medical settings are unstable, with rankings driven by statistical noise and CV-protocol choice rather than algorithmic superiority.
articles.contribution: Shows model rankings flip between LOOCV and 3-fold CV and are highly sensitive to data splits at N=9, so leaderboard rankings are not a fair or reproducible basis for model selection in low-data regimes.

articles.title: Challenges in Deep Learning-Based Small Organ Segmentation: A Benchmarking Perspective for Medical Research with Limited Datasets
articles.tldr: Systematic study showing deep-learning segmentation benchmarks in low-data medical settings are unstable, with rankings driven by statistical noise and CV-protocol choice rather than algorithmic superiority.
articles.contribution: Evaluation on an independent OOD dataset (N=153) shows ranking inversions under distribution shift, with foundation models maintaining performance while classical CNNs fail, so in-distribution metrics overstate clinical/deployment utility.

articles.title: BELDE: Building a Large-scale Earth-observation Land-cover Dataset for Europe
articles.tldr: Continental-scale RGB land-cover dataset released with two geographically distinct OOD extensions to quantify external validity under cross-region domain shift.
articles.contribution: Constructs controlled out-of-distribution benchmarks (Korea, California-Nevada) demonstrating that in-domain segmentation performance does not transfer across continents and that geographic variability, not model capacity, is the dominant limiting factor for cross-region generalization.

articles.title: Predictive Representativity: Uncovering Racial Bias in AI-based Skin Cancer Detection
articles.tldr: Fairness-auditing framework (Predictive Representativity) showing that dataset input-representativity fails to guarantee equitable predictive performance across skin tones.
articles.contribution: Argues that dataset 'representativity' defined by matching input population proportions is an inadequate construct for predictive fairness under conditional prediction, and redefines representativity at the level of predictive outputs (Predictive Representativity).

articles.title: Predictive Representativity: Uncovering Racial Bias in AI-based Skin Cancer Detection
articles.tldr: Fairness-auditing framework (Predictive Representativity) showing that dataset input-representativity fails to guarantee equitable predictive performance across skin tones.
articles.contribution: Empirically audits five CNNs trained on HAM10000 against an independent Colombian BOSQUE test set and formalizes an External Transportability Criterion for when fairness generalizes to new subpopulations and deployment contexts.

articles.title: Faithful Model Evaluation for Model-Based Metrics
articles.tldr: Derives significance testing for model-based metrics that propagates the metric model's own prediction errors into sample variance, changing evaluation conclusions.
articles.contribution: Establishes that when a metric model (e.g. a toxicity classifier) scores outputs, its prediction errors must be folded into the sample variance, deriving the true-positive variance from the metric model's precision and false-omission rate.

articles.title: Faithful Model Evaluation for Model-Based Metrics
articles.tldr: Derives significance testing for model-based metrics that propagates the metric model's own prediction errors into sample variance, changing evaluation conclusions.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that ignoring metric-model error understates variance and produces false-positive significance, and that incorporating it flips the significance conclusion on real benchmark and production experiments.

articles.title: Magnitude Matters: a Superior Class of Similarity Metrics for Holistic Semantic Understanding
articles.tldr: Argues cosine similarity is an unreliable semantic-similarity scorer under embedding anisotropy and proposes parameter-free magnitude-aware alternatives.
articles.contribution: Shows cosine similarity discards vector magnitude and, under anisotropy/representation collapse, assigns high similarity to semantically unrelated sentences, misrepresenting semantic relatedness; proposes Overlap Similarity and Hyperbolic Tangent Similarity as more valid parameter-free scorers.

articles.title: Rate, Explain and Cite (REC): Enhanced Explanation and Attribution in Automatic Evaluation by Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Fine-tuned LLM auto-evaluators (REC-8B/12B/70B) that add verifiable citation and reduced bias to automatic content-quality evaluation.
articles.contribution: Builds general-purpose LLM auto-evaluators that rate faithfulness/instruction-following/coherence/completeness with reduced bias (assessed on the CoBBLEr cognitive-bias benchmark), improving the reliability of LLM-as-judge content evaluation.

articles.title: Rate, Explain and Cite (REC): Enhanced Explanation and Attribution in Automatic Evaluation by Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Fine-tuned LLM auto-evaluators (REC-8B/12B/70B) that add verifiable citation and reduced bias to automatic content-quality evaluation.
articles.contribution: Attaches verifiable verbatim citation/attribution as confirmatory evidence for each judgment and shows that SOTA baseline judges produce inaccurate citation that undermines their evaluation reliability.

articles.title: VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning
articles.tldr: Witness-adjudicator reward that gives reliable, Goodhart-resistant fact-level supervision for visual captioning and is validated against human factual judgments.
articles.contribution: Designs a frozen-MLLM reward that pairs a reference caption (witness) with the image (adjudicator) to verify factual consistency, providing fine-grained correctness and completeness signals that existing captioning rewards fail to deliver reliably.

articles.title: VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning
articles.tldr: Witness-adjudicator reward that gives reliable, Goodhart-resistant fact-level supervision for visual captioning and is validated against human factual judgments.
articles.contribution: Provides a closed-form hypergeometric analysis showing the reward's optimum lies at the image-information ceiling independent of reference size, so weak/imperfect references still steer toward correctness rather than collapsing into imitation of a possibly-flawed target.

articles.title: Towards Fair Rankings: Leveraging LLMs for Gender Bias Detection and Measurement
articles.tldr: Shows lexical gender-fairness metrics miss subtle bias, proposes an LLM-based detector and the CWEx exposure metric validated against human labels.
articles.contribution: Shows existing lexical/term-based gender-fairness metrics under-represent the bias construct, mislabeling passages with mixed gendered phrases (e.g. 'his mother', 'her son') as neutral, and proposes Class-wise Weighted Exposure (CWEx) as a more faithful ranking-fairness metric.

articles.title: Towards Fair Rankings: Leveraging LLMs for Gender Bias Detection and Measurement
articles.tldr: Shows lexical gender-fairness metrics miss subtle bias, proposes an LLM-based detector and the CWEx exposure metric validated against human labels.
articles.contribution: Validates an LLM-based gender-bias detector against human annotations, showing improved agreement over lexical metrics and enabling three-way neutral/male/female classification for evaluating bias in ranked lists.

articles.title: Towards More Accurate Personalized Image Generation: Addressing Overfitting and Evaluation Bias
articles.tldr: Shows personalized-image-generation evaluation on the training data overestimates performance, and curates PDST with a held-out split test set for unbiased automatic metrics.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses that computing CLIP text-image and DINO image-image similarity on the personalization training images inflates scores; introduces PDST with a separate test split to remove this train/test overlap.

articles.title: Towards More Accurate Personalized Image Generation: Addressing Overfitting and Evaluation Bias
articles.tldr: Shows personalized-image-generation evaluation on the training data overestimates performance, and curates PDST with a held-out split test set for unbiased automatic metrics.
articles.contribution: Curates a diverse, well-prompted dedicated test set so automatic metrics assess generalization to new prompts rather than fidelity to the memorized training subject.

articles.title: CreativityPrism: A Holistic Evaluation Framework for Large Language Model Creativity
articles.tldr: Holistic LLM-creativity benchmark showing that single-metric creativity scores misrepresent the construct because creativity dimensions rarely correlate.
articles.contribution: Consolidates creativity into three dimensions (quality, novelty, diversity) across 8 tasks / 3 domains, and shows novelty metrics have weak or negative correlations with the others so any single-metric creativity score misrepresents the construct.

articles.title: CreativityPrism: A Holistic Evaluation Framework for Large Language Model Creativity
articles.tldr: Holistic LLM-creativity benchmark showing that single-metric creativity scores misrepresent the construct because creativity dimensions rarely correlate.
articles.contribution: Validates every automatic LLM judge with two requirements before use: human inter-annotator agreement (task well-defined) and a Calderon-et-al. replaceability test that the LLM judge can substitute for human annotators.

articles.title: Reconstructing Item Characteristic Curves using Fine-Tuned Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Fine-tunes LLMs to simulate student responses and reconstruct Item Characteristic Curves, estimating IRT difficulty/discrimination without expensive field testing.
articles.contribution: Reconstructs synthetic ICCs from LLM-simulated responses conditioned on ability descriptors to estimate IRT item parameters, quantifying agreement (Pearson/RMSE) with field-calibrated parameters as a reliability check on the instrument.

articles.title: Human- vs. AI-generated tests: dimensionality and information accuracy in latent trait evaluation
articles.tldr: Compares two ChatGPT-adapted questionnaires with a validated human test via a Bayesian Graded Response Model; reliability is similar but dimensionality and item/test information differ.
articles.contribution: Shows AI-generated questionnaires with similar surface wording yield a non-trivial/different dimensional structure vs the validated BAQ, so surface similarity and high reliability do not guarantee the intended construct is measured.

articles.title: Human- vs. AI-generated tests: dimensionality and information accuracy in latent trait evaluation
articles.tldr: Compares two ChatGPT-adapted questionnaires with a validated human test via a Bayesian Graded Response Model; reliability is similar but dimensionality and item/test information differ.
articles.contribution: Uses IRT item/test information functions to reveal that AI-generated items distribute measurement accuracy differently across the latent trait and lack co-monotonicity with the human test, despite comparable reliability indices.

articles.title: Designing Psychometric Bias Measures for ChatBots: An Application to Racial Bias Measurement
articles.tldr: Introduces STAMP-LLM, a principled two-phase psychometric protocol for designing and validating bias measures for chatbots, illustrated on racial bias.
articles.contribution: The Definitional phase performs construct mapping, item development and expert review so that chatbot 'bias' is theory-grounded and mapped before any measure is built.

articles.title: Designing Psychometric Bias Measures for ChatBots: An Application to Racial Bias Measurement
articles.tldr: Introduces STAMP-LLM, a principled two-phase psychometric protocol for designing and validating bias measures for chatbots, illustrated on racial bias.
articles.contribution: The Data/Analysis phase adds protocol control (prompts/decoding), automated sampling, pre-specified scoring and reliability/validity checks, demonstrated on racial bias with one explicit and two implicit measures.

articles.title: When Correct Isn't Usable: Improving Structured Output Reliability in Small Language Models
articles.tldr: Reveals a structured-output reliability gap in small LMs (high task accuracy but 0% usable JSON-valid output) and shows an LLM prompt-optimizer closes it.
articles.contribution: Defines 'output accuracy' (joint math-correctness AND valid JSON structure) and shows raw task accuracy misrepresents deployable performance: NAIVE prompting hits 85% task accuracy on GSM8K but 0% output accuracy across all models.

articles.title: When Correct Isn't Usable: Improving Structured Output Reliability in Small Language Models
articles.tldr: Reveals a structured-output reliability gap in small LMs (high task accuracy but 0% usable JSON-valid output) and shows an LLM prompt-optimizer closes it.
articles.contribution: Quantifies scoring reliability with 29/30 paired McNemar comparisons significant at p<0.05 over five runs, plus an ablation showing meta-agent capability drives run-to-run std from <1pp to 21.8pp.

articles.title: Towards Characterizing Scientific Image Utility and Upgradability
articles.tldr: Shows perceptual-quality metrics poorly correlate with scientific validity of images and proposes SIU2A utility/upgradability evaluation with expert annotations.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates perceptual quality metrics (appearance) poorly correlate with scientific validity, so they misrepresent the construct of scientific image correctness; proposes Utility (error detection + correction feasibility) and Upgradability dimensions instead.

articles.title: Towards Characterizing Scientific Image Utility and Upgradability
articles.tldr: Shows perceptual-quality metrics poorly correlate with scientific validity of images and proposes SIU2A utility/upgradability evaluation with expert annotations.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-as-judge lacks domain-specific verification for scientific images and builds SIU2A-Benchmark with expert annotations over four corruption types (Detail Distortion, Incompleteness, False Content, Entity Confusion) as ground truth for a two-stage protocol.

articles.title: Self-Evolving Deep Research via Joint Generation and Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues static evaluators for open-ended deep-research reports saturate optimization pressure and invite reward hacking, and proposes a co-evolving evaluator-solver framework.
articles.contribution: Identifies that static LLM-judge/rubric rewards for ground-truth-free deep-research reports are unverifiable and gameable: decoupled Plan-and-Execute agents show premature collapse and severe reward hacking versus step-by-step ReAct policies.

articles.title: Self-Evolving Deep Research via Joint Generation and Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues static evaluators for open-ended deep-research reports saturate optimization pressure and invite reward hacking, and proposes a co-evolving evaluator-solver framework.
articles.contribution: Shows static evaluators cannot adapt as the solver improves, saturating optimization pressure over training (temporal drift), and adds a meta-harness that dynamically controls the evaluation environment by solver performance to keep evaluation valid.

articles.title: CoreCodeBench: Decoupling Code Intelligence via Fine-Grained Repository-Level Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows coarse pass-rate code benchmarks obscure cognitive bottlenecks and are prone to contamination/saturation, and introduces a fine-grained, difficulty-scalable repo-level benchmark.
articles.contribution: Argues coarse-grained pass rates treat programming as a monolithic capability and obscure specific cognitive bottlenecks; atomized tasks isolate distinct cognitive demands within identical code contexts.

articles.title: CoreCodeBench: Decoupling Code Intelligence via Fine-Grained Repository-Level Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows coarse pass-rate code benchmarks obscure cognitive bottlenecks and are prone to contamination/saturation, and introduces a fine-grained, difficulty-scalable repo-level benchmark.
articles.contribution: Addresses static-benchmark vulnerability to data contamination and performance saturation via controllable difficulty scaling and better data quality, reporting a 78.55% validity yield vs SWE-bench-Verified's 31.7% retention.

articles.title: CoreCodeBench: Decoupling Code Intelligence via Fine-Grained Repository-Level Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows coarse pass-rate code benchmarks obscure cognitive bottlenecks and are prone to contamination/saturation, and introduces a fine-grained, difficulty-scalable repo-level benchmark.
articles.contribution: Shows significant capability misalignment (distinct model ranking shifts across cognitive dimensions), evidence that a single aggregated pass-rate ranking misrepresents non-monolithic coding proficiency.

articles.title: Disentangling Visual and Factual Correctness in LVLMs'Visualization Literacy
articles.tldr: Existing visualization-literacy tests conflate genuine visual reasoning with memorized factual priors; a counterfactual test and reliance index disentangle them.
articles.contribution: Shows standard VLAT scores are confounded by memorized factual priors rather than genuine visual reasoning, while randomized-data reVLAT instead underestimates literacy when correct visual interpretation conflicts with priors.

articles.title: Disentangling Visual and Factual Correctness in LVLMs'Visualization Literacy
articles.tldr: Existing visualization-literacy tests conflate genuine visual reasoning with memorized factual priors; a counterfactual test and reliance index disentangle them.
articles.contribution: Introduces CVLAT counterfactual items plus capability-normalized arbitration and a visual-factual reliance index (VFRI), with an N=30 human baseline, as falsification evidence separating visual from factual correctness.

articles.title: Reliability of Large Language Models for Design Synthesis: An Empirical Study of Variance, Prompt Sensitivity, and Method Scaffolding
articles.tldr: Empirical study of LLM reliability/variance in UML design synthesis, proposing a Stability Index as a first-class evaluation criterion alongside correctness.
articles.contribution: Quantifies run-to-run and paraphrase non-determinism of LLM design synthesis via a Stability Index, showing model choice dominates measured reliability.

articles.title: Reliability of Large Language Models for Design Synthesis: An Empirical Study of Variance, Prompt Sensitivity, and Method Scaffolding
articles.tldr: Empirical study of LLM reliability/variance in UML design synthesis, proposing a Stability Index as a first-class evaluation criterion alongside correctness.
articles.contribution: Argues syntactic diagram validity under-represents true design-synthesis quality (abstraction, design patterns), exposing a construct gap between diagram translation and design.

articles.title: The CompMath-MCQ Dataset: Are LLMs Ready for Higher-Level Math?
articles.tldr: CompMath-MCQ, a leakage-free graduate-math MCQ benchmark with two-stage item validation and deterministic log-likelihood scoring for objective, reproducible LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Guarantees leakage-free evaluation by authoring all 1,500 graduate-math questions originally rather than sourcing them from public materials in LLM training corpora.

articles.title: The CompMath-MCQ Dataset: Are LLMs Ready for Higher-Level Math?
articles.tldr: CompMath-MCQ, a leakage-free graduate-math MCQ benchmark with two-stage item validation and deterministic log-likelihood scoring for objective, reproducible LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Two-stage validation using cross-LLM disagreement statistics (per-item error rate, wrong-answer consensus, binomial anomaly test) plus expert review to remove mislabeled/ambiguous items.

articles.title: The CompMath-MCQ Dataset: Are LLMs Ready for Higher-Level Math?
articles.tldr: CompMath-MCQ, a leakage-free graduate-math MCQ benchmark with two-stage item validation and deterministic log-likelihood scoring for objective, reproducible LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Length-normalized log-likelihood ranking gives deterministic, reproducible MCQ scoring free of answer-parsing failures, decoding stochasticity, and option-order/length bias.

articles.title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Reliable and Explainable Offline Evaluation in Top-K Recommendation
articles.tldr: Shows offline Top-K recommendation metrics are unreliable under missing-not-at-random feedback and proposes an LLM-as-a-Judge semantic proxy that recovers unbiased model rankings.
articles.contribution: Identifies missing-not-at-random item exposure as the bias that makes holdout Top-K metrics deviate from the true-preference gold standard, replacing rigid ID matching with a semantic proxy.

articles.title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Reliable and Explainable Offline Evaluation in Top-K Recommendation
articles.tldr: Shows offline Top-K recommendation metrics are unreliable under missing-not-at-random feedback and proposes an LLM-as-a-Judge semantic proxy that recovers unbiased model rankings.
articles.contribution: Validates the LLM judge as a reliable evaluation instrument, recovering unbiased model rankings (Pearson up to ~87.6%) where standard offline testing fails.

articles.title: Reliability Gated Multi-Teacher Distillation for Low Resource Abstractive Summarization
articles.tldr: A reliability-gated multi-teacher distillation paper whose in-scope contribution is a human-validated multi-judge protocol exposing systematic calibration bias in single-LLM-judge summarization evaluation.
articles.contribution: Human-validated multi-judge protocol quantifies single-judge LLM calibration bias (GPT-5.2 systematic positive/faithfulness bias), motivating multi-judge summarization evaluation.

articles.title: LexInstructEval: Lexical Instruction Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: LexInstructEval, a rule-based programmatic benchmark for fine-grained lexical instruction following that replaces biased LLM-judge scoring with a deterministic verifier validated against human experts.
articles.contribution: Replaces biased/unreliable LLM-judge scoring with a transparent deterministic verification engine validated at 97% agreement with human experts.

articles.title: LexInstructEval: Lexical Instruction Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: LexInstructEval, a rule-based programmatic benchmark for fine-grained lexical instruction following that replaces biased LLM-judge scoring with a deterministic verifier validated against human experts.
articles.contribution: A formal (Procedure, Relation, Value) grammar enables fine-grained compositional lexical constraints beyond IFEval's expressiveness, avoiding format-leak shortcut cues.

articles.title: Evaluating Cross-Modal Reasoning Ability and Problem Characteristics with Multimodal Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: M3IRT decomposes multimodal item-response ability and difficulty into image, text, and cross-modal components to detect shortcut questions and produce reliable, contamination-robust MLLM rankings.
articles.contribution: Detects single-modality shortcut questions that break cross-modal construct validity by decomposing item difficulty into image-only, text-only, and cross-modal terms.

articles.title: Evaluating Cross-Modal Reasoning Ability and Problem Characteristics with Multimodal Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: M3IRT decomposes multimodal item-response ability and difficulty into image, text, and cross-modal components to detect shortcut questions and produce reliable, contamination-robust MLLM rankings.
articles.contribution: IRT-based subset selection stays robust to 50% low-quality/shortcut item contamination, preserving ranking fidelity with as little as 1-10% of items.

articles.title: Enhancing Classifier Evaluation: A Fairer Benchmarking Strategy Based on Ability and Robustness
articles.tldr: Combines Item Response Theory with the Glicko-2 rating system for fairer classifier benchmarking that accounts for dataset difficulty and flags low-quality benchmark datasets.
articles.contribution: Shows aggregate accuracy misrepresents ability by ignoring instance difficulty, and derives difficulty-aware, order-consistent classifier rankings via IRT True-Score plus Glicko-2.

articles.title: Enhancing Classifier Evaluation: A Fairer Benchmarking Strategy Based on Ability and Robustness
articles.tldr: Combines Item Response Theory with the Glicko-2 rating system for fairer classifier benchmarking that accounts for dataset difficulty and flags low-quality benchmark datasets.
articles.contribution: Uses IRT to reveal that most OpenML-CC18 datasets are non-challenging and that negative-discrimination datasets are inconsistent, enabling a 50% subset with comparable evaluation power.

articles.title: Automatic Design of Optimization Test Problems with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: EoTF uses LLM-driven evolution to auto-generate interpretable optimization test functions matching target ELA features, closing benchmark coverage gaps and mitigating benchmark contamination.
articles.contribution: Generates functions matching target ELA feature vectors to close the coverage gap in BBOB/CEC suites that biases black-box-optimizer evaluation.

articles.title: Automatic Design of Optimization Test Problems with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: EoTF uses LLM-driven evolution to auto-generate interpretable optimization test functions matching target ELA features, closing benchmark coverage gaps and mitigating benchmark contamination.
articles.contribution: Addresses benchmark memorization by generating novel MA-BBOB-hybrid targets and verifying via manual inspection that generated code does not recall known BBOB functions.

articles.title: CEI: A Benchmark for Evaluating Pragmatic Reasoning in Language Models
articles.tldr: CEI benchmark for pragmatic reasoning that treats deliberately low inter-annotator agreement as informative and uses a multi-level QC pipeline to build human-validated ambiguous-inference items.
articles.contribution: Documents low inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss kappa 0.06-0.25) as informative signal for ambiguous items and defines a 4-level QC pipeline for pragmatic-inference annotation.

articles.title: CEI: A Benchmark for Evaluating Pragmatic Reasoning in Language Models
articles.tldr: CEI benchmark for pragmatic reasoning that treats deliberately low inter-annotator agreement as informative and uses a multi-level QC pipeline to build human-validated ambiguous-inference items.
articles.contribution: Grounds a pragmatic-inference construct (5 subtypes x power relations) while acknowledging that multiple valid readings undermine any single-label ground truth.

articles.title: LiveFact: A Dynamic, Time-Aware Benchmark for LLM-Driven Fake News Detection
articles.tldr: LiveFact is a continuously-updated, time-aware fake-news benchmark that mitigates benchmark data contamination and uses dual-mode temporal evidence slices to measure reasoning under uncertainty rather than memorization.
articles.contribution: Combats benchmark data contamination with monthly-updated unseen news events plus a Semantic Sensitivity Amplifier entity-shift mechanism that explicitly monitors BDC risk.

articles.title: LiveFact: A Dynamic, Time-Aware Benchmark for LLM-Driven Fake News Detection
articles.tldr: LiveFact is a continuously-updated, time-aware fake-news benchmark that mitigates benchmark data contamination and uses dual-mode temporal evidence slices to measure reasoning under uncertainty rather than memorization.
articles.contribution: Introduces time-sliced evidence sets (pre/at/post-event) to test reasoning under temporal uncertainty and validates temporal robustness across monthly benchmark versions.

articles.title: LiveFact: A Dynamic, Time-Aware Benchmark for LLM-Driven Fake News Detection
articles.tldr: LiveFact is a continuously-updated, time-aware fake-news benchmark that mitigates benchmark data contamination and uses dual-mode temporal evidence slices to measure reasoning under uncertainty rather than memorization.
articles.contribution: Dual-mode evaluation with an 'Ambiguous' class shows binary accuracy misrepresents verification ability, exposing an alignment-tax 'Reasoning Gap' from over-caution and safety refusals.

articles.title: Training Data Size Sensitivity in Unsupervised Rhyme Recognition
articles.tldr: Establishes human inter-annotator agreement as the realistic ceiling for rhyme recognition and shows one-shot LLMs fail for lacking phonetic representation.
articles.contribution: Argues the appropriate benchmark for machine rhyme recognition is human inter-annotator agreement rather than an overfit single gold annotator, and models annotator (dis)agreement with a Bayesian mixed-effects logistic regression stratified by corpus.

articles.title: Training Data Size Sensitivity in Unsupervised Rhyme Recognition
articles.tldr: Establishes human inter-annotator agreement as the realistic ceiling for rhyme recognition and shows one-shot LLMs fail for lacking phonetic representation.
articles.contribution: Shows one-shot LLM rhyme recognizers latch onto orthographic/graphemic surface endings (a proxy) instead of phonetics, missing phonetically-identical rhymes (praise:days) and chaining orthographically-similar non-rhymes.

articles.title: CURE: Controlled Unlearning for Robust Embeddings - Mitigating Conceptual Shortcuts in Pre-Trained Language Models
articles.tldr: Diagnoses conceptual shortcuts (e.g. food->positive) as a confounding threat to text classifiers and quantifies/controls concept-bias impact on OOD robustness.
articles.contribution: Quantifies concept->label bias via mutual information and builds biased i.i.d. vs concept-balanced OOD splits to show PLMs latch onto conceptual shortcuts, then remaps the semantic space to controllably suppress or exploit those shortcuts.

articles.title: CURE: Controlled Unlearning for Robust Embeddings - Mitigating Conceptual Shortcuts in Pre-Trained Language Models
articles.tldr: Diagnoses conceptual shortcuts (e.g. food->positive) as a confounding threat to text classifiers and quantifies/controls concept-bias impact on OOD robustness.
articles.contribution: Validates the GPT-4o concept annotations used as ground truth with a 7-rater human study, confirming label quality before the concept labels drive the biased/OOD benchmark construction.

articles.title: From Static Risk to Dynamic Trajectories: Toward World-Model-Inspired Clinical Prediction
articles.tldr: Review arguing clinical trajectory models must target causal estimands under time-varying confounding, not predictive accuracy, and validate with decision-grade / target-trial designs.
articles.contribution: Frames treatment-confounder feedback (time-varying confounding) as a structural threat: high predictive accuracy on logged care data can coexist with systematically biased treatment-effect estimates unless g-methods and overlap/positivity diagnostics are used.

articles.title: From Static Risk to Dynamic Trajectories: Toward World-Model-Inspired Clinical Prediction
articles.tldr: Review arguing clinical trajectory models must target causal estimands under time-varying confounding, not predictive accuracy, and validate with decision-grade / target-trial designs.
articles.contribution: Advocates aligning claim strength with intended clinical use via target-trial-aligned validation, off-policy evaluation, and transport/overlap diagnostics, warning against benchmark-prediction claims that ignore external/criterion validity.

articles.title: Colosseum V2: Benchmarking Generalization for Vision Language Action Models
articles.tldr: VLA generalization benchmark showing strong base performance does not imply robustness, and that simulation predicts real-world relative degradation (ecological validity).
articles.contribution: Validates the ecological validity of the simulation benchmark: absolute success rates do not transfer to hardware, but relative per-perturbation degradation does (average R^2=0.798, Spearman 0.916 across three real tasks).

articles.title: Colosseum V2: Benchmarking Generalization for Vision Language Action Models
articles.tldr: VLA generalization benchmark showing strong base performance does not imply robustness, and that simulation predicts real-world relative degradation (ecological validity).
articles.contribution: Introduces a 28-task, 13-category, 16-perturbation benchmark isolating visual/language/action generalization, demonstrating that strong in-distribution success masks large generalization gaps and enabling reproducible, fair comparison.

articles.title: Revitalizing Dense Material Segmentation: Stabilized Vision Transformers and the Generalization Paradox
articles.tldr: Shows a data-rich IID re-split inflates material-segmentation mIoU while degrading real-world OOD performance, a benchmark 'Generalization Paradox'.
articles.contribution: Documents a Generalization Paradox where an 80/10/10 IID re-split raises SegFormer-B5 to 0.5276 mIoU (vs 0.4572 on the rigorous 54/23/23 split) yet experts judge the higher-scoring model worse on out-of-distribution real images.

articles.title: Revitalizing Dense Material Segmentation: Stabilized Vision Transformers and the Generalization Paradox
articles.tldr: Shows a data-rich IID re-split inflates material-segmentation mIoU while degrading real-world OOD performance, a benchmark 'Generalization Paradox'.
articles.contribution: Attributes the inflated metric to distributional homogenization: the IID-split model exploits dataset-level priors (lighting, scene type, photographic style) instead of robust material cues, e.g. misclassifying polished stone as glass under glare.

articles.title: Stylized Meta-Album: Group-bias injection with style transfer to study robustness against distribution shifts
articles.tldr: A style-transfer meta-dataset (4800 groups) whose group diversity flips fairness-algorithm rankings, yielding a Top-M worst-group tuning metric and tighter UDA error bars.
articles.contribution: Shows the relative rankings and superiority of group-robustness algorithms change as configurable group diversity K increases, so low-diversity benchmarks yield misleading algorithm comparisons; proposes Top-M worst-group accuracy as a fairer selection metric.

articles.title: Stylized Meta-Album: Group-bias injection with style transfer to study robustness against distribution shifts
articles.tldr: A style-transfer meta-dataset (4800 groups) whose group diversity flips fairness-algorithm rankings, yielding a Top-M worst-group tuning metric and tighter UDA error bars.
articles.contribution: Its unsupervised-domain-adaptation benchmark leverages large group diversity to reduce evaluation error bars by 73% (closed-set) and 28% (UniDA), enabling more statistically reliable UDA algorithm comparison.

articles.title: ACWM-Phys: Investigating Generalized Physical Interaction in Action-Conditioned Video World Models
articles.tldr: A physically-diverse benchmark for action-conditioned world models showing OoD generalization tracks task complexity and that models capture appearance statistics, not physics.
articles.contribution: Uses controlled, exactly-reproducible InD/OoD splits across 8 environments and 4 physics regimes to measure the generalization gap, showing OoD degradation tracks task complexity and that models rely on visual appearance statistics rather than internalized physics.

articles.title: ACWM-Phys: Investigating Generalized Physical Interaction in Action-Conditioned Video World Models
articles.tldr: A physically-diverse benchmark for action-conditioned world models showing OoD generalization tracks task complexity and that models capture appearance statistics, not physics.
articles.contribution: Introduces Masked-MSE (motion-weighted MSE) because standard MSE is dominated by static backgrounds and under-emphasizes physically-meaningful prediction failures, e.g. Cloth Move's high M-MSE (63.68) is invisible in raw MSE.

articles.title: Mat-Pref: Verifiable-Reward Training Improves Compositional Reasoning in Inorganic Materials

articles.title: Mat-Pref: Verifiable-Reward Training Improves Compositional Reasoning in Inorganic Materials
articles.authors: S. R. M. Leung et al.
articles.tldr: A DFT-grounded materials benchmark that decomposes generalization (structural/property/memorization) and scores by distractor-permutation consistency to expose surface-cue gaming.
articles.contribution: Decomposes generalization with three orthogonal DFT-grounded splits (IID, entirely held-out structure families, and cross-property band-gap transfer) to isolate structural transfer, property transfer, and memorization.

articles.title: Rethinking Molecular OOD Generalization via Target-Aware Source Selection

articles.title: Rethinking Molecular OOD Generalization via Target-Aware Source Selection

articles.title: Towards Reliable Domain Generalization: A New Dataset and Evaluations

articles.contribution: Shows the standard leave-one-domain-out DG protocol yields unstable method rankings that reverse under different training-domain choices, and proposes Domain+ and swap-test (ST) criteria for more reliable comparison.

articles.title: Towards Reliable Domain Generalization: A New Dataset and Evaluations

articles.contribution: Demonstrates DG models exploit pixel-statistic shortcuts rather than character structure: printed-to-handwritten accuracy collapses on grayscale but recovers after binarization, exposing a spurious-feature confound.

articles.title: Evaluating and Improving the Robustness of Speech Command Recognition Models to Noise and Distribution Shifts
articles.tldr: Tests whether the accuracy-on-the-line ID-OOD correlation holds for speech command recognition and flags noise-seen test leakage.

articles.title: Evaluating and Improving the Robustness of Speech Command Recognition Models to Noise and Distribution Shifts

articles.tldr: Benchmarks LLM intent-to-transaction generation and shows exact-match metrics badly underestimate functional correctness versus execution-based state analysis.

articles.tldr: A multi-stage framework to validate large-scale LLM clinical extraction under weak supervision using judge-LLM confirmation and predictive validity.

articles.title: A Multi-Stage Validation Framework for Trustworthy Large-scale Clinical Information Extraction using Large Language Models
articles.tldr: A multi-stage framework to validate large-scale LLM clinical extraction under weak supervision using judge-LLM confirmation and predictive validity.

articles.title: Non-Linear Scoring Model for Translation Quality Evaluation

articles.title: Non-Linear Scoring Model for Translation Quality Evaluation
articles.tldr: Length-dependent non-linear (logarithmic) MQM tolerance model that fixes linear scoring's systematic over/under-penalization across translation sample sizes.
articles.contribution: Argues micro-range (<250 word) scoring is statistically unstable (relative uncertainty ~1/sqrt(np), Wald/Wilson CIs) and that the calibrated tolerance function improves inter-rater reliability by removing length-induced disagreement.

articles.title: Semantic Reward Collapse and the Preservation of Epistemic Integrity in Adaptive AI Systems
articles.tldr: Position/theory framework arguing scalarized RLHF reward collapses distinct evaluative categories (Semantic Reward Collapse), proposing partitioned Constitutional Reward Stratification to protect uncertainty disclosure.
articles.contribution: Frames Semantic Reward Collapse — compression of semantically distinct dissatisfaction categories into a single scalar reward R(x,y)=Σ w_i f_i — as a Goodhart-style proxy-collapse mechanism that pressures models toward suppressing visible epistemic failure.

articles.title: Semantic Reward Collapse and the Preservation of Epistemic Integrity in Adaptive AI Systems
articles.tldr: Position/theory framework arguing scalarized RLHF reward collapses distinct evaluative categories (Semantic Reward Collapse), proposing partitioned Constitutional Reward Stratification to protect uncertainty disclosure.
articles.contribution: Proposes Constitutional Reward Stratification, a partitioned reward vector with uncertainty disclosure as a protected independent channel, so the reward construct preserves differentiated epistemic attribution rather than entangling factual, format, and social preference signals.

articles.title: WildRoadBench: A Wild Aerial Road-Damage Grounding Benchmark for Vision-Language Models and Autonomous Agents

articles.title: WildRoadBench: A Wild Aerial Road-Damage Grounding Benchmark for Vision-Language Models and Autonomous Agents
articles.tldr: Two-track aerial road-damage grounding benchmark (fixed VLM vs autonomous agent) that also audits validity failures like agent data leakage and online-vs-regraded metric divergence.

articles.title: WildRoadBench: A Wild Aerial Road-Damage Grounding Benchmark for Vision-Language Models and Autonomous Agents
articles.tldr: Two-track aerial road-damage grounding benchmark (fixed VLM vs autonomous agent) that also audits validity failures like agent data leakage and online-vs-regraded metric divergence.

articles.title: MINDGAMES: A Live Arena for Evaluating Social and Strategic Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLMs

articles.contribution: Identifies an environment-dependent error-survival confound where rankings reflect robustness to opponent failure rather than strategic ability — Secret Mafia's top model caused errors in only 4 of 130 games but won by surviving 129 opponent-error games — breaking the link between rating and the strategic-reasoning construct.

articles.title: MINDGAMES: A Live Arena for Evaluating Social and Strategic Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLMs
articles.tldr: Live multi-game arena for social/strategic LLM reasoning that audits leaderboard measurement validity, surfacing an error-survival confound and TrueSkill-vs-reward divergence.
articles.contribution: Shows TrueSkill rating and cumulative reward capture different signals (TrueSkill compresses to ~0..+50 while raw reward spans -120..+170) and proposes environment-level diagnostics — game error rate >30% and median termination depth below half of expected length flag a leaderboard as measuring error-survival, not skill.

articles.title: Are we chasing ghosts? Quantifying unattributable polarization, and attributing the rest to annotator groups
articles.tldr: Introduces apunim, a statistically-tested metric attributing annotation polarization to demographic annotator groups, and identifies unattributable inherent polarization in sparse NLP datasets.
articles.contribution: Provides apunim, a metric that attributes annotation polarization to specific annotator subgroups while avoiding subset-vs-complement pitfalls, showing gender and race systematically drive labeling disagreement that majority-vote aggregation hides (DICES-990 Race=AfricanAmerican +0.091***, Latino -0.133***).

articles.title: Are we chasing ghosts? Quantifying unattributable polarization, and attributing the rest to annotator groups
articles.tldr: Introduces apunim, a statistically-tested metric attributing annotation polarization to demographic annotator groups, and identifies unattributable inherent polarization in sparse NLP datasets.
articles.contribution: Pairs apunim with a parametric one-sample t-test against random-partition null distributions plus Holm multiple-comparison correction, and empirically shows no more than 20 annotators per item are needed for reliable estimation while a hard reliability ceiling persists regardless of annotator count.

articles.title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
articles.tldr: Pancreatic-oncology benchmark of real patient questions with expert rubrics that dissociates rubric completeness from factual accuracy and validates LLM-as-judge against oncologists.
articles.contribution: Argues multiple-choice accuracy and simulated queries (HealthBench) are poor proxies for real clinical utility, building PanCanBench from 282 authentic de-identified PanCAN patient questions with 3,130 expert-designed rubric criteria for disease-specific ecological validity.

articles.title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
articles.tldr: Pancreatic-oncology benchmark of real patient questions with expert rubrics that dissociates rubric completeness from factual accuracy and validates LLM-as-judge against oncologists.
articles.contribution: Validates the GPT-5 LLM-as-judge grader against two oncology fellows (LLM-human Cohen's κ 0.528 ≈ human-human 0.518; F1 0.838 vs 0.855) and validates a two-model factual-error detector at FPR 5.8% / FNR 3.2%.

articles.title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
articles.tldr: Pancreatic-oncology benchmark of real patient questions with expert rubrics that dissociates rubric completeness from factual accuracy and validates LLM-as-judge against oncologists.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates rubric-based completeness dissociates from factual correctness: o3 achieves the highest rubric score (82.3%) yet produces more factual errors than other GPT-family models, so completeness alone misrepresents the reliability construct and joint factuality evaluation is required.

articles.title: Finetuning with Scientific Data Increases Hallucinations: A Multi-domain Factuality Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: SciFactCheck benchmark showing scientific fine-tuning increases hallucination and that fine-tuned models sound more assertive while being internally less confident.
articles.contribution: Shows linguistic assertiveness confounds factual reliability: fine-tuned models exhibit higher linguistic certainty yet lower parametric certainty (length-normalized logprobs), so confident scientific-discourse style masks internal uncertainty rather than reflecting knowledge.

articles.title: Finetuning with Scientific Data Increases Hallucinations: A Multi-domain Factuality Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: SciFactCheck benchmark showing scientific fine-tuning increases hallucination and that fine-tuned models sound more assertive while being internally less confident.
articles.contribution: A human pilot finds current automated fact-checking tools only modestly agree with expert judgments on scientific content and that defining scientifically check-worthy claims is contested even among annotators (low per-concept Cohen's κ, ~0.19-0.31 global), undermining ground-truth for scientific factuality.

articles.title: Finetuning with Scientific Data Increases Hallucinations: A Multi-domain Factuality Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: SciFactCheck benchmark showing scientific fine-tuning increases hallucination and that fine-tuned models sound more assertive while being internally less confident.
articles.contribution: Uses a controlled minimal-pairing design comparing each scientifically fine-tuned model against its general-purpose base across 18 LLMs and five domains to causally attribute factuality degradation to the fine-tuning intervention across all three hallucination types.

articles.title: FECT: Factuality Evaluation of Interpretive AI-Generated Claims in Contact Center Conversation Transcripts
articles.tldr: FECT benchmark and 3D (Decompose-Decouple-Detach) paradigm for factuality evaluation of interpretive LLM claims about contact-center conversations, aligning humans then LLM-judges.
articles.contribution: Introduces the 3D (Decompose, Decouple, Detach) annotation paradigm that grounds human factuality judgments in compositional-semantics criteria, raising inter-annotator agreement from Cohen's κ 0.28 (unguided) to 0.58 and to 0.82 after excluding inherently ambiguous claims.

articles.title: FECT: Factuality Evaluation of Interpretive AI-Generated Claims in Contact Center Conversation Transcripts
articles.tldr: FECT benchmark and 3D (Decompose-Decouple-Detach) paradigm for factuality evaluation of interpretive LLM claims about contact-center conversations, aligning humans then LLM-judges.
articles.contribution: Aligns LLM-judges to the same 3D paradigm to detect non-factual interpretive claims without fine-tuning or heavy prompt tuning, reaching mean F1 0.86 (o1 with 3D+test-time-compute) and showing reasoning models align with humans even without explicit reasoning cues.

articles.title: FECT: Factuality Evaluation of Interpretive AI-Generated Claims in Contact Center Conversation Transcripts
articles.tldr: FECT benchmark and 3D (Decompose-Decouple-Detach) paradigm for factuality evaluation of interpretive LLM claims about contact-center conversations, aligning humans then LLM-judges.
articles.contribution: Argues factuality of analytical/interpretive claims (sentiment, causal relations) lacks a straightforward ground truth, and deliberately excludes conversation-claim pairs where humans could reasonably judge either way so the benchmark measures a well-defined evidence-groundable construct.

articles.title: FinReflectKG - HalluBench: GraphRAG Hallucination Benchmark for Financial Question Answering Systems

articles.title: FinReflectKG - HalluBench: GraphRAG Hallucination Benchmark for Financial Question Answering Systems
articles.tldr: GraphRAG hallucination-detection benchmark over SEC 10-K filings that stress-tests six detectors' robustness to noisy knowledge-graph triplets.
articles.contribution: Defines a conservative evidence-linkage annotation protocol requiring support from both textual chunks and relational triplets with explicit rejection rules (missing/assumed units, insufficient evidence) to make groundedness labels less reliant on finance domain expertise, and confirms detector differences via Cochran's Q and McNemar tests (p<0.001).

articles.title: VACT: A Video Automatic Causal Testing System and a Benchmark

articles.title: VACT: A Video Automatic Causal Testing System and a Benchmark
articles.tldr: Automated causal-intervention testing framework (VACT) that measures whether video-generation models truly learn physical causal rules versus exploiting shortcuts.

articles.title: VACT: A Video Automatic Causal Testing System and a Benchmark
articles.tldr: Automated causal-intervention testing framework (VACT) that measures whether video-generation models truly learn physical causal rules versus exploiting shortcuts.

articles.tldr: Human-preference dataset and reward model for graphic layout that shows frontier VLM judges are unreliable and image-reward models fail to transfer to the layout construct.

articles.tldr: Tool-use framework whose ToolEval provides a ChatGPT-based automatic evaluator (pass/win rate) validated against humans for agentic API use.

articles.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations

articles.tldr: EvalCrafter, a multi-aspect text-to-video benchmark with 17 metrics regressed onto human opinions, exposing that popular metrics like CLIP-Score correlate poorly with humans.

articles.title: Head-to-Tail: How Knowledgeable are Large Language Models (LLMs)? A.K.A. Will LLMs Replace Knowledge Graphs?

articles.title: Head-to-Tail: How Knowledgeable are Large Language Models (LLMs)? A.K.A. Will LLMs Replace Knowledge Graphs?

articles.title: What Can We Learn from Collective Human Opinions on Natural Language Inference Data?
articles.tldr: ChaosNLI collects 100 annotations per example (464,500 total) to show large human disagreement on NLI and that models cannot recover the human label distribution.

articles.title: What Can We Learn from Collective Human Opinions on Natural Language Inference Data?
articles.tldr: ChaosNLI collects 100 annotations per example (464,500 total) to show large human disagreement on NLI and that models cannot recover the human label distribution.

articles.title: Element-aware Summarization with Large Language Models: Expert-aligned Evaluation and Chain-of-Thought Method
articles.tldr: Shows standard summarization references (CNN/DM, XSum) are noisy and builds expert element-aware test sets that resolve the human-preference-versus-ROUGE paradox.

articles.title: A Performance Study of LLM-Generated Code on Leetcode

articles.title: NICO++: Towards Better Benchmarking for Domain Generalization
articles.tldr: Better domain-generalization benchmarking via covariate/concept-shift metrics that fix oracle-knowledge leak in model selection.

articles.title: Probing out-of-distribution generalization in machine learning for materials

articles.title: Probing out-of-distribution generalization in machine learning for materials

articles.title: An Investigation into Pre-Training Object-Centric Representations for Reinforcement Learning

articles.title: BAMBOO: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Long Text Modeling Capacities of Large Language Models

articles.title: BAMBOO: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Long Text Modeling Capacities of Large Language Models

articles.title: LLMs for Relational Reasoning: How Far are We?

articles.title: LLMs for Relational Reasoning: How Far are We?
articles.tldr: Argues shallow textual/numerical reasoning benchmarks overstate LLM reasoning; uses an ILP benchmark demanding strict cause-effect logic.
