articles.title: Towards A Better Metric for Text-to-Video Generation
articles.tldr: Shows FVD/IS/CLIPScore correlate poorly with human judgment for text-to-video generation and proposes the validated T2VScore metric.
articles.contribution: Collects the TVGE human-judgment dataset to provide confirmatory validation evidence, showing existing objective metrics are unreliable and that the proposed metric better aligns with human raters.

articles.title: KIEval: A Knowledge-grounded Interactive Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: KIEval uses an LLM 'interactor' for dynamic multi-round knowledge dialogues to give contamination-resilient LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Dynamic multi-round interactor dialogues probe deep comprehension so benchmark memorization no longer inflates the reported score.

articles.title: KIEval: A Knowledge-grounded Interactive Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: KIEval uses an LLM 'interactor' for dynamic multi-round knowledge dialogues to give contamination-resilient LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Employs an LLM interactor+judge whose scores are meta-validated for correlation with human judgment across five datasets.

articles.title: The Curse of Multi-Modalities: Evaluating Hallucinations of Large Multimodal Models across Language, Visual, and Audio
articles.tldr: The CMM benchmark isolates two hallucination causes in multimodal LMMs: overreliance on unimodal priors and spurious inter-modality correlations.
articles.contribution: Probes with balanced existence/non-existence items to expose spurious inter-modality correlations that would otherwise inflate hallucination-free scores.

articles.title: The Curse of Multi-Modalities: Evaluating Hallucinations of Large Multimodal Models across Language, Visual, and Audio
articles.tldr: The CMM benchmark isolates two hallucination causes in multimodal LMMs: overreliance on unimodal priors and spurious inter-modality correlations.
articles.contribution: Shows models answer from unimodal language priors rather than the actual visual/audio input, so accuracy misrepresents grounded multimodal understanding.

articles.title: On Leakage of Code Generation Evaluation Datasets
articles.tldr: Documents three contamination routes in code-generation benchmarks and releases the uncontaminated LBPP benchmark.
articles.contribution: Shows direct plus synthetic-data leakage inflate HumanEval/MBPP and releases 161-problem LBPP as a cleaner re-measurement set.

articles.title: On Leakage of Code Generation Evaluation Datasets
articles.tldr: Documents three contamination routes in code-generation benchmarks and releases the uncontaminated LBPP benchmark.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that repeated model selection on public test sets overfits and inflates reported code-gen scores, undermining fair model comparison.

articles.title: RL-ViGen: A Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Visual Generalization
articles.tldr: RL-ViGen is a visual-RL benchmark spanning many tasks and generalization types for more reliable OOD-generalization conclusions.
articles.contribution: Argues existing visual-RL benchmarks cover only isolated tasks/generalization types, and assembles diverse tasks plus a broad generalization spectrum for representative evaluation.

articles.title: RL-ViGen: A Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Visual Generalization
articles.tldr: RL-ViGen is a visual-RL benchmark spanning many tasks and generalization types for more reliable OOD-generalization conclusions.
articles.contribution: Unifies latest generalization visual-RL algorithms and finds no single algorithm dominates across tasks, cautioning against narrow-benchmark generalization claims.

articles.title: Your Code Secret Belongs to Me: Neural Code Completion Tools Can Memorize Hard-Coded Credentials
articles.tldr: HCR is an evaluation tool that reveals neural code-completion tools memorize and leak hard-coded credentials from training data.
articles.contribution: Builds credential-prompt tests plus format filters and live validity checks to detect verbatim training-data memorization in commercial and open NCCTs.

articles.title: Your Code Secret Belongs to Me: Neural Code Completion Tools Can Memorize Hard-Coded Credentials
articles.tldr: HCR is an evaluation tool that reveals neural code-completion tools memorize and leak hard-coded credentials from training data.
articles.contribution: Four filters remove ill-formatted candidates and a live validity check confirms real secrets, so the measured leakage rate reflects verified credentials, not superficial matches.

articles.title: Dual Indicators to Analyze AI Benchmarks: Difficulty, Discrimination, Ability, and Generality
articles.tldr: Applies item response theory to AI benchmarks, adding difficulty/discrimination and a new agent 'generality' indicator.
articles.contribution: Adapts IRT to estimate item difficulty/discrimination and agent ability, giving a psychometric alternative to raw average benchmark scores.

articles.title: Dual Indicators to Analyze AI Benchmarks: Difficulty, Discrimination, Ability, and Generality
articles.tldr: Applies item response theory to AI benchmarks, adding difficulty/discrimination and a new agent 'generality' indicator.
articles.contribution: Defines a new 'generality' metric capturing whether an agent is consistently good on easy and bad on hard items, beyond aggregate ability.

articles.title: HelloBench: Evaluating Long Text Generation Capabilities of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: HelloBench plus HelloEval: an open-ended long-text-generation benchmark with a human-aligned checklist LLM-judge.
articles.contribution: HelloEval fits checklist weights by regression on human ratings then LLM-judges each checklist item, achieving the highest human correlation among evaluated methods.

articles.title: HelloBench: Evaluating Long Text Generation Capabilities of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: HelloBench plus HelloEval: an open-ended long-text-generation benchmark with a human-aligned checklist LLM-judge.
articles.contribution: Argues single-response checklist grading avoids the length bias that pairwise LLM judges exhibit, reducing a surface-length confound in quality scores.

articles.title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: MedHallu is a 10k PubMedQA-derived benchmark for detecting medical hallucinations across easy/medium/hard difficulty tiers.
articles.contribution: A controlled generation-and-grading pipeline crafts easy/medium/hard hallucinations so detection cannot rely on surface cues; hard items sit closest to ground truth.

articles.title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: MedHallu is a 10k PubMedQA-derived benchmark for detecting medical hallucinations across easy/medium/hard difficulty tiers.
articles.contribution: Best LLM detector reaches only F1=0.625 on 'hard' hallucinations; adding a 'not sure' option and domain knowledge lifts precision/F1 by up to 38%.

articles.title: Towards Interactive Evaluations for Interaction Harms in Human-AI Systems
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing static model-only evaluations lack construct and external validity for sustained human-AI interaction harms.
articles.contribution: Argues static single-turn safety tests fail to transport to real multi-turn deployment where interaction harms accumulate over time.

articles.title: Towards Interactive Evaluations for Interaction Harms in Human-AI Systems
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing static model-only evaluations lack construct and external validity for sustained human-AI interaction harms.
articles.contribution: Proposes defining and measuring human-impact constructs (belief/affect/dependency shifts) via causal traces, since capability tests cannot capture interaction harms.

articles.title: Towards Interactive Evaluations for Interaction Harms in Human-AI Systems
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing static model-only evaluations lack construct and external validity for sustained human-AI interaction harms.
articles.contribution: Critiques the 'universal user' assumption, since models adapt responses to perceived user identity so evaluations must sample diverse user groups.

articles.title: H-ARC: A Robust Estimate of Human Performance on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus Benchmark
articles.tldr: Robust human-performance baseline on the full 800-task ARC benchmark from 1729 participants, anchoring human-machine comparison.
articles.contribution: Replaces a prior 40-task subset estimate (83.8%) with a full 400+400-task human baseline, correcting an unrepresentative human-performance figure for ARC.

articles.title: H-ARC: A Robust Estimate of Human Performance on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus Benchmark
articles.tldr: Robust human-performance baseline on the full 800-task ARC benchmark from 1729 participants, anchoring human-machine comparison.
articles.contribution: Reports pessimistic/optimistic bounds via 1000-run imputation over 10.3% dropout data; t-tests confirm the eval split is significantly harder (t(798)=7.67, p<.001).

articles.title: H-ARC: A Robust Estimate of Human Performance on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus Benchmark
articles.tldr: Robust human-performance baseline on the full 800-task ARC benchmark from 1729 participants, anchoring human-machine comparison.
articles.contribution: Despite similar edit-distance-to-truth, humans and machines make different errors (copy errors 10% vs 3.5%/1.6%), so machine ARC scores do not reflect human-like solving.

articles.title: MLR-Bench: Evaluating AI Agents on Open-Ended Machine Learning Research
articles.tldr: MLR-Bench evaluates AI research agents with rubric-based LLM judges (MLR-Judge) validated against expert reviewers.
articles.contribution: MLR-Judge scores research papers on five shared rubrics; LLM-human agreement is close to human-human agreement, supporting it as a reliable proxy reviewer.

articles.title: MLR-Bench: Evaluating AI Agents on Open-Ended Machine Learning Research
articles.tldr: MLR-Bench evaluates AI research agents with rubric-based LLM judges (MLR-Judge) validated against expert reviewers.
articles.contribution: Finds coding agents fabricate or invalidate experimental results in about 80% of tasks (e.g. simulated results, unrealistic R^2) and hallucinate citations in 50%, breaking scientific validity.

articles.title: Towards Domain Generalization for ECG and EEG Classification: Algorithms and Benchmarks
articles.tldr: Open-source leave-one-domain-out benchmark exposing OOD generalization failure of ECG/EEG classifiers under distribution shift.
articles.contribution: Argues standard leave-one/multi-subjects-out splits keep distributions similar and overstate generalization; proposes leave-one-domain-out across distinct PhysioNet/SEED datasets to make the eval representative of real shift.

articles.title: Towards Domain Generalization for ECG and EEG Classification: Algorithms and Benchmarks
articles.tldr: Open-source leave-one-domain-out benchmark exposing OOD generalization failure of ECG/EEG classifiers under distribution shift.
articles.contribution: Provides the BioDG benchmark to measure the intra-distribution vs OOD generalization gap for biosignal classifiers, quantifying how far i.i.d. test scores overestimate deployment performance.

articles.title: CURI: A Benchmark for Productive Concept Learning Under Uncertainty
articles.tldr: Introduces a model-independent 'compositionality gap' metric to quantify difficulty of OOD compositional generalization in a concept-learning benchmark.
articles.contribution: Defines the compositionality gap as strong-oracle minus weak-oracle performance, a model-independent measure of how much a split truly requires out-of-distribution compositional extrapolation.

articles.title: CURI: A Benchmark for Productive Concept Learning Under Uncertainty
articles.tldr: Introduces a model-independent 'compositionality gap' metric to quantify difficulty of OOD compositional generalization in a concept-learning benchmark.
articles.contribution: Shows the choice of hard vs random negatives (dataset design), not just the train/test concept split, changes measured compositional novelty, a confound in benchmark difficulty.

articles.title: Mitigating and Evaluating Static Bias of Action Representations in the Background and the Foreground
articles.tldr: Creates SCUBA/SCUFO synthetic OOD benchmarks to pinpoint background vs foreground static shortcut bias in action recognition.
articles.contribution: SCUBA (background swapped) and SCUFO (single-frame, motion-removed) probe whether action classifiers rely on static shortcut cues, disentangling motion from static-cue confounds.

articles.title: Mitigating and Evaluating Static Bias of Action Representations in the Background and the Foreground
articles.tldr: Creates SCUBA/SCUFO synthetic OOD benchmarks to pinpoint background vs foreground static shortcut bias in action recognition.
articles.contribution: Shows IID top-1 accuracy fails to reveal OOD robustness of video representations, so static-bias benchmarks are needed to predict real-world generalization.

articles.title: MEDIC: Comprehensive Evaluation of Leading Indicators for LLM Safety and Utility in Clinical Applications
articles.tldr: MEDIC framework shows saturated static medical benchmarks fail to predict clinical execution and active-safety utility of LLMs.
articles.contribution: Documents a knowledge-execution gap where high USMLE-style MCQ recall does not predict operational tasks (MedCalc, EHRSQL), making static benchmarks necessary-but-insufficient leading indicators.

articles.title: MEDIC: Comprehensive Evaluation of Leading Indicators for LLM Safety and Utility in Clinical Applications
articles.tldr: MEDIC framework shows saturated static medical benchmarks fail to predict clinical execution and active-safety utility of LLMs.
articles.contribution: Shows standardized medical licensing benchmarks have saturated (median >75%) and become disconnected from functional clinical requirements, eroding their discriminative validity over time.

articles.title: MEDIC: Comprehensive Evaluation of Leading Indicators for LLM Safety and Utility in Clinical Applications
articles.tldr: MEDIC framework shows saturated static medical benchmarks fail to predict clinical execution and active-safety utility of LLMs.
articles.contribution: Introduces a reference-free Cross-Examination Framework for hallucination/fidelity scoring and validates pairwise LLM-judge Elo ranking robustness across judges.

articles.title: LMM4LMM: Benchmarking and Evaluating Large-Multimodal Image Generation With LMMs
articles.tldr: Builds a large human-MOS T2I benchmark and an LMM-based metric, showing classic metrics misalign with human perception and confound quality dimensions.
articles.contribution: Proposes LMM4LMM, an LMM-based T2I evaluation metric validated against human MOS, and shows classic metrics (FID/IS/CLIPScore) align poorly with human preference.

articles.title: LMM4LMM: Benchmarking and Evaluating Large-Multimodal Image Generation With LMMs
articles.tldr: Builds a large human-MOS T2I benchmark and an LMM-based metric, showing classic metrics misalign with human perception and confound quality dimensions.
articles.contribution: Argues perceptual quality and text-image correspondence must be scored as separate dimensions because prior correspondence scores are confounded by perceptual quality.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models with Psychometrics
articles.tldr: A psychometric benchmark quantifying reliability and construct validity of LLM psychological constructs, exposing self-report vs behavior discrepancies.
articles.contribution: Establishes appropriateness and meaningfulness guidelines to identify theory-grounded psychological dimensions (personality, values, emotion, ToM, self-efficacy) before building LLM measures.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models with Psychometrics
articles.tldr: A psychometric benchmark quantifying reliability and construct validity of LLM psychological constructs, exposing self-report vs behavior discrepancies.
articles.contribution: Contrasts self-report (rating-scale) with open-ended vignette responses to show the self-report measure fails to capture the intended latent trait.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models with Psychometrics
articles.tldr: A psychometric benchmark quantifying reliability and construct validity of LLM psychological constructs, exposing self-report vs behavior discrepancies.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes five reliability forms (internal consistency, parallel-forms, inter-rater, position-bias, adversarial robustness) to check when reliable conclusions can be drawn about LLMs.

articles.title: LLMs Are Biased Towards Output Formats! Systematically Evaluating and Mitigating Output Format Bias of LLMs
articles.tldr: First systematic study of LLM output-format bias, with a reliable estimator disentangling format-following from true performance.
articles.contribution: Shows output format is a confound: correct answers get scored 0 due to rule-based extraction under format constraints, and performance varies substantially across 15 formats.

articles.title: LLMs Are Biased Towards Output Formats! Systematically Evaluating and Mitigating Output Format Bias of LLMs
articles.tldr: First systematic study of LLM output-format bias, with a reliable estimator disentangling format-following from true performance.
articles.contribution: Proposes EstTrueE, a consistent estimator normalizing SysE by the format-following score, with a reliability bound (Theorem 3.1) enabling automatic large-scale format-bias measurement.

articles.title: Progress or Regress? Self-Improvement Reversal in Post-training
articles.tldr: Reveals 'self-improvement reversal': pass@1 gains from iterative post-training mask declines in diversity and OOD generalization.
articles.contribution: Shows optimizing the single pass@1 metric via iterative self-training inflates it while corrupting what 'improvement' means, so pass@1 is a surface proxy for genuine capability.

articles.title: Progress or Regress? Self-Improvement Reversal in Post-training
articles.tldr: Reveals 'self-improvement reversal': pass@1 gains from iterative post-training mask declines in diversity and OOD generalization.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that pass@1 gains from self-improvement come with consistent declines in output diversity and out-of-distribution generalization.

articles.title: OLAPH: Improving Factuality in Biomedical Long-form Question Answering
articles.tldr: MedLFQA benchmark plus expert-validated automatic factuality metrics for evaluating biomedical long-form answers.
articles.contribution: Validates GPT-4-generated gold answers and must-have/nice-to-have statements against three medical experts to build reliable factuality-evaluation ground truth from question-only datasets.

articles.title: OLAPH: Improving Factuality in Biomedical Long-form Question Answering
articles.tldr: MedLFQA benchmark plus expert-validated automatic factuality metrics for evaluating biomedical long-form answers.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes cost-effective factuality metrics Hallucination (fraction of statements contradicted) and Comprehensiveness (fraction of must-have statements entailed) via a BioBERT NLI classifier.

articles.title: Characterizing Generalization under Out-Of-Distribution Shifts in Deep Metric Learning
articles.tldr: ooDML benchmark builds train-test splits of measurable, increasing FID difficulty, showing standard DML splits are near-i.i.d.
articles.contribution: Shows standard fixed single DML splits are close to i.i.d. and unrepresentative, so disjoint train/test classes do not imply the intended distribution shift for zero-shot evaluation.

articles.title: Characterizing Generalization under Out-Of-Distribution Shifts in Deep Metric Learning
articles.tldr: ooDML benchmark builds train-test splits of measurable, increasing FID difficulty, showing standard DML splits are near-i.i.d.
articles.contribution: Constructs ooDML splits of measurably increasing FID to characterize OOD generalization across a spectrum of shift difficulties rather than a single arbitrary split.

articles.title: StoryBench: A Multifaceted Benchmark for Continuous Story Visualization
articles.tldr: StoryBench benchmark with rich human annotations and evaluation protocol showing automatic video-generation metrics misalign with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Reports 5 automatic metrics (FID, FVD, VTM, PQA, SIM) and shows they do not align well with human judgment, reaffirming the need for better automatic video-generation metrics.

articles.title: StoryBench: A Multifaceted Benchmark for Continuous Story Visualization
articles.tldr: StoryBench benchmark with rich human annotations and evaluation protocol showing automatic video-generation metrics misalign with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Defines a multifaceted human evaluation protocol (5 side-by-side dimensions, 3 raters) plus 34 segment-level failure-mode labels to operationalize the story-visualization quality construct.

articles.title: Models See Hallucinations: Evaluating the Factuality in Video Captioning
articles.tldr: Human-annotated video-captioning factuality datasets show n-gram metrics fail to capture factual errors; proposes model-based FactVC.
articles.contribution: Shows n-gram metrics (BLEU4/CIDEr) measure surface overlap not factuality, correlating poorly with human factuality annotation, and proposes a CLIP-based FactVC metric that correlates much better.

articles.title: Models See Hallucinations: Evaluating the Factuality in Video Captioning
articles.tldr: Human-annotated video-captioning factuality datasets show n-gram metrics fail to capture factual errors; proposes model-based FactVC.
articles.contribution: Builds two triply-annotated factuality datasets (ActivityNet-Fact, YouCook2-Fact) with a 3-granularity protocol and reports Krippendorff alpha 0.56-0.78 quantifying ground-truth reliability.

articles.title: Reassessing Evaluation Practices in Visual Question Answering: A Case Study on Out-of-Distribution Generalization
articles.tldr: Cross-dataset OOD evaluation shows pretrained VQA models learn the benchmark, not the VQA skill, and stringent string-match metrics penalize correct answers.
articles.contribution: Uses zero-shot cross-dataset (IID to OOD) evaluation of ViLBERT/ALBEF to show large accuracy drops, demonstrating models solve specific benchmarks rather than the general VQA task.

articles.title: Reassessing Evaluation Practices in Visual Question Answering: A Case Study on Out-of-Distribution Generalization
articles.tldr: Cross-dataset OOD evaluation shows pretrained VQA models learn the benchmark, not the VQA skill, and stringent string-match metrics penalize correct answers.
articles.contribution: Identifies answer-prior overfitting and question-format overfitting as dataset-specific shortcuts that inflate IID scores without genuine visual grounding.

articles.title: Reassessing Evaluation Practices in Visual Question Answering: A Case Study on Out-of-Distribution Generalization
articles.tldr: Cross-dataset OOD evaluation shows pretrained VQA models learn the benchmark, not the VQA skill, and stringent string-match metrics penalize correct answers.
articles.contribution: Shows the standard string-match VQA accuracy metric penalizes semantically correct responses; human evaluation raises accuracy by up to 33.5%, especially in generative and OOD settings.

articles.title: Safer or Luckier? LLMs as Safety Evaluators Are Not Robust to Artifacts
articles.tldr: Eleven LLM safety judges are highly non-robust to superficial artifacts (apology, position), and human-agreement does not predict artifact robustness.
articles.contribution: Shows apology artifacts skew LLM-judge safety preference up to 98% (tie-detection) and position bias shifts model winrate up to 30%, undermining comparative safety evaluations.

articles.title: Safer or Luckier? LLMs as Safety Evaluators Are Not Robust to Artifacts
articles.tldr: Eleven LLM safety judges are highly non-robust to superficial artifacts (apology, position), and human-agreement does not predict artifact robustness.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates judges rely on statistical correlations (apology-equals-refusal) as a proxy rather than the safety construct; Command R, trained without apologetic language, is uniquely robust.

articles.title: Safer or Luckier? LLMs as Safety Evaluators Are Not Robust to Artifacts
articles.tldr: Eleven LLM safety judges are highly non-robust to superficial artifacts (apology, position), and human-agreement does not predict artifact robustness.
articles.contribution: Finds GPT-4 family judges are non-deterministic even at temperature 0 (up to 5.7% sample-level flips), so single-run safety judgments are not reproducible and should be repeated and averaged.

articles.title: SFR-RAG: Towards Contextually Faithful LLMs
articles.tldr: Introduces ContextualBench standardizing inconsistent RAG evaluation setups for reproducible comparison and uses FaithEval to disentangle contextual faithfulness from parametric knowledge.
articles.contribution: Proposes ContextualBench aggregating 7 RAG benchmarks under one standardized instruction/context setup with three scoring methods (EM/EasyM/F1) to enable reproducible, fair cross-model comparison.

articles.title: SFR-RAG: Towards Contextually Faithful LLMs
articles.tldr: Introduces ContextualBench standardizing inconsistent RAG evaluation setups for reproducible comparison and uses FaithEval to disentangle contextual faithfulness from parametric knowledge.
articles.contribution: Uses FaithEval (counterfactual/conflict/unknown contexts) to disentangle context-faithfulness from the parametric-knowledge confound in contextual-QA scores.

articles.title: DiaHalu: A Dialogue-level Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: First dialogue-level hallucination benchmark that is naturally generated by LLMs and covers faithfulness hallucination, not just factuality.
articles.contribution: Collects hallucinations naturally emitted by LLMs in multi-turn dialogue rather than induced by trigger prompts, better operationalizing real hallucination phenomena.

articles.title: DiaHalu: A Dialogue-level Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: First dialogue-level hallucination benchmark that is naturally generated by LLMs and covers faithfulness hallucination, not just factuality.
articles.contribution: Extends the hallucination construct beyond factuality to five subtypes spanning faithfulness (incoherence/irrelevance/overreliance) plus reasoning errors at the dialogue level.

articles.title: DiaHalu: A Dialogue-level Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: First dialogue-level hallucination benchmark that is naturally generated by LLMs and covers faithfulness hallucination, not just factuality.
articles.contribution: Provides expert annotations of hallucination presence, subtype and location with Fleiss Kappa 0.8842 (almost perfect agreement) to ensure label quality.

articles.title: Beyond Correctness: Benchmarking Multi-dimensional Code Generation for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Correctness-only code benchmarks are gameable by data contamination; RACE adds readability/maintainability/efficiency dimensions that resist contamination.
articles.contribution: Argues correctness alone under-represents code quality and adds readability/maintainability/efficiency dimensions measured via AST static analysis and runtime monitoring.

articles.title: Beyond Correctness: Benchmarking Multi-dimensional Code Generation for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Correctness-only code benchmarks are gameable by data contamination; RACE adds readability/maintainability/efficiency dimensions that resist contamination.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates correctness benchmarks inflate under contamination while RACE's instruction-following rate stays stable, making it robust to data leakage.

articles.title: MemSim: A Bayesian Simulator for Evaluating Memory of LLM-based Personal Assistants
articles.tldr: Bayesian simulator (MemSim) that generates reliable QA ground truths for evaluating LLM-assistant memory, mitigating LLM hallucination in dataset construction.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-generated QA ground truths are unreliable and uses a Bayesian Relation Network plus causal generation to construct correct ground truths without human annotators.

articles.title: MemSim: A Bayesian Simulator for Evaluating Memory of LLM-based Personal Assistants
articles.tldr: Bayesian simulator (MemSim) that generates reliable QA ground truths for evaluating LLM-assistant memory, mitigating LLM hallucination in dataset construction.
articles.contribution: Addresses LLMs' tendency to generate the most-plausible non-diverse user profiles by sampling diverse hierarchical profiles from BRNet's factorized joint distribution.

articles.title: CIFAR-10-Warehouse: Broad and More Realistic Testbeds in Model Generalization Analysis
articles.tldr: A 180-domain mostly real-world testbed (CIFAR-10-W) for more realistic out-of-distribution generalization and accuracy-prediction evaluation.
articles.contribution: Provides 180 mostly real-world domains (608,691 images) versus prior small or synthetic-corruption testbeds, giving broader and more realistic OOD distribution coverage for evaluation.

articles.title: CIFAR-10-Warehouse: Broad and More Realistic Testbeds in Model Generalization Analysis
articles.tldr: A 180-domain mostly real-world testbed (CIFAR-10-W) for more realistic out-of-distribution generalization and accuracy-prediction evaluation.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks accuracy-prediction and domain-generalization methods, showing prediction error grows with domain gap and DG gains vanish on far-OOD domains.

articles.title: The Fault in our Stars: Quality Assessment of Code Generation Benchmarks
articles.tldr: First quality audit of code-generation benchmark prompts, finding pervasive quality issues, unrepresentative coverage, and data contamination.
articles.contribution: Manual open-coding of 3,566 prompts finds 82% have at least one quality issue (spelling/grammar, docstring formatting, name-intent mismatch), degrading benchmark prompt validity.

articles.title: The Fault in our Stars: Quality Assessment of Code Generation Benchmarks
articles.tldr: First quality audit of code-generation benchmark prompts, finding pervasive quality issues, unrepresentative coverage, and data contamination.
articles.contribution: Uses NiCad clone detection to find test-set contamination (memorized HumanEval solutions) in GPT-3.5-Turbo and CodeGen-2.5 generations.

articles.title: The Fault in our Stars: Quality Assessment of Code Generation Benchmarks
articles.tldr: First quality audit of code-generation benchmark prompts, finding pervasive quality issues, unrepresentative coverage, and data contamination.
articles.contribution: Shows code benchmarks are unrepresentative of real development: mostly Python, simple self-contained tasks with very limited contextual dependency.

articles.title: VBench++: Comprehensive and Versatile Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
articles.tldr: Comprehensive video-generation benchmark decomposing quality into 16 human-validated dimensions, since IS/FID/FVD/CLIPSIM misalign with human perception.
articles.contribution: Shows IS/FID/FVD/CLIPSIM misalign with human perception and decomposes video-generation quality into 16 disentangled dimensions to isolate individual quality aspects.

articles.title: VBench++: Comprehensive and Versatile Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
articles.tldr: Comprehensive video-generation benchmark decomposing quality into 16 human-validated dimensions, since IS/FID/FVD/CLIPSIM misalign with human perception.
articles.contribution: Collects per-dimension human preference annotations as confirmatory evidence that each automated evaluation dimension correlates with human perception.

articles.title: VBench++: Comprehensive and Versatile Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
articles.tldr: Comprehensive video-generation benchmark decomposing quality into 16 human-validated dimensions, since IS/FID/FVD/CLIPSIM misalign with human perception.
articles.contribution: Introduces an adaptive-resolution Image Suite so image-to-video models are compared at optimal settings, removing input resolution as a confounder in I2V evaluation.

articles.title: Flaw or Artifact? Rethinking Prompt Sensitivity in Evaluating LLMs
articles.tldr: Argues LLM prompt sensitivity is largely an artifact of heuristic scoring; LLM-as-a-judge yields far more stable scores and rankings.
articles.contribution: Shows heuristic scoring (log-likelihood, rigid answer-matching) inflates apparent prompt sensitivity by missing semantically-correct paraphrases, whereas LLM-judge scoring collapses the variance.

articles.title: Flaw or Artifact? Rethinking Prompt Sensitivity in Evaluating LLMs
articles.tldr: Argues LLM prompt sensitivity is largely an artifact of heuristic scoring; LLM-as-a-judge yields far more stable scores and rankings.
articles.contribution: Shows model rankings that flip across prompt formats under heuristic scoring stabilize with LLM-judge, so reported prompt-induced ranking instability is an evaluation artifact.

articles.title: Causal Mediation Analysis with Hidden Confounders
articles.tldr: Deep latent-variable model recovers hidden confounders from proxies to de-bias causal mediation estimates, exposing gaps between causal and statistical fairness.
articles.contribution: CMAVAE infers hidden confounders from proxy variables to relax the sequential-ignorability assumption, reducing bias in average causal direct effect (ACDE) and ATE mediation estimates.

articles.title: Causal Mediation Analysis with Hidden Confounders
articles.tldr: Deep latent-variable model recovers hidden confounders from proxies to de-bias causal mediation estimates, exposing gaps between causal and statistical fairness.
articles.contribution: Decomposes discrimination into causal direct and indirect components and shows a model satisfying statistical demographic parity can still be causally unfair, exposing a construct gap in statistical fairness metrics.

articles.title: Rethinking Out-of-Distribution Detection for Reinforcement Learning: Advancing Methods for Evaluation and Detection
articles.tldr: Shows RL out-of-distribution-detection benchmarks use unrealistic i.i.d. noise and that AUROC ignores detection timeliness; proposes realistic scenarios and DEXTER+C.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that RL OOD-detection benchmarks inject unrealistic i.i.d. noise anomalies and introduces temporally-correlated realistic anomaly scenarios that better represent deployment.

articles.title: Rethinking Out-of-Distribution Detection for Reinforcement Learning: Advancing Methods for Evaluation and Detection
articles.tldr: Shows RL out-of-distribution-detection benchmarks use unrealistic i.i.d. noise and that AUROC ignores detection timeliness; proposes realistic scenarios and DEXTER+C.
articles.contribution: Argues AUROC alone misrepresents what a good OOD detector is because it ignores detection latency, and adds detection-time as a distinct validity dimension.

articles.title: Sparsity in Continuous-Depth Neural Networks

articles.title: Sparsity in Continuous-Depth Neural Networks
articles.tldr: Separates weight sparsity from feature sparsity in Neural ODEs, showing only feature sparsity recovers the true governing variables while weight sparsity learns shortcut dependencies.
articles.contribution: Defines feature sparsity (via PathReg) as the construct that identifies which input variables truly govern the dynamics, distinct from weight sparsity which only compresses the network.

articles.title: Quantifying Generalization Complexity for Large Language Models

articles.title: Quantifying Generalization Complexity for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Scylla dynamically generates ID/OOD algorithmic tasks to disentangle LLM reasoning generalization from memorization, revealing a non-monotonic 'generalization valley'.
articles.contribution: Separates intrinsic task complexity from input length and required knowledge so measured scores reflect reasoning, and defines a Generalization Score that penalizes ID-OOD overfitting.

articles.title: Toward Robust Hyper-Detailed Image Captioning: A Multiagent Approach and Dual Evaluation Metrics for Factuality and Coverage
articles.tldr: Shows standard caption metrics and hallucination detectors fail on hyper-detailed captions; proposes a multimodal GPT-4o factuality+coverage evaluation and a training-free multiagent corrector.

articles.title: Toward Robust Hyper-Detailed Image Captioning: A Multiagent Approach and Dual Evaluation Metrics for Factuality and Coverage
articles.tldr: Shows standard caption metrics and hallucination detectors fail on hyper-detailed captions; proposes a multimodal GPT-4o factuality+coverage evaluation and a training-free multiagent corrector.
articles.contribution: Shows reference-only metrics like FactScore carry stylistic bias tied to reference-caption phrasing, unfairly penalizing hallucination-free human captions relative to a multimodal metric.

articles.title: Toward Robust Hyper-Detailed Image Captioning: A Multiagent Approach and Dual Evaluation Metrics for Factuality and Coverage
articles.tldr: Shows standard caption metrics and hallucination detectors fail on hyper-detailed captions; proposes a multimodal GPT-4o factuality+coverage evaluation and a training-free multiagent corrector.
articles.contribution: Shows high VQA-benchmark performance does not predict detailed-captioning factuality (e.g. MiniCPM-V-2.6 beats GPT-4V on benchmarks but underperforms on captioning), questioning VQA-centric evaluation.

articles.title: MIRAGE: Assessing Hallucination in Multimodal Reasoning Chains of MLLM
articles.tldr: MIRAGE isolates reasoning-induced hallucinations (holding perception correct) in MLLMs and introduces multi-level metrics validated against human experts.
articles.contribution: Isolates reasoning-induced hallucination by constructing items where the image is correctly perceived yet reasoning fails, separating a construct that prior benchmarks (POPE, MMVP, HallusionBench, MME) conflate with perception-induced hallucination.

articles.title: MIRAGE: Assessing Hallucination in Multimodal Reasoning Chains of MLLM
articles.tldr: MIRAGE isolates reasoning-induced hallucinations (holding perception correct) in MLLMs and introduces multi-level metrics validated against human experts.
articles.contribution: Proposes an LLM Hallucination Score aggregating 3 LLM judges over 3 rewritten reference chains to reduce single-judge variance, and validates its reliability against human experts.

articles.title: A little less conversation, a little more action, please: Investigating the physical common-sense of LLMs in a 3D embodied environment
articles.tldr: Advocates embodied 3D (Animal-AI) evaluation of LLM physical common-sense reasoning to fix static benchmarks' ecological/construct-validity and contamination flaws; LLMs lag human children.
articles.contribution: Argues static text/image physics benchmarks lack ecological validity and proposes embodying LLMs as agents in a 3D Animal-AI arena so evaluation reflects noisy real-world interaction rather than clean vignettes.

articles.title: A little less conversation, a little more action, please: Investigating the physical common-sense of LLMs in a 3D embodied environment
articles.tldr: Advocates embodied 3D (Animal-AI) evaluation of LLM physical common-sense reasoning to fix static benchmarks' ecological/construct-validity and contamination flaws; LLMs lag human children.
articles.contribution: Grounds the physical-common-sense construct in cognitive-science tests independently validated on children and animals, enabling direct human/animal/RL comparison as criterion validity.

articles.title: A little less conversation, a little more action, please: Investigating the physical common-sense of LLMs in a 3D embodied environment
articles.tldr: Advocates embodied 3D (Animal-AI) evaluation of LLM physical common-sense reasoning to fix static benchmarks' ecological/construct-validity and contamination flaws; LLMs lag human children.
articles.contribution: Notes that static benchmarks with fixed items risk train/test contamination and that out-of-the-box embodied testing on unseen dynamic tasks avoids models being trained to predict test answers.

articles.title: Benchmarking Llama2, Mistral, Gemma and GPT for Factuality, Toxicity, Bias and Propensity for Hallucinations
articles.tldr: Benchmarks Llama2/Mistral/Gemma/GPT for factuality, toxicity, bias and hallucination, surfacing metric-design and baseline-saturation validity problems in safety evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows the safety metric penalizes off-format answers, conflating instruction-following with genuine safety, and that the 'safety' construct itself is subjective and underdefined.

articles.title: Benchmarking Llama2, Mistral, Gemma and GPT for Factuality, Toxicity, Bias and Propensity for Hallucinations
articles.tldr: Benchmarks Llama2/Mistral/Gemma/GPT for factuality, toxicity, bias and hallucination, surfacing metric-design and baseline-saturation validity problems in safety evaluation.
articles.contribution: Documents severe baseline saturation on the jailbreaking task where a naive always-refuse baseline already scores about 92%, leaving the metric unable to differentiate models.

articles.title: VLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: VLUE adds a private cross-cultural OOD test set to vision-language evaluation, exposing large generalization gaps and rank changes hidden by pretraining-overlapping benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Shows standard vision-language benchmarks overlap the pretraining image distribution, inflating apparent generalization, and adds a private OOD test set to remove this leakage.

articles.title: VLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: VLUE adds a private cross-cultural OOD test set to vision-language evaluation, exposing large generalization gaps and rank changes hidden by pretraining-overlapping benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Its cross-cultural OOD test reveals large generalization gaps and reshuffles model rankings and efficiency-performance trade-offs relative to standard in-domain leaderboards.

articles.title: Towards a Holistic Approach: Understanding Sociodemographic Biases in NLP Models using an Interdisciplinary Lens
articles.tldr: Argues via an interdisciplinary lens that 'sentiment' and 'bias' constructs are ill-defined in NLP and that automatic proxies miss societal impact, advocating human-aided evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows that constructs such as 'sentiment' and 'bias' are inconsistently defined across NLP, social science and linguistics, so bias measurement lacks a shared theoretical grounding before a measure is built.

articles.title: Towards a Holistic Approach: Understanding Sociodemographic Biases in NLP Models using an Interdisciplinary Lens
articles.tldr: Argues via an interdisciplinary lens that 'sentiment' and 'bias' constructs are ill-defined in NLP and that automatic proxies miss societal impact, advocating human-aided evaluation.
articles.contribution: Argues automatic bias metrics are surface proxies that fail to capture real societal impact and advocates human-aided evaluation, introducing the model-independent BITS corpus for explicit bias.

articles.title: SALAD: Systematic Assessment of Machine Unlearning on LLM-Aided Hardware Design
articles.tldr: Assesses machine unlearning to remove contaminated benchmarks/IP/malicious code from Verilog-generation LLMs, quantifying benchmark contamination.
articles.contribution: Quantifies severe train/test contamination in Verilog code benchmarks (Min-K% up to 100% on RTLLM, 94.23% on VerilogEval) and shows leaked test sets inflate Pass@k via memorization rather than genuine understanding.

articles.title: KNN-LM Does Not Improve Open-ended Text Generation
articles.tldr: Shows kNN-LM perplexity gains do not translate to open-ended generation quality, exposing perplexity as a misleading proxy.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that perplexity is a surface proxy that decouples from the target construct of generation quality: kNN-LM lowers GPT-2 perplexity 14.8->12.6 yet MAUVE/RankGen/Entity-F1 show no consistent gain.

articles.title: KNN-LM Does Not Improve Open-ended Text Generation
articles.tldr: Shows kNN-LM perplexity gains do not translate to open-ended generation quality, exposing perplexity as a misleading proxy.
articles.contribution: Human evaluation used as the real-world criterion shows the perplexity advantage does not generalize to perceived quality (GPT-2 baseline preferred 51% vs 49% for kNN-LM).

articles.title: OODRobustBench: a Benchmark and Large-Scale Analysis of Adversarial Robustness under Distribution Shift
articles.tldr: Large-scale benchmark showing in-distribution adversarial robustness overestimates and misranks out-of-distribution robustness.
articles.contribution: Shows ID adversarial-robustness evaluation is not representative of deployment: robustness drops 18/20/27% under dataset shift and up to 46% under Gaussian-noise shift across 706 models and 60K+ evaluations.

articles.title: OODRobustBench: a Benchmark and Large-Scale Analysis of Adversarial Robustness under Distribution Shift
articles.tldr: Large-scale benchmark showing in-distribution adversarial robustness overestimates and misranks out-of-distribution robustness.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates leaderboard ranking by ID robustness misranks OOD robustness (HAT drops rank 22->57 under catastrophic noise degradation, HE jumps 70->3 under threat shift), invalidating ID-based model selection.

articles.title: LCA-on-the-Line: Benchmarking Out-of-Distribution Generalization with Class Taxonomies
articles.tldr: Introduces in-distribution LCA (taxonomic) distance as a predictor of OOD accuracy that unifies vision and vision-language models.
articles.contribution: Proposes ID LCA distance as an OOD-performance predictor robust across model families (75 models, 5 OOD sets) where ID accuracy (Accuracy-on-the-Line) fails to explain the VM-vs-VLM effective-robustness gap.

articles.title: LCA-on-the-Line: Benchmarking Out-of-Distribution Generalization with Class Taxonomies
articles.tldr: Introduces in-distribution LCA (taxonomic) distance as a predictor of OOD accuracy that unifies vision and vision-language models.
articles.contribution: Links lower LCA distance to reliance on class-hierarchy-consistent, non-spurious features (e.g. not associating 'ostrich' with 'grass'), explaining why such models resist shortcut-driven OOD failure.

articles.title: RPGBENCH: Evaluating Large Language Models as Role-Playing Game Engines
articles.tldr: Benchmark for LLMs as RPG engines pairing judge-free rule-based mechanic checks with LLM-as-judge subjective metrics, exposing subjective-metric unreliability.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-as-judge subjective scores (interestingness, TIPI personality consistency) are high-variance and poorly aligned with humans, with automatic-vs-human PER Pearson of -0.691.

articles.title: RPGBENCH: Evaluating Large Language Models as Role-Playing Game Engines
articles.tldr: Benchmark for LLMs as RPG engines pairing judge-free rule-based mechanic checks with LLM-as-judge subjective metrics, exposing subjective-metric unreliability.
articles.contribution: Introduces a BFS validity checker and automatic event-condition/variable-update error checks (MEC) that score game mechanics without any judge, providing a stable objective measurement.

articles.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
articles.tldr: Survey tracing the shift from LLM-as-a-Judge to Agent-as-a-Judge to improve evaluation reliability and verifiability.
articles.contribution: Taxonomizes how agentic judges (planning, tool-augmented verification, multi-agent collaboration, memory) mitigate the reliability limits of single-pass LLM judges, establishing a developmental framework for evaluation validity.

articles.title: HaRiM^+: Evaluating Summary Quality with Hallucination Risk
articles.tldr: Proposes HaRiM+, a reference-free summary-quality metric derived from decoder hallucination risk on token likelihoods.
articles.contribution: Reinterprets a decoder overconfidence-regularizing objective as a hallucination-risk term, giving a reference-free factual-consistency measure that needs no training or human-aligned modules.

articles.title: HaRiM^+: Evaluating Summary Quality with Hallucination Risk
articles.tldr: Proposes HaRiM+, a reference-free summary-quality metric derived from decoder hallucination risk on token likelihoods.
articles.contribution: Shows HaRiM+ achieves state-of-the-art correlation with human summary-quality judgments on FRANK, QAGS and SummEval using only an off-the-shelf summarization model.

articles.title: PersoBench: Benchmarking Personalized Response Generation in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: PersoBench benchmarks personalized response generation using NLI/embedding reference-free metrics instead of n-gram overlap or LLM judges.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes the personalization construct as persona consistency (NLI-based C-score on DNLI) plus persona coverage (P-dist embedding distance), arguing BLEU/ROUGE n-gram overlap is ill-suited to lexically-divergent personalized responses.

articles.title: PersoBench: Benchmarking Personalized Response Generation in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: PersoBench benchmarks personalized response generation using NLI/embedding reference-free metrics instead of n-gram overlap or LLM judges.
articles.contribution: Unifies three persona-aware datasets (BST, FoCus, IT-ConvAI2) covering distinct personalization regimes under one protocol for more representative, generalizable benchmarking of personalized generation.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Generalization and Robustness via Data Compression
articles.tldr: Proposes lossless-compression evaluation of LLMs on post-cutoff data to avoid contamination and prompt sensitivity and measure temporal robustness.
articles.contribution: Introduces a compression-rate (bits-per-character) evaluation on data emerging after a model's training cutoff to sidestep benchmark contamination and prompt-engineering interference that inflate MMLU/SQuAD-style scores (est. 30-80% contaminated).

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Generalization and Robustness via Data Compression
articles.tldr: Proposes lossless-compression evaluation of LLMs on post-cutoff data to avoid contamination and prompt sensitivity and measure temporal robustness.
articles.contribution: Measures validity drift over time by comparing training-period vs testing-period compression; the train/test gap quantifies robustness and reveals divergence exactly at each model's cutoff date.

articles.title: Debate, Deliberate, Decide (D3): A Cost-Aware Adversarial Framework for Reliable and Interpretable LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: D3 is a cost-aware adversarial multi-agent debate framework that raises LLM-judge reliability and audits positional/self-enhancement bias.
articles.contribution: Improves LLM-judge agreement with human judgments to 85-86% (Cohen kappa up to 0.60) on MT-Bench/AlignBench/AUTO-J via role-specialized advocate/judge/juror debate, versus 72.5% for a single judge.

articles.title: Debate, Deliberate, Decide (D3): A Cost-Aware Adversarial Framework for Reliable and Interpretable LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: D3 is a cost-aware adversarial multi-agent debate framework that raises LLM-judge reliability and audits positional/self-enhancement bias.
articles.contribution: Provides a systematic bias-audit methodology showing anonymization and juror-persona diversification mitigate positional and self-enhancement bias, raising positional-swap consistency from 81.7% to 94.8%.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Contamination Detection Methods in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Survey and taxonomy of contamination-detection methods for LLM benchmark evaluation.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Contamination Detection Methods in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Survey and taxonomy of contamination-detection methods for LLM benchmark evaluation.
articles.contribution: Prescribes best-practices to prevent future contamination: scanning new eval sets, encrypting benchmarks, not leaking data to closed APIs, and benchmark perturbation / dynamic / protected evaluation.

articles.title: MDK12-Bench: A Multi-Discipline Benchmark for Evaluating Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

articles.title: MDK12-Bench: A Multi-Discipline Benchmark for Evaluating Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Multi-discipline K-12 MLLM reasoning benchmark with a dynamic anti-contamination evaluation framework.

articles.title: Consultation Checklists: Standardising the Human Evaluation of Medical Note Generation
articles.tldr: Consultation Checklist protocol standardizes human evaluation of medical note generation to raise reliability.
articles.contribution: Grounds subjective note evaluation in an expert-built checklist (marked critical/non-critical/irrelevant) so raters share a common reference, sharply raising inter-annotator agreement over prior audio-only protocols.

articles.title: Consultation Checklists: Standardising the Human Evaluation of Medical Note Generation
articles.tldr: Consultation Checklist protocol standardizes human evaluation of medical note generation to raise reliability.
articles.contribution: Shows using the checklist as the reference for automatic metrics (ROUGE/BERTScore) improves their correlation with human judgement versus using a single clinician note.

articles.title: AutoSCORE: Enhancing Automated Scoring with Multi-Agent Large Language Models via Structured Component Recognition
articles.tldr: Multi-agent structured-component-extraction framework to make LLM automated scoring more reliable and rubric-aligned.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses end-to-end LLM raters' low accuracy, prompt sensitivity, and rubric misalignment, and shows a rubric-aligned component-extraction stage before scoring improves human-machine agreement (QWK/QWK, MAE/RMSE).

articles.title: Face identification proficiency test designed using item response theory

articles.title: Face identification proficiency test designed using item response theory

articles.title: Confidence-aware Reward Optimization for Fine-tuning Text-to-Image Models
articles.tldr: Benchmark and calibration method exposing reward-model misalignment and overoptimization in text-to-image fine-tuning.

articles.title: Confidence-aware Reward Optimization for Fine-tuning Text-to-Image Models

articles.title: Silenced Biases: The Dark Side LLMs Learned to Refuse

articles.contribution: Argues standard QA fairness benchmarks create a false sense of fairness by treating safety-alignment refusals as unbiased answers, and proposes refusal activation steering to surface latent 'silenced' biases the metric otherwise misses.

articles.title: Silenced Biases: The Dark Side LLMs Learned to Refuse

articles.title: ODE: Open-Set Evaluation of Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models

articles.title: ODE: Open-Set Evaluation of Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models

articles.title: Assessing the Impact of Code Changes on the Fault Localizability of Large Language Models

articles.title: Assessing the Impact of Code Changes on the Fault Localizability of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Contamination-free mutation-based framework showing LLM fault localization relies on syntactic cues, not semantics.

articles.title: LLM-Symbolic Integration for Robust Temporal Tabular Reasoning

articles.title: ReliableEval: A Recipe for Stochastic LLM Evaluation via Method of Moments
articles.tldr: ReliableEval: a stochastic method-of-moments evaluation over meaning-preserving prompt perturbations that estimates how many resamplings are needed for a reliable LLM score.

articles.title: ReliableEval: A Recipe for Stochastic LLM Evaluation via Method of Moments
articles.tldr: ReliableEval: a stochastic method-of-moments evaluation over meaning-preserving prompt perturbations that estimates how many resamplings are needed for a reliable LLM score.
articles.contribution: Shows single-prompt benchmark reporting is unreproducible: overlapping score distributions mean a cherry-picked prompt can flip the model ranking.

articles.title: HawkBench: Investigating Resilience of RAG Methods on Stratified Information-Seeking Tasks
articles.tldr: HawkBench: a human-labeled, multi-domain RAG benchmark that stratifies information-seeking into four factoid/rationale query levels to measure RAG resilience.

articles.title: HawkBench: Investigating Resilience of RAG Methods on Stratified Information-Seeking Tasks
articles.tldr: HawkBench: a human-labeled, multi-domain RAG benchmark that stratifies information-seeking into four factoid/rationale query levels to measure RAG resilience.

articles.title: Evaluating Implicit Bias in Large Language Models by Attacking From a Psychometric Perspective
articles.tldr: Psychometric-inspired Disguise/Deception/Teaching attacks plus the BUMBLE benchmark to elicit and measure implicit bias hidden in LLMs.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes a bias-agreement task via psychometric attacks that capture implicit bias missed by explicit-harmful-word measures.

articles.title: Evaluating Implicit Bias in Large Language Models by Attacking From a Psychometric Perspective
articles.tldr: Psychometric-inspired Disguise/Deception/Teaching attacks plus the BUMBLE benchmark to elicit and measure implicit bias hidden in LLMs.

articles.title: Exploring the Potential of Large Language Models for Estimating the Reading Comprehension Question Difficulty

articles.title: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks

articles.title: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks
articles.tldr: Graph-structured mobile-agent benchmark that simulates dynamic device states to give reproducible, multi-valid-path evaluation of long-horizon tasks.

articles.title: Task Matters: Knowledge Requirements Shape LLM Responses to Context-Memory Conflict

articles.title: Task Matters: Knowledge Requirements Shape LLM Responses to Context-Memory Conflict
articles.tldr: A model-agnostic diagnostic showing that context-memory conflict effects are task-dependent and bias the reliability of LLM-as-judge evaluation.

articles.title: Comprehensive Algorithm Portfolio Evaluation using Item Response Theory

articles.title: Comprehensive Algorithm Portfolio Evaluation using Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: AIRT inverts Item Response Theory to evaluate a portfolio of algorithms across datasets, eliciting consistency, difficulty limits and anomalousness.

articles.title: Monitoring Shortcut Learning using Mutual Information

articles.title: Monitoring Shortcut Learning using Mutual Information

articles.title: What Defines Good Reasoning in LLMs? Dissecting Reasoning Steps with Multi-Aspect Evaluation
articles.tldr: Causal stepwise evaluation (CaSE) scores reasoning steps on relevance and coherence from preceding context only, avoiding hindsight bias.

articles.title: What Defines Good Reasoning in LLMs? Dissecting Reasoning Steps with Multi-Aspect Evaluation
articles.tldr: Causal stepwise evaluation (CaSE) scores reasoning steps on relevance and coherence from preceding context only, avoiding hindsight bias.

articles.title: CodeReviewQA: The Code Review Comprehension Assessment for Large Language Models

articles.title: CodeReviewQA: The Code Review Comprehension Assessment for Large Language Models

articles.title: BEAMetrics: A Benchmark for Language Generation Evaluation Evaluation

articles.title: BEAMetrics: A Benchmark for Language Generation Evaluation Evaluation
articles.tldr: BEAMetrics is a benchmark for evaluating NLG evaluation metrics against human judgements across diverse tasks, languages and quality dimensions.
articles.contribution: Shows metric validity fails to transport across tasks: metrics proven on machine translation (BERTScore, BLEURT) degrade on summarization, open-domain QA and VQA as answer space and required general knowledge grow.

articles.title: Inverse IFEval: Can LLMs Unlearn Stubborn Training Conventions to Follow Real Instructions?
articles.tldr: Inverse IFEval benchmarks LLMs on out-of-distribution counter-intuitive instructions that conflict with SFT-induced conventions, exposing cognitive inertia.
articles.contribution: Introduces Counter-intuitive Ability as an evaluation dimension and shows model rankings on IFEval do not transfer to OOD counter-intuitive instructions, revealing hidden instruction-following robustness gaps.

articles.title: Inverse IFEval: Can LLMs Unlearn Stubborn Training Conventions to Follow Real Instructions?
articles.tldr: Inverse IFEval benchmarks LLMs on out-of-distribution counter-intuitive instructions that conflict with SFT-induced conventions, exposing cognitive inertia.
articles.contribution: Optimizes the LLM-as-a-Judge scorer via an adaptive per-type judge matrix plus template and system-prompt tuning, raising judging accuracy from an 88% baseline to 98% validated against human-verified ground truth.

articles.title: Curve Fitting from Probabilistic Emissions and Applications to Dynamic Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: DynAEsti extends item response theory with a non-parametric Gaussian-process curve-fitting technique (CurvFiFE) to estimate dynamically-varying latent ability over time.
articles.contribution: Extends IRT via EM plus Gaussian-process curve fitting (CurvFiFE) to estimate the latent-ability construct with full posterior distributions and confidence intervals rather than point estimates.

articles.title: Curve Fitting from Probabilistic Emissions and Applications to Dynamic Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: DynAEsti extends item response theory with a non-parametric Gaussian-process curve-fitting technique (CurvFiFE) to estimate dynamically-varying latent ability over time.
articles.contribution: Shows the static-ability assumption of standard IRT misrepresents a time-varying latent trait, and modeling ability as a continuous non-parametric curve captures drift, growth and atrophy.

articles.title: Evaluation of Reliability Criteria for News Publishers with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Evaluates GPT-4o as an automated annotator of expert-designed news-publisher reliability criteria, measuring agreement with human experts.
articles.contribution: Measures GPT-4o annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) with human experts across six journalistic reliability criteria over 6,120 annotations, finding scorer reliability varies sharply by criterion.

articles.title: Evaluation of Reliability Criteria for News Publishers with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Evaluates GPT-4o as an automated annotator of expert-designed news-publisher reliability criteria, measuring agreement with human experts.
articles.contribution: Shows collapsing four-point rating scales to binary raises LLM-human agreement (ArtBias kappa 0.21 to 0.48, SensLang 0.17 to 0.55) and that the LLM can resolve disagreements between human expert annotators.

articles.title: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild
articles.tldr: AmbiBench adds an instruction-clarity taxonomy to shift mobile-GUI-agent evaluation from instruction-following to intent alignment, paired with an MLLM-as-judge evaluator MUSE.
articles.contribution: Argues one-shot-instruction benchmarks conflate instruction with intent, under-representing alignment capability; introduces a four-level clarity taxonomy to measure bidirectional intent alignment.

articles.title: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild
articles.tldr: AmbiBench adds an instruction-clarity taxonomy to shift mobile-GUI-agent evaluation from instruction-following to intent alignment, paired with an MLLM-as-judge evaluator MUSE.
articles.contribution: Validates the MUSE MLLM-as-judge auditor against human labels, reporting Jaccard 0.92 (outcome) and 0.84 (steps) and 96% valid-parameter-fill detection under Fleiss kappa 0.91 ground truth.

articles.title: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild
articles.tldr: AmbiBench adds an instruction-clarity taxonomy to shift mobile-GUI-agent evaluation from instruction-following to intent alignment, paired with an MLLM-as-judge evaluator MUSE.
articles.contribution: Exposes a deceptive pattern where agents keep high requirement-coverage yet zero task success by guessing from parametric priors, and adds a Forced Non-Default Principle to block scoring via system defaults.

articles.title: Multi-Metric Preference Alignment for Generative Speech Restoration
articles.tldr: A multi-metric unanimous-agreement preference signal for DPO that mitigates single-metric reward hacking in generative speech restoration.
articles.contribution: Shows single-metric preference signals are reward-hacked under DPO optimization pressure and that a unanimous multi-metric agreement criterion (perceptual, fidelity, content, timbre) yields holistic, non-gamed improvement.

articles.title: ECKGBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models in E-commerce Leveraging Knowledge Graph
articles.tldr: KG-grounded multiple-choice benchmark for e-commerce factuality that replaces unreliable LLM/human judges with verifiable knowledge-graph ground truth and negative-sampling-controlled distractors.
articles.contribution: Converts factuality scoring from open-ended LLM/human judging into KG-verifiable multiple-choice items and quantifies reliability with an 'Inconsistency' metric (two questions from the same triple), which their sampling keeps below ~10% for GPT-4/Qwen-max versus much higher under random distractor sampling.

articles.title: ECKGBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models in E-commerce Leveraging Knowledge Graph
articles.tldr: KG-grounded multiple-choice benchmark for e-commerce factuality that replaces unreliable LLM/human judges with verifiable knowledge-graph ground truth and negative-sampling-controlled distractors.
articles.contribution: A three-stage negative-sampling pipeline (candidate pool, coarse cosine-similarity filtering, fine-grained LLM filtering) tunes distractor difficulty so items are neither trivially easy nor unanswerable, so the score reflects genuine knowledge rather than distractor artifacts.

articles.title: INFACT: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Induced Faithfulness and Factuality Hallucinations in Video-LLMs
articles.tldr: Video-LLM hallucination benchmark with induced perturbation modes and reliability metrics (Resist Rate, Temporal Sensitivity Score) that separate clean accuracy from robustness and expose temporal-shortcut exploitation.
articles.contribution: The Temporal Sensitivity Score exposes 'temporal inertia': many open-source Video-LLMs give near-zero factuality TSS because predictions are unchanged after frame shuffling/reversal, revealing that clean accuracy is confounded by order-invariant shortcut cues rather than genuine temporal grounding.

articles.title: INFACT: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Induced Faithfulness and Factuality Hallucinations in Video-LLMs
articles.tldr: Video-LLM hallucination benchmark with induced perturbation modes and reliability metrics (Resist Rate, Temporal Sensitivity Score) that separate clean accuracy from robustness and expose temporal-shortcut exploitation.
articles.contribution: By adding Visual Degradation, Evidence Corruption and Temporal Intervention modes to a clean base set, it shows clean-only benchmarks under-sample the operating conditions that matter: base accuracy correlates with reliability (Pearson r=0.978) but model rankings diverge under perturbation.

articles.title: Precise Information Control in Long-Form Text Generation
articles.tldr: Reframes faithfulness hallucination as claim-level precision/recall against a fixed input claim set and validates an LLM claim-extractor/verifier against human judgments.
articles.contribution: Precise Information Control operationalizes faithfulness as coverage/precision over a set of verifiable atomic claims (decomposed by GPT-4o-mini) checked for semantic-equivalence support against the provided input, rather than a holistic fluency or similarity score, making the measured construct explicitly claim-grounded.

articles.title: Precise Information Control in Long-Form Text Generation
articles.tldr: Reframes faithfulness hallucination as claim-level precision/recall against a fixed input claim set and validates an LLM claim-extractor/verifier against human judgments.
articles.contribution: Both the claim extractor and the claim verifier are validated to agree strongly with human judgments, establishing the automated PIC scorer as a reliable measurement instrument before it is used to rank models.

articles.title: Poly-FEVER: A Multilingual Fact Verification Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Multilingual (11-language) fact-verification benchmark of identical claims that exposes language-specific bias and shows online-resource availability confounds measured hallucination detection.
articles.contribution: By translating the same 77,973 claims into 11 languages, Poly-FEVER shows English-only fact-verification benchmarks vastly overstate reliability: accuracy is highest in English and near chance for most other languages (LLaMA-2 70B drops to 19.47% on Tamil).

articles.title: Poly-FEVER: A Multilingual Fact Verification Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Multilingual (11-language) fact-verification benchmark of identical claims that exposes language-specific bias and shows online-resource availability confounds measured hallucination detection.
articles.contribution: Automated web-search resource counts correlate with per-language detection accuracy (low for Amharic/Tamil), and LDA topic-aware prompting plus RAG lift low-resource languages (Arabic +14.23%) while slightly hurting English/Chinese, evidence that resource availability confounds apparent hallucination rates.

articles.title: Breaking Bad Molecules: Are MLLMs Ready for Structure-Level Molecular Detoxification?
articles.tldr: Molecular toxicity-repair benchmark (ToxiMol) with a strict multi-criteria evaluation framework (ToxiEval) that defines valid 'repair success' as simultaneous satisfaction of safety, drug-likeness, synthesizability and structural similarity.
articles.contribution: ToxiEval deems a repair successful only if ALL criteria hold at once (toxicity-endpoint safety, QED drug-likeness, Lipinski Rule of Five, synthetic accessibility, and Tanimoto structural similarity), a conjunctive protocol that prevents trivially 'safe' but chemically meaningless molecules from scoring as valid repairs.

articles.title: Breaking Bad Molecules: Are MLLMs Ready for Structure-Level Molecular Detoxification?
articles.tldr: Molecular toxicity-repair benchmark (ToxiMol) with a strict multi-criteria evaluation framework (ToxiEval) that defines valid 'repair success' as simultaneous satisfaction of safety, drug-likeness, synthesizability and structural similarity.
articles.contribution: The framework hinges on choosing a high-quality reproducible surrogate toxicity predictor (TxGemma-Predict) as the evaluation oracle and ablates evaluation metrics, candidate diversity and failure attribution, treating the reliability of the automated judge as a first-class design concern.

articles.title: Seeing is Not Reasoning: MVPBench for Graph-based Evaluation of Multi-path Visual Physical CoT
articles.tldr: Visual physical-reasoning benchmark with a graph-based multi-path Chain-of-Thought consistency metric and shortcut-minimized items that scores reasoning-path validity rather than only the final answer.
articles.contribution: MVPBench items deliberately minimize text-prior shortcuts (using arrows/letters instead of textual cues) so scores reflect visual physical reasoning rather than exploitation of language-prior artifacts.

articles.title: Seeing is Not Reasoning: MVPBench for Graph-based Evaluation of Multi-path Visual Physical CoT
articles.tldr: Visual physical-reasoning benchmark with a graph-based multi-path Chain-of-Thought consistency metric and shortcut-minimized items that scores reasoning-path validity rather than only the final answer.
articles.contribution: A graph-based CoT metric (Path Validity Rate, Path Coverage Score over multiple annotated reasoning paths) measures whether the reasoning process is valid, not just whether the final answer is right, so answer-only accuracy is shown to overstate genuine physical understanding.

articles.title: Examining Exams Using Rasch Models and Assessment of Measurement Invariance
articles.tldr: Psychometric (Rasch item-response-theory) analysis of a real exam that estimates item difficulty and reliability on a latent scale and tests measurement invariance / differential item functioning for fairness.
articles.contribution: Fits the Rasch model to place item difficulties and student abilities on a common latent scale, providing a principled reliability-aware measurement model for exam scores instead of raw percent-correct.

articles.title: Examining Exams Using Rasch Models and Assessment of Measurement Invariance
articles.tldr: Psychometric (Rasch item-response-theory) analysis of a real exam that estimates item difficulty and reliability on a latent scale and tests measurement invariance / differential item functioning for fairness.
articles.contribution: Assesses measurement invariance / differential item functioning (via classical anchoring, Rasch trees and Rasch mixture models) across covariates such as gender and prior knowledge to detect items that are unfairly easier/harder at equal ability, i.e. whether the same construct is measured across subgroups.

articles.title: Benchmarking Out-of-Distribution Generalization Capabilities of DNN-based Encoding Models for the Ventral Visual Cortex
articles.tldr: Large macaque IT-cortex dataset showing DNN encoding models collapse out-of-distribution, with a train/test feature-distance metric that predicts the generalization drop that IID evaluation hides.
articles.contribution: On attribute-based OOD splits (hue, contrast, saturation, intensity, temperature) DNN encoding models retain as little as ~20% of their in-distribution neural predictivity, showing conventional IID random-split evaluation drastically overstates how well cortex models generalize.

articles.title: Benchmarking Out-of-Distribution Generalization Capabilities of DNN-based Encoding Models for the Ventral Visual Cortex
articles.tldr: Large macaque IT-cortex dataset showing DNN encoding models collapse out-of-distribution, with a train/test feature-distance metric that predicts the generalization drop that IID evaluation hides.
articles.contribution: Introduces a Closest-Cosine-Distance between train/test ResNet features that predicts the OOD predictivity drop (Spearman -0.45 to -0.49), outperforming MMD and covariate-shift metrics as a diagnostic for when a reported predictivity score will transfer.

articles.title: Ensemble-Based Deepfake Detection using State-of-the-Art Models with Robust Cross-Dataset Generalisation
articles.tldr: Cross-dataset study showing deepfake-detector rankings are unstable out-of-domain and that probability-level ensembling gives more reliable model selection than any single detector.
articles.contribution: Six SOTA detectors trained on FaceForensics++ degrade sharply on out-of-domain sets: CORE tops UADFV (AUROC 0.961) but falls to 0.741 on Celeb-DF-v2, showing single-source benchmark scores do not transfer to unseen manipulations.

articles.title: Ensemble-Based Deepfake Detection using State-of-the-Art Models with Robust Cross-Dataset Generalisation
articles.tldr: Cross-dataset study showing deepfake-detector rankings are unstable out-of-domain and that probability-level ensembling gives more reliable model selection than any single detector.
articles.contribution: Bump-chart analysis reveals steep rank shifts across datasets (CORE/FFD fall, UCF rises), so single-dataset leaderboards give unreliable model rankings; probability-level ensembles (simple and skill-weighted averaging) never rank worst and stay near-optimal, making them a more robust selection criterion.

articles.title: DRA-GRPO: Your GRPO Needs to Know Diverse Reasoning Paths for Mathematical Reasoning
articles.tldr: Shows the scalar correctness reward in GRPO is non-injective and blind to reasoning diversity, causing mode collapse.
articles.contribution: Argues the scalar correctness reward is a surface proxy that under-represents the reasoning-path construct: distinct valid reasoning trajectories receive near-identical rewards, empirically shown via Spearman correlation between reward distance and semantic-embedding distance.

articles.title: DRA-GRPO: Your GRPO Needs to Know Diverse Reasoning Paths for Mathematical Reasoning
articles.tldr: Shows the scalar correctness reward in GRPO is non-injective and blind to reasoning diversity, causing mode collapse.
articles.contribution: Frames vanilla GRPO's scalar reward as a sampling-bias problem where optimization pressure collapses the policy onto dominant modes; the SMI-based inverse-propensity reweighting de-biases the gradient to cover rare high-reward reasoning paths.

articles.title: MORQA: Benchmarking Evaluation Metrics for Medical Open-Ended Question Answering
articles.tldr: Benchmarks NLG evaluation metrics for medical open-ended QA, showing LLM-judges beat n-gram metrics but reference-based metrics have a limited upper bound.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks LLM-judges (GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-pro, DeepSeekV3) against BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore/BLEURT on 16,041 expert judgments, showing LLM-based evaluators correlate far better with expert medical ratings than traditional metrics.

articles.title: MORQA: Benchmarking Evaluation Metrics for Medical Open-Ended Question Answering
articles.tldr: Benchmarks NLG evaluation metrics for medical open-ended QA, showing LLM-judges beat n-gram metrics but reference-based metrics have a limited upper bound.
articles.contribution: Shows n-gram/embedding metrics reward surface lexical overlap rather than clinical correctness — GPT-4o responses beat gold references on BLEU/ROUGE-L/GPT-4o-as-judge, revealing metrics favor fluency over valid but divergent human answers.

articles.title: MORQA: Benchmarking Evaluation Metrics for Medical Open-Ended Question Answering
articles.tldr: Benchmarks NLG evaluation metrics for medical open-ended QA, showing LLM-judges beat n-gram metrics but reference-based metrics have a limited upper bound.
articles.contribution: Uses 2-4+ expert gold references and a gold-holdout protocol to quantify ground-truth variability, showing reference count and reference variability materially affect metric-human correlation.
