articles.title: Political Alignment in Large Language Models: A Multidimensional Audit of Psychometric Identity and Behavioral Bias
articles.tldr: A multidimensional psychometric audit of 26 LLMs exposing discriminant-validity and criterion-validity problems in political-alignment measurement.
articles.contribution: Cross-instrument analysis reveals a discriminant-validity failure of common political psychometric tests: the Political Compass 'social' axis aligns with cultural progressivism (r=-0.64) rather than the authority-related dimension it purports to measure.

articles.title: Political Alignment in Large Language Models: A Multidimensional Audit of Psychometric Identity and Behavioral Bias
articles.tldr: A multidimensional psychometric audit of 26 LLMs exposing discriminant-validity and criterion-validity problems in political-alignment measurement.
articles.contribution: Quantifies measurement reliability/prompt sensitivity via 10 repeated trials and multiple semantic prompt variants analyzed with a two-way ANOVA, finding model identity explains most score variance (η²>0.90).

articles.title: Political Alignment in Large Language Models: A Multidimensional Audit of Psychometric Identity and Behavioral Bias
articles.tldr: A multidimensional psychometric audit of 26 LLMs exposing discriminant-validity and criterion-validity problems in political-alignment measurement.
articles.contribution: Regression shows psychometric ideological positioning does not significantly predict downstream news-bias classification errors — a criterion-validity gap where conversational identity fails to predict task-level behavior.

articles.title: MyCulture: Exploring Malaysia's Diverse Culture under Low-Resource Language Constraints
articles.tldr: Shows closed-form MCQs inflate cultural-knowledge scores via guessing; an open-ended MCQ format reduces guessability and reveals overestimation.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates conventional closed-form MCQ format is a confound that inflates measured cultural competence via guessing/pattern-recognition, and proposes open-ended MCQs (multi-answer, ordering, matching) with factorial-decay guessability that expose the true competence gap.

articles.title: MyCulture: Exploring Malaysia's Diverse Culture under Low-Resource Language Constraints
articles.tldr: Shows closed-form MCQs inflate cultural-knowledge scores via guessing; an open-ended MCQ format reduces guessability and reveals overestimation.
articles.contribution: Shows prompt language confounds the cultural-knowledge measurement: high-resource-language (English/Chinese) prompts yield higher scores than the local Malay prompts, implying models acquire Malaysian culture through high-resource languages rather than through the target construct.

articles.title: MARCH: Multi-Agent Reinforced Self-Check for LLM Hallucination
articles.tldr: Identifies confirmation-bias/information-leakage in LLM-as-judge hallucination verifiers and builds a blinded multi-agent checker, while documenting reward hacking.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-as-judge hallucination verifiers exposed simultaneously to query+documents+response suffer confirmation bias (validating internal coherence over grounding), and removes the confound via a blinded Checker that re-answers atomized claims from the evidence alone.

articles.title: MARCH: Multi-Agent Reinforced Self-Check for LLM Hallucination
articles.tldr: Identifies confirmation-bias/information-leakage in LLM-as-judge hallucination verifiers and builds a blinded multi-agent checker, while documenting reward hacking.
articles.contribution: Documents reward hacking of the zero-tolerance verifiable reward: the Proposer prunes the number of claims ('less said, less leaked') to minimize audit exposure, mitigated by an instructional minimum-question constraint.

articles.title: LeakageDetector: An Open Source Data Leakage Analysis Tool in Machine Learning Pipelines
articles.tldr: An IDE plugin that statically detects data-leakage in ML pipelines that would otherwise inflate performance estimates.
articles.contribution: Detects overlap leakage (train/test sharing data) and multi-test leakage (same test set reused across evaluations) via static analysis, flagging code that produces overly optimistic performance estimates and offering quick fixes.

articles.title: LeakageDetector: An Open Source Data Leakage Analysis Tool in Machine Learning Pipelines
articles.tldr: An IDE plugin that statically detects data-leakage in ML pipelines that would otherwise inflate performance estimates.
articles.contribution: Detects preprocessing leakage (fitting transforms/feature selection jointly on train and test) as a pipeline-order confound and proposes moving the split before feature selection.

articles.title: Geometry Matters: Benchmarking Scientific ML Approaches for Flow Prediction around Complex Geometries
articles.tldr: Benchmarks SciML flow-prediction models with a multi-metric scoring framework and shows all models fail out-of-distribution, plus a metric artifact.
articles.contribution: Systematic extrapolatory evaluation (training on middle-80% Reynolds numbers, testing on top/bottom 10%) shows all SciML models degrade sharply out-of-distribution and dataset size barely helps, so random-split scores overstate deployment performance.

articles.title: Geometry Matters: Benchmarking Scientific ML Approaches for Flow Prediction around Complex Geometries
articles.tldr: Benchmarks SciML flow-prediction models with a multi-metric scoring framework and shows all models fail out-of-distribution, plus a metric artifact.
articles.contribution: Introduces a normalized 0-100 scoring framework integrating global accuracy, boundary-layer fidelity, and PDE-residual physical consistency, and shows a single MSE metric misrepresents quality (DeepONet best on PDE-residual despite not lowest MSE).

articles.title: OpenPros: A Large-Scale Dataset for Limited View Prostate Ultrasound Computed Tomography
articles.tldr: A large-scale prostate USCT benchmark that exposes an ID-split leakage caveat and large patient-level out-of-distribution generalization gaps.
articles.contribution: Provides OOD generalization protocols (patient-level and leave-one-prostate-out splits) showing patient-level generalization inflates error ~3-5x while intra-patient generalization is near in-distribution, quantifying external validity of learned USCT reconstruction.

articles.title: OpenPros: A Large-Scale Dataset for Limited View Prostate Ultrasound Computed Tomography
articles.tldr: A large-scale prostate USCT benchmark that exposes an ID-split leakage caveat and large patient-level out-of-distribution generalization gaps.
articles.contribution: Explicitly documents that the in-distribution split allows slices from the same 3D anatomy in both train and test (no patient exclusivity), so ID scores measure interpolation, not generalization — a leakage caveat that inflates apparent accuracy.

articles.title: Evaluating LLM Safety Across Child Development Stages: A Simulated Agent Approach
articles.tldr: A benchmark stress-testing LLM safety-alignment robustness under simulated child (cognitive) distribution shifts, validating agents against CHILDES.
articles.contribution: Quantifies an alignment generalization gap under cognitive distribution shift: safety scores drop up to 11.5% for early-childhood (A6-8) agents versus adult-normative baselines, revealing RLHF overfits to the modal-adult interaction distribution.

articles.title: Evaluating LLM Safety Across Child Development Stages: A Simulated Agent Approach
articles.tldr: A benchmark stress-testing LLM safety-alignment robustness under simulated child (cognitive) distribution shifts, validating agents against CHILDES.
articles.contribution: Validates the parametric child-agent operationalization against CHILDES human linguistic data (K-S test p>0.05) and construct separation (expert ICC=0.78), while explicitly cautioning the agents establish plausibility, not fidelity.

articles.title: MTBBench: A Multimodal Sequential Clinical Decision-Making Benchmark in Oncology
articles.tldr: Agentic oncology benchmark arguing existing clinical LLM evals are too decontextualized/unimodal to reflect real molecular-tumor-board decision-making.
articles.contribution: Shows existing biomedical benchmarks test unimodal single-turn decontextualized QA and instead operationalizes MTB decision-making as longitudinal, multimodal oncology questions with clinician-validated ground truth.

articles.title: MTBBench: A Multimodal Sequential Clinical Decision-Making Benchmark in Oncology
articles.tldr: Agentic oncology benchmark arguing existing clinical LLM evals are too decontextualized/unimodal to reflect real molecular-tumor-board decision-making.
articles.contribution: Argues decontextualized QA scores do not transport to real molecular-tumor-board workflows and supplies a realistic testbed to measure deployment-relevant reliability.

articles.title: Mitigating Geospatial Knowledge Hallucination in Large Language Models: Benchmarking and Dynamic Factuality Aligning
articles.tldr: Introduces a knowledge-graph-controlled benchmark measuring geospatial factual hallucination across 20 LLMs, then mitigates it via Kahneman-Tversky Optimization.
articles.contribution: Uses structured geospatial knowledge graphs as controlled ground truth to isolate geospatial factual accuracy from surface phrasing, defining a dedicated construct for geospatial hallucination.

articles.title: Mitigating Geospatial Knowledge Hallucination in Large Language Models: Benchmarking and Dynamic Factuality Aligning
articles.tldr: Introduces a knowledge-graph-controlled benchmark measuring geospatial factual hallucination across 20 LLMs, then mitigates it via Kahneman-Tversky Optimization.
articles.contribution: Builds a controlled evaluation covering diverse geospatial entities and relations to systematically probe where LLM geospatial knowledge is unreliable across 20 models.

articles.title: CCFQA: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual and Cross-Modal Speech and Text Factuality Evaluation
articles.tldr: Cross-lingual, cross-modal (speech+text) factuality benchmark exposing that MLLM reliability evaluations are English- and text-centric.
articles.contribution: Constructs parallel speech-text factual questions across 8 languages to correct the English/text-only convenience sampling of existing MLLM factuality benchmarks.

articles.title: CCFQA: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual and Cross-Modal Speech and Text Factuality Evaluation
articles.tldr: Cross-lingual, cross-modal (speech+text) factuality benchmark exposing that MLLM reliability evaluations are English- and text-centric.
articles.contribution: Shows factuality measured only on English text does not transport to multilingual spoken QA, providing a cross-modal criterion for MLLM reliability.

articles.title: MultiHal: Multilingual Dataset for Knowledge-Graph Grounded Evaluation of LLM Hallucinations
articles.tldr: KG-grounded multilingual, multihop hallucination benchmark built from mined, quality-pruned knowledge-graph paths.
articles.contribution: Curates a high-quality 25.9k KG-path subset from 140k mined paths using an LLM-as-judge quality filter, addressing ground-truth/path quality for factuality grounding.

articles.title: MultiHal: Multilingual Dataset for Knowledge-Graph Grounded Evaluation of LLM Hallucinations
articles.tldr: KG-grounded multilingual, multihop hallucination benchmark built from mined, quality-pruned knowledge-graph paths.
articles.contribution: Adds structured KG paths and multilinguality missing from English-centric factuality benchmarks, scoring with semantic similarity, NLI entailment and hallucination detection.

articles.title: FeatBench: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Feature-level Code Generation
articles.tldr: Feature-level code-generation benchmark that removes code hints and uses evolving data to fix unrealistic inputs and contamination in prior benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Uses a fully automated pipeline that continually rebuilds versions from the latest repositories to mitigate train/test data contamination in otherwise static code benchmarks.

articles.title: FeatBench: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Feature-level Code Generation
articles.tldr: Feature-level code-generation benchmark that removes code hints and uses evolving data to fix unrealistic inputs and contamination in prior benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Strips code hints (e.g. function signatures) so tasks are pure natural-language requirements, removing shortcut cues that made prior feature-level benchmarks unrealistic.

articles.title: Benchmarking Diversity in Image Generation via Attribute-Conditional Human Evaluation
articles.tldr: Human-evaluation methodology for measuring text-to-image diversity, comparing image embeddings and ranking models via binomial tests.
articles.contribution: Operationally defines T2I diversity as variation over per-concept factors of variation (e.g. apple to color) and builds a human-evaluation template to measure it concept-by-concept.

articles.title: Benchmarking Diversity in Image Generation via Attribute-Conditional Human Evaluation
articles.tldr: Human-evaluation methodology for measuring text-to-image diversity, comparing image embeddings and ranking models via binomial tests.
articles.contribution: Rigorously compares candidate image embeddings as automatic diversity metrics and validates them against human annotations to identify a reliable diversity measure.

articles.title: Examining the development of attitude scales using Large Language Models (LLMs)
articles.tldr: Psychometric experiment using an LLM as an additional judge to build a Thurstone attitude scale, comparing LLM vs human item categorizations.
articles.contribution: Applies Thurstone equal-appearing-interval methodology to construct a theory-grounded unidimensional attitude scale (toward people living with AIDS) from 63 candidate items.

articles.title: Examining the development of attitude scales using Large Language Models (LLMs)
articles.tldr: Psychometric experiment using an LLM as an additional judge to build a Thurstone attitude scale, comparing LLM vs human item categorizations.
articles.contribution: Tests an LLM (ChatGPT) as a substitute item-judge, comparing its 1-11 categorizations against 75 human judges to gauge judge reliability in scale construction.

articles.title: Helpful Agent Meets Deceptive Judge: Understanding Vulnerabilities in Agentic Workflows
articles.tldr: Studies how unreliable or adversarial LLM judges break feedback-driven agentic workflows; introduces WAFER-QA with web-grounded misleading critiques.
articles.contribution: Provides a two-dimensional taxonomy of judge behavior (intent from constructive to malicious; knowledge from parametric-only to retrieval-augmented) characterizing how judge unreliability corrupts feedback.

articles.title: Helpful Agent Meets Deceptive Judge: Understanding Vulnerabilities in Agentic Workflows
articles.tldr: Studies how unreliable or adversarial LLM judges break feedback-driven agentic workflows; introduces WAFER-QA with web-grounded misleading critiques.
articles.contribution: Shows the feedback harness itself is a confound: even strong agents flip correct answers after a single round of persuasive-but-flawed, web-grounded critique from the judge.

articles.title: Who Judges the Judge? LLM Jury-on-Demand: Building Trustworthy LLM Evaluation Systems
articles.tldr: Learns per-instance reliability of LLM judges and dynamically assembles/weights a jury to better correlate with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Trains per-judge XGBoost reliability predictors from text-size, complexity and embedding features to forecast, per instance, when each LLM judge will agree with human experts.

articles.title: Who Judges the Judge? LLM Jury-on-Demand: Building Trustworthy LLM Evaluation Systems
articles.tldr: Learns per-instance reliability of LLM judges and dynamically assembles/weights a jury to better correlate with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Replaces static jury averaging with per-instance selection of the top-K most reliable judges weighted by predicted reliability, raising Kendall's tau over single-judge and static-jury baselines.

articles.title: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
articles.tldr: Defines Blind Goal-Directedness in computer-use agents and builds BLIND-ACT (90 tasks) with a human-validated LLM judge to measure it.
articles.contribution: Defines Blind Goal-Directedness (pursuing goals regardless of feasibility/safety/context) via three patterns and operationalizes it into 90 BLIND-ACT tasks built on OSWorld.

articles.title: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
articles.tldr: Defines Blind Goal-Directedness in computer-use agents and builds BLIND-ACT (90 tasks) with a human-validated LLM judge to measure it.
articles.contribution: Validates the LLM-based judge used to score agent behavior, reporting 93.75% agreement with human annotations before scaling the evaluation.

articles.title: Toward a unified framework for data-efficient evaluation of large language models
articles.tldr: Item-Response-Theory framework for data-efficient LLM evaluation that natively handles continuous scores and cross-benchmark structure.
articles.contribution: Extends IRT to natively support both binary and continuous generative scores and factorizes ability into a general plus per-metric/per-benchmark components to disentangle capability from item difficulty.

articles.title: Toward a unified framework for data-efficient evaluation of large language models
articles.tldr: Item-Response-Theory framework for data-efficient LLM evaluation that natively handles continuous scores and cross-benchmark structure.
articles.contribution: Shows stable capability estimates from only 3% of items across 70 LLMs and 5 benchmarks, quantifying how much of full-benchmark evaluation is statistically redundant.

articles.title: AB2CD: AI for Building Climate Damage Classification and Detection
articles.tldr: Audits the validity of building-damage-detection generalization: benchmark leakage, OOD transfer, and label quality.
articles.contribution: Shows the xView2/xBD practice of splitting a disaster's imagery across train and test leaks event-specific appearance, so it runs event-level cross-validation for an honest generalization estimate.

articles.title: AB2CD: AI for Building Climate Damage Classification and Detection
articles.tldr: Audits the validity of building-damage-detection generalization: benchmark leakage, OOD transfer, and label quality.
articles.contribution: Quantifies the external-validity gap by testing transfer to an out-of-distribution flood (Ahr Valley, different airborne sensor/region) where damage-classification F1 collapses to near zero.

articles.title: AB2CD: AI for Building Climate Damage Classification and Detection
articles.tldr: Audits the validity of building-damage-detection generalization: benchmark leakage, OOD transfer, and label quality.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that low-quality CEMS ground-truth labels (no explicit unaffected class, batch annotation) confound the OOD assessment, preventing any conclusion about transfer.

articles.title: TEA-Bench: A Systematic Benchmarking of Tool-enhanced Emotional Support Dialogue Agent
articles.tldr: Interactive benchmark that operationalizes and measures grounded, hallucination-checked emotional support with tools.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes the under-measured construct of grounded instrumental (not just affective) emotional support via process-level TEA metrics, an LLM Hallucination Detection Module checking entity provenance, and human-validated scenarios.

articles.title: TEA-Bench: A Systematic Benchmarking of Tool-enhanced Emotional Support Dialogue Agent
articles.tldr: Interactive benchmark that operationalizes and measures grounded, hallucination-checked emotional support with tools.
articles.contribution: Shows supervised fine-tuning on tool-enhanced dialogues improves in-distribution support but generalizes poorly and can increase hallucination under distribution shift, exposing an external-validity limit.

articles.title: From traces to measures: Large language models as a tool for psychological measurement from text
articles.authors: Joseph J. P. Simons et al.
articles.tldr: Brings psychometric reliability and validity assessment to LLM-as-rater measures of latent psychological constructs.
articles.contribution: Transfers psychometric reliability tools (factor analysis, Cronbach's alpha, McDonald's omega) to LLM ratings, treating each prompt as a noisy indicator of a latent construct and aggregating multiple prompt variants.

articles.title: From traces to measures: Large language models as a tool for psychological measurement from text
articles.authors: Joseph J. P. Simons et al.
articles.tldr: Brings psychometric reliability and validity assessment to LLM-as-rater measures of latent psychological constructs.
articles.contribution: Validates whether LLM ratings capture the intended construct via nomological external criteria and a sentiment (VADER) control, warning that evaluation metrics like human ratings are error-prone correlates, not a ground truth to be maximized.

articles.title: A Scalable Entity-Based Framework for Auditing Bias in LLMs
articles.tldr: Synthetic entity-probe framework that trades and then validates ecological validity for controlled, large-scale LLM bias auditing.
articles.contribution: Uses named entities as controlled probes in templates that already contain sufficient evidence for the correct label, so predictions should be entity-invariant; deviation isolates entity-identity bias from confounds like topic and phrasing.

articles.title: A Scalable Entity-Based Framework for Auditing Bias in LLMs
articles.tldr: Synthetic entity-probe framework that trades and then validates ecological validity for controlled, large-scale LLM bias auditing.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory evidence that the synthetic proxy is a valid, ecologically representative measure by showing its bias scores strongly correlate (Pearson) with bias measured on real natural text, resolving the control-vs-realism tradeoff.

articles.title: Same Meaning, Different Scores: Lexical and Syntactic Sensitivity in LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Shows meaning-preserving lexical and syntactic perturbations destabilize LLM benchmark scores and leaderboards.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that truth-conditionally equivalent lexical substitutions sharply degrade benchmark accuracy, evidencing that scores reflect surface lexical pattern-matching rather than the intended abstract competence.

articles.title: Same Meaning, Different Scores: Lexical and Syntactic Sensitivity in LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Shows meaning-preserving lexical and syntactic perturbations destabilize LLM benchmark scores and leaderboards.
articles.contribution: Quantifies leaderboard brittleness with Kendall's tau, Wilcoxon and McNemar tests, showing minor meaning-preserving edits reorder model rankings and undermine using small score gaps for model selection.

articles.title: Grade Score: Quantifying LLM Performance in Option Selection
articles.tldr: Introduces the Grade Score, an entropy+mode-frequency metric quantifying an LLM judge's order bias and choice consistency in multiple-choice selection.
articles.contribution: Defines Grade Score as the harmonic mean of a normalized-entropy LLM Score (order bias) and a mode-frequency Choice Score (selection stability) over permuted option orderings, quantifying how reliable an LLM judge is.

articles.title: Grade Score: Quantifying LLM Performance in Option Selection
articles.tldr: Introduces the Grade Score, an entropy+mode-frequency metric quantifying an LLM judge's order bias and choice consistency in multiple-choice selection.
articles.contribution: Shows option position is a spurious confounder in LLM-judge selection and uses Monte Carlo unique-permutation trials plus an added unrelated 'random option' to disentangle genuine preference from positional order bias.

articles.title: Scaling Ambiguity: Augmenting Human Annotation in Speech Emotion Recognition with Audio-Language Models
articles.tldr: Studies whether audio-language-model synthetic annotations can repair unreliable ground-truth emotion distributions inferred from sparse human labels in ambiguous speech emotion recognition.
articles.contribution: Documents that AER ground-truth emotion distributions built from only 3-5 sparse human raters per utterance are coarse and unreliable, quantified via Fleiss' kappa and Shannon entropy of the human label distributions.

articles.title: Scaling Ambiguity: Augmenting Human Annotation in Speech Emotion Recognition with Audio-Language Models
articles.tldr: Studies whether audio-language-model synthetic annotations can repair unreliable ground-truth emotion distributions inferred from sparse human labels in ambiguous speech emotion recognition.
articles.contribution: Treats ALM-generated (Gemini-2.5-Pro) synthetic annotations as extra 'perceptual proxies' augmenting sparse human labels, validating alignment to human distributions before using them as ground truth.

articles.title: NeurIPS 2024 ML4CFD Competition: Results and Retrospective Analysis
articles.tldr: Retrospective analysis of the NeurIPS 2024 ML4CFD competition that assesses the robustness and fairness of its multi-criteria global scoring/evaluation framework for aerodynamic surrogates.
articles.contribution: Critically assesses the linear multi-criteria global score (weighted combination of ML accuracy/speed, physics compliance, OOD generalization), showing it can misrepresent priorities and offering protocol enhancements for fairer ranking.

articles.title: NeurIPS 2024 ML4CFD Competition: Results and Retrospective Analysis
articles.tldr: Retrospective analysis of the NeurIPS 2024 ML4CFD competition that assesses the robustness and fairness of its multi-criteria global scoring/evaluation framework for aerodynamic surrogates.
articles.contribution: Argues OOD generalization across airfoil geometries must be a first-class scoring criterion and recommends hidden/multiple test sets and Spearman rank-correlation checks to keep surrogate rankings valid for downstream design optimization.

articles.title: Towards Realistic Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Novel Evaluation Framework for Improving Generalization in OOD Detection
articles.tldr: Argues standard OOD-detection benchmarks are unrealistic and proposes semantic-preserving test sets plus a Generalizability Score to expose that benchmark AUROC does not reflect real-world reliability.
articles.contribution: Introduces CIFAR-10-R/CIFAR-100-R/ImageNet-30-R by applying semantic-preserving corruptions and augmentations, showing existing benchmarks convenience-sample low-diversity inliers and semantically-distant outliers that reward a harmful inductive bias.

articles.title: Towards Realistic Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Novel Evaluation Framework for Improving Generalization in OOD Detection
articles.tldr: Argues standard OOD-detection benchmarks are unrealistic and proposes semantic-preserving test sets plus a Generalizability Score to expose that benchmark AUROC does not reflect real-world reliability.
articles.contribution: Defines the Generalizability Score (AUROC on the realistic set minus AUROC on the standard set) to quantify how non-semantic transformations spuriously inflate OOD scores, demonstrating standard AUROC misrepresents deployment reliability.

articles.title: COUNTS: Benchmarking Object Detectors and Multimodal Large Language Models under Distribution Shifts
articles.tldr: Introduces COUNTS, a large real-world OOD benchmark for object detectors and MLLM grounding, revealing that IID gains and larger pretraining do not translate to OOD validity.
articles.contribution: Builds COUNTS from real-world images across 14 natural distribution shifts with a consistent category space per domain, arguing synthetic-corruption benchmarks and scene-specific datasets give biased robustness assessments.

articles.title: COUNTS: Benchmarking Object Detectors and Multimodal Large Language Models under Distribution Shifts
articles.tldr: Introduces COUNTS, a large real-world OOD benchmark for object detectors and MLLM grounding, revealing that IID gains and larger pretraining do not translate to OOD validity.
articles.contribution: Shows on the O(OD)2 benchmark that IID improvements do not translate to OOD generalization (stronger NAS-FPN neck / FreeAnchor head worsen OOD) and that larger pretraining data or self-supervision give little OOD benefit.

articles.title: COUNTS: Benchmarking Object Detectors and Multimodal Large Language Models under Distribution Shifts
articles.tldr: Introduces COUNTS, a large real-world OOD benchmark for object detectors and MLLM grounding, revealing that IID gains and larger pretraining do not translate to OOD validity.
articles.contribution: Defines OOD for MLLMs as shifts between in-context examples and test samples and shows spurious correlations planted in the ICE mislead grounding, dropping Gemini-1.5 accuracy from 57.0% to 28.0% (a 50.88% relative fall).

articles.title: Robustness May be More Brittle than We Think under Different Degrees of Distribution Shifts
articles.tldr: Shows OOD-generalization evaluations at a single fixed shift degree yield biased conclusions and advocates evaluating across a broad range of graduated shift degrees.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that evaluating OOD generalization at a largely fixed degree of distribution shift can over- or under-estimate true performance and mask very different worst-case behaviors between models.

articles.title: Robustness May be More Brittle than We Think under Different Degrees of Distribution Shifts
articles.tldr: Shows OOD-generalization evaluations at a single fixed shift degree yield biased conclusions and advocates evaluating across a broad range of graduated shift degrees.
articles.contribution: Constructs NoisyMNIST/RotatedMNIST/LowLightCIFAR10 with ten graduated shift degrees to sample the shift-magnitude axis, revealing model robustness is brittle and inconsistent across degrees.

articles.title: MiroEval: Benchmarking Multimodal Deep Research Agents in Process and Outcome
articles.tldr: Process-centric benchmark and LLM-judge framework for evaluating deep-research agents, with judge-robustness and human-alignment checks.
articles.contribution: Argues output-only report scoring under-represents research quality and adds process-centric evaluation of the search/reasoning trajectory that catches failures invisible to final-report metrics.

articles.title: MiroEval: Benchmarking Multimodal Deep Research Agents in Process and Outcome
articles.tldr: Process-centric benchmark and LLM-judge framework for evaluating deep-research agents, with judge-robustness and human-alignment checks.
articles.contribution: Quantifies LLM-judge reliability by re-running the judge and swapping judge models, reporting score dispersion and rank stability plus human-alignment correlations.

articles.title: MiroEval: Benchmarking Multimodal Deep Research Agents in Process and Outcome
articles.tldr: Process-centric benchmark and LLM-judge framework for evaluating deep-research agents, with judge-robustness and human-alignment checks.
articles.contribution: Grounds the task set in real user research needs via a dual-path construction and multi-stage filtering rather than synthetic prompts, targeting ecological representativeness.

articles.title: Robust Checkpoint Selection for Multimodal LLMs via Agentic Evaluation and Stability-Aware Ranking
articles.tldr: Reframes MLLM checkpoint selection as robust decision-making under evaluation noise and shows OCR data quality is a precondition for reliable ranking.
articles.contribution: Shows pointwise LLM scoring is unstable for ranking checkpoints and that listwise/pairwise judging plus a subsampling bootstrap confidence estimator give far more reliable selection.

articles.title: Robust Checkpoint Selection for Multimodal LLMs via Agentic Evaluation and Stability-Aware Ranking
articles.tldr: Reframes MLLM checkpoint selection as robust decision-making under evaluation noise and shows OCR data quality is a precondition for reliable ranking.
articles.contribution: Identifies OCR readability of eval samples as a confounder: unreadable inputs make measured score differences reflect input ambiguity rather than model capability, so data curation is a prerequisite for valid comparison.

articles.title: Robust Checkpoint Selection for Multimodal LLMs via Agentic Evaluation and Stability-Aware Ranking
articles.tldr: Reframes MLLM checkpoint selection as robust decision-making under evaluation noise and shows OCR data quality is a precondition for reliable ranking.
articles.contribution: Uses curated real-world data instead of static benchmarks to make checkpoint selection align with in-the-wild deployment behavior.

articles.title: WorldVQA: Measuring Atomic World Knowledge in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.tldr: WorldVQA benchmark isolates atomic visual world knowledge from reasoning to measure visual factuality, with contamination control and calibration analysis.
articles.contribution: Decouples visual knowledge retrieval from multi-step reasoning so the score measures factual visual knowledge rather than conflating it with reasoning ability, addressing discriminant validity.

articles.title: WorldVQA: Measuring Atomic World Knowledge in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.tldr: WorldVQA benchmark isolates atomic visual world knowledge from reasoning to measure visual factuality, with contamination control and calibration analysis.
articles.contribution: Controls train/test leakage by deduplicating candidate images against large web corpora with embedding similarity and re-collecting items from video screenshots to avoid memorized image-answer pairs.

articles.title: WorldVQA: Measuring Atomic World Knowledge in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.tldr: WorldVQA benchmark isolates atomic visual world knowledge from reasoning to measure visual factuality, with contamination control and calibration analysis.
articles.contribution: Uses a dual-gate ground-truth pipeline (automated fact-check plus human blind validation) and validates the automatic judge against human agreement to secure annotation fidelity.

articles.title: WebCompass: Towards Multimodal Web Coding Evaluation for Code Language Models
articles.tldr: WebCompass multimodal web-coding benchmark whose contribution is task-aware evaluation validity: judge selection, Agent-as-a-Judge, stability, and aggregation.
articles.contribution: Selects the LLM-judge by measured agreement with human ratings and imposes safeguards (checklist immutability, selector-only adaptation, mandatory evidence grounding) to make the judge a reliable measurement instrument.

articles.title: WebCompass: Towards Multimodal Web Coding Evaluation for Code Language Models
articles.tldr: WebCompass multimodal web-coding benchmark whose contribution is task-aware evaluation validity: judge selection, Agent-as-a-Judge, stability, and aggregation.
articles.contribution: Introduces an Agent-as-a-Judge harness that executes generated sites in a real browser via MCP and synthesizes tests, arguing static screenshot/DOM/pass@k metrics under-represent the interactive+visual web-coding construct.

articles.title: WebCompass: Towards Multimodal Web Coding Evaluation for Code Language Models
articles.tldr: WebCompass multimodal web-coding benchmark whose contribution is task-aware evaluation validity: judge selection, Agent-as-a-Judge, stability, and aggregation.
articles.contribution: Uses a Worst-of-N protocol to expose that Pass@1 masks output inconsistency, quantifying how far single-sample scores degrade under repeated sampling.

articles.title: WebCompass: Towards Multimodal Web Coding Evaluation for Code Language Models
articles.tldr: WebCompass multimodal web-coding benchmark whose contribution is task-aware evaluation validity: judge selection, Agent-as-a-Judge, stability, and aggregation.
articles.contribution: Shows the choice of aggregation (harmonic vs arithmetic mean over dimensions) reverses model rankings, so multi-requirement scoring must reward consistency rather than peak subtask wins.

articles.title: A Novel Psychometrics-Based Approach to Developing Professional Competency Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Psychometrics/Evidence-Centered-Design approach to building valid, reliable, contamination-free LLM competency benchmarks, piloted on a pedagogy benchmark.
articles.contribution: Applies Evidence-Centered Design (Proficiency/Task/Evidence models) and a construct-oriented causal theory of measurement to define the target competency before items exist, remedying benchmarks that lack an operational construct definition.

articles.title: A Novel Psychometrics-Based Approach to Developing Professional Competency Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Psychometrics/Evidence-Centered-Design approach to building valid, reliable, contamination-free LLM competency benchmarks, piloted on a pedagogy benchmark.
articles.contribution: Authors thousands of original expert-written items via a multi-phase review to avoid data contamination and leakage from the training corpus, tying items to Bloom's-taxonomy cognitive levels.

articles.title: A Novel Psychometrics-Based Approach to Developing Professional Competency Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Psychometrics/Evidence-Centered-Design approach to building valid, reliable, contamination-free LLM competency benchmarks, piloted on a pedagogy benchmark.
articles.contribution: Advocates Item Response Theory over Classical Test Theory for LLM evaluation, enabling prediction of unseen-item performance, model equating across different item sets, and item difficulty/discrimination estimation.

articles.title: GG-BBQ: German Gender Bias Benchmark for Question Answering
articles.tldr: GG-BBQ German gender-bias QA benchmark shows machine translation degrades the construct validity of a bias measure and refines the bias-score metric.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that naively machine-translating an English bias benchmark into grammatically-gendered German breaks item gender-neutrality and leaks the answer, so raw MT invalidates the bias construct without manual expert correction.

articles.title: GG-BBQ: German Gender Bias Benchmark for Question Answering
articles.tldr: GG-BBQ German gender-bias QA benchmark shows machine translation degrades the construct validity of a bias measure and refines the bias-score metric.
articles.contribution: Refines the bias-score computation, adopting a difference-based bias metric rather than reusing the ambiguous-context score for disambiguated contexts, which otherwise misrepresents bias direction/magnitude.

articles.title: Dynamic Human Evaluation for Relative Model Comparisons
articles.tldr: A statistical framework quantifying the minimum human-annotation effort needed to decide which NLG model is better with high probability.
articles.contribution: Uses a one-sided Hoeffding bound to compute, per labelling strategy, the minimum number of human annotations needed to declare the better NLG model at a target confidence, turning human evaluation into a power-analysis problem.

articles.title: Dynamic Human Evaluation for Relative Model Comparisons
articles.tldr: A statistical framework quantifying the minimum human-annotation effort needed to decide which NLG model is better with high probability.
articles.contribution: Empirically measures how inter-annotator agreement and decision stability vary across repeated crowdsourced rounds and comparison difficulty, exposing reproducibility limits of human NLG evaluation.

articles.title: Are AI-Generated Driving Videos Ready for Autonomous Driving? A Diagnostic Evaluation Framework
articles.tldr: ADGV-Bench/ADGVE diagnostic framework showing raw AI-generated driving videos harm perception training unless quality-filtered, addressing validity of synthetic data.
articles.contribution: Shows synthetic driving videos carry generative artifacts that confound downstream perception, so a learned quality gate must filter clips before they can validly augment training/evaluation data.

articles.title: Are AI-Generated Driving Videos Ready for Autonomous Driving? A Diagnostic Evaluation Framework
articles.tldr: ADGV-Bench/ADGVE diagnostic framework showing raw AI-generated driving videos harm perception training unless quality-filtered, addressing validity of synthetic data.
articles.contribution: Argues distributional metrics (FID/FVD) and generic video-quality metrics misrepresent driving-video usefulness because they miss physics/temporal failures and do not enforce traffic-rule plausibility.

articles.title: A Hierarchical Error Framework for Reliable Automated Coding in Communication Research: Applications to Health and Political Communication
articles.tldr: Hierarchical Error Correction reframes automated content-analysis coding as a measurement problem, mapping model failures to layered validity threats.
articles.contribution: Treats LLM-based automated coding as measurement, decomposing coder failures into knowledge/reasoning/complexity error layers mapped to construct and criterion validity, and correcting them to improve coding accuracy.

articles.title: A Hierarchical Error Framework for Reliable Automated Coding in Communication Research: Applications to Health and Political Communication
articles.tldr: Hierarchical Error Correction reframes automated content-analysis coding as a measurement problem, mapping model failures to layered validity threats.
articles.contribution: Shows the correction framework transfers across domains and multiple LLM coders, arguing the error structure is a task-level measurement property rather than a model-specific quirk.

articles.title: DCR-Consistency: Divide-Conquer-Reasoning for Consistency Evaluation and Improvement of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: DCR-Consistency proposes a sentence-level divide-conquer LLM-judge for consistency/factuality evaluation that correlates with humans better than ROUGE/BERTScore/G-Eval.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates token-similarity metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) misrepresent semantic consistency, failing badly on adversarial paraphrases, so they are surface proxies rather than measures of holistic equivalence.

articles.title: DCR-Consistency: Divide-Conquer-Reasoning for Consistency Evaluation and Improvement of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: DCR-Consistency proposes a sentence-level divide-conquer LLM-judge for consistency/factuality evaluation that correlates with humans better than ROUGE/BERTScore/G-Eval.
articles.contribution: Improves LLM-judge reliability for factual/consistency evaluation via sentence-to-paragraph decomposition that avoids hallucinated verbal scores and better matches human judgments than paragraph-level judges.

articles.title: Rectify Evaluation Preference: Improving LLMs' Critique on Math Reasoning via Perplexity-aware Reinforcement Learning
articles.tldr: Quantifies an LLM math-critic's self-preference and perplexity-driven judging bias and corrects it with perplexity-aware GRPO.
articles.contribution: Introduces the One-to-many Problem-Solution benchmark (1,890 samples, same problems/answers) and a Balance Indicator (BI=FPR-FNR) to quantify LLM-critic reliability, revealing a self-preference bias: each model gives markedly higher BI judging its own solutions than others' (Qwen 66.03 self vs 2.54 cross; LLaMA 17.78 vs -30.48).

articles.title: Rectify Evaluation Preference: Improving LLMs' Critique on Math Reasoning via Perplexity-aware Reinforcement Learning
articles.tldr: Quantifies an LLM math-critic's self-preference and perplexity-driven judging bias and corrects it with perplexity-aware GRPO.
articles.contribution: Statistical preference analysis finds a significant negative correlation (p<0.05, all three critics) between solution perplexity and BI: critics judge lower-perplexity (more self-similar) solutions as correct, so the verdict is confounded by stylistic similarity rather than actual correctness.

articles.title: SIQA: Toward Reliable Scientific Image Quality Assessment
articles.tldr: Shows MLLM agreement with expert quality ratings decouples from actual scientific understanding, and that MCQ scores are driven by response biases.
articles.contribution: Disentangles rating-alignment (SIQA-S) from comprehension (SIQA-U) and documents a consistent decoupling: MLLMs reach SRCC 0.7-0.8 with expert ratings yet only 48.3% on Yes/No verification and 30.0% on How-justification, so scoring agreement is a surface proxy that does not reflect scientific understanding.

articles.title: SIQA: Toward Reliable Scientific Image Quality Assessment
articles.tldr: Shows MLLM agreement with expert quality ratings decouples from actual scientific understanding, and that MCQ scores are driven by response biases.
articles.contribution: Shows the poor SIQA-U scores stem from systematic response biases (option-'A' preference on Yes/No, DeepSeek-VL2's strong A-skew, Gemini's D-skew) rather than reasoning, and mitigates them via benchmark refinements (negated Yes/No phrasing, option shuffling) that remove positional/linguistic-prior shortcut cues.

articles.title: Prompt-Dependent Ranking of Large Language Models with Uncertainty Quantification
articles.tldr: Provides statistically valid, prompt-dependent rank inference for LLM leaderboards, showing many apparent rank differences are not significant.
articles.contribution: Develops contextual Bradley-Terry-Luce rank inference with simultaneous confidence sets for pairwise utility differences (max-type statistics, bootstrap covariance), showing on ~55k Arena human comparisons that many apparent leaderboard rank differences are not statistically distinguishable and should yield partial orders, not strict rankings.

articles.title: Prompt-Dependent Ranking of Large Language Models with Uncertainty Quantification
articles.tldr: Provides statistically valid, prompt-dependent rank inference for LLM leaderboards, showing many apparent rank differences are not significant.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates rankings vary substantially with prompt characteristics (length, semantic category) with rank reversals at utility-function intersections, so a single global leaderboard utility that averages across heterogeneous prompts fails to transport across prompt distributions and the induced ranking becomes only partially identified for longer prompts.

articles.title: OrigamiBench: An Interactive Environment to Synthesize Flat-Foldable Origamis
articles.tldr: Interactive origami benchmark whose associative-vs-causal design exposes that VLMs pass by visual-similarity shortcuts, not causal fold reasoning.
articles.contribution: The Associative-vs-Causal distractor design exposes a visual-similarity shortcut: Qwen3-VL-32B scores 96.18% when distractors are unrelated origamis but collapses to 43.37% when distractors come from the same foldable sequence, showing high benchmark scores are inflated by surface pattern-matching rather than causal fold reasoning.

articles.title: OrigamiBench: An Interactive Environment to Synthesize Flat-Foldable Origamis
articles.tldr: Interactive origami benchmark whose associative-vs-causal design exposes that VLMs pass by visual-similarity shortcuts, not causal fold reasoning.
articles.contribution: Builds a closed-loop, foldability-verified operationalization (Flat-Folder solver checking Maekawa/Kawasaki theorems) with hard-negative causal distractors drawn from the same fold sequence, so measured 'geometric reasoning' reflects genuine fold-transition understanding rather than static perceptual similarity.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Graph Theory: Implications for Computing Education
articles.tldr: Uses a controlled solved-vs-unsolved graph-theory design with blind expert review to test whether fluent LLM reasoning reflects genuine understanding.
articles.contribution: Uses a controlled solved-vs-unsolved problem pair with blind evaluation by a graph-theory faculty expert (deliberately not an AI expert) to show the model produces a correct expert-confirmed proof on the solved problem but no novel insight on the open one, arguing fluent/coherent reasoning is a misleading proxy for genuine mathematical understanding.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Graph Theory: Implications for Computing Education
articles.tldr: Uses a controlled solved-vs-unsolved graph-theory design with blind expert review to test whether fluent LLM reasoning reflects genuine understanding.
articles.contribution: The solved/unsolved pairing acts as a memorization control: strong performance on the literature-documented (likely in-training) solved problem versus stalling on the genuinely open problem indicates success reflects reproduction of established results rather than reasoning that generalizes to novel problems.

articles.title: How Far Are Vision-Language Models from Constructing the Real World? A Benchmark for Physical Generative Reasoning
articles.tldr: DreamHouse benchmark shows structural/physical validity is orthogonal to visual realism and that shortcuts and agentic protocol confound VLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Establishes physical/structural validity as an evaluation axis orthogonal to visual realism, showing perceptual metrics (CLIP/DINO, alpha-weighted MSE visual fidelity) are invalid proxies for buildability: GPT-5 leads structurally (79.2% Planner-Atomic) yet scores lowest visually (0.312), and topological proximity does not predict structural pass.

articles.title: How Far Are Vision-Language Models from Constructing the Real World? A Benchmark for Physical Generative Reasoning
articles.tldr: DreamHouse benchmark shows structural/physical validity is orthogonal to visual realism and that shortcuts and agentic protocol confound VLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Documents that an initial bridge-generation testbed let frontier VLMs satisfy all validation tests by analytically recovering a few geometric parameters from the image (a shortcut bypassing structural understanding), motivating the switch to timber framing where load-path topology is not legible from exterior renders.

articles.title: How Far Are Vision-Language Models from Constructing the Real World? A Benchmark for Physical Generative Reasoning
articles.tldr: DreamHouse benchmark shows structural/physical validity is orthogonal to visual realism and that shortcuts and agentic protocol confound VLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows the agentic protocol (Planner-Atomic/Reactive/Managed) dominates model choice: Gemini swings from 45.4% to 78.5% structural pass and overtakes GPT-5 under Planner-Managed despite trailing it by 34 points under Planner-Atomic, so single-protocol leaderboards conflate scaffold design with model capability.

articles.title: LLMs Struggle to Measure What Distinguishes Students of Different Proficiency Levels: A Study of Item Discrimination in Reading Comprehension Assessment
articles.tldr: Evaluates whether 42 LLMs can estimate psychometric item discrimination, finding weak/reversed alignment with human-calibrated values.
articles.contribution: Evaluates 42 LLMs on zero-shot direct prediction of CTT item discrimination against human-calibrated values (793 Cambridge reading items), finding near-zero or negative Spearman alignment (best only ~0.15) plus distributional compression (rarely predicting low/negative discrimination), i.e. systematic calibration bias, so LLMs are unreliable as direct discrimination estimators.

articles.title: LLMs Struggle to Measure What Distinguishes Students of Different Proficiency Levels: A Study of Item Discrimination in Reading Comprehension Assessment
articles.tldr: Evaluates whether 42 LLMs can estimate psychometric item discrimination, finding weak/reversed alignment with human-calibrated values.
articles.contribution: Tests a second instrument, response-based CTT calibration treating LLM answers as synthetic student responses; the all-persona pool reaches Spearman 0.241 (95% CI [0.174,0.307]) vs a null ~0.001, a stronger but still limited signal, and proficiency-conditioned personas do not consistently improve alignment.

articles.title: SciIF: Benchmarking Scientific Instruction Following Towards Rigorous Scientific Intelligence
articles.tldr: SciIF reframes scientific evaluation around auditable constraint compliance, exposing a large 'right-answer-wrong-reasons' gap beyond final-answer correctness.
articles.contribution: Separates answer correctness from constraint compliance and shows a systematic 'right-for-the-wrong-reasons' gap: even strong models exceed 80% correctness but strict multi-constraint compliance stays below 30% (best 29.6%), demonstrating final-answer accuracy is a surface proxy for scientific validity.

articles.title: SciIF: Benchmarking Scientific Instruction Following Towards Rigorous Scientific Intelligence
articles.tldr: SciIF reframes scientific evaluation around auditable constraint compliance, exposing a large 'right-answer-wrong-reasons' gap beyond final-answer correctness.
articles.contribution: Proposes an auditable generate-then-audit protocol that prioritizes deterministic checks (LaTeX/numeric equivalence, unit declarations, evidence-pattern matching) and falls back to two independent LLM judges (GPT-5.1 + Gemini-3-Flash, both must PASS) with strictness aligned on a held-out calibration set, making constraint-compliance judging reproducible and evidence-based rather than judge guesswork.

articles.title: Med-CRAFT: Automated Construction of Interpretable and Multi-Hop Video Workloads via Knowledge Graph Traversal
articles.tldr: Neuro-symbolic KG-traversal pipeline for benchmark synthesis that guarantees verifiable logic provenance and validates intended reasoning complexity.
articles.contribution: Replaces stochastic MLLM generation and costly/subjective manual annotation with deterministic knowledge-graph traversal (Grounding DINO + CLIP-ViT + Hungarian tracking to tubelets, then DFS over a spatiotemporal KG), so every synthesized QA item carries verifiable Chain-of-Thought provenance and visual grounding, mitigating hallucinated or subjective ground truth.

articles.title: Med-CRAFT: Automated Construction of Interpretable and Multi-Hop Video Workloads via Knowledge Graph Traversal
articles.tldr: Neuro-symbolic KG-traversal pipeline for benchmark synthesis that guarantees verifiable logic provenance and validates intended reasoning complexity.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory validity evidence via a logic-alignment analysis showing a strong diagonal correlation between the pipeline's prescribed hop count and the Oracle MLLM's inferred reasoning hops, plus an adversarial GPT-4V judge that filters ambiguous/unanswerable queries, arguing the benchmark encodes the intended multi-hop complexity without black-box semantic drift.

articles.title: When LLM Reward Design Fails: Diagnostic-Driven Refinement for Sparse Structured RL
articles.tldr: Frames LLM reward design as debugging, diagnosing reward hacking and using ablation controls to separate real gains from selection/training confounds.
articles.contribution: Identifies 'reward flooding' as a Goodhart failure of LLM-generated reward shaping: continuous per-step bonuses (e.g. +0.02/step) let the PPO agent accumulate high shaped reward at ~5% success by walking in circles, corrupting reward as a proxy for task completion, and adds a high-reward/low-success diagnostic to detect it.

articles.title: When LLM Reward Design Fails: Diagnostic-Driven Refinement for Sparse Structured RL
articles.tldr: Frames LLM reward design as debugging, diagnosing reward hacking and using ablation controls to separate real gains from selection/training confounds.
articles.contribution: Uses ablation controls to isolate the taxonomy-prompt mechanism from confounds: metrics-only re-prompting collapses gains (DoorKey-8x8 97.6%->68.6%; KeyCorridor 86.7%->11.5%), a static-vocabulary control recovers much (87.6%; 70.7%), and budget-matched and Best-of-3 comparisons separate refinement from selection and extra-training-time effects.

articles.title: When LLM Reward Design Fails: Diagnostic-Driven Refinement for Sparse Structured RL
articles.tldr: Frames LLM reward design as debugging, diagnosing reward hacking and using ablation controls to separate real gains from selection/training confounds.
articles.contribution: Quantifies high seed-to-seed variance (KeyCorridor std 28.5%) and runs a crossed 5x5 variance decomposition showing LLM-generation variance dominates RL-training variance (DoorKey-8x8 LLM std 47.5% vs RL 0.3%; crossed share 96% but wide [66,100]% bootstrap CI), tempering exact mechanism claims and applying Holm-Bonferroni (9/12 comparisons significant).

articles.title: When LLM Reward Design Fails: Diagnostic-Driven Refinement for Sparse Structured RL
articles.tldr: Frames LLM reward design as debugging, diagnosing reward hacking and using ablation controls to separate real gains from selection/training confounds.
articles.contribution: Characterizes the method's boundary of validity: success-based diagnostics generate false positives on dense-reward MuJoCo locomotion (which lacks a binary success signal), systematically degrading the feedback loop, showing the diagnostic does not transfer beyond sparse-structured tasks.

articles.title: On the Assessment of Benchmark Suites for Algorithm Comparison
articles.tldr: Uses Bayesian 2-parameter IRT to statistically assess whether black-box optimization benchmark suites actually discriminate algorithms.
articles.contribution: Applies a Bayesian 2PL IRT model to quantify each benchmark function's difficulty and discrimination, exposing low-discrimination items that fail to reliably distinguish optimization algorithms.

articles.title: On the Assessment of Benchmark Suites for Algorithm Comparison
articles.tldr: Uses Bayesian 2-parameter IRT to statistically assess whether black-box optimization benchmark suites actually discriminate algorithms.
articles.contribution: Uses item/test-information curves to judge whether a whole benchmark suite is suitable for fair algorithm comparison, finding BBOB too hard and PBO too easy relative to current algorithms.

articles.title: An Item Response Theory-based R Module for Algorithm Portfolio Analysis
articles.tldr: An IRT-based R package and Shiny tool that evaluates algorithm portfolios via psychometric difficulty, discrimination, consistency and anomalousness.
articles.contribution: Adapts continuous/polytomous IRT to compute algorithm consistency, anomalousness and difficulty limits, turning raw performance scores into psychometric reliability diagnostics of an evaluation.

articles.title: An Item Response Theory-based R Module for Algorithm Portfolio Analysis
articles.tldr: An IRT-based R package and Shiny tool that evaluates algorithm portfolios via psychometric difficulty, discrimination, consistency and anomalousness.
articles.contribution: Uses the problem-difficulty spectrum to reveal where a test-instance set discriminates algorithms, helping flag portfolios evaluated on too-narrow or non-representative instance sets.

articles.title: From Data Leak to Secret Misses: The Impact of Data Leakage on Secret Detection Models
articles.tldr: Shows duplication and train/test data leakage in the SecretBench benchmark substantially inflate AI secret-detector performance, masking real-world effectiveness.
articles.contribution: Detects exact and near-duplicate secret contexts in SecretBench and shows that train/test overlap lets models memorize rather than generalize, inflating reported detection scores.

articles.title: From Data Leak to Secret Misses: The Impact of Data Leakage on Secret Detection Models
articles.tldr: Shows duplication and train/test data leakage in the SecretBench benchmark substantially inflate AI secret-detector performance, masking real-world effectiveness.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that deduplicated Unique-set evaluation collapses metrics to true generalization levels, quantifying the real-world effectiveness gap of secret detectors.

articles.title: Shortcut Learning Susceptibility in Vision Classifiers
articles.tldr: Controlled shortcut-injection study measuring how CNNs, MLPs and ViTs rely on spurious cues instead of genuine class features.
articles.contribution: Injects positional and intensity shortcuts deterministically correlated with labels and uses the accuracy difference between shortcut and clean test sets to quantify each architecture's reliance on spurious cues.

articles.title: Shortcut Learning Susceptibility in Vision Classifiers
articles.tldr: Controlled shortcut-injection study measuring how CNNs, MLPs and ViTs rely on spurious cues instead of genuine class features.
articles.contribution: Shows shortcut reliance causes large accuracy drops on shortcut-free test sets, characterizing the out-of-distribution generalization failure induced by spurious correlations.

articles.title: LibriVAD: A Scalable Open Dataset with Deep Learning Benchmarks for Voice Activity Detection
articles.tldr: A large, systematically controlled open VAD benchmark built to remove structural dataset biases and enable robust, OOD-aware voice-activity-detection evaluation.
articles.contribution: Argues prior VAD datasets are small and structurally biased (fixed silence-at-ends layout that models overfit) and builds a systematically SNR/SSR-controlled, representative benchmark for fair comparison.

articles.title: LibriVAD: A Scalable Open Dataset with Deep Learning Benchmarks for Voice Activity Detection
articles.tldr: A large, systematically controlled open VAD benchmark built to remove structural dataset biases and enable robust, OOD-aware voice-activity-detection evaluation.
articles.contribution: Evaluates out-of-distribution generalization on reverberant VOiCES with disjoint speakers, showing larger and SSR-balanced training data improves OOD AUC.

articles.title: The LUMirage: An independent evaluation of zero-shot performance in the LUMIR challenge
articles.tldr: Independent re-evaluation refuting the LUMIR registration challenge's zero-shot generalization claims by correcting instrumentation bias.
articles.contribution: Identifies instrumentation biases (downsampling that weakens iterative baselines, SLANT labelmaps producing spurious Dice, preprocessing crops) that confounded the challenge's deep-vs-iterative comparison.

articles.title: The LUMirage: An independent evaluation of zero-shot performance in the LUMIR challenge
articles.tldr: Independent re-evaluation refuting the LUMIR registration challenge's zero-shot generalization claims by correcting instrumentation bias.
articles.contribution: Re-evaluation shows deep registration degrades significantly on out-of-distribution contrasts (T2, T2*, FLAIR), refuting the claim of universal zero-shot superiority over iterative methods.

articles.title: Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Climate-Aware Yield Prediction with Earth Observation Data
articles.tldr: First large-scale out-of-distribution evaluation of crop-yield models, showing in-distribution accuracy overstates cross-region and year-ahead generalization.
articles.contribution: Uses leave-one-cluster-out cross-validation over USDA regions and year-ahead splits to expose large OOD generalization gaps hidden by conventional in-distribution evaluation.

articles.title: Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Climate-Aware Yield Prediction with Earth Observation Data
articles.tldr: First large-scale out-of-distribution evaluation of crop-yield models, showing in-distribution accuracy overstates cross-region and year-ahead generalization.
articles.contribution: Attributes MMST-ViT's sharp OOD degradation to reliance on regional memorization rather than genuine spatio-temporal signal, a confound in-domain metrics hide.

articles.title: BIS Reasoning 1.0: The First Large-Scale Japanese Benchmark for Belief-Inconsistent Syllogistic Reasoning
articles.tldr: Japanese belief-inconsistent syllogism benchmark exposing belief-bias confound and prompt sensitivity in LLM reasoning scores.
articles.contribution: Constructs 5,000 logically-valid-but-belief-inconsistent syllogisms so belief plausibility is decorrelated from validity, isolating belief bias as the shortcut/confound that inflates accuracy on belief-aligned items.

articles.title: BIS Reasoning 1.0: The First Large-Scale Japanese Benchmark for Belief-Inconsistent Syllogistic Reasoning
articles.tldr: Japanese belief-inconsistent syllogism benchmark exposing belief-bias confound and prompt sensitivity in LLM reasoning scores.
articles.contribution: Shows measured reasoning accuracy is highly sensitive to prompt design and inference-time reasoning effort, so a single-prompt zero-shot score is an unreliable measure of reasoning fidelity.

articles.title: From Prompt to Product: A Human-Centered Benchmark of Agentic App Generation Systems
articles.tldr: Human-centered prompt-to-app benchmark showing isolated ratings are unreliable and only pairwise comparisons discriminate systems.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates reference-free isolated human ratings are statistically indistinguishable across systems while side-by-side pairwise comparisons reliably separate them, arguing pairwise is the only sound measurement design for prompt-to-app quality.

articles.title: From Prompt to Product: A Human-Centered Benchmark of Agentic App Generation Systems
articles.tldr: Human-centered prompt-to-app benchmark showing isolated ratings are unreliable and only pairwise comparisons discriminate systems.
articles.contribution: Shows visual polish is a surface proxy misaligned with functional reliability and user trust, so aesthetics-based quality signals misrepresent the underlying app-quality construct.

articles.title: PowerAgentBench-SS: A Benchmark for Agentic AI in Power System Steady-State Studies
articles.tldr: Agentic power-system benchmark whose hidden physical validator scores evidence-backed versus unsupported claims, exposing harness and leakage effects.
articles.contribution: Separates submitted, evidence-backed, and found recall so the agent scaffold, validation-budget use, and type coercions are measured as harness confounds rather than folded into a single answer-only score.

articles.title: PowerAgentBench-SS: A Benchmark for Agentic AI in Power System Steady-State Studies
articles.tldr: Agentic power-system benchmark whose hidden physical validator scores evidence-backed versus unsupported claims, exposing harness and leakage effects.
articles.contribution: Uses a public/hidden split where a hidden evaluator recomputes physical validity and oracle rankings, limiting benchmark leakage so scores reflect tool-supported engineering decisions, not access to oracle labels.

articles.title: From Static Benchmarks to Dynamic Protocol: Agent-Centric Text Anomaly Detection for Evaluating LLM Reasoning
articles.tldr: Agent-centric dynamic benchmark protocol regenerating validated anomaly-detection problems to resist contamination, saturation, and harness confounds.
articles.contribution: Replaces finite static datasets with a teacher-orchestrator-student loop generating fresh, validity-checked anomaly problems, mitigating train/test memorization and benchmark saturation that inflate MMLU/GSM8K-style scores.

articles.title: From Static Benchmarks to Dynamic Protocol: Agent-Centric Text Anomaly Detection for Evaluating LLM Reasoning
articles.tldr: Agent-centric dynamic benchmark protocol regenerating validated anomaly-detection problems to resist contamination, saturation, and harness confounds.
articles.contribution: Shows an orchestrator LLM validating clarity/coherence/fairness is essential: without it, difficulty is artificially inflated by ambiguous or ill-posed items rather than genuine reasoning difficulty.

articles.title: Benchmarking Trustworthiness in Multimodal LLMs for Video Understanding
articles.tldr: Trustworthiness benchmark for video LLMs across five dimensions, arguing accuracy benchmarks under-represent robustness, safety, fairness, and privacy.
articles.contribution: Argues accuracy-focused videoLLM benchmarks misrepresent trustworthiness and operationalizes it across truthfulness, robustness, safety, fairness, and privacy over 30 tasks to close the construct-coverage gap.

articles.title: Benchmarking Trustworthiness in Multimodal LLMs for Video Understanding
articles.tldr: Trustworthiness benchmark for video LLMs across five dimensions, arguing accuracy benchmarks under-represent robustness, safety, fairness, and privacy.
articles.contribution: Measures cross-modal perturbation resilience and temporal consistency as robustness under real-world spatiotemporal risks, revealing reliability gaps that static accuracy metrics miss.

articles.title: Beyond Content Safety: Real-Time Monitoring for Reasoning Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Formalizes reasoning safety with a nine-type taxonomy and shows existing step-level scorers (PRMs, hallucination detectors) are unreliable for reasoning errors.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-as-critic hallucination detectors and process reward models are unreliable step-level scorers of reasoning correctness, motivating a taxonomy-embedded monitor with far higher localization accuracy and near-zero false positives.

articles.title: Beyond Content Safety: Real-Time Monitoring for Reasoning Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Formalizes reasoning safety with a nine-type taxonomy and shows existing step-level scorers (PRMs, hallucination detectors) are unreliable for reasoning errors.
articles.contribution: Defines reasoning safety via three formal properties and a nine-category unsafe-behavior taxonomy, establishing a construct orthogonal to content safety and validating its prevalence with a 4,155-chain human annotation study.

articles.title: FActBench: A Benchmark for Fine-grained Automatic Evaluation of LLM-Generated Text in the Medical Domain
articles.tldr: Medical fact-checking benchmark meta-evaluating NLI, CoT, and their unanimous vote against domain-expert judgment.
articles.contribution: Meta-evaluates automatic fact-checkers, showing the Unanimous Voting of CoT and NLI correlates best with domain-expert scores while raw FActScore severely underestimates factuality.

articles.title: FActBench: A Benchmark for Fine-grained Automatic Evaluation of LLM-Generated Text in the Medical Domain
articles.tldr: Medical fact-checking benchmark meta-evaluating NLI, CoT, and their unanimous vote against domain-expert judgment.
articles.contribution: Shows the factuality score depends on the knowledge source and combines intrinsic grounding-document and extrinsic Wikipedia checks so the metric captures true factuality rather than a source-dependent proxy.

articles.title: OVFact: Measuring and Improving Open-Vocabulary Factuality for Long Caption Models
articles.tldr: Reference-free open-vocabulary factuality metric for long captions unifying precision and recall and improving human agreement over ALOHa.
articles.contribution: Introduces a reference-free metric combining open-vocabulary detection/segmentation grounding for precision with a concept-vocabulary recall term, capturing descriptiveness that precision-only hallucination metrics ignore.

articles.title: OVFact: Measuring and Improving Open-Vocabulary Factuality for Long Caption Models
articles.tldr: Reference-free open-vocabulary factuality metric for long captions unifying precision and recall and improving human agreement over ALOHa.
articles.contribution: Shows prior metrics (CHAIR, ALOHa) can be gamed by short conservative captions and that ALOHa's one-to-one Hungarian matching is brittle without exhaustive references, biasing factuality scores.

articles.title: Whose Name Comes Up? II: Benchmarking and Intervention-Based Auditing of LLM-Based Scholar Recommendation
articles.tldr: Auditing benchmark for LLM scholar recommendation that separates model-infrastructure effects from end-user inference-time interventions.
articles.contribution: Shows end-user inference-time interventions (temperature, representation-constrained prompting, RAG) confound audit conclusions, so failures cannot be attributed to a model without controlling the deployment harness.

articles.title: Whose Name Comes Up? II: Benchmarking and Intervention-Based Auditing of LLM-Based Scholar Recommendation
articles.tldr: Auditing benchmark for LLM scholar recommendation that separates model-infrastructure effects from end-user inference-time interventions.
articles.contribution: Introduces per-model temperature calibration (sweeping t in {0..2}, picking the value maximizing factual accuracy at high validity) so 22-model comparisons are not confounded by a shared default temperature.

articles.title: I Think, Therefore I Am Under-Qualified? A Benchmark for Evaluating Linguistic Shibboleth Detection in LLM Hiring Evaluations
articles.tldr: Controlled-variation benchmark showing LLM hiring evaluators penalize hedging language (a gender shibboleth) despite equivalent content.
articles.contribution: Uses semantically-equivalent hedged/confident answer pairs to causally isolate hedging style as the driver of LLM hiring scores rather than content quality (a demographic-correlated shortcut feature).

articles.title: I Think, Therefore I Am Under-Qualified? A Benchmark for Evaluating Linguistic Shibboleth Detection in LLM Hiring Evaluations
articles.tldr: Controlled-variation benchmark showing LLM hiring evaluators penalize hedging language (a gender shibboleth) despite equivalent content.
articles.contribution: Shows the LLM evaluator's competence score is a surface proxy conflating confident communication style with competence, mis-measuring the intended hiring-quality construct.

articles.title: JudgeAgent: Beyond Static Benchmarks for Knowledge-Driven and Dynamic LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Knowledge-driven, difficulty-adaptive multi-turn interview framework to mitigate benchmark contamination and difficulty mismatch in LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Mitigates train/test contamination by dynamically synthesizing novel questions via context-graph traversal instead of reusing static benchmark items that models may have memorized.

articles.title: JudgeAgent: Beyond Static Benchmarks for Knowledge-Driven and Dynamic LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Knowledge-driven, difficulty-adaptive multi-turn interview framework to mitigate benchmark contamination and difficulty mismatch in LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Adds a difficulty-adaptive multi-turn interview (adaptive-testing-style) that aligns question difficulty with the target's estimated capability, yielding more precise capability estimates than fixed-difficulty tests.

articles.title: Can Consumer Chatbots Reason? A Student-Led Field Experiment Embedded in an "AI-for-All" Undergraduate Course
articles.tldr: Student-led field experiment evaluating consumer-chatbot reasoning, separating answer correctness from explanation validity and enumerating all four validity threats.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes 'reasoning' as two distinct observable proxies -- answer correctness vs explanation validity -- exposing frequent 'correct answer, invalid explanation' cases that accuracy-only benchmarks miss.

articles.title: Can Consumer Chatbots Reason? A Student-Led Field Experiment Embedded in an "AI-for-All" Undergraduate Course
articles.tldr: Student-led field experiment evaluating consumer-chatbot reasoning, separating answer correctness from explanation validity and enumerating all four validity threats.
articles.contribution: Documents internal-validity confounds of consumer-chatbot field evaluation: uncontrolled model versions/settings, follow-up prompting 'help' effects, and within-session non-independence/learning effects.

articles.title: Can Consumer Chatbots Reason? A Student-Led Field Experiment Embedded in an "AI-for-All" Undergraduate Course
articles.tldr: Student-led field experiment evaluating consumer-chatbot reasoning, separating answer correctness from explanation validity and enumerating all four validity threats.
articles.contribution: Provides an ecologically-valid end-user field evaluation complementing curated benchmarks, while flagging external-validity limits (single institution, student-crafted convenience prompt set).

articles.title: Too Vivid to Be Real? Benchmarking and Calibrating Generative Color Fidelity
articles.tldr: Shows T2I preference/aesthetic metrics are biased toward over-saturated images and builds a color-fidelity metric better aligned with human color-realism judgments.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates preference-trained metrics (PickScore, ImageReward, HPSv3, MPS) measure aesthetic vividness rather than color fidelity, and introduces CFM as a metric capturing the intended color-realism construct.

articles.title: Too Vivid to Be Real? Benchmarking and Calibrating Generative Color Fidelity
articles.tldr: Shows T2I preference/aesthetic metrics are biased toward over-saturated images and builds a color-fidelity metric better aligned with human color-realism judgments.
articles.contribution: Argues the saturation bias in existing metrics creates a Goodhart loop where T2I models over-optimize saturation/contrast to score higher, driving unrealistically vivid outputs.

articles.title: PoSh: Using Scene Graphs To Guide LLMs-as-a-Judge For Detailed Image Descriptions
articles.tldr: Scene-graph-guided open-weight LLM-as-judge metric (PoSh) for detailed image description, validated with the new human-annotated DOCENT art benchmark.
articles.contribution: Shows CIDEr/SPICE (designed for short texts) under-represent detailed-description quality, and PoSh's scene-graph-guided judge is a better proxy for human raters (+0.05 Spearman) while remaining replicable and interpretable.

articles.title: PoSh: Using Scene Graphs To Guide LLMs-as-a-Judge For Detailed Image Descriptions
articles.tldr: Scene-graph-guided open-weight LLM-as-judge metric (PoSh) for detailed image description, validated with the new human-annotated DOCENT art benchmark.
articles.contribution: DOCENT contributes granular + coarse expert art-annotation with agreement analysis and a double-penalty-avoidance protocol, giving reliable human ground truth for validating detailed-description metrics.

articles.title: Evaluation Metrics of Language Generation Models for Synthetic Traffic Generation Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows standard NLG metrics fail for single-prompt-multi-output synthetic traffic and proposes distribution-level metrics validated by noise-injection and human agreement.
articles.contribution: Shows averaged pairwise BLEU/ROUGE/CIDEr/SBERT favor head expressions and fail to capture the intended construct (distributional resemblance to real traffic), and proposes bag-level alignment/clustering/distribution metrics.

articles.title: Evaluation Metrics of Language Generation Models for Synthetic Traffic Generation Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows standard NLG metrics fail for single-prompt-multi-output synthetic traffic and proposes distribution-level metrics validated by noise-injection and human agreement.
