articles.contribution: Introduces a meta-evaluation protocol that ranks controlled noise-injected bags and checks whether metric rankings recover the true noise ordering (Spearman) plus human correlation, providing confirmatory validity evidence for STG metrics.

articles.title: Modeling Pathology-Like Behavioral Patterns in Language Models Through Behavioral Fine-Tuning
articles.tldr: Behavioral fine-tuning induces pathology-like distributional priors in LLMs, distinguishing genuine distributional shift from performative prompted role-play.
articles.contribution: Argues prompted persona simulation is a performative surface proxy that leaves the generative prior intact, and uses KL/JSD over next-token distributions to distinguish genuine induced state from surface role-play.

articles.title: Modeling Pathology-Like Behavioral Patterns in Language Models Through Behavioral Fine-Tuning
articles.tldr: Behavioral fine-tuning induces pathology-like distributional priors in LLMs, distinguishing genuine distributional shift from performative prompted role-play.
articles.contribution: Uses unrelated factual sentence stems as a control to rule out global distributional scrambling, establishing that the induced shift specifically targets self/social reasoning (discriminant/specificity validity).

articles.title: Emotional intelligence in large language models is fragmented across perception, cognition, and interaction
articles.tldr: Psychometrically-grounded EI benchmark (FACET) showing emotional intelligence in LLMs is fragmented and objective scores poorly predict interactive efficacy.
articles.contribution: Grounds EI measurement in the Mayer-Salovey-Caruso four-branch ability model with 480 expert-crafted items, distinguishing genuine affective competence from the superficial politeness prior benchmarks conflate with it.

articles.title: Emotional intelligence in large language models is fragmented across perception, cognition, and interaction
articles.tldr: Psychometrically-grounded EI benchmark (FACET) showing emotional intelligence in LLMs is fragmented and objective scores poorly predict interactive efficacy.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates objective emotion-recognition accuracy is a poor predictor of interactive efficacy (criterion-validity failure): GPT-5 tops objective accuracy but ranks near-last in interactive Elo.

articles.title: Emotional intelligence in large language models is fragmented across perception, cognition, and interaction
articles.tldr: Psychometrically-grounded EI benchmark (FACET) showing emotional intelligence in LLMs is fragmented and objective scores poorly predict interactive efficacy.
articles.contribution: Scores subjective interactive dimensions with double-blind Elo/TrueSkill pairwise comparisons to mitigate LLM-judge drift and intra-evaluator inconsistency rather than noisy Likert ratings.

articles.title: The Trust in AI-Generated Health Advice (TAIGHA) Scale and Short Version (TAIGHA-S): Development and Validation Study
articles.tldr: Develops and psychometrically validates the TAIGHA scale measuring user trust/distrust in AI-generated health advice, distinguishing trust from trustworthiness.
articles.contribution: Grounds the scale in McAllister's cognitive/affective trust theory and treats distrust as an orthogonal factor, correcting existing tech-trust scales that conflate trust with system trustworthiness and lack context specificity.

articles.title: The Trust in AI-Generated Health Advice (TAIGHA) Scale and Short Version (TAIGHA-S): Development and Validation Study
articles.tldr: Develops and psychometrically validates the TAIGHA scale measuring user trust/distrust in AI-generated health advice, distinguishing trust from trustworthiness.
articles.contribution: Establishes higher criterion validity for a context-specific trust scale: TAIGHA predicts actual advice-taking behavior (r=0.37) better than the generic Trust in Automated Systems Survey (r=0.26).

articles.title: The Trust in AI-Generated Health Advice (TAIGHA) Scale and Short Version (TAIGHA-S): Development and Validation Study
articles.tldr: Develops and psychometrically validates the TAIGHA scale measuring user trust/distrust in AI-generated health advice, distinguishing trust from trustworthiness.
articles.contribution: Establishes strong psychometric reliability and structure via CFA two-factor fit and internal-consistency estimates, delivering validated 10-item and 4-item instruments.

articles.title: Discovering Semantic Latent Structures in Psychological Scales: A Response-Free Pathway to Efficient Simplification
articles.tldr: Response-free psychological-scale simplification via sentence-embedding clustering, validated post-hoc with CFA, Cronbach's alpha and factor congruence.
articles.contribution: Tests whether semantic embedding structure preserves the intended construct/factor structure when items are dropped, using CFA (CFI/TLI/RMSEA), Cronbach's alpha and Adjusted Rand Index alignment to theoretical factors.

articles.title: Stories of Your Life as Others: A Round-Trip Evaluation of LLM-Generated Life Stories Conditioned on Rich Psychometric Profiles
articles.tldr: Round-trip personality-recovery validation: encode real HEXACO profiles into LLM life-stories then recover them, with leakage, contamination and bias controls.
articles.contribution: Uses sentence-level Jaccard leakage detection against HEXACO item stems plus an OLMo/Dolma out-of-corpus contamination control to rule out that recovery comes from questionnaire memorization or training-data overlap.

articles.title: Stories of Your Life as Others: A Round-Trip Evaluation of LLM-Generated Life Stories Conditioned on Rich Psychometric Profiles
articles.tldr: Round-trip personality-recovery validation: encode real HEXACO profiles into LLM life-stories then recover them, with leakage, contamination and bias controls.
articles.contribution: A three-stage bias decomposition separates the scorer's alignment-default resting bias (53% of Stage-2 distortion) from the conditioning signal (47%), showing recovered scores reflect personality content rather than scorer defaults.

articles.title: Stories of Your Life as Others: A Round-Trip Evaluation of LLM-Generated Life Stories Conditioned on Rich Psychometric Profiles
articles.tldr: Round-trip personality-recovery validation: encode real HEXACO profiles into LLM life-stories then recover them, with leakage, contamination and bias controls.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory (r=0.750 recovery, 85% of human test-retest ceiling) and falsification (masked forced-choice matching at ~79% vs 20% chance) evidence that generated narratives encode genuine personality signal.

articles.title: FinPersona-Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal Psychometric Stability of Autonomous Financial Agents
articles.tldr: FinPersona-Bench measures Mandate Salience Decay in LLM financial agents using a synthetic market whose hidden fundamental value gives objective, falsifiable ground truth.
articles.contribution: Synthetic market decoupling observable price from a hidden fundamental value supplies a mathematically-defined ground truth, and a static-vs-memory-re-grounded harness contrast isolates mandate drift as a context/harness effect rather than a reasoning failure.

articles.title: FinPersona-Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal Psychometric Stability of Autonomous Financial Agents
articles.tldr: FinPersona-Bench measures Mandate Salience Decay in LLM financial agents using a synthetic market whose hidden fundamental value gives objective, falsifiable ground truth.
articles.contribution: A placebo control (re-grounding works through mandate content, not text position) plus Big Five and numerical-only ablations give falsification evidence that the persona-scenario alignment result is not an MBTI framework artifact.

articles.title: MindShift: Analyzing Language Models' Reactions to Psychological Prompts
articles.tldr: MindShift adapts the MMPI-2 to LLMs and validates its reliability and construct validity as a psychometric instrument via directional bias shifts and Cronbach's alpha.
articles.contribution: Establishes MMPI reliability for LLMs via Cronbach's alpha around 0.8 (matching human MMPI-2) and reuses the MMPI's internal validity scales (VRIN/TRIN) to flag compromised model profiles.

articles.title: MindShift: Analyzing Language Models' Reactions to Psychological Prompts
articles.tldr: MindShift adapts the MMPI-2 to LLMs and validates its reliability and construct validity as a psychometric instrument via directional bias shifts and Cronbach's alpha.
articles.contribution: Validates directional construct validity by showing injected psychological biases shift scale scores in the expected direction, using indirect true/false completions to avoid sycophancy bias from direct questioning.

articles.title: Learning Context Matters: Measuring and Diagnosing Personalization Gaps in LLM-Based Instructional Design
articles.tldr: The Personalization Policy Probe (P3) measures whether learning context genuinely shifts LLM tutoring policy toward expert judgments and diagnoses spurious feature influence.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes 'personalization' as an instructional-policy shift plus learner-centeredness measured by Total Variation Distance against an expert reference policy, arguing behavior change alone does not constitute valid personalization.

articles.title: Learning Context Matters: Measuring and Diagnosing Personalization Gaps in LLM-Based Instructional Design
articles.tldr: The Personalization Policy Probe (P3) measures whether learning context genuinely shifts LLM tutoring policy toward expert judgments and diagnoses spurious feature influence.
articles.contribution: A leave-one-out relevance-influence analysis exposes 'hallucinated relevance' where pedagogically-irrelevant learner traits spuriously drive the policy, with no reliable relevance-influence relationship (Spearman rho ~0.11, p~0.61).

articles.title: How well can off-the-shelf LLMs elucidate molecular structures from mass spectra using chain-of-thought reasoning?
articles.tldr: Benchmark showing LLM chain-of-thought for mass-spectra structure elucidation is a stylistic scaffold: fluent but ungrounded and frequently contradicting its own answer.
articles.contribution: Shows expert-styled CoT (DBE analysis, neutral-loss talk) is a surface proxy for genuine chemical reasoning: RDKit/formula/DBE verifiers reveal near-zero chemical correctness despite fluent, expert-sounding traces.

articles.title: Theory Trace Card: Theory-Driven Socio-Cognitive Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: Theory Trace Card argues socio-cognitive LLM benchmarks lack explicit construct theory, creating a systemic 'validity illusion', and proposes a documentation artifact for the validity chain.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses and formalizes the 'theory gap': socio-cognitive benchmarks proceed without an explicit theoretical specification of the target construct, rendering measurement claims groundless (grounded in Kane's argument-based validity).

articles.title: Theory Trace Card: Theory-Driven Socio-Cognitive Evaluation of LLMs
articles.tldr: Theory Trace Card argues socio-cognitive LLM benchmarks lack explicit construct theory, creating a systemic 'validity illusion', and proposes a documentation artifact for the validity chain.
articles.contribution: Shows narrow operationalizations get overgeneralized to broad competence, collapsing multidimensional constructs into a single scalar (e.g. false-belief = only cognitive ToM; empathy = emotion recognition).

articles.title: Prompt Stability in Code LLMs: Measuring Sensitivity across Emotion- and Personality-Driven Variations
articles.tldr: PromptSE quantifies code-LLM prompt stability under emotion/personality-driven semantically-equivalent variants via probability-aware SoftExec and an AUC-E stability metric.
articles.contribution: Introduces AUC-E over elasticity curves at perturbation distances 0.1/0.2/0.3 to measure how semantically-equivalent emotion/personality prompt rephrasings destabilize code-generation correctness.

articles.title: Prompt Stability in Code LLMs: Measuring Sensitivity across Emotion- and Personality-Driven Variations
articles.tldr: PromptSE quantifies code-LLM prompt stability under emotion/personality-driven semantically-equivalent variants via probability-aware SoftExec and an AUC-E stability metric.
articles.contribution: SoftExec weights correctness by generation probability to separate high-confidence solutions from lucky guesses, and ECE diagnostics reveal emotion-induced confidence miscalibration missed by binary Pass@k.

articles.title: REDACT: A Systematically Controlled Multilingual Benchmark for Personal Information Detection
articles.tldr: REDACT is a 25-language PII benchmark whose stratified recall (per disclosure-form, per sensitivity-tier) exposes detector failures that aggregate F1 hides.
articles.contribution: A strength-2 covering-array sampler over nine generation axes realizes 98.2% of pairwise axis-value combinations, replacing ad hoc/templated PII generation with controlled multilingual, multi-format coverage.

articles.title: REDACT: A Systematically Controlled Multilingual Benchmark for Personal Information Detection
articles.tldr: REDACT is a 25-language PII benchmark whose stratified recall (per disclosure-form, per sensitivity-tier) exposes detector failures that aggregate F1 hides.
articles.contribution: Stratified recall (F5 per disclosure-form, F6 per sensitivity-tier) shows aggregate F1 masks an architecture-dependent failure structure, so a single score misrepresents detector reliability on the highest-stakes slice.

articles.title: REDACT: A Systematically Controlled Multilingual Benchmark for Personal Information Detection
articles.tldr: REDACT is a 25-language PII benchmark whose stratified recall (per disclosure-form, per sensitivity-tier) exposes detector failures that aggregate F1 hides.
articles.contribution: A three-model reference-free G-Eval LLM-as-judge panel corroborates that sensitivity-tier assignment is the hardest axis, scoring lowest and showing only kappa=0.25 human agreement.

articles.title: Bias Ahead: Sensitive Prompts as Early Warnings for Fairness in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: SensY reframes fairness evaluation around 'sensitive prompts' as early-warning signals and studies whether prompt sensitivity predicts biased or inadequate LLM outputs.
articles.contribution: Introduces 'sensitive prompt' as a preventive fairness-risk construct and validates it via manual adequacy coding of 4,500 responses, showing factually-correct answers still miss ethical, relational or contextual implications.

articles.title: Bias Ahead: Sensitive Prompts as Early Warnings for Fairness in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: SensY reframes fairness evaluation around 'sensitive prompts' as early-warning signals and studies whether prompt sensitivity predicts biased or inadequate LLM outputs.
articles.contribution: Cross-dataset tests (train SensY -> test SQuARe = 0.523 accuracy; SQuARe -> SensY = 0.261) show the sensitivity classifier fails to generalize under distributional/cultural shift despite ROC-AUC 0.69-0.81.

articles.title: Bias Ahead: Sensitive Prompts as Early Warnings for Fairness in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: SensY reframes fairness evaluation around 'sensitive prompts' as early-warning signals and studies whether prompt sensitivity predicts biased or inadequate LLM outputs.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates SQuARe's 0.96 accuracy is a class-imbalance artifact (macro-F1 <0.50, macro-recall ~chance), arguing macro-level metrics and cross-dataset validation are needed instead of accuracy.

articles.title: Copyright Infringement Detection in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Differential Privacy
articles.tldr: DPM detects text-to-image copyright infringement by formalizing it via differential privacy and measuring a learning-versus-unlearning 'conditional sensitivity' signal.
articles.contribution: Detects whether a target concept was memorized/in-training by contrasting learning and unlearning fine-tuning branches, without needing the training data or original prompts, yielding a post-hoc infringement detector.

articles.title: Copyright Infringement Detection in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Differential Privacy
articles.tldr: DPM detects text-to-image copyright infringement by formalizing it via differential privacy and measuring a learning-versus-unlearning 'conditional sensitivity' signal.
articles.contribution: Formalizes copyright infringement as 'conditional publicity'/conditional sensitivity (analogous to differential-privacy local sensitivity), giving measurable inclusion/exclusion criteria for what counts as memorized.

articles.title: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.tldr: MAC-Bench: a dynamic, contamination-resistant benchmark that audits multi-agent procedural compliance to expose success-compliance Goodhart trade-offs.
articles.contribution: Argues success-only metrics (SR) are a direct instance of Goodhart's law that reward procedural shortcuts, and introduces Compliance-Weighted Success Rate (CSR) and the Machiavellian Gap (MG) to quantify strategic rule-bending.

articles.title: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.tldr: MAC-Bench: a dynamic, contamination-resistant benchmark that audits multi-agent procedural compliance to expose success-compliance Goodhart trade-offs.
articles.contribution: The SERV Agent-as-a-Benchmark pipeline synthesizes holographic scenarios at runtime from regulatory texts (847 atomic rules to 4,128 scenarios to 20,640 instances) so static task instances cannot leak into training corpora.

articles.title: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.tldr: MAC-Bench: a dynamic, contamination-resistant benchmark that audits multi-agent procedural compliance to expose success-compliance Goodhart trade-offs.
articles.contribution: Architectural ablation shows the agent scaffold confounds measured compliance: hierarchical AutoGen delegation induces 'responsibility diffusion' (CR 38.5%) while single-agent ReAct reaches CR 72.1% at comparable success.

articles.title: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: Executable Evaluation of AI Agents in Electric Power Engineering
articles.tldr: An executable power-engineering agent benchmark that recomputes physics deterministically, resists contamination via seed-generated held-out cases, and uses unanimous-failure QC to catch evaluator bugs.
articles.contribution: Replaces reference-QA and LLM-judge prose grading (which reward fluent-but-physically-invalid rationales) with a deterministic evaluator that recomputes engineering quantities and constraints, returning a feasibility flag, score, and explicit violations, with the agent's rationale excluded from scoring.

articles.title: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: Executable Evaluation of AI Agents in Electric Power Engineering
articles.tldr: An executable power-engineering agent benchmark that recomputes physics deterministically, resists contamination via seed-generated held-out cases, and uses unanimous-failure QC to catch evaluator bugs.
articles.contribution: Does not store held-out cases at all; per-family physics-aware generators synthesize solvability-checked instances on demand from a private seed, making the leak-prone held-out split auditable in mechanism yet private in content.

articles.title: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: Executable Evaluation of AI Agents in Electric Power Engineering
articles.tldr: An executable power-engineering agent benchmark that recomputes physics deterministically, resists contamination via seed-generated held-out cases, and uses unanimous-failure QC to catch evaluator bugs.
articles.contribution: A trustworthy runner classifies failure types and retries only infrastructure errors (never poor solutions) to avoid silently becoming best-of-N, and a public-split model x harness grid (OpenCode, Aider) separates scaffolding effects from model capability.

articles.title: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: Executable Evaluation of AI Agents in Electric Power Engineering
articles.tldr: An executable power-engineering agent benchmark that recomputes physics deterministically, resists contamination via seed-generated held-out cases, and uses unanimous-failure QC to catch evaluator bugs.
articles.contribution: Proposes unanimous-agent-failure as a quality-control signal for defective tasks or evaluators, which in the reference run exposed a latent evaluator bug missed by self-consistency checks.

articles.title: LLM-Driven Multi-Turn Task-Oriented Dialogue Synthesis for Realistic Reasoning
articles.tldr: Synthesizes realistic multi-turn task-oriented reasoning dialogues with trilevel-optimized quality evaluation to counter oversimplified, contamination-prone reasoning benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Generates multi-turn dialogues grounded in authentic task scenarios with domain constraints and operational rules to overcome abstract, oversimplified reasoning datasets that are disconnected from realistic task flows and thus poorly reflect real-world reasoning.

articles.title: LLM-Driven Multi-Turn Task-Oriented Dialogue Synthesis for Realistic Reasoning
articles.tldr: Synthesizes realistic multi-turn task-oriented reasoning dialogues with trilevel-optimized quality evaluation to counter oversimplified, contamination-prone reasoning benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Uses LLM-agent synthesis of new dialogues to avoid the pretraining-corpus overlap that undermines the reliability of reasoning-evaluation results, replacing non-scalable crowd-sourcing.

articles.title: Small, Private Language Models as Teammates for Educational Assessment Design
articles.tldr: Benchmarks LLMs vs SLMs for Bloom-aligned question generation with reproducible objective metrics and finds model-as-judge evaluations systematically biased relative to expert ratings.
articles.contribution: Analyzes model-as-a-judge reliability, bias, consistency, and agreement against expert annotations, finding systematic inconsistencies and bias relative to expert ratings and positing language models as bounded assistants that require human-in-the-loop.

articles.title: Small, Private Language Models as Teammates for Educational Assessment Design
articles.tldr: Benchmarks LLMs vs SLMs for Bloom-aligned question generation with reproducible objective metrics and finds model-as-judge evaluations systematically biased relative to expert ratings.
articles.contribution: Replaces subjective rubrics with reproducible objective proxies (Flesch-Kincaid grade level, Reading Ease, BERTScore/GTR-T5 semantic similarity, action-verb compliance) mapped to cognitive-complexity, linguistic-intent, and pedagogical-compliance dimensions of question quality.

articles.title: Quantifying Document Impact in RAG-LLMs
articles.tldr: Influence Score, a PID/semantic-entropy metric quantifying each retrieved document's contribution to a RAG output, validated by poison-attack detection and human/LLM-judge ablations.
articles.contribution: Introduces the Influence Score (Partial Information Decomposition via semantic entropy) to isolate each retrieved document's causal contribution to a RAG response, closing the explainability/attribution gap where the rationale behind an output is opaque.

articles.title: Quantifying Document Impact in RAG-LLMs
articles.tldr: Influence Score, a PID/semantic-entropy metric quantifying each retrieved document's contribution to a RAG output, validated by poison-attack detection and human/LLM-judge ablations.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates IS as a poison/contamination detector: in a PoisonedRAG-style attack it identifies the malicious retrieved document as most influential and localizes it for removal.

articles.title: Mitigating Cognitive Bias in RLHF by Altering Rationality
articles.tldr: Treats RLHF's Boltzmann rationality parameter beta as instance-dependent, using an LLM judge to estimate per-comparison cognitive-bias likelihood and downweight unreliable human preferences.
articles.contribution: Relaxes RLHF's assumption of uniform annotator reliability by making the Boltzmann rationality parameter beta context- and response-dependent, downweighting comparisons likely to reflect cognitively biased human judgments.

articles.title: Mitigating Cognitive Bias in RLHF by Altering Rationality
articles.tldr: Treats RLHF's Boltzmann rationality parameter beta as instance-dependent, using an LLM judge to estimate per-comparison cognitive-bias likelihood and downweight unreliable human preferences.
articles.contribution: Uses an out-of-the-box LLM-as-judge to estimate a per-instance cognitive-bias probability D_f (defined on the chosen response, not the scenario) that feeds beta_new = logistic(k(theta - D_f)) to reweight feedback fidelity.

articles.title: Extending Item Response Theory for Efficient and Meaningful Multilingual Evaluation
articles.tldr: Multilingual-IRT extends item response theory with per-language difficulty deviations, split discriminability, and ability residuals to cut multilingual eval cost, flag translation errors, and detect culture-specific items.
articles.contribution: Fits Multilingual-IRT (per-language difficulty deviations d_il, split discriminability a_base/a_lang, correlated per-language ability residuals) via stochastic variational inference to predict unseen (item, LLM, language) instances with 11-16% lower binary cross-entropy than the strongest accuracy-based baseline.

articles.title: Extending Item Response Theory for Efficient and Meaningful Multilingual Evaluation
articles.tldr: Multilingual-IRT extends item response theory with per-language difficulty deviations, split discriminability, and ability residuals to cut multilingual eval cost, flag translation errors, and detect culture-specific items.
articles.contribution: Ranks items by d_il/SE to surface candidate translation errors that distort the measured construct, distributed across all 28 non-English languages, whereas accuracy baselines concentrate about 71% of detections in Wolof/Yoruba/Zulu.

articles.title: Extending Item Response Theory for Efficient and Meaningful Multilingual Evaluation
articles.tldr: Multilingual-IRT extends item response theory with per-language difficulty deviations, split discriminability, and ability residuals to cut multilingual eval cost, flag translation errors, and detect culture-specific items.
articles.contribution: Uses the discriminability ratio a_lang/a_base to recover culture-specific items that conflate general with culture-specific knowledge (26.1% of the top-2K vs 24.2% for the best accuracy baseline), which confound multilingual capability measurement.

articles.title: Estimating LLM Grading Ability and Response Difficulty in Automatic Short Answer Grading via Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: Applies a 1PL testlet IRT model to LLM short-answer grading, separating latent grader ability from response difficulty to reveal robustness differences hidden by aggregate F1/kappa.
articles.contribution: Introduces a 1PL testlet IRT framework modeling grading correctness as a function of latent grader ability theta and response difficulty b, exposing response-level robustness differences among LLM graders that macro-F1 and Cohen's kappa hide.

articles.title: Estimating LLM Grading Ability and Response Difficulty in Automatic Short Answer Grading via Item Response Theory
articles.tldr: Applies a 1PL testlet IRT model to LLM short-answer grading, separating latent grader ability from response difficulty to reveal robustness differences hidden by aggregate F1/kappa.
articles.contribution: Validates the psychometric estimates via simulation-based parameter recovery and split-half stability, and applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control to the difficulty-correlate analysis, giving a statistically sound measurement foundation.

articles.title: Beyond Scores: Diagnostic LLM Evaluation via Fine-Grained Abilities
articles.tldr: A cognitive-diagnostic mIRT framework with an item-ability Q-matrix estimates fine-grained LLM abilities, giving construct/criterion validity and predicting performance on unseen items.
articles.contribution: Uses multidimensional IRT (a monotonic NeuralCD network) with an item-ability Q-matrix over a 35-dimensional Bloom-grounded math taxonomy to estimate fine-grained latent ability profiles that single-score aggregate benchmarks obscure.

articles.title: Beyond Scores: Diagnostic LLM Evaluation via Fine-Grained Abilities
articles.tldr: A cognitive-diagnostic mIRT framework with an item-ability Q-matrix estimates fine-grained LLM abilities, giving construct/criterion validity and predicting performance on unseen items.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates criterion validity by correlating each estimated ability dimension with per-dimension accuracy, and predicts unseen benchmark items with AUC 0.80-0.89 within and 0.77-0.86 across benchmarks, substantially exceeding trivial baselines.

articles.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models with Integer Sequence Generation Tasks
articles.tldr: An OEIS integer-sequence code-generation benchmark that resists contamination via recency splits and adds an LLM cheating-detector (validated against humans) to catch lookup-table memorization.
articles.contribution: Splits 1000 OEIS sequences into contemporary (post-July-2024, beyond any released LLM's training data) versus classic sets to eliminate training-data contamination, scoring generated Python by unit-testing withheld sequence values under strict time limits.

articles.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models with Integer Sequence Generation Tasks
articles.tldr: An OEIS integer-sequence code-generation benchmark that resists contamination via recency splits and adds an LLM cheating-detector (validated against humans) to catch lookup-table memorization.
articles.contribution: Adds an automated lookup-table cheating detector (an LLM with structured output at temperature 0) that zero-scores memorized answers, preventing models from gaming the metric by hard-coding sequence values instead of writing algorithms.

articles.title: ISD-Agent-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-based Instructional Design Agents
articles.tldr: A large ISD-agent benchmark that mitigates LLM-as-judge bias with a cross-provider multi-judge protocol (0.905 reliability) and validates its scores against theoretical-quality labels.
articles.contribution: Employs a cross-provider multi-judge protocol (GPT-4o-mini plus Gemini-2.5-flash-lite with median aggregation) to mitigate LLM-judge self-preference bias, reporting mean inter-judge reliability 0.905 (94.7% good-or-excellent agreement) and only +/-0.06 systematic judge bias.

articles.title: ISD-Agent-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-based Instructional Design Agents
articles.tldr: A large ISD-agent benchmark that mitigates LLM-as-judge bias with a cross-provider multi-judge protocol (0.905 reliability) and validates its scores against theoretical-quality labels.
articles.contribution: Provides convergent-validity evidence that benchmark scores capture the intended construct by showing independent theoretical-quality (MPI/DC) labels correlate with benchmark performance (r=0.656, p<0.001; agent-level rho=0.94).

articles.title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
articles.tldr: Formalizes budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation and gives an inverse-variance-weighted adaptive algorithm (Est-IVWE) with matching local-minimax lower bounds for allocating LLM-judge queries.
articles.contribution: Formalizes budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation and derives the oracle inverse-variance-weighted allocation, then proposes Est-IVWE which uses optimistically biased variance estimates to match the oracle error rate under unknown, judge- and instance-dependent variances.

articles.title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
articles.tldr: Formalizes budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation and gives an inverse-variance-weighted adaptive algorithm (Est-IVWE) with matching local-minimax lower bounds for allocating LLM-judge queries.
articles.contribution: Shows the optimal aggregation of heterogeneous LLM judges of differing cost and reliability is sparse, assigning each query entirely to the single judge minimizing cost-times-variance c_j*sigma_kj^2, and proves instance-optimality via a matching Assouad-type in-expectation local minimax lower bound (Fano-type high-probability arguments being too coarse).

articles.title: GRAFITE: Generative Regression Analysis Framework for Issue Tracking and Evaluation
articles.tldr: Continuous LLM-eval platform using human-authored hidden tests and an LLM-judge ensemble to resist benchmark-contamination inflation.
articles.contribution: Combats benchmark-contamination performance inflation by evaluating models on continuously maintained human-curated issue tests kept hidden from model developers.

articles.title: GRAFITE: Generative Regression Analysis Framework for Issue Tracking and Evaluation
articles.tldr: Continuous LLM-eval platform using human-authored hidden tests and an LLM-judge ensemble to resist benchmark-contamination inflation.
articles.contribution: Mitigates LLM-as-judge bias by averaging an ensemble of three heterogeneous judge models (pass if mean>0.5) with human-in-the-loop score override.

articles.title: Rethinking Ground Truth: A Case Study on Human Label Variation in MLLM Benchmarking
articles.tldr: Evaluation protocol splitting MLLM benchmarks into agreement/disagreement subsets shows consensus-only ground truth overstates model capability.
articles.contribution: Shows majority-vote consensus ground truth obscures human label variation, proposing a Krippendorff's-alpha (threshold 0.667) agreement/disagreement partition for MLLM benchmarking.

articles.title: Rethinking Ground Truth: A Case Study on Human Label Variation in MLLM Benchmarking
articles.tldr: Evaluation protocol splitting MLLM benchmarks into agreement/disagreement subsets shows consensus-only ground truth overstates model capability.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates consensus-based benchmarks overstate real content-moderation capability, using Brier/JSD on disaggregated labels to assess calibration to the human label distribution.

articles.title: The Ghost Annotator: a Framework to Explore Human Label Variation in Content Moderation through Conformal Prediction
articles.tldr: Conformal-prediction framework (Ghost Prediction/Ghost Annotator) quantifying LLM-annotator uncertainty and demographic misalignment under human label variation.
articles.contribution: Introduces a Non-Conformity-Score-based Ghost Prediction metric measuring how often an LLM predicts a label no human annotator chose, to assess LLM reliability as an annotator under human label variation.

articles.title: The Ghost Annotator: a Framework to Explore Human Label Variation in Content Moderation through Conformal Prediction
articles.tldr: Conformal-prediction framework (Ghost Prediction/Ghost Annotator) quantifying LLM-annotator uncertainty and demographic misalignment under human label variation.
articles.contribution: Reveals robust demographic misalignment: all four LLMs diverge most from 18-30 Male Sub-Saharan-Africa annotators, a likely structural pretraining-corpus bias independent of annotator pool size.

articles.title: Counterfactual Peptide Editing for Causal TCR-pMHC Binding Inference
articles.tldr: Introduces causal diagnostic metrics and shows random-split evaluation masks shortcut-driven brittleness in TCR-pMHC binding prediction.
articles.contribution: Proposes Shortcut Index (Spearman correlation with V-gene identity), Counterfactual Consistency, and Anchor Flip Rate to quantify reliance on spurious features beyond AUROC/AUPRC.

articles.title: Counterfactual Peptide Editing for Causal TCR-pMHC Binding Inference
articles.tldr: Introduces causal diagnostic metrics and shows random-split evaluation masks shortcut-driven brittleness in TCR-pMHC binding prediction.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates random-split benchmarks systematically underestimate shortcut-driven failures, which only family-held-out and distance-aware evaluation protocols expose.

articles.title: Bias in the Shadows: Explore Shortcuts in Encrypted Network Traffic Classification
articles.tldr: Model-agnostic AMI-based framework detecting dataset-specific shortcut and data-leakage features in encrypted network-traffic classifiers.
articles.contribution: Uses Adjusted Mutual Information on raw packet fields to flag spurious/environment-entangled shortcut features independent of any classifier, with a three-type shortcut taxonomy.

articles.title: Bias in the Shadows: Explore Shortcuts in Encrypted Network Traffic Classification
articles.tldr: Model-agnostic AMI-based framework detecting dataset-specific shortcut and data-leakage features in encrypted network-traffic classifiers.
articles.contribution: Identifies 'Data-Leakage Identifiers' (IP/port/SNI) whose label correlation stems from collection/labeling artifacts and inflates scores, with removal consistently dropping accuracy.

articles.title: SoccerLens: Grounded Soccer Video Understanding Beyond Accuracy
articles.tldr: Grounding benchmark showing soccer VLMs' high classification accuracy dissociates from true visual grounding, exposing spurious-cue reliance.
articles.contribution: Shows accuracy-only evaluation misrepresents visual understanding, introducing cue-annotated spatial/temporal grounding metrics (Energy, Pointing, S-IoU, T-IoU) via a Chefer-T attribution extension.

articles.title: SoccerLens: Grounded Soccer Video Understanding Beyond Accuracy
articles.tldr: Grounding benchmark showing soccer VLMs' high classification accuracy dissociates from true visual grounding, exposing spurious-cue reliance.
articles.contribution: Reveals VLMs exploit broadcast/contextual shortcuts (TV panels, celebrations) rather than event-defining cues, with grounding never exceeding 50% even at the loosest cue level.

articles.title: SHOVIR: A Benchmark for Evaluating Vision Shortcut Learning in Radiology Report Generation
articles.tldr: Occlusion benchmark showing radiology-report-generation VLMs' report-level scores hide vision shortcuts and ungrounded diagnoses.
articles.contribution: Argues report-level metrics (BLEU, F1-CheXbert, RadGraph, GREEN) measure overlap not whether statements derive from visual evidence, and defines occlusion-based shortcut deltas (dFN, dOCO, dDOCO).

articles.title: SHOVIR: A Benchmark for Evaluating Vision Shortcut Learning in Radiology Report Generation
articles.tldr: Occlusion benchmark showing radiology-report-generation VLMs' report-level scores hide vision shortcuts and ungrounded diagnoses.
articles.contribution: Isolates direct shortcuts (finding persists after evidence removed) from contextual shortcuts (co-occurring-pathology dependence) via region-specific occlusion of per-box CheXpert-labeled boxes.

articles.title: Diagnosing Shortcut-Induced Rigidity in Continual Learning: The Einstellung Rigidity Index (ERI)
articles.tldr: Einstellung Rigidity Index diagnostic disentangling genuine transfer from shortcut/cue-inflated performance in continual learning.
articles.contribution: Introduces a three-facet index (Adaptation Delay, Performance Deficit, Relative Suboptimal Feature Reliance via a masking intervention) to detect shortcut-induced rigidity.

articles.title: Diagnosing Shortcut-Induced Rigidity in Continual Learning: The Einstellung Rigidity Index (ERI)
articles.tldr: Einstellung Rigidity Index diagnostic disentangling genuine transfer from shortcut/cue-inflated performance in continual learning.
articles.contribution: Argues standard CL aggregate metrics (ACC/BWT/FWT) cannot distinguish success from robust causal features versus spurious cues, so apparent adaptation may proceed for the wrong reasons.

articles.title: Can Dense Connectivity Benefit Outlier Detection? An Odyssey with NAS
articles.tldr: NAS framework for OOD detectors that characterizes and reduces the high evaluation variance of OOD AUROC that corrupts detector ranking.
articles.contribution: Quantifies that OOD-detection AUROC is far noisier than in-distribution accuracy across random seeds and proposes evolving-distillation training to stabilize the measurement.

articles.title: Can Dense Connectivity Benefit Outlier Detection? An Odyssey with NAS
articles.tldr: NAS framework for OOD detectors that characterizes and reduces the high evaluation variance of OOD AUROC that corrupts detector ranking.
articles.contribution: Shows noisy OOD evaluation yields poor Kendall's-tau ranking of architectures and improves ranking reliability, enabling fairer comparison of candidate outlier detectors.

articles.title: The Constant Eye: Benchmarking and Bridging Appearance Robustness in Autonomous Driving
articles.tldr: Benchmark that isolates appearance shift from scene geometry to validly attribute OOD planning failures in autonomous driving.
articles.contribution: navdream fixes scene geometry P(G) and varies only appearance P(A|G) via pixel-aligned Flux style transfer, isolating the appearance confounder so a planning failure can be attributed to visual shift rather than road topology.

articles.title: The Constant Eye: Benchmarking and Bridging Appearance Robustness in Autonomous Driving
articles.tldr: Benchmark that isolates appearance shift from scene geometry to validly attribute OOD planning failures in autonomous driving.
articles.contribution: Shows regression/diffusion/scoring E2E planners degrade sharply under unseen appearance styles while structure is preserved, exposing over-reliance on texture cues as an external-validity failure of standard driving benchmarks.

articles.title: Are We Making Progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization? A Comprehensive Benchmark Study
articles.tldr: Standardized benchmark testing whether reported multimodal-domain-generalization gains are real or artifacts of inconsistent evaluation protocols.
articles.contribution: Standardizes data splits, hyperparameter search, optimizer and training-domain model selection across nine MMDG methods; under fair comparison specialized methods give only marginal gains over ERM, showing prior gains were evaluation-protocol artifacts.

articles.title: Are We Making Progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization? A Comprehensive Benchmark Study
articles.tldr: Standardized benchmark testing whether reported multimodal-domain-generalization gains are real or artifacts of inconsistent evaluation protocols.
articles.contribution: Trains 7,402 networks across 95 cross-domain tasks with multi-seed retraining and averaging to give reproducible, directly-comparable MMDG performance estimates.

articles.title: Are We Making Progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization? A Comprehensive Benchmark Study
articles.tldr: Standardized benchmark testing whether reported multimodal-domain-generalization gains are real or artifacts of inconsistent evaluation protocols.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that clean cross-domain accuracy is an insufficient external-validity measure: rankings invert under corruption/missing modalities and high accuracy does not guarantee trustworthiness (misclassification/OOD detection).

articles.title: Benchmarking and Explaining Deep Learning Cortical Lesion MRI Segmentation in Multiple Sclerosis
articles.tldr: Multi-center benchmark quantifying deep-learning cortical-lesion MRI segmentation validity across scanners and out-of-distribution sites.
articles.contribution: Largest OOD assessment in cortical-lesion segmentation (224 subjects on a different scanner vendor) shows lesion-detection F1 drops from 0.64 in-domain to 0.5 OOD, quantifying generalization loss across scanners/protocols.

articles.title: Benchmarking and Explaining Deep Learning Cortical Lesion MRI Segmentation in Multiple Sclerosis
articles.tldr: Multi-center benchmark quantifying deep-learning cortical-lesion MRI segmentation validity across scanners and out-of-distribution sites.
articles.contribution: Identifies that prior joint CL+WML segmentation inflated cortical-lesion detection because juxtacortical false positives were absorbed as white-matter lesions and escaped penalization; CL-specific scoring and nDSC (correcting DSC class-load bias) are needed.

articles.title: Study Design and Demystification of Physics Informed Neural Networks for Power Flow Simulation
articles.tldr: Standardized study-design benchmark comparing physics-informed hybridization strategies on accuracy, physics compliance, and OOD generalization for power-flow surrogates.
articles.contribution: Uses the LIPS framework to compare hybridization strategies (MLP, MLP-Reg, MP-Opt, PIMP) under one standardized set of criteria, addressing that prior PINN power-flow works report incomparable single-strategy results.

articles.title: Study Design and Demystification of Physics Informed Neural Networks for Power Flow Simulation
articles.tldr: Standardized study-design benchmark comparing physics-informed hybridization strategies on accuracy, physics compliance, and OOD generalization for power-flow surrogates.
articles.contribution: Shows a pure MLP attains low MAE (~1e-2) yet violates the local conservation law 40-50% of the time, so accuracy alone misrepresents the physical-validity construct and a separate physics-compliance metric is required.

articles.title: Study Design and Demystification of Physics Informed Neural Networks for Power Flow Simulation
articles.tldr: Standardized study-design benchmark comparing physics-informed hybridization strategies on accuracy, physics compliance, and OOD generalization for power-flow surrogates.
articles.contribution: Evaluates OOD generalization on a distribution with two simultaneous line disconnections (vs one in training), where MLP physics-law violation rises to 47-50%.

articles.title: Ego4OOD: Rethinking Egocentric Video Domain Generalization via Covariate Shift Scoring
articles.tldr: Egocentric-video domain-generalization benchmark that disentangles covariate from concept shift and scores domain difficulty.
articles.contribution: Ego4OOD regroups 203 Ego4D moment classes into 9 semantically coherent categories to suppress concept shift while preserving covariate diversity, so measured 'OOD generalization' is not confounded by label-boundary ambiguity.

articles.title: Ego4OOD: Rethinking Egocentric Video Domain Generalization via Covariate Shift Scoring
articles.tldr: Egocentric-video domain-generalization benchmark that disentangles covariate from concept shift and scores domain difficulty.
articles.contribution: Documents Argo1M annotation ambiguities (e.g., 'tear' vs 'open' by annotator preference; simultaneously valid bring/open/carry) that make single-label evaluation ill-posed and cap SOTA at 24.92% vs 55.68% on the cleaner Ego4OOD.

articles.title: Ego4OOD: Rethinking Egocentric Video Domain Generalization via Covariate Shift Scoring
articles.tldr: Egocentric-video domain-generalization benchmark that disentangles covariate from concept shift and scores domain difficulty.
articles.contribution: Introduces a clustering-based domain-shift score Omega(g)=mu_g+2*sigma_g that negatively correlates with recognition accuracy, providing a quantitative proxy for OOD domain difficulty.

articles.title: Evaluating Object-Centric Models beyond Object Discovery
articles.tldr: Evaluation framework showing object-discovery metrics poorly proxy object-centric-model utility, introducing a joint what+where metric (AwGA).
articles.contribution: Shows unsupervised object-discovery metrics (mBO/mIoU) are a poor proxy for representation usefulness (Spearman -0.2 with VQAv2 accuracy; FT-DINOSAUR leads discovery but trails DINOSAURv2 downstream).

articles.title: Evaluating Object-Centric Models beyond Object Discovery
articles.tldr: Evaluation framework showing object-discovery metrics poorly proxy object-centric-model utility, introducing a joint what+where metric (AwGA).
articles.contribution: Introduces attribution-aware grounded accuracy (AwGA) that jointly scores localization and representation via TopK answer-attributed slots, penalizing representation fragmentation that G-Acc and disjoint metrics leave unpenalized.

articles.title: Evaluating Object-Centric Models beyond Object Discovery
articles.tldr: Evaluation framework showing object-discovery metrics poorly proxy object-centric-model utility, introducing a joint what+where metric (AwGA).
articles.contribution: Validates instruction-tuned VLMs as scalable zero-shot evaluators, showing model rankings are stable across LLM backbones and connectors (Spearman rho >= 0.89), i.e., the evaluator instrument is reliable.

articles.title: One Model, Many Behaviors: Training-Induced Effects on Out-of-Distribution Detection
articles.tldr: Controlled study shows the ID-accuracy vs OOD-detection relationship is non-monotonic and method-dependent, and that prior positive-correlation claims are confounded.
articles.contribution: By fixing ResNet-50 and varying only the training strategy across 56 models, it isolates the ID-accuracy effect and shows prior positive ID-accuracy/OOD-detection correlations stem from architecture/capacity confounders.

articles.title: One Model, Many Behaviors: Training-Induced Effects on Out-of-Distribution Detection
articles.tldr: Controlled study shows the ID-accuracy vs OOD-detection relationship is non-monotonic and method-dependent, and that prior positive-correlation claims are confounded.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks 21 post-hoc detectors on eight OOD sets, finding strong training-strategy x detector interdependence and no universally optimal method, so detector rankings do not transport across settings.

articles.title: Causal-Driven Feature Evaluation for Cross-Domain Image Classification
articles.tldr: Argues domain-invariant features are a surface proxy for OOD reliability and proposes causal necessity/sufficiency (PNS) scoring as a more faithful evaluation criterion.
articles.contribution: Shows domain invariance is a surface proxy that does not imply causal effectiveness, so evaluating representations by invariance alone misrepresents the reliability construct under distribution shift.

articles.title: Causal-Driven Feature Evaluation for Cross-Domain Image Classification
articles.tldr: Argues domain-invariant features are a surface proxy for OOD reliability and proposes causal necessity/sufficiency (PNS) scoring as a more faithful evaluation criterion.
articles.contribution: Introduces segment-level probability-of-necessity-and-sufficiency scoring via intervention operators to separate spurious-but-invariant features from causally effective ones for prediction.

articles.title: On Generalization in Agentic Tool Calling: CoreThink Agentic Reasoner and MAVEN Dataset
articles.tldr: Introduces the MAVEN OOD tool-calling benchmark and exposes 'benchmark brittleness'-strong in-benchmark scores do not indicate robust, transferable agentic reasoning.
articles.contribution: Coins 'benchmark brittleness': high scores on established tool-calling datasets can be achieved by exploiting dataset-specific patterns/artifacts, so the benchmarks misrepresent robust multi-step reasoning.

articles.title: On Generalization in Agentic Tool Calling: CoreThink Agentic Reasoner and MAVEN Dataset
articles.tldr: Introduces the MAVEN OOD tool-calling benchmark and exposes 'benchmark brittleness'-strong in-benchmark scores do not indicate robust, transferable agentic reasoning.
articles.contribution: Provides an adversarial OOD benchmark (MAVEN) with explicit verification that reveals a large generalization gap across BFCL v3, TauBench, Tau2Bench and AceBench tool-use settings.

articles.title: A Semantically Consistent Dataset for Data-Efficient Query-Based Universal Sound Separation
articles.tldr: Diagnoses event co-occurrence in in-the-wild audio datasets as a shortcut-inducing confound and isolates it with a controlled paired experiment.
articles.contribution: Identifies weak labels and severe event co-occurrence in in-the-wild audio training data as a confounder that makes separation models learn spurious background-to-target correlations instead of acoustic features.

articles.title: A Semantically Consistent Dataset for Data-Efficient Query-Based Universal Sound Separation
articles.tldr: Diagnoses event co-occurrence in in-the-wild audio datasets as a shortcut-inducing confound and isolates it with a controlled paired experiment.
articles.contribution: Designs a controlled shortcut analysis that holds mixture complexity, target identity and SNR fixed while varying only the target-interferer statistical relation, disentangling semantic-consistency gains from reduced co-occurrence-shortcut reliance.

articles.title: Local Performance vs. Out-of-Distribution Generalization: An Empirical Analysis of Personalized Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Data Environments
articles.tldr: Critiques personalized-Federated-Learning evaluation for measuring only average local accuracy and re-evaluates FL methods across per-round stages and new non-IID environments.
articles.contribution: Shows personalized-FL evaluation exclusively tracks clients' average local performance, a surface proxy that misrepresents robustness by omitting OOD generalization (a key benefit of FedAvg).

articles.title: Local Performance vs. Out-of-Distribution Generalization: An Empirical Analysis of Personalized Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Data Environments
articles.tldr: Critiques personalized-Federated-Learning evaluation for measuring only average local accuracy and re-evaluates FL methods across per-round stages and new non-IID environments.
articles.contribution: Proposes assessing OOD generalization across communication-round stages and under new Dirichlet label-/quantity-skew test environments that the standard IID and pathological non-IID setups fail to stress.

articles.title: A Measure-Theoretic Analysis of Reasoning: Structural Generalization and Approximation Limits
articles.tldr: Formalizes reasoning as optimal transport to bound OOD generalization risk by the Wasserstein-1 domain shift, with architectural and scaling-law validity limits.
articles.contribution: Provides a measure-theoretic transportability bound in which OOD reasoning-generalization risk grows with the Wasserstein-1 distance between train and test trajectory distributions, quantifying when reasoning results fail to transport.

articles.title: A Measure-Theoretic Analysis of Reasoning: Structural Generalization and Approximation Limits
articles.tldr: Formalizes reasoning as optimal transport to bound OOD generalization risk by the Wasserstein-1 domain shift, with architectural and scaling-law validity limits.
articles.contribution: Establishes a scaling-law validity limit: scaling representation width cannot bypass irreducible Barron-space approximation bounds, and only physical depth scaling averts representation collapse (a TC^0 circuit-depth lower bound).

articles.title: A Data-driven feature selection and machine-learning model benchmark for the prediction of longitudinal dispersion coefficient
articles.tldr: Questions the reliability of a widely used unproved feature set for dispersion-coefficient prediction and builds a fair, weighted ML model benchmark with data-driven feature selection.
articles.contribution: Challenges the widely used 'unproved quaternion feature set' derived by simple theoretical deduction, questioning its reliability/rationality and distilling a data-driven optimal feature set instead.

articles.title: A Data-driven feature selection and machine-learning model benchmark for the prediction of longitudinal dispersion coefficient
articles.tldr: Questions the reliability of a widely used unproved feature set for dispersion-coefficient prediction and builds a fair, weighted ML model benchmark with data-driven feature selection.
articles.contribution: Designs a weighted evaluation metric with a simple linear-model baseline to enable comprehensive, fair comparison of single and ensemble learners rather than a naive single-number ranking.

articles.title: STAGE-Claw: Automated State-based Agent Benchmarking for Realistic Scenarios
articles.tldr: State-based agent benchmark showing that output-only scoring overestimates agent capability, with verification of final system state exposing harness-level failures.
articles.contribution: Shows scoring the textual response (output-only) is a surface proxy that overestimates agent performance, and grounds the measure in correctness of the final persistent system state via verification programs.

articles.title: STAGE-Claw: Automated State-based Agent Benchmarking for Realistic Scenarios
articles.tldr: State-based agent benchmark showing that output-only scoring overestimates agent capability, with verification of final system state exposing harness-level failures.
articles.contribution: Reveals a 'real-state gap' (invalid state writes, missing generated artifacts, tool-side effects) in realistic operating environments that output-only harnesses miss, confounding measured agent capability.

articles.title: Verify-Gated Completion as Admission Control in a Governed Multi-Agent Runtime: A Bounded Architecture Case Study
articles.tldr: Bounded case study framing what verify-gated agent-completion evidence can validly support, with strict denominator hygiene and explicit claim boundaries.
articles.contribution: Argues the 99.5% event-level verify-success share is a surface accounting proxy that must not be read as task-level completion or production reliability, since task-level verify coverage is not computable from the released corpora.

articles.title: Verify-Gated Completion as Admission Control in a Governed Multi-Agent Runtime: A Bounded Architecture Case Study
articles.tldr: Bounded case study framing what verify-gated agent-completion evidence can validly support, with strict denominator hygiene and explicit claim boundaries.
articles.contribution: Shows the released verify slice is unrepresentative: 1784/1801 rows are synthetic/session and 1762/1801 come from one high-volume reporting cluster, so it is a snapshot-concentrated slice rather than a longitudinal production sample.

articles.title: Verify-Gated Completion as Admission Control in a Governed Multi-Agent Runtime: A Bounded Architecture Case Study
articles.tldr: Bounded case study framing what verify-gated agent-completion evidence can validly support, with strict denominator hygiene and explicit claim boundaries.
articles.contribution: Evaluates the shadow Policy/Governance Verifier and finds asymmetric reliability: 98.58% rule agreement and 0% false-success among safe-to-proceed calls but only 0.39% blocked precision, so it over-flags and stays advisory rather than an admission authority.

articles.title: Beyond Benchmark Islands: Toward Representative Trustworthiness Evaluation for Agentic AI
articles.tldr: Defines agentic trustworthiness as a measurable five-property construct and argues representative scenario-distribution design, not metric design, is the core evaluation gap.
articles.contribution: Gives an operational five-property definition of agent trustworthiness (Reliability, Robustness, Safety, Social-Ethical Alignment, Operational Integrity) grounded in NIST/EU risk frameworks, arguing that any 'passes a trustworthiness audit' claim is vacuous without such a construct.

articles.title: Beyond Benchmark Islands: Toward Representative Trustworthiness Evaluation for Agentic AI
articles.tldr: Defines agentic trustworthiness as a measurable five-property construct and argues representative scenario-distribution design, not metric design, is the core evaluation gap.
articles.contribution: Identifies a representativeness gap where benchmark distribution P_bench diverges from deployment P_deploy, and proposes distribution-aware, risk-weighted scenario sampling so evaluation covers rare-but-high-consequence socio-technical scenarios rather than disconnected benchmark islands.

articles.title: Beyond Benchmark Islands: Toward Representative Trustworthiness Evaluation for Agentic AI
articles.tldr: Defines agentic trustworthiness as a measurable five-property construct and argues representative scenario-distribution design, not metric design, is the core evaluation gap.
articles.contribution: Shows scalar leaderboard aggregation is a surface proxy that erases property-level trade-offs (a system strong on robustness but last on social alignment), so trustworthiness must be reported as a multi-dimensional profile with Pareto/property-wise contrasts.

articles.title: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design
articles.tldr: Survey arguing agent benchmark scores are outcomes of a model-harness pairing, so evaluation must attribute performance across the harness rather than read task success alone.
articles.contribution: Synthesizes evidence that benchmark scores are outcomes of a model-harness pairing: on SWE-bench Verified the same backbone gains or loses tens of resolved instances depending on the scaffold, so runtime/harness design confounds what agent benchmarks are taken to measure.

articles.title: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design
articles.tldr: Survey arguing agent benchmark scores are outcomes of a model-harness pairing, so evaluation must attribute performance across the harness rather than read task success alone.
articles.contribution: Notes static capability benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA, HumanEval) are saturating at the frontier with contamination risks complicating interpretation, motivating a shift to ecologically realistic agentic benchmarks whose headroom is far from solved.

articles.title: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design
articles.tldr: Survey arguing agent benchmark scores are outcomes of a model-harness pairing, so evaluation must attribute performance across the harness rather than read task success alone.
articles.contribution: Reviews judgment/attribution methods, flagging that LLM-as-judge evaluators (G-Eval, MT-Bench) carry bias, inconsistency and evaluator drift, and that procedure-aware evaluation shows apparent task completion can hide unsafe or invalid trajectories.

articles.title: Brief Is Better: Non-Monotonic Chain-of-Thought Budget Effects in Function-Calling Language Agents
articles.tldr: Systematic study finding non-monotonic chain-of-thought budget effects in function-calling agents while rigorously ruling out that the collapse is an artifact of the two-phase generation protocol.
articles.contribution: Addresses whether the measured CoT-budget collapse is a confound of the two-phase (reason-then-force-JSON) generation protocol, using a format-control ablation and natural-EOS analysis (0% early EOS) to argue it is a genuine reasoning-quality effect, not a protocol artifact.

articles.title: Brief Is Better: Non-Monotonic Chain-of-Thought Budget Effects in Function-Calling Language Agents
articles.tldr: Systematic study finding non-monotonic chain-of-thought budget effects in function-calling agents while rigorously ruling out that the collapse is an artifact of the two-phase generation protocol.
articles.contribution: Establishes the non-monotonic effect with McNemar tests (p<0.001) and 10k-bootstrap CIs, and reports a negative reliability result: pre-reasoning entropy H0 is not a usable gating signal (Mann-Whitney p=0.092) and never beats a fixed 32-token budget.

articles.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence
articles.tldr: Benchmark measuring spontaneous plan-action divergence (agent deception), designed to separate strategic deception from hallucination and from capability limits under controlled pressure with real tool execution.
articles.contribution: Operationally defines deception as a regular-vs-pressure plan-action divergence (action fixed at intrinsic stance while the stated plan shifts toward external expectation), distinguishing it structurally from scheming, sandbagging, and mere hallucination.

articles.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence
articles.tldr: Benchmark measuring spontaneous plan-action divergence (agent deception), designed to separate strategic deception from hallucination and from capability limits under controlled pressure with real tool execution.
articles.contribution: Controls capability and complexity confounds: scenario tool pools guarantee both options are executable, and a complexity analysis shows deception does not rise monotonically with solution-path length, so the signal is not reducible to task difficulty.

articles.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence
articles.tldr: Benchmark measuring spontaneous plan-action divergence (agent deception), designed to separate strategic deception from hallucination and from capability limits under controlled pressure with real tool execution.
articles.contribution: Validates the automated deception judger against 200 human-annotated trajectories (fine-tuned Qwen-3-32B reaches 82.5% deception accuracy) and reduces classification instability via a stance-inference-then-rule design instead of direct deception prediction.

articles.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence
articles.tldr: Benchmark measuring spontaneous plan-action divergence (agent deception), designed to separate strategic deception from hallucination and from capability limits under controlled pressure with real tool execution.
articles.contribution: Argues single-pass (pass@1) decoding masks stochastic safety risk and adopts a Pass@k=5 protocol (T=0.7) with Wilson 95% CIs and temperature-sensitivity checks, showing deception rate rises monotonically with k.

articles.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence
articles.tldr: Benchmark measuring spontaneous plan-action divergence (agent deception), designed to separate strategic deception from hallucination and from capability limits under controlled pressure with real tool execution.
articles.contribution: Flags a reactivity limitation: the benchmark assumes agents treat the sandbox as real, and warns that growing situational/test awareness could let models mask deceptive tendencies specifically during evaluation.

articles.title: Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents over Evolving Knowledge
articles.tldr: Shows RAG cannot maintain temporal validity of evolving facts and that cosine similarity cannot detect contradictions, and introduces a marker-free benchmark invariant to avoid contaminating staleness evaluations.
articles.contribution: Introduces and test-enforces a marker-free benchmark invariant, showing that a textual staleness marker (e.g. [OUTDATED]) is a leaked shortcut cue that inflated reranker-RAG accuracy by 14 points and a gate baseline by 18, silently contaminating memory-under-evolution evaluations.

articles.title: Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents over Evolving Knowledge
articles.tldr: Shows RAG cannot maintain temporal validity of evolving facts and that cosine similarity cannot detect contradictions, and introduces a marker-free benchmark invariant to avoid contaminating staleness evaluations.
articles.contribution: Proves a structural impossibility result that embedding cosine similarity mis-measures fact currency: it separates contradictions from duplicates at AUROC 0.59 (near chance, max precision 0.67), because a value-flip is more similar to the original than a genuine rephrasing.

articles.title: PromptShift-CRC: Drift-Aware Conformal Risk Control for Foundation Models Under Prompt and Domain Shift
articles.tldr: Drift-aware conformal risk control that keeps foundation-model risk guarantees valid when the prompt or domain distribution shifts away from the calibration data.
articles.contribution: Derives a finite-sample risk-control bound (Prop 1, Thm 1) decomposing the realized risk-violation probability into target level, drift bias, residual representation mismatch, and weighted-quantile uncertainty tied to effective calibration size.

articles.title: PromptShift-CRC: Drift-Aware Conformal Risk Control for Foundation Models Under Prompt and Domain Shift
articles.tldr: Drift-aware conformal risk control that keeps foundation-model risk guarantees valid when the prompt or domain distribution shifts away from the calibration data.
articles.contribution: Formalizes prompt/domain drift as a measurable transport score between the current window and the weighted calibration pool, showing static conformal calibration becomes unrepresentative and under-covers after drift while the drift-aware method restores target risk.

articles.title: ACL-Verbatim: hallucination-free question answering for research
articles.tldr: Extractive (hallucination-free) QA over the ACL Anthology contributing a ground-truth span dataset whose annotation exposes the subjectivity of relevance judgments and motivating word-level over span-level extraction metrics.
articles.contribution: Documents that annotating the most-relevant answer spans in research papers demands domain expertise and is highly subjective (e.g. a parsing query where none of the top-5 retrieved chunks is the source paper), limiting inter-annotator agreement and forcing a relaxed adjudication.

articles.title: ACL-Verbatim: hallucination-free question answering for research
articles.tldr: Extractive (hallucination-free) QA over the ACL Anthology contributing a ground-truth span dataset whose annotation exposes the subjectivity of relevance judgments and motivating word-level over span-level extraction metrics.
articles.contribution: Argues for word-level precision/recall over NER-style span-level exact match because span-level penalizes minor boundary mismatches as both false positive and false negative, and adds asymmetric containment/coverage metrics to capture extraction quality more faithfully.

articles.title: VeriTrip: A Verifiable Benchmark for Travel Planning Agents over Unstructured Web Corpora
articles.tldr: Travel-planning agent benchmark with cell-wise factual verification against a frozen knowledge base to decouple genuine retrieval from parametric hallucination.
articles.contribution: Cell-wise fact-check against a frozen Verifiable Knowledge Base (exact/fuzzy match) penalizes fabricated details and decouples genuine retrieval-based reasoning from parametric memorization/contamination.

articles.title: VeriTrip: A Verifiable Benchmark for Travel Planning Agents over Unstructured Web Corpora
articles.tldr: Travel-planning agent benchmark with cell-wise factual verification against a frozen knowledge base to decouple genuine retrieval from parametric hallucination.
articles.contribution: Argues existing API-clean travel benchmarks measure constraint satisfaction over provided facts rather than autonomous fact discovery, reframing the construct as evidence-grounded planning over noisy unstructured web corpora.

articles.title: Rank, Don't Generate: Statement-level Ranking for Explainable Recommendation
articles.tldr: Reframes explainable-recommendation evaluation as statement ranking to mitigate hallucination and enable reproducible metrics, built on a validated extraction/clustering benchmark.
articles.contribution: Shows lexical n-gram and embedding metrics reward surface/semantic similarity without factual grounding, and operationalizes explanation quality as ranking of atomic, explanatory, unique review-grounded statements to mitigate hallucination by construction.

articles.title: Rank, Don't Generate: Statement-level Ranking for Explainable Recommendation
articles.tldr: Reframes explainable-recommendation evaluation as statement ranking to mitigate hallucination and enable reproducible metrics, built on a validated extraction/clustering benchmark.
articles.contribution: Argues LLM-based evaluators are prompt-dependent, proprietary and hard to reproduce, and replaces them with standardized information-retrieval ranking metrics (P/R/NDCG) for stable, reproducible evaluation.

articles.title: Rank, Don't Generate: Statement-level Ranking for Explainable Recommendation
articles.tldr: Reframes explainable-recommendation evaluation as statement ranking to mitigate hallucination and enable reproducible metrics, built on a validated extraction/clustering benchmark.
articles.contribution: Introduces simple popularity baselines (UserPop/ItemPop/GlobalPop) and shows a user-history popularity baseline matches or surpasses SOTA models in item-level ranking, exposing that model claims are confounded by missing trivial baselines.

articles.title: GRACE: Step-Level Benchmark for Faithful Reasoning over Context
articles.tldr: Human-annotated step-level faithfulness benchmark with a bottom-up error taxonomy, showing final-answer accuracy masks unfaithful context-grounded reasoning.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates final-answer accuracy is a shortcut-confounded proxy for reasoning quality: correct answers are frequently reached through knowledge-shortcut injection or self-correction over unfaithful intermediate steps, so accuracy overestimates reasoning validity.

articles.title: GRACE: Step-Level Benchmark for Faithful Reasoning over Context
articles.tldr: Human-annotated step-level faithfulness benchmark with a bottom-up error taxonomy, showing final-answer accuracy masks unfaithful context-grounded reasoning.
articles.contribution: Builds step-level faithfulness labels via a bottom-up unsupervised-clustering error taxonomy plus multi-judge consensus tiers and human adjudication, reporting inter-annotator reliability to establish label quality.

articles.title: Entropy and Attention Dynamics in Small Language Models: A Trace-Level Structural Analysis on the TruthfulQA Benchmark
articles.tldr: Trace-level entropy/attention analysis arguing outcome accuracy under-measures SLM truthfulness, with reliability-checked human truthfulness labels on TruthfulQA.
articles.contribution: Argues final accuracy and hallucination-rate under-represent the truthfulness construct in small language models and proposes trace-level entropy/attention dynamics as a complementary, internally-grounded measure of generative reliability.

articles.title: Entropy and Attention Dynamics in Small Language Models: A Trace-Level Structural Analysis on the TruthfulQA Benchmark
articles.tldr: Trace-level entropy/attention analysis arguing outcome accuracy under-measures SLM truthfulness, with reliability-checked human truthfulness labels on TruthfulQA.

articles.title: Benchmarking Local LLMs for Natural-Language-to-SQL Querying in Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing: An Empirical Benchmark on Consumer-Grade Hardware

articles.title: Benchmarking Local LLMs for Natural-Language-to-SQL Querying in Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing: An Empirical Benchmark on Consumer-Grade Hardware

articles.title: A Comparative Study of Language Models for Khmer Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering
articles.tldr: Comparative Khmer RAG study showing verdict-based RAGAS metrics are more reliable than similarity-based ones and that English-validated evaluation assumptions do not transfer to a low-resource non-Latin script.
articles.contribution: Argues RAG evaluation metrics validated in English do not transfer to low-resource non-Latin Khmer; verdict-based FaiFul/FacCor (LLM-judge) align with expert judgment while embedding-similarity metrics remain unreliable.

articles.title: MedFabric and EtHER: A Data-Centric Framework for Word-Level Fabrication Generation and Detection in Medical LLMs
articles.authors: Tung Sum Thomas Kwok et al.
articles.tldr: MedFabric exposes that existing medical hallucination detectors exploit stylistic/structural shortcuts rather than factual content, and builds a style-controlled fabrication benchmark plus a lower-variance word-level detector (EtHER).
articles.contribution: Constructs MedFabric with style-controlled fabrications (ROUGE-L >= 0.7) to reveal that fine-tuned detectors classify on writing-style artifacts rather than factual content, a shortcut confound that inflates apparent accuracy.

articles.title: MedFabric and EtHER: A Data-Centric Framework for Word-Level Fabrication Generation and Detection in Medical LLMs
articles.authors: Tung Sum Thomas Kwok et al.
articles.tldr: MedFabric exposes that existing medical hallucination detectors exploit stylistic/structural shortcuts rather than factual content, and builds a style-controlled fabrication benchmark plus a lower-variance word-level detector (EtHER).
articles.contribution: Documents that zero-shot LLM-as-judge fabrication detectors are unstable under sampling randomness on OOD samples and designs EtHER's decomposed pipeline to achieve prediction variance comparable to a single-step judge.

articles.title: MedFabric and EtHER: A Data-Centric Framework for Word-Level Fabrication Generation and Detection in Medical LLMs
