articles.contribution: Shows existing medical hallucination datasets under-cover the fabrication construct (only 0.5% of MedHallu are fabrications) and suffer distributional drift during synthesis, so benchmarks under-represent the highest-risk error type.

articles.title: MISID: A Multimodal Multi-turn Dataset for Complex Intent Recognition in Strategic Deception Games
articles.tldr: MISID is a multimodal multi-turn deception-game benchmark whose fact-grounded causal annotation and reasoning metrics expose that binary accuracy overstates capability and that added visual modality acts as a confounding noise source.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes hidden-intent recognition to resist textual-shortcut over-reliance (unlike prior 'transparent' benchmarks) via a two-tier fact-based causal annotation scheme (3,962 segments, 154-555 turns) verified by four annotators with cross-modal consistency audits.

articles.title: MISID: A Multimodal Multi-turn Dataset for Complex Intent Recognition in Strategic Deception Games
articles.tldr: MISID is a multimodal multi-turn deception-game benchmark whose fact-grounded causal annotation and reasoning metrics expose that binary accuracy overstates capability and that added visual modality acts as a confounding noise source.
articles.contribution: Shows binary accuracy overstates genuine capability (models hit the correct lie label but flawed reasoning) and adds evidence-based reasoning metrics with a hard-truncation rule that caps the intent score when the state judgment is wrong, suppressing fact-detached logical hallucinations.

articles.title: MISID: A Multimodal Multi-turn Dataset for Complex Intent Recognition in Strategic Deception Games
articles.tldr: MISID is a multimodal multi-turn deception-game benchmark whose fact-grounded causal annotation and reasoning metrics expose that binary accuracy overstates capability and that added visual modality acts as a confounding noise source.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses text-prior visual hallucination (models force visual descriptions to match deceptive text) and 'impaired modal synergy' where adding the visual modality acts as noise and lowers measured reasoning.

articles.title: Building Reliable Long-Form Generation via Hallucination Rejection Sampling
articles.tldr: SHARS is an inference-time hallucination-mitigation framework whose HalluSE detector diagnoses and fixes construct-validity flaws in naive long-form semantic entropy and quantifies detection reliability.
articles.contribution: Identifies that naive long-form semantic entropy mis-measures hallucination because answer multiplicity confounds the entropy signal and the wrong entity gets probed; HalluSE fixes this via entity-claim decomposition and eliciting all valid answers.

articles.title: Building Reliable Long-Form Generation via Hallucination Rejection Sampling
articles.tldr: SHARS is an inference-time hallucination-mitigation framework whose HalluSE detector diagnoses and fixes construct-validity flaws in naive long-form semantic entropy and quantifies detection reliability.
articles.contribution: Quantifies detector reliability (HalluSE AUROC 72.9 vs Naive SE 66.2, P(True) 69.8, Self-Check 57.6) and reports 3-run mean+/-std (e.g., FactScore FPrec 77.32+/-1.36) to show gains are not stochastic artifacts.

articles.title: Can AI Reason Like an Urban Planner? Benchmarking Large Language Models Against Professional Judgment
articles.tldr: UPBench is a theory-grounded urban-planning reasoning benchmark whose Bloom-based construct, dual-track (automated+expert) scoring, and non-monotonic cognitive curve expose that lower-order recall resists generalization.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes urban-planning expertise via a theory-grounded 4x5 matrix (four knowledge pillars x Bloom's five cognitive levels), with a five-member expert panel validating content validity and two-rater cognitive-level tagging over 405 scenarios.

articles.title: Can AI Reason Like an Urban Planner? Benchmarking Large Language Models Against Professional Judgment
articles.tldr: UPBench is a theory-grounded urban-planning reasoning benchmark whose Bloom-based construct, dual-track (automated+expert) scoring, and non-monotonic cognitive curve expose that lower-order recall resists generalization.
articles.contribution: Adopts a dual-track protocol combining automated LLM scoring with expert-panel assessment to reliably score judgment-dependent planning tasks, motivated by the tension that automated scoring alone cannot capture situated judgment.

articles.title: Can AI Reason Like an Urban Planner? Benchmarking Large Language Models Against Professional Judgment
articles.tldr: UPBench is a theory-grounded urban-planning reasoning benchmark whose Bloom-based construct, dual-track (automated+expert) scoring, and non-monotonic cognitive curve expose that lower-order recall resists generalization.
articles.contribution: The non-monotonic cognitive curve (models stronger on higher-order analysis than lower-order recall) shows Bloom's assumed difficulty ordering breaks for planning because jurisdiction/temporal-specific knowledge resists pattern-generalization, codified as four epistemic diagnostics.

articles.title: AdversaRiskQA: An Adversarial Factuality Benchmark for High-Risk Domains
articles.tldr: AdversaRiskQA is a verified adversarial-factuality benchmark for Health/Finance/Law that validates its LLM judge against humans, controls invalid-response confounds, and finds long-form factuality uncorrelated with injected misinformation.
articles.contribution: Uses GPT-5-mini as judge (deliberately distinct from GPT-5 used for curation to reduce self-consistency bias) and validates it against human review on a 20% stratified subset, reporting 90-95% agreement.

articles.title: AdversaRiskQA: An Adversarial Factuality Benchmark for High-Risk Domains
articles.tldr: AdversaRiskQA is a verified adversarial-factuality benchmark for Health/Finance/Law that validates its LLM judge against humans, controls invalid-response confounds, and finds long-form factuality uncorrelated with injected misinformation.
articles.contribution: Shows raw accuracy is confounded by malformed responses (null outputs, prompt echo, template leakage); filtering them raises mean accuracy from 75.6% to 85.1% and flips the ranking, so unfiltered scores misattribute generation failures to reasoning errors.

articles.title: AdversaRiskQA: An Adversarial Factuality Benchmark for High-Risk Domains
articles.tldr: AdversaRiskQA is a verified adversarial-factuality benchmark for Health/Finance/Law that validates its LLM judge against humans, controls invalid-response confounds, and finds long-form factuality uncorrelated with injected misinformation.
articles.contribution: Builds a verified, difficulty-balanced (basic/advanced) adversarial benchmark grounded in authoritative Health/Finance/Law sources, while flagging small English-only datasets and a common-knowledge contamination effect in law as generalizability threats.

articles.title: EVE: A Domain-Specific LLM Framework for Earth Intelligence
articles.tldr: EVE is a domain-specific Earth-Intelligence LLM whose evaluation contributes a judge-family-bias confound control and a token-level RAG retrieval metric that critiques the construct validity of conventional order-based IR metrics.
articles.contribution: Controls the confound that synthetic-data-generation model families overlap with the LLM-judge panel by adding two independent judge families (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash); rankings shift by at most +/-0.25, showing no systematic self-favoring bias.

articles.title: EVE: A Domain-Specific LLM Framework for Earth Intelligence
articles.tldr: EVE is a domain-specific Earth-Intelligence LLM whose evaluation contributes a judge-family-bias confound control and a token-level RAG retrieval metric that critiques the construct validity of conventional order-based IR metrics.
articles.contribution: Argues conventional order-based IR metrics do not measure what matters for RAG (LLMs are insensitive to chunk position; inter-chunk ranking is ambiguous) and proposes a token-granularity IoU/precision/recall protocol on a semi-synthetic set built to avoid embedding-model contamination.

articles.title: Retromorphic Testing with Hierarchical Verification for Hallucination Detection in RAG
articles.tldr: RT4CHART is a claim-level RAG hallucination detector whose re-annotation of RAGTruth reveals standard benchmarks massively under-label hallucinations, plus judge-model robustness and run-to-run reproducibility checks.
articles.contribution: Re-annotation shows RAGTruth ground-truth labels contain substantial false negatives (spans grow 86->865 on the 408-sample subset; RAGTruth-Enhance uncovers 1.68x more cases and 3.1x more spans), so standard benchmark labels systematically understate hallucination prevalence.

articles.title: Retromorphic Testing with Hierarchical Verification for Hallucination Detection in RAG
articles.tldr: RT4CHART is a claim-level RAG hallucination detector whose re-annotation of RAGTruth reveals standard benchmarks massively under-label hallucinations, plus judge-model robustness and run-to-run reproducibility checks.
articles.contribution: Assesses detector reliability by swapping the judge model (GPT-4o mini -> GLM-4.7, performance stays strong) and repeating runs (F1 0.779+/-0.014 over 3 runs), showing detection is stable under nondeterministic APIs.

articles.title: Council Mode: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Consensus Framework for Reducing LLM Hallucination and Bias
articles.tldr: Council Mode is a multi-agent consensus system whose evaluation audits LLM-judge self-preference bias, empirically measures correlated errors that undermine agreement-as-truth, and controls a synthesizer-as-baseline confound.
articles.contribution: Audits the GPT-5.4 claim-level judge against adjudicated human labels (F1 0.89, Cohen's kappa 0.83) and tests self-assessment bias (F1 0.88 on its own outputs vs 0.89 on others), finding minimal self-preference bias under a rubric-constrained protocol.

articles.title: Council Mode: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Consensus Framework for Reducing LLM Hallucination and Bias
articles.tldr: Council Mode is a multi-agent consensus system whose evaluation audits LLM-judge self-preference bias, empirically measures correlated errors that undermine agreement-as-truth, and controls a synthesizer-as-baseline confound.
articles.contribution: Empirically measures pairwise error correlation (rho = 0.32-0.38) between frontier experts, refuting the independence assumption behind consensus/voting; 19% of failures are 'Correlated Hallucination' where consensus mistakes shared error (shared corpora/benchmark contamination) for validated truth.

articles.title: Council Mode: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Consensus Framework for Reducing LLM Hallucination and Bias
articles.tldr: Council Mode is a multi-agent consensus system whose evaluation audits LLM-judge self-preference bias, empirically measures correlated errors that undermine agreement-as-truth, and controls a synthesizer-as-baseline confound.
articles.contribution: Identifies and controls the confound that the synthesis model (Seed 2.0 Pro) is also a baseline, via a synthesizer-swap ablation (gpt-4.1-mini still reaches 89.5% quality) and a same-model-ensemble control (3x GPT-5.4 only 83.1%).

articles.title: Cross-Language Bias Examination in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Cross-lingual LLM bias study showing explicit (BBQ) and implicit (IAT) bias diverge and vary widely across five languages, exposing that standard benchmarks miss implicit bias.
articles.contribution: Shows explicit BBQ benchmarks fail to capture implicit associative bias (age has the lowest explicit but the highest implicit bias), so standard bias benchmarks under-represent the bias construct.

articles.title: Cross-Language Bias Examination in Large Language Models

articles.title: PROXYQA: An Alternative Framework for Evaluating Long-Form Text Generation with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: ProxyQA evaluates long-form generation by measuring how well an evaluator answers hidden expert-annotated proxy-questions using the generated text, avoiding references and contamination.
articles.contribution: Proxy-question scoring gives an 88% self-consistent metric that removes the GPT-as-judge self-preference bias and correlates strongly with human majority preference.

articles.title: PROXYQA: An Alternative Framework for Evaluating Long-Form Text Generation with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: ProxyQA evaluates long-form generation by measuring how well an evaluator answers hidden expert-annotated proxy-questions using the generated text, avoiding references and contamination.
articles.contribution: Keeps proxy-questions and answers private and periodically refreshed, preventing benchmark data leakage into models under test.

articles.title: INSTRUCTSCORE: Explainable Text Generation Evaluation with Finegrained Feedback
articles.tldr: Explainable learned metric (LLaMA fine-tuned on GPT-4 data) that scores generation and emits a fine-grained diagnostic report of errors.
articles.contribution: Builds an interpretable 7B scorer for generation quality that reports each error's phrase, type, and severity, improving the reliability/transparency of automatic metrics.

articles.title: Search Engines in an AI Era: The False Promise of Factual and Verifiable Source-Cited Responses
articles.tldr: User study plus automated benchmark (AEE) showing LLM answer engines give a false promise of factual, verifiable source-cited responses.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes answer-engine quality into 8 automated metrics (answer-text, source, and citation metrics) capturing factuality and citation accuracy rather than surface fluency.

articles.title: Search Engines in an AI Era: The False Promise of Factual and Verifiable Source-Cited Responses
articles.tldr: User study plus automated benchmark (AEE) showing LLM answer engines give a false promise of factual, verifiable source-cited responses.
articles.contribution: Grounds the automated metrics in a 21-participant real-use study whose insights the automated eval mirrors, giving ecological/criterion validity to the answer-engine limitations.

articles.title: Is Your World Simulator a Good Story Presenter? A Consecutive Events-Based Benchmark for Future Long Video Generation
articles.tldr: StoryEval: a story-completion benchmark for text-to-video that uses VLM verifiers with unanimous voting to reliably measure event-level story presentation.
articles.contribution: Improves reliability of VLM-judge scoring of generated videos via N-over-N unanimous voting that counters VLM overestimation on blurry synthetic footage.

articles.title: Is Your World Simulator a Good Story Presenter? A Consecutive Events-Based Benchmark for Future Long Video Generation
articles.tldr: StoryEval: a story-completion benchmark for text-to-video that uses VLM verifiers with unanimous voting to reliably measure event-level story presentation.
articles.contribution: Argues detail-oriented metrics (aesthetics, temporal consistency) are surface proxies and introduces story-completion rate as the intended higher-level construct.

articles.title: FETA: Towards Specializing Foundation Models for Expert Task Applications
articles.tldr: FETA benchmark for expert-document retrieval, with a fully automatic co-location annotation whose metric is validated as consistent with human-curated ground truth.
articles.contribution: Shows a fully automatic image-text co-location annotation (MIL bags) yields performance rankings consistent with human-curated annotations, validating it as a low-noise ground-truth proxy.

articles.title: Scaling Laws Do Not Scale
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing scaling laws do not scale because performance metrics are imperfect, value-laden proxies whose validity breaks down as datasets and communities grow.
articles.contribution: Argues performance metrics are imperfect proxies for model quality that do not correspond to how different communities perceive output quality.

articles.title: Scaling Laws Do Not Scale
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing scaling laws do not scale because performance metrics are imperfect, value-laden proxies whose validity breaks down as datasets and communities grow.
articles.contribution: Challenges the temporal/scale validity of scaling-law claims that performance monotonically improves with dataset size.

articles.title: Scaling Laws Do Not Scale
articles.tldr: Position paper arguing scaling laws do not scale because performance metrics are imperfect, value-laden proxies whose validity breaks down as datasets and communities grow.
articles.contribution: Shows that as datasets grow the number of represented subgroups grows and their metrics can be mutually incompatible, threatening external validity of scale claims.

articles.title: ValueBench: Towards Comprehensively Evaluating Value Orientations and Understanding of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: ValueBench: a psychometric benchmark from 44 inventories that critiques Likert self-report testing and evaluates LLM value orientations via authentic-interaction prompts scored by an LLM judge.
articles.contribution: Grounds value measurement in 44 established psychometric inventories and 453 value dimensions with hierarchies, giving a theory-grounded construct instead of ad-hoc value spaces.

articles.title: ValueBench: Towards Comprehensively Evaluating Value Orientations and Understanding of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: ValueBench: a psychometric benchmark from 44 inventories that critiques Likert self-report testing and evaluates LLM value orientations via authentic-interaction prompts scored by an LLM judge.
articles.contribution: Shows Likert self-report items are an invalid proxy for LLM values and replaces them with advice-seeking authentic-interaction questions that better capture the construct.

articles.title: ValueBench: Towards Comprehensively Evaluating Value Orientations and Understanding of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: ValueBench: a psychometric benchmark from 44 inventories that critiques Likert self-report testing and evaluates LLM value orientations via authentic-interaction prompts scored by an LLM judge.
articles.contribution: Assesses reliability of the GPT-4 Turbo evaluator that rates responses 0-10, reporting 80.0% agreement with human annotators.

articles.title: Multimodal Large Language Model is a Human-Aligned Annotator for Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Argues a multimodal LLM (GPT-4 Vision) is a human-aligned annotator for text-to-image preference, validating AI annotations and a reward model (VP-Score) against human preferences.
articles.contribution: Validates GPT-4 Vision as a preference annotator whose accuracy (~70%) matches human-human agreement, supporting AI annotation as a reliable scoring instrument.

articles.title: Multimodal Large Language Model is a Human-Aligned Annotator for Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Argues a multimodal LLM (GPT-4 Vision) is a human-aligned annotator for text-to-image preference, validating AI annotations and a reward model (VP-Score) against human preferences.
articles.contribution: Trains VP-Score reward model on AI-annotated preferences and shows its preference-prediction accuracy is competitive with reward models trained on human data.

articles.title: Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Assessing Logical and Arithmetic Errors across Wide Numerical Ranges
articles.tldr: GSM-Ranges perturbs GSM8K numbers across six scales and adds a GPT-4o-to-Python grading method that separates logical from arithmetic errors, exposing OOD numerical brittleness and contamination.
articles.contribution: Introduces a grading methodology that translates a response into executable Python to isolate logical from non-logical (arithmetic) errors, validated at 98.5% accuracy.

articles.title: Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Assessing Logical and Arithmetic Errors across Wide Numerical Ranges
articles.tldr: GSM-Ranges perturbs GSM8K numbers across six scales and adds a GPT-4o-to-Python grading method that separates logical from arithmetic errors, exposing OOD numerical brittleness and contamination.
articles.contribution: Shows math benchmarks are unrepresentative in numerical range (numbers <1000 are 94.9% of GSM8K) and generates wider-range items revealing OOD degradation.

articles.title: Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Assessing Logical and Arithmetic Errors across Wide Numerical Ranges
articles.tldr: GSM-Ranges perturbs GSM8K numbers across six scales and adds a GPT-4o-to-Python grading method that separates logical from arithmetic errors, exposing OOD numerical brittleness and contamination.
articles.contribution: Uses the gap between level-1 (same-digit) perturbations and original GSM8K questions as a signal of dataset contamination in certain models.

articles.title: VidCapBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Video Captioning for Controllable Text-to-Video Generation
articles.tldr: Video-caption benchmark exposing GPT-4o judge instability and validating that caption-evaluation scores predict downstream text-to-video quality.
articles.contribution: Quantifies GPT-4o-as-judge instability across repeated runs and splits QA items into an auto-evaluable (stable) subset versus a human-evaluated (unstable) subset to keep the scorer reliable.

articles.title: VidCapBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Video Captioning for Controllable Text-to-Video Generation
articles.tldr: Video-caption benchmark exposing GPT-4o judge instability and validating that caption-evaluation scores predict downstream text-to-video quality.
articles.contribution: Establishes criterion validity by showing benchmark caption scores correlate strongly (Pearson ~0.89-0.92) with the quality of videos generated from those captions, so the caption metric predicts real downstream T2V performance.

articles.title: Dialogue Games for Benchmarking Language Understanding: Motivation, Taxonomy, Strategy
articles.tldr: Position paper importing psychometric construct validity and nomological networks to argue situated Dialogue Games give language-understanding benchmarks an explicit construct.
articles.contribution: Argues NLU benchmarks rest only on face validity of the task without specifying the understanding construct, and proposes a situated-language-understanding capability model as the nomological network that Dialogue Games operationalize.

articles.title: Dialogue Games for Benchmarking Language Understanding: Motivation, Taxonomy, Strategy
articles.tldr: Position paper importing psychometric construct validity and nomological networks to argue situated Dialogue Games give language-understanding benchmarks an explicit construct.
articles.contribution: Shows existing tests conflate understanding with world-knowledge recall (a surface proxy) and that dialogue games control world knowledge so success discriminates genuine understanding from confounds.

articles.title: A Study on the Generality of Neural Network Structures for Monocular Depth Estimation
articles.tldr: Analysis showing KITTI-only monocular-depth benchmarks hide poor out-of-distribution generalization, driven by CNN texture-bias shortcut versus Transformer shape-bias.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that evaluating depth models only on KITTI overstates performance, measuring large error increases on five unseen datasets and exposing a benchmark-driven external-validity gap.

articles.title: A Study on the Generality of Neural Network Structures for Monocular Depth Estimation
articles.tldr: Analysis showing KITTI-only monocular-depth benchmarks hide poor out-of-distribution generalization, driven by CNN texture-bias shortcut versus Transformer shape-bias.
articles.contribution: Identifies texture-bias as a shortcut confound behind the generalization gap, using texture-shifted probe datasets and CKA representation similarity to show shape-biased self-attention models generalize better.

articles.title: GenRES: Rethinking Evaluation for Generative Relation Extraction in the Era of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Shows exact-match precision/recall/F1 are invalid for generative relation extraction and proposes GenRES, a multi-dimensional metric validated against human preference.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that exact-match precision/recall/F1 are a surface proxy that misrepresents generative-RE quality, and introduces multi-dimensional metrics (topical similarity, uniqueness, factualness, granularity, completeness) that better capture the construct.

articles.title: GenRES: Rethinking Evaluation for Generative Relation Extraction in the Era of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Shows exact-match precision/recall/F1 are invalid for generative relation extraction and proposes GenRES, a multi-dimensional metric validated against human preference.
articles.contribution: Documents that human-annotated reference relations are incomplete and error-ridden, so reference-based scoring is unreliable ground truth for generative relation extraction.

articles.title: CEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Counterfactual Text Generation
articles.tldr: Unified benchmark for counterfactual text generation that enables fair cross-method comparison and reveals LLM-evaluator bias and target-classifier miscalibration.
articles.contribution: Unifies inconsistent datasets, metrics, and baselines from prior counterfactual-generation papers into one benchmark so methods can be compared fairly under identical conditions.

articles.title: CEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Counterfactual Text Generation
articles.tldr: Unified benchmark for counterfactual text generation that enables fair cross-method comparison and reveals LLM-evaluator bias and target-classifier miscalibration.
articles.contribution: Exposes LLM-evaluator bias where ChatGPT and GPT-2 perplexity prefer machine-generated counterfactuals over human ones, and validates an open Mistral judge as a correlated alternative to ChatGPT.

articles.title: AGHI-QA: A Subjective-Aligned Dataset and Metric for AI-Generated Human Images
articles.tldr: First fine-grained subjective benchmark and metric for AI-generated human-image quality, showing existing IQA methods under-measure anatomical distortions.
articles.contribution: Defines a fine-grained quality construct for AI-generated human images (perceptual quality, text-image correspondence, and per-body-part distortion) that global single-score IQA methods fail to represent.

articles.title: AGHI-QA: A Subjective-Aligned Dataset and Metric for AI-Generated Human Images
articles.tldr: First fine-grained subjective benchmark and metric for AI-generated human-image quality, showing existing IQA methods under-measure anatomical distortions.
articles.contribution: Runs a rigorous subjective study (multi-rater MOS following ITU-R BT.500 with outlier rejection and Z-score normalization) to produce reliable human ground-truth quality labels for the benchmark.

articles.title: PPM: Automated Generation of Diverse Programming Problems for Benchmarking Code Generation Models
articles.tldr: Automated programming-problem merging that generates diverse, contamination-resistant code benchmarks, exposing inflated LCGM scores.
articles.contribution: Randomized problem-merging with a private offset gives probabilistic long-term data integrity, preventing benchmark leakage into future code-model training corpora.

articles.title: PPM: Automated Generation of Diverse Programming Problems for Benchmarking Code Generation Models
articles.tldr: Automated programming-problem merging that generates diverse, contamination-resistant code benchmarks, exposing inflated LCGM scores.
articles.contribution: Shows perturbation-based benchmarks produce semantically homogeneous problems with identical canonical solutions, under-representing coding capability; merging yields genuinely diverse solutions (100% different-implementation rate).

articles.title: Check-Eval: A Checklist-based Approach for Evaluating Text Quality
articles.tldr: Check-Eval decomposes LLM-as-judge text-quality scoring into yes/no checklists to raise correlation with human judgments.
articles.contribution: Checklist-based decomposition of the LLM judge produces a more reliable, interpretable NLG-quality scorer with higher human correlation than G-Eval/GPTScore.

articles.title: DeepCRCEval: Revisiting the Evaluation of Code Review Comment Generation
articles.tldr: DeepCRCEval shows text-similarity metrics are invalid for code-review-comment generation and validates human+LLM criteria-based evaluation instead.
articles.contribution: Argues BLEU/ROUGE are surface proxies misaligned with the true code-review objective (defect detection/code improvement), so <1% BLEU gains do not reflect quality improvements.

articles.title: DeepCRCEval: Revisiting the Evaluation of Code Review Comment Generation
articles.tldr: DeepCRCEval shows text-similarity metrics are invalid for code-review-comment generation and validates human+LLM criteria-based evaluation instead.
articles.contribution: Empirically shows the human-authored OSS reference comments used as ground truth are arbitrary/low-quality, undermining any reference-based similarity metric.

articles.title: DeepCRCEval: Revisiting the Evaluation of Code Review Comment Generation
articles.tldr: DeepCRCEval shows text-similarity metrics are invalid for code-review-comment generation and validates human+LLM criteria-based evaluation instead.
articles.contribution: Validates GPT-4 evaluators against human raters via ICC to justify LLM judges as a cheaper, scalable scoring instrument for review comments.

articles.title: Evaluating and mitigating bias in AI-based medical text generation
articles.tldr: Measures and mitigates demographic bias in medical text generation, showing disparities are metric-dependent and confounded.
articles.contribution: Shows which subgroup looks disadvantaged flips with the metric (young/black higher ROUGE, aged/white higher CheXpert), so metric choice determines the measured fairness verdict; introduces the MFD indicator.

articles.title: Evaluating and mitigating bias in AI-based medical text generation
articles.tldr: Measures and mitigates demographic bias in medical text generation, showing disparities are metric-dependent and confounded.
articles.contribution: Traces subgroup score gaps to confounds in the metrics themselves: ROUGE tracks reference length (r=-0.21), CheXpert tracks positive-label rate (r=0.26).

articles.title: Evaluating and mitigating bias in AI-based medical text generation
articles.tldr: Measures and mitigates demographic bias in medical text generation, showing disparities are metric-dependent and confounded.
articles.contribution: Quantifies compounded intersectional bias across race/sex/age and model scales (100M-13B), showing doubly-underserved groups get lower-quality generated diagnoses.

articles.title: Questioning the Validity of Summarization Datasets and Improving Their Factual Consistency
articles.tldr: Questions the validity of popular summarization datasets, showing reference summaries are factually inconsistent, and releases a filtered SummFC benchmark.
articles.contribution: Shows CNN/DM, XSUM and XLSUM reference summaries are highlights/lead-lines ('pitch generation'), not faithful summaries, so the datasets misrepresent the summarization construct.

articles.title: Questioning the Validity of Summarization Datasets and Improving Their Factual Consistency
articles.tldr: Questions the validity of popular summarization datasets, showing reference summaries are factually inconsistent, and releases a filtered SummFC benchmark.
articles.contribution: Uses combined factuality models to filter inconsistent samples into SummFC and demonstrates that training on the cleaner subset improves generated-summary quality.

articles.title: When AIs Judge AIs: The Rise of Agent-as-a-Judge Evaluation for LLMs
articles.tldr: Survey of agent-as-a-judge evaluation, critically comparing single-LLM, multi-agent and agentic judges on reliability, bias and gameability.
articles.contribution: Traces the evolution from single-LLM judges to multi-agent and agentic judges, cataloguing reliability, human-alignment, cost and bias trade-offs of each evaluation paradigm.

articles.title: When AIs Judge AIs: The Rise of Agent-as-a-Judge Evaluation for LLMs
articles.tldr: Survey of agent-as-a-judge evaluation, critically comparing single-LLM, multi-agent and agentic judges on reliability, bias and gameability.
articles.contribution: Highlights that LLM/agent judges are gameable (null responses win, verbosity/self-model bias) and raises the unsolved meta-evaluation problem of validating the evaluators.

articles.title: Decoding machine learning benchmarks
articles.authors: L. F. F. Cardoso et al.
articles.tldr: Applies Item Response Theory plus Glicko-2 to audit whether the OpenML-CC18 benchmark actually discriminates classifier ability.
articles.contribution: IRT difficulty/discrimination analysis shows most OpenML-CC18 datasets are too easy to push classifier ability, questioning the benchmark's fitness as a gold standard.

articles.title: Decoding machine learning benchmarks
articles.authors: L. F. F. Cardoso et al.
articles.tldr: Applies Item Response Theory plus Glicko-2 to audit whether the OpenML-CC18 benchmark actually discriminates classifier ability.
articles.contribution: Uses IRT True-Score plus a Glicko-2 rating tournament for a difficulty-aware ranking of classifiers, then tests whether the ranking is statistically separable.

articles.title: SynthTRIPs: A Knowledge-Grounded Framework for Benchmark Data Generation for Personalized Tourism Recommenders
articles.tldr: SynthTRIPs generates KB-grounded synthetic travel queries and validates their realism, groundedness and LLM-judge-vs-expert agreement.
articles.contribution: Builds persona+filter, KB-grounded synthetic query benchmark covering sustainability/off-peak preferences underrepresented in existing travel datasets, validated for realism and coverage.

articles.title: SynthTRIPs: A Knowledge-Grounded Framework for Benchmark Data Generation for Personalized Tourism Recommenders
articles.tldr: SynthTRIPs generates KB-grounded synthetic travel queries and validates their realism, groundedness and LLM-judge-vs-expert agreement.
articles.contribution: Compares a gpt-4o judge-LLM against domain-expert evaluations across groundedness/persona/clarity, exposing where the automated judge misses nuances humans catch.

articles.title: SynthTRIPs: A Knowledge-Grounded Framework for Benchmark Data Generation for Personalized Tourism Recommenders
articles.tldr: SynthTRIPs generates KB-grounded synthetic travel queries and validates their realism, groundedness and LLM-judge-vs-expert agreement.
articles.contribution: Preliminary downstream analysis reveals a popularity bias in the recommender LLM that surfaces popular cities regardless of the query's stated low-popularity constraint.

articles.title: BEDS-Bench: Behavior of EHR-models under Distributional Shift-A Benchmark
articles.tldr: Benchmark measuring EHR ML models' calibration and generalization under distributional shift, and a critique of the OOD-detection metric itself.
articles.contribution: Benchmark quantifying EHR models' AUC/ECE drop under deliberately dissimilar OOD train-test splits across demographics.

articles.title: BEDS-Bench: Behavior of EHR-models under Distributional Shift-A Benchmark
articles.tldr: Benchmark measuring EHR ML models' calibration and generalization under distributional shift, and a critique of the OOD-detection metric itself.
articles.contribution: Shows the OOD-detection confidence metric is ill-defined under class imbalance, undermining its validity as a measure.

articles.title: Dissecting Logical Reasoning in LLMs: A Fine-Grained Evaluation and Supervision Study
articles.tldr: Argues final-answer accuracy misrepresents reasoning quality; adds stepwise soundness and representation-level probing to diagnose logical-reasoning validity.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates final-answer accuracy fails to capture reasoning-process validity; adds validity/relevance/atomicity stepwise metrics.

articles.title: Dissecting Logical Reasoning in LLMs: A Fine-Grained Evaluation and Supervision Study
articles.tldr: Argues final-answer accuracy misrepresents reasoning quality; adds stepwise soundness and representation-level probing to diagnose logical-reasoning validity.
articles.contribution: Validates GPT-4.1-mini as a step-validity and atomicity judge, reporting >98% agreement on 200 human-annotated steps.

articles.title: LikePhys: Evaluating Intuitive Physics Understanding in Video Diffusion Models via Likelihood Preference
articles.tldr: Training-free likelihood metric (PPE) for intuitive physics in video diffusion models that disentangles physics correctness from visual appearance and beats VLM-judge baselines.
articles.contribution: PPE uses appearance-matched valid/invalid video pairs so the likelihood gap isolates physics, cancelling visual-appearance confounds.

articles.title: LikePhys: Evaluating Intuitive Physics Understanding in Video Diffusion Models via Likelihood Preference
articles.tldr: Training-free likelihood metric (PPE) for intuitive physics in video diffusion models that disentangles physics correctness from visual appearance and beats VLM-judge baselines.
articles.contribution: Shows VLM-judge physics evaluators suffer appearance bias and interpretive variance, whereas PPE correlates better with humans.

articles.title: VABench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Audio-Video Generation
articles.tldr: Multi-dimensional audio-video generation benchmark whose QA-based automatic metrics are validated against human preference.
articles.contribution: Defines 15 evaluation dimensions (sync, lip-speech, VQA/AQA) for audio-video generation and validates them against human perception.

articles.title: CLOMO: Counterfactual Logical Modification with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Counterfactual logical modification benchmark with a decomposed Self-Evaluation Score (SES) that evaluates free-form output directly and aligns with human preference.
articles.contribution: Proposes SES to score generative counterfactual edits directly, avoiding the multiple-choice format shortcut of prior operationalizations.

articles.title: CLOMO: Counterfactual Logical Modification with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Counterfactual logical modification benchmark with a decomposed Self-Evaluation Score (SES) that evaluates free-form output directly and aligns with human preference.
articles.contribution: Decomposed Self-Evaluation Score is an automatic LLM-based metric shown to align well with human preference.

articles.title: Automated Evaluation of Personalized Text Generation using Large Language Models
articles.tldr: LLM-as-evaluator (AuPEL) for personalized text generation that separates personalization, quality and relevance and is validated on accuracy, consistency and sensitivity.
articles.contribution: Defines and discriminates three dimensions (personalization, quality, relevance) that BLEU/ROUGE conflate into surface lexical similarity.

articles.title: Automated Evaluation of Personalized Text Generation using Large Language Models
articles.tldr: LLM-as-evaluator (AuPEL) for personalized text generation that separates personalization, quality and relevance and is validated on accuracy, consistency and sensitivity.
articles.contribution: Assesses the LLM evaluator on accuracy, consistency and sensitivity and mitigates order bias via balanced A/B swap testing.

articles.title: MathGAP: Out-of-Distribution Evaluation on Problems with Arbitrarily Complex Proofs
articles.tldr: Contamination-free data-generation framework (MathGAP) testing LLM out-of-distribution generalization on arbitrarily complex arithmetic proofs.
articles.contribution: Generates novel proof-structured problems and CoT traces to avoid train/test contamination that inflates math-benchmark scores.

articles.title: MathGAP: Out-of-Distribution Evaluation on Problems with Arbitrarily Complex Proofs
articles.tldr: Contamination-free data-generation framework (MathGAP) testing LLM out-of-distribution generalization on arbitrarily complex arithmetic proofs.
articles.contribution: Systematically measures easy-to-hard generalization as arithmetic proof trees get deeper and wider beyond training complexity.

articles.title: MathGAP: Out-of-Distribution Evaluation on Problems with Arbitrarily Complex Proofs
articles.tldr: Contamination-free data-generation framework (MathGAP) testing LLM out-of-distribution generalization on arbitrarily complex arithmetic proofs.
articles.contribution: Reveals models rely on sentence ordering, a surface confound in how problems are operationalized rather than genuine inference.

articles.title: Uncertainty Estimation of Large Language Models in Medical Question Answering
articles.tldr: Benchmarks uncertainty-estimation methods for hallucination detection in medical QA and proposes a probability-free Two-phase Verification measure.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks uncertainty-estimation methods (semantic/predictive/length-normalized entropy, lexical similarity) via AUROC and shows they poorly detect medical hallucinations.

articles.title: Uncertainty Estimation of Large Language Models in Medical Question Answering
articles.tldr: Benchmarks uncertainty-estimation methods for hallucination detection in medical QA and proposes a probability-free Two-phase Verification measure.
articles.contribution: Shows entropy misrepresents true uncertainty because models fabricate confidently, yielding misleadingly low entropy for wrong answers.

articles.title: 3DGen-Bench: Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for 3D Generative Models
articles.tldr: 3D generation human-preference dataset with CLIP- and MLLM-based automatic evaluators validated to correlate with human ranks better than existing 3D metrics.
articles.contribution: Trains 3DGen-Score (CLIP) and 3DGen-Eval (MLLM) automatic evaluators that predict human preference better than existing 3D metrics.

articles.title: 3DGen-Bench: Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for 3D Generative Models
articles.tldr: 3D generation human-preference dataset with CLIP- and MLLM-based automatic evaluators validated to correlate with human ranks better than existing 3D metrics.
articles.contribution: Collects large-scale multi-criteria human preference votes (comparisons plus absolute scores) via the 3DGen-Arena as evaluation ground truth.

articles.title: Surveying the Dead Minds: Historical-Psychological Text Analysis with Contextualized Construct Representation (CCR) for Classical Chinese
articles.tldr: Psychometric-survey-conditioned transformer pipeline (CCR) that measures psychological constructs in classical Chinese and validates the measure against objective external data.
articles.contribution: Grounds construct measurement in psychological surveys via contextualized construct representations so that traditionalism/norm-strength/collectivism scores reflect the theoretical construct rather than a surface lexical proxy.

articles.title: Surveying the Dead Minds: Historical-Psychological Text Analysis with Contextualized Construct Representation (CCR) for Classical Chinese
articles.tldr: Psychometric-survey-conditioned transformer pipeline (CCR) that measures psychological constructs in classical Chinese and validates the measure against objective external data.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks CCR scores against objective external historical data as an explicit criterion/external-validity check rather than relying only on internal test-set performance.

articles.title: Predicting the Big Five Personality Traits in Chinese Counselling Dialogues Using Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Evaluates whether LLMs can validly measure Big Five personality traits from counseling dialogues, using role-play/questionnaire prompting and correlation with ground-truth BFI as validity evidence.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes personality measurement by having the LLM role-play the client and answer the Big Five Inventory, testing whether LLM-derived trait scores capture the intended personality construct.

articles.title: Predicting the Big Five Personality Traits in Chinese Counselling Dialogues Using Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Evaluates whether LLMs can validly measure Big Five personality traits from counseling dialogues, using role-play/questionnaire prompting and correlation with ground-truth BFI as validity evidence.
articles.contribution: Uses Pearson correlation between LLM-predicted and actual Big Five traits on 853 real counseling sessions as criterion-validity evidence that the measure tracks the real trait.

articles.title: Neural Image Compression: Generalization, Robustness, and Spectral Biases
articles.tldr: Builds an OOD benchmark suite (CLIC-C/Kodak-C, 15 corruptions) and spectral inspection tools to reliably assess the out-of-distribution generalization and robustness of neural image compression.
articles.contribution: Introduces CLIC-C and Kodak-C by adding 15 corruptions to CLIC/Kodak so NIC evaluation covers train-deployment distribution shift instead of only in-distribution test images.

articles.title: Neural Image Compression: Generalization, Robustness, and Spectral Biases
articles.tldr: Builds an OOD benchmark suite (CLIC-C/Kodak-C, 15 corruptions) and spectral inspection tools to reliably assess the out-of-distribution generalization and robustness of neural image compression.
articles.contribution: Proposes spectrally-inspired inspection tools (Fourier sensitivity heatmaps) because scalar rate-distortion/PSNR metrics are limited and can be misleading about what compression quality actually is.

articles.title: Evaluating Subtitle Segmentation for End-to-end Generation Systems
articles.tldr: Systematically analyzes subtitle-segmentation evaluation metrics and proposes Sigma, a score that disentangles segmentation quality from text quality, while flagging metric reliability limits.
articles.contribution: Introduces Sigma (from an approximate BLEU upper-bound on boundaries) plus a boundary-projection method so segmentation accuracy can be measured independently of textual content when hypotheses differ from the reference.

articles.title: Evaluating Subtitle Segmentation for End-to-end Generation Systems
articles.tldr: Systematically analyzes subtitle-segmentation evaluation metrics and proposes Sigma, a score that disentangles segmentation quality from text quality, while flagging metric reliability limits.
articles.contribution: Shows existing segmentation metrics differ in sensitivity to error type, so which system is ranked best depends on the chosen metric, undermining measurement reliability.

articles.title: Antibody DomainBed: Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Therapeutic Protein Design
articles.tldr: Releases an antibody domain-generalization benchmark (extending DomainBed) with five design-cycle domains to test OOD generalization and shortcut/confounding in ML-guided therapeutic design.
articles.contribution: Provides an antibody-antigen stability dataset split into five design-cycle domains so that OOD generalization of surrogate models across active-design distribution shifts can be measured.

articles.title: Antibody DomainBed: Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Therapeutic Protein Design
articles.tldr: Releases an antibody domain-generalization benchmark (extending DomainBed) with five design-cycle domains to test OOD generalization and shortcut/confounding in ML-guided therapeutic design.
articles.contribution: Stress-tests domain-generalization algorithms against selection bias, confounding factors and spurious correlations in active drug design, seeking predictors that rely on causal rather than spurious factors.

articles.title: Are We Done with Object-Centric Learning?
articles.tldr: Argues object-discovery benchmarks no longer capture object-centric learning's real goals and uses a training-free probe (OCCAM) to test OOD generalization under spurious background cues.
articles.contribution: Introduces OCCAM, a training-free probe that encodes segmentation-masked individual objects, to isolate whether spurious background cues confound classification and drive OOD-generalization failures.

articles.title: Are We Done with Object-Centric Learning?
articles.tldr: Argues object-discovery benchmarks no longer capture object-centric learning's real goals and uses a training-free probe (OCCAM) to test OOD generalization under spurious background cues.
articles.contribution: Argues unsupervised object-discovery benchmarks are largely saturated and no longer measure OCL's real downstream goals, calling for benchmarks aligned with those fundamental objectives.

articles.title: Verifying the Generalization of Deep Learning to Out-of-Distribution Domains
articles.tldr: Uses DNN formal verification to measure and provide evidence of robust out-of-distribution generalization by quantifying agreement between independently trained networks over an input domain.
articles.contribution: Harnesses off-the-shelf DNN verification engines to produce verification-guided generalization scores spanning multiple distributions in an input domain, targeting external validity of decision rules under OOD inputs.

articles.title: Verifying the Generalization of Deep Learning to Out-of-Distribution Domains
articles.tldr: Uses DNN formal verification to measure and provide evidence of robust out-of-distribution generalization by quantifying agreement between independently trained networks over an input domain.
articles.contribution: Measures agreement between independently trained DNNs (differing only in stochastic training elements) over a domain as verifiable positive evidence that a learned decision rule generalizes robustly.

articles.title: BOOM: Benchmarking Out-Of-distribution Molecular Property Predictions of Machine Learning Models
articles.tldr: OOD molecular-property benchmark showing no ML model generalizes; even the best has ~3x higher OOD than in-distribution error.
articles.contribution: Builds chemically-informed OOD splits (BOOM) showing in-distribution accuracy massively overstates the extrapolative discovery performance that molecular ML is actually used for.

articles.title: BOOM: Benchmarking Out-Of-distribution Molecular Property Predictions of Machine Learning Models
articles.tldr: OOD molecular-property benchmark showing no ML model generalizes; even the best has ~3x higher OOD than in-distribution error.
articles.contribution: Shows high-inductive-bias models beat chemical foundation models OOD, implicating shortcut/spurious features that break the link between measured accuracy and true generalization.

articles.title: ARM-Thinker: Reinforcing Multimodal Generative Reward Models with Agentic Tool Use and Visual Reasoning
articles.tldr: Agentic multimodal reward model plus ARMBench-VL benchmark targeting the grounding/reliability of reward-model (LLM-judge) scoring.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses that static reward models hallucinate and lack visual grounding, and shows agentic tool-based verification makes the judge's scores more reliable (+16.2% on reward benchmarks).

articles.title: ARM-Thinker: Reinforcing Multimodal Generative Reward Models with Agentic Tool Use and Visual Reasoning
articles.tldr: Agentic multimodal reward model plus ARMBench-VL benchmark targeting the grounding/reliability of reward-model (LLM-judge) scoring.
articles.contribution: Argues non-interactive reward scores mis-capture correctness; grounding judgments in tool-verified evidence better captures the intended quality construct, measured via the new ARMBench-VL benchmark.

articles.title: Towards a Holistic Evaluation of LLMs on Factual Knowledge Recall
articles.tldr: FACT-BENCH holistically measures LLM factual-knowledge recall across 20 domains and probes the factors that confound it.
articles.contribution: Constructs a representative FACT-BENCH covering 20 domains, 134 property types, 3 answer types and multiple knowledge-popularity levels so factual-recall claims are not driven by convenience sampling.

articles.title: Towards a Holistic Evaluation of LLMs on Factual Knowledge Recall
articles.tldr: FACT-BENCH holistically measures LLM factual-knowledge recall across 20 domains and probes the factors that confound it.
articles.contribution: Uses counterfactual in-context demonstrations to isolate that exemplars contradicting a model's known knowledge (a confound) degrade measured factual recall.

articles.title: Assessing the Quality of AI-Generated Exams: A Large-Scale Field Study
articles.tldr: Large-scale IRT field study finding AI-generated exam questions are psychometrically comparable to expert-written standardized items.
articles.contribution: Applies item response theory (difficulty/discrimination) to assess the psychometric quality of AI-generated exam items rather than trusting surface generation correctness.

articles.title: Assessing the Quality of AI-Generated Exams: A Large-Scale Field Study
articles.tldr: Large-scale IRT field study finding AI-generated exam questions are psychometrically comparable to expert-written standardized items.
articles.contribution: Runs a real-world field study across 91 classes, dozens of colleges and ~1700 students in multiple disciplines, giving ecological validity to the item-quality claim.

articles.title: Adaptive Prediction-Powered AutoEval with Reliability and Efficiency Guarantees
articles.tldr: R-AutoEval+ gives finite-sample reliable model evaluation from biased LLM-judge synthetic data via adaptive prediction-powered inference.
articles.contribution: Provides finite-sample reliability guarantees on model-performance estimates while ensuring sample efficiency no worse than real-data-only evaluation.

articles.title: Adaptive Prediction-Powered AutoEval with Reliability and Efficiency Guarantees
articles.tldr: R-AutoEval+ gives finite-sample reliable model evaluation from biased LLM-judge synthetic data via adaptive prediction-powered inference.
articles.contribution: Adaptively tunes reliance on LLM-as-judge synthetic scores, reverting to conventional methods when the autoevaluator is insufficiently accurate, correcting judge bias without efficiency loss.

articles.title: Evaluating the Generalization Ability of Spatiotemporal Model in Urban Scenario
articles.tldr: ST-OOD benchmark shows spatiotemporal urban models degrade sharply out-of-distribution, often below a simple MLP.
articles.contribution: Introduces six-scenario next-year OOD splits exposing that same-year (in-distribution) evaluation overstates the real generalization of spatiotemporal urban models.

articles.title: Evaluating the Generalization Ability of Spatiotemporal Model in Urban Scenario
articles.tldr: ST-OOD benchmark shows spatiotemporal urban models degrade sharply out-of-distribution, often below a simple MLP.
articles.contribution: Shows leading models over-rely on parameters to overfit training data; a slight dropout rate substantially improves OOD generalization with minimal in-distribution cost.

articles.title: AgentHallu: Benchmarking Automated Hallucination Attribution of LLM-based Agents
articles.tldr: AgentHallu defines and benchmarks step-level hallucination attribution in multi-step LLM agents, which even top models fail at.
articles.contribution: Defines the new construct/task of automated hallucination attribution (which step diverges and why) with a 5-category, 14-sub-category taxonomy and multi-level human annotations.

articles.title: AgentHallu: Benchmarking Automated Hallucination Attribution of LLM-based Agents
articles.tldr: AgentHallu defines and benchmarks step-level hallucination attribution in multi-step LLM agents, which even top models fail at.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-based attributors are unreliable at this measurement: the best model reaches only 41.1% step-localization accuracy and 11.6% on tool-use hallucinations.

articles.title: Jurassic is (almost) All You Need: Few-Shot Meaning-to-Text Generation for Open-Domain Dialogue
articles.tldr: Few-shot meaning-to-text dialogue NLG that validates BLEURT against human judgment and finds it fails to capture coherence.
articles.contribution: Uses human evaluation to test whether BLEURT is a valid proxy, finding it tracks semantic accuracy but essentially not coherence, so BLEURT mis-measures the coherence construct.

articles.title: Jurassic is (almost) All You Need: Few-Shot Meaning-to-Text Generation for Open-Domain Dialogue
articles.tldr: Few-shot meaning-to-text dialogue NLG that validates BLEURT against human judgment and finds it fails to capture coherence.
articles.contribution: Shows measured generation quality does not transport across domains: 2-shot cross-domain prompting collapses semantic accuracy and inflates untrue hallucinations.

articles.title: Generating Biographies on Wikipedia: The Impact of Gender Bias on the Retrieval-Based Generation of Women Biographies
articles.tldr: Studies how gender-linked web-evidence scarcity confounds and caps retrieval-based generation of women's Wikipedia biographies.
articles.contribution: Isolates web-evidence availability (correlated with gender and region) as the confound driving lower generation quality, not model capability, via a dependency analysis on retrieval.

articles.title: Generating Biographies on Wikipedia: The Impact of Gender Bias on the Retrieval-Based Generation of Women Biographies
articles.tldr: Studies how gender-linked web-evidence scarcity confounds and caps retrieval-based generation of women's Wikipedia biographies.
articles.contribution: Curates a purpose-built evaluation set of 1,527 women biographies (incl. Science/Asia/Africa) to test whether generation quality generalizes to under-documented populations.

articles.title: α3-Bench: A Unified Benchmark of Safety, Robustness, and Efficiency for LLM-Based UAV Agents over 6G Networks
articles.tldr: Alpha^3-Bench unifies safety, robustness and efficiency measurement for LLM UAV agents under degraded 6G conditions via a composite metric.
articles.contribution: Adds degraded-6G stress conditions (latency, jitter, packet loss, throughput, edge load) so evaluation reflects real deployment, revealing Network Robustness drops of up to 30-40% that nominal-only benchmarks hide.

articles.title: α3-Bench: A Unified Benchmark of Safety, Robustness, and Efficiency for LLM-Based UAV Agents over 6G Networks
articles.tldr: Alpha^3-Bench unifies safety, robustness and efficiency measurement for LLM UAV agents under degraded 6G conditions via a composite metric.
articles.contribution: Defines a composite alpha^3 metric weighting six pillars (Task Outcome 0.30, Safety Policy 0.20, Tool Consistency 0.20, Interaction Quality 0.15, Network Robustness 0.10, Communication Cost) to capture holistic agent quality rather than task success alone.

articles.title: α3-Bench: A Unified Benchmark of Safety, Robustness, and Efficiency for LLM-Based UAV Agents over 6G Networks
articles.tldr: Alpha^3-Bench unifies safety, robustness and efficiency measurement for LLM UAV agents under degraded 6G conditions via a composite metric.
articles.contribution: Shows the agentic harness/network context confounds measured capability: efficiency-normalized performance varies by more than 2x across models under identical missions.

articles.title: AutoLabs: cognitive multi-agent systems with self-correction for autonomous chemical experimentation
articles.tldr: AutoLabs pairs a multi-agent chemistry-protocol system with a granular evaluation framework that exposes single-ground-truth and human-rater limits.
articles.contribution: Systematic ablation of 20 agent configurations disentangles how reasoning capacity, single- vs multi-agent design, tool use and self-checks each confound measured task success.

articles.title: AutoLabs: cognitive multi-agent systems with self-correction for autonomous chemical experimentation
articles.tldr: AutoLabs pairs a multi-agent chemistry-protocol system with a granular evaluation framework that exposes single-ground-truth and human-rater limits.
articles.contribution: Shows rigid reliance on a single ground-truth ordering under-measures agents when multiple valid procedures exist: correcting a valid alternative order raised average Spearman from 0.61 to 0.93.

articles.title: AutoLabs: cognitive multi-agent systems with self-correction for autonomous chemical experimentation
articles.tldr: AutoLabs pairs a multi-agent chemistry-protocol system with a granular evaluation framework that exposes single-ground-truth and human-rater limits.
articles.contribution: Finds human raters are imperfect scorers: even a domain expert overlooked procedural errors (stir rates, plate capping) and non-expert input degraded results below the fully automated system.

articles.title: PROPHET: An Inferable Future Forecasting Benchmark with Causal Intervened Likelihood Estimation
articles.tldr: PROPHET is a future-forecasting RAG benchmark filtered by Causal Intervened Likelihood (CIL) so questions are genuinely inferable from retrieved news, with explicit controls against answer leakage.
articles.contribution: CIL, a causal-inference statistic, filters out non-inferable questions so benchmark scores reflect evidence-based forecasting ability rather than guessing.

articles.title: PROPHET: An Inferable Future Forecasting Benchmark with Causal Intervened Likelihood Estimation
articles.tldr: PROPHET is a future-forecasting RAG benchmark filtered by Causal Intervened Likelihood (CIL) so questions are genuinely inferable from retrieved news, with explicit controls against answer leakage.
articles.contribution: Controls answer leakage by discarding post-resolution-date news and LLM-rated answer-revealing articles, and pledges periodic updates against model-evolution leakage.

articles.title: PROPHET: An Inferable Future Forecasting Benchmark with Causal Intervened Likelihood Estimation
articles.tldr: PROPHET is a future-forecasting RAG benchmark filtered by Causal Intervened Likelihood (CIL) so questions are genuinely inferable from retrieved news, with explicit controls against answer leakage.
articles.contribution: Validates CIL with one-sided t-tests: top-CIL articles improve Brier by >7.7 points on the inferable subset L1 (p=0.026) but negligibly on L2, evidencing the benchmark's inferability.

articles.title: NLPStatTest: A Toolkit for Comparing NLP System Performance
articles.tldr: NLPStatTest is a toolkit and three-stage procedure for comparing NLP systems that goes beyond p-values with assumption checks, effect-size estimation, and power analysis.
articles.contribution: Adds effect-size indices (Cohen's d, Hedges' g, Wilcoxon r, Hodges-Lehmann) beyond p-values to distinguish statistical from practical significance in NLP system comparison.

articles.title: NLPStatTest: A Toolkit for Comparing NLP System Performance
articles.tldr: NLPStatTest is a toolkit and three-stage procedure for comparing NLP systems that goes beyond p-values with assumption checks, effect-size estimation, and power analysis.
articles.contribution: Provides prospective and retrospective (Monte-Carlo/bootstrap) power analysis to size test corpora and bound Type II error, enabling sound and fair system-to-system ranking.

articles.title: Counterfactual Segmentation Reasoning: Diagnosing and Mitigating Pixel-Grounding Hallucination
articles.tldr: HalluSegBench is a counterfactual visual-reasoning benchmark and new metrics showing that label-only evaluation misses vision-driven pixel-grounding hallucinations in segmentation VLMs.
articles.contribution: Replaces easily-rejected label-only negatives with visually coherent counterfactual object edits, a more faithful operationalization that actually elicits grounding hallucinations.

articles.title: Counterfactual Segmentation Reasoning: Diagnosing and Mitigating Pixel-Grounding Hallucination
articles.tldr: HalluSegBench is a counterfactual visual-reasoning benchmark and new metrics showing that label-only evaluation misses vision-driven pixel-grounding hallucinations in segmentation VLMs.
articles.contribution: Introduces Confusion Mask Score (CMS/CCMS) and delta-IoU metrics that quantify and disentangle vision- vs language-driven hallucination severity, which plain IoU/Tversky collapse and hide.

articles.title: Counterfactual Segmentation Reasoning: Diagnosing and Mitigating Pixel-Grounding Hallucination
articles.tldr: HalluSegBench is a counterfactual visual-reasoning benchmark and new metrics showing that label-only evaluation misses vision-driven pixel-grounding hallucinations in segmentation VLMs.
articles.contribution: Controlled factual/counterfactual image pairs isolate whether masks are grounded in true visual evidence or driven by spurious semantic priors.

articles.title: KG-FPQ: Evaluating Factuality Hallucination in LLMs with Knowledge Graph-based False Premise Questions
articles.tldr: KG-FPQ is an automated, scalable pipeline that edits knowledge-graph triplets into false premises to build 178k false-premise questions at six confusability levels for evaluating factuality hallucination, with a validated automatic judge.
articles.contribution: Automated KG-based generation scales false-premise coverage to ~178k questions across three domains, overcoming the small, convenience-scale manual FPQ sets of prior work.

articles.title: KG-FPQ: Evaluating Factuality Hallucination in LLMs with Knowledge Graph-based False Premise Questions
articles.tldr: KG-FPQ is an automated, scalable pipeline that edits knowledge-graph triplets into false premises to build 178k false-premise questions at six confusability levels for evaluating factuality hallucination, with a validated automatic judge.
articles.contribution: Six editing methods (neighbor/non-neighbor, same/different concept or relation) calibrate FPQ confusability so item difficulty systematically probes factuality hallucination.

articles.title: KG-FPQ: Evaluating Factuality Hallucination in LLMs with Knowledge Graph-based False Premise Questions
articles.tldr: KG-FPQ is an automated, scalable pipeline that edits knowledge-graph triplets into false premises to build 178k false-premise questions at six confusability levels for evaluating factuality hallucination, with a validated automatic judge.
articles.contribution: FPQ-Judge, a LoRA-tuned Llama3 classifier, scores open-ended generative answers, reaching 93% agreement with human labels to make generative hallucination evaluation reliable and cheap.

articles.title: Diversifying Question Generation over Knowledge Base via External Natural Questions
articles.tldr: Rethinks diversity evaluation for question generation, showing Distinct-n measures duplication and proposing Diverse@k, a semantics-aware metric validated against human ratings.
articles.contribution: Re-defines diversity as same-semantics-different-surface-form and operationalizes it as pairwise token-set difference over top-k relevant generations, rather than raw n-gram uniqueness.

articles.title: Diversifying Question Generation over Knowledge Base via External Natural Questions
articles.tldr: Rethinks diversity evaluation for question generation, showing Distinct-n measures duplication and proposing Diverse@k, a semantics-aware metric validated against human ratings.
articles.contribution: Shows Distinct-n = |unique n-grams|/|total n-grams| is a surface proxy that measures duplication, not diversity, and gates Diverse@k with a SimCSE relevance threshold to avoid rewarding irrelevant outputs.

articles.title: T2A-Feedback: Improving Basic Capabilities of Text-to-Audio Generation via Fine-grained AI Feedback
articles.tldr: Builds and validates fine-grained AI audio scoring pipelines (event occurrence/sequence/acoustic quality) that correlate with human preference far better than CLAP/FAD, exposing those metrics as poor proxies.
articles.contribution: Shows sentence-level CLAP and FAD misrepresent fine-grained event occurrence/order and proposes event-level EOS/ESS plus a trained acoustic predictor as scorers that better track human judgments.

articles.title: SciML Agents: Write the Solver, Not the Solution
articles.tldr: Introduces benchmarks that measure the scientific/numerical validity (not just executability) of LLM-generated ODE-solver code, with adversarial 'misleading' problems probing genuine reasoning vs shortcut pattern matching.
articles.contribution: Argues syntactic correctness / passing execution is a surface proxy for scientific code and instead scores numerical validity via relative L2 error against SymPy analytical solutions.

articles.title: SciML Agents: Write the Solver, Not the Solution
articles.tldr: Introduces benchmarks that measure the scientific/numerical validity (not just executability) of LLM-generated ODE-solver code, with adversarial 'misleading' problems probing genuine reasoning vs shortcut pattern matching.
articles.contribution: Constructs adversarial ODEs that superficially look stiff but algebraically reduce to non-stiff forms, exposing shortcut cue (large coefficient) pattern matching rather than genuine symbolic reasoning.

articles.title: Turning the Tide: Repository-based Code Reflection
articles.tldr: Dynamic, decontaminated repository-level code-reflection benchmark built specifically to avoid the train/test contamination and saturation that undermine static benchmarks like Aider-polyglot.
articles.contribution: Uses an automatic dynamic-generation pipeline plus MinHash/LSH decontamination (removing Jaccard>0.8 overlaps then exact-match) so training cases cannot leak into the 1,888 test cases.

articles.title: Turning the Tide: Repository-based Code Reflection
articles.tldr: Dynamic, decontaminated repository-level code-reflection benchmark built specifically to avoid the train/test contamination and saturation that undermine static benchmarks like Aider-polyglot.
articles.contribution: Argues static benchmarks saturate and get memorized over time, and uses never-before-seen repositories through May 2025 to provide a less-biased moving-target evaluation.

articles.title: Do-GOOD: Towards Distribution Shift Evaluation for Pre-Trained Visual Document Understanding Models
articles.tldr: Fine-grained OOD benchmark (Do-GOOD) for visual document understanding that decomposes distribution shifts into image/text/layout and exposes the brittleness of pre-trained VDU models and OOD algorithms.
articles.contribution: Constructs 9 OOD datasets across 3 VDU tasks and shows a large, consistent ID-to-OOD performance gap, revealing that i.i.d.-designed document benchmarks overstate real robustness.

articles.title: Do-GOOD: Towards Distribution Shift Evaluation for Pre-Trained Visual Document Understanding Models
articles.tldr: Fine-grained OOD benchmark (Do-GOOD) for visual document understanding that decomposes distribution shifts into image/text/layout and exposes the brittleness of pre-trained VDU models and OOD algorithms.
articles.contribution: Isolates image/text/layout modalities to show models lean on shortcut modalities (e.g., LayoutLMv3 barely uses image on NER), attributing scores to spurious cues rather than true document understanding.

articles.title: LAION-C: An Out-of-Distribution Benchmark for Web-Scale Vision Models
articles.tldr: Introduces LAION-C, an OOD vision benchmark motivated by evidence that ImageNet-C corruptions are already in web-scale training data and thus no longer measure OOD robustness.
articles.contribution: Shows ImageNet-C is saturated and effectively contaminated for web-scale models, since its corruptions appear in LAION training data, so high ImageNet-C scores no longer indicate OOD robustness.

articles.title: LAION-C: An Out-of-Distribution Benchmark for Web-Scale Vision Models
articles.tldr: Introduces LAION-C, an OOD vision benchmark motivated by evidence that ImageNet-C corruptions are already in web-scale training data and thus no longer measure OOD robustness.
articles.contribution: Provides six genuinely-OOD synthetic distortions plus a controlled 11,400-trial human psychophysics baseline to validly measure OOD robustness and human-machine error consistency.

articles.title: Wild-Tab: A Benchmark For Out-Of-Distribution Generalization In Tabular Regression
articles.tldr: Benchmark for OOD generalization in tabular regression that reveals large ID-to-OOD gaps and shows no method beats ERM under fair tuning, with in-distribution validation insufficient for OOD model selection.
articles.contribution: Curates 3 real-world tabular OOD datasets (weather, vessel power) and shows a significant generalization gap, with OOD performance markedly below in-distribution performance.

articles.title: Wild-Tab: A Benchmark For Out-Of-Distribution Generalization In Tabular Regression
articles.tldr: Benchmark for OOD generalization in tabular regression that reveals large ID-to-OOD gaps and shows no method beats ERM under fair tuning, with in-distribution validation insufficient for OOD model selection.
articles.contribution: Finds that under equal tuning/compute no OOD method significantly outperforms ERM, and that ID validation performance is not a valid criterion for selecting models that generalize OOD.

articles.title: Beyond Facts: Evaluating Intent Hallucination in Large Language Models

articles.contribution: Defines 'intent hallucination' (omission/misinterpretation of query constraints) as a construct distinct from factual hallucination.

articles.title: Beyond Facts: Evaluating Intent Hallucination in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces the 'intent hallucination' construct plus FAITHQA benchmark and Constraint Score metric, showing zero-shot LLM-as-judge baselines are biased vs humans.
articles.contribution: Shows plain zero-shot LLM-as-judge scoring is biased while constraint-decomposition Constraint Score aligns far better with humans.

articles.title: OnionEval: An Unified Evaluation of Fact-conflicting Hallucination for Small-Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Layered-context benchmark plus Context-Influence (CI) metric revealing small LLMs detect atomic-fact hallucination but collapse once facts are wrapped in context.

articles.title: OnionEval: An Unified Evaluation of Fact-conflicting Hallucination for Small-Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Layered-context benchmark plus Context-Influence (CI) metric revealing small LLMs detect atomic-fact hallucination but collapse once facts are wrapped in context.

articles.title: HalluHard: A Hard Multi-Turn Hallucination Benchmark

articles.title: HalluHard: A Hard Multi-Turn Hallucination Benchmark
articles.tldr: A hard multi-turn hallucination benchmark with a full-text citation-verifying LLM judge; frontier models still hallucinate ~30% even with web search.

articles.title: HalluHard: A Hard Multi-Turn Hallucination Benchmark

articles.title: CodeInsight: A Curated Dataset of Practical Coding Solutions from Stack Overflow
articles.tldr: A curated 3,409-example Stack Overflow code dataset with unit tests, explicitly designed to reduce data contamination and enable robust pass@1 evaluation.

articles.title: GRADEO: Towards Human-Like Evaluation for Text-to-Video Generation via Multi-Step Reasoning

articles.title: GRADEO: Towards Human-Like Evaluation for Text-to-Video Generation via Multi-Step Reasoning

articles.title: Measuring LLM Novelty As The Frontier Of Original And High-Quality Output

articles.title: ImagenWorld: Stress-Testing Image Generation Models with Explainable Human Evaluation on Open-ended Real-World Tasks

articles.title: Benchmarking Vision, Language, & Action Models in Procedurally Generated, Open Ended Action Environments
