articles.contribution: Demonstrates PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FID fail to separate valid vs invalid synthesized views, mis-representing view quality

articles.title: Appreciate the View: A Task-Aware Evaluation Framework for Novel View Synthesis
articles.tldr: Shows standard novel-view-synthesis metrics mis-rank outputs and proposes task-aware feature metrics aligned with human judgment
articles.contribution: Proposes PRISM feature distances (full-reference and no-reference) that align with human preference and give stable rankings

articles.title: Self-Rationalization in the Wild: A Large Scale Out-of-Distribution Evaluation on NLI-related tasks
articles.tldr: Large-scale OOD study of self-rationalization that also validates reference-free explanation-quality metrics against human judgment
articles.contribution: Assesses external/OOD validity of self-rationalization label prediction across 19 datasets in NLI, fact-checking and hallucination detection

articles.title: Self-Rationalization in the Wild: A Large Scale Out-of-Distribution Evaluation on NLI-related tasks
articles.tldr: Large-scale OOD study of self-rationalization that also validates reference-free explanation-quality metrics against human judgment
articles.contribution: Runs a human study to test which reference-free automatic metric most reliably scores free-text explanation quality

articles.title: A Content-Based Novelty Measure for Scholarly Publications: A Proof of Concept
articles.tldr: Operationalizes scholarly novelty as information-theoretic surprisal and gathers face and construct validity evidence
articles.contribution: Defines scholarly novelty as surprisal relative to a language-model-approximated discourse distribution before building the measure

articles.title: A Content-Based Novelty Measure for Scholarly Publications: A Proof of Concept
articles.tldr: Operationalizes scholarly novelty as information-theoretic surprisal and gathers face and construct validity evidence
articles.contribution: Provides face-validity and known-groups construct-validity evidence that the surprisal measure captures novelty

articles.title: Enhancing LLM-Based Data Annotation with Error Decomposition
articles.tldr: Proposes an error-decomposition paradigm that separates task-inherent ambiguity from model-specific error in LLM annotation, critiquing alignment-only metrics
articles.contribution: Decomposes LLM annotation error into task-inherent ambiguity vs model-specific inaccuracy to diagnose annotation reliability

articles.title: Enhancing LLM-Based Data Annotation with Error Decomposition
articles.tldr: Proposes an error-decomposition paradigm that separates task-inherent ambiguity from model-specific error in LLM annotation, critiquing alignment-only metrics
articles.contribution: Shows single alignment metrics (kappa/accuracy) collapse distinct error types and can reward overfitting to label noise

articles.title: Do LLMs Game Formalization? Evaluating Faithfulness in Logical Reasoning
articles.tldr: High Lean-4 compilation and accuracy do not imply faithful formalization; a two-stage NL->intermediate->Lean pipeline relocates rather than removes unfaithful axiom fabrication and premise mistranslation.
articles.contribution: Shows a proof that passes the Lean-4 verifier can rest on a gamed/unfaithful formalization, so compilation success is a gameable proxy for correct logical reasoning.

articles.title: Do LLMs Game Formalization? Evaluating Faithfulness in Logical Reasoning
articles.tldr: High Lean-4 compilation and accuracy do not imply faithful formalization; a two-stage NL->intermediate->Lean pipeline relocates rather than removes unfaithful axiom fabrication and premise mistranslation.
articles.contribution: Documents that an LLM-as-judge (Claude Opus) misses subtle premise mistranslation, producing false negatives when auditing formalization faithfulness.

articles.title: Using LLMs to identify features of personal and professional skills in an open-response situational judgment test
articles.tldr: LLMs can extract construct-relevant features from open-response situational-judgment tests, but zero-shot LLM-human agreement falls well short of human inter-rater reliability except for lexically cued features.
articles.contribution: Grounds automated SJT scoring in nine construct-relevant features so the measure targets professional-skill constructs rather than surface proxies like fluency or grammar.

articles.title: Using LLMs to identify features of personal and professional skills in an open-response situational judgment test
articles.tldr: LLMs can extract construct-relevant features from open-response situational-judgment tests, but zero-shot LLM-human agreement falls well short of human inter-rater reliability except for lexically cued features.
articles.contribution: Quantifies LLM-versus-human agreement (Cohen's kappa) across 5 models and 7 features, exposing sub-human agreement and rater-threshold misalignment in automated scoring.

articles.title: Psychometric Personality Shaping Modulates Capabilities and Safety in Language Models
articles.tldr: Big-Five personality prompting acts as a latent confounder that shifts safety and capability benchmark scores, providing an axis orthogonal to model scale for stress-testing eval validity and safetywashing.
articles.contribution: Reveals personality induced via the system prompt as a confounder that moves WMDP, TruthfulQA, ETHICS and Sycophancy scores partly independently of underlying capability.

articles.title: Psychometric Personality Shaping Modulates Capabilities and Safety in Language Models
articles.tldr: Big-Five personality prompting acts as a latent confounder that shifts safety and capability benchmark scores, providing an axis orthogonal to model scale for stress-testing eval validity and safetywashing.
articles.contribution: Uses persona perturbations that hold capability roughly fixed while shifting safety scores as an orthogonal stress test exposing safety metrics that merely proxy competence (safetywashing).

articles.title: Reliable Decision Support with LLMs: A Framework for Evaluating Consistency in Binary Text Classification Applications
articles.tldr: A psychometric framework for LLM binary text classification measuring intra- and inter-rater reliability; demonstrates that high annotation consistency need not imply predictive (criterion) validity against an external ground truth.
articles.contribution: Adapts Cohen, Fleiss, Gwet's AC and Krippendorff coefficients to quantify LLM intra-rater and inter-rater annotation reliability across 14 models.

articles.title: Reliable Decision Support with LLMs: A Framework for Evaluating Consistency in Binary Text Classification Applications
articles.tldr: A psychometric framework for LLM binary text classification measuring intra- and inter-rater reliability; demonstrates that high annotation consistency need not imply predictive (criterion) validity against an external ground truth.
articles.contribution: Provides psychometric sample-size guidance (Gwet tables, Sidak correction) plus NA-penalized/dropped handling so reliability estimates are statistically sound and replicable.

articles.title: Reliable Decision Support with LLMs: A Framework for Evaluating Consistency in Binary Text Classification Applications
articles.tldr: A psychometric framework for LLM binary text classification measuring intra- and inter-rater reliability; demonstrates that high annotation consistency need not imply predictive (criterion) validity against an external ground truth.
articles.contribution: Shows reliability is not validity: highly consistent sentiment labels replicate a benchmark yet predict real market moves only at chance, exposing a criterion-validity gap.

articles.title: Text2GQL-Bench: A Text to Graph Query Language Benchmark [Experiment, Analysis & Benchmark]
articles.tldr: A multi-GQL, multi-domain Text-to-GQL benchmark with a four-part evaluation suite (grammar validity, similarity, semantic alignment, execution accuracy) that exposes bottlenecks a single end-to-end metric hides.
articles.contribution: Broadens coverage to 34 databases across 13 domains and multiple GQL dialects, countering the narrow single-GQL/single-domain sampling of prior Text-to-GQL datasets.

articles.title: Text2GQL-Bench: A Text to Graph Query Language Benchmark [Experiment, Analysis & Benchmark]
articles.tldr: A multi-GQL, multi-domain Text-to-GQL benchmark with a four-part evaluation suite (grammar validity, similarity, semantic alignment, execution accuracy) that exposes bottlenecks a single end-to-end metric hides.
articles.contribution: Decomposes evaluation into grammar validity, similarity, GLEU and execution accuracy, showing that execution accuracy alone misrepresents true Text-to-GQL ability and its failure modes.

articles.title: Text2GQL-Bench: A Text to Graph Query Language Benchmark [Experiment, Analysis & Benchmark]
articles.tldr: A multi-GQL, multi-domain Text-to-GQL benchmark with a four-part evaluation suite (grammar validity, similarity, semantic alignment, execution accuracy) that exposes bottlenecks a single end-to-end metric hides.
articles.contribution: Cross-schema and cross-GQL splits diagnose that syntactic dialect gaps, not underlying query logic, are the main confounder bottlenecking generalization across graph query languages.

articles.title: MedObvious: Exposing the Medical Moravec's Paradox in VLMs via Clinical Triage
articles.tldr: MedObvious isolates pre-diagnostic visual sanity-checking in medical VLMs, revealing that fluent diagnostic text masks unreliable input validation, false-alarm bias, degradation under grid scaling, and strong answer-format sensitivity.
articles.contribution: Isolates the input-validation/perceptual-sanity construct that standard medical VQA benchmarks omit, showing fluent diagnostic narratives can mask invalid low-level perception.

articles.title: MedObvious: Exposing the Medical Moravec's Paradox in VLMs via Clinical Triage
articles.tldr: MedObvious isolates pre-diagnostic visual sanity-checking in medical VLMs, revealing that fluent diagnostic text masks unreliable input validation, false-alarm bias, degradation under grid scaling, and strong answer-format sensitivity.
articles.contribution: Uses five answer formats to show MCQ framing overestimates grounded ability relative to open-ended framing, exposing format-dependent measurement of the same underlying skill.

articles.title: One prompt is not enough: Instruction Sensitivity Undermines Embedding Model Evaluation
articles.tldr: Single-prompt evaluation of instruction-tuned embedding models is invalid: prompt phrasing swings scores substantially, and adversarial prompt selection ('prompt hacking') can push any model to leaderboard rank 1.
articles.contribution: Quantifies instruction/prompt sensitivity of embedding models (high coefficient of variation across prompts), showing a single default prompt misrepresents the underlying score distribution.

articles.title: One prompt is not enough: Instruction Sensitivity Undermines Embedding Model Evaluation
articles.tldr: Single-prompt evaluation of instruction-tuned embedding models is invalid: prompt phrasing swings scores substantially, and adversarial prompt selection ('prompt hacking') can push any model to leaderboard rank 1.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates 'prompt hacking': adversarial per-model prompt choice can promote any of six models to rank 1, breaking the validity of single-prompt leaderboard comparisons.

articles.title: Regularized Bayesian calibration and scoring of the WD-FAB IRT model improves predictive performance over marginal maximum likelihood
articles.tldr: Bayesian cross-validation study showing regularized full-Bayesian IRT calibration plus compact-support EAP scoring is more predictive and reliable than marginal-maximum-likelihood/WLE for the WD-FAB graded response model.
articles.contribution: Shows regularized Bayesian calibration plus compactly-supported EAP scoring yields more reliable, self-consistent IRT ability estimates than MML/WLE, and that Warm's WLE bias correction does more harm than good.

articles.title: Regularized Bayesian calibration and scoring of the WD-FAB IRT model improves predictive performance over marginal maximum likelihood
articles.tldr: Bayesian cross-validation study showing regularized full-Bayesian IRT calibration plus compact-support EAP scoring is more predictive and reliable than marginal-maximum-likelihood/WLE for the WD-FAB graded response model.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that Bayesian-calibrated IRT models transfer better to an out-of-subpopulation control sample than MML, and that compact-support scoring guards against facetious tail extrapolation beyond the calibration range.

articles.title: A latent variable model with change-points and its application to time pressure effects in educational assessment
articles.tldr: Extends 2-PL IRT with person-specific latent change-points to detect and account for time-pressure/speededness that contaminates the ability signal and biases score interpretation in educational tests.
articles.contribution: Models within-person response-behavior change-points (rapid guessing under time pressure) as construct-irrelevant variance so that post-change responses no longer corrupt the latent-ability estimate.

articles.title: A latent variable model with change-points and its application to time pressure effects in educational assessment
articles.tldr: Extends 2-PL IRT with person-specific latent change-points to detect and account for time-pressure/speededness that contaminates the ability signal and biases score interpretation in educational tests.
articles.contribution: Provides an empirical-Bayes/MML estimator that simultaneously infers item parameters, abilities and per-respondent change-point locations, reducing bias in ability estimates from speededness confounds.

articles.title: EP-Diffuser: An Efficient Diffusion Model for Traffic Scene Generation and Prediction via Polynomial Representations
articles.tldr: Traffic-scene prediction paper that argues standard regression metrics (ADE/FDE) misrepresent generative prediction quality and that same-dataset splits confound generalization via memorization, motivating coverage metrics and OOD testing.
articles.contribution: Argues regression metrics (ADE/FDE) fail to measure diversity/coverage and plausibility of predicted scenes, and introduces coverage/plausibility metrics to better capture the true generative-prediction construct.

articles.title: EP-Diffuser: An Efficient Diffusion Model for Traffic Scene Generation and Prediction via Polynomial Representations
articles.tldr: Traffic-scene prediction paper that argues standard regression metrics (ADE/FDE) misrepresent generative prediction quality and that same-dataset splits confound generalization via memorization, motivating coverage metrics and OOD testing.
articles.contribution: Shows that same-dataset train/test splits share biases (road layouts, flow patterns) that let memorizing generative models look good, so proper generalization requires an out-of-distribution test set.

articles.title: T2MBench: A Benchmark for Out-of-Distribution Text-to-Motion Generation
articles.tldr: OOD text-to-motion benchmark arguing existing in-distribution metrics (R-Precision/FID) under-represent physical feasibility and that LLM/VLM judges suffer a 3D-to-2D representation gap, with a 1,025-prompt OOD set and multi-dimensional evaluation.
articles.contribution: Builds a 1,025-prompt out-of-distribution benchmark (Dynamics/Complexity/Interaction/Accuracy) to expose that T2M models evaluated only on in-distribution prompts overstate generalization.

articles.title: T2MBench: A Benchmark for Out-of-Distribution Text-to-Motion Generation
articles.tldr: OOD text-to-motion benchmark arguing existing in-distribution metrics (R-Precision/FID) under-represent physical feasibility and that LLM/VLM judges suffer a 3D-to-2D representation gap, with a 1,025-prompt OOD set and multi-dimensional evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows R-Precision/FID are biased toward statistical distributional matching and under-represent physical feasibility, so it adds multi-factor physical-quality and fine-grained accuracy evaluation.

articles.title: T2MBench: A Benchmark for Out-of-Distribution Text-to-Motion Generation
articles.tldr: OOD text-to-motion benchmark arguing existing in-distribution metrics (R-Precision/FID) under-represent physical feasibility and that LLM/VLM judges suffer a 3D-to-2D representation gap, with a 1,025-prompt OOD set and multi-dimensional evaluation.
articles.contribution: Identifies that LLM/VLM-as-judge pipelines render 3D kinematics into 2D frames, creating a representation gap (and text-caption information loss) that degrades reliability of motion scoring.

articles.title: Rethinking Reward Signals in Video GRPO: When Scores Become Targets
articles.tldr: Diagnoses that video-GRPO reward models lose fidelity as proxies for true quality under sustained optimization (Goodhart), causing shortcut ascent and reward saturation, and proposes target-robust reward signaling to mitigate.
articles.contribution: Shows that under GRPO the reward stops being a valid proxy for true video quality (Goodhart), enabling directional/shortcut ascent that boosts one component (e.g. motion) while degrading visual fidelity and text alignment.

articles.title: Rethinking Reward Signals in Video GRPO: When Scores Become Targets
articles.tldr: Diagnoses that video-GRPO reward models lose fidelity as proxies for true quality under sustained optimization (Goodhart), causing shortcut ascent and reward saturation, and proposes target-robust reward signaling to mitigate.
articles.contribution: Identifies a discriminability failure where reward scores compress/saturate along the training trajectory, collapsing within-group separation so group-relative advantages become low signal-to-noise.

articles.title: Beyond Single-Reward: Multi-Pair, Multi-Perspective Preference Optimization for Machine Translation
articles.tldr: Machine-translation preference-optimization paper whose core analysis shows Quality-Estimation reward metrics are blind to partial hallucinations, assigning high scores to fluent-but-inaccurate translations.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that QE reward models capture fluency/adequacy but overlook factuality, mis-representing translation quality by scoring fluent partial hallucinations highly.

articles.title: Beyond Single-Reward: Multi-Pair, Multi-Perspective Preference Optimization for Machine Translation
articles.tldr: Machine-translation preference-optimization paper whose core analysis shows Quality-Estimation reward metrics are blind to partial hallucinations, assigning high scores to fluent-but-inaccurate translations.
articles.contribution: Quantifies the QE-metric blind spot via correlation with human labels on the HalOmi benchmark, showing correlation rises sharply once partial-error examples are removed.

articles.title: Towards Unification of Hallucination Detection and Fact Verification for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: UniFact is a unified, dynamic evaluation framework enabling fair instance-level head-to-head comparison of Hallucination Detection vs Fact Verification by generating outputs and reference-based factuality labels in real time.
articles.contribution: Removes the benchmark-incompatibility confound (distinct datasets/assumptions/protocols) that previously made HD vs FV incomparable, enabling a fair instance-level head-to-head comparison on the same generated content.

articles.title: Towards Unification of Hallucination Detection and Fact Verification for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: UniFact is a unified, dynamic evaluation framework enabling fair instance-level head-to-head comparison of Hallucination Detection vs Fact Verification by generating outputs and reference-based factuality labels in real time.
articles.contribution: Uses dynamic real-time output generation plus reference-based labeling instead of static benchmarks, so evaluation can extend to new/out-of-distribution models and capture dynamic generative signals HD methods need.

articles.title: NotSoTiny: A Large, Living Benchmark for RTL Code Generation
articles.tldr: Large 'living' RTL code-generation benchmark showing syntax/testbench checks overestimate functional correctness and mitigating train/test contamination via periodic Tiny Tapeout updates and formal equivalence checking.
articles.contribution: Applies Min-K% membership analysis across 11 LLMs to quantify train/test contamination, showing NotSoTiny is substantially less memorized than the older RTLLM benchmark.

articles.title: NotSoTiny: A Large, Living Benchmark for RTL Code Generation
articles.tldr: Large 'living' RTL code-generation benchmark showing syntax/testbench checks overestimate functional correctness and mitigating train/test contamination via periodic Tiny Tapeout updates and formal equivalence checking.
articles.contribution: Designs a periodically refreshed 'living' benchmark sourced from newly fabricated Tiny Tapeout shuttles to keep evaluation ahead of training-corpus cutoffs and resist saturation over time.

articles.title: NotSoTiny: A Large, Living Benchmark for RTL Code Generation
articles.tldr: Large 'living' RTL code-generation benchmark showing syntax/testbench checks overestimate functional correctness and mitigating train/test contamination via periodic Tiny Tapeout updates and formal equivalence checking.
articles.contribution: Shows syntax checks and low-coverage Tiny Tapeout testbenches overestimate functional correctness, and adopts Yosys formal equivalence checking as a valid measure of RTL functional correctness.

articles.title: Color Bind: Exploring Color Perception in Text-to-Image Models
articles.tldr: Shows coarse CLIP-similarity and VQAScore metrics fail to capture multi-color object binding in text-to-image models and introduces a perceptually-grounded CIELAB benchmark (CompColor) validated against human perception.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates CLIP-similarity and VQAScore can score color-misaligned images higher than aligned ones, and replaces them with perceptually-uniform CIELAB (Delta-E) distance as a construct-valid color-fidelity measure.

articles.title: Color Bind: Exploring Color Perception in Text-to-Image Models
articles.tldr: Shows coarse CLIP-similarity and VQAScore metrics fail to capture multi-color object binding in text-to-image models and introduces a perceptually-grounded CIELAB benchmark (CompColor) validated against human perception.
articles.contribution: Validates the CIELAB accuracy threshold against a human color-perception user study (best AUC/G-mean) and adds a color-leakage metric to isolate cross-object color-swap as the dominant failure mode.

articles.title: CaTS-Bench: Can Language Models Describe Time Series?
articles.tldr: Time-series-captioning benchmark that validates the quality and reliability of its semi-synthetic (LLM-generated) ground-truth captions and shows its evaluation is robust to paraphrasing.
articles.contribution: Validates semi-synthetic (oracle-LLM) reference captions through manual multi-tier accuracy verification of thousands of captions and explicitly flags single-oracle bias as a ground-truth risk.

articles.title: CaTS-Bench: Can Language Models Describe Time Series?
articles.tldr: Time-series-captioning benchmark that validates the quality and reliability of its semi-synthetic (LLM-generated) ground-truth captions and shows its evaluation is robust to paraphrasing.
articles.contribution: Shows the evaluation framework preserves model rankings under LLM-paraphrased references (high mean Spearman rank correlation), evidence that it measures semantic content rather than surface wording.

articles.title: Open-Domain Text Evaluation via Contrastive Distribution Methods
articles.tldr: Proposes reference-free Contrastive Distribution Methods for open-domain text evaluation, validated by higher correlation with human judgment than BLEU/BERTScore/G-Eval and a purpose-built metric meta-evaluation set.
articles.contribution: Introduces a contrastive expert-vs-amateur log-probability metric and shows it correlates with human judgments of dialogue coherence/overall quality better than existing automatic and LLM-based metrics.

articles.title: Open-Domain Text Evaluation via Contrastive Distribution Methods
articles.tldr: Proposes reference-free Contrastive Distribution Methods for open-domain text evaluation, validated by higher correlation with human judgment than BLEU/BERTScore/G-Eval and a purpose-built metric meta-evaluation set.
articles.contribution: Frames automatic metrics as approximations of an oracle quality function and argues reference-based n-gram metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) misrepresent quality for high-diversity open-ended generation.

articles.title: Trade-R1: Bridging Verifiable Rewards to Stochastic Environments via Process-Level Reasoning Verification
articles.tldr: Identifies noisy market return as an invalid reward proxy causing reward hacking in financial RL and adds a triangular reasoning-consistency validity filter so only grounded reasoning is rewarded.
articles.contribution: Shows outcome-only market-return rewards induce Goodhart-style reward hacking, and gates them with a triangular Factuality/Deduction/Consistency judge score so returns count only when reasoning is grounded.

articles.title: Trade-R1: Bridging Verifiable Rewards to Stochastic Environments via Process-Level Reasoning Verification
articles.tldr: Identifies noisy market return as an invalid reward proxy causing reward hacking in financial RL and adds a triangular reasoning-consistency validity filter so only grounded reasoning is rewarded.
articles.contribution: Decomposes reward into signal plus market noise and shows a directional reward mechanism suppresses gradient variance on low-consistency samples, preventing exploitation of spurious momentum over causal reasoning.

articles.title: PIPE-RDF: An LLM-Assisted Pipeline for Enterprise RDF Benchmarking
articles.tldr: Pipeline for building category-balanced, schema-grounded NL-to-SPARQL benchmarks with execution validation and semantic audits to avoid factoid-skewed, unfaithful enterprise evaluations.
articles.contribution: Balances nine query categories to prevent factoid-skewed evaluation bias and grounds items in a fixed enterprise ontology so the benchmark represents realistic query distributions.

articles.title: PIPE-RDF: An LLM-Assisted Pipeline for Enterprise RDF Benchmarking
articles.tldr: Pipeline for building category-balanced, schema-grounded NL-to-SPARQL benchmarks with execution validation and semantic audits to avoid factoid-skewed, unfaithful enterprise evaluations.
articles.contribution: Uses reverse querying to ground templates in real graph bindings plus execution-based validation/repair and a manual semantic-alignment audit to ensure NL and SPARQL faithfully match.

articles.title: LaoBench: A Large-Scale Multidimensional Lao Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Contamination-resistant large-scale Lao LLM benchmark with a held-out black-box evaluation service, expert annotation with inter-annotator agreement, and arena LLM-judge reliability checks.
articles.contribution: Provides a held-out black-box evaluation subset plus contamination/overlap checks to mitigate test-set leakage and leaderboard overfitting for a low-resource language benchmark.

articles.title: LaoBench: A Large-Scale Multidimensional Lao Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Contamination-resistant large-scale Lao LLM benchmark with a held-out black-box evaluation service, expert annotation with inter-annotator agreement, and arena LLM-judge reliability checks.
articles.contribution: Runs arena-style LLM-judge scoring with judge-agreement analysis, position-bias mitigation, tie handling, and a human sanity check to assess scorer reliability.

articles.title: LaoBench: A Large-Scale Multidimensional Lao Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Contamination-resistant large-scale Lao LLM benchmark with a held-out black-box evaluation service, expert annotation with inter-annotator agreement, and arena LLM-judge reliability checks.
articles.contribution: Constructs the benchmark via expert authoring with inter-annotator agreement, adjudication, and agent-assisted verification to control annotation quality.

articles.title: Towards Anytime-Valid Statistical Watermarking
articles.tldr: Anytime-valid (e-value based) statistical watermarking framework that permits valid optional stopping in machine-text detection while maintaining Type-I error guarantees.
articles.contribution: Replaces fixed-horizon p-value testing with a test supermartingale of e-values so watermark detection supports valid early/optional stopping without inflating the Type-I error rate.

articles.title: Scalable Text-Embedding-informed Cognitive Diagnosis of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Adapts psychometric cognitive-diagnosis models (Q-matrix, mastery profiles) to benchmark-scale LLM evaluation, replacing coarse summary accuracy with fine-grained, interpretable skill diagnosis backed by consistency guarantees.
articles.contribution: Develops a scalable stochastic-approximation estimator that jointly recovers LLM mastery profiles and the item-attribute Q-matrix at benchmark scale (K>20, 1000+ items) with consistency guarantees and accurate parameter recovery.

articles.title: Scalable Text-Embedding-informed Cognitive Diagnosis of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Adapts psychometric cognitive-diagnosis models (Q-matrix, mastery profiles) to benchmark-scale LLM evaluation, replacing coarse summary accuracy with fine-grained, interpretable skill diagnosis backed by consistency guarantees.
articles.contribution: Argues coarse summary accuracy metrics obscure underlying reasoning abilities and models multidimensional discrete skill mastery for construct-valid, interpretable evaluation.

articles.title: Psychometric-Based Evaluation for Theorem Proving with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Applies item-response-theory psychometrics (difficulty, discrimination, adaptive testing) to LLM theorem proving, replacing Pass@N with more discriminative, contamination-aware ability estimation.
articles.contribution: Annotates miniF2F-Graded with IRT difficulty/discrimination and estimates prover ability adaptively, giving a more reliable and efficient measurement than raw Pass@N.

articles.title: Psychometric-Based Evaluation for Theorem Proving with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Applies item-response-theory psychometrics (difficulty, discrimination, adaptive testing) to LLM theorem proving, replacing Pass@N with more discriminative, contamination-aware ability estimation.
articles.contribution: Shows Pass@N aggregation fails to separate provers of different ability, whereas an IRT ability score yields a sounder ranking of models.

articles.title: Prompt Engineering for Scale Development in Generative Psychometrics
articles.tldr: Monte-Carlo study of how prompting strategy (adaptive vs zero/few-shot/persona) affects the structural validity and redundancy of LLM-generated psychometric scale items in the AI-GENIE pipeline.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that adaptive prompting drastically cuts redundant generated items and raises the structural (construct) validity of automatically generated scale items.

articles.title: Prompt Engineering for Scale Development in Generative Psychometrics
articles.tldr: Monte-Carlo study of how prompting strategy (adaptive vs zero/few-shot/persona) affects the structural validity and redundancy of LLM-generated psychometric scale items in the AI-GENIE pipeline.
articles.contribution: Uses network psychometrics (EGA/UVA/bootEGA, normalized mutual information) as a deterministic instrument to quantify the structural stability and reliability of generated item pools.

articles.title: Language Shapes Mental Health Evaluations in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Audits measurement invariance of LLM mental-health evaluations across English and Chinese, showing prompt language systematically shifts stigma scores and depression-severity judgments.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-produced stigma scores are not invariant to prompt language, so the same construct is measured inconsistently across English and Chinese.

articles.title: Language Shapes Mental Health Evaluations in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Audits measurement invariance of LLM mental-health evaluations across English and Chinese, showing prompt language systematically shifts stigma scores and depression-severity judgments.
articles.contribution: Isolates prompt language as a confounder that shifts downstream depression-severity classification, producing systematic under-estimation under Chinese prompts.

articles.title: Measuring Iterative Temporal Reasoning with Time Puzzles
articles.tldr: Introduces algorithmically-generated Time Puzzles to evaluate iterative tool-augmented temporal reasoning, disentangling genuine constraint reasoning from mere factual lookup.
articles.contribution: Pairs implicit-fact puzzles with explicit-date rewrites to isolate whether models fail at iterative reasoning versus at factual lookup, controlling that confound.

articles.title: Measuring Iterative Temporal Reasoning with Time Puzzles
articles.tldr: Introduces algorithmically-generated Time Puzzles to evaluate iterative tool-augmented temporal reasoning, disentangling genuine constraint reasoning from mere factual lookup.
articles.contribution: Shows benchmark scores are stable when regenerating a fresh puzzle set and under prompt variants, evidencing the measurement's reliability and continual-eval resistance to saturation.

articles.title: Unified Deployment-Aware Evaluation of Open Reasoning Language Models
articles.authors: Md. Motaleb Hossen Manik et al.
articles.tldr: Unified matched-size protocol for evaluating open reasoning LLMs that reframes evaluation as deployment-aware operating points and exposes prompt-sensitivity and interface-robustness confounds.
articles.contribution: Enforces a fully matched 84-condition protocol on an identical example subset so model rankings are not confounded by mixed sample sizes or inconsistent prompting.

articles.title: Unified Deployment-Aware Evaluation of Open Reasoning Language Models
articles.authors: Md. Motaleb Hossen Manik et al.
articles.tldr: Unified matched-size protocol for evaluating open reasoning LLMs that reframes evaluation as deployment-aware operating points and exposes prompt-sensitivity and interface-robustness confounds.
articles.contribution: Adds Wilson confidence intervals, bootstrap resampling and paired permutation tests, showing gaps among top configurations are statistically modest.

articles.title: Unified Deployment-Aware Evaluation of Open Reasoning Language Models
articles.authors: Md. Motaleb Hossen Manik et al.
articles.tldr: Unified matched-size protocol for evaluating open reasoning LLMs that reframes evaluation as deployment-aware operating points and exposes prompt-sensitivity and interface-robustness confounds.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses that a model's catastrophic dataset score is an interface/answer-extraction breakdown rather than a reasoning failure, separating harness artifacts from capability.

articles.title: Bias Testing and Mitigation in Black Box LLMs using Metamorphic Relations
articles.tldr: Uses six metamorphic relations to surface hidden social bias in black-box LLMs that direct prompts miss, then reuses them to fine-tune models for bias resilience.
articles.contribution: Shows semantics-preserving metamorphic transformations of prompts capture latent bias that direct BiasAsker questions under-measure, improving construct coverage of the bias measure.

articles.title: Bias Testing and Mitigation in Black Box LLMs using Metamorphic Relations
articles.tldr: Uses six metamorphic relations to surface hidden social bias in black-box LLMs that direct prompts miss, then reuses them to fine-tune models for bias resilience.

articles.title: From Reviewers' Lens: Understanding Bug Bounty Report Invalid Reasons with LLMs
articles.tldr: LLM reviewers of bug-bounty report validity show acceptance bias and rely on surface cues, while human ground-truth review decisions are reputation-biased.
articles.contribution: GPT-5/DeepSeek as validity reviewers show strong acceptance bias (GPT-5 invalid recall 0.28, ~72% FNR) and high overall accuracy masks per-class collapse, exposing unreliable LLM scoring of report validity.

articles.title: From Reviewers' Lens: Understanding Bug Bounty Report Invalid Reasons with LLMs
articles.tldr: LLM reviewers of bug-bounty report validity show acceptance bias and rely on surface cues, while human ground-truth review decisions are reputation-biased.
articles.contribution: Shows the ground-truth reviewer labels depend on non-content factors: high-reputation reporters get higher-ranked outcomes (FPR gap +0.16, val|inval +28pp), a rater/label bias confounding the target.

articles.title: Online Shift Detection and Conformal Adaptation for Deployed Safety Classifiers
articles.tldr: Online KS-based shift monitor plus weighted conformal adaptation for deployed safety classifiers, with a pre-registered factorial and falsification of monitor assumptions.
articles.contribution: Detects silent validity decay of deployed safety classifiers under distribution shift via a sliding-window KS statistic: 86.6% valid detection at mean latency 39.5 steps across 800 pre-registered cells.

articles.title: Online Shift Detection and Conformal Adaptation for Deployed Safety Classifiers
articles.tldr: Online KS-based shift monitor plus weighted conformal adaptation for deployed safety classifiers, with a pre-registered factorial and falsification of monitor assumptions.
articles.contribution: Exposes a conformal failure mode: density-ratio estimation collapses in 3584-4096-dim embeddings (weights clip to zero); projecting to <=32 dimensions restores post-shift coverage guarantees.

articles.title: Online Shift Detection and Conformal Adaptation for Deployed Safety Classifiers
articles.tldr: Online KS-based shift monitor plus weighted conformal adaptation for deployed safety classifiers, with a pre-registered factorial and falsification of monitor assumptions.
articles.contribution: Falsifies three assumptions about the canary: architectural diversity does not drive it (eta^2=0.011), it is GCG-specific not generic OOD (p<1e-12), and a confident canary resists adaptive suppression.

articles.title: Online Shift Detection and Conformal Adaptation for Deployed Safety Classifiers
articles.tldr: Online KS-based shift monitor plus weighted conformal adaptation for deployed safety classifiers, with a pre-registered factorial and falsification of monitor assumptions.
articles.contribution: Derives an exact security boundary where a monitor-aware adaptive attacker stalls at gap=1/(2*lambda) (a confidence-gated equilibrium), giving principled limits on evading the monitor.

articles.title: From Accuracy to Auditability: A Survey of Determinism in Financial AI Systems
articles.tldr: Survey plus first-party experiments on nondeterminism in financial AI: standard accuracy metrics miss run-to-run variance, and rankings/explanations fail to reproduce.
articles.contribution: Quantifies mechanical nondeterminism invisible to AUROC/F1: GNN labels flip for 22-30% of nodes across seeds and LLM outputs diverge for 14-18% of prompts across tensor-parallel sizes even under greedy decoding.

articles.title: From Accuracy to Auditability: A Survey of Determinism in Financial AI Systems
articles.tldr: Survey plus first-party experiments on nondeterminism in financial AI: standard accuracy metrics miss run-to-run variance, and rankings/explanations fail to reproduce.
articles.contribution: Shows benchmark rankings are non-reproducible: GNN model rankings flip across random data splits (3/10 splits change the winner on Elliptic Bitcoin), undermining sound model comparison.

articles.title: From Accuracy to Auditability: A Survey of Determinism in Financial AI Systems
articles.tldr: Survey plus first-party experiments on nondeterminism in financial AI: standard accuracy metrics miss run-to-run variance, and rankings/explanations fail to reproduce.
articles.contribution: Post-hoc explanations used for ECOA adverse-action notices are unstable (KernelSHAP J@3=0.71-0.76 across seeds) whereas exact TreeSHAP restores J@3=1.0, making denial reasons a nondeterministic artifact.

articles.title: Compositional Jailbreaking: An Empirical Analysis of Mutator Chain Interactions in Aligned LLMs
articles.authors: Reinelle Jan C. Bugnot et al.
articles.tldr: Systematic study of two-step jailbreak mutator chains introducing completeness/validity metrics that guard against selection bias and ASR inflation; synergy is rare and model-specific.
articles.contribution: Its 'validity' criterion requires a chain to beat BOTH constituents, revealing that apparent 'fictional' synergy is a baseline-choice artifact of a dominant single mutator rather than genuine composition.

articles.title: Compositional Jailbreaking: An Empirical Analysis of Mutator Chain Interactions in Aligned LLMs
articles.authors: Reinelle Jan C. Bugnot et al.
articles.tldr: Systematic study of two-step jailbreak mutator chains introducing completeness/validity metrics that guard against selection bias and ASR inflation; synergy is rare and model-specific.
articles.contribution: Identifies selection bias in conditional ASR: pairs with few complete cases give unstable ASR, so median-based completeness filtering removes sparsely-sampled degenerate mutator pairs.

articles.title: Compositional Jailbreaking: An Empirical Analysis of Mutator Chain Interactions in Aligned LLMs
articles.authors: Reinelle Jan C. Bugnot et al.
articles.tldr: Systematic study of two-step jailbreak mutator chains introducing completeness/validity metrics that guard against selection bias and ASR inflation; synergy is rare and model-specific.
articles.contribution: Requires attack success to be both unsafe AND intent-satisfied via an intent-fidelity classifier, preventing ASR inflation from outputs that are unsafe but irrelevant to the attacker's goal.

articles.title: Decomposed Prompting Does Not Fix Knowledge Gaps, But Helps Models Say "I Don't Know"
articles.tldr: Cross-regime disagreement between direct and decomposed prompting is a reliable error-detection signal, exposing LLMs' logical-invariance failures.
articles.contribution: Treats cross-prompt disagreement (Direct vs decomposed) as a training-free reliability signal / error detector for closed-book answers, outperforming self-reported confidence baselines.

articles.title: Decomposed Prompting Does Not Fix Knowledge Gaps, But Helps Models Say "I Don't Know"
articles.tldr: Cross-regime disagreement between direct and decomposed prompting is a reliable error-detection signal, exposing LLMs' logical-invariance failures.
articles.contribution: Documents that semantically-equivalent prompting regimes yield inconsistent answers (logical-invariance failure), so measured accuracy depends on the prompting harness, not just knowledge.

articles.title: Seeing Isn't Believing: Uncovering Blind Spots in Evaluator Vision-Language Models
articles.authors: Mohammed Safi Ur Rahman Khan et al.
articles.tldr: Systematic stress-test shows evaluator VLMs miss over 50% of quality-degrading perturbations, exposing the unreliability of LLM/VLM judges for benchmarking.
articles.contribution: Quantifies blind spots of Evaluator VLMs used as scorers across I2T and T2I tasks, showing they fail to reflect object hallucinations, spatial and compositional errors in their judgments.

articles.title: Seeing Isn't Believing: Uncovering Blind Spots in Evaluator Vision-Language Models
articles.authors: Mohammed Safi Ur Rahman Khan et al.

articles.title: Small Updates, Big Doubts: Does Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Enhance Hallucination Detection ?
articles.tldr: Empirical study showing PEFT reshapes how uncertainty is encoded, consistently improving black-box hallucination-detector AUROC while disrupting white-box probes.
articles.contribution: Shows an intervention (PEFT) that leaves accuracy nearly unchanged still substantially changes detector reliability, acting as an epistemic regularizer that shifts scores out of the overconfident regime.

articles.title: Small Updates, Big Doubts: Does Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Enhance Hallucination Detection ?
articles.tldr: Empirical study showing PEFT reshapes how uncertainty is encoded, consistently improving black-box hallucination-detector AUROC while disrupting white-box probes.
articles.contribution: Argues token-level entropy detectors capture lexical/syntactic diversity orthogonal to factual correctness (a surface proxy), explaining their inconsistent gains vs semantic detectors.

articles.title: INTRYGUE: Induction-Aware Entropy Gating for Reliable RAG Uncertainty Estimation
articles.tldr: Reveals entropy-based uncertainty estimation is confounded and unreliable in RAG due to an induction-head/entropy-neuron tug-of-war, then gates entropy to fix it.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that standard entropy-based uncertainty scores fail to separate hallucinated from grounded RAG outputs, making them unreliable hallucination signals in retrieval settings.

articles.title: INTRYGUE: Induction-Aware Entropy Gating for Reliable RAG Uncertainty Estimation
articles.tldr: Reveals entropy-based uncertainty estimation is confounded and unreliable in RAG due to an induction-head/entropy-neuron tug-of-war, then gates entropy to fix it.
articles.contribution: Identifies a mechanistic confound (induction heads triggering entropy neurons) that inflates predictive entropy on correct answers, breaking the link between entropy and true uncertainty.

articles.title: DSC2025 - ViHallu Challenge: Detecting Hallucination in Vietnamese LLMs
articles.tldr: First large-scale Vietnamese hallucination-detection benchmark (10k triplets) isolating contextual faithfulness with rigorous annotation and balanced, representative splits.
articles.contribution: Builds a stratified 10k-sample benchmark with balanced no/intrinsic/extrinsic labels and validated train/test distribution overlap so detectors cannot exploit majority-class priors.

articles.title: DSC2025 - ViHallu Challenge: Detecting Hallucination in Vietnamese LLMs
articles.tldr: First large-scale Vietnamese hallucination-detection benchmark (10k triplets) isolating contextual faithfulness with rigorous annotation and balanced, representative splits.
articles.contribution: Establishes a multi-stage annotation protocol (12 trained annotators, peer cross-checking, senior adjudication) to produce reliable ground-truth hallucination labels.

articles.title: DSC2025 - ViHallu Challenge: Detecting Hallucination in Vietnamese LLMs
articles.tldr: First large-scale Vietnamese hallucination-detection benchmark (10k triplets) isolating contextual faithfulness with rigorous annotation and balanced, representative splits.
articles.contribution: Defines hallucination as contextual faithfulness (intrinsic vs extrinsic) rather than world-knowledge factuality, so factually true but ungrounded content counts as extrinsic hallucination.

articles.contribution: Proposes a nearest-neighbor sentence-embedding classifier that separates abstentions from hallucinations (statement-but-not-fully-correct) without needing model internals or token probabilities.

articles.title: FATHOMS-RAG: A Framework for the Assessment of Thinking and Observation in Multimodal Systems that use Retrieval Augmented Generation

articles.tldr: Factorised study disentangling what actually drives probe-based uncertainty-estimation performance and transfer.

articles.title: From Signals to Transfer: A Factorised Study of Probe-Based Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Factorised study disentangling what actually drives probe-based uncertainty-estimation performance and transfer.

articles.title: From Signals to Transfer: A Factorised Study of Probe-Based Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Factorised study disentangling what actually drives probe-based uncertainty-estimation performance and transfer.
articles.contribution: Shows the ground-truth annotation choice (LLM-judge vs lexical ROUGE/AlignScore) strongly shapes probe evaluation; lexical labels misrepresent semantic correctness.

articles.tldr: Controlled benchmark showing contradictory and outdated retrieved evidence degrades medical RAG factual accuracy.

articles.title: CangjieBench: Benchmarking LLMs on a Low-Resource General-Purpose Programming Language

articles.title: CangjieBench: Benchmarking LLMs on a Low-Resource General-Purpose Programming Language

articles.title: OpenBibleTTS: Large-Scale Speech Resources and TTS Models for Low-Resource Languages

articles.title: On the Importance and Evaluation of Narrativity in Natural Language AI Explanations

articles.title: SeqBench: Benchmarking Sequential Narrative Generation in Text-to-Video Models
articles.tldr: T2V narrative-coherence benchmark with a Dynamic-Temporal-Graph MLLM metric validated against human ratings.
articles.contribution: Validates the DTG MLLM-based coherence metric against 2,560 human annotations, reporting Spearman rho=0.857 overall.

articles.title: SeqBench: Benchmarking Sequential Narrative Generation in Text-to-Video Models
articles.tldr: T2V narrative-coherence benchmark with a Dynamic-Temporal-Graph MLLM metric validated against human ratings.
articles.contribution: Shows visual-quality-only T2V benchmarks under-represent the narrative-coherence construct and adds temporal decomposition to capture it.

articles.title: LLM-ReSum: A Framework for LLM Reflective Summarization through Self-Evaluation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation of 14 automatic summarization metrics and LLM evaluators across seven datasets, plus a self-reflective refinement framework and a new legal benchmark.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks single- vs multi-agent LLM evaluators, showing majority-voting reaches tau=0.84 human correlation on SummEval accuracy.

articles.title: LLM-ReSum: A Framework for LLM Reflective Summarization through Self-Evaluation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation of 14 automatic summarization metrics and LLM evaluators across seven datasets, plus a self-reflective refinement framework and a new legal benchmark.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates lexical overlap metrics act as surface proxies, e.g. BLEU correlates tau=-0.61 with human accuracy on Arxiv.

articles.title: LLM-ReSum: A Framework for LLM Reflective Summarization through Self-Evaluation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation of 14 automatic summarization metrics and LLM evaluators across seven datasets, plus a self-reflective refinement framework and a new legal benchmark.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-evaluator reliability fails to generalize across document lengths, collapsing to tau~0.02 on 27k-word GovReport.

articles.title: PosterIQ: A Design Perspective Benchmark for Poster Understanding and Generation
articles.tldr: Design-perspective poster understanding/generation benchmark that finds MLLM automatic raters insensitive and validates its decoupled LLM-as-judge metrics against humans.
articles.contribution: Shows frontier MLLMs act as insensitive automatic raters with low correlation to human quality scores (best cosine sim ~0.48).

articles.title: PosterIQ: A Design Perspective Benchmark for Poster Understanding and Generation
articles.tldr: Design-perspective poster understanding/generation benchmark that finds MLLM automatic raters insensitive and validates its decoupled LLM-as-judge metrics against humans.
articles.contribution: Argues a single holistic quality score misrepresents poster design quality and proposes decoupled task-specific metrics across 24 tasks.

articles.title: RWGBench: Evaluating Scholarly Positioning in Related Work Generation
articles.tldr: Related-work-generation benchmark reframing evaluation as citation decision-making, showing surface and LLM-judge metrics miss scholarly-positioning validity.
articles.contribution: Reframes RWG as scholarly positioning and shows ROUGE/BERTScore reward fluent text while missing citation-level validity.

articles.title: RWGBench: Evaluating Scholarly Positioning in Related Work Generation
articles.tldr: Related-work-generation benchmark reframing evaluation as citation decision-making, showing surface and LLM-judge metrics miss scholarly-positioning validity.
articles.contribution: Finds LLM-as-judge scores only 35.8% pairwise agreement with experts (below 50% random) vs citation metrics at 61-69%.

articles.title: RWGBench: Evaluating Scholarly Positioning in Related Work Generation
articles.tldr: Related-work-generation benchmark reframing evaluation as citation decision-making, showing surface and LLM-judge metrics miss scholarly-positioning validity.
articles.contribution: Oracle experiments with ground-truth citations disentangle retrieval vs generation bottlenecks, isolating the confounded failure source.

articles.title: The illusion of a perfect metric: Why evaluating AI's words is harder than it looks
articles.tldr: Position/survey paper arguing NLG evaluation metrics (lexical, semantic, LLM-judge) have inconsistent human correlation and that the 'perfect metric' is a misguided quest.
articles.contribution: Surveys metric validation histories showing correlations with human judgment are inconsistent and non-comparable across tasks/datasets.

articles.title: The illusion of a perfect metric: Why evaluating AI's words is harder than it looks
articles.tldr: Position/survey paper arguing NLG evaluation metrics (lexical, semantic, LLM-judge) have inconsistent human correlation and that the 'perfect metric' is a misguided quest.
articles.contribution: Argues each metric captures only specific text-quality aspects, so pursuing a single universal metric misrepresents the quality construct.

articles.title: The illusion of a perfect metric: Why evaluating AI's words is harder than it looks
articles.tldr: Position/survey paper arguing NLG evaluation metrics (lexical, semantic, LLM-judge) have inconsistent human correlation and that the 'perfect metric' is a misguided quest.
articles.contribution: Criticizes RAG evaluation validity, noting RAGAS was validated with only two human annotators, undermining statistical soundness.

articles.title: Pareto-Guided Optimal Transport for Multi-Reward Alignment
articles.tldr: Multi-reward text-to-image alignment method that theoretically and empirically characterizes reward hacking and introduces principled detection metrics.
articles.contribution: Proves optimizing a unified global reward target under heterogeneous prompt-wise bounds inevitably induces reward hacking for some samples.

articles.title: Pareto-Guided Optimal Transport for Multi-Reward Alignment
articles.tldr: Multi-reward text-to-image alignment method that theoretically and empirically characterizes reward hacking and introduces principled detection metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows population-mean reward metrics mask hacking and introduces JDR/JCR aggregation to reveal per-sample joint collapse.

articles.title: Pareto-Guided Optimal Transport for Multi-Reward Alignment
articles.tldr: Multi-reward text-to-image alignment method that theoretically and empirically characterizes reward hacking and introduces principled detection metrics.
articles.contribution: Identifies weak reward models (CLIP 60.3% human-pref accuracy) as hacking-prone and builds a VLM detector agreeing 90.5% with human experts.

articles.title: VideoWeaver: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Agentic Long Video Generation
articles.tldr: Agentic long-video-generation benchmark with an evidence-grounded agent-as-judge that scores both execution traces and outputs, validated against humans.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses process-level failures from execution traces and shows harness-model compatibility confounds the measured generation quality.

articles.title: VideoWeaver: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Agentic Long Video Generation
articles.tldr: Agentic long-video-generation benchmark with an evidence-grounded agent-as-judge that scores both execution traces and outputs, validated against humans.
articles.contribution: Reports agent-as-judge aligns with humans far better on process metrics (Clip-Merging tau_b=0.892) than open-ended output metrics.

articles.title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
articles.tldr: G-Eval uses GPT-4 with chain-of-thought and probability-weighted form-filling as an NLG evaluator, and analyzes its bias toward LLM-generated text.
articles.contribution: Introduces a CoT probability-weighted LLM judge reaching Spearman 0.514 on SummEval, outperforming prior neural/LLM evaluators.

articles.title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
articles.tldr: G-Eval uses GPT-4 with chain-of-thought and probability-weighted form-filling as an NLG evaluator, and analyzes its bias toward LLM-generated text.
articles.contribution: Documents a self-preference bias: G-Eval-4 rates GPT-3.5 summaries above human ones even when humans prefer the human text.

articles.title: Meta-World: A Benchmark and Evaluation for Multi-Task and Meta Reinforcement Learning
articles.tldr: Meta-World argues narrow meta-RL task distributions cannot validly test generalization and proposes 50 diverse manipulation tasks with structured evaluation protocols.
articles.contribution: Argues single-parameter (running-velocity) task distributions are unrepresentative and samples 50 diverse manipulation tasks instead.

articles.title: Meta-World: A Benchmark and Evaluation for Multi-Task and Meta Reinforcement Learning
articles.tldr: Meta-World argues narrow meta-RL task distributions cannot validly test generalization and proposes 50 diverse manipulation tasks with structured evaluation protocols.
articles.contribution: Defines ML1/ML10/ML45 held-out meta-test protocols so generalization is measured validly, exposing weak transfer (PEARL 13% on ML10).

articles.title: GenEval: An Object-Focused Framework for Evaluating Text-to-Image Alignment
articles.tldr: GenEval is an object-focused text-to-image evaluation framework using object detection to verify compositional properties, validated against human agreement.
articles.contribution: Object-detector-based GenEval reaches 83% human agreement, more reliable than threshold-tuned CLIPScore (80%) on compositional tasks.

articles.title: GenEval: An Object-Focused Framework for Evaluating Text-to-Image Alignment
articles.tldr: GenEval is an object-focused text-to-image evaluation framework using object detection to verify compositional properties, validated against human agreement.
articles.contribution: Shows holistic CLIPScore/FID mis-measure counting and positioning; decomposing prompts into checkable object properties captures compositional alignment.

articles.title: MoverScore: Text Generation Evaluating with Contextualized Embeddings and Earth Mover Distance
articles.tldr: Proposes MoverScore, a semantic NLG metric (contextual BERT embeddings + Earth Mover's Distance) validated by correlation with human judgment across four generation tasks.
articles.contribution: Argues n-gram overlap metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) measure surface form rather than meaning (a surface proxy), and builds an embedding+EMD metric that better tracks the intended semantic-quality construct.

articles.title: HPSv3: Towards Wide-Spectrum Human Preference Score
articles.tldr: Introduces HPSv3, a wide-spectrum VLM human-preference scorer for text-to-image evaluation that correlates with human annotation better than prior metrics.
articles.contribution: Builds a VLM-based preference scorer trained with an uncertainty-aware ranking loss over 1.08M pairs, improving the reliability/validity of automatic text-to-image quality scoring.

articles.title: Emotional intelligence of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Develops a theory-grounded psychometric emotion-understanding test (SECEU) normed on 541 adults and applies it to LLMs; GPT-4 scores EQ 117 but pattern analysis shows some models reach high scores via non-human mechanisms.
articles.contribution: Shows a high EQ score gives only 'weak equivalence': item-wise representational-pattern analysis reveals several models achieve above-average EQ via mechanisms qualitatively different from humans, a discriminant/construct-validity gap.

articles.title: Emotional intelligence of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Develops a theory-grounded psychometric emotion-understanding test (SECEU) normed on 541 adults and applies it to LLMs; GPT-4 scores EQ 117 but pattern analysis shows some models reach high scores via non-human mechanisms.
articles.contribution: Establishes the psychometric reliability/validity of the SECEU instrument itself (consensus scoring, Cronbach's alpha, expert differentiation, absence of ceiling/floor effects) before scoring LLMs on it.

articles.title: VALSE: A Task-Independent Benchmark for Vision and Language Models Centered on Linguistic Phenomena
articles.tldr: VALSE benchmarks vision-and-language grounding on six linguistic phenomena using carefully constructed 'valid foils' designed to stop models exploiting statistical artefacts.
articles.contribution: Introduces novel foiling methods to guard against artefacts/statistical biases so that solving items requires genuine visio-linguistic grounding rather than exploitable shortcut cues.

articles.title: VALSE: A Task-Independent Benchmark for Vision and Language Models Centered on Linguistic Phenomena
articles.tldr: VALSE benchmarks vision-and-language grounding on six linguistic phenomena using carefully constructed 'valid foils' designed to stop models exploiting statistical artefacts.
articles.contribution: Validates foil quality with human annotation, quantifying the fraction of valid instances per instrument and its relation to annotator agreement to certify the test items.

articles.title: T2V-CompBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Compositional Text-to-video Generation
articles.tldr: T2V-CompBench benchmarks compositional text-to-video generation and, crucially, designs MLLM/detection/tracking-based metrics validated against human judgment.
articles.contribution: Designs MLLM-based, detection-based and tracking-based scorers for seven compositional categories and validates them against human evaluation, showing higher agreement than conventional similarity metrics.

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms
articles.tldr: Empirically formalizes reward over-optimization (Goodhart) in direct alignment algorithms: GPT-4-judged win-rate degrades with more optimization despite proxy improvement.
articles.contribution: Formalizes reward over-optimization for DPO/IPO/SLiC, demonstrating that pushing the implicit proxy reward corrupts true (GPT-4-judged) quality via a hump-shaped degradation.

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms
articles.tldr: Empirically formalizes reward over-optimization (Goodhart) in direct alignment algorithms: GPT-4-judged win-rate degrades with more optimization despite proxy improvement.
articles.contribution: Fits scaling-law curves to the over-optimization degradation across KL budgets and model scales, characterizing how validity of the proxy drifts with optimization pressure and scale.

articles.title: OoD-Bench: Quantifying and Understanding Two Dimensions of Out-of-Distribution Generalization
articles.tldr: OoD-Bench quantifies two orthogonal distribution-shift dimensions (diversity vs correlation shift) and shows OOD benchmarks are each dominated by one, making algorithm comparisons misleading.
articles.contribution: Provides quantitative measures of diversity and correlation shift and shows common datasets are dominated by only one, so evaluating on a single benchmark misrepresents an algorithm's OOD coverage.

articles.title: OoD-Bench: Quantifying and Understanding Two Dimensions of Out-of-Distribution Generalization
articles.tldr: OoD-Bench quantifies two orthogonal distribution-shift dimensions (diversity vs correlation shift) and shows OOD benchmarks are each dominated by one, making algorithm comparisons misleading.
articles.contribution: Shows apparent OOD-generalization gains are confounded by which shift a benchmark contains: an algorithm strong on one shift is weak on the other, and advanced methods barely beat ERM.

articles.title: Skywork: A More Open Bilingual Foundation Model
articles.tldr: Skywork-13B foundation-model report whose validity contribution is a loss-based leakage-detection method that reveals GSM8K test contamination in several public LLMs.
articles.contribution: Proposes detecting benchmark leakage by comparing language-modeling loss on the GSM8K train split, test split, and a GPT-4-generated reference set, which should be equal absent contamination.

articles.title: CRAG - Comprehensive RAG Benchmark
articles.tldr: CRAG is a factual RAG QA benchmark deliberately built for real-world dynamism/popularity/complexity, exposing representativeness gaps and low factual accuracy of RAG systems.
articles.contribution: Argues existing RAG datasets fail to represent real-world QA and constructs a benchmark spanning entity popularity (popular to long-tail) and temporal dynamism to test ecological representativeness of RAG evaluation.

articles.title: Provably Mitigating Overoptimization in RLHF: Your SFT Loss is Implicitly an Adversarial Regularizer
articles.tldr: Analyzes RLHF reward over-optimization as distributional shift/uncertainty and proposes RPO, which adds an SFT loss as an implicit adversarial regularizer against spurious high proxy rewards.
articles.contribution: Identifies the source of reward over-optimization as distributional shift and uncertainty in the learned proxy reward, and derives a principled penalty preventing the policy from chasing spurious high proxy rewards.

articles.title: Learning Multi-Dimensional Human Preference for Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Argues statistical T2I metrics and single-score preference models misrepresent multi-dimensional human preference, and builds a multi-dimensional scorer.
articles.contribution: Defines human preference as a four-dimensional construct (aesthetics, semantic alignment, detail quality, overall) before building a measure, rather than a single scalar.

articles.title: Learning Multi-Dimensional Human Preference for Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Argues statistical T2I metrics and single-score preference models misrepresent multi-dimensional human preference, and builds a multi-dimensional scorer.
articles.contribution: Shows a single overall preference score collapses weakly-correlated dimensions, so the scorer captures a surface proxy rather than the full preference construct.

articles.title: Confronting Reward Model Overoptimization with Constrained RLHF
articles.tldr: First study of reward-model overoptimization in composite RMs, showing correlation between component RMs shifts the Goodhart 'proxy points', with constrained RL keeping each RM in its useful proxy range.
articles.contribution: Shows a reward model is only a proxy for human evaluation, so past a 'proxy point' higher reward correlates with worse true preference (Goodhart), corrupting the measured objective.

articles.title: Confronting Reward Model Overoptimization with Constrained RLHF
articles.tldr: First study of reward-model overoptimization in composite RMs, showing correlation between component RMs shifts the Goodhart 'proxy points', with constrained RL keeping each RM in its useful proxy range.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates correlation among component RMs moves where the aggregated composite reward stops tracking human ratings; dynamic Lagrange-multiplier weights hold each RM below its proxy point.

articles.title: “I’m fully who I am”: Towards Centering Transgender and Non-Binary Voices to Measure Biases in Open Language Generation
articles.tldr: Builds a community-grounded framework and TANGO dataset to measure misgendering and gender-disclosure harms toward transgender and non-binary identities in open language generation.
articles.contribution: Grounds TGNB harm constructs (misgendering and gender-disclosure stigma) in community voices and interdisciplinary literature rather than binary-centric gender norms.

articles.title: “I’m fully who I am”: Towards Centering Transgender and Non-Binary Voices to Measure Biases in Open Language Generation
articles.tldr: Builds a community-grounded framework and TANGO dataset to measure misgendering and gender-disclosure harms toward transgender and non-binary identities in open language generation.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes misgendering via templated real-world TGNB text and pronoun-consistency checks contrasting binary pronouns, singular they and neopronouns.

articles.title: MedAlign: A Clinician-Generated Dataset for Instruction Following with Electronic Medical Records
articles.tldr: Clinician-generated EHR instruction benchmark used to test whether automated NLG metrics can validly substitute for expert human evaluation of clinical LLM outputs.
articles.contribution: Argues existing EHR-QA datasets fail to capture real clinician information needs, curating 983 clinician-written instructions over 276 longitudinal EHRs for ecologically valid evaluation.

articles.title: MedAlign: A Clinician-Generated Dataset for Instruction Following with Electronic Medical Records
articles.tldr: Clinician-generated EHR instruction benchmark used to test whether automated NLG metrics can validly substitute for expert human evaluation of clinical LLM outputs.
articles.contribution: Assesses correspondence between automated NLG metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, BERTScore, COMET) and clinician rankings, noting little prior work validates these metrics for clinical NLG.

articles.title: Detecting semantic anomalies
articles.tldr: Critiques OOD-detection benchmarks as ill-motivated (dataset-vs-dataset shifts measure low-level idiosyncrasies not semantic novelty) and recommends hold-out-class benchmarks and AUPRC over AUROC.
articles.contribution: Shows dataset-as-OOD benchmarks let trivial low-level features win, so detection scores reflect dataset bias rather than the intended semantic-anomaly construct.

articles.title: Detecting semantic anomalies
articles.tldr: Critiques OOD-detection benchmarks as ill-motivated (dataset-vs-dataset shifts measure low-level idiosyncrasies not semantic novelty) and recommends hold-out-class benchmarks and AUPRC over AUROC.
articles.contribution: Recommends hold-out-class evaluation (CIFAR-10/STL-10, ImageNet fine-grained subsets) that holds dataset-bias invariant, arguing arbitrary different-dataset OOD is unrepresentative of realistic anomalies.

articles.title: Detecting semantic anomalies
articles.tldr: Critiques OOD-detection benchmarks as ill-motivated (dataset-vs-dataset shifts measure low-level idiosyncrasies not semantic novelty) and recommends hold-out-class benchmarks and AUPRC over AUROC.
articles.contribution: Argues AUROC is insensitive to class skew and yields optimistic scores when anomalies are rare, recommending average precision (AUPRC) for anomaly-detection evaluation.

articles.title: Survey of Bias In Text-to-Image Generation: Definition, Evaluation, and Mitigation
articles.tldr: Survey of how text-to-image bias is defined, evaluated and mitigated, finding fragmented datasets/metrics with no unified measurement framework and neglect of non-binary identities.
articles.contribution: Catalogs how gender, skintone and geo-cultural bias constructs are inconsistently defined and notes almost all gender-bias work overlooks non-binary identities.

articles.title: Survey of Bias In Text-to-Image Generation: Definition, Evaluation, and Mitigation
articles.tldr: Survey of how text-to-image bias is defined, evaluated and mitigated, finding fragmented datasets/metrics with no unified measurement framework and neglect of non-binary identities.
articles.contribution: Reviews classification-based versus embedding-based bias metrics and finds datasets/metrics are scattered with no unified framework, so bias measurements are not comparable across studies.

articles.title: VideoHallucer: Evaluating Intrinsic and Extrinsic Hallucinations in Large Video-Language Models
articles.tldr: First video-LLM hallucination benchmark using adversarial basic/hallucinated question pairs with balanced yes/no answers to validly measure intrinsic and extrinsic hallucinations.
articles.contribution: Pairs each basic question with a hallucinated counterpart and balances 'yes'/'no' answers to remove the yes-bias / language-bias confound in binary VideoQA hallucination scoring.

articles.title: VideoHallucer: Evaluating Intrinsic and Extrinsic Hallucinations in Large Video-Language Models
articles.tldr: First video-LLM hallucination benchmark using adversarial basic/hallucinated question pairs with balanced yes/no answers to validly measure intrinsic and extrinsic hallucinations.
articles.contribution: Defines a fine-grained hallucination taxonomy (intrinsic vs extrinsic; object-relation, temporal, semantic-detail, extrinsic factual and non-factual) for video-language models.

articles.title: ExplaGraphs: An Explanation Graph Generation Task for Structured Commonsense Reasoning
articles.tldr: New generative structured explanation-graph task for stance prediction, motivated by discriminative benchmarks enabling reasoning shortcuts, with an iterative annotation pipeline and multi-level graph evaluation.
articles.contribution: Argues discriminative multiple-choice commonsense tasks leak shortcut/artifact cues, and reoperationalizes the task as generating a connected-DAG explanation graph with HAMLET adversarial collection so models must be 'right for the right reasons'.

articles.title: ExplaGraphs: An Explanation Graph Generation Task for Structured Commonsense Reasoning
articles.tldr: New generative structured explanation-graph task for stance prediction, motivated by discriminative benchmarks enabling reasoning shortcuts, with an iterative annotation pipeline and multi-level graph evaluation.
articles.contribution: Its Create-Verify-And-Refine crowd pipeline iteratively raises the semantic correctness of gold explanation graphs from 67% to 90%, controlling annotation quality for a structured-reasoning ground truth.

articles.title: ChronoMagic-Bench: A Benchmark for Metamorphic Evaluation of Text-to-Time-lapse Video Generation
articles.tldr: Text-to-time-lapse-video benchmark arguing existing T2V metrics only measure single-frame visual quality, and proposing MTScore/CHScore metrics cross-verified against human evaluation.
articles.contribution: Defines metamorphic amplitude and temporal coherence as target constructs that existing FVD/CLIP-style T2V benchmarks fail to capture by focusing only on per-frame visual quality and text relevance.

articles.title: ChronoMagic-Bench: A Benchmark for Metamorphic Evaluation of Text-to-Time-lapse Video Generation
articles.tldr: Text-to-time-lapse-video benchmark arguing existing T2V metrics only measure single-frame visual quality, and proposing MTScore/CHScore metrics cross-verified against human evaluation.
articles.contribution: Introduces MTScore and CHScore that align better with human judgment than existing metrics, using human evaluation to cross-verify the reliability of its four automatic metrics.

articles.title: Towards a holistic framework for multimodal LLM in 3D brain CT radiology report generation
articles.tldr: 3D brain-CT report-generation study showing traditional NLG metrics fail to capture clinical diagnostic essence, proposing the feature-oriented FORTE metric plus a physician Turing test.
articles.contribution: Shows BLEU/ROUGE measure only surface similarity and are insensitive to the clinical construct, and proposes FORTE (degree/landmark/feature/impression F1) whose low correlation with traditional metrics evidences its discriminant validity.

articles.title: Towards a holistic framework for multimodal LLM in 3D brain CT radiology report generation
articles.tldr: 3D brain-CT report-generation study showing traditional NLG metrics fail to capture clinical diagnostic essence, proposing the feature-oriented FORTE metric plus a physician Turing test.
articles.contribution: Identifies a 'sharpshooter fallacy' in single-slice 2D CT captioning datasets and curates an 18,885 text-scan 3D-BrainCT dataset to represent real volumetric diagnostic complexity.

articles.title: Evaluation of Text-to-Video Generation Models: A Dynamics Perspective
articles.tldr: Text-to-video evaluation protocol (DEVIL) centered on video dynamics, showing existing metrics negatively correlate with dynamics and can be gamed by low-dynamic videos, and proposing human-aligned dynamics scores.
articles.contribution: Argues existing T2V protocols capture only temporal consistency and continuity and ignore the dynamics dimension, defining dynamics range, controllability, and dynamics-based quality as the missing construct.

articles.title: Evaluation of Text-to-Video Generation Models: A Dynamics Perspective
articles.tldr: Text-to-video evaluation protocol (DEVIL) centered on video dynamics, showing existing metrics negatively correlate with dynamics and can be gamed by low-dynamic videos, and proposing human-aligned dynamics scores.
articles.contribution: Shows several existing metrics have considerable negative correlation with dynamics, letting models score high by generating low-dynamic videos, and integrates human-aligned dynamics scores to prevent this metric gaming.

articles.title: UNION: An Unreferenced Metric for Evaluating Open-ended Story Generation
articles.tldr: Learnable unreferenced metric (UNION) for open-ended story generation, motivated by referenced metrics' poor human correlation from the one-to-many problem, and shown robust to dataset and quality drift.
articles.contribution: Shows referenced metrics (BLEU, MoverScore) correlate poorly with human judgments on open-ended generation because of the one-to-many issue, and proposes a reference-free BERT scorer that captures story quality without penalizing valid dissimilar outputs.

articles.title: UNION: An Unreferenced Metric for Evaluating Open-ended Story Generation
articles.tldr: Learnable unreferenced metric (UNION) for open-ended story generation, motivated by referenced metrics' poor human correlation from the one-to-many problem, and shown robust to dataset and quality drift.
articles.contribution: Trains UNION on model-agnostic auto-constructed negatives (repetition/substitution/reordering/negation), giving a metric that generalizes across datasets and quality levels with less variance than discriminator or BLEURT baselines.

articles.title: GenAI Arena: An Open Evaluation Platform for Generative Models
articles.tldr: Open community-voting Elo platform (GenAI-Arena) for image/video generative models plus GenAI-Bench, showing automatic metrics and MLLM judges poorly match human preference.
articles.contribution: Motivates that automatic metrics like FID, CLIP, and FVD fail to capture the nuanced quality and user satisfaction of generative outputs, using collective human preference votes as the evaluation gold standard instead.
