articles.title: GenAI Arena: An Open Evaluation Platform for Generative Models
articles.tldr: Open community-voting Elo platform (GenAI-Arena) for image/video generative models plus GenAI-Bench, showing automatic metrics and MLLM judges poorly match human preference.
articles.contribution: Releases GenAI-Bench and measures MLLM-judge agreement with human votes, showing the best judge GPT-4o reaches only 49.19% average accuracy and open-source MLLMs far worse.

articles.title: GenAI Arena: An Open Evaluation Platform for Generative Models
articles.tldr: Open community-voting Elo platform (GenAI-Arena) for image/video generative models plus GenAI-Bench, showing automatic metrics and MLLM judges poorly match human preference.
articles.contribution: Adopts Bradley-Terry MLE with bootstrap/sandwich confidence intervals for stable ranking and shows Elo can be biased by imbalance between 'easy games' and 'hard games' in matchups.

articles.title: ImagenHub: Standardizing the evaluation of conditional image generation models
articles.tldr: Standardizes datasets, inference, and human evaluation for conditional image generation, defining Semantic Consistency and Perceptual Quality with high inter-rater agreement and showing auto-metrics barely correlate with humans.
articles.contribution: Provides a unified inference pipeline with fixed hyperparameters and prompts plus standardized datasets across 7 tasks, so ~30 conditional-generation models can be compared fairly and reproducibly.

articles.title: ImagenHub: Standardizing the evaluation of conditional image generation models
articles.tldr: Standardizes datasets, inference, and human evaluation for conditional image generation, defining Semantic Consistency and Perceptual Quality with high inter-rater agreement and showing auto-metrics barely correlate with humans.
articles.contribution: Designs two three-valued human metrics (Semantic Consistency, Perceptual Quality) with explicit rating guidelines that achieve Krippendorff's alpha above 0.4 on 76% of models.

articles.title: ImagenHub: Standardizing the evaluation of conditional image generation models
articles.tldr: Standardizes datasets, inference, and human evaluation for conditional image generation, defining Semantic Consistency and Perceptual Quality with high inter-rater agreement and showing auto-metrics barely correlate with humans.
articles.contribution: Shows no automatic metric (FID, CLIP, LPIPS, DINO, DreamSim) exceeds Spearman 0.2 correlation with human ratings except subject-driven generation, exposing auto-metrics as poor quality proxies.

articles.title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
articles.tldr: Automated pipeline for continuously collecting fresh, decontaminated SWE-agent tasks, showing static benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified may inflate scores via contamination and standardizing scaffold plus statistical reporting.
articles.contribution: Builds a contamination-free benchmark from continuously collected fresh GitHub-issue tasks and tracks issue/PR creation dates against model release dates to flag potentially contaminated evaluations, showing some models' scores are inflated by leakage.

articles.title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
articles.tldr: Automated pipeline for continuously collecting fresh, decontaminated SWE-agent tasks, showing static benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified may inflate scores via contamination and standardizing scaffold plus statistical reporting.
articles.contribution: Standardizes the agent scaffold to isolate model capability from confounds like engineered prompts, multi-agent frameworks, retries, and best-of-N sampling that inflate SWE-bench performance.

articles.title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
articles.tldr: Automated pipeline for continuously collecting fresh, decontaminated SWE-agent tasks, showing static benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified may inflate scores via contamination and standardizing scaffold plus statistical reporting.
articles.contribution: Accounts for agent stochasticity by running each model five times and reporting standard error of the mean and pass@5 for a statistically grounded, more reliable performance estimate.

articles.title: On the Limitations of Reference-Free Evaluations of Generated Text
articles.tldr: Argues reference-free NLG metrics are equivalent to generation models, so they are optimizable at test time and biased toward their own/similar model outputs and against human text, and should not measure task progress.
articles.contribution: Proves a reference-free metric M(x,y) is itself a conditional generation model whose argmax output is the theoretical best, so simple direct-optimization or reranking inference can be run at test time to inflate the metric's score.

articles.title: On the Limitations of Reference-Free Evaluations of Generated Text
articles.tldr: Argues reference-free NLG metrics are equivalent to generation models, so they are optimizable at test time and biased toward their own/similar model outputs and against human text, and should not measure task progress.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates reference-free metrics are biased toward outputs of their own and similar models and against higher-quality human text, so improving them optimizes similarity to the metric rather than true quality.

articles.title: MARKMyWORDS: Analyzing and Evaluating Language Model Watermarks
articles.tldr: A benchmark for LLM text watermarks measuring quality, detection size, and tamper-resistance, using a validated LLM-judge for quality and standardized comparison across schemes.
articles.contribution: Provides a standardized benchmark (MarkMyWords) that isolates quality, detection size, and tamper-resistance so different LLM watermarking schemes can be compared fairly under controlled natural-language tasks.

articles.title: MARKMyWORDS: Analyzing and Evaluating Language Model Watermarks
articles.tldr: A benchmark for LLM text watermarks measuring quality, detection size, and tamper-resistance, using a validated LLM-judge for quality and standardized comparison across schemes.
articles.contribution: Uses Llama-2 as a scalable quality rater and validates its reliability against GPT-3.5 (R^2 = 0.97 on average non-perturbed ratings) to enable reproducible local quality scoring.

articles.title: WritingBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Generative Writing
articles.tldr: WritingBench evaluates generative writing with per-query LLM-generated criteria scored by a fine-tuned critic, targeting the construct-validity gap of static writing-quality dimensions.
articles.contribution: Argues static predefined dimensions (fluency/coherence) under-represent multi-dimensional writing quality, and generates five instance-specific criteria per query to better cover the construct.

articles.title: WritingBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Generative Writing
articles.tldr: WritingBench evaluates generative writing with per-query LLM-generated criteria scored by a fine-tuned critic, targeting the construct-validity gap of static writing-quality dimensions.
articles.contribution: Fine-tuned critic model with criteria-aware scoring reaches 84% agreement with human judgment, versus 67% and 58% for static-criteria baselines.

articles.title: Uncovering the Limits of Machine Learning for Automatic Vulnerability Detection
articles.tldr: Shows ML-for-vulnerability-detection benchmarks credit models that overfit to label-unrelated code features and cannot tell a vulnerable function from its patch, and proposes cross-transformation and patch-pair evaluation to expose it.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates six SOTA token-based LLM detectors predict from features unrelated to the vulnerability; on VulnPatchPairs (26.2k C functions, half patched) accuracy is worse than random, so high benchmark accuracy does not reflect the intended construct.

articles.title: Uncovering the Limits of Machine Learning for Automatic Vulnerability Detection
articles.tldr: Shows ML-for-vulnerability-detection benchmarks credit models that overfit to label-unrelated code features and cannot tell a vulnerable function from its patch, and proposes cross-transformation and patch-pair evaluation to expose it.
articles.contribution: Shows training-data-augmentation gains do not generalize to different transformations, revealing that standard-benchmark scores overstate real detection capability out of distribution.

articles.title: T3Bench: Benchmarking Current Progress in Text-to-3D Generation
articles.tldr: T3Bench proposes multi-view automatic quality and alignment metrics for text-to-3D that correlate with human judgment (Spearman >0.75), fixing single-view CLIP metrics that miss 3D/view inconsistency.
articles.contribution: Shows single-view CLIP R-precision misrepresents 3D quality; the new quality metric combines multi-view text-image scores with regional convolution to detect the Janus (view-inconsistency) problem.

articles.title: T3Bench: Benchmarking Current Progress in Text-to-3D Generation
articles.tldr: T3Bench proposes multi-view automatic quality and alignment metrics for text-to-3D that correlate with human judgment (Spearman >0.75), fixing single-view CLIP metrics that miss 3D/view inconsistency.
articles.contribution: Alignment metric using multi-view captioning plus GPT-4 evaluation quantifies text-3D consistency and correlates with human 1-5 ratings, providing a validated automatic scorer.

articles.title: A New Benchmark and Reverse Validation Method for Passage-level Hallucination Detection
articles.tldr: Builds the PHD passage-level hallucination-detection benchmark with a rigorous two-stage human annotation protocol and a data-volume-proxy sampling scheme, then evaluates zero-resource detection methods.
articles.contribution: Establishes ground-truth label quality via a two-stage annotation with a qualification test and inter-rater agreement (Cohen's Kappa 0.848, Fleiss 0.77), addressing annotation reliability for passage-level hallucination labels.

articles.title: A New Benchmark and Reverse Validation Method for Passage-level Hallucination Detection
articles.tldr: Builds the PHD passage-level hallucination-detection benchmark with a rigorous two-stage human annotation protocol and a data-volume-proxy sampling scheme, then evaluates zero-resource detection methods.
articles.contribution: Samples entities by a Google-search data-volume proxy into PHD-Low/Medium/High tiers to naturally elicit hallucinations, so the benchmark distribution reflects realistic knowledge-gap-driven hallucination rather than forced examples.

articles.title: Synthetic Dialogue Dataset Generation using LLM Agents
articles.tldr: Generates LP synthetic dialogues but contributes an extrinsic evaluation comparing a GPT-4 judge with human raters, exposing weak inter-annotator agreement and a systematic GPT-4 leniency bias.
articles.contribution: Finds the GPT-4 evaluator mimicking human metrics only reaches Spearman rho about 0.58 and did not outperform ROUGE-L (0.69), and was systematically more generous than human raters.

articles.title: Synthetic Dialogue Dataset Generation using LLM Agents
articles.tldr: Generates LP synthetic dialogues but contributes an extrinsic evaluation comparing a GPT-4 judge with human raters, exposing weak inter-annotator agreement and a systematic GPT-4 leniency bias.
articles.contribution: Reports poor human inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss Kappa 0.205 recall, 0.387 precision, 0.235 readability, -0.009 repetition), undermining the reliability of the human reference the judge is validated against.

articles.title: ResearchRubrics: A Benchmark of Prompts and Rubrics For Evaluating Deep Research Agents
articles.tldr: ResearchRubrics evaluates deep-research agents with 2,593 expert-authored rubrics and an LLM-as-judge protocol, surfacing rubric-design circularity and a length-quality conflation confound in compliance scoring.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes deep-research quality via 2,593 human-written, human-reviewed fine-grained rubrics (including negative rubrics), explicitly avoiding LLM-generated rubrics whose circularity limits oversight.

articles.title: ResearchRubrics: A Benchmark of Prompts and Rubrics For Evaluating Deep Research Agents
articles.tldr: ResearchRubrics evaluates deep-research agents with 2,593 expert-authored rubrics and an LLM-as-judge protocol, surfacing rubric-design circularity and a length-quality conflation confound in compliance scoring.
articles.contribution: Develops an LLM-as-judge rubric-compliance scorer validated against human judgment and shows ternary vs binary grading and rubric-detail level materially change human-judge agreement.

articles.title: ResearchRubrics: A Benchmark of Prompts and Rubrics For Evaluating Deep Research Agents
articles.tldr: ResearchRubrics evaluates deep-research agents with 2,593 expert-authored rubrics and an LLM-as-judge protocol, surfacing rubric-design circularity and a length-quality conflation confound in compliance scoring.
articles.contribution: Identifies a length-quality conflation problem where response length confounds rubric-compliance scores, threatening the internal validity of the measured compliance.

articles.title: SoK: Membership Inference Attacks on LLMs are Rushing Nowhere (and How to Fix It)
articles.tldr: A systematization showing that post-hoc member/non-member datasets used to evaluate LLM membership-inference attacks are confounded by distribution shift, so a model-less bag-of-words classifier often beats the MIAs.
articles.contribution: Quantifies with a model-less bag-of-words classifier that post-hoc datasets carry a strong temporal distribution shift confound, so reported MIA success cannot be attributed to LLM memorization.

articles.title: SoK: Membership Inference Attacks on LLMs are Rushing Nowhere (and How to Fix It)
articles.tldr: A systematization showing that post-hoc member/non-member datasets used to evaluate LLM membership-inference attacks are confounded by distribution shift, so a model-less bag-of-words classifier often beats the MIAs.
articles.contribution: Shows that constructing members/non-members via post-hoc informed guesses (rather than randomized splits) makes 6 widely-reused datasets unrepresentative, invalidating claims of strong real-world memorization.

articles.title: OpenS2V-Nexus: A Detailed Benchmark and Million-Scale Dataset for Subject-to-Video Generation
articles.tldr: OpenS2V-Nexus critiques VBench-inherited subject-to-video metrics that reward unnatural/low-fidelity subjects, and proposes NexusScore/NaturalScore/GmeScore that align better with human preference.
articles.contribution: Shows existing benchmarks compute subject consistency as similarity on uncropped frames, introducing background noise and giving high scores to unnatural subjects; NexusScore uses image-prompt detection plus multimodal retrieval to fix this.

articles.title: OpenS2V-Nexus: A Detailed Benchmark and Million-Scale Dataset for Subject-to-Video Generation
articles.tldr: OpenS2V-Nexus critiques VBench-inherited subject-to-video metrics that reward unnatural/low-fidelity subjects, and proposes NexusScore/NaturalScore/GmeScore that align better with human preference.
articles.contribution: Introduces NaturalScore, a GPT-based metric bridging the subject-naturalness dimension that prior coarse-grained metrics neglect, and GmeScore replacing CLIPScore for text relevance.

articles.title: LeetCodeDataset: A Temporal Dataset for Robust Evaluation and Efficient Training of Code LLMs
articles.tldr: Temporal LeetCode benchmark giving contamination-free evaluation of code LLMs via pre/post July-2024 splits.
articles.contribution: Uses publicly-known LeetCode weekly-contest release dates as anchors to build temporal (pre/post July 2024) splits so post-cutoff problems give contamination-free evaluation, scored with 100+ unit tests per problem.

articles.title: Quantifying and Improving Transferability in Domain Generalization
articles.tldr: Formally defines and quantifies domain-generalization transferability, bounds target error, and audits whether existing DG algorithms actually learn transferable features.
articles.contribution: Introduces a computable transfer measure (an integral-probability-metric over a delta-minimal classifier set) with a finite-sample estimation guarantee and a new target-error upper bound, giving a principled quantification of external/OOD validity of learned features.

articles.title: TRAIL: Trace Reasoning and Agentic Issue Localization
articles.tldr: TRAIL benchmark of 148 human-annotated agentic traces with an error taxonomy, showing frontier LLMs are unreliable at trace debugging.
articles.contribution: Builds an ecologically-valid benchmark of real single/multi-agent traces (software engineering, open-world IR) to test whether LLMs can scalably localize errors, exposing that current long-context LLM judges are unreliable at trace debugging.

articles.title: TRAIL: Trace Reasoning and Agentic Issue Localization
articles.tldr: TRAIL benchmark of 148 human-annotated agentic traces with an error taxonomy, showing frontier LLMs are unreliable at trace debugging.
articles.contribution: Provides a formal human-annotated error taxonomy over 148 traces grounded in established agentic benchmarks, giving a gold-standard construct for what counts as an agentic error.

articles.title: Exposure Bias versus Self-Recovery: Are Distortions Really Incremental for Autoregressive Text Generation?
articles.tldr: Proposes EB-M/EB-C metrics to quantify exposure bias and finds, contrary to popular belief, its distortion is limited and non-incremental due to LM self-recovery.
articles.contribution: Designs a controlled comparison feeding ground-truth vs model-generated prefixes so the training-generation discrepancy is the only varying factor, isolating whether exposure bias causally induces incremental distortion.

articles.title: Exposure Bias versus Self-Recovery: Are Distortions Really Incremental for Autoregressive Text Generation?
articles.tldr: Proposes EB-M/EB-C metrics to quantify exposure bias and finds, contrary to popular belief, its distortion is limited and non-incremental due to LM self-recovery.
articles.contribution: Provides negative/falsification evidence against the exposure-bias construct and surfaces a competing 'self-recovery' construct that the metrics reveal.

articles.title: WOODS: Benchmarks for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Time Series Tasks
articles.tldr: WOODS: eight time-series OOD-generalization benchmarks with a fair evaluation framework, exposing large gaps and a confound in OOD-algorithm gains.
articles.contribution: Provides eight open-source time-series OOD benchmarks (video, EEG/brain, sensor signals) under a systematic fair-evaluation framework to measure external/OOD validity for a setting previously underexplored beyond static vision.

articles.title: WOODS: Benchmarks for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Time Series Tasks
articles.tldr: WOODS: eight time-series OOD-generalization benchmarks with a fair evaluation framework, exposing large gaps and a confound in OOD-algorithm gains.
articles.contribution: Constructs a domain-agnostic 'Unbalanced' IEMOCAP variant to disentangle whether OOD algorithms' gains over ERM come from genuine OOD ability or merely from upsampling minority domains when computing empirical risk.

articles.title: Re-evaluating ADEM: A Deeper Look at Scoring Dialogue Responses
articles.tldr: Adversarially re-evaluates the learned ADEM dialogue-scoring metric, showing it is easily gamed and unreliable.
articles.contribution: Red-teams the neural ADEM evaluator with targeted attacks, including a white-box guided-backpropagation attack that manipulates response embeddings to obtain arbitrarily favorable scores.

articles.title: Re-evaluating ADEM: A Deeper Look at Scoring Dialogue Responses
articles.tldr: Adversarially re-evaluates the learned ADEM dialogue-scoring metric, showing it is easily gamed and unreliable.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses ADEM's reliability by connecting its scoring function to linear system theory to predict its shortcomings and shows its scores collapse to a conservative average.

articles.title: CTRLEval: An Unsupervised Reference-Free Metric for Evaluating Controlled Text Generation
articles.tldr: CTRLEval, an unsupervised reference-free metric for controlled text generation built from text-infilling patterns, validated against human judgments and drift.
articles.contribution: Builds a training-free metric that formulates coherence/consistency/attribute-relevance as multiple text-infilling tasks and ensembles a pre-trained LM's generation probabilities, achieving higher correlation with human judgments than baselines.

articles.title: CTRLEval: An Unsupervised Reference-Free Metric for Evaluating Controlled Text Generation
articles.tldr: CTRLEval, an unsupervised reference-free metric for controlled text generation built from text-infilling patterns, validated against human judgments and drift.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates the metric generalizes across generation models (model drift) and text-quality levels (quality drift) with smaller variance, unlike supervised metrics that overfit task-specific data.

articles.title: Localization is All You Evaluate: Data Leakage in Online Mapping Datasets and How to Fix it
articles.tldr: Shows geographic data leakage in nuScenes/Argoverse online-mapping splits inflates scores, and geographically disjoint splits reveal much lower true performance.
articles.contribution: Quantifies geographic train/test overlap in standard online-mapping datasets and proposes geographically disjoint (Near/Far extrapolation, city-wise CV) splits to remove the leakage that inflates mAP.

articles.title: Localization is All You Evaluate: Data Leakage in Online Mapping Datasets and How to Fix it
articles.tldr: Shows geographic data leakage in nuScenes/Argoverse online-mapping splits inflates scores, and geographically disjoint splits reveal much lower true performance.
articles.contribution: Re-runs prior design-choice ablations on leakage-free splits, showing conclusions about lifting methods and auxiliary tasks diverge from those drawn on the original overlapping split.

articles.title: Evaluating Cultural and Social Awareness of LLM Web Agents
articles.tldr: CASA benchmark measures cultural/social awareness of LLM web agents, exposing very low awareness and high norm-violation rates in agentic settings.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes the under-measured construct of cultural/social awareness via norm-violating queries and observations across shopping and forum tasks, with metrics for awareness coverage, helpfulness and violation rate.

articles.title: Evaluating Cultural and Social Awareness of LLM Web Agents
articles.tldr: CASA benchmark measures cultural/social awareness of LLM web agents, exposing very low awareness and high norm-violation rates in agentic settings.
articles.contribution: Shows the agentic web harness itself confounds measured awareness: LLMs score far higher in non-agent than in web-agent settings, exposing a scaffold-dependent validity gap.

articles.title: Inference-Time Text-to-Video Alignment with Diffusion Latent Beam Search
articles.tldr: Inference-time text-to-video alignment method that first shows perceptual video metrics don't correlate with human/VLM preference and calibrates a weighted reward to fix the mismatch.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that many perceptual video-naturalness metrics do not correlate with human/VLM preference, and builds a preference-calibrated weighted-metric reward that captures perceptual quality.

articles.title: Inference-Time Text-to-Video Alignment with Diffusion Latent Beam Search
articles.tldr: Inference-time text-to-video alignment method that first shows perceptual video metrics don't correlate with human/VLM preference and calibrates a weighted reward to fix the mismatch.
articles.contribution: Shows that maximizing a single video-quality metric over-optimizes and unintentionally reduces motion magnitude, so a multi-objective calibrated reward is needed to avoid Goodhart-style corruption.

articles.title: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Task-Specific Exam Generation
articles.tldr: Automatically generates task-specific multiple-choice exams and uses a 3-parameter IRT model to weight questions, quantify exam informativeness, and iteratively prune uninformative items for robust RAG evaluation.
articles.contribution: Fits a 3PL IRT model (difficulty, discrimination, guessing) that weights each question by inferred quality so RAG ability scores are robust to noisy or uninformative exam items.

articles.title: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Task-Specific Exam Generation
articles.tldr: Automatically generates task-specific multiple-choice exams and uses a 3-parameter IRT model to weight questions, quantify exam informativeness, and iteratively prune uninformative items for robust RAG evaluation.
articles.contribution: Uses question filtering (self-contained constraint, candidate shuffling to defeat position bias) plus IRT informativeness to iteratively remove low-quality exam items from the auto-generated MCQ instrument.

articles.title: AIGCBench: Comprehensive Evaluation of Image-to-Video Content Generated by AI
articles.tldr: AIGCBench is an open-domain Image-to-Video benchmark with 11 metrics across four dimensions, built to fix unrepresentative eval sets and validated to correlate with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Addresses the lack of diverse datasets in prior I2V benchmarks by building a varied open-domain image-text dataset that evaluates all algorithms under equivalent conditions.

articles.title: AIGCBench: Comprehensive Evaluation of Image-to-Video Content Generated by AI
articles.tldr: AIGCBench is an open-domain Image-to-Video benchmark with 11 metrics across four dimensions, built to fix unrepresentative eval sets and validated to correlate with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory evidence for its 11-metric standard by showing (via a user study) that the metric suite correlates with human judgment of generated video quality.

articles.title: β3-IRT: A New Item Response Model and its Applications
articles.tldr: Introduces the beta-3 IRT model, a continuous-response item response model producing non-logistic item characteristic curves and an instance-wise metric for classifier probability quality.
articles.contribution: Proposes beta-3 IRT, a continuous IRT model with richer (non-logistic) ICC shapes and [0,1]-bounded ability/difficulty, giving an instance-wise ability metric for evaluating classifier probability estimates.

articles.title: β3-IRT: A New Item Response Model and its Applications
articles.tldr: Introduces the beta-3 IRT model, a continuous-response item response model producing non-logistic item characteristic curves and an instance-wise metric for classifier probability quality.
articles.contribution: Uses inferred negative item discrimination to flag noisy/mislabeled test instances, offering a ground-truth-quality diagnostic derived directly from the item parameters.

articles.title: Exploring Precision and Recall to assess the quality and diversity of LLMs
articles.tldr: Imports distribution-based Precision (quality) and Recall (diversity) metrics from image generation to text, exposing a quality-diversity tradeoff that single-score benchmarks miss.
articles.contribution: Introduces Precision and Recall for text generation to capture the diversity dimension of generation quality that traditional single-number benchmarks under-represent, without needing aligned corpora.

articles.title: Exploring Precision and Recall to assess the quality and diversity of LLMs
articles.tldr: Imports distribution-based Precision (quality) and Recall (diversity) metrics from image generation to text, exposing a quality-diversity tradeoff that single-score benchmarks miss.
articles.contribution: Provides criterion validation showing Precision correlates with GPT-3.5 quality evaluation and Recall correlates with human-like diversity judgments.

articles.title: Fairness in Language Models Beyond English: Gaps and Challenges
articles.tldr: Survey/position paper arguing that dataset-driven fairness measurement is narrowly scoped, unreliable, and cannot be transported or scaled across languages and cultures.
articles.contribution: Reviews how common bias measures misrepresent the fairness construct - e.g. WEAT can be exploited to overestimate bias and 'semantically bleached' templates still carry semantic signal - questioning construct validity of bias scores.

articles.title: Fairness in Language Models Beyond English: Gaps and Challenges
articles.tldr: Survey/position paper arguing that dataset-driven fairness measurement is narrowly scoped, unreliable, and cannot be transported or scaled across languages and cultures.
articles.contribution: Documents data-quality/annotation flaws in crowdsourced fairness benchmarks such as invalid stereotype/anti-stereotype pairs in StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs (per Blodgett et al.).

articles.title: Fairness in Language Models Beyond English: Gaps and Challenges
articles.tldr: Survey/position paper arguing that dataset-driven fairness measurement is narrowly scoped, unreliable, and cannot be transported or scaled across languages and cultures.
articles.contribution: Argues English/Euro-American-centric, dataset-driven fairness evaluation cannot transport or scale across the diversity of world languages and cultures.

articles.title: MedHalu: Hallucinations in Responses to Healthcare Queries by Large Language Models
articles.tldr: MedHalu is a real-world patient-query medical hallucination benchmark showing LLM judges detect hallucinations no better than laypeople and far worse than medical experts.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM judges are unreliable hallucination detectors (GPT-4 macro-F1 ~0.56), performing no better than laypeople and well below medical experts (~0.70).

articles.title: MedHalu: Hallucinations in Responses to Healthcare Queries by Large Language Models
articles.tldr: MedHalu is a real-world patient-query medical hallucination benchmark showing LLM judges detect hallucinations no better than laypeople and far worse than medical experts.
articles.contribution: Argues standardized medical-exam MCQ benchmarks lack ecological validity for real patient interactions and builds a benchmark from ambiguous, real-world consumer healthcare queries.

articles.title: Judge the Judges: A Large-Scale Evaluation Study of Neural Language Models for Online Review Generation
articles.tldr: Large-scale meta-evaluation of NLG evaluators (human, adversarial/discriminative, word-overlap) for review generation, showing adversarial accuracy anti-correlates with human quality judgments.
articles.contribution: Shows discriminative/adversarial evaluators negatively correlate with human generator rankings, so adversarial accuracy misrepresents the review-quality construct while word-overlap (BLEU) tracks humans best.

articles.title: Judge the Judges: A Large-Scale Evaluation Study of Neural Language Models for Online Review Generation
articles.tldr: Large-scale meta-evaluation of NLG evaluators (human, adversarial/discriminative, word-overlap) for review generation, showing adversarial accuracy anti-correlates with human quality judgments.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates discriminative evaluators trained on imperfect 'natural' labels are biased; re-testing against a human majority-vote subset realigns them, exposing ground-truth-quality dependence of the evaluation.

articles.title: CARE: a Benchmark Suite for the Classification and Retrieval of Enzymes
articles.tldr: CARE benchmark suite for enzyme classification and retrieval, with sequence-identity and functional train/test splits designed to measure genuine OOD generalization and to flag data-leakage-inflated scores.
articles.contribution: Designs sequence-identity (<30%, 30-50%) and functional EC-level train/test splits so that reported accuracy validly reflects OOD generalization rather than convenience-split leakage of similar sequences.

articles.title: CARE: a Benchmark Suite for the Classification and Retrieval of Enzymes
articles.tldr: CARE benchmark suite for enzyme classification and retrieval, with sequence-identity and functional train/test splits designed to measure genuine OOD generalization and to flag data-leakage-inflated scores.
articles.contribution: Flags data leakage that inflates retrieval scores (e.g., ChatGPT-with-text) and residual sequence-identity leakage between clustering algorithms, cautioning against contaminated enzyme-function evaluation.

articles.title: T2VPhysBench: A First-Principles Benchmark for Physical Consistency in Text-to-Video Generation
articles.tldr: T2VPhysBench, a first-principles human-scored benchmark showing text-to-video models fail 12 physical laws, and a counterfactual test revealing apparent compliance is surface pattern-matching, not physical understanding.
articles.contribution: Argues pixel-level video metrics misrepresent physical-law adherence, and builds a first-principles human-scored benchmark of twelve laws that better operationalizes the physical-consistency construct.

articles.title: T2VPhysBench: A First-Principles Benchmark for Physical Consistency in Text-to-Video Generation
articles.tldr: T2VPhysBench, a first-principles human-scored benchmark showing text-to-video models fail 12 physical laws, and a counterfactual test revealing apparent compliance is surface pattern-matching, not physical understanding.
articles.contribution: Counterfactual prompts (asking models to violate physics) show standard-prompt success does not transfer, indicating benchmark scores are confounded by surface pattern-matching rather than genuine physical reasoning.

articles.title: Holistic Evaluation for Interleaved Text-and-Image Generation
articles.tldr: InterleavedBench plus InterleavedEval: a benchmark and reference-free GPT-4o multi-aspect LLM-judge for interleaved text-and-image generation that meta-evaluates correlation with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Introduces a reference-free GPT-4o LLM-judge scoring five aspects and meta-evaluates it against human ratings, quantifying where the judge is reliable and where it fails (perceptual quality).

articles.title: Holistic Evaluation for Interleaved Text-and-Image Generation
articles.tldr: InterleavedBench plus InterleavedEval: a benchmark and reference-free GPT-4o multi-aspect LLM-judge for interleaved text-and-image generation that meta-evaluates correlation with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Shows reference-based metrics (BLEU, FID, CLIPScore, DreamSim) barely correlate with human judgment on open-ended interleaved generation, so they misrepresent generation quality and motivate reference-free evaluation.

articles.title: SemScore: Automated Evaluation of Instruction-Tuned LLMs based on Semantic Textual Similarity
articles.tldr: SemScore: meta-evaluation of automatic NLG metrics against human ranking of instruction-tuned LLMs, proposing a semantic-textual-similarity metric that correlates best with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Shows n-gram metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) misrepresent response quality by penalizing valid paraphrases, and proposes SemScore (embedding cosine similarity) which correlates best with human judgment.

articles.title: SemScore: Automated Evaluation of Instruction-Tuned LLMs based on Semantic Textual Similarity
articles.tldr: SemScore: meta-evaluation of automatic NLG metrics against human ranking of instruction-tuned LLMs, proposing a semantic-textual-similarity metric that correlates best with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks a GPT-4 G-Eval LLM-judge among eight metrics and notes its positional bias and proprietary-model reproducibility issues, unlike the transparent SemScore metric.

articles.title: Assessing out-of-domain generalization for robust building damage detection
articles.tldr: IID benchmark scores fail to predict OOD deployment performance for building-damage detection; argues for group-wise OOD evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows IID xView2 benchmark scores fail to predict OOD deployment performance (generalization gap up to 0.30), so real-world evaluation requires OOD test sets.

articles.title: Assessing out-of-domain generalization for robust building damage detection
articles.tldr: IID benchmark scores fail to predict OOD deployment performance for building-damage detection; argues for group-wise OOD evaluation.
articles.contribution: Argues random IID holdout splits of grouped disaster imagery are convenience-sampled and overestimate generalization; proposes group-wise OOD-xBD three-fold splits.

articles.title: Prompting Large Language Models with Knowledge Graphs for Question Answering Involving Long-tail Facts
articles.tldr: Template-free long-tail QA benchmark built to avoid contamination from memorized factual-QA datasets.
articles.contribution: Builds a contamination-resistant, template-free long-tail factual-QA benchmark (LTGen) so memorized test items cannot inflate measured factual-knowledge scores.

articles.title: ResearchCodeBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Implementing Novel Machine Learning Research Code
articles.tldr: Contamination-controlled research-code benchmark using execution tests; even the best LLM passes under 40%.
articles.contribution: Uses repository first-commit dates vs model knowledge-cutoffs to construct a contamination-safe 13-paper subset, isolating memorization from genuine novel-code implementation ability.

articles.title: ResearchCodeBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Implementing Novel Machine Learning Research Code
articles.tldr: Contamination-controlled research-code benchmark using execution tests; even the best LLM passes under 40%.
articles.contribution: Argues deterministic execution-based equivalence and unit tests give more reliable code-correctness scores than LLM-as-judge or string/representation similarity metrics.

articles.title: Fairness Testing of Large Language Models in Role-Playing
articles.tldr: Fairness-testing framework for role-playing LLMs with human-validated oracles and non-determinism analysis.
articles.contribution: Validates an LLM-judge bias oracle against human labels (80.7% agreement), showing it far outperforms the prior rule-based phrase-detection oracle (60.4%).

articles.title: Fairness Testing of Large Language Models in Role-Playing
articles.tldr: Fairness-testing framework for role-playing LLMs with human-validated oracles and non-determinism analysis.
articles.contribution: Validates the LLM-generated 550 roles and 32,864 bias-triggering questions as faithful test inputs (92.8% relevant, 96.4% clear, Cohen's kappa ~0.82).

articles.title: Fairness Testing of Large Language Models in Role-Playing
articles.tldr: Fairness-testing framework for role-playing LLMs with human-validated oracles and non-determinism analysis.
articles.contribution: Handles LLM non-determinism via three-trial majority vote and two-proportion z-tests, quantifying role-effect significance and 79-97% response consistency.

articles.title: EMGBench: Benchmarking Out-of-Distribution Generalization and Adaptation for Electromyography
articles.tldr: First OOD-generalization benchmark for EMG classification, standardizing cross-paper comparison for real-world deployment.
articles.contribution: Introduces the first OOD (intersubject) generalization benchmark for EMG classifiers, arguing in-distribution accuracy is unrealistic for control-interface deployment.

articles.title: EMGBench: Benchmarking Out-of-Distribution Generalization and Adaptation for Electromyography
articles.tldr: First OOD-generalization benchmark for EMG classification, standardizing cross-paper comparison for real-world deployment.
articles.contribution: Standardizes nine EMG datasets and train/test protocols so accuracy results are comparable across papers, addressing the lack of fair open-source benchmarks.

articles.title: Decoding Decoded: Understanding Hyperparameter Effects in Open-Ended Text Generation
articles.tldr: Large-scale decoding-hyperparameter sensitivity study exposing weak correlation between automatic NLG metrics and human judgment.
articles.contribution: Shows automatic text-quality metrics (QText, MAUVE, coherence, diversity) correlate only moderately with human ranking (Pearson r=0.64) and diversity is non-significant.

articles.title: Decoding Decoded: Understanding Hyperparameter Effects in Open-Ended Text Generation
articles.tldr: Large-scale decoding-hyperparameter sensitivity study exposing weak correlation between automatic NLG metrics and human judgment.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates decoding-strategy hyperparameters confound model-quality comparisons as much as model size, so assessing strategies uniformly across models misleads.

articles.title: Data Contamination Calibration for Black-box LLMs
articles.tldr: Membership-inference method (PAC) plus a time-stamped benchmark to detect train/test data contamination in black-box LLMs.
articles.contribution: PAC extends membership-inference with random-swap augmentation and a polarized-distance calibration to detect benchmark contamination in black-box LLMs, beating six baselines by 4.5-5.9% AUC.

articles.title: Data Contamination Calibration for Black-box LLMs
articles.tldr: Membership-inference method (PAC) plus a time-stamped benchmark to detect train/test data contamination in black-box LLMs.
articles.contribution: Introduces StackMIA, a time-stamped, dynamically-updatable member/non-member benchmark so contamination can be reliably tested on newly released post-2023 LLMs where WikiMIA fails.

articles.title: Towards Dataset-Scale and Feature-Oriented Evaluation of Text Summarization in Large Language Model Prompts
articles.tldr: Argues traditional quality metrics and LLM-judges are unreliable for dataset-scale summarization prompt evaluation and proposes interpretable feature metrics instead.
articles.contribution: Argues ROUGE/BERTScore cannot differentiate high-quality LLM summaries and proposes multi-faceted feature metrics as a better realization of the quality construct.

articles.title: Towards Dataset-Scale and Feature-Oriented Evaluation of Text Summarization in Large Language Model Prompts
articles.tldr: Argues traditional quality metrics and LLM-judges are unreliable for dataset-scale summarization prompt evaluation and proposes interpretable feature metrics instead.
articles.contribution: Runs an experiment varying prompt definition levels showing LLM-as-evaluator nondeterminism/variance makes it unreliable for dataset-scale summarization scoring.

articles.title: Back-to-Bones: Rediscovering the Role of Backbones in Domain Generalization
articles.tldr: Shows domain-generalization algorithm gains vanish under fair modern-backbone comparison, exposing a confounded and statistically weak benchmarking practice.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates DG-algorithm gains are confounded by outdated backbones; under fair modern-backbone comparison plain ERM matches or beats DG algorithms.

articles.title: Back-to-Bones: Rediscovering the Role of Backbones in Domain Generalization
articles.tldr: Shows domain-generalization algorithm gains vanish under fair modern-backbone comparison, exposing a confounded and statistically weak benchmarking practice.
articles.contribution: Shows prior DG papers omit multi-run variance and proper model selection; reports mean plus/minus std over 3 seeds with random hyperparameter search.

articles.title: What Makes a Good Story and How Can We Measure It? A Comprehensive Survey of Story Evaluation
articles.tldr: Comprehensive survey of story evaluation mapping construct definitions and metric-human correlation across traditional and LLM-based approaches.
articles.contribution: Surveys and standardizes story-evaluation criteria and their definitions to combat the long-standing vague, inconsistent construct problem.

articles.title: What Makes a Good Story and How Can We Measure It? A Comprehensive Survey of Story Evaluation
articles.tldr: Comprehensive survey of story evaluation mapping construct definitions and metric-human correlation across traditional and LLM-based approaches.
articles.contribution: Taxonomizes and meta-evaluates traditional and LLM-based metrics, noting low human correlation of lexical metrics and the limits of LLM-based ones.

articles.title: Benchmarking Music Generation Models and Metrics via Human Preference Studies
articles.tldr: Benchmarks music-generation metrics against a large human-preference study, finding which objective metrics best correlate with human quality perception.
articles.contribution: Empirically tests which objective music metrics (FAD/CLAP variants) actually capture human-perceived quality and text-audio alignment.

articles.title: Benchmarking Music Generation Models and Metrics via Human Preference Studies
articles.tldr: Benchmarks music-generation metrics against a large human-preference study, finding which objective metrics best correlate with human quality perception.
articles.contribution: Builds a large-scale human-preference gold standard by aggregating 15.6k pairwise judgments via Elo/Bradley-Terry with attention checks.

articles.title: Counterfactual (Non-)identifiability of Learned Structural Causal Models
articles.tldr: Warns that counterfactual predictions from learned deep structural causal models are non-identifiable and offers a worst-case error diagnostic.
articles.contribution: Proves counterfactual inference from learned SCMs is non-identifiable even without unobserved confounding and with known structure, since observational fit is a surface proxy for the true mechanism.

articles.title: Counterfactual (Non-)identifiability of Learned Structural Causal Models
articles.tldr: Warns that counterfactual predictions from learned deep structural causal models are non-identifiable and offers a worst-case error diagnostic.
articles.contribution: Proposes a worst-case counterfactual-error estimator as a validity diagnostic for deciding whether a learned DSCM is trustworthy in a given setting.

articles.title: Plot-guided Adversarial Example Construction for Evaluating Open-domain Story Generation
articles.tldr: Improves learnable story-generation evaluation metrics by constructing plot-guided adversarial negatives that better reflect real machine-generated implausibility.
articles.contribution: Shows learnable story-evaluation metrics trained on plot-guided adversarial negatives correlate far better with human judgment than heuristic-data baselines.

articles.title: Plot-guided Adversarial Example Construction for Evaluating Open-domain Story Generation
articles.tldr: Improves learnable story-generation evaluation metrics by constructing plot-guided adversarial negatives that better reflect real machine-generated implausibility.
articles.contribution: Identifies that heuristic negative examples inject unnatural surface/stylistic shortcuts; adversarial filtering removes them so the metric learns genuine implausibility.

articles.title: LMLPA: Language Model Linguistic Personality Assessment
articles.tldr: Develops a validated open-ended linguistic-personality assessment for LLMs, arguing human self-report questionnaires are invalid and unreliable for machines.
articles.contribution: Argues human personality psychometrics misrepresent LLMs (which lack emotions) and defines an AI-native linguistic-personality construct via an adapted Big Five Inventory.

articles.title: LMLPA: Language Model Linguistic Personality Assessment
articles.tldr: Develops a validated open-ended linguistic-personality assessment for LLMs, arguing human self-report questionnaires are invalid and unreliable for machines.
articles.contribution: Shows MCQ self-report items leak option-order cues, giving statistically inconsistent personality scores, and redesigns the items as open-ended.

articles.title: LMLPA: Language Model Linguistic Personality Assessment
articles.tldr: Develops a validated open-ended linguistic-personality assessment for LLMs, arguing human self-report questionnaires are invalid and unreliable for machines.
articles.contribution: Builds an AI rater to score open-ended answers, validated with inter-item correlation, intra-class correlation, and PCA reliability/validity tests.

articles.title: Is LLM an Overconfident Judge? Unveiling the Capabilities of LLMs in Detecting Offensive Language with Annotation Disagreement
articles.tldr: Shows LLM judges are overconfident on ambiguous offensive-language cases and misalign with human annotation disagreement.
articles.contribution: Uses 5-annotator soft labels to show the binary-consensus assumption oversimplifies the inherently subjective offensive-language construct.

articles.title: Is LLM an Overconfident Judge? Unveiling the Capabilities of LLMs in Detecting Offensive Language with Annotation Disagreement
articles.tldr: Shows LLM judges are overconfident on ambiguous offensive-language cases and misalign with human annotation disagreement.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM judges are overconfident and miscalibrated on low-agreement offensive-language cases, failing to reflect human uncertainty.

articles.title: Human-Activity AGV Quality Assessment: A Benchmark Dataset and an Objective Evaluation Metric
articles.tldr: Human-AGVQA subjective dataset (6,000 AI-generated human-activity videos, 80-subject MOS) shows existing quality metrics correlate poorly with human perception; proposed GHVQ reaches SRCC 0.805.
articles.contribution: Shows existing IQA/AQA/VQA metrics capture human-perceived AGV quality poorly, with zero-shot SRCC only ~0.22-0.37 against human MOS.

articles.title: Human-Activity AGV Quality Assessment: A Benchmark Dataset and an Objective Evaluation Metric
articles.tldr: Human-AGVQA subjective dataset (6,000 AI-generated human-activity videos, 80-subject MOS) shows existing quality metrics correlate poorly with human perception; proposed GHVQ reaches SRCC 0.805.
articles.contribution: Builds the human MOS ground truth (80 subjects rating appearance/action/overall, 5 experts labeling body-part semantic issues) that serves as the quality benchmark.

articles.title: Do Natural Language Explanations Represent Valid Logical Arguments? Verifying Entailment in Explainable NLI Gold Standards
articles.tldr: Proposes Explanation Entailment Verification (EEV) to quantify logical validity of human-annotated NLI explanation gold standards, finding 57.66% represent logically invalid arguments.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that the human-annotated explanations used as ground truth are mostly logically invalid, so the gold standard misrepresents the 'valid explanation' construct.

articles.title: Do Natural Language Explanations Represent Valid Logical Arguments? Verifying Entailment in Explainable NLI Gold Standards
articles.tldr: Proposes Explanation Entailment Verification (EEV) to quantify logical validity of human-annotated NLI explanation gold standards, finding 57.66% represent logically invalid arguments.
articles.contribution: Argues the inferential properties of explanations are poorly formalised, i.e. the construct of a valid explanation was never theory-grounded before the gold standards were built.

articles.title: Automatic Generation and Evaluation of Reading Comprehension Test Items with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces 'text informativity' (answerability minus guessability) to evaluate multiple-choice reading-comprehension items and shows GPT-4 as an automatic evaluator matches human annotators.
articles.contribution: Validates GPT-4 as an item evaluator whose response agreement with humans (Cohen's kappa 0.724) exceeds human-human agreement (0.683), while Llama-2 is unreliable.

articles.title: Automatic Generation and Evaluation of Reading Comprehension Test Items with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Introduces 'text informativity' (answerability minus guessability) to evaluate multiple-choice reading-comprehension items and shows GPT-4 as an automatic evaluator matches human annotators.
articles.contribution: Defines text informativity to detect items answerable from world knowledge alone (guessable shortcut), i.e. items that fail to measure comprehension.

articles.title: A Study on Agreement in PICO Span Annotations
articles.tldr: Studies inter-annotator agreement of PICO span annotations in EBM-PICO; exact-span F1 is very low (<0.1 for I/O) but relaxed token-overlap agreement is high, so exact metrics underestimate agreement.
articles.contribution: Quantifies that human PICO span annotations have very low exact-boundary agreement even among medical experts, revealing unreliable ground-truth span boundaries.

articles.title: A Study on Agreement in PICO Span Annotations
articles.tldr: Studies inter-annotator agreement of PICO span annotations in EBM-PICO; exact-span F1 is very low (<0.1 for I/O) but relaxed token-overlap agreement is high, so exact metrics underestimate agreement.
articles.contribution: Shows the exact-span F1 scorer undermines apparent agreement and argues relaxed one-side-boundary and token-overlap agreements are needed for valid PICO span evaluation.

articles.title: Insect Identification in the Wild: The AMI Dataset
articles.tldr: AMI benchmark tests out-of-distribution generalization from curated human photos (AMI-GBIF, 2.5M images) to in-the-wild insect camera-trap images (AMI-Traps), where fine-grained accuracy drops sharply.
articles.contribution: Measures the OOD gap: fine-grained species accuracy falls from ~90% in-distribution on AMI-GBIF to ~72-77% on real camera-trap images, exposing weak external validity of curated-photo training.

articles.title: Insect Identification in the Wild: The AMI Dataset
articles.tldr: AMI benchmark tests out-of-distribution generalization from curated human photos (AMI-GBIF, 2.5M images) to in-the-wild insect camera-trap images (AMI-Traps), where fine-grained accuracy drops sharply.
articles.contribution: Builds an expert-entomologist-annotated in-the-wild test set (2,893 trap images, 52,948 labeled insects) to evaluate realistic field deployment instead of convenience-sampled photos.

articles.title: One-Step Weighting to Generalize and Transport Treatment Effect Estimates to a Target Population
articles.tldr: Proposes one-step balancing weights to generalize/transport treatment-effect estimates to a target population, giving more stable estimators than multiplicative two-step weights (86%/70% RMSE reduction).
articles.contribution: Provides a one-step weighting method to transport/generalize treatment-effect estimates from a study sample to a target population under covariate distribution shift, needing only target summary statistics.

articles.title: One-Step Weighting to Generalize and Transport Treatment Effect Estimates to a Target Population
articles.tldr: Proposes one-step balancing weights to generalize/transport treatment-effect estimates to a target population, giving more stable estimators than multiplicative two-step weights (86%/70% RMSE reduction).
articles.contribution: Shows multiplicative two-step weights produce highly variable/extreme weights and unstable estimators, whereas the one-step estimator is consistent, asymptotically Normal, multiply robust and semiparametrically efficient.

articles.title: HalluVerse25: Fine-grained Multilingual Benchmark Dataset for LLM Hallucinations
articles.tldr: HalluVerse25 is a fine-grained multilingual (English/Arabic/Turkish) LLM-hallucination dataset built by LLM injection plus human annotation, used to benchmark LLM hallucination detectors.
articles.contribution: Uses a rigorous two-annotator human validation (Cohen's kappa up to 0.805) to verify the LLM-injected fine-grained hallucination labels serving as ground truth.

articles.title: HalluVerse25: Fine-grained Multilingual Benchmark Dataset for LLM Hallucinations
articles.tldr: HalluVerse25 is a fine-grained multilingual (English/Arabic/Turkish) LLM-hallucination dataset built by LLM injection plus human annotation, used to benchmark LLM hallucination detectors.
articles.contribution: Extends hallucination benchmarks beyond English to Arabic and Turkish, exposing cross-language detector gaps, though the Wikipedia biographical source is acknowledged as unrepresentative.

articles.title: HalluVerse25: Fine-grained Multilingual Benchmark Dataset for LLM Hallucinations
articles.tldr: HalluVerse25 is a fine-grained multilingual (English/Arabic/Turkish) LLM-hallucination dataset built by LLM injection plus human annotation, used to benchmark LLM hallucination detectors.
articles.contribution: Notes GPT-4o's top detection scores are confounded by GPT-4o also being the model that generated the hallucinated data.

articles.title: JALMBench: Benchmarking Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Audio Language Models
articles.tldr: Audio-LM jailbreak safety benchmark (11k text, 245k audio) with a human-validated GPT-4o attack-success judge; safety depends strongly on modality and architecture.
articles.contribution: Validates the GPT-4o attack-success judge on three axes: repeatability under greedy/sampling decoding, cross-model consistency with alternative judges, and human agreement with only a 1.7% false-positive rate.

articles.title: JALMBench: Benchmarking Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Audio Language Models
articles.tldr: Audio-LM jailbreak safety benchmark (11k text, 245k audio) with a human-validated GPT-4o attack-success judge; safety depends strongly on modality and architecture.
articles.contribution: Assembles broad adversarial coverage (12 LALMs, 8 attacks, 5 defenses, 245k audio samples across 7 topic categories) to counter narrow convenience sampling in audio-safety evaluation.

articles.title: CTBENCH: A Library and Benchmark for Certified Training
articles.tldr: Unified library and benchmark for certified training under fair schedules, a common verifier and tuned hyperparameters; recent algorithms' claimed advantages shrink drastically under fair comparison.
articles.contribution: Removes the unfair-comparison confound in certified-training claims by evaluating all algorithms with the same MN-BaB verifier, training schedule and systematically tuned hyperparameters.

articles.title: CTBENCH: A Library and Benchmark for Certified Training
articles.tldr: Unified library and benchmark for certified training under fair schedules, a common verifier and tuned hyperparameters; recent algorithms' claimed advantages shrink drastically under fair comparison.
articles.contribution: Provides a single reproducible codebase and checkpoints that re-establish SOTA, exposing that literature comparisons via quoted numbers under differing verifiers were unreliable.

articles.title: Episodic Memories Generation and Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Cognitive-science-grounded, contamination-free synthetic benchmark for LLM episodic memory; even GPT-4o, Claude, o1-mini struggle with multi-event spatio-temporal recall.
articles.contribution: Grounds the episodic-memory construct in cognitive science (Tulving, hippocampal spatio-temporal indexing), structuring events with temporal, spatial and entity contexts before building the measure.

articles.title: Episodic Memories Generation and Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Cognitive-science-grounded, contamination-free synthetic benchmark for LLM episodic memory; even GPT-4o, Claude, o1-mini struggle with multi-event spatio-temporal recall.
articles.contribution: Synthesizes contamination-free books with uniqueness constraints on time-space/time-entity pairs and multi-step verification, avoiding the uncontrolled ground truth and leakage of real-book benchmarks.

articles.title: SESCORE2: Learning Text Generation Evaluation via Synthesizing Realistic Mistakes
articles.tldr: Self-supervised reference-based NLG evaluation metric trained on retrieval-augmented synthetic mistakes; correlates with human MQM judgments better than unsupervised metrics and rivals supervised BLEURT/COMET.
articles.contribution: Builds a model-based quality metric whose severity-graded score aligns with human MQM judgments, better capturing generation quality than surface n-gram metrics like BLEU/chrF.

articles.title: SESCORE2: Learning Text Generation Evaluation via Synthesizing Realistic Mistakes
articles.tldr: Self-supervised reference-based NLG evaluation metric trained on retrieval-augmented synthetic mistakes; correlates with human MQM judgments better than unsupervised metrics and rivals supervised BLEURT/COMET.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates cross-domain external validity: the metric keeps the smallest News->TED correlation gap among learned metrics, and warns that human-rating fine-tuning overfits the training domain.

articles.title: Brittlebench: Quantifying LLM robustness via prompt sensitivity
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation framework quantifying LLM prompt brittleness via variance decomposition; semantics-preserving perturbations degrade accuracy up to 12% and flip model rankings in 63% of cases.
articles.contribution: A unified taxonomy of semantics-preserving perturbations exposes that static-benchmark scores conflate ability with surface-form robustness, degrading accuracy by up to 12% from format artifacts.

articles.title: Brittlebench: Quantifying LLM robustness via prompt sensitivity
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation framework quantifying LLM prompt brittleness via variance decomposition; semantics-preserving perturbations degrade accuracy up to 12% and flip model rankings in 63% of cases.
articles.contribution: Shows leaderboard comparisons are unstable: a single perturbation flips the relative ranking of six models in 63% of cases (Spearman rank correlation as low as 0.63).

articles.title: Brittlebench: Quantifying LLM robustness via prompt sensitivity
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation framework quantifying LLM prompt brittleness via variance decomposition; semantics-preserving perturbations degrade accuracy up to 12% and flip model rankings in 63% of cases.
articles.contribution: Benchmark-level brittleness scores reveal saturation: MMLU and GPQA now separate models mainly by perturbation robustness (over half of variance), masking semantic competence.

articles.title: Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors in Language Models
articles.tldr: Unsupervised weight-space elicitation (CPE) surfaces hidden behaviors including sandbagging and reward hacking, recovering 77-85% of password-locked capability from a single example.
articles.contribution: Reveals sandbagging as an eval-validity threat by restoring 77-85% of a password-locked Llama3-70B's BigCodeBench pass rate, uncovering hidden capability that naive evaluations miss.

articles.title: Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors in Language Models
articles.tldr: Unsupervised weight-space elicitation (CPE) surfaces hidden behaviors including sandbagging and reward hacking, recovering 77-85% of password-locked capability from a single example.
articles.contribution: Shows CPE-initialized GRPO on GPT-OSS-20B stays in an aligned basin whereas random initialization collapses into reward hacking and a drop in gold-standard reward tracked by a monitor judge.

articles.title: Diversity vs. Recognizability: Human-like generalization in one-shot generative models
articles.tldr: Argues FID/IS/likelihood are biased for one-shot generation and proposes a human-psychophysics-grounded diversity-vs-recognizability framework to evaluate one-shot generative models.
articles.contribution: Grounds one-shot generation quality in two human-derived axes (sample diversity and recognizability) from psychophysics, since FID/IS/likelihood are biased in the novel-concept one-shot regime.

articles.title: Diversity vs. Recognizability: Human-like generalization in one-shot generative models
articles.tldr: Argues FID/IS/likelihood are biased for one-shot generation and proposes a human-psychophysics-grounded diversity-vs-recognizability framework to evaluate one-shot generative models.
articles.contribution: Measures recognizability via a classifier and diversity as intra-class variability, disentangling quality dimensions that FID conflates and separating GAN-like from VAE-like models.

articles.title: Is PRM Necessary? Problem-Solving RL Implicitly Induces PRM Capability in LLMs
articles.tldr: Shows RL-trained models are strong process judges while existing PRMs underperform majority voting, and Self-PRM has low precision on hard problems.
articles.contribution: Empirically shows discriminative PRMs are unreliable scorers of reasoning-step correctness, being surpassed by RL-trained models prompted as generative PRMs.

articles.title: Is PRM Necessary? Problem-Solving RL Implicitly Induces PRM Capability in LLMs
articles.tldr: Shows RL-trained models are strong process judges while existing PRMs underperform majority voting, and Self-PRM has low precision on hard problems.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates PRM and Self-PRM reranking fails to beat the trivial majority-voting baseline on frontier models, a fair-baseline check on best-of-N aggregation.

articles.title: RES-Q: Evaluating Code-Editing Large Language Model Systems at the Repository Scale
articles.tldr: Repository-scale code-editing benchmark from real GitHub commits that resists saturation and contamination better than HumanEval/MMLU.
articles.contribution: Provides a harder repo-scale editing task that keeps discriminating models as saturated benchmarks like HumanEval lose resolving power.

articles.title: RES-Q: Evaluating Code-Editing Large Language Model Systems at the Repository Scale
articles.tldr: Repository-scale code-editing benchmark from real GitHub commits that resists saturation and contamination better than HumanEval/MMLU.
articles.contribution: Reduces train/test contamination by avoiding raw GitHub instruction text and pinning forked repositories at fixed commits.

articles.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models in Scientific Document Reasoning
articles.tldr: Finds retrieval-augmented LLMs reach high task accuracy while justifying answers with fabricated, irrelevant retrieved evidence.
articles.contribution: Shows high task accuracy does not warrant the inference that answers are evidence-grounded, since retrieved passages are unrelated to the answered query.

articles.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models in Scientific Document Reasoning
articles.tldr: Finds retrieval-augmented LLMs reach high task accuracy while justifying answers with fabricated, irrelevant retrieved evidence.
articles.contribution: Introduces relevance and diversity metrics for retrieved evidence, exposing that accuracy alone misses evidence fabrication.

articles.title: BioKGBench: A Knowledge Graph Checking Benchmark of AI Agent for Biomedical Science
articles.tldr: Benchmark decomposing literature understanding into claim verification and KGQA that also uncovers factual errors in a widely-used biomedical knowledge graph.
articles.contribution: Decomposes the vague 'understanding literature' construct into measurable atomic abilities (scientific claim verification and KG question-answering) to avoid hallucination-prone factual QA.

articles.title: BioKGBench: A Knowledge Graph Checking Benchmark of AI Agent for Biomedical Science
articles.tldr: Benchmark decomposing literature understanding into claim verification and KGQA that also uncovers factual errors in a widely-used biomedical knowledge graph.
articles.contribution: The KGCheck task discovers 90+ factual errors in a widely-used biomedical knowledge graph treated as ground truth, exposing ground-truth quality problems.

articles.title: FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning
articles.tldr: Contamination-free symbolic benchmark for verifiable chain-of-thought financial reasoning with a step-level ChainEval measure.
articles.contribution: Parameterized symbolic templates with executable Python enable scalable contamination-free generation of fresh reasoning problems.

articles.title: FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning
articles.tldr: Contamination-free symbolic benchmark for verifiable chain-of-thought financial reasoning with a step-level ChainEval measure.
articles.contribution: ChainEval jointly scores step-level reasoning consistency and final-answer correctness, exposing that final-answer-only metrics mask flawed intermediate reasoning.

articles.title: Perception Score, A Learned Metric for Open-ended Text Generation Evaluation
articles.tldr: A learned NLG evaluation metric that scores holistic quality with uncertainty and correlates better with human judgment than BLEU/BERTScore.
articles.contribution: Learns a holistic quality metric that transcends surface n-gram/semantic overlap and correlates far better with human judgment for open-ended generation.

articles.title: Perception Score, A Learned Metric for Open-ended Text Generation Evaluation
articles.tldr: A learned NLG evaluation metric that scores holistic quality with uncertainty and correlates better with human judgment than BLEU/BERTScore.
articles.contribution: Estimates per-item data and model (dropout-variance) uncertainty and reweights confident scores for a more reliable system-level metric.

articles.title: Promptception: How Sensitive Are Large Multimodal Models to Prompts?
articles.tldr: Systematic study showing minor prompt phrasing changes swing LMM MCQA accuracy up to 15%, undermining transparent and fair evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows prompt phrasing/structure acts as a nuisance factor causing up to 15% accuracy swings, confounding the intended capability measurement.

articles.title: Promptception: How Sensitive Are Large Multimodal Models to Prompts?
articles.tldr: Systematic study showing minor prompt phrasing changes swing LMM MCQA accuracy up to 15%, undermining transparent and fair evaluation.
articles.contribution: Exposes best-case prompt cherry-picking as an unfair comparison practice and proposes standardized Prompting Principles for robust evaluation.

articles.title: Tasting the cake: evaluating self-supervised generalization on out-of-distribution multimodal MRI data
articles.tldr: Shows self-supervised models are far less OOD-robust on medical MRI than natural-image benchmarks suggest, motivating OOD evaluation standards.
articles.contribution: Shows natural-image benchmark results overestimate self-supervised OOD robustness on medical MRI, arguing downstream performance parity does not imply robust generalization.

articles.title: Tasting the cake: evaluating self-supervised generalization on out-of-distribution multimodal MRI data
articles.tldr: Shows self-supervised models are far less OOD-robust on medical MRI than natural-image benchmarks suggest, motivating OOD evaluation standards.
articles.contribution: Finds distortions drive models to exploit trivial shortcut biomarkers (e.g., reduced ventricle size), a spurious feature confounding the measured capability.

articles.title: Stellar: Systematic Evaluation of Human-Centric Personalized Text-to-Image Methods
articles.tldr: Standardized personalized text-to-image benchmark with specialized metrics that correlate better with human judgment and resist metric exploitation.
articles.contribution: Introduces identity/attribute/object/relation metrics (IPS/APS/SIS/GOA/RFS) that capture personalization properties subject-agnostic CLIP/FID miss.

articles.title: Stellar: Systematic Evaluation of Human-Centric Personalized Text-to-Image Methods
articles.tldr: Standardized personalized text-to-image benchmark with specialized metrics that correlate better with human judgment and resist metric exploitation.
articles.contribution: Identifies image-to-image metric exploitation (copying the input scores perfectly) and adds a prompt-similarity penalty to block the loophole.

articles.title: Sycophancy in vision-language models: A systematic analysis and an inference-time mitigation framework
articles.tldr: Systematic analysis showing leading/deceptive prompts (sycophancy) break LVLM visual grounding, exposing that neutral-query hallucination benchmarks under-measure prompt robustness.
articles.contribution: Shows leading/deceptive prompt clauses act as a linguistic confound that overrides visual evidence, collapsing POPE accuracy by 12-42% and F1 by 15-88% across five LVLMs.

articles.title: Sycophancy in vision-language models: A systematic analysis and an inference-time mitigation framework
articles.tldr: Systematic analysis showing leading/deceptive prompts (sycophancy) break LVLM visual grounding, exposing that neutral-query hallucination benchmarks under-measure prompt robustness.
articles.contribution: Argues existing hallucination benchmarks convenience-sample only neutral queries and thus fail to cover realistic biased-prompt conditions; extends five datasets with curated leading queries.

articles.title: Uncovering Systematic Failures of LLMs in Verifying Code Against Natural Language Specifications
articles.tldr: Uncovers that LLM code-review judges systematically misjudge correct code as non-conforming, and that more elaborate explanation/fix prompting worsens the judge's reliability.
articles.contribution: Quantifies that LLMs judging code-to-spec conformance without test cases achieve only 52-78% requirement-conformance recognition, exhibiting an over-correction bias toward false negatives.

articles.title: Uncovering Systematic Failures of LLMs in Verifying Code Against Natural Language Specifications
articles.tldr: Uncovers that LLM code-review judges systematically misjudge correct code as non-conforming, and that more elaborate explanation/fix prompting worsens the judge's reliability.
articles.contribution: Shows the prompting protocol itself confounds the judge: adding explanation and fix steps counterintuitively lowers RCRR by ~20-40 points, and proposes contract/behavioral-comparison prompts to recover accuracy.

articles.title: From Blind Solvers to Logical Thinkers: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Integrity on Faulty Mathematical Problems
articles.tldr: FaultyMath benchmark of unsolvable/flawed math problems probes whether accuracy is a surface proxy that hides lack of logical integrity, and validates an LLM auto-evaluator against a PhD gold standard.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes faulty math problems (common-sense violations, contradictions, ambiguity) to show standard solve-accuracy is a surface proxy: LLMs act as 'Blind Solvers', computing answers to unsolvable problems instead of detecting flaws.

articles.title: From Blind Solvers to Logical Thinkers: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Integrity on Faulty Mathematical Problems
articles.tldr: FaultyMath benchmark of unsolvable/flawed math problems probes whether accuracy is a surface proxy that hides lack of logical integrity, and validates an LLM auto-evaluator against a PhD gold standard.
articles.contribution: Calibrates an LLM auto-evaluator against a two-PhD-reviewer gold standard (17.36% human-identified rate), selecting GPT-4 Simple Prompt (Acc 88.15%, F1 80.44%) after showing CoT/explanation prompts diverge from human judgment.

articles.title: Is This a Bad Table? A Closer Look at the Evaluation of Table Generation from Text
articles.tldr: Shows existing text-to-table metrics (exact-match, BertScore) misrepresent table quality by scoring cells independently, and proposes TabEval (LLM unrolling + NLI entailment) that better correlates with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates cell/tuple-independent metrics fail to capture table semantics, unfairly rewarding bad tables and penalizing good ones (Tables B and D score ~100% BertScore precision/recall despite wrong values).

articles.title: Is This a Bad Table? A Closer Look at the Evaluation of Table Generation from Text
articles.tldr: Shows existing text-to-table metrics (exact-match, BertScore) misrepresent table quality by scoring cells independently, and proposes TabEval (LLM unrolling + NLI entailment) that better correlates with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Introduces TabEval, unrolling tables into atomic NL statements via CoT prompting then scoring with RoBERTa-MNLI entailment; validates the unrolling step (correctness 4.67/5, coverage 4.87/5, 97.3% atomic).

articles.title: Neuro-Symbolic Evaluation of Text-to-Video Models using Formal Verification
articles.tldr: NeuS-V is a neuro-symbolic text-to-video metric using temporal-logic specifications and formal verification, arguing existing metrics misrepresent temporal fidelity and achieving 5x higher human correlation.
articles.contribution: Argues existing T2V metrics emphasize visual quality/smoothness and neglect temporal fidelity and text-to-video alignment; NeuS-V converts prompts to temporal-logic specs and formally verifies a video automaton against them.

articles.title: Neuro-Symbolic Evaluation of Text-to-Video Models using Formal Verification
articles.tldr: NeuS-V is a neuro-symbolic text-to-video metric using temporal-logic specifications and formal verification, arguing existing metrics misrepresent temporal fidelity and achieving 5x higher human correlation.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory/falsification evidence via an ablation that replaces the temporal-logic + model-checking components with VLM-only yes/no scoring, showing formal grounding is necessary for the metric's human alignment.

articles.title: IE-Bench: Advancing the Measurement of Text-Driven Image Editing for Human Perception Alignment
articles.tldr: IE-Bench builds the first human-MOS IQA dataset for text-driven image editing and IE-QA, showing single-perspective objective metrics (CLIP/SSIM) fail to model the source-target relationship and human perception.
articles.contribution: Shows CLIP/DINO/LPIPS/SSIM each evaluate editing from a single dimension (text-image OR source-target) and fail to capture overall quality, so IE-QA jointly models image-text alignment, source-target fidelity, and visual quality.

articles.title: IE-Bench: Advancing the Measurement of Text-Driven Image Editing for Human Perception Alignment
articles.tldr: IE-Bench builds the first human-MOS IQA dataset for text-driven image editing and IE-QA, showing single-perspective objective metrics (CLIP/SSIM) fail to model the source-target relationship and human perception.
articles.contribution: Collects 3,010 MOS from 25 human subjects (ITU standard, Z-score normalization, BT.500 outlier filtering) as ground truth and shows IE-QA reaches SROCC 0.752 versus 0.12-0.21 for objective metrics.

articles.title: Re:Form - Reducing Human Priors in Scalable Formal Software Verification with RL in LLMs: A Preliminary Study on Dafny
articles.tldr: Re:Form trains LLMs to produce verifiable Dafny specs with RL from a formal verifier, and analyzes reward hacking of the verification signal plus rules out contamination as the source of gains.
articles.contribution: Documents reward hacking of the formal-verifier reward: training on verification reward alone yields high verification rates but overly weak specifications easily accepted by the verifier, motivating an added spec-superiority reward.
