articles.title: Re:Form - Reducing Human Priors in Scalable Formal Software Verification with RL in LLMs: A Preliminary Study on Dafny
articles.tldr: Re:Form trains LLMs to produce verifiable Dafny specs with RL from a formal verifier, and analyzes reward hacking of the verification signal plus rules out contamination as the source of gains.
articles.contribution: Explicitly rules out data contamination as the explanation for RL gains (fully synthetic data, negligible public Dafny specs, and uniformly poor proprietary/base-model performance) before attributing improvements to genuine learning.

articles.title: Gravity-Bench-v1: A Benchmark on Gravitational Physics Discovery for Agents
articles.tldr: Gravity-Bench-v1 is an environment-based scientific-discovery benchmark using out-of-distribution physics to test genuine generalization (guarding against memorization) and exposing agent shortcut/harness confounds.
articles.contribution: Designs out-of-distribution physics (modified gravity F proportional to r^-(2+alpha), drag) unlikely in pretraining data to test true scientific generalization rather than memorized textbook knowledge; only o1 and Claude solve some OOD tasks.

articles.title: Gravity-Bench-v1: A Benchmark on Gravitational Physics Discovery for Agents
articles.tldr: Gravity-Bench-v1 is an environment-based scientific-discovery benchmark using out-of-distribution physics to test genuine generalization (guarding against memorization) and exposing agent shortcut/harness confounds.
articles.contribution: Reveals harness/planning confounds and shortcut behaviors: agents drastically under-use the 100-observation budget (GPT-4o ~12) and take shortcuts like assuming stellar mass=1 ('science hallucination') that correlate strongly with wrong answers.

articles.title: $OneMillion-Bench: How Far are Language Agents from Human Experts?
articles.tldr: OneMillion-Bench: 400 expert-curated professional agent tasks with rubric grading, plus LM-judge sensitivity and ecological-validity analysis.
articles.contribution: Multi-judge sensitivity analysis: agent rankings stay stable but absolute scores vary with judge strictness, urging judge-identity reporting and multi-judge grading.

articles.title: $OneMillion-Bench: How Far are Language Agents from Human Experts?
articles.tldr: OneMillion-Bench: 400 expert-curated professional agent tasks with rubric grading, plus LM-judge sensitivity and ecological-validity analysis.
articles.contribution: Reality-grounded, wage-anchored professional-deliverable tasks test external validity beyond saturated exam-style benchmarks.

articles.title: DefAn: Definitive Answer Dataset for LLMs Hallucination Evaluation
articles.tldr: DefAn: 75k definitive-answer prompts across eight domains with automated exact-match scoring of factual and prompt-misalignment hallucination plus consistency.
articles.contribution: Definitive-answer QA design so generative hallucination is exact-match scorable, avoiding MCQ guessing artifacts that hide true generative failure.

articles.title: DefAn: Definitive Answer Dataset for LLMs Hallucination Evaluation
articles.tldr: DefAn: 75k definitive-answer prompts across eight domains with automated exact-match scoring of factual and prompt-misalignment hallucination plus consistency.
articles.contribution: Held-out hidden benchmark segment guards integrity against contamination-inflated scores from training familiarity.

articles.title: DefAn: Definitive Answer Dataset for LLMs Hallucination Evaluation
articles.tldr: DefAn: 75k definitive-answer prompts across eight domains with automated exact-match scoring of factual and prompt-misalignment hallucination plus consistency.
articles.contribution: Response-Consistency metric over 15 paraphrases quantifies measurement reliability across prompt rewordings.

articles.title: FaceScore: Benchmarking and Enhancing Face Quality in Human Generation
articles.tldr: FaceScore: a face-quality reward metric plus a human-preference benchmark showing existing image metrics align poorly with human face judgments.
articles.contribution: Shows global image-preference metrics mis-measure face quality, and builds a face-specific metric with markedly higher human-preference alignment.

articles.title: Beyond Next Token Probabilities: Learnable, Fast Detection of Hallucinations and Data Contamination on LLM Output Distributions
articles.tldr: LOS-Net: attention model over full next-token distribution sequences that detects both hallucinations and training-data contamination in gray-box LLMs.
articles.contribution: Learnable hallucination detector over the full output-distribution signature, improving reliability of black-box honesty measurement.

articles.title: Beyond Next Token Probabilities: Learnable, Fast Detection of Hallucinations and Data Contamination on LLM Output Distributions
articles.tldr: LOS-Net: attention model over full next-token distribution sequences that detects both hallucinations and training-data contamination in gray-box LLMs.
articles.contribution: Same LLM Output Signature detects train/test data contamination and copyright leakage across models.

articles.title: Trustworthy AI for Medicine: Continuous Hallucination Detection and Elimination with CHECK
articles.tldr: CHECK: an information-theoretic hallucination classifier plus continuous-learning framework detecting factual and reasoning hallucinations in clinical LLMs.
articles.contribution: Information-theoretic classifier reliably scores factual and reasoning hallucinations (AUC 0.95-0.96) as an honesty-measurement instrument.

articles.title: Linguistics Theory Meets LLM: Code-Switched Text Generation via Equivalence Constrained Large Language Models
articles.tldr: EZSwitch generates code-switched text via Equivalence Constraint Theory and studies how automatic metrics correlate with human fluency/accuracy judgments.
articles.contribution: Correlation study showing automatic metrics under-capture code-switch fluency, questioning them as valid proxies for human judgment.

articles.title: On the Usefulness of Embeddings, Clusters and Strings for Text Generator Evaluation
articles.tldr: Analysis showing the Mauve NLG metric succeeds not from its new divergence but from embedding-cluster substitution encoding coherence features.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates the metric's validity stems from embedding-cluster features rather than the claimed information-theoretic divergence.

articles.title: Democratic or Authoritarian? Probing a New Dimension of Political Biases in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Measures LLM democracy-authoritarianism bias via the F-scale psychometric instrument, a new FavScore metric, and role-model probing, with prompt-robustness and judge-bias checks.
articles.contribution: Grounds an 'authoritarian bias' construct in the Adorno F-scale psychometric instrument and a survey-adapted FavScore, extending LLM bias measurement beyond the usual left-right axis to the orthogonal democracy-authoritarianism dimension.

articles.title: Democratic or Authoritarian? Probing a New Dimension of Political Biases in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Measures LLM democracy-authoritarianism bias via the F-scale psychometric instrument, a new FavScore metric, and role-model probing, with prompt-robustness and judge-bias checks.
articles.contribution: Runs an explicit LLM-as-judge bias study for the political-classification, regime-determination and refusal judges that score model outputs, probing scorer bias in the measurement pipeline.

articles.title: SER Evals: In-domain and Out-of-domain Benchmarking for Speech Emotion Recognition
articles.tldr: Cross-lingual speech-emotion-recognition benchmark stressing in-domain vs out-of-domain generalization, using logit adjustment and macro-F1 for fair cross-dataset comparison.
articles.contribution: Argues existing SER benchmarks over-emphasize in-domain evaluation on a few well-studied corpora; builds a 19-dataset multilingual OOD benchmark where OOD macro-F1 (~0.19) collapses far below in-domain (~0.78), exposing weak external validity of SER results.

articles.title: SER Evals: In-domain and Out-of-domain Benchmarking for Speech Emotion Recognition
articles.tldr: Cross-lingual speech-emotion-recognition benchmark stressing in-domain vs out-of-domain generalization, using logit adjustment and macro-F1 for fair cross-dataset comparison.
articles.contribution: Employs logit adjustment to correct for differing class distributions across datasets and reports macro-F1, so class-imbalance confounds do not distort the cross-dataset model comparison.

articles.title: Can Multi-modal (reasoning) LLMs detect document manipulation?
articles.tldr: Benchmarks multimodal LLMs on receipt-forgery detection and exposes that prior CNN patch-level F1 (~0.8) collapses to image-level AUROC ~0.5, a metric-misreporting/reproducibility finding.
articles.contribution: Shows prior work's patch-level F1 (~0.79-0.80) collapses to image-level AUROC ~0.5 once patch predictions are OR-aggregated to the image, exposing that the reported patch metric badly overstated real detection ability.

articles.title: Can Multi-modal (reasoning) LLMs detect document manipulation?
articles.tldr: Benchmarks multimodal LLMs on receipt-forgery detection and exposes that prior CNN patch-level F1 (~0.8) collapses to image-level AUROC ~0.5, a metric-misreporting/reproducibility finding.
articles.contribution: Reproduces the prior SVM and OH-JPEG CNN baselines and finds most models (SVM 0.49, CNN 0.51) plus most LLMs hover near the 0.5 random-guess AUC, so previously claimed detection performance does not replicate at the image level.

articles.title: τ-Knowledge: Evaluating Conversational Agents over Unstructured Knowledge
articles.tldr: tau-Knowledge extends tau-Bench to evaluate agents over ~700 unstructured knowledge docs, exposing low pass^1 (~25.5%), reliability decay across trials, and retrieval-config confounds.
articles.contribution: Disentangles retrieval/search from information usage in the agentic harness and shows retrieval configuration (reranker, grep tool, number of retrieved documents, write tools) materially changes measured agent success and solve time.

articles.title: τ-Knowledge: Evaluating Conversational Agents over Unstructured Knowledge
articles.tldr: tau-Knowledge extends tau-Bench to evaluate agents over ~700 unstructured knowledge docs, exposing low pass^1 (~25.5%), reliability decay across trials, and retrieval-config confounds.
articles.contribution: Argues prior benchmarks test retrieval or tool use in isolation, misrepresenting realistic deployment; tau-Banking couples ~700 interlinked natural-language knowledge docs with verifiable tool-mediated, policy-compliant state changes for ecologically valid agentic evaluation.

articles.title: τ-Knowledge: Evaluating Conversational Agents over Unstructured Knowledge
articles.tldr: tau-Knowledge extends tau-Bench to evaluate agents over ~700 unstructured knowledge docs, exposing low pass^1 (~25.5%), reliability decay across trials, and retrieval-config confounds.
articles.contribution: Documents reliability collapse: frontier-model pass^1 of ~25.5% degrades sharply over repeated trials (pass^k), quantifying how nondeterministic runs make single-run agent scores unreliable.

articles.title: ModelingAgent: Bridging LLMs and Mathematical Modeling for Real-World Challenges
articles.tldr: Introduces ModelingBench (open-ended math modeling) and ModelingJudge, a multi-expert LLM-as-judge, while cautioning that cross-model scores are non-comparable due to judge scoring bias.
articles.contribution: Builds ModelingJudge, an expert-role multi-perspective LLM-as-judge for open-ended, multi-valid-solution modeling reports, and explicitly warns that absolute scores across models are not comparable due to potential LLM scoring bias.

articles.title: ModelingAgent: Bridging LLMs and Mathematical Modeling for Real-World Challenges
articles.tldr: Introduces ModelingBench (open-ended math modeling) and ModelingJudge, a multi-expert LLM-as-judge, while cautioning that cross-model scores are non-comparable due to judge scoring bias.
articles.contribution: Argues decontextualized, well-posed math benchmarks misrepresent real-world modeling intelligence; defines the construct via open-ended competition problems that admit multiple valid solutions and demand tool use and interdisciplinary reasoning.

articles.title: T2VEval: Benchmark dataset and objective evaluation method for T2V-generated videos
articles.tldr: Benchmark + learned metric for text-to-video quality, meta-evaluated against human MOS, exposing that existing metrics miss AI-generated distortions.
articles.contribution: Shows existing objective metrics under-represent perceived T2V quality and proposes a multi-branch metric (consistency/realness/technical) aligned to human MOS.

articles.title: T2VEval: Benchmark dataset and objective evaluation method for T2V-generated videos
articles.tldr: Benchmark + learned metric for text-to-video quality, meta-evaluated against human MOS, exposing that existing metrics miss AI-generated distortions.
articles.contribution: Collects MOS via a subjective experiment scoring each video on four dimensions, providing the human ground truth against which objective metrics are validated.

articles.title: TokBench: Evaluating Your Visual Tokenizer before Visual Generation
articles.tldr: Benchmark showing PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FID misrepresent fine-grained text/face reconstruction, proposing OCR- and face-recognition-based metrics aligned to human vision.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates traditional reconstruction metrics fail to reflect fine-grained text/face fidelity, proposing OCR-accuracy (T-ACC/T-NED) and face-similarity (F-Sim) metrics as valid complements.

articles.title: TokBench: Evaluating Your Visual Tokenizer before Visual Generation
articles.tldr: Benchmark showing PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FID misrepresent fine-grained text/face reconstruction, proposing OCR- and face-recognition-based metrics aligned to human vision.
articles.contribution: Uses established OCR and face-recognition models as scorers instead of VLMs, ensuring accuracy while keeping assessment lightweight (2GB memory, 4 minutes).

articles.title: Gen3DEval: Using vLLMs for Automatic Evaluation of Generated 3D Objects
articles.tldr: vLLM-based text-to-3D quality evaluator fine-tuned to align with human judgment, addressing that PSNR/CLIP need ground truth or only measure prompt fidelity.
articles.contribution: Introduces a fine-tuned vLLM judge scoring text fidelity, appearance and surface quality (via surface normals) without ground truth, addressing that CLIP/PSNR mis-measure 3D quality.

articles.title: Gen3DEval: Using vLLMs for Automatic Evaluation of Generated 3D Objects
articles.tldr: vLLM-based text-to-3D quality evaluator fine-tuned to align with human judgment, addressing that PSNR/CLIP need ground truth or only measure prompt fidelity.
articles.contribution: Fine-tunes the vLLM to align with human preferences, outperforming task-agnostic models in user-aligned evaluation of generated 3D objects.

articles.title: TRUE: Re-evaluating Factual Consistency Evaluation
articles.tldr: Standardized meta-evaluation of factual-consistency metrics across 11 datasets using example-level ROC AUC instead of system-level correlation.
articles.contribution: Proposes example-level ROC AUC meta-evaluation, more actionable and interpretable than prior system-level correlations, exposing per-example metric accuracy.

articles.title: TRUE: Re-evaluating Factual Consistency Evaluation
articles.tldr: Standardized meta-evaluation of factual-consistency metrics across 11 datasets using example-level ROC AUC instead of system-level correlation.
articles.contribution: Standardizes 11 diverse datasets under one factual-consistency definition, testing whether metrics capture consistency across tasks rather than a single-dataset proxy.

articles.title: Cloud-OpsBench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Agentic Root Cause Analysis in Cloud Systems
articles.tldr: Reproducible agentic RCA benchmark using a deterministic State Snapshot digital twin and process-centric evaluation to reconcile ecological validity with reproducibility.
articles.contribution: State Snapshot Paradigm freezes cloud state into a deterministic digital twin (452 faults, 40 root-cause types), making otherwise-stochastic agentic RCA evaluation reproducible.

articles.title: Cloud-OpsBench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Agentic Root Cause Analysis in Cloud Systems
articles.tldr: Reproducible agentic RCA benchmark using a deterministic State Snapshot digital twin and process-centric evaluation to reconcile ecological validity with reproducibility.
articles.contribution: Reconciles ecological validity with reproducibility by evaluating active reasoning on a realistic full Kubernetes-stack twin rather than passive fault classification.

articles.title: Cloud-OpsBench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Agentic Root Cause Analysis in Cloud Systems
articles.tldr: Reproducible agentic RCA benchmark using a deterministic State Snapshot digital twin and process-centric evaluation to reconcile ecological validity with reproducibility.
articles.contribution: Process-centric protocol scores reasoning trajectories rather than only final outcomes, reducing outcome-only confounds and diagnosing multi-agent architectural bottlenecks.

articles.title: MolmoSpaces: A Large-Scale Open Ecosystem for Robot Navigation and Manipulation
articles.tldr: Open robot-learning ecosystem/benchmark validating strong sim-to-real correlation and exposing policy sensitivity to prompts, joint init, and camera occlusion.
articles.contribution: Establishes strong sim-to-real correlation (R=0.96, rho=0.98), validating that simulated benchmark scores transport to real-world robot performance.

articles.title: MolmoSpaces: A Large-Scale Open Ecosystem for Robot Navigation and Manipulation
articles.tldr: Open robot-learning ecosystem/benchmark validating strong sim-to-real correlation and exposing policy sensitivity to prompts, joint init, and camera occlusion.
articles.contribution: Identifies key sensitivities to prompt phrasing, initial joint positions and camera occlusion that confound measured policy performance.

articles.title: MolmoSpaces: A Large-Scale Open Ecosystem for Robot Navigation and Manipulation
articles.tldr: Open robot-learning ecosystem/benchmark validating strong sim-to-real correlation and exposing policy sensitivity to prompts, joint init, and camera occlusion.
articles.contribution: Provides 230k+ diverse environments and 130k annotated assets to cover the long tail of scene/object/task variation underrepresented in prior robot benchmarks.

articles.title: Evaluating and Mitigating Social Bias for Large Language Models in Open-ended Settings
articles.tldr: Extends BBQ to open-ended fill-in-the-blank/short-answer bias evaluation, adds LLM-assisted scoring, and fixes debiasing over-correction with Composite Prompting.
articles.contribution: Argues multiple-choice BBQ under-represents real-world bias and adds fill-in-the-blank and short-answer formats (Open-BBQ) for a fuller operationalization.

articles.title: Evaluating and Mitigating Social Bias for Large Language Models in Open-ended Settings
articles.tldr: Extends BBQ to open-ended fill-in-the-blank/short-answer bias evaluation, adds LLM-assisted scoring, and fixes debiasing over-correction with Composite Prompting.
articles.contribution: Develops an LLM-assisted process to detect bias in open-ended sentences and paragraphs, since free-form outputs cannot be scored by exact match.

articles.title: Say My Name: a Model's Bias Discovery Framework
articles.tldr: Framework that semantically names the spurious/shortcut features (biases) a deep model has learned, aiding diagnosis and debiasing.
articles.contribution: Detects and semantically names the spurious/shortcut features a model relies on (e.g., background in Waterbirds), exposing confounded predictions with a bias score.

articles.title: Say My Name: a Model's Bias Discovery Framework
articles.tldr: Framework that semantically names the spurious/shortcut features (biases) a deep model has learned, aiding diagnosis and debiasing.
articles.contribution: Validates discovered biases with a human study and shows on an unbiased dataset that SaMyNa correctly disclaims spurious biases (negative controls).

articles.title: DAHL: Domain-specific Automated Hallucination Evaluation of Long-Form Text through a Benchmark Dataset in Biomedicine
articles.tldr: Automated atomic-fact hallucination benchmark (DAHL) for biomedical long-form generation, validated against human factuality judgments.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes hallucination as averaged atomic-unit factual precision scored by an LLM splitter (gpt-4o) plus an online-grounded checker (pplx-API), quantifying scorer reliability of the DAHL Score.

articles.title: DAHL: Domain-specific Automated Hallucination Evaluation of Long-Form Text through a Benchmark Dataset in Biomedicine
articles.tldr: Automated atomic-fact hallucination benchmark (DAHL) for biomedical long-form generation, validated against human factuality judgments.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory criterion evidence that the automated DAHL Score is valid by correlating it with two-annotator human factuality scores over 99 balanced-category responses.

articles.title: Resource for Error Analysis in Text Simplification: New Taxonomy and Test Collection
articles.tldr: Formal error taxonomy and human-annotated test collection for detecting information-distortion errors in automatic text simplification, showing existing metrics fail.
articles.contribution: Defines a formal set-theoretic taxonomy of ATS errors (faithfulness/factuality hallucination, topic shift, over-generalization, loss of content) as a grounded construct for evaluating simplification quality.

articles.title: Resource for Error Analysis in Text Simplification: New Taxonomy and Test Collection
articles.tldr: Formal error taxonomy and human-annotated test collection for detecting information-distortion errors in automatic text simplification, showing existing metrics fail.
articles.contribution: Shows current ATS/hallucination-detection metrics fail to capture the error construct, with FactCC reaching only 0.68 binary AUROC and BERTScore 0.23.

articles.title: Resource for Error Analysis in Text Simplification: New Taxonomy and Test Collection
articles.tldr: Formal error taxonomy and human-annotated test collection for detecting information-distortion errors in automatic text simplification, showing existing metrics fail.
articles.contribution: Quantifies annotation subjectivity via inter-annotator agreement, reporting low Fleiss kappa for Information (0.02) and Simplification (0.26) error classes vs higher for Alignment (0.45).

articles.title: Learning Evaluation Models From Large Language Models for Sequence Generation
articles.tldr: Transfers LLM evaluation capability into lightweight metric models and studies their alignment with prompt-defined aspects and correlation with human judgments.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates single-aspect learned metrics align with the prompt-specified evaluation aspect (coherence/relevance) on SummEval, evidence the metric captures the intended construct rather than a surface proxy.

articles.title: Learning Evaluation Models From Large Language Models for Sequence Generation
articles.tldr: Transfers LLM evaluation capability into lightweight metric models and studies their alignment with prompt-defined aspects and correlation with human judgments.
articles.contribution: Measures sample- and system-level correlation of the learned reward/metric models with human MQM judgments, establishing the reliability/validity of the scorer relative to BLEU/chrF.

articles.title: UI2V-Bench: An Understanding-based Image-to-video Generation Benchmark
articles.tldr: Understanding-and-reasoning-based image-to-video benchmark (UI2V-Bench) with MLLM evaluation pipelines validated against human ratings.
articles.contribution: Argues existing I2V benchmarks under-represent the target construct by measuring only visual quality/temporal consistency, and defines four semantic-understanding and reasoning dimensions instead.

articles.title: UI2V-Bench: An Understanding-based Image-to-video Generation Benchmark
articles.tldr: Understanding-and-reasoning-based image-to-video benchmark (UI2V-Bench) with MLLM evaluation pipelines validated against human ratings.
articles.contribution: Validates MLLM-based instance-level and feedback-based scoring pipelines against human judgment, reporting strong correlation for Spatial (rho=0.7345) and Reasoning (rho=0.7329) dimensions.

articles.title: CSVQA: A Chinese Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating STEM Reasoning Capabilities of VLMs
articles.tldr: Chinese STEM VQA benchmark with explanation-driven evaluation to distinguish genuine multimodal reasoning from lucky guessing and text shortcuts.
articles.contribution: Introduces explanation-driven evaluation where GPT-4o checks whether correct answers follow valid reasoning steps, exposing that correctness can arise from pattern matching rather than genuine reasoning.

articles.title: CSVQA: A Chinese Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating STEM Reasoning Capabilities of VLMs
articles.tldr: Chinese STEM VQA benchmark with explanation-driven evaluation to distinguish genuine multimodal reasoning from lucky guessing and text shortcuts.
articles.contribution: Builds the CSVQA-Hard subset by filtering items answerable from text alone (feeding text-only to LLMs and keeping consistently-wrong cases), isolating questions that genuinely require visual reasoning.

articles.title: OVERVIEW OF THE CXR-LT 2026 CHALLENGE: MULTI-CENTER LONG-TAILED AND ZERO SHOT CHEST X-RAY CLASSIFICATION
articles.tldr: Multi-center long-tailed and zero-shot chest X-ray classification challenge separating noisy report labels from expert annotations and testing open-world OOD generalization.
articles.contribution: Separates large-scale noisy report-derived training labels from radiologist image-level evaluation labels (PadChest-GR; NIH cases needing 2-of-3 radiologist agreement) to give higher-quality ground truth.

articles.title: OVERVIEW OF THE CXR-LT 2026 CHALLENGE: MULTI-CENTER LONG-TAILED AND ZERO SHOT CHEST X-RAY CLASSIFICATION
articles.tldr: Multi-center long-tailed and zero-shot chest X-ray classification challenge separating noisy report labels from expert annotations and testing open-world OOD generalization.
articles.contribution: Defines an open-world task over 6 unseen classes plus an external NIH test set to measure external/OOD validity under multi-center domain shift beyond closed-set single-institution benchmarks.

articles.title: OVERVIEW OF THE CXR-LT 2026 CHALLENGE: MULTI-CENTER LONG-TAILED AND ZERO SHOT CHEST X-RAY CLASSIFICATION
articles.tldr: Multi-center long-tailed and zero-shot chest X-ray classification challenge separating noisy report labels from expert annotations and testing open-world OOD generalization.
articles.contribution: Documents a calibration-vs-discrimination mismatch, showing top ranking metrics (mAP/AUROC) do not imply optimal threshold-based F1 and arguing both must be reported.

articles.title: BenchGuard: Who Guards the Benchmarks? Automated Auditing of LLM Agent Benchmarks
articles.tldr: Frontier LLMs act as automated auditors that expose spec/gold/eval defects in execution-based agent benchmarks that multiple rounds of human review missed.
articles.contribution: Uses LLM auditors to catch underspecified/contradictory task instructions (wrong input file, SMILES-vs-drug-name) that make agent tasks mis-measure the intended capability.

articles.title: BenchGuard: Who Guards the Benchmarks? Automated Auditing of LLM Agent Benchmarks
articles.tldr: Frontier LLMs act as automated auditors that expose spec/gold/eval defects in execution-based agent benchmarks that multiple rounds of human review missed.
articles.contribution: Detects evaluation-script flaws (judge bias, wrong tolerances, rigid scripts that reject valid alternative solutions) that corrupt execution-based benchmark scores.

articles.title: From Aesthetics to Human Preferences: Comparative Perspectives of Evaluating Text-to-Music Systems
articles.tldr: Case study on text-to-music evaluation showing automatic metrics (learned aesthetics predictors, MAD, KAD) disagree with each other and align poorly with human preference.
articles.contribution: Shows learned aesthetics scores predict human musicality/fidelity preference only barely above chance, so the automatic metric fails to capture the intended human-preference construct.

articles.title: From Aesthetics to Human Preferences: Comparative Perspectives of Evaluating Text-to-Music Systems
articles.tldr: Case study on text-to-music evaluation showing automatic metrics (learned aesthetics predictors, MAD, KAD) disagree with each other and align poorly with human preference.
articles.contribution: Reveals the learned aesthetic predictor encodes latent content/genre bias (higher Production-Complexity for electronic/'synth' clusters), a confound in the metric independent of quality.

articles.title: KITTEN: A Knowledge-Intensive Evaluation of Image Generation on Visual Entities
articles.tldr: Knowledge-intensive text-to-image benchmark for entity fidelity showing existing metrics capture alignment/aesthetics not visual-world knowledge, and that automatic metrics correlate only moderately with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Introduces the entity-fidelity construct grounded in Wikipedia knowledge, exposing that prior T2I benchmarks measuring text-alignment/aesthetics fail to capture factual visual accuracy of real-world entities.

articles.title: KITTEN: A Knowledge-Intensive Evaluation of Image Generation on Visual Entities
articles.tldr: Knowledge-intensive text-to-image benchmark for entity fidelity showing existing metrics capture alignment/aesthetics not visual-world knowledge, and that automatic metrics correlate only moderately with human judgment.
articles.contribution: Quantifies that popular automatic metrics (CLIP-T, CLIP-I, DINO) are weak proxies for human fidelity judgments, with only DINO reaching moderate correlation.

articles.title: Human Cognitive Benchmarks Reveal Foundational Visual Gaps in MLLMs
articles.tldr: FRCT-grounded MLLM vision benchmark (VisFactor) arguing high scores on omnibus benchmarks are 'castles in the air' rather than genuine visual cognition, with reported construct validity and internal consistency.
articles.contribution: Grounds MLLM vision assessment in FRCT cognitive factors and provides psychometric evidence (Cronbach's alpha, cross-benchmark construct validity) that omnibus-benchmark scores overstate genuine visual cognition.

articles.title: Human Cognitive Benchmarks Reveal Foundational Visual Gaps in MLLMs

articles.tldr: Enterprise computer-use-agent benchmark arguing task-completion accuracy misrepresents operational reliability, using programmatic state oracles instead of fragile LLM/string judges and systematic interface+resolution coverage.
articles.contribution: Replaces fragile LLM-judge/string-match scoring with deterministic test() oracles over window.app_state, motivated by documented judge failures that accept wrong trajectories or penalize valid alternatives.

articles.title: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
articles.tldr: Enterprise computer-use-agent benchmark arguing task-completion accuracy misrepresents operational reliability, using programmatic state oracles instead of fragile LLM/string judges and systematic interface+resolution coverage.
articles.contribution: Replaces organic/convenience task sampling with a systematic interface taxonomy (22 control, 27 structure, 27 action types) plus multi-resolution testing to expose deployment brittleness.

articles.title: Unveiling and Bridging the Functional Perception Gap in MLLMs: Atomic Visual Alignment and Hierarchical Evaluation via PET-Bench
articles.tldr: Large PET functional-imaging benchmark that isolates pure PET to expose a functional perception gap, a Chain-of-Thought hallucination trap, and prevents test leakage via patient-level splits.
articles.contribution: Builds SUV-normalized pure-PET QA (no PET/CT overlay) to remove the morphological CT confound whereby fused-modality models score via high-res anatomy while ignoring the functional PET signal.

articles.title: Unveiling and Bridging the Functional Perception Gap in MLLMs: Atomic Visual Alignment and Hierarchical Evaluation via PET-Bench
articles.tldr: Large PET functional-imaging benchmark that isolates pure PET to expose a functional perception gap, a Chain-of-Thought hallucination trap, and prevents test leakage via patient-level splits.
articles.contribution: Documents a CoT hallucination trap where chain-of-thought amplifies language priors and decouples generation from visual evidence, producing fluent but factually ungrounded diagnoses.

articles.title: Unveiling and Bridging the Functional Perception Gap in MLLMs: Atomic Visual Alignment and Hierarchical Evaluation via PET-Bench
articles.tldr: Large PET functional-imaging benchmark that isolates pure PET to expose a functional perception gap, a Chain-of-Thought hallucination trap, and prevents test leakage via patient-level splits.
articles.contribution: Enforces a strict patient-level split so Level-5 diagnosis test patients are never seen during AVA training, preventing memorization of patient-specific physiological distributions.

articles.title: Generative Induction of Dialogue Task Schemas with Streaming Refinement and Simulated Interactions
articles.tldr: Slot-schema-induction method that first exposes benchmark leakage and human-misaligned metrics, then builds a leak-free simulated eval set and human-validated matcher/metrics.
articles.contribution: Quantitatively verifies that MultiWOZ 2.4 and SGD test sets leaked to popular LLMs and introduces an unexposed simulated evaluation set (Dots) to restore a true generalization measurement.

articles.title: Generative Induction of Dialogue Task Schemas with Streaming Refinement and Simulated Interactions
articles.tldr: Slot-schema-induction method that first exposes benchmark leakage and human-misaligned metrics, then builds a leak-free simulated eval set and human-validated matcher/metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows the prior BERT-similarity slot matcher poorly reflects human judgment and proposes a matcher validated against a human slot mapping for far higher agreement.

articles.title: Generative Induction of Dialogue Task Schemas with Streaming Refinement and Simulated Interactions
articles.tldr: Slot-schema-induction method that first exposes benchmark leakage and human-misaligned metrics, then builds a leak-free simulated eval set and human-validated matcher/metrics.
articles.contribution: Redefines precision so each redundant predicted slot counts as an error, fixing prior many-to-one mappings that inflate scores and reward predicting far more slots than exist in gold.

articles.title: Performance of diverse evaluation metrics in NLP-based assessment and text generation of consumer complaints
articles.tldr: Text-classification study that centers on comparing evaluation metrics (accuracy, F1, MCC, Cohen's kappa) for consumer-complaint classification and flags measurements that misrepresent model capability.
articles.contribution: Compares accuracy, F1, MCC and Cohen's kappa as classifier performance measures under class imbalance and flags invalid measurements that do not reflect true model capability.

articles.title: Evaluating the Evaluators: Metrics for Compositional Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation study correlating 12 automatic compositional text-to-image metrics against human judgment, showing no single metric is consistently valid and diagnosing metric distribution pathologies.
articles.contribution: Shows widely used automatic metrics are adopted by convention and no single metric captures human-judged compositional alignment across the eight T2I-CompBench++ categories.

articles.title: Evaluating the Evaluators: Metrics for Compositional Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation study correlating 12 automatic compositional text-to-image metrics against human judgment, showing no single metric is consistently valid and diagnosing metric distribution pathologies.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses reliability pathologies: VQA-based metrics saturate near 1.0 (poor discrimination) while CLIP is compressed into a narrow mid-range, undermining their use as scorers and reward models.

articles.title: RCTs for Frontier AI Governance: Methodological Challenges and Solutions for Human Uplift Studies
articles.tldr: Interview synthesis of 16 experts mapping methodological challenges in AI human-uplift RCTs to construct, internal, external and temporal validity threats amplified by frontier AI.
articles.contribution: Identifies internal-validity threats specific to uplift RCTs: ambiguous control conditions, uneven AI-literacy confounds, unblindable expectancy effects, and intervention infidelity from silent model changes.

articles.title: RCTs for Frontier AI Governance: Methodological Challenges and Solutions for Human Uplift Studies
articles.tldr: Interview synthesis of 16 experts mapping methodological challenges in AI human-uplift RCTs to construct, internal, external and temporal validity threats amplified by frontier AI.
articles.contribution: Shows external validity is strained by proxy populations (students standing in for adversaries), convenience sampling, and constrained pathway coverage that cannot represent real-world action spaces.

articles.title: RCTs for Frontier AI Governance: Methodological Challenges and Solutions for Human Uplift Studies
articles.tldr: Interview synthesis of 16 experts mapping methodological challenges in AI human-uplift RCTs to construct, internal, external and temporal validity threats amplified by frontier AI.
articles.contribution: Highlights temporal-validity erosion: models can change mid-experiment, user proficiency and baselines shift ('boiling frog'), so point-in-time uplift estimates fail to transport across models and time.

articles.title: CodeSpecBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Executable Behavioral Specification Generation
articles.tldr: Executable behavioral-spec benchmark arguing code-generation pass rate is not a valid proxy for a model's understanding of intended program semantics.
articles.contribution: Argues code-generation pass rate is a surface proxy: models with strong solution pass rates still fail executable-spec generation, so coding benchmarks conflate coding with understanding program semantics.

articles.title: CodeSpecBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Executable Behavioral Specification Generation
articles.tldr: Executable behavioral-spec benchmark arguing code-generation pass rate is not a valid proxy for a model's understanding of intended program semantics.
articles.contribution: Improves reliability of execution-based scoring by generating 200+ curated correct/incorrect test cases per problem (96.3% statement, 93.6% branch coverage) and reporting strict vs fraction-based metrics.

articles.title: LLM-Assisted Web Measurements
articles.tldr: Assesses whether LLM classifiers are a valid, reliable instrument for targeted web-measurement studies and whether the resulting research inferences hold.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks LLMs as website classifiers and shows reliability of the resulting labels depends heavily on model/config choice, treating the LLM as a scientific measurement instrument.

articles.title: LLM-Assisted Web Measurements
articles.tldr: Assesses whether LLM classifiers are a valid, reliable instrument for targeted web-measurement studies and whether the resulting research inferences hold.
articles.contribution: Validates external validity of research inferences from LLM-assisted web measurements and proposes a two-step Tranco-filtering methodology to make targeted sampling sound and scalable.

articles.title: Developing the PsyCogMetrics AI Lab to Evaluate Large Language Models and Advance Cognitive Science - A Three-Cycle Action Design Science Study
articles.tldr: Design-science platform operationalizing Classical Test Theory and psychometric validity (reliability, convergent/discriminant/predictive/external validity) for LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Builds a reliability pipeline computing Cronbach's alpha, Composite Reliability and AVE, plus normality tests and SEM fit indices, to quantify measurement reliability of LLM evaluations.

articles.title: Developing the PsyCogMetrics AI Lab to Evaluate Large Language Models and Advance Cognitive Science - A Three-Cycle Action Design Science Study
articles.tldr: Design-science platform operationalizing Classical Test Theory and psychometric validity (reliability, convergent/discriminant/predictive/external validity) for LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Grounds LLM evaluation in Validity Theory (convergent, discriminant, predictive, external validity via factor analysis) so measures target latent constructs rather than surface benchmark scores.

articles.title: Developing the PsyCogMetrics AI Lab to Evaluate Large Language Models and Advance Cognitive Science - A Three-Cycle Action Design Science Study
articles.tldr: Design-science platform operationalizing Classical Test Theory and psychometric validity (reliability, convergent/discriminant/predictive/external validity) for LLM evaluation.
articles.contribution: Argues open-ended psychometric measures (no single correct answer) resist data contamination and benchmark saturation because item leakage does not inflate internal-consistency scores.

articles.title: Contrast sensitivity in multimodal large language models: A psychophysics-inspired evaluation
articles.tldr: Psychophysics-inspired behavioral method to measure MLLM contrast sensitivity that avoids classifier/embedding readout confounds but reveals strong prompt-phrasing unreliability.
articles.contribution: Shows prior CSF readouts (trained classifiers, embedding distance) confound model perception with the readout instrument, and proposes a behavioral end-to-end-observer measure that removes this confound.

articles.title: Contrast sensitivity in multimodal large language models: A psychophysics-inspired evaluation
articles.tldr: Psychophysics-inspired behavioral method to measure MLLM contrast sensitivity that avoids classifier/embedding readout confounds but reveals strong prompt-phrasing unreliability.
articles.contribution: Quantifies with entropy/consistency metrics that CSF estimates are highly sensitive to prompt phrasing, so the measurement's reliability depends on linguistic formulation of the query.

articles.title: neuralFOMO: Can LLMs Handle Being Second Best? Measuring Envy-Like Preferences in Multi-Agent Settings
articles.tldr: Measures envy-like preferences in LLMs by adapting human psychometric scales, finding human factor structure does not transfer and self-report diverges from behavior.
articles.contribution: Finds LLM WEAS factor loadings systematically invert relative to human loadings (mean rho=-0.80 for challenge appraisals), showing adapted human envy instruments may not validly capture the same construct in LLMs.

articles.title: neuralFOMO: Can LLMs Handle Being Second Best? Measuring Envy-Like Preferences in Multi-Agent Settings
articles.tldr: Measures envy-like preferences in LLMs by adapting human psychometric scales, finding human factor structure does not transfer and self-report diverges from behavior.
articles.contribution: Shows a direct-question vs behavior dissociation: models deny envious behavior in direct Q&A but shift choices under quiet competition, a social-desirability/reactivity threat to self-report measures.

articles.title: Models Recall What They Violate: Constraint Adherence in Multi-Turn LLM Ideation
articles.tldr: Benchmark for constraint drift in multi-turn ideation showing an LLM judge under-detects violations and that constraint recall is an invalid proxy for actual adherence.
articles.contribution: Human validation shows the LLM judge has 97% specificity but only 15% sensitivity (humans found 34 violations, judge only 7), so reported constraint-adherence scores are conservatively biased.

articles.title: Models Recall What They Violate: Constraint Adherence in Multi-Turn LLM Ideation
articles.tldr: Benchmark for constraint drift in multi-turn ideation showing an LLM judge under-detects violations and that constraint recall is an invalid proxy for actual adherence.
articles.contribution: The knows-but-violates finding (KBV 8-99%; 100% recall yet violation) and 'surface fidelity gap' show restatement/recall is an invalid proxy for behavioral constraint adherence.

articles.title: Do LLMs Hold Their Values? MANTA: A Multi-Turn Adversarial Benchmark for Animal Welfare Reasoning
articles.tldr: Multi-turn adversarial animal-welfare benchmark separating welfare recognition from value stability, with judge-validity, eval-awareness and self-preference-confound analyses.
articles.contribution: Distinguishes 'value expression' from 'value stability' (rubric grounded in Rest's Four Component Model), showing single-turn explicit benchmarks under-represent the construct: 4/7 models change rank vs Turn-1 scores.

articles.title: Do LLMs Hold Their Values? MANTA: A Multi-Turn Adversarial Benchmark for Animal Welfare Reasoning
articles.tldr: Multi-turn adversarial animal-welfare benchmark separating welfare recognition from value stability, with judge-validity, eval-awareness and self-preference-confound analyses.
articles.contribution: Reports judge validity: human-judge Spearman rho=0.61 at T1 but 0.47 pooled T3-5, and the LLM judge overscores hedged welfare statements by 0.27 vs humans, treating hedging as more value-stable.

articles.title: Do LLMs Hold Their Values? MANTA: A Multi-Turn Adversarial Benchmark for Animal Welfare Reasoning
articles.tldr: Multi-turn adversarial animal-welfare benchmark separating welfare recognition from value stability, with judge-validity, eval-awareness and self-preference-confound analyses.
articles.contribution: Uses naturalistic implicit framing to reduce evaluation awareness and runs a framing-sensitivity audit finding a small AWMS shift (Delta_eval=+0.052) under explicit evaluation framing.

articles.title: Do LLMs Hold Their Values? MANTA: A Multi-Turn Adversarial Benchmark for Animal Welfare Reasoning
articles.tldr: Multi-turn adversarial animal-welfare benchmark separating welfare recognition from value stability, with judge-validity, eval-awareness and self-preference-confound analyses.
articles.contribution: Flags a self-preference/generation-bias confound (all scenarios generated by Claude Sonnet 4 inflate Claude's AWMS) and mitigates it with cross-family judging for fair cross-model comparison.

articles.title: Evaluation of student proficiency through a multidimensional finite mixture IRT model
articles.tldr: Multidimensional latent-class IRT model that jointly models exam skipping so non-ignorable (MNAR) missingness does not bias student-ability estimates.
articles.contribution: Shows exam-skipping is a non-ignorable (MNAR) confounder of latent-ability estimation and that a shared-parameter IRT model jointly fitting the enrollment/response process removes the bias.

articles.title: Evaluation of student proficiency through a multidimensional finite mixture IRT model
articles.tldr: Multidimensional latent-class IRT model that jointly models exam skipping so non-ignorable (MNAR) missingness does not bias student-ability estimates.
articles.contribution: Estimates per-item discrimination/difficulty via a graded-response 2PL model, quantifying how reliably each exam item measures the latent ability trait.

articles.title: Floating-Point Usage on GitHub: A Large-Scale Study of Statically Typed Languages
articles.tldr: First large-scale GitHub mining of floating-point code, used to test whether the benchmarks that evaluate automated FP-reasoning tools are representative of real-world code.
articles.contribution: Empirically checks representativeness of FP-reasoning benchmarks against real GitHub code, finding they match on some statistics but diverge on others, questioning external validity of tool evaluations.

articles.title: Detecting Distillation Data from Reasoning Models
articles.tldr: Defines distillation-data detection and proposes Token Probability Deviation (TPD) to catch benchmark contamination hidden in reasoning-distillation data.
articles.contribution: Formalizes detecting whether a benchmark question leaked into a model's distillation data and gives TPD, an output-token-probability-deviation score that works under partial (question-only) availability.

articles.title: Contamination Detection for VLMs using Multi-Modal Semantic Perturbation
articles.tldr: Multi-modal semantic-perturbation method to detect contaminated Vision-Language Models that memorized benchmark test sets.
articles.contribution: Detects test-set leakage in VLMs by perturbing image+answer semantics: memorized models keep the stale answer and fail to generalize under controlled perturbations.

articles.title: MIMM-X: Disentangling Spurious Correlations for Medical Image Analysis
articles.tldr: MIMM-X disentangles multiple coexisting spurious correlations in medical imaging by minimizing mutual information so predictions rely on causal rather than shortcut features.
articles.contribution: Shows multiple coexisting spurious correlations (e.g. disease-to-sex association) confound medical-image classifiers, and that minimizing mutual information between causal and spurious features removes the shortcut confound.

articles.title: MIMM-X: Disentangling Spurious Correlations for Medical Image Analysis
articles.tldr: MIMM-X disentangles multiple coexisting spurious correlations in medical imaging by minimizing mutual information so predictions rely on causal rather than shortcut features.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that shortcut-reliant models fail to generalize to new environments and that disentangling causal features restores out-of-distribution performance.

articles.title: Omni-Fake: Benchmarking Unified Multimodal Social Media Deepfake Detection
articles.tldr: Omni-Fake builds a 1M+ four-modality deepfake-detection benchmark with a held-out OOD split to fix prior benchmarks' unrepresentative distributions and test real-world generalization.
articles.contribution: Argues existing deepfake benchmarks are single-modality with simplified manipulations and unrealistic distributions, so it assembles a large 4-modality dataset to better assess real-world robustness.

articles.title: Omni-Fake: Benchmarking Unified Multimodal Social Media Deepfake Detection
articles.tldr: Omni-Fake builds a 1M+ four-modality deepfake-detection benchmark with a held-out OOD split to fix prior benchmarks' unrepresentative distributions and test real-world generalization.
articles.contribution: Introduces Omni-Fake-OOD (200k+ samples intentionally excluded from training) as a dedicated out-of-distribution test of detector generalization.

articles.title: Generalization Boundaries of Fine-Tuned Small Language Models for Graph Structural Inference
articles.tldr: Systematic study mapping where fine-tuned small language models stop generalizing on graph structural inference (across graph size and graph-family distribution).
articles.contribution: Argues in-distribution competence is necessary but insufficient and delineates external-validity boundaries of fine-tuned SLM graph estimators beyond the training size range and across held-out graph families.

articles.title: Towards Generalized Open Information Extraction
articles.tldr: Shows that in-domain i.i.d. OpenIE benchmarks overstate generalization and introduces the multi-domain GLOBE benchmark, revealing up to 70% relative F1 collapse out-of-domain.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that standard in-domain i.i.d. OpenIE evaluation fails to measure true open-domain generalization: state-of-the-art models drop 35-70% relative F1 under domain shift, so in-domain scores do not transport to real out-of-domain extraction.

articles.title: Towards Generalized Open Information Extraction
articles.tldr: Shows that in-domain i.i.d. OpenIE benchmarks overstate generalization and introduces the multi-domain GLOBE benchmark, revealing up to 70% relative F1 collapse out-of-domain.
articles.contribution: Argues existing OpenIE test sets are drawn from the same domain as training (violating the domain-independence task principle) and builds GLOBE (110,122 human-annotated facts over 6 disjoint domains) as a representative multi-domain evaluation set.

articles.title: ELViS: Efficient Visual Similarity from Local Descriptors that Generalizes Across Domains
articles.tldr: Introduces the first extensive single-source domain-generalization protocol for instance retrieval and shows transformer descriptor-based re-rankers overfit the training domain while similarity-based models generalize, exposing that in-domain evaluation overstates generalization.
articles.contribution: Compiles an 8-dataset single-source domain-generalization benchmark showing that conventional in-domain instance-retrieval evaluation hides overfitting: descriptor-based re-rankers excel in-domain but lag out-of-domain, so in-domain mAP is not a valid proxy for cross-domain deployment.

articles.title: Capable but Unreliable: Canonical Path Deviation as a Causal Mechanism of Agent Failure in Long-Horizon Tasks
articles.tldr: Uses a within-unit natural experiment on the Toolathlon benchmark to causally separate reliability (stochastic canonical-path drift) from capability in agent failure, showing single-run pass rates conflate the two.
articles.contribution: Shows 22.5% of model x task units are mixed-outcome across identical repeated runs, so single-run pass@1 conflates capability and reliability; proposes reporting the mixed-outcome fraction alongside mean performance as an addressable-unreliability metric.

articles.title: Capable but Unreliable: Canonical Path Deviation as a Causal Mechanism of Agent Failure in Long-Horizon Tasks
articles.tldr: Uses a within-unit natural experiment on the Toolathlon benchmark to causally separate reliability (stochastic canonical-path drift) from capability in agent failure, showing single-run pass rates conflate the two.
articles.contribution: Exploits a within-unit natural experiment (holding model and task fixed, varying only sampling seed) to causally identify stochastic drift from a task's canonical solution path as the mechanism of agent failure, +0.060 Jaccard adherence gap, p<0.0001.

articles.title: Symbolic Guardrails for Domain-Specific Agents: Stronger Safety and Security Guarantees Without Sacrificing Utility
articles.tldr: Systematic review of 80 agent safety/security benchmarks finds 85% lack concrete policies and rely on ambiguous 'common-sense', undermining what these safety evaluations actually measure.
articles.contribution: A systematic literature review of 80 tool-using agent safety/security benchmarks shows the target 'safety/security' construct is largely undefined: 63% provide no explicit policy and 23.8% only vague goal-setting policies, so the evaluated property is underspecified before measurement.

articles.title: Randomization Inference for Before-and-After Studies with Multiple Units: An Application to a Criminal Procedure Reform in Uruguay
articles.tldr: A randomization-inference framework for before-and-after policy studies that yields finite-sample-valid short-term causal inference without parametric time-series assumptions, backed by falsification tests.
articles.contribution: Develops finite-sample-valid randomization inference for multi-unit before-and-after designs, avoiding parametric time-series extrapolation that can make significance claims unreliable.

articles.title: Randomization Inference for Before-and-After Studies with Multiple Units: An Application to a Criminal Procedure Reform in Uruguay
articles.tldr: A randomization-inference framework for before-and-after policy studies that yields finite-sample-valid short-term causal inference without parametric time-series assumptions, backed by falsification tests.
articles.contribution: Grounds internal validity in a no-local-time-trends identifying assumption and provides falsification tests as explicit negative/confirmatory evidence that the assumption holds near adoption.

articles.title: Cinéaste: A Fine-grained Contextual Movie Question Answering Benchmark
articles.tldr: A long-form movie-QA benchmark whose two-stage filtering removes text-only-answerable (shortcut) questions and validates factual veracity of auto-generated items to keep the evaluation valid.
articles.contribution: Context-Independence filtering removes questions answerable without video so the benchmark measures genuine narrative comprehension rather than a text/language-prior shortcut.

articles.title: Cinéaste: A Fine-grained Contextual Movie Question Answering Benchmark
articles.tldr: A long-form movie-QA benchmark whose two-stage filtering removes text-only-answerable (shortcut) questions and validates factual veracity of auto-generated items to keep the evaluation valid.
articles.contribution: Contextual Veracity filtering validates factual consistency of GPT-4o-generated QA against movie content, mitigating hallucinated (wrong) ground-truth labels.

articles.title: ErrEval: Error-Aware Evaluation for Question Generation through Explicit Diagnostics
articles.tldr: Argues black-box holistic LLM evaluators overestimate question-generation quality and proposes an error-aware two-stage (diagnose-then-score) evaluator that better aligns with human judgments.
articles.contribution: Shows holistic LLM-judge scoring is unreliable because it neglects defects, and adds an Error Identifier stage whose diagnostics reduce overestimation of low-quality questions.

articles.title: ErrEval: Error-Aware Evaluation for Question Generation through Explicit Diagnostics
articles.tldr: Argues black-box holistic LLM evaluators overestimate question-generation quality and proposes an error-aware two-stage (diagnose-then-score) evaluator that better aligns with human judgments.
articles.contribution: Reformulates the measure so the score reflects explicit structural/linguistic/content error evidence rather than a surface holistic impression, improving construct fidelity.

articles.title: Halluverse-M^3: A multitask multilingual benchmark for hallucination in LLMs
articles.tldr: A multilingual, multitask hallucination benchmark built by controlled single-hallucination editing with human validation, enabling fine-grained detection analysis across languages and tasks.
articles.contribution: Constructs labels via a controlled editing process enforcing exactly one injected, reference-unsupported hallucination and human validation, ensuring clean alignment between original and hallucinated text.

articles.title: Halluverse-M^3: A multitask multilingual benchmark for hallucination in LLMs
articles.tldr: A multilingual, multitask hallucination benchmark built by controlled single-hallucination editing with human validation, enabling fine-grained detection analysis across languages and tasks.
articles.contribution: Extends hallucination-detection coverage beyond English to Arabic, Hindi, and Turkish across QA and dialogue summarization, exposing that English-centric benchmarks miss lower-resource behavior.

articles.title: LLM Performance for Code Generation on Noisy Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows LLMs solve code/math tasks obfuscated beyond human legibility only for pre-cutoff (contaminated) data, and proposes performance decay under obfuscation as a contamination detector.
articles.contribution: Proposes measuring accuracy decay under increasing obfuscation (noise/redaction) as a diagnostic that distinguishes memorized/contaminated benchmark items from genuine reasoning.

articles.title: LLM Performance for Code Generation on Noisy Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows LLMs solve code/math tasks obfuscated beyond human legibility only for pre-cutoff (contaminated) data, and proposes performance decay under obfuscation as a contamination detector.
articles.contribution: Uses the model knowledge-cutoff date as a natural cut to show contamination-driven inflation exists on old tasks but vanishes on post-cutoff tasks, a temporal-validity signal for saturating benchmarks.

articles.title: IE-Critic-R1: Advancing the Explanatory Measurement of Text-Driven Image Editing for Human Perception Alignment
articles.tldr: Builds a human-MOS image-editing quality benchmark and an RLVR-trained explanatory critic that better aligns automated edit-quality scores with human perception.
articles.contribution: Shows prior metrics (CLIP/SSIM-style) capture only text-image consistency and misrepresent perceived edit quality, and trains IE-Critic-R1 to align explanatory scores with human MOS.

articles.title: IE-Critic-R1: Advancing the Explanatory Measurement of Text-Driven Image Editing for Human Perception Alignment
articles.tldr: Builds a human-MOS image-editing quality benchmark and an RLVR-trained explanatory critic that better aligns automated edit-quality scores with human perception.
articles.contribution: Documents that RLVR without a cold-start SFT phase is prone to reward hacking, with the critic emitting short fixed useless chain-of-thought before a score, corrupting the learned metric.

articles.title: Assertion Messages with Large Language Models (LLMs) for Code
articles.tldr: Systematically evaluates FIM LLMs at generating unit-test assertion messages and argues conventional text metrics fail to capture assertion-message quality, using a human-like rubric instead.
articles.contribution: Argues conventional text-similarity metrics cannot capture the diverse structures of assertion messages, so they mis-measure the intended quality construct.

articles.title: Assertion Messages with Large Language Models (LLMs) for Code
articles.tldr: Systematically evaluates FIM LLMs at generating unit-test assertion messages and argues conventional text metrics fail to capture assertion-message quality, using a human-like rubric instead.
articles.contribution: Adopts a human-like 5-point quality scoring approach as a more faithful instrument than automated text metrics for judging generated assertion messages.

articles.title: Seeing Through the MiRAGE: Evaluating Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
articles.tldr: Introduces a claim-centric multimodal-RAG evaluation (InfoF1/CiteF1) and shows text-centric metrics poorly or negatively correlate with human quality judgments in audiovisual settings.
articles.contribution: Proposes a claim-centric measure (InfoF1 for factuality/coverage, CiteF1 for citation support) that, applied by humans, has the highest agreement with extrinsic quality judgments of multimodal RAG.

articles.title: Seeing Through the MiRAGE: Evaluating Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
articles.tldr: Introduces a claim-centric multimodal-RAG evaluation (InfoF1/CiteF1) and shows text-centric metrics poorly or negatively correlate with human quality judgments in audiovisual settings.
articles.contribution: Empirically compares metric-human agreement and shows prominent text-centric RAG metrics (ALCE, ARGUE, RAGAS) correlate poorly or negatively with human judgments in multimodal settings.

articles.title: 3DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agentic Procedural 3D Modeling Via Code
articles.tldr: A procedural-3D-code benchmark that validates automated perception metrics against a human-preference arena and audits VLM-as-judge agreement with human votes.
articles.contribution: Validates that automated multi-view similarity metrics track perceived 3D quality by correlating them against human-preference Elo, treating human votes as the criterion for construct validity.

articles.title: 3DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agentic Procedural 3D Modeling Via Code
articles.tldr: A procedural-3D-code benchmark that validates automated perception metrics against a human-preference arena and audits VLM-as-judge agreement with human votes.
articles.contribution: Audits LLM/VLM-as-a-judge reliability against the human arena using accuracy, Cohen's kappa, and Pearson phi on decisive-decisive rows to test how well judges reproduce human verdicts.

articles.title: MSG Score: Automated Video Verification for Reliable Multi-Scene Generation
articles.tldr: Builds a hierarchical video-quality metric (MSG) and validates its 93.48% human alignment plus VQA-based thematic-consistency robustness.
articles.contribution: Validates the automated video scorer against human judgment (93.48% vs DOVER 86.67%) and shows a VQA judge is more robust than a ViT (DINOv2) encoder at catching subtle thematic inconsistencies.

articles.title: MSG Score: Automated Video Verification for Reliable Multi-Scene Generation
articles.tldr: Builds a hierarchical video-quality metric (MSG) and validates its 93.48% human alignment plus VQA-based thematic-consistency robustness.
articles.contribution: Aggregating 20 sub-metrics via learned shot-dependent attention into a single score better matches human-perceived quality than individual VBench sub-metrics, avoiding masking of single-dimension failures.

articles.title: PodEval: A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for Podcast Audio Generation
articles.tldr: Multimodal evaluation framework for open-ended long-form podcast audio, pairing reference-free metrics with reliability-hardened subjective listening tests.
articles.contribution: Constructs the Real-Pod real-world reference dataset (17 categories x 3 topics) as a human-level quality reference for open-ended long-form audio, addressing the absence of a representative reference set.

articles.title: PodEval: A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for Podcast Audio Generation
articles.tldr: Multimodal evaluation framework for open-ended long-form podcast audio, pairing reference-free metrics with reliability-hardened subjective listening tests.
articles.contribution: Hardens subjective MOS/MUSHRA tests against inattentive raters using high/low anchors, attention-check questions, and mandatory justifications (spammer detection), raising pass rate 75% to 90%.

articles.title: PodEval: A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for Podcast Audio Generation
articles.tldr: Multimodal evaluation framework for open-ended long-form podcast audio, pairing reference-free metrics with reliability-hardened subjective listening tests.
articles.contribution: Argues reference-based text metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) are invalid for open-ended podcasts and designs reference-free intrinsic metrics (Distinct-N, SPTD, CASP harmony) matched to the intended construct.

articles.title: VidAudio-Bench: Benchmarking V2A and VT2A Generation across Four Audio Categories
articles.tldr: Task-specific reference-free V2A/VT2A audio-generation benchmark validating 13 metrics against human preference and adding a leak-free design to probe visual grounding vs text shortcuts.
articles.contribution: Introduces a zero-information-leak VT2A protocol supplying only muted-video visual captions (not acoustic prompts) to prevent models from exploiting acoustic text shortcuts, isolating genuine visual grounding.

articles.title: VidAudio-Bench: Benchmarking V2A and VT2A Generation across Four Audio Categories
articles.tldr: Task-specific reference-free V2A/VT2A audio-generation benchmark validating 13 metrics against human preference and adding a leak-free design to probe visual grounding vs text shortcuts.
articles.contribution: Validates all 13 reference-free metrics (incl. MLLM-as-Judge for identity/affective/instruction-following) against human preference via Pearson correlation and binary-classification accuracy.

articles.title: VidAudio-Bench: Benchmarking V2A and VT2A Generation across Four Audio Categories
articles.tldr: Task-specific reference-free V2A/VT2A audio-generation benchmark validating 13 metrics against human preference and adding a leak-free design to probe visual grounding vs text shortcuts.
articles.contribution: Critiques the raw VGG-Sound test set (co-occurring classes, modality misalignment per VGGSounder) and curates strictly audio-visually-correlated subsets across four audio categories.

articles.title: Towards Fine-Grained Text-to-3D Quality Assessment: A Benchmark and A Two-Stage Rank-Learning Metric
articles.tldr: Fine-grained Text-to-3D quality-assessment benchmark (129,600 human ratings, 12 dimensions) plus a rank-learning metric, exposing robustness limits of existing T23DQA metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows existing zero-shot and regression evaluators give inconsistent, non-robust cross-dimension predictions (HyperScore scores intact geometry only 3.32) and proposes Rank2Score better aligned with human MOS (SRCC 0.908 vs 0.809).

articles.title: Towards Fine-Grained Text-to-3D Quality Assessment: A Benchmark and A Two-Stage Rank-Learning Metric
articles.tldr: Fine-grained Text-to-3D quality-assessment benchmark (129,600 human ratings, 12 dimensions) plus a rank-learning metric, exposing robustness limits of existing T23DQA metrics.
articles.contribution: Argues coarse single-score metrics under-represent T23D quality and defines 12 fine-grained sub-dimensions (alignment, geometry loss/redundancy/roughness, authenticity) capturing distinct generative failure modes.

articles.title: On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation
articles.tldr: Builds and validates a large synthetic texture dataset (PTD, 246k images), confirming representativeness vs real DTD and uncovering a texture-driven NSFW-filter bias.
articles.contribution: Validates that prompt-generated PTD is more diverse yet still realistic vs real DTD (higher Inception, lower FID, matched Fourier power spectra), overcoming the convenience-sampled sub-100-image texture sets prior work relied on.

articles.title: On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation
articles.tldr: Builds and validates a large synthetic texture dataset (PTD, 246k images), confirming representativeness vs real DTD and uncovering a texture-driven NSFW-filter bias.
articles.contribution: A 9-rater, 900-image study validates each refinement stage (+3.4% quality, +4.5% representativeness) and confirms CLIP score tracks human representativeness judgments even on texture data.

articles.title: On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation
articles.tldr: Builds and validates a large synthetic texture dataset (PTD, 246k images), confirming representativeness vs real DTD and uncovering a texture-driven NSFW-filter bias.
articles.contribution: Uncovers that Stable Diffusion's NSFW safety filter flags up to 60% of benign texture images (nearly 100% of 'paisley' prompts), revealing a texture-driven confound in the safety classifier.

articles.title: Evaluating Cognitive Age Alignment in Interactive AI Agents
articles.tldr: WISC-grounded interactive benchmark measuring cognitive-age alignment of MLLM agents with construct-preserving tasks and harness confound controls, finding prompting changes surface style not underlying cognition.
articles.contribution: Grounds ten interactive subtests in WISC-IV / CHC cognitive constructs (Gc, Gf/Gv, WM, PSI) with child-psychologist review, mapping clinical items into web tasks while preserving the target construct.

articles.title: Evaluating Cognitive Age Alignment in Interactive AI Agents
articles.tldr: WISC-grounded interactive benchmark measuring cognitive-age alignment of MLLM agents with construct-preserving tasks and harness confound controls, finding prompting changes surface style not underlying cognition.
articles.contribution: Controls harness confounds: numbered-DOM labels ensure errors reflect reasoning not visual-localization failure, and item sequences are split across pages to prevent context-window leakage.

articles.title: Evaluating Cognitive Age Alignment in Interactive AI Agents
articles.tldr: WISC-grounded interactive benchmark measuring cognitive-age alignment of MLLM agents with construct-preserving tasks and harness confound controls, finding prompting changes surface style not underlying cognition.
articles.contribution: Uses age-normed WISC composite z-scores and trajectory monotonicity to distinguish genuine developmental differentiation from flat prompting, showing age labels change surface style not structural cognition.

articles.title: Simulating Eating Disorder Patients with LLMs: Evaluating Psychological Persona Stability in Multi-Turn Conversations
articles.tldr: Evaluates the validity of LLM eating-disorder patient simulation via dual self/observer assessment against validated EDE-Q ground truth, finding personas 'too stable and too inaccurate' through selective stereotyping.
articles.contribution: Shows selective stereotyping: cognitive-affective EDE-Q items saturate at ceiling regardless of case severity (case explains only 3% of Shape-Concern variance) while only behavioral Restraint tracks case, so the measure captures a lay stereotype not the graded clinical construct.

articles.title: Simulating Eating Disorder Patients with LLMs: Evaluating Psychological Persona Stability in Multi-Turn Conversations
articles.tldr: Evaluates the validity of LLM eating-disorder patient simulation via dual self/observer assessment against validated EDE-Q ground truth, finding personas 'too stable and too inaccurate' through selective stereotyping.
articles.contribution: Mitigates LLM-as-judge bias with three cross-provider observer raters yet still finds systematic judge bias (Gemini-as-judge rates 0.43 pts higher than GPT-as-judge) and poor inter-rater agreement (ICC .14-.43).

articles.title: AssertLLM2: A Comprehensive LLM Benchmark for Assertion Generation from Design Specifications
articles.tldr: Benchmark for LLM SystemVerilog assertion generation that fixes evaluation-validity flaws by using golden/buggy RTL as oracle (not input) and mutation-based bug detection beyond syntax/FPV.
articles.contribution: Shows syntax + FPV + COI coverage overestimate assertion quality (proven assertions can be trivial/vacuous/weak) and adds proof coverage plus mutation-based bug-kill ratio to measure true verification value.

articles.title: AssertLLM2: A Comprehensive LLM Benchmark for Assertion Generation from Design Specifications
articles.tldr: Benchmark for LLM SystemVerilog assertion generation that fixes evaluation-validity flaws by using golden/buggy RTL as oracle (not input) and mutation-based bug detection beyond syntax/FPV.
articles.contribution: Identifies that prior benchmarks feed golden RTL as generation input (oracle leakage that reduces the task to translation) and instead uses golden RTL only as an evaluation oracle, adding a buggy-RTL bug-hunting setting.

articles.title: AssertLLM2: A Comprehensive LLM Benchmark for Assertion Generation from Design Specifications
articles.tldr: Benchmark for LLM SystemVerilog assertion generation that fixes evaluation-validity flaws by using golden/buggy RTL as oracle (not input) and mutation-based bug detection beyond syntax/FPV.
articles.contribution: Uses structured specifications to remove document-quality variation so evaluation isolates model capability rather than being confounded by raw-PDF specification quality.

articles.title: CTIS-QA: Clinical Template-Informed Slide-Level Question Answering for Pathology
articles.tldr: Clinical-template pipeline and benchmark for pathology slide-level VQA that removes question-stem answer leakage and non-visual shortcuts and enforces CAP-protocol construct coverage.
articles.contribution: Replaces LLM-autogenerated VQA that leaks answers in question stems and includes image-independent questions with closed-ended, visually-grounded questions requiring genuine slide understanding.

articles.title: CTIS-QA: Clinical Template-Informed Slide-Level Question Answering for Pathology
articles.tldr: Clinical-template pipeline and benchmark for pathology slide-level VQA that removes question-stem answer leakage and non-visual shortcuts and enforces CAP-protocol construct coverage.
articles.contribution: Grounds question design in the CAP Cancer Protocols via a Clinical Pathology Report Template (38 diagnostic elements, six dimensions) with pathologist filtering to prevent omission of essential features and hallucinated content.

articles.title: CCiV: A Benchmark for Structure, Rhythm and Quality in LLM-Generated Chinese \textit{Ci} Poetry
articles.tldr: Benchmark for LLM-generated Chinese Ci poetry showing standard structural scoring underestimates capability because models emit valid historical variants; tonal harder than structural.
articles.contribution: Shows standard-form structural matching under-counts valid historical Cipai variants, misrepresenting true generation capability; variant-aware scoring recovers up to 18.66pp.

articles.title: CCiV: A Benchmark for Structure, Rhythm and Quality in LLM-Generated Chinese \textit{Ci} Poetry
articles.tldr: Benchmark for LLM-generated Chinese Ci poetry showing standard structural scoring underestimates capability because models emit valid historical variants; tonal harder than structural.
articles.contribution: Uses three top-tier LLM judges for literary quality and finds formal correctness does not predict aesthetic/informativeness scores (Deepseek-R1 leads quality without leading formal metrics).

articles.title: BenchBrowser: Retrieving Evidence for Evaluating Benchmark Validity
articles.tldr: BenchBrowser is a retrieval tool surfacing use-case-relevant benchmark items to help practitioners diagnose low content validity and low convergent validity across 20+ suites.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses content-validity gaps (narrow coverage of a capability's facets): swapping 'Python'->'Go' in a coding use-case sharply drops available relevant items, showing anchoring to one facet.

articles.title: BenchBrowser: Retrieving Evidence for Evaluating Benchmark Validity
articles.tldr: BenchBrowser is a retrieval tool surfacing use-case-relevant benchmark items to help practitioners diagnose low content validity and low convergent validity across 20+ suites.
articles.contribution: Quantifies convergent-validity failures via Kendall-tau rank divergence between gold and retrieved subsets, showing benchmarks purporting to measure the same capability can invert model rankings.

articles.title: Application of Propensity Score Models and Causal Estimators in Observational Studies under Model Misspecification
articles.tldr: Simulation study of causal estimators (IPW/AIPW/RSM) with ML-based propensity scores under model misspecification; doubly-robust AIPW stays stable while IPW is fragile.
articles.contribution: Systematically shows IPW is highly sensitive to propensity-score misspecification (large bias) while doubly-robust AIPW stays near-unbiased, guiding confounding control in observational studies.

articles.title: Application of Propensity Score Models and Causal Estimators in Observational Studies under Model Misspecification
articles.tldr: Simulation study of causal estimators (IPW/AIPW/RSM) with ML-based propensity scores under model misspecification; doubly-robust AIPW stays stable while IPW is fragile.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates flexible ML propensity-score estimators (random forest, SVM) produce extreme weights and unstable IPW estimates even when correctly specified, but remain safe within AIPW.
