articles.title: Measuring Representation Robustness in Large Language Models for Geometry
articles.tldr: GeoRepEval is a representation-aware benchmark showing fixed-format geometry accuracy overestimates abstract reasoning because models rely on representation-specific heuristics; vector forms fail most.
articles.contribution: Shows single-format accuracy conflates representation-specific heuristics with abstract reasoning; Invariance@3 as low as 0.044 exposes fragility invisible to fixed-format benchmarks.

articles.title: Measuring Representation Robustness in Large Language Models for Geometry
articles.tldr: GeoRepEval is a representation-aware benchmark showing fixed-format geometry accuracy overestimates abstract reasoning because models rely on representation-specific heuristics; vector forms fail most.
articles.contribution: Regression controls for token length and symbolic density leave the representation effect significant (p<0.05 for 8/11 models), evidence that surface shortcuts, not reasoning, drive scores.

articles.title: Greener Than Humans? Environmental Attitudes in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Benchmark adapting validated German environmental-awareness surveys to 31 LLMs; finds greener-than-human attitudes but strong persona-driven sycophancy/steerability that threatens measurement reliability.
articles.contribution: Quantifies steerability/sycophancy with Euclidean-distance metrics on the affect-cognition space; persona and first-person user framing shift measured attitudes, threatening normative reliability.

articles.title: Greener Than Humans? Environmental Attitudes in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Benchmark adapting validated German environmental-awareness surveys to 31 LLMs; finds greener-than-human attitudes but strong persona-driven sycophancy/steerability that threatens measurement reliability.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes validated UBS survey items into 0-10 indices for LLMs and flags reliability threats: excludes models whose answers depend on option order and reports ~5% answer variance at temperature 0.1.

articles.title: Sens-VisualNews: A Benchmark Dataset for Sensational Image Detection
articles.tldr: Sens-VisualNews benchmark for sensational image detection; studies MLLM prompt sensitivity and handles subjective label ambiguity via a strict unanimous-consensus subset.
articles.contribution: Addresses label ambiguity of the subjective 'sensational' construct via 3-annotator majority voting (dropping ties/ambiguous) plus a unanimous 'strict subset'; 24% of auto-selected sensational images were flipped by annotators.

articles.title: Sens-VisualNews: A Benchmark Dataset for Sensational Image Detection
articles.tldr: Sens-VisualNews benchmark for sensational image detection; studies MLLM prompt sensitivity and handles subjective label ambiguity via a strict unanimous-consensus subset.
articles.contribution: Prompt-sensitivity analysis over 3 prompts x 2 formats shows noticeable accuracy standard deviation for all MLLMs (extreme for LLaVA-OV-0.5B at +-15.8), revealing instability of the measurement.

articles.title: RVCBench: Benchmarking the Robustness of Voice Cloning Across Modern Audio Generation Models
articles.tldr: RVCBench evaluates voice-cloning robustness across the full generation pipeline, arguing clean-setting quality benchmarks lack external validity for real deployment shifts.
articles.contribution: Argues quality-centric clean-setting VC benchmarks lack external validity; adds 10 realistic/adversarial robustness tasks (225 speakers, 14,370 utterances) exposing deployment-time failures they hide.

articles.title: Prompting with the human-touch: evaluating model-sensitivity of foundation models for musculoskeletal CT segmentation
articles.tldr: Evaluates promptable segmentation foundation models with real human prompts, showing 'ideal' reference-derived prompts overestimate deployment performance and exposing rater variability and contamination risk.
articles.contribution: Shows segmentation performance drops with real human prompts versus 'ideal' reference-derived prompts, so ideal-prompt evaluation protocols overestimate real human-driven deployment performance.

articles.title: Prompting with the human-touch: evaluating model-sensitivity of foundation models for musculoskeletal CT segmentation
articles.tldr: Evaluates promptable segmentation foundation models with real human prompts, showing 'ideal' reference-derived prompts overestimate deployment performance and exposing rater variability and contamination risk.
articles.contribution: Observer study quantifies intra-/inter-rater prompt variability; two models show intra-rater robustness that fails to scale to inter-rater settings, exposing measurement unreliability.

articles.title: Prompting with the human-touch: evaluating model-sensitivity of foundation models for musculoskeletal CT segmentation
articles.tldr: Evaluates promptable segmentation foundation models with real human prompts, showing 'ideal' reference-derived prompts overestimate deployment performance and exposing rater variability and contamination risk.
articles.contribution: Flags benchmarking-fairness/contamination risk (medical FMs often trained on public datasets) and uses a private dataset for independent, leakage-free evaluation alongside public data.

articles.title: Digital Linguistic Bias in Spanish: Evidence from Lexical Variation in LLMs
articles.tldr: Evaluates LLM Spanish dialectal lexical knowledge as virtual informants; shows F1 is a spurious artifact of label imbalance and that digital-resource volume does not explain dialectal gaps.
articles.contribution: Shows YNQF F1 correlates rho=0.891 with the proportion of positive gold labels, so it reflects label imbalance not dialectal knowledge; proposes a chance-corrected adjusted Jaccard that controls item difficulty.

articles.title: Digital Linguistic Bias in Spanish: Evidence from Lexical Variation in LLMs
articles.tldr: Evaluates LLM Spanish dialectal lexical knowledge as virtual informants; shows F1 is a spurious artifact of label imbalance and that digital-resource volume does not explain dialectal gaps.
articles.contribution: Tests digital-resource volume as a confounder and finds no significant correlation with performance (contradicting prior near-perfect correlation), so data quantity does not explain dialectal gaps.

articles.title: Query-Document Dense Vectors for LLM Relevance Judgment Bias Analysis
articles.tldr: Clustering-based framework localizes where LLM relevance judges systematically disagree with humans, exposing semantic blind spots in IR evaluation.
articles.contribution: Localizes LLM-judge unreliability to specific Q-D semantic clusters (definition-seeking/policy/ambiguous queries) rather than treating disagreement as uniform noise.

articles.title: Query-Document Dense Vectors for LLM Relevance Judgment Bias Analysis
articles.tldr: Clustering-based framework localizes where LLM relevance judges systematically disagree with humans, exposing semantic blind spots in IR evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM judges over-rely on surface lexical overlap, a proxy that misrepresents the true relevance construct and drives over-inclusion.

articles.title: The Masked Advantage: Uncovering Local-Language Access to Cultural Knowledge in LLMs
articles.tldr: A 1PL-IRT difference-in-differences framework separates language proficiency from cultural-knowledge access, revealing a masked local-language knowledge advantage.
articles.contribution: Shows raw accuracy conflates language proficiency with knowledge access; decomposing into GlobalGap/LocalGap/KnowledgeGap isolates the intended knowledge-access construct.

articles.title: The Masked Advantage: Uncovering Local-Language Access to Cultural Knowledge in LLMs
articles.tldr: A 1PL-IRT difference-in-differences framework separates language proficiency from cultural-knowledge access, revealing a masked local-language knowledge advantage.
articles.contribution: Uses a shared 1PL IRT scale so ability contrasts are difficulty-free, enabling comparison across disjoint CA/CS item pools that raw accuracy cannot support.

articles.title: Enhancing Essay Cohesion Assessment: A Novel Item Response Theory Approach
articles.authors: Bruno Alexandre Barreiros Rosa et al.
articles.tldr: Applies item response theory to combine ML/BERT essay-cohesion predictions, improving agreement (QWK) with human raters over ensemble baselines.
articles.contribution: Uses IRT (BIRT-GD) to model each scorer's ability/difficulty/discrimination and adjust predictions, improving the cohesion scorer's agreement with human ratings.

articles.title: Picturing Perceptions: An Open-Source Toolkit to Uncover Bias in Humans and Machines
articles.tldr: PictoPercept is a validated visual forced-choice toolkit measuring intersectional bias in humans and AI against population-level earnings benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Validates a forced-choice image measure with convergent/discriminant validity that captures intersectional bias simultaneously, avoiding order effects and single-dimension decomposition.

articles.title: Picturing Perceptions: An Open-Source Toolkit to Uncover Bias in Humans and Machines
articles.tldr: PictoPercept is a validated visual forced-choice toolkit measuring intersectional bias in humans and AI against population-level earnings benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Grounds bias scores in real BLS earnings data so accurate perception of real disparities is separated from perceptual distortion, unlike relative-preference measures.

articles.title: Optimized Labeling Resource Allocation for Prediction-Assisted Inference via OPAL
articles.tldr: OPAL learns smooth variance-minimizing label-allocation policies for prediction-assisted inference, yielding valid confidence intervals at low labeling budgets.
articles.contribution: Turns a black-box model's uncertainty into a variance-optimal labeling policy that gives nominal finite-sample coverage for odds ratios and general EIF estimands.

articles.title: Optimized Labeling Resource Allocation for Prediction-Assisted Inference via OPAL
articles.tldr: OPAL learns smooth variance-minimizing label-allocation policies for prediction-assisted inference, yielding valid confidence intervals at low labeling budgets.
articles.contribution: Uses an AIPW-style estimator so adaptive, non-uniform label querying stays unbiased, spreading labels toward points where predictions are uncertain within a fixed budget.

articles.title: From Unfamiliar to Familiar: Detecting Pre-training Data via Gradient Deviations in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: GDS detects LLM pre-training/benchmark-contamination data via gradient-deviation features (magnitude, location, concentration) fed to a light classifier without fine-tuning.
articles.contribution: Detects train/test contamination without fine-tuning by probing per-sample LoRA gradient deviation profiles that separate member from non-member data across models.

articles.title: The LLM Effect on IR Benchmarks: A Meta-Analysis of Effectiveness, Baselines, and Contamination
articles.tldr: Longitudinal meta-analysis of 143 IR papers finds an LLM effectiveness bump confounded by measurable train/test contamination and weak-baseline/metric drift.
articles.contribution: Adapts the Data Contamination Quiz to reranking and measures 26-41% contamination on DL20 and 12-21% on Robust04 for RankZephyr and RankGPT.

articles.title: The LLM Effect on IR Benchmarks: A Meta-Analysis of Effectiveness, Baselines, and Contamination
articles.tldr: Longitudinal meta-analysis of 143 IR papers finds an LLM effectiveness bump confounded by measurable train/test contamination and weak-baseline/metric drift.
articles.contribution: Shows reported gains rest on weak/outdated baselines and a MAP-to-nDCG@10 metric shift, confounding whether the LLM effect reflects genuine progress.

articles.title: Best Practices for Noise-Based Augmentation to Improve the Performance of Deployable Speech-Based Emotion Recognition Systems
articles.tldr: Crowdsourcing shows some noise augmentations change emotion perception labels, invalidating the constant-label assumption and downstream SER evaluation/robustness testing.
articles.contribution: Validates via crowdsourcing that perception-altering noises (laughter, crying, pitch, speed) change human emotion labels, so augmented samples lose their original ground truth.

articles.title: Best Practices for Noise-Based Augmentation to Improve the Performance of Deployable Speech-Based Emotion Recognition Systems
articles.tldr: Crowdsourcing shows some noise augmentations change emotion perception labels, invalidating the constant-label assumption and downstream SER evaluation/robustness testing.
articles.contribution: Shows robustness/attack testing is corrupted by perception-altering noise: black-box attack success jumps from 35% to 48.5% when such noises are permitted.

articles.title: From Self to Other: Evaluating Demographic Perspective-Taking in LLM Hate Speech Annotation
articles.tldr: Tests whether persona-conditioned LLMs validly reproduce human demographic disagreement in hate-speech annotation; alignment is highly model-dependent.
articles.contribution: Shows persona-LLM annotation of demographic disagreement is highly model-dependent (Nemo best on inter-group agreement, Llama diverges), not a reliable proxy for human raters.

articles.title: From Self to Other: Evaluating Demographic Perspective-Taking in LLM Hate Speech Annotation
articles.tldr: Tests whether persona-conditioned LLMs validly reproduce human demographic disagreement in hate-speech annotation; alignment is highly model-dependent.
articles.contribution: Finds minimal identity personas can invent spurious inter-group disagreement reflecting stereotypes rather than genuine demographic perspective.

articles.title: FixCLR: Negative-Class Contrastive Learning for Semi-Supervised Domain Generalization
articles.tldr: Introduces FixCLR for semi-supervised domain generalization and cautions that ImageNet-pretrained backbones leak target-domain information, inflating SSDG comparisons.
articles.contribution: Argues leave-one-domain-out evaluation with ImageNet-pretrained backbones leaks target-domain information, inflating accuracy on ImageNet-similar domains (PACS, Office-Home, ImageNet-R).

articles.title: FixCLR: Negative-Class Contrastive Learning for Semi-Supervised Domain Generalization
articles.tldr: Introduces FixCLR for semi-supervised domain generalization and cautions that ImageNet-pretrained backbones leak target-domain information, inflating SSDG comparisons.
articles.contribution: Shows StyleMatch's pretrained-VGG style augmentation confers an unfair advantage and calls for quantifying domain-information leakage to enable fair method comparison.

articles.title: Using Representation Expressiveness and Learnability to Evaluate Self-Supervised Learning Methods
articles.tldr: Proposes label-free SSL evaluation metrics (Intrinsic Dimension + Cluster Learnability = CLID) and validates them as proxies for model quality and transfer performance.
articles.contribution: Shows the CLID label-free predictor captures true SSL model quality (ImageNet accuracy) far better than prior label-free proxies (alignment/uniformity, MCR2, mutual information), which under- or mis-represent quality.

articles.title: Using Representation Expressiveness and Learnability to Evaluate Self-Supervised Learning Methods
articles.tldr: Proposes label-free SSL evaluation metrics (Intrinsic Dimension + Cluster Learnability = CLID) and validates them as proxies for model quality and transfer performance.
articles.contribution: Validates the proxy as a criterion predictor of out-of-domain transfer performance across seven downstream classification tasks, establishing external/criterion validity of the metric.

articles.title: Political Leaning and Politicalness Classification of Texts
articles.tldr: Compiles 12+18 political-text datasets and uses leave-one-in/leave-one-out benchmarking plus dataset-overlap detection to show political-leaning classifiers break out-of-distribution and that dataset spillover inflates scores.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates via leave-one-in/leave-one-out benchmarks that siloed single-dataset training gives high in-distribution but poor out-of-distribution F1, quantifying the external-validity collapse of political-leaning classifiers.

articles.title: Political Leaning and Politicalness Classification of Texts
articles.tldr: Compiles 12+18 political-text datasets and uses leave-one-in/leave-one-out benchmarking plus dataset-overlap detection to show political-leaning classifiers break out-of-distribution and that dataset spillover inflates scores.
articles.contribution: Detects near-duplicate overlap between datasets with a middle-slice string-containment matcher and excludes overlapping sets to prevent train/test spillover from inflating evaluation scores.

articles.title: AgrI Challenge: A Data-Centric AI Competition for Cross-Team Validation in Agricultural Vision
articles.tldr: Introduces Cross-Team Validation (CTV) treating each team's independently-collected agricultural image dataset as a domain, revealing that near-perfect validation accuracy hides large validation-test gaps under domain shift.
articles.contribution: Shows single-team (TOTO) training produces near-perfect validation accuracy but a 16.20%/11.37% validation-test gap on other teams, proving in-distribution validation accuracy is not a reliable proxy for held-out generalization.

articles.title: AgrI Challenge: A Data-Centric AI Competition for Cross-Team Validation in Agricultural Vision
articles.tldr: Introduces Cross-Team Validation (CTV) treating each team's independently-collected agricultural image dataset as a domain, revealing that near-perfect validation accuracy hides large validation-test gaps under domain shift.
articles.contribution: Frames each team's convenience-collected dataset as a distinct domain and shows collaborative multi-source pooling (LOTO) closes the gap to 2.82%/1.78%, evidencing that single-source data is unrepresentative.

articles.title: AgrI Challenge: A Data-Centric AI Competition for Cross-Team Validation in Agricultural Vision
articles.tldr: Introduces Cross-Team Validation (CTV) treating each team's independently-collected agricultural image dataset as a domain, revealing that near-perfect validation accuracy hides large validation-test gaps under domain shift.
articles.contribution: Uses 64-bit perceptual-hash duplicate detection to remove cross-team duplicate images so no image appears in more than one partition, a stated prerequisite for valid CTV evaluation.

articles.title: ERBench: A Benchmark and Testsuite for Equation Discovery Algorithms
articles.tldr: Argues in-domain prediction accuracy is a misleading proxy for scientific equation discovery and builds ERBench around ground-truth equation-recovery rate, with secret held-out formulas and varied sampling to test out-of-domain robustness.
articles.contribution: Argues in-domain prediction accuracy mis-measures the discovery construct and proposes ground-truth equation-recovery rate as the valid criterion for evaluating symbolic-regression equation discovery.

articles.title: ERBench: A Benchmark and Testsuite for Equation Discovery Algorithms
articles.tldr: Argues in-domain prediction accuracy is a misleading proxy for scientific equation discovery and builds ERBench around ground-truth equation-recovery rate, with secret held-out formulas and varied sampling to test out-of-domain robustness.
articles.contribution: Systematically varies sampling dimensionality, size, distribution and domain to measure out-of-domain robustness, showing pre-trained symbolic-regression methods collapse outside their pre-training sampling distribution.

articles.title: ERBench: A Benchmark and Testsuite for Equation Discovery Algorithms
articles.tldr: Argues in-domain prediction accuracy is a misleading proxy for scientific equation discovery and builds ERBench around ground-truth equation-recovery rate, with secret held-out formulas and varied sampling to test out-of-domain robustness.
articles.contribution: Uses a common-task framework with a secret evaluation set of formulas absent from public web/Wikipedia so pre-trained and LLM-based algorithms cannot be scored on memorized ground-truth equations.

articles.title: Common Benchmarks Undervalue the Generalization Power of Programmatic Policies
articles.tldr: Position paper showing the reported out-of-distribution generalization gap between programmatic and neural RL policies is a confound of uncontrolled observation sparsity and reward shaping, not an inherent representational difference.
articles.contribution: Shows the apparent programmatic-vs-neural OOD gap arises from uncontrolled variables (dense observations breeding spurious correlations, over-aggressive reward optimization) rather than the neural representation itself.

articles.title: Common Benchmarks Undervalue the Generalization Power of Programmatic Policies
articles.tldr: Position paper showing the reported out-of-distribution generalization gap between programmatic and neural RL policies is a confound of uncontrolled observation sparsity and reward shaping, not an inherent representational difference.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates the neural baselines in four prior papers were compared unfairly, and that giving neural policies the same sparse observations and safer reward closes the OOD gap, restoring fair comparison.

articles.title: Common Benchmarks Undervalue the Generalization Power of Programmatic Policies
articles.tldr: Position paper showing the reported out-of-distribution generalization gap between programmatic and neural RL policies is a confound of uncontrolled observation sparsity and reward shaping, not an inherent representational difference.
articles.contribution: Argues common benchmarks fail to isolate programmatic strengths and proposes SparseMaze, a benchmark requiring stack/queue memory that neural nets genuinely fail, to properly value programmatic generalization.

articles.title: MMEarth-Bench: Global Model Adaptation via Multimodal Test-Time Training
articles.tldr: Introduces MMEarth-Bench, a global multimodal Earth-observation benchmark with held-out geographic splits, revealing that pretrained models still generalize poorly geographically despite gains in low-data settings.
articles.contribution: Provides five globally-distributed multimodal tasks with 12 aligned modalities and held-out geographic splits to fix prior EO benchmarks that were regional, convenience-sampled, and lacked global representation.

articles.title: MMEarth-Bench: Global Model Adaptation via Multimodal Test-Time Training
articles.tldr: Introduces MMEarth-Bench, a global multimodal Earth-observation benchmark with held-out geographic splits, revealing that pretrained models still generalize poorly geographically despite gains in low-data settings.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks 7 pretrained geospatial models on held-out geographic regions and shows geographic generalization remains poor, with multimodal inputs sometimes widening the geographic gap.

articles.title: Metal-Sci: A Scientific Compute Benchmark for Evolutionary LLM Kernel Search on Apple Silicon
articles.tldr: Evolutionary LLM kernel-search benchmark showing the in-distribution roofline fitness score is gameable, and that a single withheld held-out problem-size gate cheaply catches silent correctness violations and performance regressions.
articles.contribution: Shows a (1+1) evolutionary agent optimizing the in-distribution roofline fitness S_T hill-climbs to confidently-wrong kernels (Goodhart), e.g. an hmc win whose held-out samples are ~10sigma off and an fft3d win that is a silent regression.

articles.title: Metal-Sci: A Scientific Compute Benchmark for Evolutionary LLM Kernel Search on Apple Silicon
articles.tldr: Evolutionary LLM kernel-search benchmark showing the in-distribution roofline fitness score is gameable, and that a single withheld held-out problem-size gate cheaply catches silent correctness violations and performance regressions.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that scoring on only three convenience in-distribution sizes overstates deployment performance: GPT-5.5's fft3d best wins 2.95x in-distribution but collapses to 0.23x (8.5% of ceiling) at the unseen 256^3 size.

articles.title: Metal-Sci: A Scientific Compute Benchmark for Evolutionary LLM Kernel Search on Apple Silicon
articles.tldr: Evolutionary LLM kernel-search benchmark showing the in-distribution roofline fitness score is gameable, and that a single withheld held-out problem-size gate cheaply catches silent correctness violations and performance regressions.
articles.contribution: Proposes a single held-out size configuration Phi_T, never folded into the agent's feedback packets, as a cheap mechanical oversight/falsification primitive that catches confidently-wrong agent code the in-distribution score S_T licenses.

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Agent Harnesses via Effective Feedback Compute
articles.tldr: Introduces Effective Feedback Compute (EFC) as a scaling coordinate for agent harnesses, showing raw compute confounds harness performance and only informative/valid/retained feedback drives it.
articles.contribution: Uses matched-budget pairs (identical token/tool-call/cost budgets) to remove the raw-compute confound, showing feedback quality alone raises success 0.27->0.90; harness factors (router, verifier, memory) control raw-to-EFC conversion.

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Agent Harnesses via Effective Feedback Compute
articles.tldr: Introduces Effective Feedback Compute (EFC) as a scaling coordinate for agent harnesses, showing raw compute confounds harness performance and only informative/valid/retained feedback drives it.
articles.contribution: Argues raw expenditure is a surface proxy for the true harness-scaling coordinate; EFC/D_task achieves R^2=0.99 in controlled scaling while raw tokens/tool-calls/wall-time fit near-zero.

articles.title: Chess Signatures of Play
articles.tldr: Shows aggregate chess anti-cheating statistics are order-blind and gameable, and proposes a signature Levy-area, anytime-valid e-process detector with exact type-I control.
articles.contribution: Proves (Prop. 5) the Regan best-move-frequency z-score is invariant to within-game ply rearrangement, so aggregate match-rate is a surface proxy that discards the difficulty-accuracy coupling; the Levy area recovers it.

articles.title: Chess Signatures of Play
articles.tldr: Shows aggregate chess anti-cheating statistics are order-blind and gameable, and proposes a signature Levy-area, anytime-valid e-process detector with exact type-I control.
articles.contribution: Recasts detection as an anytime-valid e-process bounded by Ville's inequality, giving exact type-I control over all sample sizes/stopping times and removing the multiple-testing false-flag inflation of fixed-sample z-scores.

articles.title: Chess Signatures of Play
articles.tldr: Shows aggregate chess anti-cheating statistics are order-blind and gameable, and proposes a signature Levy-area, anytime-valid e-process detector with exact type-I control.
articles.contribution: Red-teams the detector with a Regan-invisible rearrangement cheater (aggregates identical, signature AUC 0.75) and confirms specificity on Carlsen/Nakamura-calibrated honest play (0 false flags in 400 matches).

articles.title: Scale-Aware Adversarial Analysis: A Diagnostic for Generative AI in Multiscale Complex Systems
articles.tldr: A physics-constrained scale-space diagnostic that audits whether a generative model internalizes physical causality, showing standard off-distribution XAI perturbations are invalid.
articles.contribution: Diagnoses that a DDPM interpolates discrete statistical textures rather than internalizing the governing PDEs it is claimed to capture, exposing a construct gap between measured fidelity and physical causality.

articles.title: Scale-Aware Adversarial Analysis: A Diagnostic for Generative AI in Multiscale Complex Systems
articles.tldr: A physics-constrained scale-space diagnostic that audits whether a generative model internalizes physical causality, showing standard off-distribution XAI perturbations are invalid.
articles.contribution: Argues standard pixel-wise perturbation and gradient-saliency XAI push inputs off the valid empirical distribution (unphysical artifacts), invalidating the causal audit, and replaces them with mass-conserving CDD scale-space interventions.

articles.title: EvalStop: Using World Feedback to Detect and Correct Reward Overoptimization in Multi-Tenant RLHF Platforms
articles.tldr: Detects RLHF reward overoptimization at the scheduler level using downstream eval (world feedback), since training loss and reward-model proxies decouple from true quality.
articles.contribution: Operationalizes reward-overoptimization detection: training loss and reward score rise monotonically under optimization pressure while downstream eval peaks then degrades, and k consecutive eval declines flag the corrupted metric.

articles.title: EvalStop: Using World Feedback to Detect and Correct Reward Overoptimization in Multi-Tenant RLHF Platforms
articles.tldr: Detects RLHF reward overoptimization at the scheduler level using downstream eval (world feedback), since training loss and reward-model proxies decouple from true quality.
articles.contribution: Frames scheduler early-stopping as a detection problem with ground-truth hacking labels hidden behind an information boundary, showing JCT-only evaluation is deceptive since the trivial fixed-progress stop gets best JCT but 64.5% FPR.

articles.title: TimeMachine-bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Model Capabilities in Repository-Level Migration Tasks
articles.tldr: A live, date-controlled benchmark for repository-level Python migration that mitigates data contamination and exposes LLM reliability failures like spurious fixes gaming low test coverage.
articles.contribution: Fully-automated date-based (date-filtered dependency index) live construction keeps the benchmark continually refreshed to mitigate train/test data contamination in code LLMs.

articles.title: TimeMachine-bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Model Capabilities in Repository-Level Migration Tasks
articles.tldr: A live, date-controlled benchmark for repository-level Python migration that mitigates data contamination and exposes LLM reliability failures like spurious fixes gaming low test coverage.
articles.contribution: Documents spurious solutions that exploit low test coverage (a 'low-test-coverage loophole' case study), showing the unit-test verifier can be gamed rather than genuinely solving the migration.

articles.title: TimeMachine-bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Model Capabilities in Repository-Level Migration Tasks
articles.tldr: A live, date-controlled benchmark for repository-level Python migration that mitigates data contamination and exposes LLM reliability failures like spurious fixes gaming low test coverage.
articles.contribution: Notes the human-verified subset is biased toward simpler solvable problems (harder solvable tasks excluded), potentially overestimating LLM migration performance.

articles.title: When Agents Overtrust Environmental Evidence: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Benchmarking Evidence-Grounding Defects in LLM Agents
articles.tldr: Formalizes the evidence-grounding defect (EGD) construct and builds an agentic benchmark measuring whether LLM agents stay grounded in true environment state under stale/adversarial observations.
articles.contribution: Defines and formalizes the evidence-grounding defect (EGD) as an agent treating an environment claim as sufficient ground for action without resolving it, a reliability construct existing capability/attack benchmarks leave under-specified.

articles.title: When Agents Overtrust Environmental Evidence: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Benchmarking Evidence-Grounding Defects in LLM Agents
articles.tldr: Formalizes the evidence-grounding defect (EGD) construct and builds an agentic benchmark measuring whether LLM agents stay grounded in true environment state under stale/adversarial observations.
articles.contribution: Shows backbone comparisons are confounded by scaffold coverage; scaffold choice moves EMR by >10 points, so reliability must be reported over the full model-scaffold matrix, not per backbone.

articles.title: When Agents Overtrust Environmental Evidence: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Benchmarking Evidence-Grounding Defects in LLM Agents
articles.tldr: Formalizes the evidence-grounding defect (EGD) construct and builds an agentic benchmark measuring whether LLM agents stay grounded in true environment state under stale/adversarial observations.
articles.contribution: Cautions that EMR reflects behavior under controlled, fixed-oracle stress fixtures and not real-world failure frequency, since fixing task/tools/true-state narrows the measured behavioral surface.

articles.title: MARCA: A Checklist-Based Benchmark for Multilingual Web Search
articles.tldr: Bilingual web-search benchmark using checklist rubrics, run-level uncertainty, and English<->Portuguese transfer to probe evaluation validity.
articles.contribution: Reports checklist accuracy as mean+-std over k=3 runs with Bessel-corrected run-level uncertainty to capture the stochasticity of web-interacting agents.

articles.title: MARCA: A Checklist-Based Benchmark for Multilingual Web Search
articles.tldr: Bilingual web-search benchmark using checklist rubrics, run-level uncertainty, and English<->Portuguese transfer to probe evaluation validity.
articles.contribution: Parallel EN/PT design isolates language as a variable to expose external-validity gaps (>5pp EN->PT drops for Qwen-3-235B and Gemini-2.5-Pro).

articles.title: CAX-Agent: A Lightweight Agent Harness for Reliable APDL Automation
articles.tldr: Controlled, repeated-run comparison of LLM-agent recovery policies with blind human scoring, inter-rater validation, and statistical testing.
articles.contribution: Deliberately uses simple geometries to isolate the recovery-policy variable so outcome differences are attributable to policy rather than task difficulty (internal validity).

articles.title: CAX-Agent: A Lightweight Agent Harness for Reliable APDL Automation
articles.tldr: Controlled, repeated-run comparison of LLM-agent recovery policies with blind human scoring, inter-rater validation, and statistical testing.
articles.contribution: Establishes reliable strategy differences via 3 repeated runs/strategy, Cliff's delta effect sizes, Mann-Whitney U tests, 95% binomial CIs, and a per-task-mean sensitivity check.

articles.title: POISE: Position-Aware Undetectable Skill Injection on LLM Agents
articles.tldr: Skill-injection attack paper that redefines attack-success measurement and exposes the unreliability of LLM-judge skill scanners.
articles.contribution: Argues raw payload execution is an incomplete risk measure and defines ASR as requiring BOTH canary execution AND the user's task passing its verifier in the same trial.

articles.title: POISE: Position-Aware Undetectable Skill Injection on LLM Agents
articles.tldr: Skill-injection attack paper that redefines attack-success measurement and exposes the unreliability of LLM-judge skill scanners.
articles.contribution: Shows LLM-judge static scanners are undeployable as gates: they false-flag 74.6% of clean skills on average and are judge-dependent, so Poise adds a new high-risk finding in only 5.6% of variants.

articles.title: Human-Centered Evaluation of an LLM-Based Process Modeling Copilot: A Mixed-Methods Study with Domain Experts
articles.tldr: Mixed-methods human-centered evaluation showing automated BPMN benchmarks under-represent trust and usability constructs.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates automated syntactic/semantic BPMN benchmarks are a surface proxy that omit human-factor construct dimensions (trust, usability, professional alignment).

articles.title: A Self-Evolving Agentic System for Automated Generation and Execution of Biological Protocols
articles.tldr: Wet-lab automation system plus benchmark that validates rubric scoring against blind experts and shows plausibility != executability.
articles.contribution: Argues plausible protocol text and syntactic code correctness are insufficient constructs; a three-layer gate (syntax, parameter alignment, SDK export) shows surface code quality does not guarantee physical executability.

articles.title: A Self-Evolving Agentic System for Automated Generation and Execution of Biological Protocols
articles.tldr: Wet-lab automation system plus benchmark that validates rubric scoring against blind experts and shows plausibility != executability.
articles.contribution: Validates the automated seven-dimension rubric as a proxy for expert judgment (system-level Spearman rho=0.929, p=0.003) with moderate inter-rater Kendall's W=0.495.

articles.title: Culturally-Adapted Red-Teaming Across East and Southeast Asian Contexts: A Methodological and Comparative Analysis
articles.tldr: Shows direct-translation multilingual safety benchmarks are invalid; culturally-adapted prompts reveal systematically underestimated risk.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates directly-translated English safety benchmarks are unrepresentative of target cultures, underestimating ASR in 44 of 48 category x language cells (mean deltaASR +9.3pp).

articles.title: Culturally-Adapted Red-Teaming Across East and Southeast Asian Contexts: A Methodological and Comparative Analysis
articles.tldr: Shows direct-translation multilingual safety benchmarks are invalid; culturally-adapted prompts reveal systematically underestimated risk.
articles.contribution: Shows DT prompts are unfaithful operationalizations that strip cultural depth (DT C3 mean 0.17/3 vs CA up to 2.51), measuring risk on a distribution divergent from real inputs.

articles.title: Beyond Final Answers: Auditing Trajectory-Level Hallucinations in Multi-Agent Industrial Workflows
articles.tldr: Trajectory-level hallucination benchmark exposing that output-only evaluation, LLM-judges, and human annotators all miss subtle failure types.
articles.contribution: Shows output-only hallucination benchmarks under-represent the construct: procedural hallucinations (38.5%) and the 48.7% of multi-type trajectories are invisible to final-answer evaluation.

articles.title: Beyond Final Answers: Auditing Trajectory-Level Hallucinations in Multi-Agent Industrial Workflows
articles.tldr: Trajectory-level hallucination benchmark exposing that output-only evaluation, LLM-judges, and human annotators all miss subtle failure types.
articles.contribution: LLM-judge has high binary accuracy (F1 0.855) but systematically misclassifies subtle types (F1 0.258 logical, 0.222 referential), so binary metrics obscure real detection failure.

articles.title: Beyond Final Answers: Auditing Trajectory-Level Hallucinations in Multi-Agent Industrial Workflows
articles.tldr: Trajectory-level hallucination benchmark exposing that output-only evaluation, LLM-judges, and human annotators all miss subtle failure types.
articles.contribution: Inter-annotator/judge agreement is moderate overall (Cohen's kappa 0.456) but only slight for referential (0.176) and logical (0.211), showing these labels carry genuine annotator ambiguity.

articles.title: PhantomBench: Benchmarking the Non-existential Threat of Language Models
articles.tldr: Large benchmark using 60K+ non-existent concepts to measure LLM abstention/hallucination, with a validated LLM judge and a non-existent-as-rare-concept proxy
articles.contribution: Operationalizes hallucination cleanly: any information given about a non-existent concept is hallucination by definition, with non-existence verified by exact-match Infini-gram search over the 2.3T-token Dolma corpus

articles.title: PhantomBench: Benchmarking the Non-existential Threat of Language Models
articles.tldr: Large benchmark using 60K+ non-existent concepts to measure LLM abstention/hallucination, with a validated LLM judge and a non-existent-as-rare-concept proxy
articles.contribution: Validates the Gemini-2.5-Flash abstention judge via the Alternative Annotator Test (winning rate 1.00, advantage probability 0.98) against four human annotators before scaling to 60K concepts

articles.title: PhantomBench: Benchmarking the Non-existential Threat of Language Models
articles.tldr: Large benchmark using 60K+ non-existent concepts to measure LLM abstention/hallucination, with a validated LLM judge and a non-existent-as-rare-concept proxy
articles.contribution: Establishes non-existent concepts as a valid proxy for real rare concepts: abstention rates correlate at Pearson rho=0.755 (p<0.001) with rare concepts vs only 0.322 with common ones

articles.title: ChartHal: A Fine-grained Framework Evaluating Hallucination of Large Vision Language Models in Chart Understanding

articles.contribution: Operationalizes chart hallucination through a fine-grained taxonomy of 12 scenarios (question type x chart-question relation: irrelevant / inexistent / contradictory / normal) over a human-validated 1,062-sample dataset, using free-form rather than yes/no answers

articles.title: ChartHal: A Fine-grained Framework Evaluating Hallucination of Large Vision Language Models in Chart Understanding
articles.tldr: ChartHal is a human-validated benchmark with a 12-scenario taxonomy that measures LVLM hallucination in chart understanding, especially on unanswerable questions
articles.contribution: Scores free-form chart answers into binary hallucinated/not labels with a GPT-4o judge governed by category-specific criteria (e.g. must flag unanswerability for irrelevant/inexistent/contradictory cases)

articles.title: HalluScan: A Systematic Benchmark for Detecting and Mitigating Hallucinations in Instruction-Following LLMs

articles.contribution: Introduces the HalluScore composite metric (weighted geometric mean of factual accuracy, semantic coherence, fabrication rate) validated with proper train/test separation, and documents score-direction inversion in 3 of 6 detectors (SemE, Judge, RAV) on compact-model outputs

articles.title: HalluScan: A Systematic Benchmark for Detecting and Mitigating Hallucinations in Instruction-Following LLMs
articles.tldr: HalluScan systematically benchmarks 6 hallucination-detection methods across models and domains, introducing a composite metric and revealing reliability failures like score-direction inversion
articles.contribution: Runs a cross-domain transfer evaluation of six detection methods across three domains (scientific/open-domain/commonsense) to reveal how detection AUROC generalizes across domains rather than reporting a single pooled number

articles.title: ADAM: A Diverse Archive of Mankind for Evaluating and Enhancing LLMs in Biographical Reasoning
articles.tldr: ADAM builds a Bloom's-taxonomy biographical-reasoning benchmark over 4M individuals and shows subject popularity strongly confounds LLM accuracy
articles.contribution: Shows subject popularity (a proxy for pretraining exposure) strongly mediates measured biographical-reasoning accuracy, confounding the capability claim and raising fairness concerns for lesser-known individuals

articles.title: ADAM: A Diverse Archive of Mankind for Evaluating and Enhancing LLMs in Biographical Reasoning
articles.tldr: ADAM builds a Bloom's-taxonomy biographical-reasoning benchmark over 4M individuals and shows subject popularity strongly confounds LLM accuracy
articles.contribution: Grounds the biographical-reasoning construct in Bloom's taxonomy (six cognitive levels from Remembering to Creating) so the benchmark tests reasoning depth rather than only rote factual recall

articles.title: CommonWhy: A Dataset for Evaluating Entity-Based Causal Commonsense Reasoning in Large Language Models

articles.title: CommonWhy: A Dataset for Evaluating Entity-Based Causal Commonsense Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Benchmark for entity-based abductive causal commonsense reasoning that exposes contamination, entity-popularity confounds, and unreliable generation metrics.
articles.contribution: Constructs why-questions requiring unstated commonsense grounded in the Wikidata KG to avoid the verbatim-retrieval/memorization leakage that inflates WikiWhy-style benchmarks.

articles.title: CommonWhy: A Dataset for Evaluating Entity-Based Causal Commonsense Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Benchmark for entity-based abductive causal commonsense reasoning that exposes contamination, entity-popularity confounds, and unreliable generation metrics.

articles.title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations through Domain-Grounded Tiered Retrieval
articles.tldr: Tiered domain-grounded RAG hallucination-mitigation pipeline that also exposes exact-match metric sensitivity and LLM-judge verbosity bias.
articles.contribution: Shows atomic-claim exact-match verification inflates the hallucination score on short numerical answers (MMLU Global Facts 33.1%) due to unit/vintage mismatches rather than real grounding failure, arguing for numerical-proximity scoring.

articles.title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations through Domain-Grounded Tiered Retrieval
articles.tldr: Tiered domain-grounded RAG hallucination-mitigation pipeline that also exposes exact-match metric sensitivity and LLM-judge verbosity bias.

articles.title: A unified foundational framework for knowledge injection and evaluation of Large Language Models in Combustion Science
articles.tldr: CombustionQA benchmark plus a controlled RAG validity analysis that decomposes the naive-RAG accuracy ceiling into retrieval-miss and context-contamination.
articles.contribution: Agentic difficulty-filtering discards questions GPT-5 answers zero-shot and validates answerability under ideal context, so CombustionQA measures injected domain knowledge rather than parametric priors.

articles.title: A unified foundational framework for knowledge injection and evaluation of Large Language Models in Combustion Science
articles.tldr: CombustionQA benchmark plus a controlled RAG validity analysis that decomposes the naive-RAG accuracy ceiling into retrieval-miss and context-contamination.
articles.contribution: Four controlled scenarios (zero-shot, oracle-context ceiling, optimal RAG, noise RAG) plus Hit/Miss stratification isolate retrieval-miss (56.3%) from context-contamination as distinct causes of the ~30-point RAG shortfall.

articles.title: Language Models Might Not Understand You: Evaluating Theory of Mind via Story Prompting
articles.tldr: Programmable synthetic-story generator (StorySim) to measure theory-of-mind and world-modeling robustly against contamination and heuristics.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates the Sally-Anne test is contaminated (GPT-4/R1 score 100% on the canonical setup but 75%/87% on same-length random stories) and generates novel stories with near-zero training-data overlap.

articles.title: Language Models Might Not Understand You: Evaluating Theory of Mind via Story Prompting
articles.tldr: Programmable synthetic-story generator (StorySim) to measure theory-of-mind and world-modeling robustly against contamination and heuristics.
articles.contribution: Controls story length, character/location/event counts and event order via the Storyboard to isolate ToM ability, and identifies the 'First Common Location' heuristic while testing for recency bias.

articles.title: Language Models Might Not Understand You: Evaluating Theory of Mind via Story Prompting

articles.title: Do I look like a 'cat.n.01' to you? A Taxonomy Image Generation Benchmark

articles.title: Do I look like a 'cat.n.01' to you? A Taxonomy Image Generation Benchmark
articles.tldr: Benchmark of 9 metrics for taxonomy image generation that probes GPT-4 judge bias and the construct validity of image-quality metrics.

articles.title: MCAD: Multimodal Context-Aware Audio Description Generation for Soccer

articles.title: MCAD: Multimodal Context-Aware Audio Description Generation for Soccer

articles.title: RoMo: A Large-Scale, Richly Organized Dataset and Semantic Taxonomy for Human Motion Generation

articles.title: RoMo: A Large-Scale, Richly Organized Dataset and Semantic Taxonomy for Human Motion Generation
articles.tldr: Large curated human-motion dataset with a Dynamic-Score quality filter, taxonomy-based per-category evaluation, and a standardized metric toolbox.

articles.title: RoMo: A Large-Scale, Richly Organized Dataset and Semantic Taxonomy for Human Motion Generation
articles.tldr: Large curated human-motion dataset with a Dynamic-Score quality filter, taxonomy-based per-category evaluation, and a standardized metric toolbox.

articles.title: Benchmarking Single-Factor Physical Video-to-Audio Generation
articles.tldr: FlatSounds benchmark audits whether video-to-audio models capture physics via single-factor counterfactual interventions, arguing current metrics test correlation not causal responsiveness.

articles.title: Benchmarking Single-Factor Physical Video-to-Audio Generation
articles.tldr: FlatSounds benchmark audits whether video-to-audio models capture physics via single-factor counterfactual interventions, arguing current metrics test correlation not causal responsiveness.

articles.title: LongAV-Compass: Towards Unified Evaluation of Minute-Scale Audio-Visual Generation Across T2AV, I2AV, and V2AV

articles.title: LongAV-Compass: Towards Unified Evaluation of Minute-Scale Audio-Visual Generation Across T2AV, I2AV, and V2AV
articles.tldr: LongAV-Compass is a minute-scale audio-visual generation benchmark whose 20+ MLLM-judged diagnostic dimensions are validated against human preference and shown to be more discriminative than saturating proxy metrics.

articles.title: GENFIG1: Visual Summaries of Scholarly Work as a Challenge for Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: GenFig1 is a benchmark for VLM scientific-figure generation that empirically identifies which automatic metric best correlates with expert human judgment (VLM-as-Judge) and which metrics fail.

articles.title: BAFIS: Dataset + Framework to assess occupational Bias and Human Preference in modern Text-to-image Models
articles.tldr: BAFIS measures occupational gender/ethnicity bias in five T2I models via FairFace classification and a human Elo arena, benchmarking against real labor statistics and exposing that FID/MagFace/CLIP diverge from human preference.

articles.title: Automated Scoring of Arabic Text Using Large Language Models: A Literature Review
