articles.title: Automated Scoring of Arabic Text Using Large Language Models: A Literature Review
articles.tldr: A literature review of LLM-based automated scoring of Arabic essays and short answers, proposing a five-dimension taxonomy and diagnosing reliability, construct-alignment and generalizability gaps in current scoring systems.
articles.contribution: Identifies that no reviewed scoring system aligns with a recognized competency referential framework, leaving scores technically computed but pedagogically/construct-invalid.

articles.title: Controlling Equational Reasoning in Large Language Models with Prompt Interventions
articles.tldr: Studies LLM equational-derivation reasoning under symbolic prompt interventions and shows reference-based generation metrics strongly disagree with human and template-based error evaluation, producing misleading rankings.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that n-gram reference-based metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/BLEURT/GLEU) misrepresent mathematical-reasoning quality and yield misleading model rankings versus human evaluation.

articles.title: Controlling Equational Reasoning in Large Language Models with Prompt Interventions
articles.tldr: Studies LLM equational-derivation reasoning under symbolic prompt interventions and shows reference-based generation metrics strongly disagree with human and template-based error evaluation, producing misleading rankings.
articles.contribution: Uses controlled symbolic prompt interventions (variable renaming, expression exchange, alternative goal, step removal) whose distributional footprints causally control specific mathematical error types.

articles.title: FloAt: Flow Warping of Self-Attention for Clothing Animation Generation
articles.tldr: FloAt is a training-free clothing-animation generation method that also empirically shows standard perceptual metrics (LPIPS, SSIM, CLIP) are unsuitable for capturing the subtle motion the task cares about.
articles.contribution: Shows that well-established metrics LPIPS/SSIM/CLIP capture only high-level object/scene characteristics and fail to measure the subtle clothing-motion construct, showing near-identical scores across very different methods.

articles.title: A Benchmark for Text Expansion: Datasets, Metrics, and Baselines
articles.tldr: Introduces the Text Expansion task with datasets, baselines and evaluation metrics, proposing the Info-Gain informativeness metric validated against human judgment and documenting biases in PPL and NLI-based coherence metrics.
articles.contribution: Proposes the Info-Gain metric (infill-perplexity ratio with a diff-distinct penalty) to measure expansion informativeness and validates it against human ratings.

articles.title: A Benchmark for Text Expansion: Datasets, Metrics, and Baselines
articles.tldr: Introduces the Text Expansion task with datasets, baselines and evaluation metrics, proposing the Info-Gain informativeness metric validated against human judgment and documenting biases in PPL and NLI-based coherence metrics.
articles.contribution: Documents that PPL-based fluency favours generic high-frequency text and NLI entailment coherence is confounded by expansion length, so those metrics misrepresent quality.

articles.title: HuM-Eval: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Human-Centric Video Evaluation
articles.tldr: Existing video-gen metrics measure global scene statistics and miss human anatomical/motion fidelity; proposes a coarse-to-fine metric with higher human correlation.
articles.contribution: Shows FVD/VBench/VLM metrics track global scene quality as a surface proxy, failing to capture the intended human anatomical and motion fidelity construct.

articles.title: HuM-Eval: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Human-Centric Video Evaluation
articles.tldr: Existing video-gen metrics measure global scene statistics and miss human anatomical/motion fidelity; proposes a coarse-to-fine metric with higher human correlation.
articles.contribution: Exposes 'geometric blindness' of VLM judges (Qwen3-VL prefers a physically-impossible flip video), motivating explicit 2D-pose and 3D-motion scorers to refine the VLM prior.

articles.title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: Survey of hallucination in large vision-language models: taxonomy, evaluation methods/benchmarks, root causes, and mitigations of visual-textual faithfulness failures.
articles.contribution: Catalogs and contrasts discriminative (POPE/NOPE/CIEM accuracy) versus generative (FAITHScore, LLM-judge rating) hallucination-evaluation instruments and their differing reliability.

articles.title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: Survey of hallucination in large vision-language models: taxonomy, evaluation methods/benchmarks, root causes, and mitigations of visual-textual faithfulness failures.
articles.contribution: Defines visual hallucination as object/attribute/relation misalignment and notes object-only benchmarks under-represent the broader faithfulness construct.

articles.title: Political Compass or Spinning Arrow? Towards More Meaningful Evaluations for Values and Opinions in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Constrained multiple-choice value evaluations (Political Compass Test) give unstable, format-dependent, non-paraphrase-robust results; realistic open-ended evaluation is preferable but still unstable.
articles.contribution: Shows forcing multiple-choice compliance fabricates a construct: unforced, Zephyr and three GPT models give zero valid answers, so PCT operationalization does not reflect inherent model values.

articles.title: Political Compass or Spinning Arrow? Towards More Meaningful Evaluations for Values and Opinions in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Constrained multiple-choice value evaluations (Political Compass Test) give unstable, format-dependent, non-paraphrase-robust results; realistic open-ended evaluation is preferable but still unstable.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates measurement is unreliable: minimal semantics-preserving paraphrases move PCT coordinates more than the Biden-Trump gap and flip 23/62 propositions for GPT-3.5.

articles.title: Political Compass or Spinning Arrow? Towards More Meaningful Evaluations for Values and Opinions in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Constrained multiple-choice value evaluations (Political Compass Test) give unstable, format-dependent, non-paraphrase-robust results; realistic open-ended evaluation is preferable but still unstable.
articles.contribution: Shows constrained surveys lack ecological/external validity: realistic open-ended responses flip stance on roughly one third of propositions versus the multiple-choice setting.

articles.title: deltaBLEU: A Discriminative Metric for Generation Tasks with Intrinsically Diverse Targets
articles.tldr: Embeds human quality ratings of references directly into multi-reference BLEU (deltaBLEU) so the automatic metric correlates better with human judgments on diverse-target generation.
articles.contribution: deltaBLEU weights n-gram matches by human quality ratings of references (rewarding good, penalizing bad), reducing BLEU's surface-proxy mismatch for intrinsically diverse targets.

articles.title: deltaBLEU: A Discriminative Metric for Generation Tasks with Intrinsically Diverse Targets
articles.tldr: Embeds human quality ratings of references directly into multi-reference BLEU (deltaBLEU) so the automatic metric correlates better with human judgments on diverse-target generation.
articles.contribution: Validates the metric via rank correlation with human ratings at 100-sentence observation units, showing improved and more stable correlation than BLEU/sentence-BLEU.

articles.title: AIGCIQA2023: A Large-scale Image Quality Assessment Database for AI Generated Images: from the Perspectives of Quality, Authenticity and Correspondence
articles.tldr: Large-scale subjective IQA database for AI-generated images that benchmarks whether existing IQA metrics validly measure human-perceived quality, authenticity, and text-image correspondence.
articles.contribution: Shows no-reference IQA metrics built on natural-image priors mis-measure AI-generated-image quality, correlating poorly with human MOS especially on text-image correspondence.

articles.title: AIGCIQA2023: A Large-scale Image Quality Assessment Database for AI Generated Images: from the Perspectives of Quality, Authenticity and Correspondence
articles.tldr: Large-scale subjective IQA database for AI-generated images that benchmarks whether existing IQA metrics validly measure human-perceived quality, authenticity, and text-image correspondence.
articles.contribution: Disentangles AIGI perceptual quality into three distinct target constructs (quality, authenticity, text-image correspondence) rather than a single quality score.

articles.title: Min-K%++: Improved Baseline for Detecting Pre-Training Data from Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Reference-free pre-training data / contamination detector that normalizes token log-probability against the full vocabulary distribution to flag memorized or leaked evaluation text.
articles.contribution: Improves detection of train/test contamination and memorization via a calibrated token-probability membership-inference score requiring no reference model.

articles.title: NL-Augmenter: A Framework for Task-Sensitive Natural Language Augmentation
articles.tldr: Participatory NL augmentation framework whose perturbation transformations are used to reveal quasi-systematic robustness drops in popular language models under meaning-preserving input changes.
articles.contribution: Perturbation-based robustness testing shows clean benchmark accuracy overstates model performance on realistic input variations not covered by the evaluation set.

articles.title: Large Language Models Can be Lazy Learners: Analyze Shortcuts in In-Context Learning
articles.tldr: Shows LLMs exploit shortcut/spurious trigger-label mappings in in-context prompts, measured with anti-shortcut test sets, and that larger models rely on shortcuts more (reverse scaling).
articles.contribution: Demonstrates in-context-learning accuracy is confounded by shortcut trigger-label mappings, breaking the link between the measured score and genuine task ability.

articles.title: Large Language Models Can be Lazy Learners: Analyze Shortcuts in In-Context Learning
articles.tldr: Shows LLMs exploit shortcut/spurious trigger-label mappings in in-context prompts, measured with anti-shortcut test sets, and that larger models rely on shortcuts more (reverse scaling).
articles.contribution: Shows how injected trigger cues (words, symbols, sentences, text styles) embedded in the prompt operationalization act as exploitable shortcut features that the measurement fails to control for.

articles.title: ICE-Score: Instructing Large Language Models to Evaluate Code
articles.tldr: Instructed-LLM judge (ICE-Score) for reference-free code evaluation, validated by criterion correlation with functional correctness and human usefulness against token-matching metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows token-matching metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) mis-measure code quality and that an instructed LLM judge better tracks functional correctness and human usefulness without references or test oracles.

articles.title: ICE-Score: Instructing Large Language Models to Evaluate Code
articles.tldr: Instructed-LLM judge (ICE-Score) for reference-free code evaluation, validated by criterion correlation with functional correctness and human usefulness against token-matching metrics.
articles.contribution: Argues LLM-judge code evaluation using post-2022 generated-code annotations is minimally affected by benchmark data contamination, unlike prior NLG-judge validation studies.

articles.title: GRUEN for Evaluating Linguistic Quality of Generated Text
articles.tldr: A reference-less unsupervised metric (GRUEN) for linguistic quality of generated text, validated by high correlation with human judgments.
articles.contribution: Builds a reference-less deterministic scorer for the neglected linguistic-quality construct that content-overlap metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) mis-represent, and validates it against human quality judgments.

articles.title: Latent Jailbreak: A Benchmark for Evaluating Text Safety and Output Robustness of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: A latent-jailbreak benchmark arguing safety-only evaluation is incomplete without jointly measuring output robustness / over-refusal.
articles.contribution: Shows safety-only jailbreak benchmarks mis-represent the trustworthiness construct because over-refusal is scored as safe, and proposes a joint safety+robustness trustworthiness metric.

articles.title: Latent Jailbreak: A Benchmark for Evaluating Text Safety and Output Robustness of Large Language Models
articles.tldr: A latent-jailbreak benchmark arguing safety-only evaluation is incomplete without jointly measuring output robustness / over-refusal.
articles.contribution: Validates a fine-tuned RoBERTa auto-labeler against human safety/robustness annotations to make large-scale scoring of jailbreak outputs reliable.

articles.title: Perturbation CheckLists for Evaluating NLG Evaluation Metrics
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation showing NLG metrics fail targeted perturbation checks and cannot capture multiple mutually-uncorrelated human criteria with one score.
articles.contribution: Proposes 34 criteria-targeted perturbation checklists as falsification evidence that a metric actually detects the criterion it claims, going beyond human-correlation.

articles.title: Perturbation CheckLists for Evaluating NLG Evaluation Metrics
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation showing NLG metrics fail targeted perturbation checks and cannot capture multiple mutually-uncorrelated human criteria with one score.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that human criteria (fluency, coverage, etc.) are largely uncorrelated so a single aggregated metric score cannot represent the multi-dimensional quality construct.

articles.title: Improving Generation and Evaluation of Visual Stories via Semantic Consistency
articles.tldr: Story-visualization model paper that critiques exact-match metrics as misjudging quality and proposes character F-score plus a copying-resistant discriminative evaluation.
articles.contribution: Argues image-level exact-match character accuracy under-represents generation quality and proposes micro-averaged F-score, validated by correlation with human visual-quality ratings.

articles.title: Improving Generation and Evaluation of Visual Stories via Semantic Consistency
articles.tldr: Story-visualization model paper that critiques exact-match metrics as misjudging quality and proposes character F-score plus a copying-resistant discriminative evaluation.
articles.contribution: Introduces discriminative evaluation with hard-negative frames so a model that copies exact training frames instead of generating is not rewarded by the metric.

articles.title: HinGE: A Dataset for Generation and Evaluation of Code-Mixed Hinglish Text
articles.tldr: Code-mixed Hinglish generation/evaluation dataset (HinGE) demonstrating popular NLG metrics fail to capture code-mixed text quality.
articles.contribution: Shows five popular monolingual NLG metrics (BLEU/NIST/BERTScore/WER/TER) do not transport to code-mixed Hinglish, under-counting quality that humans rate as acceptable.

articles.title: HinGE: A Dataset for Generation and Evaluation of Code-Mixed Hinglish Text
articles.tldr: Code-mixed Hinglish generation/evaluation dataset (HinGE) demonstrating popular NLG metrics fail to capture code-mixed text quality.
articles.contribution: Analyzes metric-human correlation across quality buckets, exposing that these metrics are especially unreliable for low-quality code-mixed sentences.

articles.title: A Gold Standard Methodology for Evaluating Accuracy in Data-To-Text Systems
articles.tldr: Gold-standard human error-annotation protocol for accuracy of data-to-text NLG, used to validate automated accuracy metrics like RG.
articles.contribution: Defines a categorized (number/name/word/context/not-checkable/other) multi-annotator error-marking protocol merged by majority, giving a reproducible human gold standard for text-accuracy annotation with Fleiss kappa 0.79.

articles.title: A Gold Standard Methodology for Evaluating Accuracy in Data-To-Text Systems
articles.tldr: Gold-standard human error-annotation protocol for accuracy of data-to-text NLG, used to validate automated accuracy metrics like RG.
articles.contribution: Uses the gold standard to validate the IE-based RG accuracy metric, showing it recalls only 34-39% of gold name/number errors and cannot detect word/context/not-checkable errors, undermining prior >90% RG scores.

articles.title: DEAM: Dialogue Coherence Evaluation using AMR-based Semantic Manipulations
articles.tldr: Shows text-level negative sampling makes trainable dialogue-coherence metrics a poor proxy; DEAM uses AMR semantic manipulations to build valid negatives, tripling human correlation.
articles.contribution: Argues heuristic text-level manipulations (utterance shuffling/insertion) produce negatives that do not represent real chatbot incoherence, so the trained metric captures a surface proxy; replaces them with four AMR-level semantic perturbations (contradiction, coreference inconsistency, irrelevancy, decreased engagement).

articles.title: DEAM: Dialogue Coherence Evaluation using AMR-based Semantic Manipulations
articles.tldr: Shows text-level negative sampling makes trainable dialogue-coherence metrics a poor proxy; DEAM uses AMR semantic manipulations to build valid negatives, tripling human correlation.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates the reliability gap of the resulting scorer against human coherence judgments: baseline metrics reach near-zero or negative Spearman correlation while DEAM's negatives raise a RoBERTa metric to 0.47 (FED coherence).

articles.title: MIRAI: Evaluating LLM Agents for Event Forecasting
articles.tldr: A temporal event-forecasting agent benchmark (MIRAI) built with explicit look-ahead-leakage prevention and analysis of how the tool-use scaffold confounds measured forecasting ability.
articles.contribution: Prevents temporal look-ahead leakage when constructing the GDELT forecasting set by aligning each event date with its news publish date and filtering low-mention sources.

articles.title: MIRAI: Evaluating LLM Agents for Event Forecasting
articles.tldr: A temporal event-forecasting agent benchmark (MIRAI) built with explicit look-ahead-leakage prevention and analysis of how the tool-use scaffold confounds measured forecasting ability.
articles.contribution: Shows the code/tool-use agent scaffold confounds the measured forecasting capability, since the ability to generate coherent long code blocks distinguishes reliable agents.

articles.title: Chain of Explanation: New Prompting Method to Generate Quality Natural Language Explanation for Implicit Hate Speech
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluates automatic NLG metrics against human ratings for implicit-hate-speech explanations, finding word-overlap metrics track human judgment poorly and annotator agreement is low.
articles.contribution: Ranks automatic explanation-quality metrics by Spearman correlation with human informativeness/clarity, showing surface word-overlap metrics under-capture the quality construct.

articles.title: Chain of Explanation: New Prompting Method to Generate Quality Natural Language Explanation for Implicit Hate Speech
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluates automatic NLG metrics against human ratings for implicit-hate-speech explanations, finding word-overlap metrics track human judgment poorly and annotator agreement is low.
articles.contribution: Documents severe annotator disagreement in the ground-truth quality ratings, forcing a switch from crowdworkers to trained expert raters.

articles.title: Identity Decoupling for Multi-Subject Personalization of Text-to-Image Models
articles.tldr: Introduces the Detect-and-Compare (D&C) metric because existing CLIP-I/DINOv2 fidelity metrics ignore identity mixing, then validates it against human judgments.
articles.contribution: Argues CLIP-I and DINOv2 mis-measure multi-subject fidelity because they do not account for identity mixing, and proposes D&C to capture the intended construct.

articles.title: Identity Decoupling for Multi-Subject Personalization of Text-to-Image Models
articles.tldr: Introduces the Detect-and-Compare (D&C) metric because existing CLIP-I/DINOv2 fidelity metrics ignore identity mixing, then validates it against human judgments.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory validity evidence that D&C tracks human judgment via Spearman correlation and AUROC comparisons against baseline metrics.

articles.title: Sensitivity and Robustness of Large Language Models to Prompt Template in Japanese Text Classification Tasks
articles.tldr: Shows LLM text-classification accuracy swings wildly across semantically-equivalent Japanese prompt templates, exposing measurement instability.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that benchmark accuracy hinges on arbitrary prompt-template wording, so the prompt operationalization injects variance rather than faithfully measuring capability.

articles.title: Global Explainability of BERT-Based Evaluation Metrics by Disentangling along Linguistic Factors
articles.tldr: Regression + adversarial analysis shows BERT-based NLG metrics (BERTScore, MoverScore, BLEURT) are dominated by lexical overlap rather than pure semantics, exposing a construct/surface-proxy limitation.
articles.contribution: Linear-regression disentangling of metric scores along semantics/syntax/morphology/lexical-overlap shows all BERT-based metrics are heavily driven by lexical overlap, not the assumed semantic-similarity construct.

articles.title: Global Explainability of BERT-Based Evaluation Metrics by Disentangling along Linguistic Factors
articles.tldr: Regression + adversarial analysis shows BERT-based NLG metrics (BERTScore, MoverScore, BLEURT) are dominated by lexical overlap rather than pure semantics, exposing a construct/surface-proxy limitation.
articles.contribution: Adversarial preference test (low-overlap paraphrase B vs high-overlap non-paraphrase C) provides falsifying evidence that metrics are not robust and prefer the high-lexical-overlap non-paraphrase.

articles.title: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
articles.tldr: Auto-constructed multi-domain code benchmark (DomainEval) shows capability measurement is heavily domain-biased and that common benchmarks like HumanEval over-represent easy/common tasks.
articles.contribution: Argues common code benchmarks under-sample domain-specific tasks and builds an auto-constructed multi-domain benchmark that exposes a domain-performance gap of up to 68.94% in some LLMs, showing capability scores are unrepresentative.

articles.title: NLG Evaluation Metrics Beyond Correlation Analysis: An Empirical Metric Preference Checklist
articles.tldr: A 'metric preference checklist' assesses NLG automatic metrics beyond correlation, testing faithfulness to human preference and effectiveness at discriminating system-level performance.
articles.contribution: Introduces a five-part metric preference checklist showing correlation-to-human does not represent a metric's actual effectiveness at discerning quality levels and system-level performance.

articles.title: NLG Evaluation Metrics Beyond Correlation Analysis: An Empirical Metric Preference Checklist
articles.tldr: A 'metric preference checklist' assesses NLG automatic metrics beyond correlation, testing faithfulness to human preference and effectiveness at discriminating system-level performance.
articles.contribution: Transfer experiment tests whether the metric-human correlation level is consistent across in-domain vs out-of-domain NLG use cases (external validity of metric evaluation).

articles.title: Towards Explainable Evaluation Metrics for Natural Language Generation
articles.tldr: Position/taxonomy paper on explainable NLG evaluation metrics; argues opaque black-box metrics block adoption and shows current adversarial techniques cannot auto-identify metric limitations.
articles.contribution: Provides a taxonomy of goals/properties for explainable NLG metrics, arguing distrust/opacity of black-box metrics blocks adoption while surface metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) remain fundamentally flawed for semantics.

articles.title: Towards Explainable Evaluation Metrics for Natural Language Generation
articles.tldr: Position/taxonomy paper on explainable NLG evaluation metrics; argues opaque black-box metrics block adoption and shows current adversarial techniques cannot auto-identify metric limitations.
articles.contribution: Novel experiments find current adversarial NLP techniques are unsuitable for automatically diagnosing high-quality metric limitations because the attacks are not meaning-preserving.

articles.title: What is the Best Automated Metric for Text to Motion Generation?
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation of automated text-to-motion metrics against human ratings; none correlate at the sample level, so a learned metric (MoBERT) is proposed.
articles.contribution: Shows standard text-to-motion metrics (FID, R-Precision, coordinate errors) are weak proxies for human-judged naturalness/faithfulness and introduces MoBERT as a better-correlated learned proxy.

articles.title: What is the Best Automated Metric for Text to Motion Generation?
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation of automated text-to-motion metrics against human ratings; none correlate at the sample level, so a learned metric (MoBERT) is proposed.
articles.contribution: Quantifies that existing automated scorers are unreliable at the per-sample level (near-zero Pearson correlation with human ratings), only becoming usable when averaged to the model level.

articles.title: DOVE: A Large-Scale Multi-Dimensional Predictions Dataset Towards Meaningful LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Large-scale (250M-prediction) study showing LLM benchmark scores and rankings are highly sensitive to arbitrary prompt-format perturbations, undermining single-prompt evaluation.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that the prompt operationalization (enumerators, separators, ordering, phrasing, demonstrations) injects large arbitrary variance into multiple-choice accuracy, so single-prompt scores are unstable proxies of capability.

articles.title: DOVE: A Large-Scale Multi-Dimensional Predictions Dataset Towards Meaningful LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Large-scale (250M-prediction) study showing LLM benchmark scores and rankings are highly sensitive to arbitrary prompt-format perturbations, undermining single-prompt evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows model rankings flip under prompt perturbations and provides efficient prompt-selection strategies (independent dimension-wise selection) to make comparisons across models fairer and more reproducible.

articles.title: So-Fake: Benchmarking and Explaining Social Media Image Forgery Detection
articles.tldr: Social-media image-forgery detection benchmark with a dedicated out-of-domain test set to measure dataset representativeness and cross-domain generalization of detectors.
articles.contribution: Argues existing forgery-detection datasets lack the diversity, scale, and realism of social-media contexts and builds So-Fake-Set (>2M images from 35 generators) as a more representative evaluation set.

articles.title: So-Fake: Benchmarking and Explaining Social Media Image Forgery Detection
articles.tldr: Social-media image-forgery detection benchmark with a dedicated out-of-domain test set to measure dataset representativeness and cross-domain generalization of detectors.
articles.contribution: Establishes So-Fake-OOD, a 100K out-of-domain benchmark with commercial generators explicitly excluded from training, to measure external validity / generalization of forgery detectors to unseen generative technologies.

articles.title: Designing AI-Agents With Personalities: A Psychometric Approach
articles.tldr: Psychometric approach to assign and validate Big-Five personalities in LLM agents; construct validity holds partially while safety-alignment confounds moral responses.
articles.contribution: Applies psychometric validation (embedding cosine similarity, BFI-2/Mini-Marker correlations, factor analysis) to test whether assigned Big-Five personalities are validly captured in LLM agents rather than surface artifacts.

articles.title: Designing AI-Agents With Personalities: A Psychometric Approach
articles.tldr: Psychometric approach to assign and validate Big-Five personalities in LLM agents; construct validity holds partially while safety-alignment confounds moral responses.
articles.contribution: Tests criterion/external validity on risk-taking and moral-dilemma vignettes, finding safety-aligned models systematically inflate 'moral' ratings, a confound to the intended personality-decision measurement.

articles.title: Evaluating the Correctness of Explainable AI Algorithms for Classification
articles.tldr: Method to quantitatively evaluate the correctness/validity of XAI feature-attribution explainers (SHAP, LIME) using synthetic datasets with known explanation ground truth.
articles.contribution: Constructs classification datasets from formal grammars with known ground-truth explanations, removing dependence on subjective human labels, and defines a k-accuracy verifier to score explanation correctness.

articles.title: Evaluating the Correctness of Explainable AI Algorithms for Classification
articles.tldr: Method to quantitatively evaluate the correctness/validity of XAI feature-attribution explainers (SHAP, LIME) using synthetic datasets with known explanation ground truth.
articles.contribution: Quantitatively compares SHAP vs LIME against ground truth, showing SHAP is a more valid feature-importance measure and that explainer accuracy correlates with classification accuracy and degrades with dataset complexity.

articles.title: SMART: Simulated Students Aligned with Item Response Theory for Question Difficulty Prediction
articles.tldr: IRT-aligned LLM simulated students (trained via DPO) to predict open-ended item difficulty, validating both simulator faithfulness and the LLM scorer's reliability.
articles.contribution: Validates that IRT-aligned (DPO) simulated students faithfully represent real student ability and response distributions (via theta-Align, FID, MAUVE), so the simulated population is a valid stand-in for difficulty estimation.

articles.title: SMART: Simulated Students Aligned with Item Response Theory for Question Difficulty Prediction
articles.tldr: IRT-aligned LLM simulated students (trained via DPO) to predict open-ended item difficulty, validating both simulator faithfulness and the LLM scorer's reliability.
articles.contribution: Reports the reliability of the LLM-based scoring model used to score simulated open-ended responses, and analyzes fidelity/outlier failure modes that propagate into IRT difficulty estimates.

articles.title: Assessing ASR Model Quality on Disordered Speech using BERTScore
articles.tldr: Shows WER is a surface proxy that mis-measures disordered-speech ASR utility and that BERTScore aligns far better with expert human judgment.
articles.contribution: Argues WER captures surface word-overlap not the meaning-preserving construct; BERTScore (F_BERT) is a semantically valid proxy that scores meaning-preserving normalization/contraction errors correctly (e.g. F_BERT=1.00 vs Word Acc 0.50 for 'Beyonce').

articles.title: Assessing ASR Model Quality on Disordered Speech using BERTScore
articles.tldr: Shows WER is a surface proxy that mis-measures disordered-speech ASR utility and that BERTScore aligns far better with expert human judgment.
articles.contribution: Statistically quantifies scorer reliability: F_BERT has lower variance (SD=0.142 vs 0.274), better discriminates severity levels (ANOVA F=684 vs 209), and lower AIC (5854 vs 6733) fitting SLP assessments.

articles.title: ConceptBed: Evaluating Concept Learning Abilities of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
articles.tldr: Introduces ConceptBed and the oracle-classifier CCD metric to validly measure T2I concept learning, human-validated, exposing a concept-vs-composition trade-off.
articles.contribution: Proposes Concept Confidence Deviation (CCD) using supervised oracle concept classifiers to measure concept fidelity, arguing prior metrics (DINO/CLIPScore cosine similarity) mis-represent concept alignment and cannot rank methods.

articles.title: ConceptBed: Evaluating Concept Learning Abilities of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
articles.tldr: Introduces ConceptBed and the oracle-classifier CCD metric to validly measure T2I concept learning, human-validated, exposing a concept-vs-composition trade-off.
articles.contribution: Validates scorer reliability: CCD correlates with human MTurk judgments (correlation up to -0.9892, far above CLIPScore) and is reported as the mean across three oracle-training seeds to show stability.

articles.title: KITAB: Evaluating LLMs on Constraint Satisfaction for Information Retrieval
articles.tldr: KITAB is a controlled, leakage-resistant benchmark for constraint-satisfaction IR that decouples LLM factual failure modes across popularity, constraint type and context.
articles.contribution: Provides a dynamic data-collection workflow on a disjoint author list to confront benchmark saturation and training-data contamination (explicitly citing verbatim SQuAD/MMLU/BEIR leakage in GPT4), enabling fresh leakage-resistant test sets.

articles.title: KITAB: Evaluating LLMs on Constraint Satisfaction for Information Retrieval
articles.tldr: KITAB is a controlled, leakage-resistant benchmark for constraint-satisfaction IR that decouples LLM factual failure modes across popularity, constraint type and context.
articles.contribution: Deliberately samples 611 authors across popularity (WikiData sitelinks) and constrainedness (kappa=1-S/N) rather than convenience-sampling, controlling the evaluation set so failure modes can be attributed rather than confounded.

articles.title: FACTOID: FACtual enTailment fOr hallucInation Detection
articles.tldr: Argues textual-entailment 'support' misrepresents factuality, proposes span-based Factual Entailment plus the FACTOID benchmark and an automated HVI index to rank LLMs by hallucination.
articles.contribution: Empirically shows conventional textual entailment mis-measures hallucination (an 'Obama'-for-'Biden' text is judged 'support'), and defines Factual Entailment with span detection + factual verification as a construct-valid detector, +40% accuracy over SoTA TE.

articles.title: FACTOID: FACtual enTailment fOr hallucInation Detection
articles.tldr: Argues textual-entailment 'support' misrepresents factuality, proposes span-based Factual Entailment plus the FACTOID benchmark and an automated HVI index to rank LLMs by hallucination.
articles.contribution: Introduces the automated Hallucination Vulnerability Index (HVI_auto), a 0-100 aggregation over 2,500 prompts using damping/exponential-smoothing normalization to produce a stable comparative hallucination ranking of 15 LLMs.

articles.title: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
articles.tldr: ReliabilityBench shows single-run agent benchmarks overestimate production reliability across consistency, robustness, and fault tolerance.
articles.contribution: pass^k over repeated runs exposes that single-run pass@1 overestimates agent reliability by 20-40%.

articles.title: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
articles.tldr: ReliabilityBench shows single-run agent benchmarks overestimate production reliability across consistency, robustness, and fault tolerance.
articles.contribution: Paraphrase perturbations and fault injection show clean benchmark scores do not transfer to production-like conditions.

articles.title: Image2Text2Image: A Novel Framework for Label-Free Evaluation of Image-to-Text Generation with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
articles.tldr: A reference-free image-captioning metric via a text-to-image round-trip, better correlated with human judgment and sensitive to hallucinations.
articles.contribution: Reference-free round-trip cosine metric correlates with human caption-quality judgment better than surface BLEU/ROUGE metrics.

articles.title: Image2Text2Image: A Novel Framework for Label-Free Evaluation of Image-to-Text Generation with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
articles.tldr: A reference-free image-captioning metric via a text-to-image round-trip, better correlated with human judgment and sensitive to hallucinations.
articles.contribution: Detects VLLM caption hallucinations (non-existent objects) that n-gram and CLIP-based metrics fail to catch.

articles.title: In-Depth Look at Word Filling Societal Bias Measures
articles.tldr: Control-group and word-frequency analyses show the StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs bias measures lack validity.
articles.contribution: Shows StereoSet/CrowS scores reflect word-frequency priors, a surface proxy rather than the intended bias construct.

articles.title: In-Depth Look at Word Filling Societal Bias Measures
articles.tldr: Control-group and word-frequency analyses show the StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs bias measures lack validity.
articles.contribution: Control-group experiments reveal 30-40% false-positive rates, so scores cannot support a confound-free causal claim of bias.

articles.title: RepEval: Effective Text Evaluation with LLM Representation
articles.tldr: RepEval scores text quality by projecting LLM hidden representations, correlating with humans better than GPT-4 with far fewer parameters.
articles.contribution: A representation-projection scorer is more reliable and human-correlated than unstable generation-based LLM-prompt judges.

articles.title: STAMP Your Content: Proving Dataset Membership via Watermarked Rephrasings
articles.tldr: STAMP: watermarked-rephrasing framework that proves dataset/benchmark membership in LLM pretraining via a paired t-test, detecting contamination at <0.001% of tokens.
articles.contribution: Detects benchmark train/test contamination via a paired perplexity t-test on watermarked public/private rephrases, reaching p=1.2e-4 to 6.6e-6 even when a benchmark is <0.001% of pretraining tokens and appears once.

articles.title: STAMP Your Content: Proving Dataset Membership via Watermarked Rephrasings
articles.tldr: STAMP: watermarked-rephrasing framework that proves dataset/benchmark membership in LLM pretraining via a paired t-test, detecting contamination at <0.001% of tokens.
articles.contribution: Identifies that prior rephrase-based contamination tests confound membership with the general LLM preference for LLM-generated over human text, and removes it by generating both compared versions with the same process differing only in watermark keys.

articles.title: Can Large Language Models Address Open-Target Stance Detection?
articles.tldr: Introduces open-target stance detection and a BERT-based target-quality metric (BTSD) validated as a reliable human-correlated proxy for scoring open-ended target generation.
articles.contribution: Proposes BTSD, a fine-tuned BERTweet stance classifier used to score generated-target quality when no predefined gold-target list exists, and validates it as a reliable proxy that tracks human judgment better than embedding cosine (SemSim).

articles.title: Challenge on Sound Scene Synthesis: Evaluating Text-to-Audio Generation
articles.tldr: DCASE Sound-Scene-Synthesis challenge that validates the FAD objective metric against human perceptual ratings for text-to-audio generation.
articles.contribution: Validates Frechet Audio Distance as a system-ranking metric against human listening tests, showing the PANNs-embedding variant (FAD-P) is the only statistically-significant, human-aligned choice among candidate embeddings.

articles.title: Challenge on Sound Scene Synthesis: Evaluating Text-to-Audio Generation
articles.tldr: DCASE Sound-Scene-Synthesis challenge that validates the FAD objective metric against human perceptual ratings for text-to-audio generation.
articles.contribution: Shows FAD-P captures audio-text correspondence (foreground/background fit) but correlates only weakly with perceptual audio quality, so it under-represents the quality construct it is often assumed to measure.

articles.title: Best-of-N through the Smoothing Lens: KL Divergence and Regret Analysis
articles.tldr: Theory-plus-experiments showing Soft Best-of-N smoothing mitigates proxy-reward overoptimization (Goodhart/reward hacking) relative to Best-of-N.
articles.contribution: Derives finite-sample KL-divergence and regret bounds quantifying how a misspecified proxy reward drives Best-of-N overoptimization, and characterizes regimes where Soft Best-of-N with tuned temperature attains lower regret than BoN under a low-quality proxy reward.

articles.title: The Language of Dialogue Is Complex
articles.tldr: Argues automated integrative-complexity scoring must model linguistic structure (not content) and builds a syntactically-grounded classifier with large-scale external-validity evidence.
articles.contribution: Critiques prior automated integrative-complexity scorers as construct-misrepresenting because they score content while IC is theoretically a measure of structure, and builds a classifier from theory-motivated syntactic features that adheres to the IC coding process.

articles.title: The Language of Dialogue Is Complex
articles.tldr: Argues automated integrative-complexity scoring must model linguistic structure (not content) and builds a syntactically-grounded classifier with large-scale external-validity evidence.
articles.contribution: Provides external/ecological-validity evidence by deploying the IC tool at scale on 400k+ Reddit comments and replicating key findings of prior small-scale human-coded IC studies.

articles.title: PanorAMS: Automatic Annotation for Detecting Objects in Urban Context
articles.tldr: Automatic noisy urban bounding-box annotations plus a crowdsourced clean ground-truth set, with analysis of how label and box-location noise degrade detection.
articles.contribution: Quantifies the class-label and bounding-box-location noise of geospatially auto-generated annotations against a 147k-box crowdsourced clean ground truth and measures its downstream effect on detection performance.

articles.title: The Equilibrium Response of Atmospheric Machine-Learning Models to Uniform Sea Surface Temperature Warming
articles.tldr: Evaluates whether ML atmosphere models generalize out-of-distribution by comparing their response to uniform +2K SST warming against a physics-based GCM.
articles.contribution: Tests the out-of-distribution external validity of ML climate emulators (ACE2-ERA5, NeuralGCM, cBottle) by comparing their equilibrium response to a warming scenario outside their training distribution against physics-GCM (AM4) and observational diagnostics.

articles.title: Antidote: A Unified Framework for Mitigating LVLM Hallucinations in Counterfactual Presupposition and Object Perception
articles.tldr: CP-Bench exposes that object-hallucination benchmarks overlook counterfactual-presupposition questions, under-representing the construct.
articles.contribution: Builds CP-Bench to operationalize counterfactual-presupposition robustness, showing existing POPE/CHAIR benchmarks omit this facet of the hallucination construct.

articles.title: High-quality Data-to-Text Generation for Severely Under-Resourced Languages with Out-of-the-box Large Language Models
articles.tldr: LLMs reach human parity by human evaluation while BLEU collapses, questioning BLEU's construct validity for non-task-specific systems.
articles.contribution: Empirically shows BLEU under-represents generation quality: it collapses for four under-resourced languages while human judgments rate outputs on par with humans.

articles.title: Mark-Evaluate: Assessing Language Generation using Population Estimation Methods
articles.tldr: Population-estimation NLG metrics that separate quality and diversity and correlate better with human judgment than existing metrics.
articles.contribution: Introduces ME_Schnabel, a double-valued metric that separates quality and diversity constructs which single-valued generation metrics conflate.

articles.title: Mark-Evaluate: Assessing Language Generation using Population Estimation Methods
articles.tldr: Population-estimation NLG metrics that separate quality and diversity and correlate better with human judgment than existing metrics.
articles.contribution: Validates the metrics' reliability by demonstrating higher correlation with human judgment than existing metrics across three generation tasks.

articles.title: EquivaMap: Leveraging LLMs for Automatic Equivalence Checking of Optimization Formulations
articles.tldr: Formalizes optimization-formulation equivalence and shows heuristic equivalence checks rely on unreliable surface proxies.
articles.contribution: Defines Quasi-Karp equivalence, a formal criterion for when two optimization formulations are equivalent based on a mapping between their decision variables.

articles.title: EquivaMap: Leveraging LLMs for Automatic Equivalence Checking of Optimization Formulations
articles.tldr: Formalizes optimization-formulation equivalence and shows heuristic equivalence checks rely on unreliable surface proxies.
articles.contribution: Shows existing equivalence checks (execution accuracy and canonical/heuristic tests) are surface proxies that misjudge equivalence, e.g. failing under variable rescaling.

articles.title: SAGE: A Generic Framework for LLM Safety Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues single-turn generic safety benchmarks miss multi-turn and application-specific harms; multi-turn adversarial evaluation with a validated LLM judge.
articles.contribution: Shows single-turn generic benchmarks under-represent deployment harm: harm steadily increases with conversation length in multi-turn adversarial dialogues.

articles.title: SAGE: A Generic Framework for LLM Safety Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues single-turn generic safety benchmarks miss multi-turn and application-specific harms; multi-turn adversarial evaluation with a validated LLM judge.
articles.contribution: Motivates application-specific, persona-diverse (Big Five) adversarial seeds rather than generic single-policy test sets to represent real usage.

articles.title: SAGE: A Generic Framework for LLM Safety Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues single-turn generic safety benchmarks miss multi-turn and application-specific harms; multi-turn adversarial evaluation with a validated LLM judge.
articles.contribution: Validates the automated LLM harm evaluator against human expert agreement and checks run-to-run stability of the scoring.

articles.title: Quality Prediction of AI Generated Images and Videos: Emerging Trends and Opportunities
articles.tldr: Survey/position: existing IQA/VQA measure reconstruction fidelity, not generative quality, and GenAI quality datasets/metrics are inadequate.
articles.contribution: Argues existing IQA/VQA models measure reconstruction fidelity against a pristine reference and were not designed to assess generative artifacts, a construct mismatch for GenAI quality.

articles.title: Quality Prediction of AI Generated Images and Videos: Emerging Trends and Opportunities
articles.tldr: Survey/position: existing IQA/VQA measure reconstruction fidelity, not generative quality, and GenAI quality datasets/metrics are inadequate.

articles.title: MeDiSumQA: Patient-Oriented Question-Answer Generation from Discharge Letters
articles.tldr: Patient-oriented medical QA benchmark that validates automatic metrics against physician judgment and addresses data contamination.
articles.contribution: Reports that automated metrics (ROUGE/BERTScore) correlate with physician judgment yet misalign on brevity and relevance, probing metric validity for patient-oriented QA.

articles.title: MeDiSumQA: Patient-Oriented Question-Answer Generation from Discharge Letters
articles.tldr: Patient-oriented medical QA benchmark that validates automatic metrics against physician judgment and addresses data contamination.
articles.contribution: Discusses data contamination as a benchmark-validity threat, motivating generation from restricted MIMIC-IV discharge data to reduce train/test leakage that would inflate scores.

articles.title: Predicting Out-of-Domain Generalization with Neighborhood Invariance
articles.tldr: Label-free neighborhood-invariance measure predicts out-of-domain generalization, validated across 4,600+ models.
articles.contribution: Proposes a label-free neighborhood-invariance metric to predict OOD external validity without model gradients or matched train/test distributions.

articles.title: CodeExp: Explanatory Code Document Generation
articles.tldr: Validates automatic metrics against human judgments for code-explanation generation; BLEU/METEOR align best but weakly.
articles.contribution: Meta-evaluates seven automatic docstring-quality metrics against human ratings via adapted Kendall's tau and recommends BLEU/METEOR for code explanation.

articles.title: On Teacher Hacking in Language Model Distillation
articles.tldr: Defines 'teacher hacking': distillation over-optimizes an imperfect teacher proxy and diverges from the ground-truth distribution.
articles.contribution: Formalizes teacher hacking as a Goodhart analog where minimizing the teacher-distance proxy increases the true oracle distance.

articles.title: On Teacher Hacking in Language Model Distillation
articles.tldr: Defines 'teacher hacking': distillation over-optimizes an imperfect teacher proxy and diverges from the ground-truth distribution.
articles.contribution: Shows teacher hacking is detectable in practice as the proxy metric deviating from its polynomial (log-log linear) convergence law over training epochs.

articles.title: Detecting Errors through Ensembling Prompts (DEEP): An End-to-End LLM Framework for Detecting Factual Errors
articles.tldr: Ensembled, calibrated LLM prompts detect summary factual errors and expose threshold-tuning inflation in prior metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows prior factual-consistency models' reported accuracy collapses when thresholds are not tuned on labels from the target evaluation dataset.

articles.title: Detecting Errors through Ensembling Prompts (DEEP): An End-to-End LLM Framework for Detecting Factual Errors
articles.tldr: Ensembled, calibrated LLM prompts detect summary factual errors and expose threshold-tuning inflation in prior metrics.
articles.contribution: Calibrates ensembled LLM-prompt outputs via Platt scaling to sub-7% ECE, correcting the overconfidence of LLM factuality judges.

articles.title: ES-MemEval: Benchmarking Conversational Agents on Personalized Long-Term Emotional Support
articles.tldr: Benchmark for long-term emotional-support memory; analyzes LLM-judge reliability and hallucination-inflated memory scores.
articles.contribution: Reports LLM-as-judge agreement with humans (Cohen's kappa, Spearman, MAD) and diagnoses ceiling-effect artifacts across QA, summarization, and dialogue tasks.

articles.title: ES-MemEval: Benchmarking Conversational Agents on Personalized Long-Term Emotional Support
articles.tldr: Benchmark for long-term emotional-support memory; analyzes LLM-judge reliability and hallucination-inflated memory scores.
articles.contribution: Argues prior long-term-memory benchmarks are unrepresentative, testing only static explicit facts and missing implicit, fragmented, evolving user states.

articles.title: ContextRef: Evaluating Referenceless Metrics For Image Description Generation
articles.tldr: Benchmark testing whether referenceless caption metrics like CLIPScore truly align with human preference and survive robustness checks.
articles.contribution: Shows referenceless image-description metrics correlate with humans yet behave as surface proxies insensitive to fundamental description changes.

articles.title: ContextRef: Evaluating Referenceless Metrics For Image Description Generation
articles.tldr: Benchmark testing whether referenceless caption metrics like CLIPScore truly align with human preference and survive robustness checks.
articles.contribution: Introduces ten falsification robustness augmentations (shuffles, repetition, irrelevant sentences) that should lower scores, exposing metric failures.

articles.title: EQUATOR: A Deterministic Framework for Evaluating LLM Reasoning with Open-Ended Questions. # v1.0.0-beta
articles.tldr: Deterministic vector-database framework that scores open-ended reasoning against human answers to curb fluency bias.

articles.title: EQUATOR: A Deterministic Framework for Evaluating LLM Reasoning with Open-Ended Questions. # v1.0.0-beta
articles.tldr: Deterministic vector-database framework that scores open-ended reasoning against human answers to curb fluency bias.
articles.contribution: Provides a deterministic embedding-matched scoring evaluator that reduces scorer variance and reliance on human graders.

articles.title: Evaluating for Diversity in Question Generation over Text
articles.tldr: Argues standard n-gram metrics (BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE) misrepresent question-generation quality because reference questions are diverse rather than paraphrases, and proposes F-like coverage meta-metrics validated by human evaluation.
articles.contribution: Shows BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE implicitly treat references as paraphrases and thus mismeasure question-set diversity/coverage, a surface proxy for the intended construct; proposes generalized precision/recall (u,v) combined by harmonic mean.

articles.title: Evaluating for Diversity in Question Generation over Text
articles.tldr: Argues standard n-gram metrics (BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE) misrepresent question-generation quality because reference questions are diverse rather than paraphrases, and proposes F-like coverage meta-metrics validated by human evaluation.

articles.title: CML-Bench: A Framework for Evaluating and Enhancing LLM-Powered Movie Scripts Generation
articles.tldr: CML-Bench derives three screenwriting quality constructs (Dialogue Coherence, Character Consistency, Plot Reasonableness) from classic scripts and operationalizes them as interpretable metrics validated against expert human ratings (Spearman 0.80).
articles.contribution: Grounds three screenplay-quality constructs (DC/CC/PR) in screenwriting theory and empirically validates them by contrasting IMDb>9 vs IMDb<3 scripts before any metric is built, addressing whether the construct is defined first.

articles.title: CML-Bench: A Framework for Evaluating and Enhancing LLM-Powered Movie Scripts Generation
articles.tldr: CML-Bench derives three screenwriting quality constructs (Dialogue Coherence, Character Consistency, Plot Reasonableness) from classic scripts and operationalizes them as interpretable metrics validated against expert human ratings (Spearman 0.80).
articles.contribution: Supplies confirmatory validity evidence by aligning the automated benchmark with expert human ratings, reporting an overall Spearman rho=0.80 (p<0.0001) across 15 script sources.

articles.title: CML-Bench: A Framework for Evaluating and Enhancing LLM-Powered Movie Scripts Generation
articles.tldr: CML-Bench derives three screenwriting quality constructs (Dialogue Coherence, Character Consistency, Plot Reasonableness) from classic scripts and operationalizes them as interpretable metrics validated against expert human ratings (Spearman 0.80).
articles.contribution: Argues holistic LLM-as-judge scoring lacks domain-specific nuance for creative writing and instead grounds scores in structured parsing plus embedding-based metrics to make evaluation more objective and interpretable.

articles.title: DeepTitle - Leveraging BERT to generate Search Engine Optimized Headlines
articles.tldr: German SEO-headline generator (BertSumAbs) whose validity contribution is critiquing ROUGE for abstractive summarization, introducing an embedding-based SentenceSim metric, and proposing permutation-based significance testing for deployment A/B.
articles.contribution: Argues ROUGE's exact n-gram overlap misrepresents abstractive-summary quality by penalizing valid paraphrases, and introduces embedding-based SentenceSim (mean max cosine of FastText vectors) as a more construct-faithful metric.

articles.title: DATScore: Evaluating Translation with Data Augmented Translations
articles.tldr: DATScore extends BARTScore with data-augmented (back-translated) copies of the source/reference plus outlier-robust averaging and entropy term weighting, correlating better with human MT judgments especially for low-resource languages.
articles.contribution: Shows DATScore correlates with segment-level human translation judgments better than BLEU/BERTScore/MoverScore/BARTScore, evidence that the metric captures translation quality rather than lexical overlap, with the largest gains in low-resource from-English directions.

articles.title: DATScore: Evaluating Translation with Data Augmented Translations
articles.tldr: DATScore extends BARTScore with data-augmented (back-translated) copies of the source/reference plus outlier-robust averaging and entropy term weighting, correlating better with human MT judgments especially for low-resource languages.
articles.contribution: Introduces a one-vs-rest averaging that down-weights outlier 'failed' generation directions plus an entropy-based term weighting, both aimed at reducing noise/variance in the aggregated metric score.

articles.title: S-RRG-Bench: Structured Radiology Report Generation with Fine-Grained Evaluation Framework
articles.tldr: Proposes S-Score, a structured evaluation metric for radiology report generation, validated against GPT-4/radiologist judgment and contrasted with error-propagating clinical metrics.
articles.contribution: S-Score decomposes report quality into a disease-prediction P-Score and detail-precision D-Score, parsing structured JSON directly to avoid the NER/classifier extraction errors that CheXbert F1 and RadGraph F1 propagate into the score.

articles.title: S-RRG-Bench: Structured Radiology Report Generation with Fine-Grained Evaluation Framework
articles.tldr: Proposes S-Score, a structured evaluation metric for radiology report generation, validated against GPT-4/radiologist judgment and contrasted with error-propagating clinical metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows BLEU/ROUGE capture only surface n-gram overlap and miss clinical content; S-Score aligns far better with human-like GPT-4 judgment (Spearman 0.769) as a construct-valid report-quality measure.

articles.title: Improving and Assessing the Fidelity of Large Language Models Alignment to Online Communities

articles.contribution: Operationalizes community-alignment fidelity via a tweet-origin classifier plus emotion/toxicity/embedding distributional closeness between generated and real community text, instead of survey-response matching.

articles.title: Improving and Assessing the Fidelity of Large Language Models Alignment to Online Communities
articles.tldr: Proposes a multi-faceted framework to measure the fidelity of LLM-to-online-community alignment, arguing survey-based alignment evaluation is biased and unscalable.
articles.contribution: Uses human annotators and two eating-disorder experts to judge authenticity and harm-narrative fidelity, but reports low inter-annotator agreement for ED harm categorization as a reliability limitation.

articles.title: Improving and Assessing the Fidelity of Large Language Models Alignment to Online Communities
articles.tldr: Proposes a multi-faceted framework to measure the fidelity of LLM-to-online-community alignment, arguing survey-based alignment evaluation is biased and unscalable.
articles.contribution: Administers an eating-disorder psychometric screener to community-aligned LLMs as an external criterion, distinguishing high-risk pro-anorexia from low-risk anti-diet communities.

articles.title: Development of Cognitive Intelligence in Pre-trained Language Models
articles.tldr: Grounds PLM evaluation in Cattell-Horn-Carroll psychometric theory, measuring cognitive/developmental alignment across four ability facets while flagging construct-validity and contamination concerns.
articles.contribution: Grounds four evaluation tasks (numeric, linguistic, conceptual, fluid) in Cattell-Horn-Carroll psychometric intelligence theory, positing them as a prerequisite for construct-valid treatment of PLMs as cognitive models.

articles.title: Development of Cognitive Intelligence in Pre-trained Language Models
articles.tldr: Grounds PLM evaluation in Cattell-Horn-Carroll psychometric theory, measuring cognitive/developmental alignment across four ability facets while flagging construct-validity and contamination concerns.
articles.contribution: Flags that GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Gemini score near ceiling on the 374 SAT analogy items while open models perform poorly, hinting the set is present in the commercial models' training/tuning data.

articles.title: Development of Cognitive Intelligence in Pre-trained Language Models
articles.tldr: Grounds PLM evaluation in Cattell-Horn-Carroll psychometric theory, measuring cognitive/developmental alignment across four ability facets while flagging construct-validity and contamination concerns.
articles.contribution: Shows cognitive-alignment metrics peak in a training window then destabilize, so alignment validity is path-dependent and not captured by evaluating only final checkpoints.

articles.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
articles.tldr: Introduces STALE, a benchmark isolating implicit memory-conflict, arguing existing memory benchmarks under-represent belief revision by measuring only static fact retrieval.
articles.contribution: Argues prior memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, PersonaMem) operationalize success as static fact retrieval and under-represent update/conflict-sensitive memory; STALE reframes memory as latent-state tracking and isolates implicit conflict.

articles.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
articles.tldr: Introduces STALE, a benchmark isolating implicit memory-conflict, arguing existing memory benchmarks under-represent belief revision by measuring only static fact retrieval.
articles.contribution: Constructs 400 expert-validated conflict scenarios / 1,200 queries over 100+ everyday topics with contexts up to 150K tokens for realistic long-context coverage of belief invalidation.

articles.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
articles.tldr: Introduces STALE, a benchmark isolating implicit memory-conflict, arguing existing memory benchmarks under-represent belief revision by measuring only static fact retrieval.
articles.contribution: Uses expert manual-revision standards for ground-truth quality and validates its automatic scoring against human agreement before reporting benchmark accuracies.

articles.title: Do Instruction-Tuned Models Always Perform Better Than Base Models? Evidence from Math and Domain-Shifted Benchmarks
articles.tldr: Shows instruction-tuning gains on math benchmarks are unstable across evaluation settings and brittle under distribution shift, and that rule-based graders are unreliable.

articles.title: Do Instruction-Tuned Models Always Perform Better Than Base Models? Evidence from Math and Domain-Shifted Benchmarks
articles.tldr: Shows instruction-tuning gains on math benchmarks are unstable across evaluation settings and brittle under distribution shift, and that rule-based graders are unreliable.

articles.title: From Intervention to Domain Transportation: A Novel Perspective to Optimize Recommendation
articles.tldr: Proves that violating the overlap/positivity assumption threatens the validity of importance-weighting and domain-adaptation causal inference used to learn and evaluate recommendation.

articles.title: From Intervention to Domain Transportation: A Novel Perspective to Optimize Recommendation

articles.title: Diagnose, Localize, Align: A Full-Stack Framework for Reliable LLM Multi-Agent Systems under Instruction Conflicts

articles.title: Diagnose, Localize, Align: A Full-Stack Framework for Reliable LLM Multi-Agent Systems under Instruction Conflicts
articles.tldr: Argues macro metrics like pass@k mask micro-level role-adherence violations in multi-agent systems and proposes CRAS, a rubric-driven context-aware adherence metric.

articles.title: Faithful Chart Summarization with ChaTS-Pi

articles.title: Faithful Chart Summarization with ChaTS-Pi
articles.tldr: Reference-free chart-summary faithfulness metric (ChaTS-Critic) validated against human ratings, exposing failures of reference-based metrics.

articles.title: Unmasking the Imposters: How Censorship and Domain Adaptation Affect the Detection of Machine-Generated Tweets

articles.title: Synthesis-in-the-Loop Evaluation of LLMs for RTL Generation: Quality, Reliability, and Failure Modes

articles.title: Synthesis-in-the-Loop Evaluation of LLMs for RTL Generation: Quality, Reliability, and Failure Modes
