articles.title: VIBEPASS: Can Vibe Coders Really Pass the Vibe Check?
articles.tldr: VibePass decomposes fault-targeted reasoning, showing coverage/syntactic-validity proxies overstate LLM fault-detection ability.
articles.contribution: Argues syntactic validity and branch coverage are surface proxies that overestimate fault-detection; requires discriminative (fault-triggering) tests where buggy and silver solutions diverge, verified by execution.

articles.title: VIBEPASS: Can Vibe Coders Really Pass the Vibe Check?
articles.tldr: VibePass decomposes fault-targeted reasoning, showing coverage/syntactic-validity proxies overstate LLM fault-detection ability.
articles.contribution: Multi-stage decomposition (Valid-Input -> Valid-IO -> FT-Input -> FT-IO -> Repair) isolates the fault-hypothesis bottleneck from test-validity and code-synthesis confounds, controlling what the metric attributes capability to.

articles.title: FormalScience: Scalable Human-in-the-Loop Autoformalisation of Science with Agentic Code Generation in Lean
articles.tldr: Shows Lean formal validity (compilation) is insufficient for physics autoformalisation, characterizing semantic drift and auditing LLM-judge reliability.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates 100% formal validity (Lean compilation) coexists with low logical-preservation (72%), i.e. compilation is a surface proxy; taxonomizes drift (notational collapse, abstraction elevation) describing what Lean actually verifies.

articles.title: FormalScience: Scalable Human-in-the-Loop Autoformalisation of Science with Agentic Code Generation in Lean
articles.tldr: Shows Lean formal validity (compilation) is insufficient for physics autoformalisation, characterizing semantic drift and auditing LLM-judge reliability.
articles.contribution: Audits the LLM-as-a-judge alignment metrics (FQ/LP/MC) with a second independent 7B judge over ~6000 paired judgments, quantifying reliability and which claims are judge-dependent.

articles.title: Evaluating LLM Alignment on Personality Inference from Real-World Interview Data
articles.tldr: Benchmarks LLM inference of continuous Big Five traits against validated psychometric labels, finding weak criterion validity and critiquing binary construct oversimplification.
articles.contribution: Argues prior APP work creates a 'psychometric-to-computational translation gap' by binarizing personality; introduces an ecologically-valid benchmark of interview transcripts with validated continuous BFI-10 scores.

articles.title: Evaluating LLM Alignment on Personality Inference from Real-World Interview Data
articles.tldr: Benchmarks LLM inference of continuous Big Five traits against validated psychometric labels, finding weak criterion validity and critiquing binary construct oversimplification.
articles.contribution: Uses Pearson r as criterion validity on real-world interviews and finds all correlations below 0.26, showing LLM personality inference lacks convergent/ecological validity with ground-truth traits.

articles.title: Vectors from Larger Language Models Predict Human Reading Time and fMRI Data More Poorly when Dimensionality Expansion is Controlled
articles.tldr: Shows the 'quality-power' LLM-to-brain scaling effect is a degrees-of-freedom confound; controlling dimensionality yields inverse scaling.
articles.contribution: Identifies that using entire LLM vectors as regression predictors confounds model size with vector dimensionality (degrees of freedom); residualizing trained against untrained models removes the apparent positive scaling.

articles.title: Vectors from Larger Language Models Predict Human Reading Time and fMRI Data More Poorly when Dimensionality Expansion is Controlled
articles.tldr: Shows the 'quality-power' LLM-to-brain scaling effect is a degrees-of-freedom confound; controlling dimensionality yields inverse scaling.
articles.contribution: Shows the quality-power scaling-law claim inverts once the confound is controlled: larger LMs contribute no more beyond degrees of freedom, implying growing LLM-human misalignment with scale.

articles.title: AgentSocialBench: Evaluating Privacy Risks in Human-Centered Agentic Social Networks
articles.tldr: Privacy-leakage benchmark for human-centered agentic social networks whose LLM-judge leakage metric reveals an 'abstraction paradox' that complicates what is being measured.
articles.contribution: Abstraction paradox: the LLM-judge scores sanctioned abstraction language as partial leakage, so the leakage-rate metric may over-count real privacy harm and conflate defense compliance with disclosure.

articles.title: AgentSocialBench: Evaluating Privacy Risks in Human-Centered Agentic Social Networks
articles.tldr: Privacy-leakage benchmark for human-centered agentic social networks whose LLM-judge leakage metric reveals an 'abstraction paradox' that complicates what is being measured.
articles.contribution: Uses a defense-oblivious LLM-judge that is distinct from the agent backbone and validated by human experts, with confidence intervals, to reduce self-evaluation bias in leakage scoring.

articles.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Scaling
articles.tldr: Sensitivity/robustness re-analysis of Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling under three ambiguous model-parameter interpretations and four structured perturbations.
articles.contribution: Re-fits Chinchilla's scaling law under three ambiguous model-parameter interpretations (differing up to 15.2%) and finds the estimated exponents and the 20:1 tokens-per-parameter ratio essentially unchanged.

articles.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Scaling
articles.tldr: Sensitivity/robustness re-analysis of Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling under three ambiguous model-parameter interpretations and four structured perturbations.
articles.contribution: Structured four-way perturbation of model-parameter counts delimits when the scaling-law prescription stays valid: additive/systematic errors can flip the tokens-per-parameter trend while multiplicative/noise perturbations mostly rescale the prefactor or inflate uncertainty.

articles.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Scaling
articles.tldr: Sensitivity/robustness re-analysis of Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling under three ambiguous model-parameter interpretations and four structured perturbations.
articles.contribution: Shows that including/excluding embedding parameters (an additive perturbation) systematically shifts the fitted exponent alpha, matching known Kaplan-vs-Chinchilla discrepancies, exposing a measurement confound in how model size is counted.

articles.title: Style-News: Incorporating Stylized News Generation and Adversarial Verification for Neural Fake News Detection
articles.tldr: Adversarial stylized fake-news generator+detector framework that exposes an unfair-evaluation flaw and proposes external held-out testing plus multi-facet generation metrics.
articles.contribution: Argues prior neural-fake-news detectors trained and tested on their own paired generator's outputs are unfairly inflated ('fitting discriminators'), a train/test leakage between conditions that overstates detection performance.

articles.title: Style-News: Incorporating Stylized News Generation and Adversarial Verification for Neural Fake News Detection
articles.tldr: Adversarial stylized fake-news generator+detector framework that exposes an unfair-evaluation flaw and proposes external held-out testing plus multi-facet generation metrics.
articles.contribution: Proposes evaluating detectors on an external, separately-generated dataset (VOA-KG2txt) to measure robustness to unseen fake news; all baselines degrade on this out-of-distribution set while the proposed detector stays near-perfect.

articles.title: Style-News: Incorporating Stylized News Generation and Adversarial Verification for Neural Fake News Detection
articles.tldr: Adversarial stylized fake-news generator+detector framework that exposes an unfair-evaluation flaw and proposes external held-out testing plus multi-facet generation metrics.
articles.contribution: Argues BLEU measures content preservation not fluency (repeated patterns inflate it), so introduces facet-aligned metrics: MAUVE/Frontier for fluency, SacreBLEU/MoverScore for content, and a classifier for style adherence.

articles.title: A Scoping Review of Synthetic Data Generation by Language Models in Biomedical Research and Application: Data Utility and Quality Perspectives
articles.tldr: PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 59 biomedical LLM synthetic-data studies focused on data-quality/utility evaluation practices and their methodological gaps.
articles.contribution: Documents reproducibility barriers across the field: heavy reliance on non-deterministic proprietary APIs plus incomplete reporting of prompts, model versions, and decoding parameters make replication difficult.

articles.title: A Scoping Review of Synthetic Data Generation by Language Models in Biomedical Research and Application: Data Utility and Quality Perspectives
articles.tldr: PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 59 biomedical LLM synthetic-data studies focused on data-quality/utility evaluation practices and their methodological gaps.
articles.contribution: Notes many studies rely on n-gram metrics like ROUGE that assess textual fluency but cannot verify clinical factuality, with hallucination/factuality audits performed inconsistently - a surface-proxy construct-validity gap.

articles.title: Evaluating Implicit Regulatory Compliance in LLM Tool Invocation via Logic-Guided Synthesis
articles.tldr: Logic-guided fuzzing benchmark (LogiSafetyBench) using deterministic LTL oracles to measure implicit regulatory compliance in LLM tool use, avoiding LLM-judge bias and static-set contamination.
articles.contribution: Its logic-guided fuzzer reaches 100% safety-critical-API coverage and higher adjacent-transition coverage than LLM-only generation, which suffers a sampling-bias problem of converging on high-likelihood paths and missing rare safety-critical states.

articles.title: Evaluating Implicit Regulatory Compliance in LLM Tool Invocation via Logic-Guided Synthesis
articles.tldr: Logic-guided fuzzing benchmark (LogiSafetyBench) using deterministic LTL oracles to measure implicit regulatory compliance in LLM tool use, avoiding LLM-judge bias and static-set contamination.
articles.contribution: Safety masking removes explicit safety steps from the natural-language instruction so the task measures implicit-compliance inference rather than trivial instruction-following, preventing a shortcut that would misrepresent the construct.

articles.title: Evaluating Implicit Regulatory Compliance in LLM Tool Invocation via Logic-Guided Synthesis
articles.tldr: Logic-guided fuzzing benchmark (LogiSafetyBench) using deterministic LTL oracles to measure implicit regulatory compliance in LLM tool use, avoiding LLM-judge bias and static-set contamination.
articles.contribution: Replaces LLM-judge scoring with deterministic LTL-over-finite-traces oracles executed by a runtime monitor, eliminating the non-determinism and evaluation bias of LLM-based judges used by prior safety benchmarks.

articles.title: Can Large Language Models Learn Formal Logic? A Data-Driven Training and Evaluation Framework
articles.tldr: Training+evaluation framework using an automated proof checker and black-box tests to determine whether an LLM genuinely reasons in Boolean logic versus memorizing or guessing.
articles.contribution: Proposes automated black-box tests (favoring semantics over syntax, diversity, template transformation) to distinguish genuine reasoning from memorization/retrieval/guessing, addressing whether accuracy reflects the reasoning construct.

articles.title: Can Large Language Models Learn Formal Logic? A Data-Driven Training and Evaluation Framework
articles.tldr: Training+evaluation framework using an automated proof checker and black-box tests to determine whether an LLM genuinely reasons in Boolean logic versus memorizing or guessing.
articles.contribution: Tests generalization to deeper and wider proofs than seen in training (an out-of-distribution stress test), finding accuracy declines with proof complexity so shallow-proof success does not guarantee external validity.

articles.title: On Large Language Models as Data Sources for Policy Deliberation on Climate Change and Sustainability
articles.tldr: Exploratory study validating whether GPT-4 evaluation scores for climate/sustainability policies are credible by comparing MCDM rankings against an informed human assessment.
articles.contribution: Treats GPT-4 as a black-box scorer of policy alternatives on nine quality-of-life criteria, explicitly framing hallucination and systematic model failures as threats to the credibility of the produced evaluation scores.

articles.title: On Large Language Models as Data Sources for Policy Deliberation on Climate Change and Sustainability
articles.tldr: Exploratory study validating whether GPT-4 evaluation scores for climate/sustainability policies are credible by comparing MCDM rankings against an informed human assessment.
articles.contribution: Provides criterion-validity evidence by comparing the GPT-4-based TOPSIS policy ranking against a multi-rater informed human-assessment ranking, finding rough agreement that supports provisional use of the LLM as a starter-model input.

articles.title: UrduBench: An Urdu Reasoning Benchmark using Contextually Ensembled Translations with Human-in-the-Loop
articles.tldr: Contextual ensemble + human-in-the-loop translation to build a fidelity-preserving Urdu reasoning benchmark, and studies translation-induced construct distortion and language-consistency confounds in cross-lingual evaluation.
articles.contribution: Ensemble translation with native human validation preserves the reasoning construct when porting MGSM/MATH-500/CommonSenseQA/OpenBookQA into Urdu, mitigating machine-translation-induced construct distortion of the items.

articles.title: UrduBench: An Urdu Reasoning Benchmark using Contextually Ensembled Translations with Human-in-the-Loop
articles.tldr: Contextual ensemble + human-in-the-loop translation to build a fidelity-preserving Urdu reasoning benchmark, and studies translation-induced construct distortion and language-consistency confounds in cross-lingual evaluation.
articles.contribution: Language-consistency (code-switching) test using language identification shows measured Urdu reasoning accuracy is confounded by whether the model actually answers in Urdu, isolating a linguistic confound in the score.

articles.title: The Sound of Syntax: Finetuning and Comprehensive Evaluation of Language Models for Speech Pathology
articles.tldr: A comprehensive speech-pathology MLM benchmark with robustness/sensitivity tests that uncovers systematic gender disparities favoring male speakers, noise/accent external-validity limits, and chain-of-thought degrading classification.
articles.contribution: Documents a systematic male-favoring gender gap across nearly all 15 MLMs on UltraSuite diagnostic tasks, revealing speaker gender as a confounder in measured clinical-speech diagnostic performance.

articles.title: The Sound of Syntax: Finetuning and Comprehensive Evaluation of Language Models for Speech Pathology
articles.tldr: A comprehensive speech-pathology MLM benchmark with robustness/sensitivity tests that uncovers systematic gender disparities favoring male speakers, noise/accent external-validity limits, and chain-of-thought degrading classification.
articles.contribution: Robustness/sensitivity tests under road/classroom/office noise and across English/French/Dutch expose external-validity limits of the clean benchmark for real clinical deployment.

articles.title: The Sound of Syntax: Finetuning and Comprehensive Evaluation of Language Models for Speech Pathology
articles.tldr: A comprehensive speech-pathology MLM benchmark with robustness/sensitivity tests that uncovers systematic gender disparities favoring male speakers, noise/accent external-validity limits, and chain-of-thought degrading classification.
articles.contribution: Shows measured capability is unstable to prompting choice: chain-of-thought prompting systematically depresses F1 on classification with large label spaces and narrow decision boundaries.

articles.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
articles.tldr: A human-vs-LLM benchmark of source-trust-sensitive Turkish evidential morphology that disentangles output-compliance, base-rate suffix preference, and genuine context-sensitivity across three prompting paradigms with a human baseline.
articles.contribution: Multi-paradigm design separates three normally-conflated sources of variation (compliance/formatting, base-rate morphological preference, and true trust-sensitivity) so apparent evidential reasoning is not confounded by format artifacts.

articles.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
articles.tldr: A human-vs-LLM benchmark of source-trust-sensitive Turkish evidential morphology that disentangles output-compliance, base-rate suffix preference, and genuine context-sensitivity across three prompting paradigms with a human baseline.
articles.contribution: Shows the measured evidential choice is highly prompt-format-dependent: usable-output rate ranges from 0% to 96% across models and effects reverse between open gap-fill, explicit-past, and forced-choice prompting.

articles.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
articles.tldr: A human-vs-LLM benchmark of source-trust-sensitive Turkish evidential morphology that disentangles output-compliance, base-rate suffix preference, and genuine context-sensitivity across three prompting paradigms with a human baseline.
articles.contribution: Applies Fisher exact tests with Holm multiple-comparison correction across models; nominally significant per-model trust effects do not survive correction, tempering claims of robust LLM trust-sensitivity.

articles.title: The Lay Person's Guide to Biomedicine: Orchestrating Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Explores LLMs for generating and evaluating biomedical lay summaries and proposes two LLM-based 'layness' metrics, validating their alignment with human judgments against shallow readability metrics.
articles.contribution: Proposes LLM Rater and LLM Score metrics for layness and shows the ChatGPT-based Rater correlates strongly with human preference and matches or surpasses traditional and other LLM-based metrics.

articles.title: The Lay Person's Guide to Biomedicine: Orchestrating Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Explores LLMs for generating and evaluating biomedical lay summaries and proposes two LLM-based 'layness' metrics, validating their alignment with human judgments against shallow readability metrics.
articles.contribution: Shows traditional readability metrics such as the Coleman-Liau Index capture only shallow word/sentence-length features and conflict with human layness judgments, mis-representing the layness construct.

articles.title: Do Encoder Representations of Generative Dialogue Models have sufficient summary of the Information about the task ?
articles.tldr: Argues token-overlap metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) and human scores fail to measure dialogue models' language understanding, and proposes 17+ encoder probe tasks while exposing high human-evaluation variance and seed nondeterminism.
articles.contribution: Proposes 17+ classifier probe tasks over encoder representations as a construct-valid measure of dialogue language understanding that surface token-overlap metrics like BLEU fail to capture.

articles.title: Do Encoder Representations of Generative Dialogue Models have sufficient summary of the Information about the task ?
articles.tldr: Argues token-overlap metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) and human scores fail to measure dialogue models' language understanding, and proposes 17+ encoder probe tasks while exposing high human-evaluation variance and seed nondeterminism.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates human dialogue evaluation is unreliable: the tie fraction centers around 35% across three annotator groups, so subjective judgments cannot reliably discriminate between models.

articles.title: Do Encoder Representations of Generative Dialogue Models have sufficient summary of the Information about the task ?
articles.tldr: Argues token-overlap metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) and human scores fail to measure dialogue models' language understanding, and proposes 17+ encoder probe tasks while exposing high human-evaluation variance and seed nondeterminism.
articles.contribution: Shows generated responses vary strongly with random seed at similar BLEU, so seed-driven output changes confound evaluation and reproducibility of dialogue models.

articles.title: Agent-Driven Corpus Linguistics: A Framework for Autonomous Linguistic Discovery
articles.tldr: Framework delegating corpus-linguistics inquiry to an LLM agent, with a controlled baseline, published-study replication, and reproducibility/annotation analyses probing whether findings are grounded discovery or training-data recall.
articles.contribution: Isolates the discovery-vs-recall confound with a controlled with/without-corpus baseline (same LLM), showing hypothesis generation is largely parametric recall while precise quantification requires corpus grounding, so grounded evidence must gate the inference.

articles.title: Agent-Driven Corpus Linguistics: A Framework for Autonomous Linguistic Discovery
articles.tldr: Framework delegating corpus-linguistics inquiry to an LLM agent, with a controlled baseline, published-study replication, and reproducibility/annotation analyses probing whether findings are grounded discovery or training-data recall.
articles.contribution: Tests reproducibility of a stochastic LLM agent by rerunning the case study three times (quantitative core stable, interpretation drifts) and replicating two published corpus studies with close quantitative agreement.

articles.title: Agent-Driven Corpus Linguistics: A Framework for Autonomous Linguistic Discovery
articles.tldr: Framework delegating corpus-linguistics inquiry to an LLM agent, with a controlled baseline, published-study replication, and reproducibility/annotation analyses probing whether findings are grounded discovery or training-data recall.
articles.contribution: Validates the agent's self-devised four-way collocate polarity annotation scheme against an independent human linguist, reporting Cohen's kappa=0.83 (privative most stable at 0.88, neutral least at 0.73).

articles.title: When Prompt Under-Specification Improves Code Correctness: An Exploratory Study of Prompt Wording and Structure Effects on LLM-Based Code Generation
articles.tldr: Shows code-LLM robustness to prompt under-specification is largely an artifact of benchmark specification structure, and that retrieval cues in over-specified prompts confound code correctness.
articles.contribution: Identifies domain vocabulary, identifier names, and constraint lines as spurious retrieval cues that anchor models to memorized-but-wrong solutions, confounding the link between prompt and measured Pass@1 correctness.

articles.title: When Prompt Under-Specification Improves Code Correctness: An Exploratory Study of Prompt Wording and Structure Effects on LLM-Based Code Generation
articles.tldr: Shows code-LLM robustness to prompt under-specification is largely an artifact of benchmark specification structure, and that retrieval cues in over-specified prompts confound code correctness.
articles.contribution: Argues minimal-specification benchmarks (HumanEval) exaggerate prompt fragility, so prior robustness results do not generalize to structurally rich real-world multi-layered specifications (LiveCodeBench).

articles.title: When Prompt Under-Specification Improves Code Correctness: An Exploratory Study of Prompt Wording and Structure Effects on LLM-Based Code Generation
articles.tldr: Shows code-LLM robustness to prompt under-specification is largely an artifact of benchmark specification structure, and that retrieval cues in over-specified prompts confound code correctness.
articles.contribution: Attributes HumanEval's memorization-driven cue sensitivity to its 8-18% train/test contamination and adopts contamination-free, time-stamped LiveCodeBench to separate reasoning from recall.

articles.title: A Design-based Solution for Causal Inference with Text: Can a Language Model Be Too Large?
articles.tldr: Shows LLM text-as-treatment causal estimators encode the treatment and induce overlap/positivity violations that bias effects, and introduces a design-based writer/editor experiment giving unbiased ground-truth ATE to validate estimators.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates LLM covariate-adjustment estimators (TextCause, TI) learn representations that encode the treatment itself, inducing positivity/overlap violations that bias the ATE and break causal identification even in a setting favorable to them.

articles.title: A Design-based Solution for Causal Inference with Text: Can a Language Model Be Too Large?
articles.tldr: Shows LLM text-as-treatment causal estimators encode the treatment and induce overlap/positivity violations that bias effects, and introduces a design-based writer/editor experiment giving unbiased ground-truth ATE to validate estimators.
articles.contribution: Introduces a writer/editor experimental design that holds all latent features fixed except the treatment, yielding an unbiased ground-truth ATE that serves as a falsification testbed to validate (or invalidate) text-as-treatment estimators.

articles.title: Polyp-E: Benchmarking the Robustness of Deep Segmentation Models via Polyp Editing
articles.tldr: Polyp-E is a diffusion-edited benchmark that varies polyp size/position while holding the background fixed, isolating attribute robustness and revealing that segmentation models are highly sensitive to distribution shift under-represented in real datasets.
articles.contribution: Builds Polyp-E to measure out-of-distribution robustness to lesion size/position variations that real polyp datasets under-sample, showing Dice drops and non-zero false-positive rates that expose poor external validity of standard segmentation benchmarks.

articles.title: Polyp-E: Benchmarking the Robustness of Deep Segmentation Models via Polyp Editing
articles.tldr: Polyp-E is a diffusion-edited benchmark that varies polyp size/position while holding the background fixed, isolating attribute robustness and revealing that segmentation models are highly sensitive to distribution shift under-represented in real datasets.
articles.contribution: By inpainting the background and only minimally editing the polyp via latent-diffusion affine transforms, the benchmark holds all other content constant so a measured Dice drop is attributable to the attribute change rather than confounding image differences.

articles.title: FineDialFact: A benchmark for Fine-grained Dialogue Fact Verification
articles.tldr: FineDialFact argues response-level factuality labels are too coarse and introduces an atomic-fact dialogue verification benchmark, characterizing annotation reliability and LLM/CoT verifier reliability for hallucination detection.
articles.contribution: Shows a single response-level factuality label is an over-coarse proxy because a response mixes correct, incorrect and non-verifiable claims, and reoperationalizes dialogue factuality as verification of atomic facts to better capture the construct.

articles.title: FineDialFact: A benchmark for Fine-grained Dialogue Fact Verification
articles.tldr: FineDialFact argues response-level factuality labels are too coarse and introduces an atomic-fact dialogue verification benchmark, characterizing annotation reliability and LLM/CoT verifier reliability for hallucination detection.
articles.contribution: Quantifies ground-truth annotation quality with Cohen's kappa (0.55-0.66 for factual-claim/label tasks) and shows GPT-4o auto-annotation reaches ~0.6 agreement, characterizing label reliability of the benchmark.

articles.title: FineDialFact: A benchmark for Fine-grained Dialogue Fact Verification
articles.tldr: FineDialFact argues response-level factuality labels are too coarse and introduces an atomic-fact dialogue verification benchmark, characterizing annotation reliability and LLM/CoT verifier reliability for hallucination detection.
articles.contribution: Benchmarks LLM verifiers as the scoring instrument, finding the best F1 is only 0.74 and that few-shot CoT can induce an 'over-justification' failure mode, exposing scorer unreliability.

articles.title: Visualizing and Benchmarking LLM Factual Hallucination Tendencies via Internal State Analysis and Clustering
articles.tldr: FalseCite benchmark shows fabricated citations amplify LLM hallucination, and it quantifies an LLM 'expert' judge used to label hallucinated responses.
articles.contribution: Shows fabricated citations act as a spurious cue that inflates hallucination rates by up to +39.65 points (GPT-4o-mini), confounding the factuality measurement.

articles.title: Visualizing and Benchmarking LLM Factual Hallucination Tendencies via Internal State Analysis and Clustering
articles.tldr: FalseCite benchmark shows fabricated citations amplify LLM hallucination, and it quantifies an LLM 'expert' judge used to label hallucinated responses.
articles.contribution: Uses GPT-4.1 as an expert judge (75.2% HaluEval accuracy) that cannot verify citation authenticity, a documented scorer-reliability limitation of the benchmark.

articles.title: M2G-Eval: Enhancing and Evaluating Multi-granularity Multilingual Code Generation
articles.tldr: Multi-granularity multilingual code-generation benchmark built with post-2024 repositories and human validation to control pretraining contamination.
articles.contribution: Builds 1,286 contamination-controlled test instances from repositories created/updated after 2024-01-01, kept disjoint from the 17K training set to mitigate pretraining leakage.

articles.title: M2G-Eval: Enhancing and Evaluating Multi-granularity Multilingual Code Generation
articles.tldr: Multi-granularity multilingual code-generation benchmark built with post-2024 repositories and human validation to control pretraining contamination.
articles.contribution: Scores use length-normalized Levenshtein edit similarity rather than execution-based correctness, a surface proxy for code quality that the authors flag as a limitation.

articles.title: Behaviour Driven Development Scenario Generation with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation of automatic metrics vs LLM-judges vs human experts for BDD scenario generation, finding n-gram metrics correlate weakly with humans while a DeepSeek judge correlates best.
articles.contribution: Shows DeepSeek-R1 as an LLM-judge achieves the strongest Spearman correlation with human ratings (rho up to 0.72), outperforming GPT-4/Claude judges and all automatic metrics.

articles.title: Behaviour Driven Development Scenario Generation with Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Meta-evaluation of automatic metrics vs LLM-judges vs human experts for BDD scenario generation, finding n-gram metrics correlate weakly with humans while a DeepSeek judge correlates best.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE and most semantic metrics correlate weakly with human judgment (rho < 0.30), poor proxies for scenario quality; only BERTScore reaches rho ~0.40-0.48.

articles.title: Automating Text Naturalness Evaluation of NLG Systems
articles.tldr: Proposes an automatic text-naturalness metric (h-score) from an LM-based discriminator and studies how generator/discriminator size affects its reliability.
articles.contribution: Defines an h-score naturalness metric from an LM discriminator's probability fractions and shows larger discriminators yield more reliable, statistically significant synthetic-vs-human separation.

articles.title: Inclusive Easy-to-Read Generation for Individuals with Cognitive Impairments
articles.tldr: Introduces an Easy-to-Read generation dataset and documents that summarization/simplification metrics fail to capture ETR quality and that expert annotation of ETR criteria is highly unreliable.
articles.contribution: Reports very low inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff alpha=0.07; 0.20 binarized) across 36 ETR guideline criteria, attributed to abstract, subjective criteria.

articles.title: Inclusive Easy-to-Read Generation for Individuals with Cognitive Impairments
articles.tldr: Introduces an Easy-to-Read generation dataset and documents that summarization/simplification metrics fail to capture ETR quality and that expert annotation of ETR criteria is highly unreliable.
articles.contribution: Shows ROUGE/SARI/BERTScore rank Mistral-7B+LoRA well while human evaluation reveals it overfits and generalizes worse than mBARThez, exposing a metric-construct gap for ETR.

articles.title: Multi-Agent Game Generation and Evaluation via Audio-Visual Recordings
articles.tldr: Proposes AVR-Eval, an omni-modal LLM-judge that compares audio-visual recordings of generated games/animations, and validates it against broken, mislabeled, and human-made content.
articles.contribution: Validates AVR-Eval by showing it rarely prefers broken (0.91%) or mislabeled (6.47%) content over working content and picks human-made content 67.78% of the time (falsification-style checks).

articles.title: Multi-Agent Game Generation and Evaluation via Audio-Visual Recordings
articles.tldr: Proposes AVR-Eval, an omni-modal LLM-judge that compares audio-visual recordings of generated games/animations, and validates it against broken, mislabeled, and human-made content.
articles.contribution: Ablation shows the multiround description, relative-comparison, and text-model review components each independently improve the judge's reliability against broken and mislabeled content.

articles.title: Projective Psychological Assessment of Large Multimodal Models Using Thematic Apperception Tests
articles.tldr: Applies the TAT projective test with SCORS-G to assess LMM 'personality', validating LLM evaluators against human experts and flagging evaluation-awareness/social-desirability confounds.
articles.contribution: Selects a reliable evaluator ensemble by maximizing Krippendorff's alpha and validates it against human SCORS-G ratings (MAE 0.59-0.66, Spearman 0.60-0.68).

articles.title: Projective Psychological Assessment of Large Multimodal Models Using Thematic Apperception Tests
articles.tldr: Applies the TAT projective test with SCORS-G to assess LMM 'personality', validating LLM evaluators against human experts and flagging evaluation-awareness/social-desirability confounds.
articles.contribution: Argues low AGG/EIM/SE scores may reflect social-desirability bias from models inferring they are being assessed, a reactivity confound that cannot be separated from a genuine representational limit.

articles.title: Projective Psychological Assessment of Large Multimodal Models Using Thematic Apperception Tests
articles.tldr: Applies the TAT projective test with SCORS-G to assess LMM 'personality', validating LLM evaluators against human experts and flagging evaluation-awareness/social-desirability confounds.
articles.contribution: Grounds LMM 'personality' measurement in the psychometrically-validated TAT/SCORS-G framework while acknowledging construct extrapolation from humans to models.

articles.title: Aligning MLLM Benchmark With Human Preferences via Structural Equation Modeling
articles.tldr: Uses PLS-SEM to audit the construct/discriminant validity, redundancy and cognitive alignment of MLLM benchmarks, then rebuilds a theory-grounded Gold benchmark.
articles.contribution: Grounds MLLM capability dimensions in Piaget's developmental theory (Perception/Memory/Reasoning) before building a measure, replacing heuristic task groupings with a theory-driven latent structure.

articles.title: Aligning MLLM Benchmark With Human Preferences via Structural Equation Modeling
articles.tldr: Uses PLS-SEM to audit the construct/discriminant validity, redundancy and cognitive alignment of MLLM benchmarks, then rebuilds a theory-grounded Gold benchmark.
articles.contribution: Quantifies whether benchmark tasks measure distinct latent abilities using HTMT discriminant validity, outer loadings and VIF redundancy, exposing conflated dimensions in existing benchmarks.

articles.title: Quantal Response Equilibrium as a Measure of Strategic Sophistication: Theory and Validation for LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Grounds Theory-of-Mind LLM evaluation in quantal response equilibrium, using equilibrium convergence as a validity check and exposing prompt-framing and version instability.
articles.contribution: Uses closed-form game-theoretic equilibria and QRE rationality parameter lambda to test whether ToM scores reflect genuine strategic reasoning rather than surface heuristics, decomposing ToM into four distinct cognitive axes.

articles.title: Quantal Response Equilibrium as a Measure of Strategic Sophistication: Theory and Validation for LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Grounds Theory-of-Mind LLM evaluation in quantal response equilibrium, using equilibrium convergence as a validity check and exposing prompt-framing and version instability.
articles.contribution: Provides confirmatory validity evidence: observed convergence toward the derived equilibrium (bluff rate within 4% of beta*=0.340) is treated as positive evidence that the games elicit strategic reasoning.

articles.title: Quantal Response Equilibrium as a Measure of Strategic Sophistication: Theory and Validation for LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Grounds Theory-of-Mind LLM evaluation in quantal response equilibrium, using equilibrium convergence as a validity check and exposing prompt-framing and version instability.
articles.contribution: Shows the operationalization (prompt framing) drives measured behavior: replacing the game-theoretic narrative with formal/minimal prompts eliminates bluffing entirely, a binary sensitivity paralleling Ullman's ToM collapse.

articles.title: Quantal Response Equilibrium as a Measure of Strategic Sophistication: Theory and Validation for LLM Evaluation
articles.tldr: Grounds Theory-of-Mind LLM evaluation in quantal response equilibrium, using equilibrium convergence as a validity check and exposing prompt-framing and version instability.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates temporal instability of QRE rankings across model generations, arguing that any single evaluation snapshot is not a stable capability claim.

articles.title: Legal Reasoning Is Not Lawyering: Rethinking Legal Benchmarks for Pro Se Access to Justice
articles.tldr: Argues legal benchmarks measure lawyer-mediated 'legal reasoning' (upper bound) not deployment-relevant 'lawyering' for pro se litigants (lower bound), and demonstrates the gap with a LEXam perturbation primer.
articles.contribution: Shows benchmark scores (an upper bound on clean lawyer-preprocessed inputs) do not transport to the pro se deployment lower bound, so access-to-justice claims are not empirically supported by current benchmark performance.

articles.title: Legal Reasoning Is Not Lawyering: Rethinking Legal Benchmarks for Pro Se Access to Justice
articles.tldr: Argues legal benchmarks measure lawyer-mediated 'legal reasoning' (upper bound) not deployment-relevant 'lawyering' for pro se litigants (lower bound), and demonstrates the gap with a LEXam perturbation primer.
articles.contribution: Identifies that every legal benchmark evaluates lawyer-mediated inputs (facts pre-pruned, procedural posture clarified), which is unrepresentative of noisy, underspecified pro se prompts.

articles.title: Robustness Risk of Conversational Retrieval: Identifying and Mitigating Noise Sensitivity in Qwen3-Embedding Model
articles.tldr: Identifies a robustness vulnerability where Qwen3 embeddings let semantically-uninformative conversational noise dominate retrieval, a failure invisible under clean-query benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates a deployment-relevant failure mode invisible under standard clean-query embedding benchmarks, arguing evaluation protocols must reflect conversational/memory-oriented deployment conditions.

articles.title: Robustness Risk of Conversational Retrieval: Identifying and Mitigating Noise Sensitivity in Qwen3-Embedding Model
articles.tldr: Identifies a robustness vulnerability where Qwen3 embeddings let semantically-uninformative conversational noise dominate retrieval, a failure invisible under clean-query benchmarks.
articles.contribution: Shows structured surface artifacts (greetings, JSON fragments, metadata headers) act as spurious features that intrude into top ranks despite carrying no query-relevant information, breaking the link between similarity score and relevance.

articles.title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
articles.tldr: Systematic sensitivity analysis showing general and medical LLMs are unreliable under lexical and especially syntactic prompt perturbations on MedMCQA, threatening clinical measurement reliability.
articles.contribution: Shows that meaning-preserving lexical (BioSyn synonym swaps) and syntactic (clefting/passive/reordering) perturbations of the prompt alter clinical answers, so the operationalization does not faithfully realize the intended clinical question.

articles.title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
articles.tldr: Systematic sensitivity analysis showing general and medical LLMs are unreliable under lexical and especially syntactic prompt perturbations on MedMCQA, threatening clinical measurement reliability.
articles.contribution: Introduces stability metrics (BERTScore, USE, Response Rate, Follow-up Instruction Rate) and thresholds to quantify how reliably model outputs are preserved across syntactically equivalent prompts.

articles.title: To Adapt or not to Adapt, Rethinking the Value of Medical Knowledge-Aware Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Argues short-form MCQA benchmarks are insufficient to conclude medical-domain adaptation is worthless, introducing a perturbation-based, open-generation evaluation that separates reasoning from format-following.
articles.contribution: Contends that short-form MCQA operationalizations fail to capture genuine medical expertise, so marginal, unstable adaptation gains under such benchmarks cannot justify concluding domain adaptation is unnecessary.

articles.title: To Adapt or not to Adapt, Rethinking the Value of Medical Knowledge-Aware Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Argues short-form MCQA benchmarks are insufficient to conclude medical-domain adaptation is worthless, introducing a perturbation-based, open-generation evaluation that separates reasoning from format-following.
articles.contribution: Builds memorization- and position-resistant perturbations (Shuffle, Randomized labels, ReplaceNoto) so that correct answers cannot be retrieved by memorization or fixed-position shortcuts.

articles.title: To Adapt or not to Adapt, Rethinking the Value of Medical Knowledge-Aware Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Argues short-form MCQA benchmarks are insufficient to conclude medical-domain adaptation is worthless, introducing a perturbation-based, open-generation evaluation that separates reasoning from format-following.
articles.contribution: Replaces perplexity-based option selection (which simplifies the task and inflates scores) with strict open-generation exact-match and separates format-adherence failures from reasoning errors for fair general-vs-clinical comparison.

articles.title: Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation: Post-Training Without Rubric Verifiers
articles.tldr: A verifier-free rubric post-training method whose analysis documents reward hacking and judge-proxy bias in rubric-based RL, with a factual-claim audit quantifying metric corruption.
articles.contribution: Documents that optimizing the rubric-judge reward (GRPO) corrupts it: the policy inflates claim count and length without a quality gain, so the rubric score decouples from true response quality (Goodhart).

articles.title: Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation: Post-Training Without Rubric Verifiers
articles.tldr: A verifier-free rubric post-training method whose analysis documents reward hacking and judge-proxy bias in rubric-based RL, with a factual-claim audit quantifying metric corruption.
articles.contribution: Shows the LLM rubric verifier is unreliable: verifier-specific biases and a proxy-reward gap between the training judge (gpt-4o-mini) and stronger evaluation judge (gpt-5.4) cause scores that do not transfer, motivating removal of the judge from the loop.

articles.title: Voices of Civilizations: A Multilingual QA Benchmark for Global Music Understanding
articles.tldr: A multilingual music-QA benchmark whose validity controls (noise-input baseline, cross-song distractors) reveal audio LLMs answer via text/guessing rather than audio, with strong long-tail cultural bias.
articles.contribution: Uses a Gaussian-noise input baseline and cross-song distractors to test whether accuracy reflects audio-based cultural understanding, revealing models rely on textual context and question-language cues rather than the audio itself.

articles.title: Voices of Civilizations: A Multilingual QA Benchmark for Global Music Understanding
articles.tldr: A multilingual music-QA benchmark whose validity controls (noise-input baseline, cross-song distractors) reveal audio LLMs answer via text/guessing rather than audio, with strong long-tail cultural bias.
articles.contribution: Spans 38 languages including under-represented traditions and reports per-language accuracy, exposing a long-tail where low-resource cultures score far worse and existing benchmarks are biased toward high-resource repertoires.

articles.title: A Causal Framework for Estimating Heterogeneous Effects of On-Demand Tutoring
articles.tldr: Doubly-robust causal-forest framework with Deep-Knowledge-Tracing covariates to estimate confounded, self-selected on-demand tutoring effects, validated by placebo and sensitivity checks.
articles.contribution: Addresses time-varying self-selection confounding in observational tutoring data by conditioning a doubly-robust causal forest on a 50-dim DKT latent knowledge state plus AIPW orthogonalization to recover an unbiased session-level treatment effect.

articles.title: A Causal Framework for Estimating Heterogeneous Effects of On-Demand Tutoring
articles.tldr: Doubly-robust causal-forest framework with Deep-Knowledge-Tracing covariates to estimate confounded, self-selected on-demand tutoring effects, validated by placebo and sensitivity checks.
articles.contribution: Provides falsification/confirmatory evidence of the causal claim via a pre-intervention placebo (negative-control) outcome and a formal Robustness-Value sensitivity analysis benchmarking the strength an unmeasured confounder would need to nullify the effect.

articles.title: Early Warning Signals for OpenVLA Failure under Visual Distribution Shift
articles.tldr: Diagnostic decodability study probing OpenVLA activations for near-term failure, foregrounding train/test leakage from correlated timesteps and same-distribution vs task-held-out external validity as central limits.
articles.contribution: Identifies timestep-correlation leakage as the key validity threat to activation-probe failure monitors: adjacent highly-correlated states from one rollout appearing in both train and test can inflate reported AUROC, motivating episode-grouped/task-held-out split design.

articles.title: Early Warning Signals for OpenVLA Failure under Visual Distribution Shift
articles.tldr: Diagnostic decodability study probing OpenVLA activations for near-term failure, foregrounding train/test leakage from correlated timesteps and same-distribution vs task-held-out external validity as central limits.
articles.contribution: Shows same-distribution decodability does not establish generalization: an occlusion-trained monitor only partially transfers to camera jitter (AUROC drops from 0.972 to ~0.69-0.73), bounding the external-validity claim of the probe.

articles.title: HumanoidArena: Benchmarking Egocentric Hierarchical Whole-body Learning
articles.tldr: Hierarchical humanoid benchmark that treats the low-level motion tracker as a first-class evaluation axis, revealing that measured policy quality and ranking are confounded by the harness and that cross-tracker transfer is fragile.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates that the general-motion-tracker backend confounds the measured whole-body capability: the same policy family behaves differently under different GMTs and the best policy under one tracker is not the best under another, so treating the tracker as a hidden component invalidates rankings.

articles.title: HumanoidArena: Benchmarking Egocentric Hierarchical Whole-body Learning
articles.tldr: Hierarchical humanoid benchmark that treats the low-level motion tracker as a first-class evaluation axis, revealing that measured policy quality and ranking are confounded by the harness and that cross-tracker transfer is fragile.
articles.contribution: Uses perturbation-conditioned and cross-GMT protocols to show measured performance does not generalize: replacing the deployment tracker causes substantial drops and low retention, evidencing intermediate action intent is not tracker-invariant.

articles.title: Quantifying Hallucinations in Language Language Models on Medical Textbooks
articles.tldr: Text-grounded medical-QA benchmark that quantifies LLM hallucination against fixed textbook evidence with clinician verification, exposing plausibility-vs-faithfulness gaps.
articles.contribution: Builds ClinIQLink, a contamination-resistant benchmark linking every QA item to an authoritative public-domain textbook paragraph so hallucination is scored as any content unsupported by that source rather than memorized recall.

articles.title: Quantifying Hallucinations in Language Language Models on Medical Textbooks
articles.tldr: Text-grounded medical-QA benchmark that quantifies LLM hallucination against fixed textbook evidence with clinician verification, exposing plausibility-vs-faithfulness gaps.
articles.contribution: Shows surface plausibility is a misleading proxy for faithfulness: 98.8% of LLaMA-70B responses receive maximal plausibility yet 19.7% still hallucinate, so plausibility/accuracy scores under-represent the honesty construct.

articles.title: Quantifying Hallucinations in Language Language Models on Medical Textbooks
articles.tldr: Text-grounded medical-QA benchmark that quantifies LLM hallucination against fixed textbook evidence with clinician verification, exposing plausibility-vs-faithfulness gaps.
articles.contribution: Quantifies the reliability of its clinician-annotation instrument via inter-annotator agreement (quadratic-weighted kappa=0.92 in Experiment 1; kappa=0.57-0.61 in Experiment 2) to justify human scoring of unsupported claims.

articles.title: Reproduction Test Generation for Java SWE Issues
articles.tldr: Java reproduction-test benchmark (TDD-Bench-Java) paired with a contamination-free proprietary evaluation probing memorization and industry generalization of SWE test generators.
articles.contribution: Evaluates the e-Otter++ test generator on a private, never-published proprietary dataset of 150 Java issues to isolate genuine reproduction-test ability from training-data memorization that inflates public-benchmark scores.

articles.title: Reproduction Test Generation for Java SWE Issues
articles.tldr: Java reproduction-test benchmark (TDD-Bench-Java) paired with a contamination-free proprietary evaluation probing memorization and industry generalization of SWE test generators.
articles.contribution: Argues open-source-derived benchmarks may not represent industry Java code and shows models struggle markedly more on unseen proprietary repositories, questioning external validity of public-benchmark reproduction-test results.

articles.title: Bridging Music and Text with Crowdsourced Music Comments: A Sequence-to-Sequence Framework for Thematic Music Comments Generation
articles.tldr: Shows n-gram metrics (BLEU) misjudge NLG quality, rating generated music comments above real golden ones, and proposes discriminator-based V-Score/H-Score far better correlated with human raters.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates BLEU rewards frequent-word repetition and rates generated comments above real golden comments, so the n-gram metric misrepresents the semantic/thematic quality construct it is used to measure.

articles.title: Bridging Music and Text with Crowdsourced Music Comments: A Sequence-to-Sequence Framework for Thematic Music Comments Generation
articles.tldr: Shows n-gram metrics (BLEU) misjudge NLG quality, rating generated music comments above real golden ones, and proposes discriminator-based V-Score/H-Score far better correlated with human raters.
articles.contribution: Validates the proposed evaluator-based V-Score/H-Score against human raters as criterion, reporting Pearson 0.77/0.80 versus only 0.21 for BLEU, i.e. n-gram scores fail to predict human judgment.

articles.title: On the Fallacy of Global Token Perplexity in Spoken Language Model Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues global token perplexity mis-measures acoustic-consistency quality in spoken language models; localized/normalized perplexity and an embedding model-as-judge align far better with human MOS.
articles.contribution: Shows global token perplexity is disproportionately driven by long-range semantic tokens and thus mis-measures the local acoustic-consistency construct, a surface-proxy failure of the likelihood metric.

articles.title: On the Fallacy of Global Token Perplexity in Spoken Language Model Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues global token perplexity mis-measures acoustic-consistency quality in spoken language models; localized/normalized perplexity and an embedding model-as-judge align far better with human MOS.
articles.contribution: Uses human MOS as criterion and shows localized/normalized perplexity raises Pearson correlation with perceived quality from 0.62 to 0.73, better predicting human-rated continuation quality.

articles.title: On the Fallacy of Global Token Perplexity in Spoken Language Model Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues global token perplexity mis-measures acoustic-consistency quality in spoken language models; localized/normalized perplexity and an embedding model-as-judge align far better with human MOS.
articles.contribution: Proposes an embedding model-as-judge scorer whose distance judgments reach Pearson 0.81 with human MOS, providing a more reliable acoustic-consistency scorer than raw likelihood.

articles.title: On the Effect of Segmentation Width and Cluster Size on Speech Resynthesis and Continuation in Generative Spoken Language Models
articles.tldr: Bitrate study of GSLM speech resynthesis that finds standard automatic metrics unreliable for continuation, with perplexity negatively and VERT near-zero correlated with human MMOS and LLM-judge best but still low.
articles.contribution: Shows conventional speech-continuation metrics are unreliable proxies for human meaningfulness: Spearman correlation with MMOS is -0.105 for perplexity and 0.031 for VERT.

articles.title: On the Effect of Segmentation Width and Cluster Size on Speech Resynthesis and Continuation in Generative Spoken Language Models
articles.tldr: Bitrate study of GSLM speech resynthesis that finds standard automatic metrics unreliable for continuation, with perplexity negatively and VERT near-zero correlated with human MMOS and LLM-judge best but still low.
articles.contribution: Finds a GPT-4.1-mini LLM-as-judge pairwise scorer correlates highest with human MMOS (Spearman 0.323) yet remains too weak for reliable automatic evaluation of speech continuation.

articles.title: PromptIQ: Who Cares About Prompts? Let System Handle It - A Component-Aware Framework for T2I Generation
articles.tldr: Shows CLIP is insensitive to structural/component errors in text-to-image outputs and proposes a component-aware similarity (CAS) metric that penalizes missing or misplaced parts.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates CLIP similarity scores are near-identical for structurally flawed versus correct T2I images (roughly 0.23-0.30 vs 0.21-0.27), exposing the embedding metric's blindness to component-level structural validity.

articles.title: Decision-Oriented Text Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues intrinsic NLG metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) poorly predict downstream utility and proposes decision-oriented evaluation measuring a text's effect on human and LLM trading decisions.
articles.contribution: Introduces decision-oriented evaluation that scores market digests by the financial correctness of the trades they induce (thresholded against actual stock movements), exposing that intrinsic metrics mis-measure real decision utility.

articles.title: Decision-Oriented Text Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues intrinsic NLG metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) poorly predict downstream utility and proposes decision-oriented evaluation measuring a text's effect on human and LLM trading decisions.
articles.contribution: Reframes the target construct of NLG quality from reference-fidelity to downstream decision utility, arguing fluent summaries scoring well on BLEU/ROUGE can still guide investors into loss-making positions.

articles.title: Decision-Oriented Text Evaluation
articles.tldr: Argues intrinsic NLG metrics (BLEU/ROUGE) poorly predict downstream utility and proposes decision-oriented evaluation measuring a text's effect on human and LLM trading decisions.
articles.contribution: Argues human-investor evaluation is noisy and irreproducible and proposes deterministic (temperature-0) LLM agents as standardized, replicable decision-makers for evaluating generated text.

articles.title: KnowledgeGain: Evaluating and Optimizing Science News Generation for Reader Learning
articles.tldr: Introduces KnowledgeGain, a pre/post reader-comprehension metric for science news, validated in human studies and approximated by a calibrated LLM reader simulator, showing standard similarity and LLM-judge scores fail to capture reader learning.
articles.contribution: Argues standard similarity metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/BERTScore) and LLM-judge scores measure surface/semantic overlap, not reader learning; shows they correlate only weakly with human normalized KGain (all bootstrap CIs include zero), so KGain captures an orthogonal reader-centered construct they misrepresent.

articles.title: KnowledgeGain: Evaluating and Optimizing Science News Generation for Reader Learning
articles.tldr: Introduces KnowledgeGain, a pre/post reader-comprehension metric for science news, validated in human studies and approximated by a calibrated LLM reader simulator, showing standard similarity and LLM-judge scores fail to capture reader learning.
articles.contribution: Characterizes LLM 'hyper-accuracy distortion' as a scorer-reliability threat: a directly-prompted LLM reader is 91.6% correct vs 35.2% for humans and never abstains; adding an IDK option and verbalized sampling calibrates it (global KL 4.95 to 0.023), but it only tracks aggregate not per-topic gain, so it stays a dev-time proxy.

articles.title: Benchmarking Spatial Relationships in Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Shows existing T2I metrics cannot detect spatial-relation errors and introduces VISOR, a construct-valid metric validated against humans.
articles.contribution: Demonstrates prior automated T2I metrics (CLIPScore, BLEU/METEOR/CIDER) are near-blind to spatial correctness and proposes VISOR as a construct-valid spatial metric via a detector+predicate pipeline

articles.title: Benchmarking Spatial Relationships in Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Shows existing T2I metrics cannot detect spatial-relation errors and introduces VISOR, a construct-valid metric validated against humans.
articles.contribution: VISOR_cond disentangles object-generation ability from spatial understanding, removing object accuracy as a confounder in the aggregated spatial score

articles.title: Benchmarking Spatial Relationships in Text-to-Image Generation
articles.tldr: Shows existing T2I metrics cannot detect spatial-relation errors and introduces VISOR, a construct-valid metric validated against humans.
articles.contribution: Human study (1000 images/model, 3 workers) shows VISOR's model ranking matches human judgment, providing convergent evidence the metric is valid

articles.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Proves that inference-time reward hacking (true reward rises then falls) is inevitable for Best-of-n/Best-of-Poisson and shows hedging on the proxy reward mitigates it.
articles.contribution: Establishes a principled limit: overoptimizing a misspecified proxy reward model provably corrupts the true objective, formalizing Goodhart for inference-time alignment

articles.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
articles.tldr: Proves that inference-time reward hacking (true reward rises then falls) is inevitable for Best-of-n/Best-of-Poisson and shows hedging on the proxy reward mitigates it.
articles.contribution: Empirically shows Best-of-n/SBoN/BoP selection harnesses hack the proxy on math/reasoning setups, and HedgeTune-tuned hedging recovers the reward peak without collapse

articles.title: Can't See the Forest for the Trees: Benchmarking Multimodal Safety Awareness for Multimodal LLMs
articles.tldr: MMSafeAware benchmark exposes that MLLMs used as safety judges are both unsafe (miss unsafe content) and over-sensitive, relying on single-modality shortcut cues.
articles.contribution: Shows MLLMs are unreliable safety judges: GPT-4V misclassifies 36.1% of unsafe inputs as safe, questioning their use as safety scorers

articles.title: Can't See the Forest for the Trees: Benchmarking Multimodal Safety Awareness for Multimodal LLMs
articles.tldr: MMSafeAware benchmark exposes that MLLMs used as safety judges are both unsafe (miss unsafe content) and over-sensitive, relying on single-modality shortcut cues.
articles.contribution: Over-safety subset reveals MLLMs judge on surface single-modality lexical/visual cues (a shortcut), misclassifying 59.9% of benign pairs as unsafe

articles.title: Exposing the Achilles' Heel: Evaluating LLMs Ability to Handle Mistakes in Mathematical Reasoning
articles.tldr: MWP-MISTAKE injects reasoning-step errors into math word problems, exposing LLM mistake-detection failures and data-contamination inflating GSM-8K scores.
articles.contribution: Detects GSM-8K/MATH train-test contamination via a guided-vs-general ROUGE-L overlap gap that inflates accuracy on older datasets

articles.title: Exposing the Achilles' Heel: Evaluating LLMs Ability to Handle Mistakes in Mathematical Reasoning
articles.tldr: MWP-MISTAKE injects reasoning-step errors into math word problems, exposing LLM mistake-detection failures and data-contamination inflating GSM-8K scores.
articles.contribution: Shows final-answer accuracy is a surface proxy: models derive correct answers despite undetected reasoning-step mistakes, so accuracy misrepresents reasoning capability

articles.title: On the robustness of multimodal language model towards distractions
articles.tldr: I-ScienceQA injects visual/textual distractions into ScienceQA to test VLM robustness, revealing that clean benchmarks overstate real-world reasoning reliability.
articles.contribution: Shows clean ScienceQA overestimates robustness; 8,100 distraction-augmented samples expose accuracy degradation under realistic noisy inputs

articles.title: On the robustness of multimodal language model towards distractions
articles.tldr: I-ScienceQA injects visual/textual distractions into ScienceQA to test VLM robustness, revealing that clean benchmarks overstate real-world reasoning reliability.
articles.contribution: Irrelevant visual/textual distractions act as confounders breaking the link between exact-match score and true reasoning, with textual distractions more damaging than visual

articles.title: Operationalizing Pluralistic Values in Large Language Model Alignment Reveals Trade-offs in Safety, Inclusivity, and Model Behavior
articles.tldr: Systematic study of how rater demographics and alignment-pipeline design choices (rating scale, disagreement handling, DPO vs GRPO) shape LLM alignment outcomes.
articles.contribution: Preserving rater disagreement yields ~53% greater toxicity reduction than majority voting, and 5-point scales beat binary by ~22%, so aggregation choice materially changes alignment signal

articles.title: Operationalizing Pluralistic Values in Large Language Model Alignment Reveals Trade-offs in Safety, Inclusivity, and Model Behavior
articles.tldr: Systematic study of how rater demographics and alignment-pipeline design choices (rating scale, disagreement handling, DPO vs GRPO) shape LLM alignment outcomes.
articles.contribution: Rater demographics systematically confound alignment labels: male raters rate 18% less toxic and Black participants 44% higher on emotional awareness than baselines

articles.title: Operationalizing Pluralistic Values in Large Language Model Alignment Reveals Trade-offs in Safety, Inclusivity, and Model Behavior
articles.tldr: Systematic study of how rater demographics and alignment-pipeline design choices (rating scale, disagreement handling, DPO vs GRPO) shape LLM alignment outcomes.
articles.contribution: Validates the GPT-4o-mini scorer of fine-tuned model toxicity/emotional-awareness outputs against human expert judgements at 85% agreement

articles.tldr: DevBench is a telemetry-grounded, contamination-resistant code-completion benchmark with a validated LLM judge and cross-generator fairness checks.
articles.contribution: Derives task categories from 1B+ real developer completions with balanced 300/language sampling, giving ecological validity over convenience-scraped benchmarks

articles.contribution: Logistic-regression test finds no significant same-generator-family favoritism, with min pairwise ranking consistency rho=0.91 across generator subsets

articles.title: An Item Response Theory Framework for Persuasion
articles.tldr: Applies Item Response Theory to separate latent audience persuadability from argument persuasiveness across three persuasion datasets.
articles.contribution: Uses IRT latent variables to disentangle audience persuadability from argument persuasiveness so the persuasion measure is not confounded by the audience

articles.title: Labeling Free-text Data using Language Model Ensembles
articles.tldr: Ensembles of small open-source LLMs, guided by embedding-based relevancy scoring, improve reliability of topic labeling on free-text vs individual models.
articles.contribution: PCA relevancy-score ensembling with outlier removal balances union/intersection labels, raising F1 and inter-rater reliability over any single LLM

articles.title: Labeling Free-text Data using Language Model Ensembles
articles.tldr: Ensembles of small open-source LLMs, guided by embedding-based relevancy scoring, improve reliability of topic labeling on free-text vs individual models.
articles.contribution: Quantifies heterogeneity across same-size open-source LLM labelers (precision/sensitivity tradeoffs) and shows relevancy scores agree more than binary labels

articles.title: Modeling Variants of Prompts for Vision-Language Models
articles.tldr: RobustPrompt Benchmark + Prompt Robustness Score (PRS) quantify how VLM (CLIP) accuracy swings with superficial prompt-template phrasing, exposing prompt-sensitivity as an evaluation reliability threat.
articles.contribution: Introduces the RobustPrompt Benchmark and Prompt Robustness Score (PRS) to quantify how superficial prompt-template variation (article/synonym/length/person/tense/sentiment) destabilizes zero-shot VLM classification accuracy.

articles.title: Two-sided conformalized survival analysis
articles.tldr: Model-free conformal procedure giving finite-sample-valid two-sided/one-sided prediction intervals for right-censored survival times without modeling the censoring mechanism.
articles.contribution: Provides distribution-free finite-sample coverage for survival prediction intervals that wraps around any black-box survival model, giving valid uncertainty quantification instead of unguaranteed point predictions.

articles.title: AgentChangeBench: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework for Goal-Shift Robustness in Conversational AI
articles.tldr: Multi-dimensional agent benchmark showing pass@k obscures goal-shift robustness; adds TSR/TUE/TCRR/GSRT metrics over 315 tasks, 3 enterprise domains, 5 personas.
articles.contribution: Argues binary pass@k collapses all recovery paths into one score and misrepresents the construct of agent robustness; introduces a GSRT/TCRR/TUE/TSR decomposition so recovery latency and redundancy are measured explicitly.

articles.title: AgentChangeBench: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework for Goal-Shift Robustness in Conversational AI
articles.tldr: Multi-dimensional agent benchmark showing pass@k obscures goal-shift robustness; adds TSR/TUE/TCRR/GSRT metrics over 315 tasks, 3 enterprise domains, 5 personas.
articles.contribution: Static-goal benchmarks are unrepresentative of real multi-turn deployments; adds explicit mid-dialogue goal-shift sequences and five personas to improve the ecological/external validity of conversational-agent evaluation.

articles.title: Interpretable Difficulty-Aware Knowledge Tracing in Tutor-Student Dialogues
articles.tldr: Interpretable dialogue knowledge-tracing that separates LLM-estimated student ability from tutor-task difficulty via a 1PL IRT layer, aligning the measurement with psychometric/cognitive theory.
